items.title: focus: the committed .board/focus.json pins a stale active epic, so lanes cut from master are refused out-of-epic-pooled for the real epic child
items.body:
Parent: #1510

## Model tier

L0 — measured, mechanical (a stale tracked artifact and its consumer).

## Measured

`.board/focus.json` is **tracked** at `origin/master` with the OLD epic:

```
$ git show origin/master:.board/focus.json
{"active_epic": 706, "activated_at": "2026-09-19T01:25:03Z", "wave_cap": 12, "max_agents": 0, "pooled": []}
```

The live focus moved to `#1510` on `2026-09-20T14:20:48Z` and today exists **only as an uncommitted working-tree modification in the shared checkout**:

```
$ git status --porcelain -- .board/focus.json
 M .board/focus.json          # (active_epic: 1510)
```

## Impact — it starves the CLAIM path for every lane cut from `master`

A lane worktree is cut from `origin/master` (GR-3 / rule 15), so it inherits `active_epic: 706`. `focus.active()` resolves that pin and `order._refusal_out_of_epic()` then computes the *derived* pooled set against the WRONG epic, so a legitimate child of the real active epic is refused as pooled:

```
$ python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py claim --issue 1625 --agent ao1625-1790013760 --lane governance/dispatch
claim REFUSED: out-of-epic-pooled — #1625 is outside the active epic #1254 (parked in .board/pool.jsonl;
promoted just-in-time by a brain directive when an active-epic child declares it as a blocker)
```

Three separate errors in that one line, all measured:

1. `#1625` **is** an open child of the live active epic `#1510` (`focus` lists it among 1510's 54 open children).
2. `.board/pool.jsonl` is **empty** (`wc -l` → 0) — the pooled verdict is *derived* from the (wrong) focus, never stored, so the remedy the message names ("promoted just-in-time by a brain directive") cannot apply to a nonexistent entry.
3. The named "active epic" is `#1254`, which is itself in the *pooled* list — so the refusal names a pooled epic as the active one.

With the live focus in place the same claim is accepted with no other change:

```
$ cp <shared>/.board/focus.json ./.board/focus.json   # active_epic 1510
claim accepted: #1625 as ao1625-1790013760 (active-epic-child)
```

## Why this is a defect and not just a stale file

The committed artifact is the **only** focus a lane can read offline, and it is ~2 days behind the live pin. Nothing in `make verify` fails on it: the gate is green, and the damage surfaces later as an *unattributable refusal* in a lane that did nothing wrong. This is the same class already recorded for the board snapshot (`governance/lessons/rca/RCA-0014-stale-snapshot-no-trigger.md`, and the `unknown-issue` section of #1161) — a tracked, committed stand-in that rots because its refresh is a *write* nobody commits.

## Acceptance

- A lane cut from `origin/master` claims an open child of the live active epic **with no local edit to `.board/focus.json`**.
- The refusal for genuinely out-of-epic work still fires, and its message names the epic that is actually active and does not point at a pooled epic.
- Negative control: with the focus artifact deliberately set to a closed/nonexistent epic, the claim still refuses (fail-closed), rather than treating "unresolvable pin" as "no focus, everything pooled".

## Provisionally unblocked by (not a fix)

A local `cp` of the live focus into the lane worktree, and a `git checkout -- .board/focus.json` before staging so the artifact is never shipped inside a feature commit. That is a workaround a lane must discover for itself; it is recorded here rather than left implicit.

Refs #1510

items.title: dispatch: tiered.py (claude/deepseek) and routing.py (hermes/paperclip) are two non-composing routers
items.body:
Parent: #1268

## Gap

`governance/dispatch/tiered.py` + `governance/dispatch/tier-policy.json` and
`fleet/routing.py` + `fleet/profiles/routing.policy.json` are two separate,
non-composing dispatch systems that between them cover all four runtimes but
never hand a task from one to the other:

- `governance/dispatch/tier-policy.json`: `"tiers"` keys are only `claude` and
  `deepseek` (`default_provider: "deepseek"`); `governance/dispatch/cli.py:1037`
  `--provider` help text: "claude or deepseek". No `hermes`/`paperclip` key.
- `fleet/profiles/routing.policy.json` `personas` key set is only
  `['hermes', 'paperclip']` (verified live via `python3 -c
  "import json;print(json.load(open('fleet/profiles/routing.policy.json'))['personas'].keys()")`).
  Claude/DeepSeek are absent from this router.
- `fleet/runtimes.yaml` is the only file that lists all 7 runtime ids
  (`claude-session`, `claude-subagent`, `deepseek-sister`, `deepseek-executor`,
  `copilot-agent`, `hermes`, `paperclip`) — but it is a liveness/beat registry
  (`fleet/runtime_liveness.py`), not a router.

Consequence: a task tiered into `governance/dispatch/tiered.py` (tier-space:
L0/L1/L2 -> claude/deepseek) has no adapter to become a
`fleet/routing.py`-routed task (capability-space: persona -> hermes/paperclip),
and vice versa. Epic #1268's own definition of done ("a task actually flows
Claude -> DeepSeek -> Hermes -> Paperclip and back") cannot be met while these
two routers use disjoint vocabularies with nothing bridging them. This is not a
delivery-layer problem: the mailbox (`fleet/channel.py`, `.fleet/sent/`,
`.fleet/done/`), dead-letter (`fleet/runaway.py`), and per-runtime control-verb
authorization (`control-plane/control/verbs.yaml` `allowed_runtimes`, checked
against `fleet/schema/message.schema.json`'s `runtime` field) are all real,
mechanical, and runtime-agnostic — they would carry a task through if one
router handed it to the other. Nothing does.

Related: #1562 (open, Parent #1510) is the Hermes-only half of this gap
("Hermes agent claims work through governance/dispatch" — wiring Hermes into
the dispatcher's claim/peer-check identity classification). It does not cover
Paperclip, and does not cover unifying `tiered.py`'s tier-space with
`routing.py`'s capability-space generally. This issue is the epic-#1268-scoped
tracking issue for that broader router-unification gap; #1562 can close as a
partial fix toward it.

## Smallest fix

Not "merge the two routers" (that is an architecture decision, out of scope
for this review). The smallest fix: one adapter function that, given a
`tiered.py` dispatch outcome for a task tagged as needing a Hermes/Paperclip
capability, calls `fleet/routing.py`'s persona router with that task id — and
the reverse (a `routing.py`-routed task that names a `tier:` requirement calls
into `tiered.py`). Both routers already write/read the same mailbox
(`fleet/channel.py`), so the adapter only needs to translate the routing
*decision*, not the transport.

Done: a task can be dispatched with `tier:L1` AND `capability:hermes` (or the
reverse ordering) and both routers observe and act on it, verified by a new
`governance/dispatch/tests/test_tiered.py`-style negative control that fails
today (task has both a tier requirement and a persona requirement; assert the
outcome routes through both, not just whichever router it landed in first).

## Evidence sources

Gathered by the #1268 integrations e2e review (docs/rca/2026-09-21-integrations-e2e-review.md).

items.title: conformance: 67 milestoned open issues lack priority/area/gdc — a cascading label debt the class backfill just exposed
items.body:
Parent: #1254

## The red (measured, post-#1691 + class backfill)

`check-conformance` is a **cascading** board debt. On the committed board snapshot,
before the class backfill, the check short-circuited on the first missing dimension:

```
$ python3 governance/conformance/cli.py check
conformance: FAIL (71 error(s), 1 warning(s))
    ERROR   class-missing   issue #1254 declares no class; it cannot be held to any rung of the ladder
    … (71 total)
```

After backfilling `class:enterprise` on all 71 (the policy's declared
`filing.default_class`), the next layer is exposed — the very same issues now fail
the remaining `required` dimensions (`class, type, priority, area`):

```
conformance: FAIL (134 error(s), 71 warning(s))
    ERROR   classification-incomplete   issue #1254 declares class 'enterprise' but no `priority:` label
    ERROR   classification-incomplete   issue #1254 declares class 'enterprise' but no `area:` label
    … (134 = 67 issues × 2 missing dimensions)
```

`class-missing` is now **0**; the residual is `priority` + `area` (and, per the
policy's `expectations`, `gdc` next — `enterprise` expects `gdc`, `elite` expects
`gdc`+`pillar`).

## What happened, measured

The conformance `class` mandate (`required = [class, type, priority, area]`) never
reached the pre-existing backlog. All 71 were `pmo:triaged` with `type:*`/`tier:*`/
`handoff:*` labels but **no `class`**, and — because the check short-circuits on
`class-missing` first — their missing `priority`/`area`/`gdc` was invisible until the
class layer was cleared. The 72-hour-stale committed snapshot (fixed in #1691 /
#1692) had been masking all of it: on the stale board the same check read
`OK (13 item(s) conform, 1 deviation)`.

## Disposition so far

- `class:enterprise` backfilled on all 71 (the declared `filing.default_class`).
- `priority` and `area` have **no honest bulk default**: some of the 67 already carry
  `priority:P0`/`P1` (e.g. #1501, #1509), and `area` is a functional classification
  the policy has no universal default for (`filing.defaults.area = standards` applies
  to the filing tool's own new issues, not to this backlog). Applying a guessed
  `area:` to 67 issues would mint wrong data that later tooling would trust.

## The decision this issue owns

Three routes, not pre-empted here:

1. **PMO backfill** — triage `priority` + `area` (and `gdc`) on the 67, one by one.
2. **Grandfather the pre-mandate backlog** — the checker already has the exact seam
   for this: un-milestoned backlog is *"counted, not failed"* (`checker.py`
   `include_unmilestoned`). Un-milestoning the 67 (or declaring a cutoff date before
   which the class mandate is advisory) drops them out of enforcement scope without
   fabricating labels.
3. **A policy cutoff** — `policy.yaml` gains a `class_required_since` date; issues
   opened before it are exempt (like the un-milestoned-backlog rule, but explicit).

`check-reconcile` is no longer the box's only clock-driven red: the conformance
mandate is the next one, and it is a *label* record that lapses on every triage
change, not a repo diff.

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1485
Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1692

items.title: gate: the committed board snapshot is 72h-stale with no installed producer, so check-dispatch-queue and check-ticket-projection red every lane
items.body:
Parent: #1254

## Model tier

L0/L1 rating: **L0** — locate, refresh a committed record through its own declared remedy, and prove two checks flip rc 1 → 0.

## Escalation

Attempt at L0. Max attempts: **N = 3**. If blocked after 3 attempts, comment on this issue with the exact failure and label `escalate:L1`, then stop. Never silent abandonment.

## Lifecycle contract (no lingering)

- Closed ONLY via a merged PR whose body contains `Closes #<n>` plus acceptance output and negative-control output.
- Picking this up = owning it to closure: implement, `make verify` green on the branch, merge, confirm auto-close, delete branch, remove worktree, final evidence comment.

## Root cause

Two checks are red on **every** lane and on a pristine `origin/master 1e4050a0`, for a reason no lane's diff causes — so they refuse every landing on the box, exactly the way `check-reconcile` did in #1485:

```
$ bash scripts/check-dispatch-queue.sh          # rc=1
  == board freshness (the age this consumer tolerates) ==
    FAIL  board-snapshot-stale: .board/snapshot.json — generated_at 2026-09-18T15:14:20Z is 72.8h old, beyond the 72h this consumer tolerates — the board has moved
  freshness: FAIL — the committed board snapshot is outside the age this consumer tolerates (see above), so every exists/open answer is against a stale frontier

$ bash scripts/check-ticket-projection.sh       # rc=1
    FAIL  board-snapshot-stale: .board/snapshot.json — generated_at 2026-09-18T15:14:20Z is 72.8h old, beyond the 72h this consumer tolerates — the board has moved
check-ticket-projection: FAIL — the committed board snapshot is outside the age this consumer tolerates (see above), so every reference the projection resolves
```

The record is committed (`.board/snapshot.json` is tracked) and its age is the whole finding: **72.8h against a 72h tolerance**. Nothing about the board's content is wrong.

The producer exists but is not installed: the claim path reports
`board refresher — ao-fleet-snapshot-refresh is not installed (declared enabled:false); the entry point refreshes the board in-band, so the contract is met by self-refresh`.
So the record's age is a chore with no owner, and it re-reds the box 72h after every manual refresh. A second consumer is *tighter still*: `governance/dispatch/cli.py claim` refuses at **15 minutes** (`claim: CANNOT-ASSESS — snapshot-stale …`), so on a box whose snapshot is older than 15 minutes **not one claim of any issue can succeed** — the whole fleet's dispatch is wedged on one committed file.

This issue is **not** #1631: that one is `.board/boundary-snapshot.json`, owned by `#1510`, and there the rotted snapshot makes a gate fail **open**. Here a second snapshot makes two gates fail **closed**.

## Fix

1. Refresh the committed record through its own declared remedy and commit it: `python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py snapshot --from-github`. Measured on a clean base: `snapshot: wrote .board/snapshot.json (861 issues, 522 with declared chain edges)`, after which **both** checks read rc 0.
2. Decide the producer, do not leave it implied: either install `ao-fleet-snapshot-refresh` (a fleet rung, code-native — no workflow files, GR-15) or lower the consumers' declared tolerance so it matches the contract the claim path already states ("the contract is met by self-refresh"). A record refreshed by hand cannot outrun a box that moves hourly; #1476/#1338 own the same recurrence for the reconcile baseline.

## Acceptance

On a pristine detached `origin/master` with the record refreshed:
`bash scripts/check-dispatch-queue.sh` rc 0 and `bash scripts/check-ticket-projection.sh` rc 0, both quoting a `generated_at` inside the tolerance.

Negative control: leave the record at `2026-09-18T15:14:20Z` and re-run both — each must read rc 1 naming `board-snapshot-stale`, which is the state measured above (rc 1 on both, on the unmodified base).

items.title: train: a check declared as an inline command is permanently unrunnable, so it can never be attributed (pytest-fleet, pytest-suites, ...)
items.body:
**Status under single-dev method:** c
## Summary

`fleet/runner/train.py::run_check()` runs `bash scripts/<script>.sh`. A check declared in
`scripts/verify.sh` as an **inline command** has no such script in either naming shape, so it is
**permanently `unrunnable`** — in every wave, forever. Because `attribute_red` reaches
`attributed`/`pre-existing` only through a resolved script, such a check can never be attributed,
so it can never name a culprit, so the merge train can never drop it from the wave.

Found while proving the fix for #1685 on real data (that issue fixes the *other* cause of
`unrunnable`: a bare-vs-prefixed name shape). Both are needed; this one is not fixed by #1686.

## Evidence (measured 2026-09-21, master `1e4050a0`)

The declaration table is `name|command`:

```
$ grep -nE "'(reconcile|pytest-fleet)\|" scripts/verify.sh
373:  'reconcile|bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh'
662:  'pytest-fleet|env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q fleet/tests'
```

`reconcile` resolves, `pytest-fleet` cannot. Against the retained round tree
(`.fleet/runner/trains/20260921T141534Z-r2/tree`, head `8a58d598`), with the fix from #1686
applied:

```
reconcile                    -> scripts/check-reconcile.sh
pytest-fleet                 -> None
paperclip-control-mapping    -> scripts/check-paperclip-control-mapping.sh
...
reconcile                    run_check -> RAN
pytest-fleet                 run_check -> None (=> unrunnable)
```

`pytest-fleet` was one of only **three** real reds in that round — from the round's own
`.verify/.results.tsv`: `reconcile rc=1`, `pytest-fleet rc=1`, `paperclip-control-mapping rc=1`
(211 rows `rc=0`). So a third of that wave's red set was unattributable by construction.

The same applies to every check whose declaration is a command rather than a `check-*.sh`
script — `pytest-suites`, `pytest-control`, `code-headers`, `finops-kpi` among them, which is
exactly the set the old code kept reporting as `unrunnable`.

## Consequence

`fleet/runner/cli.py:830-838` shrinks the wave only through
`culprits = held_prs(attributions)`, and `held_prs()` returns a PR only for
`verdict == "attributed"`. An inline-command check therefore leaves `wave` byte-identical, and the
next round re-folds the same set and reds the same way. Four rounds were retired today
(`#1679 #1680 #1681 #1683`) with master unmoved at `1e4050a0`.

## Possible shape (not prescriptive)

Teach the resolver the second declaration shape: read the check's command from
`scripts/verify.sh`'s `'name|command'` table and run that, rather than only
`bash scripts/<name>.sh`. The table is already the authoritative source of both the name and the
command, so it is the natural place to resolve from — and it would let the same code answer
`check_inputs()` for such a check instead of falling back to "every candidate".

Acceptance: a red whose declaration is an inline command resolves and runs, so it reaches
`attributed`/`pre-existing`/`cannot-assess` instead of `unrunnable`; a check that is in the table
but whose command cannot run is `cannot-assess`, never a green; and the existing prefixed/bare
shape controls from #1686 keep passing.

Related: #1685 (the name-shape cause, fixed by #1686), #1661 (reds that cannot be attributed to a
lane), #1602 (`reconcile`'s orphan-lane reds).

items.title: train: every red is unrunnable — attribute_red resolves scripts/<name>.sh but the attestation names checks bare (4 trains retired today)
items.body:
## Root cause (measured 2026-09-21, master `1e4050a0`)

`fleet/runner/train.py` resolves a red check's script as `scripts/<name>.sh`, but the
name it is handed carries **no `check-` prefix** — so the path never exists, every red
is recorded `unrunnable`, and the train is retired on every round.

Three independent measurements:

1. **The name is bare.** `scripts/verify.sh:1032` `name="${entry%%|*}"` takes the part of
   the `'name|command'` entry before the pipe, and `:1180` writes `"name": name` into
   `.verify/attestation.json`. So the attestation's `checks[].name` is `reconcile`,
   `env-surface`, `verdict-contains` — never `check-reconcile`.
2. **The attestation is the preferred source.** `fleet/runner/verify.py`
   `parse_verify_evidence()` prefers the attestation (`source = "attestation"`) and only
   falls back to the transcript regex (which yields `check-docs: FAIL` style, i.e.
   PREFIXED) when the attestation is absent.
3. **The resolver cannot handle the bare shape.** `train.py:753`
   `run_check()` builds `Path(worktree)/"scripts"/f"{name}.sh"`; for `reconcile` that is
   `scripts/reconcile.sh`, which does not exist (the real file is
   `scripts/check-reconcile.sh`; `grep -cE "^ *'([a-z0-9-]+)\|bash scripts/check-\1\.sh'"
   scripts/verify.sh` = 110 entries). `run_check` therefore returns `None` and
   `attribute_red` records `unrunnable`.

## Blast radius — a train that can never converge

`attribute_red`'s whole purpose is to answer "is this red pre-existing on master, or does
this PR owe it?". A red that cannot be resolved to a script can be neither: it is
`unrunnable`, so the `pre-existing` escape ("the wave does not pay for it") never fires
and no PR is ever blamed. The train is then abandoned with `reason="red:see log"` and
re-cut, forever.

Measured on this box today — **every attribution, 21 of 21, was `unrunnable`**:

```
$ grep -a '"train-attr"' .fleet/runner/ledger.jsonl | python3 -c '...'
  check names seen : {'surface-class': 2, 'pytest-fleet': 3, 'control-verbs': 2,
    'pytest-control': 2, 'code-headers': 2, 'env-surface': 2, 'finops-kpi': 2,
    'verdict-contains': 2, 'reconcile': 2, 'paperclip-control-mapping': 1, 'pytest-suites': 1}
  verdicts seen    : {'unrunnable': 21}
  any prefixed?    : NONE — all names are BARE
```

and four trains retired the same day (`train-abandon ... reason="red:see log"` for
#1679, #1680, #1681, #1683) with master unmoved at `1e4050a0` and 30 PRs blocked.

## Why the covering test did not catch it

`fleet/runner/tests/test_train.py::test_a_failing_check_with_no_script_is_unrunnable_never_green`
passes the name `check-does-not-exist` — the PREFIXED shape — and
`scripts/check-pr-runner.sh` asserts `failing=['check-docs']`, also prefixed. Both
exercise the transcript fallback; neither exercises the attestation path that production
actually uses. A control that cannot fail is a formality.

## Fix

Resolve a check's script from **either** shape, in one place:

- `run_check()` and `check_inputs()` try `scripts/check-<name>.sh` and `scripts/<name>.sh`
  (and the name as given if it already starts with `check-`).
- The `CHECK_INPUTS` lookup tolerates both keys (its keys are `check-<name>`) so an
  undeclared check is still paid for rather than skipped.
- A check genuinely absent in both shapes stays `unrunnable` — never silently green.

## Acceptance / regression test

A new control in `fleet/runner/tests/test_train.py` that exercises the **attestation**
shape: a **bare**-named red (`["reconcile"]`) in a tree that carries
`scripts/check-reconcile.sh` must resolve and run that script (attributed or
`pre-existing`), and must NOT be `unrunnable`. The negative control — a bare name whose
script is in neither shape — must still be `unrunnable`. The existing prefixed-shape
control must keep passing, unchanged.

`Closes` trailer + `Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#<n>` will be on the PR.

Parent: #1669
**Status under single-dev method:** c

## Model tier

L0/L1 rating: **L1**.

## Escalation

Attempt at L1. Max attempts: **N = 3**. If blocked after 3 attempts, comment on this issue with the exact failure and label `escalate:L2`, then stop. Never silent abandonment.

## Lifecycle contract (no lingering)

- Closed ONLY via a merged PR whose body contains `Closes #<n>` plus acceptance output and negative-control output.
- Picking this up = owning it to closure: implement, `make verify` green on the branch, merge, confirm auto-close, delete branch, remove worktree, final evidence comment.

## Root cause
Branch protection requires only `ao/gate-of-record`; it is published solely by a LOCAL `make verify` (`scripts/gate-status.sh`), measured 15m55s wall per PR with `gate-lock` cap 4 → ~15 PRs/hour theoretical, far less in practice; the Cloud Build venue has no `gh` and cannot publish it (#1382 #1472 history). Draining 30 PRs is a full working day of the box.

## Fix
Per #1295/#1343: the shared-services PR runner verifies each PR head and publishes `ao/gate-of-record`; until it holds, a merge-train's ONE verify covers its whole fold (already #1411) and a green train head's status is re-posted for each folded PR head so merged-tree evidence exists per PR.
## Acceptance
A PR opened by a lane gets `ao/gate-of-record` without any local `make verify` within 30 min. Negative control: red head → failure status by name.

items.title: EPIC: PR lifecycle never fails — issue → implement → verify → merge → close issue + PR + artifacts, templated end to end
items.body:
**Status under single-dev method:** b
## Model tier

L0/L1 rating: **L1** — children are gate/contract work; architecture calls escalate to L2 only on observed difficulty.

## Root cause

Full RCA / gap report: `docs/rca/2026-09-21-pr-release-lifecycle.md` (PR to follow under this epic). Short form: every stage of issue → implement → verify → merge → close has a separate, hand-invoked owner (#1651); merge trains are invalidated by any individual merge to master and nothing detects it; shared files (docs indexes, ADR numbers) have no allocator so collisions surface at merge time; box-state checks (reaper schedule, reconcile baseline, orphan census) red every lane venue; the PR body contract is still hand-typed; the only producer of the required `ao/gate-of-record` is a local 16-minute `make verify` behind a box cap of 4.

## Escalation

Attempt at L1. Tiers: L0 = Claude Haiku / DeepSeek V4 Flash -> L1 = Claude Sonnet / DeepSeek V4 Pro -> L2 = Claude Opus.
- Max attempts: **N = 3**.
- If blocked after 3 attempts, comment on this issue with the exact failure and label `escalate:L2`, then stop. Never silent abandonment.

## Lifecycle contract (no lingering)

- This epic closes only when every child is closed by a merged PR and a 7-day negative control holds: zero open PRs older than 24h that are MERGEABLE with a green lane verify, zero baseline-record PRs, zero stale merge trains.
- Picking up a child = owning it to closure (implement, verify, merge, issue auto-closed, PR closed, branch/worktree/lane/lease/baseline reclaimed, final evidence comment).

## Target model

An agent that picks up an issue owns the WHOLE lifecycle. One templated state machine, each transition guarded by a gate that makes the failure impossible rather than a doctrine that asks agents not to:

claim → lease files → branch/worktree → implement → scoped tests → PR from template (trailer + `Closes` GENERATED, never typed) → lane verify → ONE guarded merge verb → post-merge attestation → close-out reclaims branch, worktree, lane record, leases, baseline rows → issue auto-closed → final evidence comment.

## Measured 2026-09-21 (33 open PRs, session close-out attempt)

- 3 merge trains (#1656 #1645 #1634) stale/CONFLICTING: 6 of 21 folded lanes landed individually underneath; no detector, no auto re-cut.
- 8 PRs CONFLICTING, 6 of them on `docs/README.md` alone; add/add on `docs/BUILT-NOT-SHIPPED-AO.md` (#1618 vs #1540); ADR-0033 claimed twice (#1628 vs #1629).

- `check-reconcile` 5 NEW rows → yet another baseline PR; `orphan-pr` census 20→31 in 20 min (blocking until #1659).
- 13 leftover zero-byte gate locks (`gate-lock.sh status`).
- 6 of 33 PR bodies failed `check-squash-message.sh` (trailer not last paragraph); 2 PRs close epic-labelled issues (train refuses); 1 draft.

items.title: gate of record is non-deterministic: governance/lifecycle reds the venue on content that does not touch it (2 of 3 samples), and the failing test is not publishable
items.body:
Parent: #1254
**Status under single-dev method:** c

## Summary

The gate of record (`control-plane-verify (purebliss-ghl)`) returns **`completed/failure` for content that does not touch the failing suite**, in 2 of 3 independent runs of the same work. The failing check is always `check-pytest-suites` → the `governance/lifecycle` suite, and the composite never publishes enough evidence to name the test inside it.

Net effect: **every merge wave is a coin flip on this suite.** Because a red gate cannot be forced, one flaky suite blocks the landing of any wave, and the red cannot be attributed to a lane — so it also cannot be fixed by a lane.

## Evidence

Three trains, three venue samples, ~the same 20-lane content on base `d0eecdc0`:

| train | build | verdict | failing check |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1656 | `cd9262de-da12-45a1-9b55-b858a7a324cd` | `1 of 232` | `check-pytest-suites` → `governance/lifecycle` |
| #1658 | `e7444a0b-178e-47b6-a885-8db036399c59` | `1 of 232` | `check-isolation-landed` → `isolation-enforce: 2 unrecorded …` (a **real** red; attributed and held: #1657) |
| #1660 | `9109401c-9929-4cd6-a559-5ea07a2e4db7` | `1 of 232` | `check-pytest-suites` → `governance/lifecycle` |

The middle sample shows the venue *does* discriminate — the method below named its owner. The outer two are the flake.

**The fold does not touch the suite.** Measured on each train's own head:

```
$ git diff --name-only origin/master..origin/tr1656 -- governance/lifecycle   # 0 files
$ git diff --name-only origin/master..origin/tr1658 -- governance/lifecycle   # 0 files
$ git diff --name-only origin/master..origin/tr1660 -- governance/lifecycle   # 0 files
```

Zero paths changed under `governance/lifecycle/` in all three folds — the suite that reddens is not modified by the work being verified.

**The suite is deterministic off-venue.** Reproducing the runner's own invocation (`git show <head>:scripts/run-pytest-suites.sh`):

```
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q governance/lifecycle/tests
```

**259 passed, rc 0** in fifteen runs:

| condition | result |
|---|---|
| clean `origin/master` | 259 passed |
| the fold head | 259 passed |
| a plain clone (real `.git` DIR, 1 worktree — the venue's repo shape, not a linked worktree) | 259 passed |
| `gh` removed from PATH (this venue has no `gh`) | 259 passed |
| `vendor/CMR` empty (the venue's submodule clone fails, log lines 48–58) | 259 passed |
| ten consecutive repeats | 0 failures |
| leftover scratch/`.verify`/`.fleet` state left in the worktree | 259 passed |

## Why this cannot be diagnosed further from a PR

The composite prints only:

```
  FAIL  governance/lifecycle (pytest exit 1 — .verify/pytest-suites/governance_lifecycle.log)
```

The per-suite log lives in the ephemeral build workspace and is not echoed into the Cloud Build log. So the failing test is **unnameable from the evidence the venue publishes**, and the build workspace is destroyed. Reproducing locally is the only lever, and locally it never fails.

## Impact

- Any merge wave reds on a check no lane can fix, and the verdict is a function of the draw rather than the content.
- It is indistinguishable, from the PR, from a lane-caused red — which invites either a wrong hold or (worse) probing until a green sample appears. Neither is acceptable.
- 21 verified lanes (all 13 content-battery arms OK on the exact folded set, including `check-isolation-landed`) are currently unable to land on this account.

## Ask

Either, measured:

1. **Publish the per-suite log.** Echo the tail of `.verify/pytest-suites/<suite>.log` (or the failing test ids) into the composite output on failure, so the flake is nameable from the venue's own evidence. This is the minimum — it turns an unattributable red into an attributable one.
2. **Make the suite deterministic in the venue** (the underlying cause is not one of: `gh` absence, `vendor/CMR` absence, repo shape, leftover worktree state, or the interpreter — all reproduced and green).
3. If neither is possible quickly, the check should **degrade to CANNOT-ASSESS by name** rather than reddening the composite on a non-reproducible failure — the repo already has this vocabulary (`skip-budget.json`, the 13 standing skips), and a suite that cannot be made deterministic is a declared precondition, not a lane's defect.

## Method (so the next responder does not redo it)

- Get the build: `gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits/<head>/check-runs --jq '...select(.name|test("control-plane-verify")).details_url'` → build id in the URL.
- Read the venue's own log: `gcloud builds log <build-id> --project=purebliss-ghl --region=us-central1`.
- Attribute a fold red to a lane: derive the **exact** folded set by ancestry (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <lane-head> <train-head>`), never by text, then reproduce the failing check in a worktree at that head.
- A check counts as failed in `verify.sh` if its rc is neither 0 nor 2 — including a check that recorded no rc at all (`case "${rc:-1}" in 0)…|2)…|*) failed+=1`). So a "count" of failures can exceed the number of named non-OK verdicts.

items.title: isolation: governance/isolation/cli.py adopt --branch <b> --pr <n> — bind an existing branch/PR to a lane record
items.body:
Parent: #1510

Measured 2026-09-20 while triaging orphan-pr for check-reconcile-orphans.sh: 29 open, active PRs (updated within hours, none stale) were flagged `orphan-pr` purely because their branch has no `.fleet/lanes/*.json` record and their body carries no matching `lane: <id>` line — the match orphans.py's PR-orphan check requires (`governance/reconcile/orphans.py:153`: `LANE_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*lane:\s*([0-9a-z][0-9a-z_-]{5,63})\s*$", re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE)`; the branch/PR is exempt only if `pr.branch in lane_branches` — a record's `branch` field — or a `lane:` line names a record's `lane_id`/`session_id`).

Examples (all open, all fresh, none closeable): #1575 (issue-board-triage-20260920), #1578 (issue-pmo-priority-dispatch), #1580 (issue-purebliss-single-tenant-org), #1588 (issue-harness-audit), #1624 (issue-1620).

## The gap

The only lane-creation path, `governance/isolation/cli.py open --issue N --agent ... [--lane ...]`, always MINTS A NEW worktree+branch cut from a base commit (see its `--help`: `--root`, `--main`, `--base`, `--fetch` — every flag is about creating a fresh checkout). There is no flag to bind an ALREADY-EXISTING branch/PR to a lane record. Several harness-spawned worktrees/sessions on this box never called `session open` in the first place (they were provisioned some other way — a subagent's own worktree, a manually created branch, a train-adjacent PR), so they have no lane record and no retroactive way to get one without either:

- hand-writing a `.fleet/lanes/<id>.json` file (explicitly against doctrine — a fabricated record the tooling doesn't actually back, since no real `open`-provisioned worktree exists to match it), or
- running `session open` again, which creates a SECOND, duplicate worktree+branch instead of registering the one that already has the real work and the real PR.

## Ask

Add `governance/isolation/cli.py adopt --branch <b> --pr <n> [--issue <n>] [--agent <slug>]`: verifies the branch exists and (optionally) the PR is open and targets it, then writes a real `.fleet/lanes/<id>.json` record pointing at the EXISTING worktree (if one is found for that branch) or explicitly at "no worktree, PR/branch only" (a lane record doesn't strictly require a live worktree entry — see `governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --lane`'s handling of `worktree` fields). Dry-run by default, `--apply` to write, following this repo's usual convention.

Effect: orphan-pr goes back to measuring genuinely dead PRs (no lane, no activity) instead of catching every legitimately active PR whose lane was provisioned outside `session open`.

Filed while landing PR #1624 (#1620) and running the orphan-PR/lane cleanup pass ahead of merge train #1647.

items.title: gates: fixture-seeding checks do not neutralise an exported GIT_DIR (SP-11)
items.body:
Parent: #1510

## Model tier

L0/L1 rating: **L0** — a mechanical `unset` addition across a measured file list, plus one
pattern row (SP-11) in a gate that already has the plant/provocation machinery for it. No design
judgment; the measurement is done and is in this brief.

## Root cause

`git -C <path>` **does not override an exported `GIT_DIR`**. Git exports `GIT_DIR` to a hook when
the hook runs **in a linked worktree** (where `.git` is a file) — measured for both `pre-push` and
`pre-commit`, and it is *not* exported in the main worktree, which is why the shape hides until a
hook in a worktree runs it. Every lane in this repository is a linked worktree (golden rule 15),
so a hook — or any other caller that exports the variable — running one of these checks makes the
check write into the **real repository** instead of its throwaway fixture.

The repository already knows this. `scripts/check-ratchets.sh:677-678` states the reason and uses
the remedy:

```
# exported GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/identity would repoint or re-sign these repos.
env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE -u GIT_INDEX_FILE -u GIT_AUTHOR_NAME \
```

The knowledge is applied in **3** places and missing in **17**.

Found while re-verifying issue #1546 against `kushin77/shared-services` pull request #4210, which
measured and fixed exactly this defect class in the sibling repo (it recurred four times there).
This issue is the `agent-orchestrator` half.

## Measured (2026-09-20, at master 5357190f)

`git grep -E 'git -C'` over tracked files, `vendor/` excluded: **285** matches across 33 files,
**141** write-capable (`init`/`add`/`commit`/`checkout`/`worktree`/`push`/`branch`/`merge`/...),
134 read-only.

Every file that seeds a throwaway repository and then writes into it — the exact shape #4210
found — against whether it treats `GIT_DIR`:

| file | write-capable `git -C` | `GIT_DIR` neutralised |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` | 44 | **no** |
| `scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` | 22 | **no** (`unset GIT_AUTHOR_*` only, line 77) |
| `scripts/check-session-isolation.sh` | 18 | **no** (`unset GIT_AUTHOR_*` only, line 68) |
| `scripts/check-reconcile.sh` | 10 | **no** |
| `scripts/check-worktree-cap.sh` | 9 | **no** |
| `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` | 9 | **no** |
| `scripts/check-lifecycle-reclaim.sh` | 8 | **no** |
| `scripts/check-landing.sh` | 7 | **no** |
| `scripts/check-scratch-safety.sh` | 3 | **no** |
| `scripts/check-watchdog-bounded.sh` | 2 | **no** |
| `scripts/check-gate-publish.sh` | 1 | **no** |
| `scripts/verify.sh` | 1 | yes — `env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE`, line 918 |

Four scripts carry the **partial** defence — they unset the identity variables and nothing else,
which covers the identity half of the defect class and none of the gitdir half:

```
scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh:77    unset GIT_AUTHOR_NAME GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL GIT_COMMITTER_NAME GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL
scripts/check-session-isolation.sh:68   unset GIT_AUTHOR_NAME GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL GIT_COMMITTER_NAME GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL
scripts/check-lifecycle-closeout.sh:32  unset GIT_AUTHOR_NAME GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL GIT_COMMITTER_NAME GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL
scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh:54   unset GIT_AUTHOR_NAME GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL GIT_COMMITTER_NAME GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL
```

Reachability today is **latent, not live**: no hook is installed in this checkout's common hooks
dir (only `.sample` files), no tracked script sets `core.hooksPath`, and the gates run from
`make verify` in a plain shell where the variable is not exported. The one deliberate export in
the repo — `governance/isolation/worktree.py:539-545`, which sets `GIT_DIR` plus a scratch
`GIT_INDEX_FILE` for `git read-tree`/`git apply --cached --check` against the *same* repository —
is correct and is not part of this.

The precondition is being built: PR #1613 (issue #1541) adds `scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit` and
`make install-hooks`, which installs it into *the common hooks dir* — the Makefile's own text:
"the hook then fires for every linked worktree of this checkout". That hook's current body does
not run these gates (it reads the claim ledger), so installing it today would not breach. The gap
this issue closes is the fixture helpers' assumption that the environment they run in is the one
`make verify` gives them.

## Goal

Every check that seeds a throwaway repository writes into **that fixture**, with
`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` neutralised, whatever environment invokes it — and a gate that refuses
the shape so it cannot come back.

## Steps

1. Add `GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY GIT_COMMON_DIR GIT_PREFIX` to
   the `unset` the four scripts already have, and add an equivalent `unset` at entry to the
   scripts that have none, following `scripts/check-ratchets.sh:678`. Prefer the entry-point
   `unset` over prefixing 141 call sites: one statement per script, and it also covers the
   `git init <dir>` positional form (`check-isolation-landed.sh:180`) which `git -C`-prefixing
   would miss.
2. Add **SP-11** to `docs/SHELL-PATTERNS.md` and `scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` — a rule row
   plus its plant and its both-ways provocation, in the shape SP-1…SP-10 already use, recording
   the measured site count the way SP-10's row does. Suggested label:
   `git-dir-not-neutralised`.
3. Add a **dynamic** arm where the fixture is built, because a textual rule cannot prove
   containment: `scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` (the owner of `seed_repo`) runs its own
   `seed_repo` against a throwaway directory with `GIT_DIR` exported and asserts the fixture took
   the repository — i.e. the gate proves its own containment rather than assuming it.
4. Reproduce first, so the fix is measured and not asserted: the current `seed_repo` bytes,
   extracted byte-for-byte (`scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh:178-188`, sha256
   `31ac7fcfd58b39d63f514bf1df95e453e886177c4a118a4b20605a195cf8eec0`), run against a throwaway
   victim repository with `GIT_DIR="$VICTIM/.git"`.

## Measured reproduction (the arm the fix must flip)

```
victim BEFORE HEAD=c38b7b7a96c4  tracked=[real.txt]
seed_repo output: 4cf9aed5822e1de1d792ac5939ebc63c8db858b8
victim AFTER  HEAD=4cf9aed5822e1de1d792ac5939ebc63c8db858b8
fixture got its own .git? NO        <-- the fixture never became a repository
VICTIM COMMITS: 2  (was 1)
VICTIM TRACKED: [real.txt seed.txt]
BREACH = YES
```

The same bytes with `GIT_DIR` unset first: the fixture gets its own `.git`, the victim's HEAD does
not move, `BREACH = NO`. `seed_repo` returns the SHA of the commit it made in the victim, so its
caller cannot notice — which is why this needs a gate rather than a careful reader.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `git grep -E 'git -C'` over tracked files yields **0** write-capable sites in a script that
      neither neutralises `GIT_DIR` at entry nor is on a declared, reasoned exception list.
- [ ] No tracked `docs/*.md` is left unindexed by the new pattern row (the docs gate covers this).
- [ ] Negative control: with the `unset` line removed from a copy of `check-isolation-landed.sh`,
      SP-11 fails naming that file — and the mutant is asserted to differ from the original by
      sha256, so a mutation that never landed cannot be reported as a passing control.
- [ ] Dynamic arm: the fixture under an exported `GIT_DIR` provably never writes to the victim.
- [ ] `make verify` green.
- [ ] clock (#506, RCA-0008) — does this work introduce a time-pinned assertion? No: the fixture
      arms compare repository state, not wall-clock time.

## Verify command

```bash
bash scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh && bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh
```

Before the fix, SP-11's repository run refuses the sites above **by name**; after it, both are
green. Both are existing gates — this issue adds no new entry point to `make verify`.

## Escalation

Attempt at L0. Tiers: L0 = Claude Haiku / DeepSeek V4 Flash -> L1 = Claude Sonnet / DeepSeek V4 Pro
-> L2 = Claude Opus.
- Max attempts: **N = 3**.
- If blocked after 3 attempts, comment on this issue with the exact failure and label
  `escalate:L1`, then stop. Never silent abandonment.

## Lane

- Branch: `issue-<n of this issue>` cut from `origin/master` in a lane worktree.
- Files this lane owns: the fixture-seeding gates named in the table above, plus
  `docs/SHELL-PATTERNS.md`, `scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` and — for the index row — the
  `docs/README.md` line it needs.
- `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` carries 44 of the sites and is also the PR-contract gate: change
  its `unset` line only, and do not touch its predicates.

## Lifecycle contract (no lingering)

- Closed ONLY via a merged PR whose body contains `Closes #<n>` and the acceptance command output
  pasted, plus the negative-control output.
- Picking this issue up = owning it to closure. Do not stop at a partial state.
- Before the PR: `make verify` green on the branch; no orphan worktrees, no stale branches, no
  leftover temp files.
- After merge: delete the branch, remove the worktree, confirm the issue auto-closed, post the
  final comment with the merged PR link and the evidence summary.

## No vaporware

DONE = the reproduction above **flipped** (fixture contained, victim unchanged) with the actual
command and its real output pasted in the PR, and SP-11 refusing the unfixed shape by name in the
negative control. Not a description of the fix.

## Non-negotiables

Secret scan clean, no direct push to `master`, no ad-hoc `terraform apply` (GR-5), no secrets in
git (GR-6), `vendor/` pinned submodules never edited directly, close citing the evidence.

items.title: indexer: classify + seed the 102 uncataloged catalog/modules entries — the stub cannot be mechanical (blocks #1529)
items.milestone: M24 - Enterprise Knowledge Index & Policy Normalization
items.body:
Parent: #1510
Blocks: #1529

## Why this exists

#1529 asked for a **mechanical (L0) stub pass**: "for each repo in the gap set, generate a minimal stub
`module.json`", with real classification deferred to a follow-up L1 issue. Measured against the target's own
validator, that split does not exist — **the stub *is* the classification**. Lane `issue-1529` was cut,
measured, and released unmerged; this issue carries the blocker and the corrected shape.

## The measurement (reproducible, all read-only)

`vendor/CMR/catalog/validate.py` (what `make catalog-validate` runs, and the hub's own `verify` depends on),
run in a full scratch copy of the hub tree — never in the submodule:

```
0. BASELINE  untouched catalog                          rc=0   11 module(s) checked, 0 failed
1. POSITIVE  {schema,id,name,type,source,governance}    rc=0   OK   zz-ok (repo check skipped)
2. NEGATIVE  #1529's literal stub                       rc=1
   FAIL zz-lit: schema: 'schema' is a required property (at /)
3. NEGATIVE  a real uppercase repo name as the id       rc=1
   FAIL ERP-CRM: schema: 'ERP-CRM' does not match '^[a-z0-9-]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)*$' (at id)
4. NEGATIVE  id != directory name                       rc=1
   FAIL zz-dir: id 'different-id' != directory name 'zz-dir'
5. NEGATIVE  shared_integrations                        rc=1
   FAIL shared_integrations: schema: 'shared_integrations' does not match '^[a-z0-9-]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)*$' (at id)
6. NEGATIVE  'role' where 'type' belongs                rc=1
7. NEGATIVE  type: "unclassified"                       rc=1
   FAIL zz-badtype: schema: 'unclassified' is not one of ['app','service','frontend','backend','middleware',
        'integration','feature','infra','workflow','template','governance'] (at type)
8. RESTORED  rc=0   12 module(s) checked, 0 failed   (11 at the pin + the passing positive control)
```

`catalog/schemas/module.schema.json` requires `["schema","id","name","type","source","governance"]`;
`type` is a **closed enum with no neutral or `unclassified` member**; `validate.py` additionally enforces
`id == directory name`, and `id` must be lowercase `[a-z0-9-]` (plus `.`-separated segments).

## Why no stub can be honest at L0

`type` is the only required field with no measured source — and there is no measured source for it:

| source | measured |
|---|---|
| `catalog/repos/repo-inventory.json` (CMR-110, hub's own per-repo inventory) rows with `module_id` | **0 of 106** |
| … rows with `module_type` | **0 of 106** |
| … rows with `custom_properties_available` | **0 of 106** |

So any stub's `type` (and its `governance` block) would be an **assertion**, not a measurement — and 19 of the
102 gap names cannot even be ids as-is (uppercase), one of them (`Shared_Integrations`) irreparably (the id
pattern admits no `_`).

## Inventory, corrected (measured 2026-09-20T20:56Z)

| | #1529 says | measured |
|---|---|---|
| repos in the account | 113 | **114** |
| cataloged | 11 | 11 at the stale pin `b6c49aa`; **12 on hub `main`** (adds `agent-orchestrator`, `pmo`, `monitoring-stack`, `twilio`) |
| gap | 99 | **102** |
| archived repos | "at least one" (the negative control) | **0** |

The cited authority `docs/INDEXER-REVIEW-2026-09-20.md` does not exist in this repo.

## Deliverable

1. **The hub-side registration** (the hub writes it — `CMR#635`: "the repo files a catalog-request on the CMR
   board; CMR registers `catalog/modules/<id>/module.json` (metadata only, NG4)"). The catalog-request is
   filed; CMR owns the entries.
2. **The classification pass that produces them** — L1, per repo, per `docs/SOLUTION-CLASSES.md`: choose `type`
   from the closed enum, a `class[]`, a `governance` block, and a schema-valid id (lowercased; `Shared_Integrations`
   and `CMR` itself need an explicit decision). The id must equal its directory name, so the id decision precedes
   the file.
3. **A corrected acceptance for the parent issue** — the missing-count must be measured by each entry's
   `source.repo`, not by a case-sensitive diff of directory names against repo names (today's diff reads 104 and
   can never reach 0: `erp-crm` ≠ `ERP-CRM`), and the archived-repo control needs a repo that is actually
   archived (there are none).

## Acceptance

- Every entry registered on the hub passes `python3 catalog/validate.py` (rc 0) with the catalog's own baseline
  also rc 0 — a positive control and one named refusal per row shape are pasted as evidence.
- The missing-count is reported by `source.repo` mapping, and reads 0 for the intended scope, with the scope
  stated (which repos are deliberately out: the hub itself, and any repo whose owner declines an entry).
- No entry is registered with an asserted `type`: each is either classified in this pass or explicitly parked
  with the reason.

## Verify

```bash
# hub clone; never the pinned submodule
python3 catalog/validate.py && echo CATALOG-OK
```

## Lane

- Branch: `issue-<this>` from `origin/master`
- Touches only this repo's docs/board artifacts plus the filed catalog-request; the `catalog/modules/**` entries
  themselves are the hub's to write (NG4).

items.title: boundary gate fails open on a rotted snapshot: the #132/#133 vendor-compliance quarantine is tracked by the closed #358 — successor tracker
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
Parent: #1510

## What

`governance/board/boundary-baseline.json` (the cross-repo boundary quarantine, issue #388) names its tracker as **`#358`** for all 22 entries excusing the 11 vendor-compliance children of the closed epic #125:

```
"tracked_by": "#358"
"reason": "Legacy CMR vendor-compliance child of #125; …"
```

The baseline's own contract (`docs/CROSS-REPO-EXECUTION-BOUNDARY.md` §5.2) requires each excused item to be *"explicitly quarantined by name with the issue that tracks it"*. **`#358` closed 2026-09-14T17:47:45Z**, so that requirement is no longer met.

## The measured defect (this issue *is* its own tracker)

`scripts/check-cross-repo-boundary.sh` resolves tracker liveness from the **committed** `.board/boundary-snapshot.json`, whose `generated_at` is **2026-09-14T03:35:16Z** — 14 hours *before* `#358` closed. It therefore still reads `#358 state=OPEN` and reports:

```
boundary: OK — 225 issue(s), 22 quarantined legacy finding(s), no boundary violation
```

Patching only that one entry to its **live** state and re-running the gate:

```
boundary: NOT-OK — #133 excused for foreign-repo-declaration but its tracking issue #358 is closed; retire the quarantine entry
…
boundary: NOT-OK — 22 finding(s)/stale quarantine(s) across 225 issue(s)    [rc=1]
```

So the gate is green on an input whose live truth is red: it **fails open on a rotted snapshot**. The gate's own negative control (c) does provoke this shape and passes — the control mutates the snapshot's `#358` to `closed` and expects rc 1 — so the check is capable of failing; what it cannot see is that its real input has gone stale.

## Secondary, same file

The quarantine never shrank. 9 of the 11 excused children (**#126–#129, #131, #134–#137**) closed 2026-09-14, so 18 of the 22 entries excuse nothing (a closed issue is not a finding) yet are still counted as `22 quarantined legacy finding(s)`. §5.2 says *"quarantine shrinks as the tracked items close, and the shrink is observable because it is recorded"* — the shrink was never recorded. Retired in the PR that declares this issue as the tracker.

## Scope

- Re-anchor `tracked_by` for the **two live** children (#132, #133) to this issue.
- Retire the 18 inert entries.
- The snapshot staleness itself is the *root* cause and is **not** fixed by this issue: refreshing the committed boundary snapshot is a board-artifact refresh and must not ride in a feature lane (`governance/board/cli.py export-boundary` is the verb).

## Verify

```
bash scripts/check-cross-repo-boundary.sh                 # rc 0, and the stale-tracker control still rc 1
bash scripts/check-cross-repo-boundary.sh                 # with the snapshot's #358 → closed: rc 1
```

## Model tier

L0/L1 rating: **L0** — backfilled default; re-assess when picked up.

## Root cause

RCA required — Step 1: determine why this issue predates the lifecycle-contract convention (created before the #1533 templates landed) and whether the root cause is otherwise already known from the original body below.

## Escalation

Attempt at L0. Tiers: L0 = Claude Haiku / DeepSeek V4 Flash -> L1 = Claude Sonnet / DeepSeek V4 Pro -> L2 = Claude Opus.
- Max attempts: **N = 3**.
- If blocked after 3 attempts, comment on this issue with the exact failure and label `escalate:L1`, then stop. Never silent abandonment.

## Lifecycle contract (no lingering)

- This issue is closed ONLY via a merged PR whose body contains `Closes #<n>` and evidence: the acceptance command output pasted, plus the negative-control output.
- Picking this issue up = owning it to closure. Do not stop at a partial state or move to another issue. Blockers are part of the task: unblock them (file the blocker as a child issue with `Parent: #1510` if it is a separate lane, fix it, then continue).
- Before the PR is opened: `make verify` green on the branch; no orphan worktrees, no stale branches, no leftover temp files.
- After merge: delete the branch, remove the worktree, confirm the issue auto-closed, post a final comment with the merged PR link and the evidence summary.
- Escalation is the only sanctioned way to hand off; it is a comment + label on THIS issue, never silent abandonment.

## What is ready

`governance/dispatch/peers.py` + `scripts/peer-check.sh` land the A2A peer-check
standard (issue #1549, PR #1623): it replays the live claim ledger, intersects
each sibling lane's files with the caller's through
`governance/dispatch/model.py::file_claims_conflict` (imported, never
re-implemented), and **refuses by name** on overlap —
`scripts/check-peer-check.sh` gates it with 14 arms, including a real provoked
overlap and a mutant that must move the verdict.

What is **not** wired is where it is *called from*. The tool works and nothing
invokes it yet, so today it is a thing a lane has to remember to run. That is the
gap this issue closes, and it is the whole of the gap: issue #1549's own
Acceptance named four cadence points, and all four sit in files a live lane owns
or outside this repository entirely.

## The four cadence points, each named with why it is not in PR #1623

| # | cadence point | what has to change | why it is not in #1623 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | before every claim | `governance/dispatch/cli.py` — `cmd_claim` runs the peer-check before it writes | `cli.py` is owned by PR #1605 (issue #1524, the tiered dispatcher), in flight |
| 2 | the fleet loop's cadence | whatever #1512's ADR decides owns `.fleet`'s loop family | #1512 (PR #1595) has not landed; pre-empting its ownership decision would duplicate that issue's scope |
| 3 | pre-dispatch | `governance/dispatch/tiered.py` — abort a dispatch whose target files overlap a live sibling | PR #1605's lane |
| 4 | session start + SME card rules | `~/.claude/settings.json` session hooks; `## Rules` in `~/.copilot/agents/*.md` | both live **outside this repository**; a lane may not edit shared operator config unilaterally |

## Acceptance

- `governance/dispatch/cli.py claim` runs the peer-check before it records, and a
  claim whose files `OVERLAP` a live sibling is refused **by name** — the refusal
  text from `peers.PeerReport.refusal()`, naming the sibling, its issue, its lane,
  its channel and the specific path — surfaced alongside the existing claim
  reasons rather than replacing them.

- Picking this issue up = owning it to closure. Do not stop at a partial state or move to another issue. Blockers are part of the task: unblock them (file the blocker as a child issue with `Parent: #1510` if it is a separate lane, fix it, then continue).

- After merge: delete the branch, remove the worktree, confirm the issue auto-closed, post a final comment with the merged PR link and the evidence summary.
- Escalation is the only sanctioned way to hand off; it is a comment + label on THIS issue, never silent abandonment.

Cross-ref: #1572 (same class)

Measured 2026-09-20 while landing PR #1581 on a box running ~50 concurrent agent sessions against the same main checkout (/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator):

## check-reconcile: _branch_age_seconds fail-closes on a git ref-write race

governance/reconcile/real_tree_baseline.py:470 `_branch_age_seconds()` runs `git log -1 --format=%ct <branch>` per unmatched branch. When that subprocess call races a concurrent ref-write from another session (e.g. another lane's `git branch -D`), it can return empty/nonzero. The caller fail-closes that as age=None -> treated as old -> reported `NEW` (governance/reconcile/real_tree_baseline.py:945-946: "not baselined and its age could not be measured (fail-closed: treated as old)").

Observed: one `check-reconcile.sh` run reported 95 new-and-old branches (e.g. issue-1003, and 94 others); a fresh re-run seconds later reported only 3, with **zero name overlap** with the first run's 95. That's only explainable as per-run flakiness from racing concurrent git writes, not a real state change — nothing was landed or reaped between the two runs that would explain 92 branches becoming matched again.

## check-worktree-cap / check-reconcile-orphans: count other sessions' trees

Both gates count worktrees / orphan branches-lanes-directives against the WHOLE box's `~/ao-worktrees` + `.claude/worktrees` + `.fleet/lanes`, not anything scoped to the PR/session running the gate. With ~50 concurrent sessions, the count moves under the gate mid-run (measured swinging worktree-cap between 58/65 and 82/65 minutes apart with no action taken by the session reporting it), so a single PR's `make verify` can go red or green purely on unrelated fleet timing.

## Impact

All three gates measure shared BOX state, not the PR's own diff, so a correct, unrelated PR can fail `make verify` (or pass it) purely due to a timing accident on a busy box, and `make verify` retries cannot converge on "clean" during high fleet load — confirmed while landing #1581 (2-line .mcp.json fix, unrelated to any of these three).

## Fix proposal

1. `_branch_age_seconds` (and any other subprocess-based per-artifact read in the real-tree walk): retry `git log`/similar ≤3x with backoff before fail-closing to NEW, so a single lost race doesn't misclassify an artifact.
2. Reclassify these three checks: advisory (reported, non-blocking) in per-lane venue runs of `make verify`; blocking only in the master post-merge attestation run, which runs serially / off-peak and isn't racing 50 other sessions' git writes.

Evidence: PR #1581's evidence comment (this run) links here.

items.title: ADR: no promotion state in the vocabulary — 'accepted' cannot be distinguished from 'live'
items.body:
Parent: #1510

## Escalation

Attempt at L0. Tiers: L0 = Claude Haiku / DeepSeek V4 Flash -> L1 = Claude Sonnet / DeepSeek V4 Pro -> L2 = Claude Opus.
- Max attempts: **N = 3**.
- If blocked after 3 attempts, comment on this issue with the exact failure and label `escalate:L1`, then stop. Never silent abandonment.

## Lifecycle contract (no lingering)

- This issue is closed ONLY via a merged PR whose body contains `Closes #<n>` and evidence: the acceptance command output pasted, plus the negative-control output.
- Picking this issue up = owning it to closure. Do not stop at a partial state or move to another issue. Blockers are part of the task: unblock them (file the blocker as a child issue with `Parent: #1510` if it is a separate lane, fix it, then continue).
- Before the PR is opened: `make verify` green on the branch; no orphan worktrees, no stale branches, no leftover temp files.
- After merge: delete the branch, remove the worktree, confirm the issue auto-closed, post a final comment with the merged PR link and the evidence summary.
- Escalation is the only sanctioned way to hand off; it is a comment + label on THIS issue, never silent abandonment.

## Model tier

L0/L1: the vocabulary change is mechanical, but deciding the closed state set and migrating 27 ADRs is a judgment call.

## Root cause

**Mechanism:** an ADR's metadata cannot distinguish "we decided" from "the decision is live", so "ADR accepted with nothing built" is **undecidable from the ADR itself**. Measured on `5357190f` (2026-09-20):

```
ls docs/decision-records/ADR-*.md | wc -l                                  # => 27
grep -l '^status: accepted' docs/decision-records/ADR-*.md | wc -l         # => 18
grep -l 'superseded_by:' docs/decision-records/ADR-*.md | wc -l            # => 0
for f in docs/decision-records/ADR-*.md; do grep -q '^status:' "$f" || echo "$f"; done
# => 9 files: ADR-0002..ADR-0009, ADR-0028 (no status key at all)
```

So the sweep's step-5 instrument — `grep -L "Superseded\|Status: Live" docs/decision-records/ADR-*.md` — returns **every** ADR: 0 true positives, 27 false positives. It is a false-positive instrument, not a finding instrument, because the repo's vocabulary is YAML `status: accepted` and nothing else. There is no `live` / `implemented` / `superseded` state in use, `superseded_by:` is declared in the front-matter template but populated in zero ADRs, and 9 of 27 ADRs carry no `status:` key at all.

## Why this matters

`ADR-0013` (paperclip) declares `status: accepted` and its subject is a terraform module count-gated OFF (`enable_paperclip`, `infra/terraform/variables.tf:82-86`). `ADR-0023` (conversational surface) declares `accepted` and its subject (`surfaces.chat`) ships OFF. Both are *correctly* off — but "accepted" reads identically for an ADR whose subject is live and one whose subject has never been promoted, so the metadata cannot be used to find either. That is exactly the debt class #1540 exists to inventory.

## Goal

A closed ADR state vocabulary that separates *decided* from *live*, applied to all 27 ADRs, with a gate that fails by name when an ADR's state is absent from the vocabulary or when a `live` ADR's subject has no corresponding resource.

## Steps

1. Extend the front-matter vocabulary (`status:` today is only `accepted`) with the states the process actually needs — at minimum `accepted` (decided, not promoted) and `live` (its subject is deployed), plus `superseded` paired with a populated `superseded_by:`.
2. Backfill all 27 ADRs, including the 9 with no `status:` key, and decide per ADR whether its subject is live (e.g. ADR-0017 diagrams authoring, ADR-0028 gate status) or still unpromoted.
3. Add `scripts/check-adr-status.sh` (auto-discovered by `scripts/discover-checks.sh`, so it is wired the moment it lands) asserting: every ADR carries a state from the closed set, `superseded` implies a populated `superseded_by:` naming an existing ADR, and a `live` ADR names the resource/service that makes it live. `--self-test` must prove both directions.
4. Record the disposition in `docs/BUILT-NOT-SHIPPED-AO.md`.

## Acceptance

- `grep -L '^status:' docs/decision-records/ADR-*.md` returns nothing.
- The state vocabulary is declared in one place and the gate refuses a state outside it by name.
- The new gate's `--self-test` provokes a missing state, an out-of-vocabulary state, and a `superseded_by:` that names a non-existent ADR.
- `make verify` green.

## Lane

- Branch: `issue-<n>` cut from `origin/master`. Touches `docs/decision-records/ADR-*.md` front-matter, `scripts/check-adr-status.sh`, and the doc's row. **Note:** 27 ADRs is a broad write surface — if a lane holds `docs/decision-records/`, coordinate before claiming.

## Non-negotiables

No secrets (GR-6), no direct push to `master`, `vendor/` never edited, close via PR only (`Closes #<n>`), assignee kushin77.

items.body:

- Picking this issue up = owning it to closure. Do not stop at a partial state or move to another issue. Blockers are part of the task: unblock them (file the blocker as a child issue with `Parent: #1510` if it is a separate lane, fix it, then continue).

- After merge: delete the branch, remove the worktree, confirm the issue auto-closed, post a final comment with the merged PR link and the evidence summary.
- Escalation is the only sanctioned way to hand off; it is a comment + label on THIS issue, never silent abandonment.

## Model tier

L0 (mechanical): add a field to a declarative file and a gate arm that fails when it is absent.

## Root cause

**Mechanism:** a *declared-but-unpromoted* surface is invisible debt because nothing records **who owes its promotion**. Measured on `5357190f` (2026-09-20):

```
grep -cE 'owner:|promotion_issue:|target_date:|due_by:' infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml
# => 0
grep -cE 'owner:|promotion_issue:' infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml
# => 0
```

Both files are the platform's own promotion ledger — `registry.yaml` is the read-only flag registry ("every control-plane surface ships OFF until a reviewed go-live promotes it") and `rollout-state.yaml` is its mirror of *current* promotion state. Between them they declare **38 entries defaulting `off`** and not one carries an owner, a promotion issue, or a target date. So the two questions the sweep in #1540 could not answer from the declarations themselves are:

1. which declared-off surface is *pending a reviewed go-live* (legitimate, DO-NOT-TOUCH), and
2. which is *drifting with nobody responsible* (debt)?

They are indistinguishable from the declarations, and the answer only exists in prose inside the entries' `description:` blocks or on the board. That is the gap #1540's own root-cause section predicted: "no gate checks 'every `enable_*` flag has an owner and a target promotion date'".

## Evidence

- `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml` — `services:` (21 entries) + `surfaces:` (17 entries); every one `default: off`; fields present are `default`/`promoted`/`phase`/`tf_flag`/`service`/`description` and nothing else.
- `infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml` — every flag `stage: "off"`, `rollout_pct: 0`, `targeted: []`; no owner field.
- The gap is *load-bearing*, not cosmetic: #1525's `.mcp.json` fix merged into a train while its own PR (#1581) closed unmerged, and #1520/#1512/#1513/#1515 landed via train #1604 while their PRs closed unmerged — the board's PR state alone cannot tell you whether a surface is shipped. An owner field on the declaration would be a signal that does not depend on reading PR state.

## Goal

Every entry in `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml` (and its `rollout-state.yaml` mirror) carries a non-empty `promotion_issue:` naming the issue that owns its promotion, or an explicit `posture: hold` naming why it has none — and a gate fails by name when an entry carries neither.

## Steps

1. Add `promotion_issue:` to every `services:` / `surfaces:` entry; use the owning issues this sweep already resolved where they exist (#1518, #1519, #1521, #1522, #1523, EPIC #706).
2. Add the same field to `infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml` for each mirrored flag, and keep the two in lock-step the way `scripts/check-feature-flags.py` already keeps `default` in lock-step with `infra/terraform/variables.tf`.
3. Extend `scripts/check-feature-flags.py` (or add `scripts/check-promotion-owners.sh`) so an entry with neither `promotion_issue:` nor `posture: hold` fails by name, with `--self-test` proving both directions (a missing owner is refused; a present owner passes) so the new arm cannot pass vacuously.
4. Record the disposition in `docs/BUILT-NOT-SHIPPED-AO.md`.

## Acceptance

- `grep -cE 'owner:|promotion_issue:' infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml` is non-zero and every `default: off` entry is covered.
- The new gate returns rc 1 naming a specific entry when an owner is removed, and rc 0 when restored (both halves provoked).
- `make verify` green.

## Lane

- Branch: `issue-<n>` cut from `origin/master`. Touches `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml`, `infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml`, one `scripts/check-*.sh` (or `check-feature-flags.py`), and the doc's row.

## Non-negotiables

No secrets (GR-6), no direct push to `master`, no ad-hoc `terraform apply` (GR-5), `vendor/` never edited, close via PR only (`Closes #<n>`), assignee kushin77.

## Original

## The blocker, measured

`check-isolation-landed` refuses a lane whose commits do not carry the ticket reference in a
**trailing trailer block**, and the remedy it names — *re-push the lane* — is **another lane's
branch**. So the finding is real, correctly refused, and **unactionable by whoever measured it**.

Found while composing the second merge train (PR #1597, landed as `0002a852`, parent `156e1940`).
Five of the then-open settled PRs could not be folded for this reason, each measured with the same
command:

```
python3 governance/isolation/cli.py landed --check --range origin/master..<pr-head>
```
(or the equivalent `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --landed --range origin/master..<head>`)

| PR | branch | finding |
|---|---|---|
| #1575 | `issue-board-triage-20260920` | `LANDED: FAIL (1)` — `commit-missing-ticket-trailer:49109da1e71b` |
| #1578 | `issue-pmo-priority-dispatch` | `LANDED: FAIL (11)` — 11 named commits without a trailing ticket trailer |
| #1580 | `issue-purebliss-single-tenant-org` | `LANDED: FAIL (2)` — `6144fa304201`, `b31347ab63b1` |
| #1583 | `issue-cfo-office-finops` | `LANDED: FAIL (1)` — `c6d0da93eb4b` |
| #1588 | `issue-harness-audit` | `LANDED: FAIL (2)` — `1647e6071f16`, `30e24596994f` |

Three of them also carry an independent, unrelated red (`check-docs`: a tracked doc not indexed in
`docs/README.md`: `docs/cto/HARVEST.md`, `docs/tenancy/PUREBLISS-ORG.md`), and #1580/#1588 conflict
with each other / with `docs/README.md` — so this issue is **only** about the trailer half.

Not folded, therefore not landed, therefore their linked issues stay open. This is 5 lanes' worth of
work held by one mechanical predicate.

## Why this needs an owner rather than a workaround

The predicate is `check-isolation-landed`, wired into `make verify`, and it exists for a good reason
(AGENTS.md rule 15 / #263: *every commit a session authors carries `Refs
kushin77/agent-orchestrator#<n>`*, so the generated history points back at the ticket that ordered
it). It should **not** be weakened.

The gap is the remediation path. Two honest options, and someone has to pick:

1. **A sanctioned re-push** — the fix is in each lane's *branch*, which means the lane owner (or an
   authorised operator) must re-push with the trailer. A fold cannot repair a lane's own commits,
   and `--amend`/force-push is forbidden on these branches, so this means new commits that carry the
   trailer, not a rewrite.
2. **A declared exemption** — if a commit predates the rule, an explicit, reviewed, shrinking
   baseline (the pattern `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` already uses) is the honest way
   to say "grandfathered", rather than an editor silently dropping the check for the fold.

Both are governance decisions, so this is filed rather than improvised.

## What was NOT done (deliberately)

- No lane branch was touched: the fold happens only on the train branch, and editing another lane's
  branch is exactly the clobbering AGENTS.md forbids.
- `check-isolation-landed` was **not** weakened, skipped, or baselined by the train.
- The three `check-docs` reds are a separate finding and are **not** addressed here.

## Evidence

Train PR #1597 (`train/20260920T182909Z-clean`), landed `0002a852`; the fold-pre-filter measurements
are recorded in `train2-fold-20260920` in repo memory, and the venue's own verdict for the landed
fold is build `d4bf1991-b2e7-4d95-b49d-662e8e8e781c` — `verify: PASS (212 of 225 checks, 13
skipped)`.

## Classification

class: enterprise
posture: human-gated
lifecycle: operate
lane: isolation
pattern: none

```
#1578  11 commits untrailered
#1588   2
#1580   2
#1583   1
#1575   1
------
       17 commits, 5 PRs
```

`scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` defines the predicate exactly:

```bash
trailer_pattern="Refs:?\s+[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+#[0-9]+"
```

i.e. the **qualified** form `Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#<n>`. Every one of those 17 commits
writes the **bare** form `Refs #<n>` instead. `check-isolation-landed.sh` then refuses each by name:

```
FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:cda38cb574ac is not recorded legacy — if the commit has not
      MERGED yet, put the reference in a trailing trailer paragraph and re-push; …
```

and the venue of record reproduces it: #1578's run ended `check-isolation-landed (6 unrecorded)`,
#1575's `(1 unrecorded)`, #1580's `(2)`.

## Why lanes keep producing it — the asymmetry

Two guards read the *same* conceptual thing and accept **different spellings**:

| guard | what it reads | bare `Closes #<n>` | bare `Refs #<n>` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scripts/check-squash-message.sh` (the merge gate) | the PR body's trailing trailer block | **accepted** by name | — |
| `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` → `check-isolation-landed.sh` (the commit gate) | each commit message | — | **refused** |

`check-squash-message.sh` was deliberately made to accept the colon-less `Closes #<n>` form, because
`gh pr merge --squash` composes exactly that shape (measured: 8 of the 12
`commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block` entries in the landed baseline). A lane that satisfies the
merge gate with a bare keyword reasonably concludes the bare form is the house style — and then
writes `Refs #<n>` in its commits, which the *commit* gate refuses. The rule is not stated in the
place the lane actually writes commit messages.

## The ask

1. **State the qualified form where the message is written.** The commit-message guidance lanes
   receive (`governance/spawn/render.py` is the one copy every spawned lane gets) should spell
   `Refs <owner>/<repo>#<n>` literally, next to the `Closes #<n>` line it also needs — or the
   predicate should accept the bare form too, if the bare form is intended. One of the two, decided
   in one place, rather than a merge-gate acceptance that implies the opposite of the commit gate.
2. **A pre-push check, not a post-push reword.** Today this class is discovered by the *venue*, after
   a push, when the only remedy is a message reword plus a force-push on the lane branch. A
   pre-commit/pre-push hook (cf. the file-lease hook work in #1541) refusing a bare `Refs #<n>` would
   catch it before it reaches the queue — and the venue queue is 12 deep at ~24 min per run.
3. **Reword the outstanding 17 commits** (5 PRs: #1578 #1588 #1580 #1583 #1575). This is the half
   that needs the owners, because a message reword rewrites history and must be a force-push on the
   lane branch. Note #1583's *other* defect is already fixed and green
   (`check-docs.sh` rc 0 at `54eede52`); the trailer half is all that remains there.

## Why this is worth a lane rather than a note

It is the single largest blocker class on the board: 5 of ~19 open PRs, i.e. **~26% of the open PR
set is unlandable for a one-line message-shape reason**, and each fix is a reword that no automated
path in the repo performs. It is also the reason the first merge train of the evening could not be
folded (46 untrailered commits in the fold), which cost a rebuild.

## Evidence

- `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` — `trailer_pattern`, and the `commit-missing-ticket-trailer` finding.
- `scripts/check-squash-message.sh` — the accepted bare `Closes #<n>` shape and its rationale.
- `scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` — the refusal text quoted above.
- The 5 PRs' own venue runs, which red on `check-isolation-landed` (builds `64df6ade` #1578,
  `091073ec` #1575, `955d5b4c` #1580).
- Reproduced locally on a clean fold of `{1589 1588 1578 1575}` on `2509de80`: the control is that the
  same checks are **OK on clean `origin/master`**.

Refs #1542
Refs #1541

items.title: indexer: bump the vendor/CMR pin to pick up the corrected .mcp.json seed
items.body:
Parent: #1510 · Follow-on to #1525 · Blocked on kushin77/CMR#1019

## Why this exists

`#1525` fixed **this repo's own** `.mcp.json`: the `cmr-indexer` entry now names
`vendor/CMR/catalog/indexer/mcp_server.py`, which resolves from the repo root the
MCP host launches it in. The file it was copied from —
`vendor/CMR/templates/module/.mcp.json` — carries the same defect, and it lives in
the **pinned `vendor/CMR` submodule**, which is never edited from a consuming repo.

The seed-side fix is `kushin77/CMR#1019` (one line, executing the direction in
`kushin77/CMR#1010`, which was filed from here on 2026-09-14 and had no decision
until `#1525` supplied one). This issue is the follow-on that makes the corrected
seed actually reach this repo.

## Blocked on

`kushin77/CMR#1019` merging into `kushin77/CMR`'s `main`. Until then the pinned
commit `b6c49aa03992dba9fe4b87b46104b8fc2f69f224` still declares the
CMR-root-relative path, so every seeding path that reads the submodule
(`vendor/CMR/templates/module/.mcp.json`) would still emit a declaration that
cannot resolve in a consumer.

Not a defect this lane can close by editing: the pin can only be moved to a hub
commit that exists.

## What "done" looks like

- `vendor/CMR` checked out at the hub commit carrying the corrected seed;
- the gitlink committed, honouring `.gitmodules`' own instruction to record the
  new `git describe --tags` output in the same commit;
- `make verify` green on the branch (the bump is its own lane precisely because it
  moves hub history into this repo, so it needs its own gate run);
- `bash scripts/check-codeidx-surface.sh` still rc 0 — the shape check reads only
  the seed's server name and entry `type`, and the liveness step exercises
  **this repo's** `.mcp.json`, so neither should change.

## Evidence that this is a real gap (not hypothetical)

At the pin, the seed declares `"args": ["catalog/indexer/mcp_server.py"]`, and
this repo has no `catalog/` directory. Measured against the vendored copy in
`#1525`:

```
$ printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}' \
    | python3 catalog/indexer/mcp_server.py
python3: can't open file '.../catalog/indexer/mcp_server.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```
