- agent-orchestrator#1515 — go/no-go decision on enable_paperclip promotion
- agent-orchestrator#1516 — real prompt-intake hook in .claude/settings.json (or documented non-routing)
- agent-orchestrator#1518 — fix or retire dead gateway/providers/hermes.py endpoint + real enable_hermes gate
- agent-orchestrator#1519 — canary-enable hermes-head-guardrails, prove one BLOCK fires

### F — Console coverage
- agent-orchestrator#1520 — add FinOps + Ops/SLO views
- agent-orchestrator#1521 — add Org Chart + Skill Studio views
- agent-orchestrator#1522 — add Task Board + fleet board views
- agent-orchestrator#1523 — resolve /api/v1/bridge consumer + wire full operator verb catalogue

### X — Tiered dispatcher
- agent-orchestrator#1524 — implement the tiered try-loop dispatcher (L0->L1->L2 escalation)

### H — Indexer (cmr-indexer is the lifeblood: front_load() context for every agent)
- agent-orchestrator#1525 — fix .mcp.json relative path for cmr-indexer (all seeds)
- agent-orchestrator#1526 — add liveness check to check-codeidx-surface.sh
- agent-orchestrator#1527 — fix context_pack.py graph path mismatch
- agent-orchestrator#1528 — run and commit a fresh --apply index
- agent-orchestrator#1529 — seed module.json stubs for the 99 uncataloged repos
- agent-orchestrator#1530 — onboard checkouts for the 13 catalog-known-but-never-indexed repos
- agent-orchestrator#1531 — classify RCA/incident docs in the asset classifier
- agent-orchestrator#1532 — wire front_load() MCP tool and register with agents

Headline indexer facts: 1 of 113 repos indexed (kushin77/CMR itself, its own
docs only), 88% of repos (99/113) unreferenced by the indexer at all, last
graph generated 2026-09-13 (stale), `.mcp.json` points at
`catalog/indexer/mcp_server.py` when the file lives at
`vendor/CMR/catalog/indexer/mcp_server.py` (identical bug in every worktree
seed), `context_pack.py` reads `catalog/indexer/out/graph.json` while
`index.py` writes `catalog/indexer/index-graph.json` (path mismatch, never
run), zero consumers (no hook/skill/agent reads indexer output today),
liveness was never gated (`check-codeidx-surface.sh` checks shape, not that
the server responds). Group H is ordered so the path fix (H1/#1525) +
liveness gate (H2/#1526) + a fresh `--apply` index (H4/#1528) land first,
unblocking everything downstream, before the front_load() wiring (H8/#1532)
that every agent (Claude, DeepSeek, Haiku, Paperclip/Hermes once live) will
front-load before task-specific work.

### J — Issue/PR templates (RCA + Parent + lifecycle + tier + escalation, enforced by a gate)
- agent-orchestrator#1533 — extend bug.yml/epic.yml/fleet-task.yml + PR template + check-issue-template.sh
- shared-services#4247 — extend incident-report.yml/regression-report.yml/audit-finding.yml + PR template
- shared-frontend#511 — extend epic.md/module-cannibalization.md/task.md + PR template

### K — Backfill open issues to the new shape
- agent-orchestrator#1534 — retrofit 32 open issues (13 unparented)
- shared-services#4248 — retrofit 92 open issues (81 unparented)
- shared-frontend#512 — retrofit 10 open issues (9 unparented)
- capital-underwriting#2800 — triage 125 open issues (repo retiring per #1295; close-with-reason or migrate)

### L — Code knowledge + review (agents stop re-asking what's already answered)
- agent-orchestrator#1535 — define the machine-readable code header standard + linter (docs/CODE-HEADER-STANDARD.md)
- agent-orchestrator#1536 — create the code-review-sme profile card
- agent-orchestrator#1537 — wire code-review-sme into PR template + branch protection + dispatcher
- agent-orchestrator#1538 — backfill code headers across 10 top-level directories
- agent-orchestrator#1539 — dedupe pass using indexer + headers, one issue per cluster

### O — Single pane of glass (console manages/controls/orchestrates every agent)
- agent-orchestrator#1559 — Nous Research as a declared provider (gateway/providers/hermes.py -> real API)
- agent-orchestrator#1560 — Hermes Agent lifecycle decision + implementation (self-host vs Nous cloud)
- agent-orchestrator#1561 — console Nous surface (native views via gateway proxy, never iframe)
- agent-orchestrator#1562 — A2A: Hermes agent claims work through governance/dispatch
- agent-orchestrator#1563 — cross-engine Sessions view v1 (read .fleet/.board/.deepseek-agent)
- agent-orchestrator#1564 — operator controls (assign/pause/reassign/escalate/kill) on Sessions view
- agent-orchestrator#1565 — nav-parity CI gate preventing future built-but-unwired surfaces
- agent-orchestrator#1566 — reconcile the "Paperclip integrated" claim with ADR-0013's actual scope

Owner doctrine: the console at ai.purebliss.app is the single pane of glass
to manage, control, and orchestrate every agent — Paperclip, Hermes (and its
portal, resolved as **Nous** — `https://portal.nousresearch.com`, Nous
Research's external SaaS behind the Hermes Agent product: "autonomous agent
that lives on your server... Portal hosts your agent in the cloud," a 300+
model catalog, a Tool Gateway, credits-based billing), Claude, DeepSeek,
Copilot, and fleet/brain. Headline facts: the console has a real OS-shell
auth bridge (`os-session-token`, `portal/server/app.py:12,377,403,1343-1345`)
but zero integration with Hermes/Paperclip/sessions today; `~/hermes-agent`
on this host **is** the Nous Hermes agent product, confirmed dead (no
container, no listener on 9501); Paperclip integration is paper-only
(ADR + code stub + policy, runtime switch off everywhere); a v1 Sessions
view can read `.fleet`/`.board` today with no new plumbing; operator
controls reuse the 63 verbs already declared in
`control-plane/control/verbs.yaml`. Integration mechanism throughout: the
existing OS-shell iframe mount (`os.origin`, `frame-ancestors`) for external
UIs that need it, and the console's own API-proxy/native-view pattern for
Nous (never a third-party iframe, per owner doctrine, since Nous integrates
as a provider + declared agent runtime through the gateway proxy) — never a
new mechanism invented from scratch. Skipped as duplicates: nav-wiring of
the six built-but-unwired surfaces is already F1-F3 (#1520-1522); the
`approvals.html`/`policies.html` syntax fix is PR #1505; the `cmr-indexer`
MCP fix is H1/#1525; the Hermes dead-endpoint issue is E4/#1518 (ON1/#1559
supersedes E4's "retire" branch with a real Nous target); the
`enable_paperclip` go/no-go decision is E2/#1515.

### M — Built-not-shipped sweep (no vaporware, enforced)
- agent-orchestrator#1540 — inventory sweep (8 known rows pre-filled: Paperclip/Hermes flags, 6 console routes, indexer, .fleet crontab; plus 2 live defects found 2026-09-20: console container present on only one node — #1513; OS gate stale on .31 — shared-services#4242)
- shared-services#4249 — inventory sweep (7 known rows pre-filled: crontab->timer gaps, compose allowlist, module source=)
- shared-frontend#513 — inventory sweep (6 known rows pre-filled: baselines, 4 unlifted overlays)

### N — Isolation + A2A coordination

- agent-orchestrator#1542 — confirm and wire (or retire) check-isolation-landed.sh
- agent-orchestrator#1543 — widen worktree-orphan audit beyond 10/65 sample + confirm prune cadence

Headline isolation facts (ISOLATION-REVIEW-2026-09-20.md): isolation is
**cooperative only** — `.git/hooks/` has stock `.sample` files, no real
`pre-commit`/`pre-push` hook exists anywhere; the file-lease system
(`governance/policy/lease.py`, `.board/claims/*.json`) is checked only by
the `claim` CLI and offline `make verify`, never at commit time;
`fleet/watchdog.py` is the only mechanism that actually *enforces* (process
lifecycle, not files); `scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` is not wired in
the Makefile; 11 real shared-checkout `git stash` collisions are on record.
Group N is ordered so the pre-commit lease-enforcement hook (N1/#1541) lands
first — it closes the single biggest gap (enforcement currently ends where
cooperation ends) — then the consolidated worktree model, the A2A protocol
of record (GitHub issue comments/labels as durable system-of-record, `.fleet`
mailboxes/SendMessage as the ephemeral fast path, controller verbs routed
through `governance/dispatch` landing ledger rows per N8/#1548), and
live-resource leases (N5/#1545) for terraform state / Cloudflare phases —
the exact failure mode that produced the two-owner Cloudflare header phase
incident (#4231). N9/#1549 codifies proactive peer-awareness as a standard

noise), and log every check as a ledger row via N8/#1548.

## Explicitly not duplicated

2026-09-18; its one live finding is already #4231).

items.title: gate: three wired suites are red in the CI venue, so check-pytest-suites.sh reds the gate of record in Cloud Build (#1497)
items.body:
Parent: #1510

## Model tier

L0/L1 rating: **L0** — backfilled default; re-assess when picked up.

## Root cause

RCA required — Step 1: determine why this issue predates the lifecycle-contract convention (created before the #1533 templates landed) and whether the root cause is otherwise already known from the original body below.

## Escalation

Attempt at L0. Tiers: L0 = Claude Haiku / DeepSeek V4 Flash -> L1 = Claude Sonnet / DeepSeek V4 Pro -> L2 = Claude Opus.
- Max attempts: **N = 3**.
- If blocked after 3 attempts, comment on this issue with the exact failure and label `escalate:L1`, then stop. Never silent abandonment.

## Lifecycle contract (no lingering)

- This issue is closed ONLY via a merged PR whose body contains `Closes #<n>` and evidence: the acceptance command output pasted, plus the negative-control output.
- Picking this issue up = owning it to closure. Do not stop at a partial state or move to another issue. Blockers are part of the task: unblock them (file the blocker as a child issue with `Parent: #1510` if it is a separate lane, fix it, then continue).
- Before the PR is opened: `make verify` green on the branch; no orphan worktrees, no stale branches, no leftover temp files.
- After merge: delete the branch, remove the worktree, confirm the issue auto-closed, post a final comment with the merged PR link and the evidence summary.
- Escalation is the only sanctioned way to hand off; it is a comment + label on THIS issue, never silent abandonment.

## Original

gate: three wired suites are red in the CI venue, so check-pytest-suites.sh reds the gate of record in Cloud Build (#1497)

## What

#1497 wired 42 of the 51 declared-but-unreached pytest suites into the gate of
record via `scripts/check-pytest-suites.sh`. In the **CI venue** (Cloud Build
`python:3.14`, `make verify`) three of the 42 fail, so `check-pytest-suites.sh`
exits 1 and the gate of record is red in the one venue it must stay green.

Measured on `origin/master` `a9f63bf4`, PR #1502 head `41fc1dd7`, build
`6845d8ad-1da6-4a8e-992b-f2f05c5a36cb` (concluded 2026-09-20T00:08:11Z):

```
FAIL  guardrails/honesty       (pytest exit 1)
FAIL  governance/lifecycle     (pytest exit 1)
FAIL  governance/reconcile     (pytest exit 1)
check-pytest-suites: NOT-OK — 3 of 42 declared suites named by no other gate failed
verify: FAIL (1 of 221 checks failed, ...)
```

## The three suites

| suite | CI verdict | lane verdict | root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `governance/reconcile` | red | green | `test_the_shipped_document_re_measures_its_own_rows` re-measures the shipped `governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json` against the **recorded** git common dir (`/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/.git`); in a fresh CI checkout the venue is `/workspace/.git`, so `venue.git_common_dir == repository_venue(REPO_ROOT)` fails. Reproduced in a no-submodule clone: `1 failed, 212 passed`, `AssertionError: this document speaks for another repository instance`. Inherently venue-bound. |
| `guardrails/honesty` | red | green | 74 passed alone in a lane worktree and in a no-submodule clone; the CI-container-specific cause was not reproducible off-box (the container transcript is lost with the build). |
| `governance/lifecycle` | red | green | 259 passed alone in a lane worktree and in a no-submodule clone; same as honesty — CI-only, cause not reproducible off-box. |

## Why this is a finding, not a deferral

A suite that is NAMED in `scripts/check-pytest-suites.sh` runs in every `make
verify`, so a CI-venue red is a red gate of record for every lane — the one
outcome worse than the honest deferral, because a gate that is red on master is
ignored. The fix is the one #1497 already established for the nine lane-venue
suites: the suite is REMOVED from the wired list and carried in
`scripts/gate-coverage-baseline.txt` as a `swept-only` row whose tracker is this
OPEN issue, so the row is owned and time-bound, not excused.

items.title: gate-status: the venue's check-run and its required context disagree — a run that ends success can leave a stale red or publish nothing, so four green PRs are unlandable
items.body:
## The measurement (2026-09-19 23:50Z, `origin/master` = `a9f63bf4`)

The required context on `master` is **`ao/gate-of-record`**. On four live PRs the venue's own
check-run says **success** and the required context says something else — or nothing:

| PR | head | venue check-run `control-plane-verify (purebliss-ghl)` | `ao/gate-of-record` status | reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #1466 | `5e9f2145` | **success**, completed `22:56:50` | **failure**, created `22:52:01` | a red posted **4 minutes before the run it belongs to finished**, never replaced by that run's success |
| #1489 | `71594b1d` | **success**, completed `22:17:43` | **failure**, created `22:07:01` | same shape — red 10 minutes before completion |
| #1493 | `f405ab02` | **success**, completed `22:57:42` | **absent** | the run completed success and **published nothing** |
| #1498 | `4a6eae88` | **success**, completed `23:05:30` | **absent** | same |
| #1500 / #1502 / #1503 | — | `in_progress` | absent | legitimately waiting; not part of this finding |

All four are `mergeStateStatus = BLOCKED`, and nothing else on those heads is failing. The two
shapes have one root, and it is worth stating precisely because the two readings differ:

- **The two signals are not the same function of one verdict.** The check-run and the published
  required context both purport to report the same run, yet on #1466/#1489 they disagree about
  it, and on #1493/#1498 one of them is missing entirely. Either the publisher is not driven by
  the run's final verdict, or the build exits 0 while its own verdict is `failure` — in which
  case the *check-run* is the false green. The data cannot tell those apart from outside; the
  publish step can.
- **#1493/#1498 have only one reading:** a run that completed **success** and published **no**
  status at all. A PR whose head carries no status for its required context can never merge.

Consequences, measured: **#1493 is the train that lands the three closing lanes** (the #1490
siblings) — its content is verified and it is unlandable. #1466, #1489 and #1498 are single
fixes in the same position.

## The ask

1. **Publish the run's own final verdict**, for the commit the run measured: `success` on pass,
   `failure` on fail — and publish it whether or not an earlier step already posted something.
2. **Never publish before the verdict exists.** A red landing at `22:52:01` on a run that is
   still in flight is a claim about a verdict that had not been reached; if the run then passes,
   that red outlives the truth it was supposed to report.
3. **Make the check-run and the required context agree, or make one of them authoritative by
   name.** Two signals for one verdict, disagreeing, is the condition this repo's own rules call
   a formality.
4. **Provoke both shapes** (GR-12): a passing run must end with `success` on the head it
   measured; a run that publishes early must be overwritten by its own outcome. Neither is
   covered today.

## Evidence (verbatim reads)

```
gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits/5e9f21454431/status   --jq '.statuses[] | .context + "=" + .state + " @" + .created_at'
  → ao/gate-of-record=failure @ 2026-09-19T22:52:01Z
gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits/5e9f21454431/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[] | .name + " " + .conclusion + " " + (.started_at) + " → " + (.completed_at)'
  → control-plane-verify (purebliss-ghl) success 2026-09-19T22:32:50Z → 2026-09-19T22:56:50Z
gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits/f405ab02d026/status   --jq '[.statuses[].context]'
  → []            # nothing at all, on a run that completed success
```

items.title: gate: a skip-budget entry whose tracking issue is closed is still honoured — the venue's 13 standing skips name #1361, closed 22h ago
items.body:
## The measurement

Every one of the venue's **13 standing skips** says, in its own message, *"the open issue that
tracks the mechanism is #1361"*. Measured on `origin/master` `a9f63bf4`:

```
$ gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/1361 --jq '.state + " " + .closed_at'
closed 2026-09-19T01:03:11Z          # "cloudbuild: the verify container supplies no gh, docker, crontab or vendor/CMR"
```

The container **still** supplies none of `gh`, `docker`, `crontab`, `vendor/CMR` — the gaps the
skips describe are as present as the day they were written — while the issue those entries name
as their tracker has been closed for ~22 hours. The composite gate honours the entries and the
venue's run is **green** (`control-plane-verify = success`).

So the gate accepts a skip whose tracker is shut. That is a false green of exactly the class
`#1268` exists to remove, and it is why `#1268`'s clause 1 cannot be read as met.

## Why it is not just bookkeeping

The **quarantine** mechanism already solved this class of problem and did it correctly: an entry
carries `tracked_by` **and** `tracking.state: open`, and is honoured *only while the issue is
open* — which is what let `#1338` retire all six of its exemptions the moment the evidence
resolved them, with the retirement itself reviewed. The skip budget holds the same kind of
exemption without holding the same condition.

## The ask (small, and it borrows the existing authority)

1. Decide per entry, by name: **re-point** at a live tracker, or **retire** it and let the venue
   red honestly on its own missing preconditions.
2. Make the ratchet refuse an entry whose tracking issue is closed, by borrowing the
   quarantine's `tracked_by` + `tracking.state` shape rather than inventing a second one.
3. Provoke it: a fixture entry pointing at a closed issue must fail the gate, or the rule is a
   formality (GR-12).

## Evidence

- `gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/1361 --jq '.state + " " + .closed_at'` → `closed 2026-09-19T01:03:11Z`
- the venue's run on the #1490 head, green, with the 13 skips named in its own output
- `scripts/lib/skip-ratchet.py` + `skip-budget.json` (the venue entries' home; `live-dependent` was added there by #1410)
- `governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json` + `baseline.json` (the pattern to borrow; emptied by #1338/`a9f63bf4`)

| `gateway/providers/contract.py:51` | `("LOW", "MED", "HIGH", "MAX")` |
| `governance/authority/model.py:89` | `("LOW", "MED", "HIGH", "MAX")` |
| `identity/onboarding/model.py:85` | `("LOW", "MED", "HIGH", "MAX")` |
| `integrations/hermes/mapping.py:67` | `("LOW", "MED", "HIGH", "MAX")` |
| `portal/server/chat.py:74` | `("LOW", "MED", "HIGH", "MAX")` |
| `registry/chat/labels.py:43` | `("flash", "pro", "auditor")` |
| `fleet/channel.py:167` | `("flash", "pro", "auditor")` |
| `governance/cto-overlay/overlay.py:79` | `("experimental", "standard", "critical")` |

The five identical tuples have **no declared authority**: nothing in the tree says
which of the five is the source, and nothing fails when one of them drifts.

The other two are not copies of a copy — they restate **declared data**:

```
$ python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('governance/finops/policy.json'));print(d['vocabulary']['tiers'], d['tier_rank'])"
['flash', 'pro', 'auditor'] {'flash': 1, 'pro': 2, 'auditor': 3}
```

`gateway/sme-routing/policies/tier-policy.yaml:27` declares those same three tiers
again (with their models, fallbacks and cost controls). `governance/cto-overlay/overlay.py`
is a different concept (evidence tiers), so it is **out of scope** — say so in the
authority rather than silently folding it in.

## Acceptance criteria

1. One declared authority for the `LOW`/`MED`/`HIGH`/`MAX` vocabulary; the five sites
   read it instead of re-declaring it — or each remaining declaration is recorded in
   the authority with the reason it is a deliberate boundary.
2. The FinOps tier names are read from `governance/finops/policy.json` by
   `registry/chat/labels.py` and `fleet/channel.py` rather than restated.
3. A check in `make verify` refuses a **new** re-declaration by name, and its refusal
   is provoked both ways (a planted copy is refused by name; the clean tree passes).
   A check whose two paths collapse into one exit code is a formality (GR-12).
4. `make verify` green at the merge, with its real output recorded.

## Verify command

`make verify`

## Evidence

(replace with the real output at merge)

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1458

items.title: reconcile: a failed teardown clears the beat anyway, so the lane leaves the sweep's input plane for good (the ordering half of #1446)
items.body:
## The defect

`#1446` was closed by the **import** half of the repair (the 13-lane train, `b5561044`):
`RepoOps.forget_lane` no longer loads `governance/isolation/worktree.py` as a top-level
module. The **ordering** half never landed, and it is the half that made the wedge
*permanent*: `_teardown` clears the session's heartbeat unconditionally, even when an
earlier step of the same teardown has already been recorded `FAILED`.

The heartbeat *is* the sweep's input — `sweep` iterates `list_sessions(root)`. A beat
cleared after a failure therefore removes the lane from the only worker that can finish
it, while its lane record stays on disk; and the `failed:` finding the same pass filed
can never be retired, because that key is resolved only for a session the sweep
*reclaims*, which it can no longer see. The lane is wedged for good.

## Measured on current `origin/master` (`00cbd753`)

One applied pass against a real git repository carrying the repository's own
`governance/` tree, a real lane record and a real stale beat, with the isolation module
made unreadable so an early step genuinely fails:

```
### master (origin/master 00cbd753) — PASS 1, isolation module unreadable
sweep module under test: …/fixture-master/governance/reconcile/sweep.py
ordering guard present: False
outcome: failed
    failed    forget-lane: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '…/governance/isolation/worktree.py'
    performed release-claim: reap: nothing to reap (no live claim older than the threshold)
    performed clear-heartbeat: cleared heartbeat
after: lane record present: True
after: beat present:        False
after: the sweep's input (list_sessions): []

### master — PASS 2, module readable again: the wedge is permanent
before: lane record present: True
before: the sweep's input (list_sessions): []
after: lane record present: True
after: the sweep's input (list_sessions): []
```

Nothing is performed in the second pass: the sweep can no longer see the lane at all.

## Why this is a separate record from `#1446`

`#1446`'s acceptance was satisfied by the import repair — a teardown no longer *dies*.
That is not the same property as *the lane remains finishable*. The two have different
observable signatures (an `ImportError` on the board vs. a silently empty sweep), and the
second is strictly worse: the first is loud and self-describing, the second is a lane that
disappears from the sweep's input plane with its record and its finding on disk.

## The remedy

`RepoOps._isolation_worktree` plus `_clear_heartbeat_if_terminal`: the beat is cleared
**last**, and only when every earlier step of that teardown succeeded; a skipped step is
named (`kept: an earlier step failed, so this lane must stay visible to the next pass`)
rather than silent. This is the rule `governance/isolation/cli.py close` already states for
the same beat — *"the beat is cleared only once the worktree is actually gone, so a kept
lane keeps its session too"*.

Proposed in PR #1466 (branch `issue-1446`), with seven controls in
`governance/reconcile/tests/test_teardown_forget_lane.py`, each against a real repository
with a real lane record and a real heartbeat, including the wedge above as an assertion
(`a failed teardown cleared the beat: the wedge`).

Measured on the branch's own tree, same fixture, same provocation:

```
### branch (c9e58491) — PASS 1, isolation module unreadable
ordering guard present: True
outcome: failed
    failed    forget-lane: IsolationUnavailable: governance.isolation.worktree cannot be imported from …: PermissionError: …
    performed release-claim: reap: nothing to reap (no live claim older than the threshold)
    skipped   clear-heartbeat: kept: an earlier step failed, so this lane must stay visible to the next pass
after: lane record present: True
after: beat present:        True
after: the sweep's input (list_sessions): ['2656d99e793e']

### branch — PASS 2, module readable again: the lane reaches its terminal state
outcome: reclaimed
    performed forget-lane: forgot lane record 2656d99e793e
    performed clear-heartbeat: cleared heartbeat
after: lane record present: False
after: the sweep's input (list_sessions): []
```

`Refs #1446` — the closed parent, whose import half landed in the train.

items.title: [bug] check-lessons: a single-branch checkout cannot resolve evidence outside its ref, so it must not report ERROR
items.body:
## Problem

`check-lessons` reports **three `ERROR evidence-unresolvable` findings that are false**, and
therefore exits `NOT-OK`, in any checkout that only ever fetched ONE branch. The gate judges a
property of the **venue** (this checkout cannot see that object) as if it were a property of the
**ledger** (that citation is wrong). The ledger's citations are correct.

This is the leak the closed parent #1482 fixed at the infra layer (`infra/cloudbuild/verify.yaml`
fetches every branch + PR ref). That fix is *partial by construction*: it repairs **one** venue. The
checker-level defect below survives in every venue that fix does not reach — a `--single-branch`
clone, a partial fetch, a runner that fetches only the ref under test. Filed as the tracking issue
for that residual class, measured on `origin/master` = `00cbd75376d6ad20c02d367cf6f435038d913aa1`.

## Observed

A `--single-branch` checkout of `origin/master` (`00cbd753`), NOT shallow, holding exactly one
remote-tracking ref. `bash scripts/check-lessons.sh`:

```
  ERROR evidence-unresolvable              LESSON-0015 names commit 52fe84d6e714eee522190c1fb8f0fe507673eb4a, which is not in this repository's history [LESSON-0015] -> cite a commit that exists (evidence must be checkable)
  ERROR evidence-unresolvable              LESSON-0022 names commit c46882200b80e59efb073caec161d1d9d4ff602e, which is not in this repository's history [LESSON-0022] -> cite a commit that exists (evidence must be checkable)
  ERROR evidence-unresolvable              LESSON-0023 names commit c46882200b80e59efb073caec161d1d9d4ff602e, which is not in this repository's history [LESSON-0023] -> cite a commit that exists (evidence must be checkable)
...
  PROBES: FAIL (1 of 37) — REAL-BOARD-HAS-NO-UNRECORDED-RECORD-LABEL
negative-control: NOT-OK — ...
RC=1
```

Every one of those three citations is real and resolvable in a wide checkout:

```
$ git cat-file -e 52fe84d6e714eee522190c1fb8f0fe507673eb4a^{commit}   -> EXISTS
  52fe84d6 fix(runner): the fan-out width is an INJECTED input, not the machine (#1343)
$ git cat-file -e c46882200b80e59efb073caec161d1d9d4ff602e^{commit}   -> EXISTS
  c4688220 feat(pr-contract): duplicate-pr-for-issue and semantic-merge-review controls
  refs containing it: refs/remotes/origin/issue-1366 refs/remotes/origin/train/20260919T033833Z
```

`c4688220` is the clean illustration: it lives on `origin/issue-1366`, a branch the narrow venue
never fetched. Neither commit is an ancestor of `master` — they exist only on other refs, which is
exactly what a single-branch fetch cannot reach.

Why this is a **false** finding, not a real one: the check's anchor is
`git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}`. In a venue that fetched one ref, that command cannot succeed for
any object outside that ref's ancestry, **for a reason unrelated to whether the citation is
correct**. `--unshallow` / `--deepen` do not help: they extend the depth of the one ref already
fetched and never reach a sibling branch's objects. The checker already accepts this nuance for a
**shallow** clone (`GitProbe.shallow` downgrades an unresolved citation to a WARNING) — a
single-branch checkout is the same inability for a different reason, and currently gets the
opposite, harsher verdict.

## Expected

1. `governance/lessons/README.md`'s finding table defines `evidence-unresolvable` as "a cited commit
   is **not in this repository's history**, or a cited artifact is absent". "This repository" is not
   a claim a one-ref checkout can make; it can only say "not in the history I hold".
2. `scripts/check-lessons.sh`'s own exit-code contract says `NOT-OK` outranks `CANNOT-ASSESS`
   because "a definite defect is never softened into 'could not assess'". The inverse is also
   required: an **indefinite** observation must not be promoted to a definite defect. Here the
   venue cannot assess the citation, so it is not entitled to an `ERROR`.
3. The precedent is already in the file: `GitProbe.shallow` downgrades the same unresolved citation
   to a WARNING with a named reason. A narrow venue is the same class of "cannot resolve", and
   should be treated the same way — **reported, never muted** (GR-12). The finding must still be
   emitted, with a remediation naming the venue, so the deviation is visible rather than swallowed.
4. Nothing about this may soften a *genuinely* broken citation: a wide, non-shallow checkout must
   keep failing `ERROR evidence-unresolvable`, or the gate has been bought off instead of fixed.

## Reproduction command

```bash
# a mirror whose ONE branch is exactly origin/master (never the shared checkout's stale local master)
M=$(mktemp -d /tmp/ao1489/mirror.XXXXXX)
git init -q --bare "$M/src.git"
git -C "$M/src.git" fetch -q --no-tags /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator \
  refs/remotes/origin/master:refs/heads/master
git clone -q --single-branch --branch master --no-tags "file://$M/src.git" "$M/narrow"

cd "$M/narrow"
git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository                    # false  <-- NOT shallow
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' refs/remotes/origin | wc -l   # 1      <-- the defect's precondition
git cat-file -e 52fe84d6e714eee522190c1fb8f0fe507673eb4a^{commit}    # fatal: Not a valid object name

bash scripts/check-lessons.sh; echo "RC=$?"              # RC=1, three false ERRORs (see Observed)
```

After copying this class's fix (`GitProbe.narrow` + the WARNING branch in `_unresolvable_evidence`)
into the same checkout, the same three findings are still **reported** — at WARNING, naming the
venue — and the gate returns `RC=0` with `PROBES: PASS (37 of 37)`:

```
  WARNING evidence-unresolvable  LESSON-0015 names commit 52fe84d6..., which this checkout's
    single-branch fetch cannot resolve (it may exist on a branch this venue never fetched)
  PROBES: PASS (37 of 37)
negative-control: OK — ...
RC=0
```

And the wide venue is unchanged by the fix (a clean `origin/master` worktree: `check-lessons.sh`
RC=0, `PROBES: PASS (37 of 37)`, 0 `evidence-unresolvable` findings).

## Severity

high

## RCA link (governance/lessons/)

`governance/lessons/rca/single-branch-venue-cannot-resolve-evidence.md` (intended landing path).

The ledger record is a **required follow-up, not done here**: `governance/lessons/ledger.jsonl` is
the id authority, and minting an `INC-*`/`RCA-*`/`LESSON-*` record is the lessons lane's file — a
fix lane that edits it would both widen its diff and race the id authority. Note also that writing
an RCA doc *without* a matching ledger record is itself refused by this very gate (a `docs/rca/*.md`
token that is not a ledger id is a finding), so the doc and the record must land together.

## Relationship to other work

- **#1482 (closed)** — the infra-layer half (`infra/cloudbuild/verify.yaml`). Closed; this class is
  the residual the checker-level fix covers. A fix must not land under a closed parent, hence this
  issue.
- **#727 (closed)** — invoked as the name of the venue-blindness class; it was about board-trigger
  refresh/park, not about checkout breadth, and is closed.
- **PR #1489** (`issue-board-gate-venue`) carries the checker-level fix and is fold-clean against
  `origin/master` = `00cbd753` (`git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only origin/master <head>` → rc
  0, no conflict files). It touches only `governance/lessons/` and does not conflict with #1483's
  files.

items.title: reconcile: the quarantine is empty and its six rule-17 artifacts are unexcused, so check-reconcile reds every lane again
items.body:
Parent: #1254

## The red

`check-reconcile` is red on a pristine detached `origin/master` (`9c2c68fe`) with the default environment,
and `verify` is never attributable — so this one red refuses **every** landing on the box, including the
open merge train.

```
$ bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh
check-reconcile: FAIL — real tree drifted from governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json (6 new-and-old, 522 stale, not fatal; 1 stale quarantine exemption(s))
real-tree-baseline: 110 unmatched artifact(s) on disk, 619 baselined, 7 young (< 24h, not failed), 522 stale (not failed), 0 vanished (not failed), 0 quarantined by name (reported, not failed)
  NEW      branch issue-1028-canon — not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or fix it)
  NEW      branch issue-1114-dispatch-master-green — not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or fix it)
  NEW      branch issue-830-reaper-schedule — not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or fix it)
  NEW      worktree …/.claude/worktrees/agent-a1b5cf2e0dceac199 — not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or fix it)
  NEW      worktree …/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad284eb1ac275c0c6 — not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or fix it)
  NEW      worktree …/.claude/worktrees/agent-afc588dba96686e4e — not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or fix it)
```

Every other former box red is green on the same tree: `check-reconcile-orphans`, `check-worktree-cap`,
`check-branch-protection`, `check-gate-status`, `check-gitignore` — all rc 0.

## What actually happened, measured

These six are exactly the artifacts the **quarantine** used to excuse by name. Earlier today the same check
reported `6 quarantined by name`; it now reports `0 quarantined by name` and
`1 stale quarantine exemption(s)`, and `governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json` reads:

```
tracking.measured_at = 2026-09-18T20:07:12Z   tracking.max_age_hours = 24   entries = 0
```

So the document is **empty**, and its lease measurement has aged past its own 24h bound. Nothing about the
six artifacts changed — the record that excused them went away, and they became `NEW…old` in one step.

## Disposition

`check-reconcile`'s own message offers three routes for such an artifact — *"add it, reviewed, or fix it"*.
Reaping is not available for these: their work is on **no** default-branch commit and on **no**
remote-tracking ref, so discarding them is the worker's decision to have authorised, not a cleanup
(AGENTS.md rule 17). So they are **recorded, reviewed**, in the baseline — the same disposition, and the same
file, as the 54-artifact catch-up that landed as `9c2c68fe` (#1476).

`Refs #1338` — the tracker that owns the per-artifact decision. [#1451] proposes that decision and is still
open and unlanded; this issue does not pre-empt it, it only stops the box reding on the clock meanwhile.

## The class (not fixed here)

Two records now lapse on the same 24h clock — the baseline's grace for an unexplained artifact, and the
quarantine's measurement lease — and each lapse re-reds every lane. A record refreshed by hand cannot outrun
a box that creates artifacts hourly; #1476 carries the recurrence and #1338 the cadence.

items.title: fix(cloudbuild): the verify venue reds for two preconditions it does not supply (locale, ref scope)
items.body:
## Problem

`control-plane-verify (purebliss-ghl)` is **red for every head on this board**, and that red is
what `scripts/gate-status.sh` defers to (#1400) — so one refusal blocks all 15 open pull requests
at once. Measured on three heads (`063cca53` PR #1475, `2e2ac5c6` PR #1478, `26385b4b` PR #1473;
builds `0030a1ed`, `5f0778f4`, `baa834ec`), the verdict is:

```
verify: FAIL (3 of 220 checks failed, 12 skipped: <the 12 budgeted venue gaps>;
  skip ratchet FAIL: 1 finding(s) -- named above)
```

The three failures are **`gate-status`** (rc 1), **`board-gate`** (NOT-OK) and **`lessons`** (FAIL).
Two of the three do not fail for a tree defect: the checks are right, and the **venue does not
supply two things they need to reach their own verdict**.

## Cause 1 — the venue's shell counts BYTES, not characters

`check-gate-status.sh` asserts a status description against the API's 140-**character** cap using
bash's `${#var}`, which counts bytes in the C locale and characters in a multi-byte one. The
production code is correct (`gate-status-map.py` yields exactly 140 chars / 142 bytes for a
500-character detail), so in the venue's byte-counting shell the check reds on its own self-test arm:

```
check-gate-status: FAIL -- the detail arm 'a 500-character detail still fits the API's
  140-character description cap' did not hold
  expect: <=140   actual: >140 (142)
```

That single arm sets `fail=1`, so the check exits **1** instead of the rc 2 CANNOT-ASSESS it reaches
with a multi-byte locale (no `gh` in the venue either) — and rc 2 is the shape the committed
`scripts/skip-budget.json` already declares for it via its `live-dependent` entry (#1382).
Reproduced in a single-branch clone of this tree: `LC_ALL=C` → 142, `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` → 140.

## Cause 2 — the venue's clone has ONE branch's ref scope

`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` is **false** in the venue, so `check-lessons`' own
shallow-clone carve-out never fires; the clone simply lacks objects reachable only from non-default
refs. Verbatim from the same builds:

```
ERROR evidence-unresolvable  LESSON-0015 names commit 52fe84d6..., which is not in this repository's history
ERROR evidence-unresolvable  SUGGEST-0018 names commit 9724c0c9..., which is not in this repository's history
```

Both commits are served by `gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits/<sha>` and are reachable
from a **closed pull request's head ref** (`refs/pull/1356/head`, `refs/pull/1408/head`); neither is
on the default branch. `check-board-gate` reds only because it folds `check-lessons`.

The class grows: a third family (`LESSON-0022`, `LESSON-0023`, `CA-0025` citing `c4688220`, which
sits only on `origin/issue-1366` and a train branch) is present on `master` and absent from any
single-branch clone.

## Fix (PR)

`infra/cloudbuild/verify.yaml`: declare `LANG`/`LC_ALL` = `C.UTF-8` on the verify step and ASSERT it
took (a named WARN, never fatal, so the gate's own verdict stays the step's outcome); and fetch the
repository's **ref scope** as well as its depth — the branch heads and the pull-request head refs —
best-effort and named.

## Evidence

Measured in a single-branch clone of this tree with no `gh` and a C locale:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `lessons` | rc 1 | rc 0 |
| `board-gate` | rc 1 | rc 0 |
| `gate-status` | rc 1 | rc 2 CANNOT-ASSESS (honoured by its existing `live-dependent` entry) |

Driven against the committed budget over the venue's own measured 200-check name set, the skip
ratchet answers **rc 1** on today's shape (refusal verbatim the venue's own line: *"its check does
not skip here (rc 1)"*) and **rc 0** on the fixed one — and still refuses an unnamed skip. **No
skip-budget entry is added, widened or deleted**: the reds were un-supplied venue preconditions, not
unbudgeted skips.

## Not this issue

The submodule-init half of #1424 is carried by PR #1430 and is **not** duplicated here. This issue is
the venue-green half only, so #1424 stays open for its own stated fix.

items.title: reconcile: three unbaselined-and-old real-tree artifacts red check-reconcile for every lane on the box (the #1034 clock red recurring)
items.body:
## The red

`check-reconcile` is red on a **pristine detached `origin/master` worktree** (`a7518cff`) with the
default environment, and because `verify` is never attributable (`governance/landing/attribution.py`)
a single red here refuses **every** landing on the box:

```
$ bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh
real-tree-baseline: 102 unmatched artifact(s) on disk, 562 baselined, 49 young (< 24h, not failed), 518 stale (not failed), 0 vanished (not failed), 6 quarantined by name
  NEW      branch issue-1310 — not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or fix it)
  NEW      branch issue-pcm-board-freshness — not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or fix it)
  NEW      worktree /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/.claude/worktrees/agent-ac93099db7773c3c9 — not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or fix it)
check-reconcile: FAIL (1 violation(s))
```

All three were inside the 24h grace earlier in the day (`young (< 24h, not failed)`). **Nothing about
the tree changed — the clock moved.** This is the #1034/#1399 class recurring: `governance/reconcile`'s
real-tree audit fails closed on an artifact it has not been told about, once that artifact is a day old.

## Why it is the box's serialization point right now

On the same pristine master, every other former red is green with the **default** environment:
`check-worktree-cap` (the scheduled reaper brought the box from 64 to 43 worktrees), `check-branch-protection`,
`check-gate-status`, `check-gitignore`, `check-reconcile-orphans` — all rc 0. `check-reconcile` is the
one red between the board and its open PRs, and the merge train the board needs cannot gate green while
it stands.

## What each artifact actually is (measured, so the record is checkable)

| artifact | measured |
|---|---|
| `branch issue-pcm-board-freshness` | on **NO remote** (`git ls-remote --heads origin refs/heads/issue-pcm-board-freshness` empty); 1 commit not on `origin/master` (`d5d0a2657917`, "fix(paperclip): classify board.freshness, restoring the control-mapping gate") — its work exists **only on this box** |
| `branch issue-1310` | local tip `16a4480eef23` is **not** an ancestor of `origin/master` (2 commits not on it); `refs/heads/issue-1310` exists on the remote but at a **different** tip (`f627b824cb2a`), so the local tip is not preserved by that ref |
| `worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-ac93099db7773c3c9` | HEAD `6c36900586f1` **is** an ancestor of `origin/master` (landed as #1315); only dirty path is machine-managed (`.board/focus.json`) — holds nothing an exemption protects |

The first two are the AGENTS.md **rule 17** keep-and-report class; the third holds nothing at all. So the
honest disposition is a **reviewed baseline record** for each — not a reap, which the check's own text
reserves for the worker's decision to authorise.

## Remedy landed with this issue

Three reviewed entries appended to `governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json` (a 15-line diff, no
reformatting), which turns `check-reconcile` green **in the lane's own tree** and therefore lets the lane
publish its own gate-of-record and land through the ordinary path.

## The class, which this issue does not fix

A baseline that must be re-measured by hand will always drift behind a box that creates artifacts faster
than they are recorded: the **next** artifact to cross the 24h grace re-reds every lane the same way.
The remedy for the class is the one #1338 already opened — a per-artifact owner call, on a cadence, so the
record is refreshed rather than chased. This issue is the recurrence, not the class.

items.title: gate: the required context can never be published while the retiring Cloud Build venue is red — the #1400 guard refuses the box-side green, so no head can satisfy ao/gate-of-record
items.body:
Parent: #1254
Refs: #1382 #1400 #1415 #1439

## Measured

A merge train of 8 verified lanes reached **`verify: PASS (218 of 218 checks)`** on a
real composite run in its own worktree (`ao-train-fold2`, head
`a18b1f84f424`), and the run's own producer **refused to publish it**:

```
$ bash scripts/gate-status.sh post --sha a18b1f84f424 --rc 0
gate-status: REFUSED — no green is published for a18b1f84f424: the CI venue's own run
for this commit concluded 'failure' (control-plane-verify (purebliss-ghl),
e74eab7a-8ebb-4657-931c-b6fa09a1369f); the required context 'ao/gate-of-record' must
be derived from the venue of record's own verdict on this commit, and a second
producer (this one) may not satisfy it first

$ gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits/a18b1f84f424/check-runs \
    --jq '.check_runs[] | "\(.name) \(.status) \(.conclusion) \(.started_at)"'
control-plane-verify (purebliss-ghl) completed failure 2026-09-19T16:46:51Z
```

So the guard is doing what #1400 asked of it — a second producer must not satisfy the
required context before the venue of record — while **the venue of record is red for
every pushed commit**, because Cloud Build is the venue the fleet is retiring (#1415)
and its runs have been failing all day.

## Why this is a board-level blocker, not a lane defect

`ao/gate-of-record` is the required status on `master`
(`{"checks":["ao/gate-of-record"],"enforce_admins":false}`). It has two halves:

1. a producer — landed by #1439 / `#1382`, so `verify.sh` and `merge-pr.sh` both post;
2. the *observation* — `scripts/check-gate-status.sh`'s probe reads the commit under
   test first, then the default branch's last 20 commits. `master`'s last 20 commits
   carry no status (measured: `[]` for each of the last five), because the landings so
   far were admin bypasses (`enforce_admins=false`), so the probe reads
   `gh-status-absent-in-last-20-commits` and refuses `REQUIRED-BUT-UNOBSERVED`.

The intended bootstrap is: a real green run posts the context for its own head, the
next run observes it, and the first `merge-pr.sh` landing posts for the landed commit,
after which every gate sees it. **The venue guard makes that bootstrap impossible**: no
box-side green may be published while a Cloud Build run for the same commit is red,
and Cloud Build is red for every commit. Measured consequence: `#1439` was merged by
the owner with **no status on the landed commit**
(`gh api …/commits/6ac617b3/statuses` → `[]`), which is precisely the "merge proceeds
only through the admin bypass" state #1382 named.

## Bounded remedy (pick one; each is small)

1. **Retire the venue** (#1415's own path): declare `disabled: true` on the three
   `infra/cloudbuild/*-trigger.yaml` and apply it (the declared control, not a console
   click), then remove the Cloud Build poster step. `check-cloudbuild.sh` proves
   declared == live. When the venue stops producing runs, the guard has no red run to
   defer to and the producer on the box becomes the single voice.
2. **Or teach the guard the venue's declared state**: the guard should refuse only
   while the venue is a venue of record. A trigger declared `disabled: true` (GR-5) is
   not one, and its stale red runs must not outrank a live box-side gate. State the
   rule in the guard and provoke it: a landed commit whose only "venue" run is a
   disabled trigger's must accept the box-side green.
3. **Or land one commit through `merge-pr.sh`** so the landed history carries the
   context and the probe's second half is satisfied from then on — but that requires
   the guard to let the green out first, so it is (1) or (2) that unblocks it.

## Acceptance

- A green `make verify` on a lane head produces a publishable `ao/gate-of-record` for
  that head, and the required context is observed on `master`'s recent commits.
- Negative control kept: a head whose gate did NOT pass must still be refused, and a
  head must never show `success` from a producer that did not run the gate.

## Evidence

Full transcript: `ao-train-fold2/.verify/verify.log` + `attestation.json`
(`git_sha a18b1f84f424`, `exit_code 0`, `check_count 218`, no non-zero check row).

items.title: fix(pr-queue): merged-tree verify execs scripts/verify.sh directly, but it is committed 100644
items.body:
## Problem
`scripts/pr-queue.sh:496` runs the merged-tree verify as
`${AO_QUEUE_VERIFY_CMD:-"scripts/verify.sh verify"}` — a direct exec. But
`scripts/verify.sh` is committed mode `100644` (no exec bit; `Makefile:154`
invokes it as `bash scripts/verify.sh verify`). Result: every
`AO_QUEUE_VERIFY_MERGED=1` run fails immediately with
`bash: line 1: scripts/verify.sh: Permission denied` and the queue reports
`merged-tree-red:verify` — a false red. The log file has exactly that one line.

Measured 2026-09-19 on master `a7518cff` for PRs #1430 and #1432
(`/home/akushnir/.cache/leaderboard/tmp/pr-queue-merged-tree-log.dd44Is`, `.pzaZ9L`).

## Fix
Either set the default to `bash scripts/verify.sh verify` (matches the Makefile),
or commit `scripts/verify.sh` as `100755` — and add a negative control so a
verify log consisting solely of a shell error is reported as CANNOT-ASSESS, not red.

## Workaround
`AO_QUEUE_VERIFY_CMD="bash scripts/verify.sh verify"`.

items.title: gate-status: post --rc 0 cannot publish for a commit the venue has no run for — an empty venue_url is sent as target_url and the API rejects the whole status
items.body:
## The defect

`scripts/gate-status.sh`'s `post` verb is the **only** producer the required context has on a commit
that has no Cloud Build run. It calls `publish_status "$sha" "$state" "$description" "$target_url"`,
and `target_url` is set from the venue-agreement branch (line ~597):

```
venue_url="${venue_rest#*$'\n'}"
case "$venue_verdict" in
  allow)
    target_url="$venue_url"
    echo "gate-status: venue agreement — $venue_reason" >&2
    ;;
```

When the venue of record produced **no run** for the commit, the agreement is `allow` but the URL it
hands back is empty, so `publish_status` takes the `[ -n "$purl" ]` branch and sends
`-f target_url=""` — and GitHub rejects the whole POST:

```
$ bash scripts/gate-status.sh post --sha a7518cff71bd46f2b9242bf0bd5f084ba91bfd4b --rc 0
gate-status: venue agreement — the CI venue produced no run for this commit, so this post is the
only producer it has
gate-status: CANNOT-ASSESS — the POST failed: gh: Validation failed: Target url must use http(s)
scheme (Validation Failed)
$ bash scripts/gate-status.sh show --sha a7518cff71bd46f2b9242bf0bd5f084ba91bfd4b
gate-status: NOT-OK — no 'ao/gate-of-record' status on this commit (it is NOT gated by the gate of record)
```

Measured 2026-09-19 on the landing commit of the verified train #1454. The status was then posted by
hand through the same endpoint with no `target_url`, and read back:

```
$ gh api -X POST repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/statuses/a7518cff… -f state=success \
    -f context=ao/gate-of-record -f description="make verify: PASS (219/219) — landed tree is byte-identical to the gated head 390ddd77"
posted: ao/gate-of-record=success
$ gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits/a7518cff…/status --jq '.state'
success
```

So the endpoint accepts the status; only the script's `target_url` handling refuses it.

## Why it matters

`publish_status` already handles the empty case correctly in its **second** branch (`else` omits
`target_url` entirely) — the bug is that `allow` with an empty `venue_url` takes the **first** branch,
because the guard is on `purl` being non-empty rather than on it being a URL. Every landing whose
commit has no CI run — which is exactly the owner/train route this board depends on — silently fails
to publish, and the verb still exits 0 with a `CANNOT-ASSESS`, so a caller that only checks the exit
code believes it published.

## Remedy (bounded)

* Only pass `target_url` when it is a URL: guard the first branch on a scheme check
  (`case "$purl" in http://*|https://*) …`), so an empty or relative value falls through to the
  branch that omits the field; **and**
* make the `allow`-with-no-URL case say so in the message (the current text asserts a venue agreement
  that carries no evidence URL).
* Worth a control: `post --rc 0` for a commit the venue has no run for must either publish or fail
  with a non-zero exit — a `CANNOT-ASSESS` that exits 0 is the shape that hides.

## Refs

* #1467 — the sibling defect in the same producer path (the green is refused outright when the venue
  of record's run is red, including when the venue cannot post at all).
* #1382 — the producer gap this path was added to close.
* Observed while landing PR #1454 (train, 15 verified PRs).

`Verify:` `bash scripts/gate-status.sh post --sha <a commit with no Cloud Build run> --rc 0` must
either publish a readable status or exit non-zero, and `show --sha <that commit>` must agree with it.

items.title: gate: the gate of record cannot be published at all — the local producer defers to a venue of record that structurally cannot publish (no gh/gcloud in its runner)
items.body:
## The deadlock

PR #1439 (landed as `6ac617b3`) added a publisher to `scripts/verify.sh` so the ordinary lane path
produces the required context `ao/gate-of-record`. It works — and it **refuses to publish a green**,
by design, in exactly the case the board is in:

```
verify: PASS (219 of 219 checks)
attestation: .verify/attestation.json   (git_sha 390ddd77, exit_code 0, verdict OK)
verify: NOTE -- the gate of record was NOT published for 390ddd77a67f (the poster exited 2):
gate-status: REFUSED — no green is published for 390ddd77a67f: the CI venue's own run for this
commit concluded 'failure' (control-plane-verify (purebliss-ghl), 38ece2de-…); the required
context 'ao/gate-of-record' must be derived from the venue of record's own verdict on this
commit, and a second producer (this one) may not satisfy it first
```

So the local producer defers to **the venue of record** (Cloud Build, `control-plane-verify
(purebliss-ghl)`). The problem: **that venue cannot publish at all.** Measured in its own build log
(`38ece2de-1412-4ae8-acd7-fe7bfd2055e2`, `gcloud builds log`):

```
gate-status: attestation .verify/attestation.json — rc 1 measured on 390ddd77a67f (1s ago)
gate-status: DRY-RUN — would POST
gate-status: SKIPPED -- this runner image carries no gcloud, so the token cannot be read
verify: NOTE -- the gate of record was NOT published for 390ddd77a67f (the poster exited 2):
              gate-status: CANNOT-ASSESS — gh not found and no GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN in env; status not posted
```

There is **no path that publishes the required context**: the local producer is forbidden from going
first, and the venue of record structurally cannot go at all (its image carries neither `gh` nor
`gcloud`). Every PR head therefore stays `BLOCKED`, exactly as before #1439 — the producer moved from
"nothing produces it" to "only a producer that cannot run is allowed to".

## Second, independent red in the same CI run (not venue-shape)

The CI run is `verify: FAIL (3 of 219 checks failed, 12 skipped …)`. Two of the three failures are the
board-venue class (`check-board-gate: NOT-OK (board enforcement=1, board triggers=0)`,
`lessons: FAIL (2 error(s), 94 deviation(s))` — the runner has no `gh`, so the committed board snapshot
cannot be refreshed). The third is **not** venue-shape:

```
check-gate-status: FAIL — the detail arm 'a 500-character detail still fits the API's 140-character
description cap' did not hold
```

The **same tree** passes that check on this box (`check-gate-status: OK` inside a `verify: PASS
(219 of 219)` run), so `--detail`'s 140-character cap arm (#1419) is **venue-dependent**: it fails in a
runner without `gh`. That is a real defect in the arm, not in the world.

It also cascades: because `check-gate-status` returns **rc 1** rather than skipping in that venue, the
new live-dependent skip-budget kind (#1410) refuses its own entry and the run adds a second failure —

```
verify: skip ratchet FAIL -- live-dependent entry 'gate-status' -- its check does not skip here (rc 1):
its LIVE mechanism it names answered, so the blindness this entry declares is over and a failing check
is a FINDING, not a skip; delete the entry from scripts/skip-budget.json and repair the finding
```

## What this means for the 20 open PRs

The board's only merge gate is `ao/gate-of-record`. It has exactly two producers, and they are mutually
exclusive by declaration:

| producer | state | why it cannot satisfy the requirement |
|---|---|---|
| the ordinary lane path (`verify.sh`, #1439) | present, runs, refuses | "a second producer (this one) may not satisfy it first" — it defers to the venue of record |
| the venue of record (Cloud Build) | runs, red | its image carries no `gh`/`gcloud`, so its poster exits 2 and publishes nothing |

So **no head can ever carry a green**, and every landing must go through the admin bypass
(`enforce_admins=false`) — which is the bypass the check `check-branch-protection` was written to
prevent.

## Remedy (bounded, pick one and state it)

1. **Remove the "may not satisfy it first" ordering** when the venue of record **cannot** publish — i.e.
   refuse only when the venue of record's own verdict is *readable and red*; a venue that cannot post
   is the `CANNOT-ASSESS` case already named in the same script, and `CANNOT-ASSESS` must not silently
   become "therefore nobody may".
2. **Give the venue of record the means to publish** (a `GH_TOKEN`/`gcloud`-free poster, or a token
   scoped to commit statuses in the runner) — #1361/#1350's territory.
3. **Fix the venue-dependent `--detail` arm** so it asserts the cap in the venue it runs in (#1419's
   file), and let the live-dependent skip entry (#1410) honour a `CANNOT-ASSESS` venue rather than
   treating the venue's inability as the check's finding.

## Refs

* #1382 — the ordinary-lane-path producer gap (PR #1439 landed the producer; this is the ordering
  defect its own refusal names).
* #1460 — the other half of the same read-back (`live_producer_state`'s 20-commit recency window).
* #1361 / #1350 — the venue shape that makes the venue of record unable to publish.
* #1419 / #1410 — the venue-dependent detail arm and the live-dependent skip kind that cascades from it.

`Verify:` on a commit that is a PR head, `bash scripts/verify.sh verify` in a lane that passes all
checks must either publish `ao/gate-of-record` or name a remedy that can.

items.title: cloudbuild(owner): disable the three ENABLED control-plane triggers, then delete them after the 7-day hold
items.body:
Parent: #1295

## Model tier

L0/L1 rating: **L0** — backfilled default; re-assess when picked up.

## Root cause

RCA required — Step 1: determine why this issue predates the lifecycle-contract convention (created before the #1533 templates landed) and whether the root cause is otherwise already known from the original body below.

## Escalation

Attempt at L0. Tiers: L0 = Claude Haiku / DeepSeek V4 Flash -> L1 = Claude Sonnet / DeepSeek V4 Pro -> L2 = Claude Opus.
- Max attempts: **N = 3**.
- If blocked after 3 attempts, comment on this issue with the exact failure and label `escalate:L1`, then stop. Never silent abandonment.

## Lifecycle contract (no lingering)

- This issue is closed ONLY via a merged PR whose body contains `Closes #<n>` and evidence: the acceptance command output pasted, plus the negative-control output.
- Picking this issue up = owning it to closure. Do not stop at a partial state or move to another issue. Blockers are part of the task: unblock them (file the blocker as a child issue with `Parent: #1510` if it is a separate lane, fix it, then continue).
- Before the PR is opened: `make verify` green on the branch; no orphan worktrees, no stale branches, no leftover temp files.
- After merge: delete the branch, remove the worktree, confirm the issue auto-closed, post a final comment with the merged PR link and the evidence summary.
- Escalation is the only sanctioned way to hand off; it is a comment + label on THIS issue, never silent abandonment.

## Original

## Measured (2026-09-19, read-only)

`gcloud builds triggers list --project=purebliss-ghl --format=json` — the triggers for this repository, and what each declaration says:

| live trigger | live state | declaration | declared state |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control-plane-verify` | **ENABLED** (no `disabled` field; `_ENABLE_VERIFY="true"`) | `infra/cloudbuild/verify-trigger.yaml` | `disabled: true`, `_ENABLE_VERIFY: "false"` |
| `control-plane-web-image` | **ENABLED** | `infra/cloudbuild/web-image-trigger.yaml` | `disabled: true` |
| `control-plane-apply` | **ENABLED** (`_ENABLE_APPLY="true"`) | `infra/cloudbuild/apply-trigger.yaml` | `disabled: true`, `_ENABLE_APPLY: "false"` |

Cloud Build omits `disabled` entirely when a trigger is on — the same capture carries `disabled: true` on two unrelated triggers, so the absence is a real reading.

The declarations are correct; the live project is not. Until #1415 nothing compared the two sides, so `scripts/check-cloudbuild.sh` was green on a project running all three. It now compares them against the recorded inventory `infra/cloudbuild/live-triggers.json` and reports these three as **baselined disagreements tracked by this issue** (`infra/cloudbuild/live-baseline.txt`).

## Do (owner — every command mutates the live project)

```bash
# 1. Bring the three live triggers in line with what the repo declares:
gcloud builds triggers update control-plane-verify    --region=us-central1 --disabled
gcloud builds triggers update control-plane-web-image --region=us-central1 --disabled
gcloud builds triggers update control-plane-apply     --region=us-central1 --disabled

# 2. AFTER the declarations have held for 7 days — delete them:
gcloud builds triggers delete control-plane-verify    --region=us-central1 --quiet
gcloud builds triggers delete control-plane-web-image --region=us-central1 --quiet
gcloud builds triggers delete control-plane-apply     --region=us-central1 --quiet

# 3. Delete the Secret Manager token the removed poster step read:
gcloud secrets delete ao-gate-status-token --quiet

# 4. Re-record the inventory — this turns the baseline rows STALE:
gcloud builds triggers list --project=purebliss-ghl --format=json > infra/cloudbuild/live-triggers.json
```

Then delete the three rows from `infra/cloudbuild/live-baseline.txt`. Run (4) **after** (1) or (2): while the three live triggers still read ENABLED the rows are live and `make verify` is green; the moment they are disabled or deleted, the gate **fails naming them** until the rows are removed, so this issue cannot be closed while the drift is live and the rows cannot outlive it.

## Precondition and why no lane can do it

Step 2 carries #1415's own 7-day hold, and every step is a live mutation, so no lane may run any of it. #1415 landed the declaration half plus the proof of drift; this issue is the residual owner work.

Refs #1415
Refs #1350
Refs #1389

items.title: gate-status: the live producer read-back uses a 20-commit recency window, so a healthy repo reds as 'the producer is genuinely not producing'
items.body:
## The red

`scripts/check-gate-status.sh::live_producer_state()` decides `enabled`/`disabled` by looking back
`${AO_GATE_STATUS_WINDOW:-20}` **default-branch commits** for the required context
`ao/gate-of-record`, probing `git rev-parse HEAD` first. When nothing is observed it returns
`disabled gh-status-absent-in-last-20-commits`, and the caller reports:

```
check-gate-status: FAIL REQUIRED-BUT-UNOBSERVED — ... the producer is genuinely not producing,
so the requirement is not satisfiable, which is never a pass
```

## Why that is wrong on this repository (measured 2026-09-19)

The producer **is** producing; the observations have merely aged out of a 20-commit recency window,
because `master` lands heavily. Measured at `origin/master = d6b3eb8d`:

```
$ gh api "repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits?per_page=20" --jq '.[].sha' | while read c; do
    s=$(gh api "repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits/$c/statuses" --jq '[.[].context]|join(",")'); \
    case "$s" in *"ao/gate-of-record"*) echo "  OBSERVED on $c";; esac; done
(scanned the 20 most recent)   -> nothing

$ ...(same, per_page=50)...
  OBSERVED on 83ff32dbcf40fe42c4ccbdcb3a41e5b4a48944f6
  OBSERVED on 0dbb0e6819979e329b615292adaa74ceecded5ee
```

and with the check's own seam widened the same pristine tree passes:

```
$ AO_GATE_STATUS_WINDOW=50 bash scripts/check-gate-status.sh
  OK  the REQUIRED context 'ao/gate-of-record' has a producer on the path that evaluates a pull request,
      and the LIVE producer state is 'gh-status-observed' — the context IS being produced
check-gate-status: OK — the mapping is exhaustive and provoked, ...
```

## Blast radius — this is a board-wide serialization point

* `check-gate-status` reds `REQUIRED-BUT-UNOBSERVED`; `check-branch-protection` reds too, because it
  delegates through `scripts/check-gate-status.sh --producer-probe`.
* Both red on a **pristine detached `origin/master` worktree**. `verify` is never attributable
  (`governance/landing/attribution.py`), so **any** red refuses **every** landing: 20 open PRs read
  `mergeable_state=blocked` for this reason.
* The failure message actively misattributes the cause: it says the producer "is genuinely not
  producing", which the live read-back contradicts.

## Proposed fix (minimal -> better)

1. **Minimal:** widen the default window, or make it configurable in `scripts/skip-budget.json`-adjacent
   policy rather than a bare env var, so the default reflects a repository that lands dozens of commits
   a day.
2. **Better:** bound the search by **age** (e.g. "observed within N days") or by observation rather than a
   fixed commit count; or treat "observed anywhere on the default branch's history" as sufficient, since
   what the check means to ask is "is the producer producing?", not "did it produce in the last 20 commits?".
3. **Also:** the refusal text should distinguish "no producer exists" from "no *recent* observation",
   because the two need different remedies and the current wording sends a reader to the wrong one
   (it is the wording that makes this look like a producer gap rather than a window).

## Refs

* #1382 — the ordinary-lane-path producer gap (a *different* defect; PR #1439 is the fix). This issue is
  the **live read-back half** the same check owns.
* #1394 — the earlier venue/declared-vs-live correction in this same function.
* #1361 — the venue-shape epic.

`Verify:` `AO_GATE_STATUS_WINDOW=20 bash scripts/check-gate-status.sh` on a pristine detached
`origin/master` worktree must be rc 0 once the observation is reachable within its declared bound.

items.title: gate: check-runtime-liveness is red only because two other checks leak beats into the repo — an order-dependent gate
items.body:
Parent: #1254

## Measured (2026-09-19, from the wave's train fold)

`check-runtime-liveness.sh` (auto-discovered into `make verify`, #1376) is **red only when
#1412 and #1413 are BOTH present** — a gate whose verdict is a function of which checks ran
before it.

The chain, measured in a detached `origin/master` worktree with the two PR heads merged:

1. #1412 adds `terminal.beat_runtime`, which writes `<beats.ROOT>/.fleet/runtime-beats/<id>.json`,
   and `run_once` now beats **before** the spawn-envelope refusal.
2. `fleet/tests/conftest.py` redirects `beats.ROOT`, so pytest is isolated — but **two CHECK
   SCRIPTS drive `run_once` in the real repo**: `scripts/check-fleet-runner-preflight.sh` and
   `scripts/check-spawn-envelope.sh` (the latter added by #1413). Each leaks a beat.
3. `runtime-liveness` then judges those leaked beats against the real clock and reports them
   stale.

```
clean tree + liveness alone      -> rc 0   (no-beats-yet, the check is inert)
check-fleet-runner-preflight.sh  -> leaks
then check-runtime-liveness.sh   -> rc 1   6 x "runtime-stale:<id> - no beat has ever been recorded"
```

`runtime-liveness` is discovered (not denylisted) and discovered checks are appended **after** the
explicit `runner-preflight` entry, so on the folded tree the gate of record reds — measured as the
only remaining refusal on the `master+#1412+#1413` tree after #1412's own lint and channel defects
were fixed.

## Why this is a real defect and not a fixture nuisance

A gate whose result depends on **what ran before it** is the `check-docs.sh find .` class
(#764): it reads runtime state no commit records, so the same tree passes or fails depending on
the order of the composite. It also means the two checks cannot both be green with the beat
producer present, i.e. #1412's own acceptance ("`check-runtime-liveness.sh` judges 7 fresh beats")
is unreachable in the composite it is gated by.

## Remedy (bounded; pick one and state it)

1. **Fixture-side (preferred):** every check script that drives the real spawn path redirects
   `beats.ROOT` to its own scratch, exactly as `fleet/tests/conftest.py` already does — the same
   `AO_FLEET_DIR`-style seam. Name the files this touches; `scripts/check-spawn-envelope.sh` is
   one of them.
2. **Producer-side:** `beats.ROOT` is derived from `fleet/runtime.py::FLEET_DIR` / `AO_FLEET_DIR`
   (#360) so a check that sets the fleet dir cannot leak into the repo's `.fleet/`.
3. **Order-independence as a property:** whatever the fix, the check must be green in the
   composite regardless of which checks ran before it, and a control must provoke the leak.

## Acceptance

- On a tree carrying both #1412 and #1413, `check-fleet-runner-preflight.sh`,
  `check-spawn-envelope.sh` and then `check-runtime-liveness.sh` are **all rc 0**, in that order
  and in any order.
- A control provokes the leak (a fixture that writes a beat into the repo's `.fleet/` makes
  `runtime-liveness` red by name), so the fix cannot regress silently.
- `git status` is clean after the two check scripts run against a clean tree.

## Verify

```
bash scripts/check-fleet-runner-preflight.sh
bash scripts/check-spawn-envelope.sh
bash scripts/check-runtime-liveness.sh
git status --porcelain
```

#1201 is the 2026-09-17 deep code review register (overlap / redundant / dead code). Its definition of
done — quoted verbatim from #1201's body — is:

> Success = every confirmed finding is either fixed by a child lane or explicitly closed as intentional.

The **first half is satisfied**: every child lane is CLOSED. Re-verified this session with
`gh issue list --repo kushin77/agent-orchestrator --state all --limit 1000 --json number,state,title,body`
and filtering for references to #1201 → #1149, #1202, #1203, #1204, #1205, #1206, #1207, #1208, #1229,
#1257, #1262, #1292, all `CLOSED`.

The **second half is not**. #1201's own text names a residual set that no child lane fixed and that was
never explicitly closed as intentional — and it was filed **nowhere**. Closing #1201 today would delete the
only record of it. This issue is that record, so #1201 can close without losing the finding.

**Measured 2026-09-19** against `origin/master` = `d6b3eb8d11a1a1072fda45d7f1b3bce970494f30` (detached
worktree). Every count below comes from the command shown next to it. Where the register's 2026-09-17
number could not be reproduced, the row says `CANNOT-ASSESS` and why — the register gave no definitions, and
copying its numbers on faith would be worse than admitting the gap.

## Residual findings

- [ ] **`~10 JSON-Schema-subset validators (already drifted)`** — `CANNOT-ASSESS` the count: no definition
  or command is given, and no grep cleanly separates *hand-rolled subset* validators from modules that
  merely mention the keywords (`grep -rlE '"required"|.required.' --include=*.py .` → 413 files, 284
  non-test — far too loose to claim equivalence). Named candidates found:
  `scripts/lib/validate-attestation.py:160 _validate_with_jsonschema`,
  `registry/prompts/registry.py:76 validate_with_schema`,
  `registry/packs/registry.py:80 _schema_valid_errors`.
- [ ] **`6 board-snapshot loaders`** — measured **3** under an explicit definition
  (`grep -rnE 'def _?load_snapshot' --include=*.py .`): `governance/lessons/checker.py:346`,
  `governance/dispatch/cli.py:74`, `governance/conformance/checker.py:170`. A looser
  `grep -rhE 'def [a-z_]*load[a-z_]*snapshot'` gives 4. `CANNOT-ASSESS` the register's 6.
- [ ] **`3 claim-ledger readers`** — measured **5 files / 11 occurrences**
  (`grep -rl 'read_claims' --include=*.py .`): `governance/ticket/sources.py:200` (the definition),
  `governance/ticket/builder.py`, `fleet/state.py`, `fleet/report.py`,
  `governance/ticket/tests/test_ticket_sources.py`.
- [ ] **`SME reviewer doctrine twice`** — `CANNOT-ASSESS`: `guardrails/instructions/` (where the register
  implies it lives) **does not exist** in this tree — `grep -rln 'SME' guardrails/instructions/` returns
  empty. The doctrine home now is `docs/SME-ROUTING.md`. No duplicate was located; if one exists it is
  described somewhere this issue could not find.
- [ ] **`the LOW/MED/HIGH/MAX tier tuple re-declared 5×`** — **reproduced exactly, 5**
  (`grep -rnE '^(TIERS|MODEL_TIERS|VALID_TIERS)\s*[:=]' --include=*.py .`):
  `portal/server/chat.py:74`, `integrations/hermes/mapping.py:67`, `identity/onboarding/model.py:85`,
  `governance/authority/model.py:89`, `gateway/providers/contract.py:51`. It is worse than duplicated —
  it is **divergent**: `registry/chat/labels.py:43` and `fleet/channel.py:166` declare a *different*
  tuple, `("flash", "pro", "auditor")`.
- [ ] **`control model 3×`, `budget model 4×`** — `CANNOT-ASSESS` the register's counts (no definition).
  The duplication is still plainly visible: 12 `*Budget`/`*Control` classes across
  `telemetry/role_health.py`, `telemetry/metering/budget.py`, `telemetry/chat/budget_guard.py` and
  `telemetry/budgets/{budget,killswitch,exporter}.py`
  (`grep -rnE '^class [A-Za-z]*Budget|^class [A-Za-z]*Control' --include=*.py .`).
- [ ] **`scripts/` copy-paste boilerplate** — register: root-detection 144/145, `contains()` ×10,
  `ok/bad` ×12, python3 guard ×106. Re-measured, each by its own command, the idiom has **grown**:
  root-detection one-liner `root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"` in **204 of 204**
  `scripts/*.sh` (`grep -rl 'dirname' --include=*.sh scripts/ | wc -l` → 204; `ls scripts/*.sh | wc -l`
  → 204); `contains()` defs **19** (`grep -rhE '^contains\(\)' --include=*.sh scripts/`);
  `ok()`/`bad()` defs **50** (`grep -rhE '^(ok|bad)\(\)' --include=*.sh scripts/`); python3 guard

  (`ls scripts/check-*-coverage.sh`): `check-control-coverage.sh`, `check-gate-coverage.sh`,
  `check-spine-coverage.sh`.
- [ ] **The root cause that hides all the rest** — the register's own words: "`make verify` runs no test in
  the three biggest pillars … and no Python linter is wired at all". The exception list has grown, not
  shrunk: `grep -vcE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' scripts/gate-coverage-baseline.txt` → **51** non-comment rows,
  and `awk '{print $3}' scripts/gate-coverage-baseline.txt | sort | uniq -c` → **51 swept-only** (the
  register measured 18). 100% of the baseline is `swept-only`. Until this row is addressed the other rows
  stay invisible to the gate.

## What done looks like

Each row above is either fixed by its own child lane carrying `Verify:` evidence, or closed `not_planned`
with the reason recorded **in this issue**. #1201's own acceptance criteria continue to apply:
`make verify` is green at each merge.
