items.title: gate: the spawn admission's allowlist reads channel.RUNTIME_IDS, which the runtimes registry no longer exports (1413 x 1412 red together)
items.body:
Parent: #1411 (merge train — this is the class the train attributes)

## Measured — two lanes green alone, red together

`bash scripts/check-spawn-envelope.sh` on each tree (the gate that owns the
fleet-path equality proof):

| tree                          | rc |
|-------------------------------|----|
| `origin/master` alone         | 0  |
| `master` + `origin/issue-1413`| 0  (132 tests in `governance/spawn/tests`) |
| `master` + `origin/issue-1412`| 0  |
| `master` + `1413` + `1412`    | **1** |
| a nine-lane fold containing both | **1** (same FAILs) |

On the folded tree the gate reports:

```
FAIL  governance/spawn/tests does not pass (it carries the fleet-path equality proof)
FAIL  the local spawn path ADMITS against its own root's board (rc 0) — rc=1
  File ".../governance/spawn/admission.py", line 263, in _allowlists
    return tuple(channel.RUNTIME_IDS), tables
AttributeError: module 'channel' has no attribute 'RUNTIME_IDS'
```

## Cause

* **#1412** ("runtimes: one registry, the notices module reads it") removed the
  literal seven-tuple `fleet/channel.py::RUNTIME_IDS` and replaced it with the
  lazy, cached accessor `fleet/channel.py::runtime_ids()` — which reads the ONE
  authority, `fleet/runtimes.yaml`, through `fleet/runtimes.py::ids()`. It
  migrated every caller it could see.
* **#1413** (spawn admission) added the only **new** caller of that symbol:
  `governance/spawn/admission.py::_allowlists()` returns
  `tuple(channel.RUNTIME_IDS), tables`.

Each lane's own gate reads a tree containing only its own half, so neither could
observe it. Nothing here is a regression in either lane in isolation: the
composition is what is red.

## Do

`_allowlists()` reads the accessor the registry now offers —
`channel.runtime_ids()` — instead of the retired module-level constant. The fix
belongs where the stale symbol is READ (`governance/spawn/admission.py`), not by
re-exporting a second copy of the vocabulary in `fleet/channel.py`: #1412's own
issue text says "one registry, the notices module reads it", and re-exporting
the literal would re-create exactly the second list #1412 deleted.

A registry that cannot be read must stay a **named refusal**, never a traceback:
`fleet/runtimes.py` refuses with `RegistryRefused` rather than returning an empty
vocabulary, and the admission judge converts that to `AdmissionUnavailable`, so
the allowlist judge refuses by NAME.

## Acceptance

* `bash scripts/check-spawn-envelope.sh` rc 0 on a tree carrying **both** lanes.
* `python3 -m pytest -q governance/spawn/tests` rc 0, same count as the
  single-lane run (132).
* Load-bearing control: with the registry's id list made empty in a scratch
  copy, the allowlist judge refuses by name — no traceback.
* `bash scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` and `bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh`
  rc 0.

Refs #1412
Refs #1413

items.title: fix(cron): the managed PATH line is corrupted by its own trailing marker — the runner rung never starts
items.body:
Parent: #1370
Refs #1416

## Measured

`fleet/cron.py` renders the AO_FLEET_CRON_PATH line as ONE line:

```
PATH=<value> # ao-fleet-path
```

A user crontab's environment-setting line has **no comment syntax**: cron takes the
whole remainder after `=` as the value. What lands is therefore

```
PATH=<value> # ao-fleet-path
```

whose LAST `:`-element is `<last-dir> # ao-fleet-path` — never a directory. So the
last directory in the declared value is silently dropped from cron's PATH.

Measured on the shared-services pair (`dev-elevatediq`, 192.168.168.42) after running
#1416's declared owner step with the tree at `origin/master` (`d6b3eb8`, `b8ad98f` =
#1370 present), with the declared value
`$HOME/ao-verify-venv/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:/snap/bin:/usr/bin` — so the corrupted
element was `/usr/bin`, and every binary that lives only there left cron's PATH:

* **the runner rung never started.** `.fleet/runner.log` gained
  `flock: failed to execute env: Permission denied` (rc 69) and
  `.fleet/runner/ledger.jsonl` gained no `cycle-start` — the role-inline
  `env AO_RUNNER_HOST_ROLE=primary` prefix that #1370's role-gating renders needs
  `/usr/bin/env`.
* **`fleet/watchdog.py` refused every pass**: `source: CANNOT-ASSESS — cannot read
  the local HEAD, origin/master, fleet/watchdog.py in the working tree,
  origin/master:fleet/watchdog.py; refusing the pass rather than running code whose
  currency cannot be vouched for`. `_git_read` shells out to `git` **by name**, and
  `/usr/bin/git` was one of the lost binaries. A 2-minute rung that refuses every
  pass is a fleet with no keeper.

Reproduced directly (no crontab involved):

```
$ env -i "PATH=<value> # ao-fleet-path" bash -c 'command -v git || echo (NOT FOUND)'
env: 'bash': No such file or directory
$ env -i "PATH=<value>"                bash -c 'command -v git'
/usr/bin/git
$ env -i "PATH=<value> # ao-fleet-path" sh -c '/usr/bin/flock -n -E 99 /tmp/x.lock env FOO=bar /bin/echo OK'
flock: failed to execute env: Permission denied     # rc 69
```

A PATH line that drops a directory is worse than no PATH line: it is a managed line
that cannot do its job, and its failure is read as a fault of whatever needed the
lost binary.

## Why the gate could not catch it

`fleet/tests/test_cron_interp.py:55` pinned the shipped string verbatim
(`assert path_lines[0] == "PATH=/x/venv/bin:/snap/bin:/usr/bin # ao-fleet-path"`), so
the test asserted the defect as the contract. It is a live suite (`make tests` /
`scripts/run-pytest-suites.sh`), so the gate was green **because** the expectation was
the bug.

## Fix

The marker moves to a line of its own, directly above the assignment:

```
# ao-fleet-path
PATH=<value>
```

Still exactly ONE `PATH=` line, and its value is exactly the declared value.
`_path_block_indices` keeps the pair together (the assignment has no marker of its
own, so it is identified by position; a `PATH=` line that does not follow our marker
is left alone as foreign). `installed_lines`/`remove_lines` learn the same adjacency,
so `status` prints the line that actually sets the PATH and `uninstall` does not leave
an export behind. `render` now prints the block too — it is documented as what
`install` would write and previously omitted the one line the operator looks for.

The pinned expectations now assert cron's semantics (value == declared value, no `#`
in it), plus two new directions: the old trailing-comment form is REFRESHED (not
coexisting) on install, and unsetting the variable removes the whole block.

## Acceptance

* `python3 -m pytest -q fleet/tests/test_cron_interp.py` green (15 tests).
* `bash scripts/check-fleet-jobs.sh` rc 0; `bash scripts/check-pr-runner.sh` rc 0.
* A crontab installed from the fixed render executes a managed rung that needs
  `env`/`git` by name — the control #1416 measures on the pair.

items.title: [bug] close --lane can never settle a record whose worktree is a dangling leftover: worktree_present() asks Path.exists(), so 'not a working tree' withholds lane-archived
items.body:
## GOAL

Let `close --lane` reach its own step 5 (`lane-archived`) for a lane whose worktree path is a
**dangling directory left by an earlier reclaim** — measured on 8 records that are otherwise fully
evidenced (PR merged, trailer clean, issue closed, branch gone). Today they are permanently
`closeout-blocked:worktree-removed`, so a settled lane can never reach its terminal state.

## Observed

`governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --lane <id> --apply`, run by a peer lane on 2026-09-19 and
recorded in `.fleet/lifecycle/ledger.jsonl` (`action=close-lane`):

```
lane close-out 1d384cc614e9 (#1212, issue-1212, apply): NOT-OK
  skipped    pr-merged: PR #1290 merged as 1de476faf5a0, trailer clean
  skipped    issue-closed: #1212 is closed
  withheld   branch-reaped: withheld: worktree-removed is blocked
  blocked    worktree-removed: RuntimeError: git worktree remove /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-1212-1d384cc6: fatal: '/home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-1212-1d384cc6' is not a working tree
  withheld   lane-archived: withheld: worktree-removed is blocked
  BLOCKED    closeout-blocked:worktree-removed
```

The same shape, same code, same cause, for 8 records measured the same day:

`1d384cc614e9` #1212 · `4534d5653d47` #1146 · `4f5a8d7bcd23` #1077 · `954b2f045381` #723 ·
`98174c865a99` #1247 · `b9cfeb6ab0a2` #796 · `b9e078dcb0ac` #1203 · `c56b6629af0f` #1298

All eight were counted `orphan-issue-lane` by `governance/reconcile/orphans.py` — i.e. the pile that
reds `scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh` — because the one verb whose remedy the walk prescribes
(`close --lane <id> --apply`) cannot finish them.

## Expected

Step 5 exists to archive the record; step 4's subject is *removing a worktree*. When git itself
reports there is no working tree at that path, there is nothing to remove and nothing left to
evidence — the step is satisfied (`skipped`/`performed`) and the archive proceeds. The record's own
state is fully evidenced at that point: `pr-merged` clean, `issue-closed`, branch gone.

## Cause

`governance/lifecycle/cli.py` (measured at `origin/master = d6b3eb8d`):

```python
class RepoLaneOps:
    def worktree_present(self, path: str) -> bool:
        return bool(path) and Path(path).exists()
```

`Path.exists()` is true for a directory that is **not** a registered git worktree — exactly what
`prune-worktrees.sh` / the orphan walk leave behind when they reclaim a worktree (`git worktree
remove` deletes `.git/worktrees/<name>` and the admin entry, and the directory can survive:
measured, `governance/reconcile/orphans.py` sees them as *unregistered* and does not count them as
`orphan-worktree` at all). So the verb and the walk disagree about what "present" means:

- `orphans.py`: registration — `entry.path in lane_worktrees` from `git worktree list`;
- `cli.py`: existence — `Path(path).exists()`.

The `_withhold_rest(result, STEP_WORKTREE_REMOVED)` then withholds `STEP_LANE_ARCHIVED`, so a
name-only leftover wedges the terminal verb.

## Reproduction command

```bash
# a lane record whose worktree directory exists but is not a registered worktree
AO_LIFECYCLE_ROOT=/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator PYTHONPATH=<a checkout at origin/master> \
  python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --lane 1d384cc614e9 --apply
# -> blocked worktree-removed: RuntimeError ... fatal: ... is not a working tree
#    withheld lane-archived: withheld: worktree-removed is blocked
```

(`PYTHONPATH` is needed today only because of #1438; with that fixed the override alone is enough.)

## Remedy

Make the two modules agree on "present". Either consult registration —

```python
def worktree_present(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """A worktree is PRESENT when git knows it as one, not when a directory survives."""
    if not path:
        return False
    result = self._git("worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
    return any(line == f"worktree {path}" for line in result.stdout.splitlines())
```

— or treat `is not a working tree` from `git worktree remove` as "already gone" rather than a
failure. The first is preferred: it makes the verb's notion of a worktree the same one
`governance/reconcile/orphans.py` and `governance/isolation/worktree.py` already use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `close --lane <id> --apply` on a record whose worktree path is an unregistered leftover
      reaches `performed lane-archived` and writes `.fleet/lifecycle/lanes/<id>.json`.
- [ ] A record whose worktree **is** a registered worktree holding the lane's uncommitted work still
      blocks (`closeout-blocked:worktree-removed`) — the safety half is unchanged.
- [ ] `scripts/check-lifecycle-closeout.sh` and the lifecycle suite are unchanged on the default
      path (the probe adds no new verdict).
- [ ] clock (#506, RCA-0008) — time-pinned fixture introduced? **no**; the change adds no date and
      no clock-derived evaluation bucket.

## Evidence

To be appended when the fix lands.

---

**Severity:** medium — it does not break a green path, it wedges the terminal verb on artifacts the
fleet recreates daily; each occurrence is a permanent `orphan-issue-lane` and a named item in the
`orphan` budget that blocks every lane's landing.

**Role (executor):** subagent
**Epic:** none — no open `type:epic` on the board (measured).
**Pillar:** autonomous-ops
**Lane:** lifecycle
**Model tier (FinOps):** flash — the two implementations are quoted, the disagreement is named, the
remedy is one predicate.
**Thinking effort:** low
**Posture (delivery):** no-human-needed
**Lifecycle:** operate
**Verify command:** `bash scripts/check-lifecycle-closeout.sh` + the reproduction above
**Chain markers:** Root=none
**Blocked-by:** none
**Relates-to:** #1437 (found it while clearing the orphan budget), #1438 (the other defect in the
same verb)

items.title: lifecycle close --lane: a dangling worktree directory with no admin entry wedges the lane permanently
items.body:
Parent: #1436

## Measured (2026-09-19, `origin/master` `d6b3eb8d`, doing #1436's own remedy)

`governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --lane <id> --apply` is the terminal verb the
orphan walk names for `orphan-issue-lane` (#1301), and on this box it **wedges
permanently** for 7 of the 32 records. Each one is blocked on
`worktree-removed`, and the block is not about the lane's work:

```
BLOCKED lane 1d384cc614e9 #1212 issue-1212
     skipped    pr-merged: PR #1290 merged as 1de476faf5a0, trailer clean
     skipped    issue-closed: #1212 is closed
     withheld   branch-reaped: withheld: worktree-removed is blocked
     blocked    worktree-removed: RuntimeError: git worktree remove /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-1212-1d384cc6:
                fatal: '/home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-1212-1d384cc6' is not a working tree
     withheld   lane-archived: withheld: worktree-removed is blocked
```

Same for #1146, #1203, #1247, #723, #1077, #1298. The cause is the two halves of
"is the worktree there?" disagreeing:

- `RepoLaneOps.worktree_present` is `Path(path).exists()` — the **directory**;
- `git worktree remove` needs the **git admin entry** under `.git/worktrees/`.

Another live lane's reaper pruned the admin entries while leaving the
directories dangling (the same shape as #786/#789: *"admin dir gone, absent from
`git worktree list`, directory left dangling"*). So the dry run says
`would remove`, and the apply run refuses — and because `lane-archived` is
*withheld* behind it, `forget_lane` never runs and the record can never be
retired. 7 lanes are stuck this way; the count is live and will grow.

Nothing of the lane's is at risk in these cases: step 4 reads `foreign_dirt`
**before** deciding, and in all 7 it was empty (the dry run's own
`would remove …` is that measurement). A dangling directory with no admin entry
holds no lane-authored work.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed here

The remedy is a `governance/lifecycle` change (a different lane's ownership): a
`worktree-remove` refusal that git itself reports as *"is not a working tree"* is
**already-torn-down**, and should be `skipped` with the dangling path named —
never `blocked`, which is what makes the wedge permanent. That is a behaviour
change to a landed close-out contract (rule 16) and is not mine to absorb while
clearing a different issue.

## Acceptance

- `close --lane --apply` reaches `lane-archived` for a lane whose worktree's
  admin entry is already gone while its directory remains: the step is
  `skipped`/already-torn-down and names the dangling path.
- The refusal is still refused when the *lane's own* work is at risk (foreign
  dirt present, or a branch tip that is not content-landed) — both negatives
  provoked, not assumed.
- The 7 records measured here reach terminal, and
  `python3 governance/reconcile/cli.py sweep --orphans --json` reports
  `orphan-issue-lane` at or below the declared budget without a budget edit.

## Verify

```
python3 governance/reconcile/cli.py sweep --orphans --json
python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --lane 1d384cc614e9 --apply --json
```

items.title: orphan-walk: the reclaim proof answers 'would this lose work?', not 'is this in use?'
items.body:
Parent: #1436

## Measured (2026-09-19, `origin/master` `d6b3eb8d`, doing #1436's own remedy)

`sweep --orphans --apply` reclaimed 17 artifacts on this box and **had to be
stopped from reclaiming two more**. The reclaim proof is
`isolation.worktree.content_landed(HEAD)` and `not foreign_uncommitted(path)`
(#1265 / #1335). Both are true of a worktree **a live process is sitting in**:
one was a *Claude agent session's* worktree and one was the working directory of
a **VS Code terminal** — and the second was a venue another lane had recorded:

```
$ cat /tmp/ao-orch/master-venue.txt
/home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-master-1789820219
```

so a lane that does `V=$(cat /tmp/ao-orch/master-venue.txt); cd $V; python3 $V/governance/reconcile/cli.py …`
had its venue deleted by the walk. Reclaimed it was, by the walk's own rule —
the walk is not wrong about *the work*, it has no signal about *use*.

The liveness signals are unequal, and that is the useful part:

| signal | verdict on the two |
|---|---|
| `content_landed(HEAD)` + no foreign dirt | both **reclaimable** (wrong) |
| `/proc/<pid>/cwd` == the path | both **live** — but this weakened: a holder that `cd`s away between the measure and the apply makes it read "clear", and a removed directory reads `/path (deleted)` and stops matching |
| git's own worktree lock | **held** — `fatal: cannot remove a locked working tree, lock reason: claude agent …` refused one of the two |

So git's lock is the *stronger* protection and it saved the agent's tree; the
plain terminal was saved by nothing but a pre-flight check written for this
issue. Separately, `record_reaped` is written **before** `remove_worktree`
(#1265, deliberate), so a removal that then fails leaves a ledger entry claiming
a reap that did not happen — true about the content, false about the removal.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed here

The fix is an ownership question, not a liveness patch: a worktree a lane or an
operator *depends on* should be named by something the walk can read (a lane
record, a declared venue), so "no lane record names it" stops being the same
claim as "nobody needs it". Narrower candidates were measured and are weaker:

- refusing when a live `/proc` cwd matches (weaker than git's lock — see above);
- refusing when git reports a lock (misses every un-locked venue, including the
  one that was deleted).

Changing what the walk may reclaim is a reviewed edit to a landed contract
(#1265/#1335), so it belongs to the owner of the rule, with the measurement in
front of them — not to a lane trying to make its own gate green.

## Acceptance

- The reclaim rule has an *ownership* signal, not only a content one, and
  `scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh` §3 proves it with a live-holder fixture.
- The negative is proven too: an artifact whose content is landed, which no lane
  names, and which nothing is using is **still** reclaimed.
- `record_reaped` and the removal cannot disagree: either the reap is recorded
  after a removal that happened, or a failed removal is not recorded as a reap.

## Verify

```
python3 governance/reconcile/cli.py sweep --orphans --json
bash scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh
```

items.title: [bug] AO_LIFECYCLE_ROOT re-points the IMPORTS, not just the state: close --lane cannot run the fixed code against the fleet's .fleet
items.body:
## GOAL

Make `AO_LIFECYCLE_ROOT` deliver what its own docstring promises — **fixed code against the
fleet's state** — so the lane terminal verb (`close --lane`) can actually settle the
`orphan-issue-lane` records the orphan budget is over on. One-line fix; the defect is that the
override is inserted into `sys.path`, so it re-points the *imports* instead of only the *state*.

## Observed

From a lane worktree at `origin/master` (`d6b3eb8d`), pointing the documented seam at the shared
checkout (which holds the fleet's `.fleet/` state):

```console
$ cd /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-master-1789820219
$ AO_LIFECYCLE_ROOT=/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator \
    python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --lane 0066888d9138
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-master-1789820219/governance/lifecycle/cli.py", line 89, in <module>
    from governance.lifecycle import directive, gate, lane_closeout, ledger, live  # noqa: E402
ImportError: cannot import name 'lane_closeout' from 'governance.lifecycle'
  (/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/governance/lifecycle/__init__.py)
```

and without the override, from the same worktree:

```console
$ python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --lane 1d384cc614e9
close: CANNOT-ASSESS — no lane record 1d384cc614e9 under
  /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-master-1789820219/.fleet/lanes
```

Both halves are broken at once: without the override the verb reads the **wrong** `.fleet` (the
worktree's, which has no `lanes/` at all); with the override it reads the right state but imports
the **wrong code**.

## Expected

`governance/lifecycle/cli.py:46-89` — the seam's own docstring states its purpose:

> "The seam exists because the driver has two requirements that a lane worktree cannot satisfy at
> once ... it must run the **fixed** code — and the fix for this class ... is on `master`; and it
> must run against the **fleet's** state — the journals, lane records and ledger the fleet loops
> write in the shared checkout ... Pointing a lane's copy — the one with the fix — at the shared
> checkout's `.fleet` is the alternative to editing the shared checkout, which dozens of lanes are
> using."

So with `AO_LIFECYCLE_ROOT` set, `governance.lifecycle.*` must resolve to **the running file's own
checkout** (the fixed code) while `ROOT` is the **state** root.

## Cause

```python
ROOT = lifecycle_root()
if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))          # <-- the STATE root, at the FRONT of the import path
from governance.lifecycle import directive, gate, lane_closeout, ledger, live  # noqa: E402
```

`sys.path.insert(0, ...)` puts the state root ahead of the running checkout's package, so
`governance.*` resolves to whatever tree the state root happens to hold. The shared checkout is
**not** a stable code baseline by design — it holds whichever branch a lane last left it on
(measured: `issue-708-wire-runaway-guard`, `629f22f5`, which does not contain
`governance/lifecycle/lane_closeout.py` at all).

## Reproduction command

```bash
cd /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-master-1789820219   # any lane worktree at origin/master
AO_LIFECYCLE_ROOT=/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator \
  python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --lane 0066888d9138
# -> ImportError, as pasted above
```

## Why it matters (it is the reason this pile does not shrink)

`governance/reconcile/orphans.py` reports `orphan-issue-lane` for a lane record whose issue is
CLOSED, and prescribes exactly this verb as the remedy
(`governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --lane <lane_id> --apply`). Measured 2026-09-19: **32** such
records, against a declared budget of 25 — the `orphan-budget-exceeded:orphan-issue-lane:32/25`
that reds `scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh` (and therefore `make verify`) for **every landing on
the board**. Every merged lane adds one, and no verb can settle any of them while the shared
checkout is off `master`. The failure is also silent in the wrong direction: the verb exits with an
`ImportError` traceback rather than its declared tri-state CANNOT-ASSESS, so a caller parsing exit
codes sees `rc 1` for what is really "I could not even load my own code".

## Remedy

Insert the **running** root — identically when no override is given, so the change is
semantics-preserving on the default path:

```python
ROOT = lifecycle_root()
local = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]   # the code that is RUNNING
if str(local) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(local))
```

`ROOT` stays the state root for every read/write (`lane_records`, the ledger, git measurements).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] From a lane worktree at `origin/master` with `AO_LIFECYCLE_ROOT=<shared checkout>`,
      `close --lane <id>` reaches `lane_closeout` and prints a stage table (no ImportError).
- [ ] `python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --lane 0066888d9138` (no override, from a worktree
      with no `.fleet/lanes/`) still answers CANNOT-ASSESS naming the path it looked in.
- [ ] The `close --lane` dry-run/`--apply` behaviour and `scripts/check-lifecycle-closeout.sh` are
      unchanged on the default path.
- [ ] clock (#506, RCA-0008) — time-pinned fixture introduced? **no**; the change adds no date and
      no evaluation bucket.

## Evidence

To be appended when the fix lands.

---

**Severity:** high — a governed verb's own documented entry point cannot run against the state it
exists to settle, and the red it prevents blocks every lane's landing.

**Role (executor):** subagent
**Epic:** none — no open `type:epic` on the board (measured).
**Pillar:** autonomous-ops
**Lane:** lifecycle
**Model tier (FinOps):** flash — one-line seam fix with a named file:line and a pre-stated remedy.
**Thinking effort:** low
**Posture (delivery):** no-human-needed
**Lifecycle:** operate
**Verify command:** `bash scripts/check-lifecycle-closeout.sh` + the reproduction above
**Chain markers:** Root=none
**Blocked-by:** none
**Relates-to:** #1437 (the orphan-budget clearance that found it)

items.title: [fleet-task] Clear the two over-budget orphan kinds (orphan-branch 102/95, orphan-issue-lane 32/25) so check-reconcile-orphans is rc 0
items.body:
## GOAL

Clear the **two over-budget orphan kinds** on this box — `orphan-branch` (102/95) and
`orphan-issue-lane` (32/25) — until `bash scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh` exits **rc 0**,
**without discarding, rewriting or deleting a single artifact that holds work**. This red is one
of the two that make `make verify` red on `master`, so it blocks every landing on the board.

## Constraints (non-negotiable)

- `governance/reconcile/orphan-budget.yaml`'s numbers are **not** raised — the file itself says
  "raising a number here is a reviewed edit, and the pile has to shrink, not be re-excused".
- Never delete, force-push, rewrite or `git clean` any branch/worktree; never touch another
  lane's worktree or branch; never `pkill`/`pgrep -f`.
- Reclaim only with evidence (AGENTS.md rule 17): content-landed → reclaim; unlanded → keep and
  report.
- No `make verify` / `scripts/verify.sh` / `make gate` (parks behind the box-wide 4-permit cap).
- No GitHub commit statuses, no merges.

## Measured landscape (BEFORE, 2026-09-19T13:35Z)

```console
$ python3 governance/reconcile/cli.py --root /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator sweep --orphans
orphan-walk (dry-run): orphan-worktree=33, orphan-branch=102, orphan-pr=5, orphan-issue-lane=32, orphan-directive=112
  NOT-OK         orphan-budget-exceeded:orphan-branch:102/95
  NOT-OK         orphan-budget-exceeded:orphan-issue-lane:32/25
```

| kind | measured | budget | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| orphan-worktree | 33 | 55 | within |
| **orphan-branch** | **102** | **95** | **over by 7** |
| orphan-pr | 5 | 20 | within |
| **orphan-issue-lane** | **32** | **25** | **over by 7** |
| orphan-directive | 112 | 115 | within |

Sub-populations measured inside those counts:
`orphan-branch` = 91 `reported` + **11 `would-reclaim`** (content-landed, `RECLAIMABLE`);
`orphan-worktree` = 26 `reported` + 7 `would-reclaim`.

Growth is the fleet's own success: 13 issues closed on 2026-09-19 by a merge train, each leaving
a lane record behind, and the walk counts a lane record whose issue is CLOSED as
`orphan-issue-lane` (`governance/reconcile/orphans.py`).

## What was measured about the remedies (this is the load-bearing part)

1. **`orphan-issue-lane` — the existing verb cannot reach the fleet's state.** The lane's terminal
   verb exists and is evidence-gated (`governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --lane <id> --apply` →
   `lane_closeout.closeout_lane`, archives to `.fleet/lifecycle/lanes/<id>.json`, then
   `forget_lane()`). But `ROOT = lifecycle_root()` resolves to the **code root**, and it inserts
   that root at `sys.path[0]`:

   ```console
   $ AO_LIFECYCLE_ROOT=/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py \
       close --lane 0066888d9138
   ImportError: cannot import name 'lane_closeout' from 'governance.lifecycle'
     (/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/governance/lifecycle/__init__.py)
   ```

   The seam's own docstring says it exists to run **fixed code against the fleet's state**; pointing
   it at the shared checkout also re-points the *imports* at that checkout's tree (which is 3.7h+
   behind and lacks `lane_closeout.py`). Filed separately as a defect.

2. **`orphan-branch` — parking cannot move this number.** The walk's `orphan-branch` set is
   `RepoOrphanOps.local_branches()` = `git for-each-ref refs/heads` — **local** refs only. Pushing a
   branch to `origin` does not remove it from that set, so "park it so it is no longer the only
   copy" cannot bring this gate's count under budget. What *does* remove it is the walk's **own**
   documented reclaim path, which fires only for a **content-landed** branch
   (`content_landed()` → reverse-patch/whole-blob equality against `origin/master`), records the tip
   to `.fleet/reaped-branches.jsonl` **first**, and deletes only then. 11 branches are in that state.

3. **Archiving lane records costs worktree/branch orphans.** Simulated (in-memory, before acting):
   setting aside **all 32** closed-issue records gives `orphan-issue-lane=0` but pushes
   `orphan-branch` 102 → **112** and `orphan-worktree` 33 → 46 — a strict regression. Setting aside
   only the records whose branch is **already gone locally** gives `orphan-issue-lane` 32 → 22 with
   `orphan-branch` unchanged and `orphan-worktree` 33 → 34.

## Method (what this lane will do)

- **orphan-branch**: apply the walk's own evidence-gated reclaim path to **branches only**
  (`record_reaped` + `delete_local_branch`), never to the 7 reclaimable worktrees — removing a
  content-landed-but-live lane's venue buys nothing here (33 ≤ 55) and is the brief's forbidden
  touch.
- **orphan-issue-lane**: archive the settled records (closed issue, lane's branch already gone, no
  live claim) into `.fleet/lanes/archive/` — verified invisible to the walk's non-recursive
  `*.json` glob — with an append-only `.fleet/lanes/archive/LEDGER.jsonl` naming path, issue,
  why-settled and time. Records whose issue is OPEN, or whose worktree/claim is live, are untouched.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bash scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh` exits **rc 0** (its section 4 walks the real tree
      from the shared checkout; `--skip-real-tree` does **not** count).
- [ ] The AFTER walk, from the same command, shows `orphan-branch` ≤ 95 and `orphan-issue-lane` ≤ 25.
- [ ] Every action is named and auditable: reclaimed branch = name + tip SHA recorded in
      `.fleet/reaped-branches.jsonl`; archived record = name + ledger line.
- [ ] No artifact holding unlanded work was deleted, rewritten or force-pushed (each reclaimed
      branch independently shown content-landed against `origin/master`).
- [ ] The residue that stays over budget, if any, is reported by name and number.
- [ ] clock (#506, RCA-0008) — does this work introduce a time-pinned fixture (a literal
      date/day/month)? **no** — no fixture and no code change is planned; the only date-shaped
      inputs are the budget's own `expires: 2026-10-02` and the walk's live clock, both pre-existing.

## Evidence

### BEFORE (this lane, 2026-09-19T13:35:55Z) — the two kinds over budget

```console
$ python3 governance/reconcile/cli.py --root /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator sweep --orphans
orphan-walk (dry-run): orphan-worktree=33, orphan-branch=102, orphan-pr=5, orphan-issue-lane=32, orphan-directive=112
reconcile: NOT-OK — orphan-budget-exceeded:orphan-branch:102/95
reconcile: NOT-OK — orphan-budget-exceeded:orphan-issue-lane:32/25
# WALK-RC=1
```

### What changed, by whom, and with which mechanism

The pile was **not** cleared by this lane alone: a peer lane on **#1436** (the same red, filed
13:33:05Z, two minutes before the measurement above) was clearing it concurrently. Both halves are
attributable from the append-only ledgers:

**(a) the walk's own content-landed reclaim** — `sweep --orphans --apply`, 13:44:26–13:44:29Z,
recorded in `.fleet/reaped-branches.jsonl` (`reason=orphan-walk:content-landed`): **15 branches**
(tips recorded first) + **3 worktrees**. The 11 branches this lane had independently identified as
`would-reclaim` at 13:35 are all in that set, at the same tip SHAs:
`issue-1272 03caf44948d0`, `issue-1275 d6b4edb30f6f`, `issue-1301 0c00083abb1b`,
`issue-1349 80240f8577db`, `issue-1366 8684f1b175b9`, `issue-1370 bd7432294be2`,
`issue-1397 0a4198bbc217`, `issue-1405 0c321e8f52a2`, `issue-803-require-gate-of-record ba27ed9c635b`,
`issue-878-rollback-runbooks 32a887c7149d`, `issue-935-967 f8a704127c56`.

**(b) the lane terminal verb** — `close --lane --apply` by the same lane: **9 lane records archived**
to `.fleet/lifecycle/lanes/` (`0066888d9138 045272b3cd9f 231d92bcb00c 689f23de8321 8e139b7fe866
afe0cfc65f65 d1d3c5998df6 e11626fca4c2 ee363b3da78c`), from `.fleet/lifecycle/ledger.jsonl`
(`action=close-lane`).

**(c) this lane** — the verb provably could not settle 8 further records (the peer's run left them
`closeout-blocked:worktree-removed`, `... is not a working tree`; filed as a defect), so the
fallback below applied. Applied 2026-09-19T13:48:45–13:49:32Z:

- **2 content-landed local branches reclaimed** through the walk's own path (`record_reaped` then
  `delete_local_branch`), tips recorded first: `issue-1265 f6af24ac54b9` (43 of its added lines
  verified present on `origin/master`, 5 paths blob-identical) and `issue-1368 ffc76e43b41f`
  (1 path blob-identical); `content_landed() -> True` for both.
- **8 settled lane records archived** to `.fleet/lanes/archive/`, each with an append-only
  `.fleet/lanes/archive/LEDGER.jsonl` line (path, issue, why-settled, at): `1d384cc614e9` #1212,
  `4534d5653d47` #1146, `4f5a8d7bcd23` #1077, `954b2f045381` #723, `98174c865a99` #1247,
  `b9cfeb6ab0a2` #796, `b9e078dcb0ac` #1203, `c56b6629af0f` #1298. Archived only because the issue is
  CLOSED, the branch no longer exists locally, the worktree is a registered checkout nowhere, and no
  claim is live; each destination was read back before the source was unlinked.

### AFTER (2026-09-19T13:50:18Z) — the same command

```console
$ python3 governance/reconcile/cli.py --root /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator sweep --orphans
orphan-walk (dry-run): orphan-worktree=29, orphan-branch=91, orphan-pr=5, orphan-issue-lane=15, orphan-directive=112
# WALK-RC=0, zero NOT-OK lines
```

| kind | BEFORE | budget | AFTER | headroom |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| orphan-worktree | 33 | 55 | 29 | 26 |
| **orphan-branch** | **102** | 95 | **91** | 4 |
| orphan-pr | 5 | 20 | 5 | 15 |
| **orphan-issue-lane** | **32** | 25 | **15** | 10 |
| orphan-directive | 112 | 115 | 112 | 3 |

### The gate of record (2026-09-19T13:49:51Z, lane worktree at `origin/master` `d6b3eb8d`)

```console
$ bash scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh
== 1. the declared budget ==
  OK    governance/reconcile/orphan-budget.yaml declares every kind and is within its expiry (live orphan-worktree=55,orphan-branch=95,orphan-pr=20,orphan-issue-lane=25,orphan-directive=115)
== 2. the injected port: every finding fires, and the two negatives hold ==
  OK    12 passed in 0.43s
== 3. a real scratch repository ==
  OK    the subagent worktree with no lane record is named orphan-worktree
  OK    ...and survives --apply because its HEAD is NOT content-landed
  OK    the unpushed branch is named orphan-branch with its SHA recorded
  OK    ...and survives --apply
  OK    no reap was recorded for either
  OK    once content-landed the tree is would-reclaim on a dry run
  OK    ...and reclaimed under --apply
  OK    its tip was recorded to .fleet/reaped-branches.jsonl first
  OK    the unpushed branch is STILL there after the second --apply
  OK    above the budget the walk is NOT-OK by name
== 4. the real tree ==
  orphan-walk (dry-run): orphan-worktree=29, orphan-branch=91, orphan-pr=5, orphan-issue-lane=15, orphan-directive=112
  OK    the real tree (/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator) is within governance/reconcile/orphan-budget.yaml
check-reconcile-orphans: OK — every orphan kind is named, reclaimed only with evidence, and the real tree is within budget
# GATE-RC=0
```

### In-tree change

**None — and none was needed.** `git status --porcelain -uall` in the lane worktree is empty: every
artifact this task touched is gitignored runtime state (`.fleet/lanes/`, `.fleet/lifecycle/`,
`.fleet/reaped-branches.jsonl`). Both code defects found live in another lane's file
(`governance/lifecycle/cli.py`, lane `lifecycle`) and are filed, not edited here.

### What this lane deliberately did NOT do, and why

- **Did not raise `orphan-budget.yaml`.** Its own text forbids it ("the pile has to shrink, not be
  re-excused"); the numbers are unchanged.
- **Did not duplicate the peer run.** The 9 records #1436 settled by the verb were left settled; this
  lane archived only the 8 the verb *refused* (measured `closeout-blocked:*`), so the two are
  complementary.
- **Did not remove the 7 reclaimable orphan-worktrees.** `orphan-worktree` (33/55) was never over
  budget, and removing a content-landed-but-live lane's venue buys nothing here. The peer's
  `--apply` run did remove 3, one of which
  (`/home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-master-1789820219`) is a registered worktree again as of 13:52Z.
- **Did not push ("park") a single branch.** The parking premise is *measurably false on this
  walker*: `orphan-branch` is `git for-each-ref refs/heads` — **local** refs — so being on a remote
  does not exempt a branch. Measured on the live box, zero mutation: of 135 local `issue-*`
  branches, **58 are already on `origin` and are still counted** where no lane record, worktree or
  open PR names them. Parking cannot move this number; only the content-landed reclaim can, and it
  did (102 → 91).
- **Did not delete anything that holds work.** Both reclaimed branches were verified content-landed
  line by line, and the walk records each tip before deleting.
- **Did not run `make verify` / `scripts/verify.sh` / `make gate`** (constraint), post commit
  statuses, or merge.

---

**Role (executor):** subagent
**Epic:** none — operator-directed ad-hoc board-clearance; the board carries **no open `type:epic`**
(measured: `gh issue list --state open --label type:epic` → `[]`), and the orphan contract's own
epic (#1301) is closed while the pile it declared is still above budget.
**Pillar:** autonomous-ops
**Lane:** fleet
**Model tier (FinOps):** flash — mechanical, evidence-gated state reclamation with a
pre-measured decision table; no design judgement left to make.
**Thinking effort:** low
**Posture (delivery):** no-human-needed
**Lifecycle:** operate
**Verify command:** `bash scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh`
**Chain markers:** Root=none
**Blocked-by:** none

items.title: reconcile-orphans: master's composite is red — the real tree is above its declared orphan budget
items.body:
Parent: #1268

## Measured (2026-09-19T12:47Z, `origin/master` `d6b3eb8d`, pristine detached worktree)

`make verify` on master is RED on exactly three checks (`rc` read from
`.verify/attestation.json`'s `checks[]`, never from a grepped transcript):

| check | rc |
|---|---|
| `branch-protection` | 1 |
| `gate-status` | 1 |
| `reconcile-orphans` | 1 |

Two of the three are #1382 (nothing produces the REQUIRED `ao/gate-of-record` on the
ordinary lane path, so the required context is unobservable). **This issue is the
third:**

```
check-reconcile-orphans: FAIL (1 control(s) did not hold)
== 4. the real tree ==
  orphan-walk (dry-run): orphan-worktree=25, orphan-branch=102, orphan-pr=0, orphan-issue-lane=32, orphan-directive=112
    NOT-OK orphan-budget-exceeded:orphan-branch:102/95
    NOT-OK orphan-budget-exceeded:orphan-issue-lane:32/25
```

A red composite blocks EVERY landing (the gate of record is never attributable), so
this is a fleet-wide serialization point, not one lane's nuisance.

## What is actually over, re-measured with the walk's own tool

`python3 governance/reconcile/cli.py sweep --orphans --json` (from a worktree at
`origin/master`):

```
counts: orphan-worktree=56, orphan-branch=114, orphan-pr=12, orphan-issue-lane=0, orphan-directive=0
budget: orphan-worktree=55, orphan-branch=95, orphan-pr=20, orphan-issue-lane=25, orphan-directive=115
exceeded: 2   (orphan-worktree 56/55, orphan-branch 114/95)
```

The walk's own dispositions over the 182 findings:

- **`orphan-branch`: 114, of which only 12 are content-landed** (the walk reclaims
  those under `--apply`). The other **102 carry the remedy "push it and open a PR, or
  open a lane for it"** — i.e. their work is NOT content-landed and exists nowhere
  else, which AGENTS.md **rule 17** forbids the worker to discard.
- **`orphan-worktree`: 56** — 25 are `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` subagent trees no lane
  record names, and the rest are `ao-worktrees/*` trees.
- `orphan-issue-lane` and `orphan-directive` are **0** in this measurement even though
  the gate's own §4 pass reported 32/112 — the two runs disagree, which is itself a
  finding to resolve before any number is trusted.

So the pile is **not** reclaimable down to the budget: the budget note's own rule is
"the pile has to shrink, not be re-excused", and the honest reading here is that 102
branches hold unique unlanded work that the rule forbids deleting while the declared
allowance was seeded from 85 branches on 2026-09-18.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

The remedy is a per-artifact OWNER call (the same shape as #1338): each of the 102
branches is *either* landed, *or* pushed with a PR, *or* deleted with an explicit
authorisation — and a re-measurement of a churn bound is a **reviewed edit** the
budget file itself says only the owner may make, never a loosening by a lane that is
trying to get its own PR through the gate.

## Remedy (bounded, three parts)

1. **Reclaim what is genuinely reclaimable** — `sweep --orphans --apply` (12 branches +
   the content-landed worktrees), tip recorded first, measured before/after.
2. **Shrink the live set**: every lane that lands closes its issue and its record, so
   the wave's own branches leave the pile; a lane's scratch worktree is removed when
   the lane is done. Attribute the residue by kind before touching a number.
3. **Re-measure, reviewed**: if the real count still exceeds the allowance, re-measure
   `governance/reconcile/orphan-budget.yaml` **with the measurement in the body**, in a
   PR, stating plainly that it is a re-measurement of a churn bound — not a claim that
   the pile shrank. Never raise a number to land an unrelated PR.

## Acceptance

- `bash scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh` is rc 0 on a pristine `origin/master`
  worktree, and its §4 real-tree comparison names no `orphan-budget-exceeded`.
- The before/after walk is recorded with real counts, and every artifact that left the
  pile is named with the evidence that allowed it (content-landed / reclaim / owner
  call) — no artifact disappears without a reason.
- The §4 disagreement between the gate's run and the standalone walk is resolved, or
  filed by name with its own measurement.

## Verify

```
python3 governance/reconcile/cli.py sweep --orphans --json
bash scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh
```

items.title: skip-budget: a third kind for a check whose assessability depends on a LIVE mechanism — the venue kind mislabels an authenticated-but-unreadable source as a check defect (#1394)
items.body:
Parent: #1254

## Measured 2026-09-19, from #1394

`scripts/skip-budget.json` has two kinds, and neither expresses *"this check's
assessability depends on a LIVE mechanism that must be observable"*:

| kind | honoured when | reds when |
|---|---|---|
| `standing-gap` | its check skips (rc 2) | the moment the check **assesses** — "stale exemption must be deleted" |
| `venue` | a NAMED precondition this venue does not supply | the precondition IS supplied and the check *still* cannot assess (#1176, "a defect of the check") |

`check-gate-status`'s producer probe now reads the producer's live state with
`gh` (#1394), so its assessability is a property of the **venue** — and it is
declared as a `venue` entry with its own probe quoted verbatim
(`{"command": "gh auth status"}`). That is right for the two common cases, both
measured with the ratchet's own seam (`--results/--names/--budget`) and the real
180 discovered check names:

```
--- BOX (gate-status rc 0)  ->  rc=0, entry UNUSED ("12 venue entr(y/ies) did not bite")
--- CI  (gate-status rc 2, venue cannot run 'gh auth status')
    ->  rc=0, honoured BY NAME:
    verify: standing skip gate-status -- venue: cannot run 'gh auth status' (the declared
      precondition of this venue), so no verdict is available here (the open issue that tracks it is #1382)
```

**The residual, measured the same way.** If `gh auth status` exits 0 and the
repository/API reads still fail — `gh-repo-unresolvable`,
`gh-statuses-unreadable` — the check answers rc 2 **naming the source**, exactly
as its honesty contract requires, and the ratchet then refuses the entry:

```
--- CI results (both rc 2) WITH gh present -- precondition supplied
    rc=1
    verify: skip ratchet FAIL -- venue precondition present but 'gate-status' still cannot assess
      -- the venue can run 'gh auth status', so this is a defect of the check, not of the venue (#1176)
```

The **red is right** (an authenticated-gh-but-unreadable-GitHub anomaly means the
required context's liveness genuinely cannot be established). The **second
reason is wrong**: it tells the operator to repair the check, when the check is
behaving correctly and GitHub is not answering.

## Why a third kind is the honest expression

A check whose verdict is a property of the *world* is not the same as one whose
verdict is a property of its own code. The third kind would say: *"this entry is
honoured by name while the check cannot assess for a LIVE-DEPENDENT reason, and
it is NOT stale when the check assesses — but it is still refused if the check
fails (rc 1), because a failing check is a finding, not a skip."* That keeps the
shrink-only property (the entry must name the open issue that tracks the
mechanism) while removing the mislabel.

## Scope

- `scripts/lib/skip-ratchet.py` — the kind, its validation, and its refusal text.
- `scripts/skip-budget.json` — `gate-status` and `branch-protection` move from
  `venue` to the new kind once it exists.
- `scripts/check-skip-ratchet.sh` — one provoked fixture per new rule, asserting
  **both** the rc and the refusal line (its own self-test currently counts
  `venue command precondition(s)`; a new kind needs its own census line).

Not filed as a blocker: the existing `venue` entry is correct in every venue the
fleet actually runs today (Cloud Build has no `gh`; a box has a working one).

Refs #1394
Refs #1382
Refs #1199

items.title: gate-status: the required status description is a fixed string per rc, so a red PR page cannot say WHY (`post --detail` does not exist)
items.body:
Parent: #1254

## The gap

`ao/gate-of-record` is the REQUIRED status on `master`, and its `description` is
the only thing a reader sees on the PR page next to a red. That description is a
**fixed string per exit code**:

```
$ grep -n 'def summarize' -A6 scripts/gate-status-map.py
def summarize(rc: int) -> str:
    """A human description, so the status is readable without the gate log."""
    return {
        0: "make verify: PASS",
        1: "make verify: FAIL",
        2: "make verify: CANNOT-ASSESS (not a pass)",
    }.get(rc, f"make verify: unknown outcome ({rc})")
```

`scripts/gate-status.sh post` accepts `--sha` / `--rc` / `--attestation` and
nothing else (`usage: $0 {post|show|dry-run} --sha <sha> [--rc <0|1|2> |
--attestation <file>]`), so a producer **cannot** say *which* check redded. Every
red PR page therefore reads `make verify: FAIL`, and the failing check's name is
only knowable by opening the Cloud Build log and reading 15 minutes of
transcript.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

The runner side of this is landing as #1384 (`fleet/runner`): a red keeps a
bounded transcript and records the failing check names, so the ledger,
`cli.py status` and the planner's refusal all name the check
(`verify-red:<pr>:local-marker:<check>`). The **poster** half cannot be reached
from that lane: `scripts/gate-status.sh` is owned by the live lane for #1400
(PR #1403 — it edits `scripts/gate-status.sh`) and is on #1384's do-not-edit
list, so editing it would clobber a neighbouring lane's file.

Measured 2026-09-19: `gh pr diff 1403 | grep '^+.*detail'` shows no `--detail`
seam being added by that lane either.

## The fix, when the poster's lane is free

1. `scripts/gate-status-map.py`: `summarize(rc: int, detail: str | None = None)`
   — the existing single-argument call keeps today's exact strings (its
   `--self-test` and `scripts/check-gate-status.sh`'s parity assertions must stay
   green), and a detail, when supplied, is appended (bounded: GitHub truncates a
   status description at 140 characters).
2. `scripts/gate-status.sh`: `post ... [--detail <text>]`, passed through to the
   description; `dry-run` prints it. **`--rc` must keep its current meaning**: a
   detail is a *suffix*, never a second source of truth for the outcome.
3. A control that provokes it: `post --rc 1 --detail 'x'` renders a description
   naming `x`, and a detail cannot turn rc 2 into a pass (the #739 defect class
   this repo has fixed before).

Once it exists, `fleet/runner/verify.py`'s `real_post_status` can pass the first
failing check it recorded (`evidence["failing_checks"][0]`), and the PR page says
WHY without anyone opening the build log.

## Refs

Refs #1384 — the runner keeps the evidence; this is the poster seam that would
let it reach the PR page.
Refs #1400 — the live lane that owns `scripts/gate-status.sh` today.

items.title: gate: NO pull request can pass control-plane-verify — check-reconcile-orphans CANNOT-ASSESSes in the Cloud Build venue (no gh) and is unnamed in scripts/skip-budget.json, so the skip ratchet reds every head
items.body:
## Measured (2026-09-19, Cloud Build project `purebliss-ghl`)

Two unrelated heads, one build each, the **identical** verdict:

```
# head de873cd6 (PR #1401, lane #1396) — build a4919733-017b-490e-a7aa-0219ed5feb4d (15m32s)
# head 0a4198bb (unrelated lane)        — build 81f8d3ff-0318-4946-ac87-925f08a63aaf
verify: skip ratchet FAIL -- unnamed skip 'reconcile-orphans' -- a check that cannot assess is a
  standing gap for the board: repair it, or name it in scripts/skip-budget.json against the open
  issue that tracks it (never a silent skip)
verify: FAIL (0 of 215 checks failed, 13 skipped: branch-protection, repo-settings, gate-status,
  module-registry, cmr-pin, module-brief, diagrams-declaration, codeidx-surface, cmr-knowledge,
  fleet-cron-dev-run, fleet-cron-image, reconcile-orphans, worktree-cap;
  skip ratchet FAIL: 1 unnamed skip -- named above)
```

**0 of 215 checks failed.** The only refusal is the ratchet, over a single skip.

## Why it skips — and why it is the one class the record does not yet cover

```
check-reconcile-orphans: CANNOT-ASSESS — gh not found; orphan-pr / orphan-issue-lane /
  orphan-directive cannot be measured on the real tree
```

The check's real-tree walk needs `gh` (its own guard is `command -v gh`,
`scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh`), and the verify container supplies none — the venue fact
#1361 records, and which `scripts/skip-budget.json` already names for twelve other checks. This
check is **not** in the record:

```
$ git show origin/master:scripts/skip-budget.json | grep -c reconcile-orphans
0
```

so the ratchet refuses it by name, exactly as designed.

## The consequence

`master` pushes do not run the composite at all — measured:
`gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits/857fd810…/check-runs` lists only
`control-plane-web-image` and `control-plane-apply`, never `control-plane-verify`. So this is
invisible on master and bites only on pull requests: **no PR can satisfy
`control-plane-verify (purebliss-ghl)` right now**, and that check is the evidence every lane's
delivery requires before merging (this one included).

## Remedy — one record entry, in the file that owns it

Add a `venue` entry for the check, naming **its own probe** and the open issue that tracks the
venue gap:

```json
{ "check": "reconcile-orphans", "kind": "venue", "issue": 1361,
  "precondition": { "command": "command -v gh" },
  "reason": "`check-reconcile-orphans: CANNOT-ASSESS — gh not found; orphan-pr / orphan-issue-lane /
             orphan-directive cannot be measured on the real tree` — the check's real-tree walk needs
             `gh`, which the verify container does not supply (#1361)." }
```

Two alternatives were considered and are worse; neither is this lane's call:

* **denylist the check** — a silent skip moved into another file, which is the ratchet's own
  complaint (#1199) and would hide a real check;
* **make the check assess without `gh`** — it cannot: the board read *is* the measurement.

`scripts/skip-budget.json` belongs to another lane, so this is reported rather than edited.

## Provenance

Found while closing #1396: PR #1401 was refused by this, not by its own diff (0 checks failed, and
the lane's own new arms are `ok` in the build log — `ok  an exported PR_NUMBER/$_PR_NUMBER naming
another PR leaves this fixture's verdict byte-identical`). Filed because the remedy lives in a file
lane #1396 is told not to touch, and because the condition blocks **every** lane, not just one.

Refs #1396
Refs #1361
Refs #1199
