```
FAILED governance/isolation/tests/test_audit.py::test_a_merge_commit_is_exempt_from_the_trailer_rule
1 failed, 192 passed in 12.19s
E       AssertionError: the merge must be authored by the session for this to prove anything
E       assert 'agent+mechan...gents.invalid' == 'agent+copilo...gents.invalid'
E         - agent+copilot-brain@agents.invalid
E         + agent+mechanical-sme@agents.invalid
governance/isolation/tests/test_audit.py:122: AssertionError
```

The lane's session identity (AGENTS.md rule 15) is **exported into the agent's environment**
— this shell carries `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=agent-mechanical-sme`,
`GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=agent+mechanical-sme@agents.invalid`, `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME`,
`GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL` — and git gives those variables precedence over `user.email`. The
fixture commits a merge and asserts the commit is authored by the identity **it** configured,
so the ambient identity wins and the assertion fails.

Control — the same single test, in **both** venues, with the ambient identity stripped:

```
$ env -u GIT_AUTHOR_NAME -u GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL -u GIT_COMMITTER_NAME -u GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL \
    python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
    governance/isolation/tests/test_audit.py::test_a_merge_commit_is_exempt_from_the_trailer_rule
1 passed      # pristine origin/master  (rc 0)
1 passed      # the lane worktree       (rc 0)
```

So it is **not** a master defect and not any lane's diff: it is a fixture that does not own its
environment — the same defect class #1396 fixed in `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` and
`scripts/check-landing.sh`. (A separate, unrelated venue artefact was also cleared while
attributing this: `governance/knowledge`'s 4 `test_live_sync` failures are an uninitialised
`vendor/CMR` — rc 0, 69 passed, in a populated venue.)

## Why it matters

`governance/isolation` is declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`, so `make gate` (and
`make merge-gate`) runs it in every venue that runs that manifest — and every agent lane on
this box exports the ambient identity, so the suite reds for every lane while CI (a fresh
container with no exported identity) is green. A gate whose verdict is a function of the
caller's shell is not a gate.

## Remedy

Pin the identity inside the fixture instead of inheriting it: set
`GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL` and `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL` explicitly in the environment the
fixture passes to its own `git` calls (or use git's `-c user.email=…` / `-c user.name=…` for
those commits), so the assertion measures the fixture's decision rather than the caller's
shell.

## Provenance

Found while closing #1396 (the same ambient-state class), reported rather than edited:
`governance/isolation/tests/` belongs to another lane.

Refs #1396

items.title: pr-contract: the landed audit has no recorded-legacy baseline, so it reports 39 post-boundary findings on master's landed history (its own header claims 0)
items.body:
Parent: #1254

## Measured (2026-09-19, pristine `origin/master` @ `857fd810`, unmodified detached worktree)

```
$ cd /tmp/ao1396-before-pristine      # git worktree add --detach ... origin/master
$ bash scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --landed
check-pr-contract: LANDED: FAIL (39 finding(s))          # rc 1
```

Every one of the 39 is **post-boundary** — `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha>
a7e7312991ae24b1047363ff36627060a810fdd8` is false for 39/39 — while the file's own header
states the opposite, as a *measurement*, on the commit that landed the gate:

> "all 37 commits that lack the trailer (e.g. `061690c`) are strictly before the boundary, and
> 0 commits after it lack one."

The same 39 findings reproduce **identically** on a lane head (`de873cd6`, itself clean) and on
pristine master, so this is master's landed history, not any lane's diff.

## Why this is a real disagreement rather than "record the residue"

`governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` is the *recorded* view of the same trailer rule, and
`scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` — which IS in `make verify` — is green because those commits
are recorded there. That is the resolution #836 settled: *recording is a first-class, reviewable
act*, and post-boundary residue on protected history is a permanent fact.

`check-pr-contract.sh --landed` is a second implementation of the same predicate with a
**different** policy: it grandfathers only commits strictly before the boundary and has no
recorded-legacy baseline. So one rule has two answers — one green in `make verify`, one reporting
a permanent 39.

It is not a gate: `pr-contract` is disabled by name in `scripts/check-denylist.txt`, so `make
verify` never runs `--landed` and master is not red from it. It is a reporting surface that
reports a number nobody can act on.

## Remedy (pick one, and state it in the file)

1. **Give `--landed` the recorded-legacy baseline the isolation gate already owns** — read
   `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` through the same loader (one rule, one record, two
   readers), and restate the header's measured claim to match.
2. Or restate the claim honestly: the boundary grandfathers **by position only**, post-boundary
   residue is reported, and its record lives in the isolation baseline — today's
   "0 commits after it lack one" is measurably false.

## Provenance

Found while closing #1396 (the ambient `$PR_NUMBER` precedence fix), reported rather than edited
because the fix is a policy decision about grandfathering and #1396's brief scopes that lane to the
precedence defect. Evidence: `/tmp/ao1396/landed-ao1396-before-pristine.log`,
`/tmp/ao1396/boundary2.txt` (39/39 post-boundary).

Refs #1396
Refs #1254

items.title: the required context is satisfied by a box-side status post while the Cloud Build run on the same sha is red (f300954d)
items.body:
## Measured

The tree that landed as `master` `b8ad98f4` ("train: land 18 verified PRs (20260919T033833Z) (#1398)")
is the train head **`f300954d8a5c9cfa5646669f8e60596cabe88afa`**. Its required status context is green:

```
$ gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits/f300954d…/statuses \
    --jq '.[]|{context,state,description,creator:.creator.login,target_url,created_at}'
{"context":"ao/gate-of-record","state":"success","description":"make verify: PASS",
 "creator":"kushin77","target_url":null,"created_at":"2026-09-19T03:51:19Z"}
{"context":"ao/gate-of-record","state":"success","description":"make verify: PASS",
 "creator":"kushin77","target_url":null,"created_at":"2026-09-19T03:53:43Z"}
```

The **only** Cloud Build run for that sha is `32cb10f7-f4c2-4522-87f9-84d9da1d56aa`
(branch `train/20260919T033833Z`) — and it was **created one second *after* the first status**
(`createTime 2026-09-19T03:51:20`, status `03:51:19Z`), so that status cannot have come from it. It
then finished **FAILURE**:

```
$ gcloud builds describe 32cb10f7… --format='value(id,status,startTime,finishTime)'
32cb10f7… FAILURE 2026-09-19T03:54:38.848143498Z 2026-09-19T04:19:01.947748Z

$ gcloud builds log 32cb10f7… | grep -E '^verify: FAIL'
verify: FAIL (1 of 215 checks failed, 13 skipped: branch-protection, repo-settings, gate-status,
module-registry, cmr-pin, module-brief, diagrams-declaration, codeidx-surface, cmr-knowledge,
fleet-cron-dev-run, fleet-cron-image, reconcile-orphans, worktree-cap; skip ratchet FAIL: 1 unnamed
skip -- named above)
```

The one failing check is **`check-reconcile: FAIL (1 violation(s))`**, plus the ratchet refusal
`unnamed skip 'reconcile-orphans'`. Neither is this lane's: the two checks this repo's `#1357` added
appear in that same run as **named standing skips** (`branch-protection`, `gate-status` → #1382),
which is their honest state.

## Why it matters

`ao/gate-of-record` is a **required** status check on `master` (#1342), and it is the one piece of
evidence `scripts/pr-queue.sh` accepts for a merged tree. Here the green came from a status posted
**outside the CI venue** (`target_url: null`, posted before any build for that sha existed) — a
box-side `scripts/gate-status.sh post --rc 0` — while the Cloud Build run on the same sha was red on
its own arrival. So the merged-tree evidence can read `success` for a sha whose CI run failed, and
neither party to that pair is lying: there are two producers of one required context (the box-side
landing driver and #1354's Cloud Build step), and only one of them is the CI venue.

Not caused by #1357's change and not fixed by it — filed because the required-context integrity is
exactly what that work is about, and because #1394 already tracks the adjacent half (the probe reads
the trigger's import stub rather than live state).

## Suggested questions to settle (a decision, not a patch)

1. May a box-side driver satisfy a required CI context at all? If yes, the status should say so
   (a distinct `context` or a description naming the venue) so the two producers are distinguishable
   and the CI one is not silently substituted.
2. If no, the poster should refuse to publish when the sha's own CI run is red — the guard
   (`scripts/pr-queue.sh`) reads the status, never the run.

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1357 kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1394 kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1361 kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1398

items.title: reconcile: record branch issue-1034 in the reviewed real-tree baseline — the 24h-grace crossing that reds every lane's gate
items.body:
## What was red

`bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh` in a **pristine master worktree** at
`origin/master = 658b041e6c8b714c2cc29e4878c28d592a96a1d4` → **rc 1**. Measured
2026-09-19T03:47Z; it is the last red on the gate of record, so it blocks
**every** lane's landing and close-out, not just this one:

```
check-reconcile: FAIL — real tree drifted from governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json (1 new-and-old, 518 stale, not fatal; 0 stale quarantine exemption(s))
  NEW      branch issue-1034 — not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or fix it)
check-reconcile: FAIL (1 violation(s))
```

The 518 STALE entries are explicitly **not fatal** by the check's own contract
(a disk artifact is meant to disappear) and are untouched here. Exactly ONE
artifact is the violation.

## The measurement (reproduced, not inherited)

| signal | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| local ref | `git rev-parse issue-1034` | `63d8b6c259d8ed46edb760a9249a470400affc2f` |
| remote ref | `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/issue-1034` (and `git ls-remote --heads origin \| grep -c 1034`) | **empty / 0 — the branch is LOCAL-ONLY** |
| tip committer date | `git log -1 --format=%cI issue-1034` | `2026-09-18T03:29:06Z` ⇒ crossed the 24h grace at **2026-09-19T03:29Z** (hence NEW-and-old, not YOUNG) |
| tip subject | `git log --oneline -1 issue-1034` | `fix(gate): carry the mutant fixture's import closure (#1034)` |
| on `origin/master`? | `git merge-base --is-ancestor issue-1034 origin/master` | rc 1 — **no** |
| its parent | `git rev-list --parents -1 <tip>` | `2dccae299b6e45eb800887ba167460523d7f2b84`, itself **on** `origin/master` (`--is-ancestor` rc 0) |
| the tip's own change | `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-status -r 63d8b6c2` | **empty** — a no-op commit: its tree `241dfc8e59fd9fa3e53e85747dd4028151e52258` is byte-identical to its parent's |
| patch identity | `git cherry origin/master issue-1034` / `git diff origin/master...issue-1034 \| git patch-id --stable` | `+ 63d8b6c2` (unlanded) / **empty** — no patch exists to match, so the proof declines by vacuity |
| refs containing the tip | `git for-each-ref --contains 63d8b6c2 --format='%(refname)'` | only `refs/heads/issue-1034` |
| how it got that way | `git reflog show issue-1034` | `branch: Created from origin/master` (`96ae0fba`) → commit `9296412e` → **`rebase (finish) … onto 2dccae29`** → commit `63d8b6c2` |
| the substance it names, on the default branch? | `git show origin/master:scripts/check-lifecycle-reclaim.sh \| grep -n 'cp -r governance'` | line 159 `cp -r governance "$1/governance"` — **already present**, and already present at its own parent `2dccae29` (so the rebase made the change redundant and left the commit empty) |
| the work item | `gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/1034 --jq '{state,closed_at}'` | `closed`, `2026-09-17T15:07:06Z` |

So: **not landed by ancestry, not landed by tree containment, and not landed by
patch identity** (the audit's own three proofs all decline — the third because
the tip carries no change at all). The same branch's earlier, pre-rebase
iteration `9296412e` (now reachable only through the reflog) was the one that
carried the real `+49/−1` to `scripts/check-lifecycle-reclaim.sh`, and that
change is already on `origin/master` in evolved form.

## The fix

ONE by-name entry in `governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json` — the home
the gate's own verdict line names (*"not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or
fix it)"*) — with the schema copied exactly from the three `issue-1145-*`
entries the #1338 lane added (`kind` / `name` / `reason`, inserted in the file's
existing sorted position), and a `reason` carrying the measurement above. The
AGENTS.md rule 17 posture is honoured: the artifact is **reported by name, not
deleted and not quarantined** — the ref belongs to another session, and the
terminal disposal call (push it, or delete a no-op branch) is the owner's, not
this lane's.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh` → **rc 0** in a worktree cut from
      `origin/master` with exactly one entry added (it is rc 1 on master — that
      delta is the load-bearing proof).
- [ ] nothing else changes: no STALE row touched, no new-and-old count edited,
      `governance/reconcile/`'s quarantine document untouched, nothing deleted,
      pruned or reaped.
- [ ] `bash scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` rc 0 and `bash scripts/check-docs.sh`
      rc 0 solo, and the baseline still parses
      (`python3 -c "import json;json.load(open('governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json'))"`).

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh
```

## Clock (#506, RCA-0008)

No time-pinned fixture: the entry is a reviewed record of a measurement, and the
audit's own 24h grace is resolved from the artifact's tip date against the live
clock inside the check — never from a literal date added here.

items.title: gate: check-pr-contract gives the AMBIENT $PR_NUMBER precedence over its own argv — a caller-exported PR context hijacks every hermetic fixture (#1341/#1344)
items.body:
## The defect class

`scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` resolves its PR number as

```bash
PR_NUMBER="${_PR_NUMBER:-${PR_NUMBER:-}}"      # line 163 — the AMBIENT caller's value
...
if [ -n "${PR_NUMBER:-}" ]; then               # line 1606 — and it WINS over argv
  pr_check "$PR_NUMBER"; exit $?
fi
...                                            # only then the --body-file/--range path
```

So a caller-exported `_PR_NUMBER`/`PR_NUMBER` **outranks the script's own explicit
argv**. Any hermetic fixture that calls the contract with `--body-file … --range …`
to *avoid* reading the host's GitHub state is silently rewritten into the LIVE PR
path — and under a stubbed `gh` (or offline) it answers `CANNOT-ASSESS`, never a
verdict about the thing it was asked to judge.

## Measured (PR #1344, head `04d7380b`, on the unchanged tree)

```
$ PR_NUMBER=1344  bash scripts/check-landing.sh   # rc 1
  FAIL  check-pr-contract refused the driver's own PR body: check-pr-contract:
        CANNOT-ASSESS — no non-merge commits between PR #1344's base
        ({"state":"MERGED","mergeCommit":{"oid":"merged-unknown"}}) and its head
        ({"state":"MERGED","mergeCommit":{"oid":"merged-unknown"}})
$ _PR_NUMBER=1344 bash scripts/check-landing.sh   # rc 1, byte-identical
$ AO_PR_NUMBER=1344 bash scripts/check-landing.sh # rc 0 — irrelevant on its own
```

The base/head blobs are `scripts/check-landing.sh`'s own **stub `gh`** output
(`pr view` → `{"state":"MERGED","mergeCommit":{"oid":"merged-unknown"}}`): the
fixture's hermetic transport received the live PR number and answered for it.

This is the CI red of build `723220bf-9b18-411e-8977-a5f43e31ca7c`
(`verify: FAIL (3 of 208 checks failed)`, one of them `check-landing`). The
in-lane half — `scripts/verify.sh` exporting `PR_NUMBER` box-wide into the
composite environment — is fixed by PR #1344, which now scopes the context to the
`pr-contract` check alone and `env -u`'s it for every other check.

## What is still owed (all three outside PR #1344's file scope)

1. **`scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` — argv must win over the ambient name.**
   An explicit `--body-file`/`--range`/`--pr` is a *statement of what to judge*;
   an exported `PR_NUMBER` is a *hint about which PR the caller is on*. The
   precedence is inverted. (Cheapest fix: resolve `PR_NUMBER` from argv first,
   and only fall back to `$_PR_NUMBER`/`$PR_NUMBER` when no argv supplied one.)
2. **`scripts/check-landing.sh` — the fixture does not own its environment.**
   Its own header says the fixtures own their environment and lists what it
   unsets (`GH_PR_STATE GH_MERGE_COMMIT GH_PR_HEAD CONTRACT_MODE AO_LAND_APPLY
   PREDICATE_MODE`); `PR_NUMBER`/`_PR_NUMBER` are missing from that list, so the
   arm's hermeticity is conditional on the caller's shell. A fixture is only
   hermetic if it *strips* the variables the code under test reads.
3. **`scripts/check-denylist.txt` denylists `pr-contract`, so #1341's wiring is
   inert.** The passthrough added by #1341 hands PR context to a check that
   `make verify` never runs (the denylist's own comment: "gate/merge-gate
   signals, NOT part of `make verify`'s composite"). Either the check should run
   in the composite when a PR context is present (and then a context-less run
   must be a SKIP, never a pass), or #1341's passthrough should be recorded as
   unexercised. Right now the wiring reads as done and does nothing — which is
   the same class of defect as the one it caused.

## Why it matters beyond this lane

The composite gate is the fleet's gate of record. While the ambient name wins,
**any** runner that exports a PR number changes the verdict of every check that
invokes the contract — including the fixtures that exist to prove the contract
is *not* being fooled. A gate whose verdict is a function of the caller's
environment is not a gate.

## Provenance

Found by lane #1341 / PR #1344, 2026-09-19, from the Cloud Build log of
`723220bf-9b18-411e-8977-a5f43e31ca7c`. Reported here rather than edited: those
three files are outside that lane's file scope.

Refs #1254

items.title: the producer probe reads the trigger import stub as live state: REQUIRED-BUT-GATED-OFF fires on a repo whose producer is enabled and posting (#1357/#1382)
items.body:
## Measured

`scripts/check-gate-status.sh` (merged into `master` by #1357's PR) refuses **by name**, rc 2:

```
probe: required=1 context=ao/gate-of-record verdict=gated-off
check-gate-status: CANNOT-ASSESS REQUIRED-BUT-GATED-OFF — 'ao/gate-of-record' is REQUIRED and its
producer exists on the PR path, but that trigger ships flag-gated OFF, so nothing produces the check
until it is promoted out of band; the requirement is not satisfiable yet, which is never a pass
```

`verdict=gated-off` is computed by `verdict_paths()` from the **import stub's** `disabled:` field:

```yaml
# infra/cloudbuild/verify-trigger.yaml
# ... Promotion ... is a live, out-of-band `gcloud builds triggers update --no-disabled` — never a
# commit to this file.
disabled: true
```

That field is **pinned `true` by this repository's own policy**, not by the live state:
`scripts/check-cloudbuild.sh:84` calls `check_trigger "$cb_dir/verify-trigger.yaml" _ENABLE_VERIFY`,
which requires `doc.get("disabled") is not True → "must ship disabled: true (GR-5)"`. So the probe's
premise ("nothing produces the check until it is promoted") can never be falsified from the tree —
and, measured, it is **false live**:

```
$ gcloud builds triggers describe control-plane-verify --region=us-central1 --project=purebliss-ghl \
    --format='value(name,disabled,filename)'
control-plane-verify		infra/cloudbuild/verify.yaml      # no `disabled` value => ENABLED

$ gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/commits/2adbe48b0013fa3321559aecc3bcc714978ca9b5/statuses \
    --jq '.[]|{context,state,created_at}'
{"context":"ao/gate-of-record","state":"success","created_at":"2026-09-19T03:22:50Z"}
{"context":"ao/gate-of-record","state":"success","created_at":"2026-09-19T03:16:50Z"}
```

The required context **is** produced where the verdict is made — the PR-verdict Cloud Build runs
(the `control-plane-verify` check-run is on open PR heads right now) and the producer posts
`ao/gate-of-record`. So a check that is supposed to be *green on a healthy repository* answers
`CANNOT-ASSESS` forever here, naming a condition that is not true. That is the same class #1357 is
about, inverted: the gate states a fact about the world that the world contradicts, and its rc 2 is
unfalsifiable from the tree it is asked to judge.

The agent CANNOT-ASSESS (never 0) half is honest and holds — this is about the **named reason**
being wrong, and about the check being unable to reach `OK` on the repository it polices.

## Why this is not a one-file change (measured consequence)

Both policing checks are skip-budgeted as `standing-gap` against #1382
(`scripts/skip-budget.json`, added while #1357 was open):

* `scripts/lib/skip-ratchet.py` marks a `standing-gap` entry **STALE the moment its check
  assesses** (`assesses now (rc N) -- the gap is closed`) and refuses the run;
* so if the probe stops treating the import stub as live state, `check-gate-status` assesses
  (rc 0) on any head that carries the status → the entry is stale → `check-skip-ratchet` refuses
  on a box;
* **deleting** the entries is not the fix either: in the Cloud Build venue there is no `gh`, so the
  check answers `CANNOT-ASSESS gh-unauthenticated` (rc 2) and an unbudgeted skip is refused
  (`unnamed skip … must be named in the budget`);
* a `venue` entry (`precondition: gh auth status`, #1361) is refused on a box the moment a head has
  no status yet — `venue precondition present but '<check>' still cannot assess`.

`standing-gap` and `venue` are each correct for one of the two cases and wrong for the other, so the
budget cannot currently express *"this check's assessability varies by commit inside one venue"* —
which is exactly what a live-read-back check is.

## Proposed fix (needs a coordinated change, hence this issue)

1. `verdict_paths()` should report the import stub's `disabled:` as an **observation**, not a
   verdict: the question it can answer from the tree is *"does a producer exist on the PR verdict
   path?"* (#1357's rule). Whether the path is live is answered by the read-back half, which is the
   only half that can be contradicted by reality.
2. Decide how the budget expresses per-commit assessability — either a third kind, or
   `check-gate-status.sh` stops asking the live question about *the commit under test* and asks it
   about the **mechanism** (producer on the PR path + the context observed on a recent
   PR-verdict commit), so that its verdict is a property of the repository rather than of one head.

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1357 kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1382 kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1361

items.title: gate: check-infra-limits' orphan-hog guard fails closed on a transient find rc=1 — one vanished /tmp entry reds the composite for every lane
items.body:
## Measured defect — the composite goes red for EVERY lane

`scripts/check-infra-limits.sh`'s `guard_orphan_hogs()` runs

```bash
find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -size "+${max_mb}M" -printf '%s\t%p\n' > "$list" 2>/dev/null
rc=$?
if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
  printf '  FAIL  orphan-hog: cannot scan %s (find rc=%s)\n' "$dir" "$rc"
  return 2
fi
```

and **fails closed on any non-zero rc**. `find` returns 1 on *any* error — including a
top-level entry that vanishes between `readdir` and `stat`, which is routine on this box's
shared tmpfs (`/tmp` measured at **21,394 entries**, 4+ lanes churning scratch dirs, a `find`
storm admitted per worktree). `2>/dev/null` hides the reason while the rc still reds the gate.

Measured tonight, same box, 19 minutes apart, no code change between them:

| log | line | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `/tmp/ao-train/land-1387/verify.log` | 5758 | `OK    orphan-hog: no scratch file in /tmp exceeds 4096 MiB` |
| `/tmp/ao-train/land-1354-attempt1/verify.log` | 5763 | `FAIL  orphan-hog: cannot scan /tmp (find rc=1)` |

`land-1354-attempt1` also shows `C1 orphan-hog ceiling` **passing in the same run** — so `find`
was healthy on the control's own directory; the failure was specific to the top-level `/tmp`
scan, i.e. the race, not an inability to scan.

Consequence: `check-infra-limits: FAIL` → the whole composite is rc 1 → `check-infra-limits` is
registered in `scripts/verify.sh`'s `checks=()`, so **every lane's gate goes red for a
transient filesystem race**, and the red carries no diagnosis (the reason was discarded by
`2>/dev/null`).

## What is wanted

1. A transient/racy non-zero rc is distinguished from a real inability to scan: retry the
   scan with a short backoff, and fail only when it stays non-zero.
2. A genuine refusal keeps the **fail-closed** property and stays **by name**.
3. The reason is captured into the report (`find rc=1: <first stderr line>`), so a future
   red names WHY instead of an unexplained rc.
4. A provoked control proves **both** directions deterministically.
5. The other guards in the script are checked for the same fail-closed-on-rc pattern.

`Verify:` `bash scripts/check-infra-limits.sh` (rc 0) plus `scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh`,
`scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh`, `scripts/check-docs.sh`.

items.title: cloudbuild: the two rollout triggers reference nine substitution templates nothing declares — refused at submission
items.body:
Parent: #1295

## What is missing

`scripts/check-cloudbuild.sh` now refuses every bare `$NAME` the submission-time
validator would refuse (issue #1369). Run against the tree at `4c7ab309` it names
**nine** such templates, in two files, and **nothing declares them**:

| file | undeclared tokens |
|---|---|
| `infra/cloudbuild/rollout-promote.yaml` | `$_DEPLOYER_SA`, `$_FLAG`, `$_TO_STAGE`, `$_APPROVAL_ID`, `$_ACTOR`, `$_APPROVALS_DIR` |
| `infra/cloudbuild/rollout-rollback.yaml` | `$_DEPLOYER_SA`, `$_CANARY_HEALTH`, `$_FLAG` |

The declared set the validator reads for a trigger submission is the config's own
`substitutions:` map **plus** the map of every trigger whose `filename:` names that
config. `rollout-promote-trigger.yaml` and `rollout-rollback-trigger.yaml` declare
`_ENABLE_ROLLOUT` and nothing else, and neither config declares anything at all.
Nothing else supplies them either — `grep -rn -- '--substitutions' .` has no hits,
and no `gcloud builds submit` site in the repo passes them — so the pair cannot be
submitted as declared: the same refusal that cost #1350 two ~20-minute CI round
trips ("key in the template … is not a valid built-in substitution") would hit the
moment a rollout trigger is imported and fires.

Both triggers are `disabled: true` (GR-5), so the defect is **latent, not live** —
which is exactly why the #1369 gate quarantines the finding by name instead of
inventing values for it.

## Remedy (bounded)

Declare the nine keys where the validator reads them: the trigger's
`substitutions:` map, mirroring `apply-trigger.yaml`, which declares every
substitution `apply.yaml` consumes (including `_DEPLOYER_SA`, "supplied at import").

The **values are the rollout lane's decision, not this issue's**. An empty
placeholder in a trigger substitution is untested here, and a committed default for
`_FLAG` / `_TO_STAGE` would silently pick a promotion target. That is why #1369's
gate carries one baseline row per token rather than a value.

## Acceptance

- `bash scripts/check-cloudbuild.sh` reports no undeclared template for either file.
- `infra/cloudbuild/template-baseline.txt` is empty — its nine rows go STALE the
  moment the keys are declared, and the gate fails naming them until they are
  removed, so this issue cannot be closed with the baseline still carrying them.
- `Verify:` `bash scripts/check-cloudbuild.sh`

## Provenance

Found by the #1369 gate while implementing the submission-template rule; measured at
`4c7ab309ca49e9563af38a459ef19b3afa4409a1`. The alternative — the gate tolerating an
undeclared token because "someone supplies it at go-live" — would be a false green:
the validator does not read prose.

items.title: runner: keep each verify's gate tail as evidence — a red with only rc=1 in the ledger cannot be diagnosed or contested
items.body:
Parent: #1343

## Measured 2026-09-19T01:33Z on the pair
Four heads (#1354 #1371 #1372 #1373) verified `rc=1` and the rung posted `ao/gate-of-record=failure` — correct — but `.fleet/runner/local-green/<pr>-<sha>` holds only `{"rc": 1, "detail": "verify rc 1 (red); master was e996eb9534c9"}` and the ledger the same. The verify output is discarded with the worktree, so the failing check's NAME is unknowable without re-running the 15-minute verify by hand.

## Fix
- `fleet/runner/verify.py`: capture verify stdout/stderr to `.fleet/runner/logs/<pr>-<sha>.log` (rotate/cap size), and extract into the marker + ledger record the `verify:` summary line plus every `^(check-[a-z0-9-]+|[a-z-]+): (FAIL|NOT-OK)` line (bounded, e.g. first 10) as `failing_checks: [...]`.
- `cli.py status`: print the failing check names next to a red head; `plan` reason for a local red becomes `verify-red:<pr>:local-marker:<first-check>`.
- Post the first failing check name in the commit status description (`gate-status.sh post --detail`), so the PR page says WHY.
- Test: a fake verify that reds with a named check → marker, ledger, status detail all carry the name; a green run records `failing_checks: []`.

Refs #1378

items.title: gate: check-lane-record's unreadable-record arm cannot fire as root, so make verify is red in the Cloud Build venue for EVERY lane
items.body:
## The red

`check-lane-record` (landed by #1363 for #1270) fails in the **Cloud Build verify venue** on every run, so `make verify` is red there for **every lane**:

```
verify: FAIL (1 of 208 checks failed, 12 skipped: branch-protection, repo-settings, …)
```
measured on build `32044290-3743-4af0-9950-1c297da4bb30` (head `0fd1b91c`, PR #1354). The single failing check is:

```
check-lane-record: FAIL — 1 violation(s)
  FAIL  unreadable-record        rc=0 (wanted 1) and the output does not name lane-record-unreadable:4242/alpha.brief.json
```

Every other arm of the check passes there (`suite 39 passed`), and the check passes **on the developer box**: `check-lane-record: OK` (rc 0, uid 1000).

## Why

The arm's fixture is an **unreadable file produced with `chmod(0)`** — `scripts/check-lane-record.sh`:

```python
if variant == "unreadable":
    (directory / ("%s.brief.json" % lane)).chmod(0)
```

Cloud Build steps run as **root**, and root reads a mode-000 file. So the fixture is not unreadable, the checker correctly accepts the record, and the arm's expectation (`rc=1`, naming `lane-record-unreadable`) cannot fire. The check is not wrong about the records — the *fixture* has no effect in this venue.

## Proof, in the venue itself

1. **The mechanism**, same image the CI step uses:
   ```
   $ docker run --rm python:3.14 bash -lc 'd=$(mktemp -d); printf x > "$d/f"; chmod 0 "$d/f"; cat "$d/f" >/dev/null && echo readable || echo unreadable'
   uid=0
   chmod-000 file IS readable -> the arm cannot fire
   ```
2. **The check itself, as root, in `python:3.14`, against a PRISTINE `origin/master` worktree** (`e996eb95`, no lane code at all):
   ```
   check-lane-record: FAIL (4 violation(s))
     FAIL  unreadable-record        rc=0 (wanted 1) and the output does not name lane-record-unreadable:4242/alpha.brief.json
   ```
   (the other three violations are only `pytest`/`PyYAML` missing in a hand-made container; CI installs them, which is why CI reports exactly one)
3. **The same tree, uid 1000**: `check-lane-record: OK -- a brief and its result are one record for every runtime, and every refusal above was provoked by name`.

Identical output on pristine `origin/master` and on the lane's head ⇒ the red is not any lane's diff.

## Fallout

* `make verify` cannot be green in the only automated venue, so no lane can produce a truthful green `ao/gate-of-record` — a requirement that `governance/platform/branch-protection.yaml` now enforces (`required_status_checks.contexts: [ao/gate-of-record]`, `strict: false`).
* It is the same class as #1361 (venue limits that a check cannot express), but #1361's ratified mechanism (`venue` entries in `scripts/skip-budget.json`) is not applicable: the check *can* assess in this venue, it is one **arm** that cannot.
* Note on how it landed: PR #1363's head `d53d0ca3` carried `control-plane-verify = failure` and an `ao/gate-of-record: success`, and the last five merges to `master` carry **no** `control-plane-verify` check-run and **no** `ao/gate-of-record` status at all. So this arm was never exercised under a root venue before it became everyone's red.

## Suggested remedy (owner's call — filed, not edited)

Pick whichever the owning lane prefers, all one-line-ish:

* make the fixture unreadable **for a privileged user** too — e.g. replace the file with a directory or a FIFO of the same name, `chmod 0` the containing directory, or drop privileges for that one read; or
* skip the arm (by name, with a printed reason) when `os.geteuid() == 0`, so the arm is honest about what it can prove in a root venue; or
* if a root venue is judged out of scope for this check, say so through the ratified venue mechanism so the ratchet can account for it.

Suggested `Verify:` `bash scripts/check-lane-record.sh` run as uid 0 in `python:3.14` (the recipe above) exits 0 **and** still fails by name when the record really is unreadable for the invoking user.

## Provenance

Found while closing #1350 (PR #1354) — the lane's own two CI reds (`check-merge-guard`, `check-isolation-landed`) were fixed and now report `OK` in the same build; this one is neither caused by that diff nor fixable from it (`scripts/check-*.sh` is a gate-sensitive path, `scripts/lib/gate-paths.txt`).

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1350
Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1361
Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1270
Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1363

items.title: gate: branch protection requires ao/gate-of-record, but nothing on the ordinary lane path produces it — 17 of 17 open PRs are BLOCKED
items.body:
Parent: #1254

## Measured: every open PR is hard-blocked, and nothing on the normal path produces the status

`335c9a34` ("feat(governance): require ao/gate-of-record on master (#803) (#1342)") made
`ao/gate-of-record` a **required status check** on `master`. Read back from the API:

```
$ gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/branches/master/protection \
    --jq '(.required_status_checks.contexts // [])|join(",")'
ao/gate-of-record
```

Result, measured 2026-09-19T01:35Z across **every** open PR:

```
TOTAL=17 BLOCKED=17 WITH_A_STATUS=4   # and all 4 of those are `failure`
```

```
#1380 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]      #1374 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]
#1379 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]      #1373 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[failure]
#1377 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]      #1372 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[failure]
#1376 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]      #1371 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[failure]
#1375 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]      #1367 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]
#1365 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]      #1364 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]
#1359 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]      #1358 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]
#1354 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[failure]  #1344 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]
#1327 BLOCKED gate-of-record=[-]
```

**13 PRs carry no status at all. The other 4 carry `failure`** — and those four are
*correct*: a lane gated each head, the gate of record genuinely did not pass, and the lane
refused to publish a green it had not observed. That is the mechanism working.

## The defect is the producer, not the check

The publish path works — `scripts/gate-status.sh post --sha <sha> --rc <rc>` (ADR-0028, a
plain `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/{sha}`) — but **nothing on the ordinary lane path
calls it**:

```
$ grep -rln 'gate-status.sh' --include='*.sh' --include='*.py' .
scripts/gate-status.sh          # the tool
scripts/check-gate-status.sh    # its checker
scripts/gate-status-map.py
scripts/verify.sh               # <- see below
scripts/check-landing.sh
governance/landing/engine.py    # <- the only POST caller on a merge path
governance/landing/ports.py
```

A parallel lane verified by grep that `scripts/verify.sh` **does not post**
`ao/gate-of-record`; only `governance/landing/engine.py` (the `make land` path) does. So:

- a lane that follows the ordinary workflow — push, open a PR, run `make verify` — **never
  produces the required status**, and its PR is BLOCKED no matter how green its gate was;
- the only PRs that can merge are those that go through `governance/landing`, or an owner
  bypass. Measured yesterday: PR #1352 merged while its own body reported
  `verify: FAIL (1 of 205: reconcile)`, and the landing commit `67798060` carries **zero
  statuses** — so `enforce_admins=false` let it through and the required check never fired.
  "It merged" is not evidence it was gated.

## Why this is urgent

This is the same class as the rule this repo already wrote down — *a required check needs a
producer* — and right now the producer is missing for every lane that is not using
`make land`. It is presently the **largest single blocker on the board**: 17 PRs, each with
finished work, all stuck.

## Bounded remedy (pick one, all are small)

1. **Make `verify.sh` publish**: at the end of a real run, `gate-status.sh post --sha
   $(git rev-parse HEAD) --rc <the run's own rc>`. The gate of record then produces the
   evidence the gate of record is required to present, on every path — which is what the
   requirement actually assumes.
2. **Or add it to the lane/PR path** (`scripts/pr-queue.sh` + the lane dispatcher), so a PR
   earns its status when its lane gates.
3. **Or drop the requirement** until a producer exists — but that reverts #803's whole point,
   so it should not be the answer.

Whichever is chosen, the negative control is the thing to keep: **an ungated PR must stay
BLOCKED**, and a PR whose gate did not pass must never show `success`. Do not make the
producer post `success` from anything other than a real gate verdict.

## What I did not do

I did not weaken branch protection, and I did not post a status for any commit whose gate I
had not seen pass. Two of my lanes' heads now carry `failure` because their gate genuinely
failed; that is the honest state.

items.title: check-lane-record: the unreadable-record fixture is not root-proof — it reds every CI run in the Cloud Build (root) venue
items.body:
## Measured (2026-09-19, Cloud Build venue = container user root)

CI build `d39635a0-577c-430f-bf64-b9cd90f98821` (PR #1359 head 427f7e60), full log `/tmp/ao-train/ci-1359.log` line 5418:

```
  FAIL  unreadable-record        rc=0 (wanted 1) and the output does not name lane-record-unreadable:4242/alpha.brief.json
  ...
check-lane-record: FAIL (1 violation(s))
```

The same script is GREEN on this box (non-root, `bash scripts/check-lane-record.sh` → rc 0). One red check in CI blocks every PR's CI-green.

## Mechanism

`scripts/check-lane-record.sh` (landed #1363, `scripts/check-lane-record.sh` sha256 `41bb16c1…`) builds arm 5's fixture through its generated `mk.py`: a clean brief+result pair, then the brief is made "unreadable" with `chmod(0)` (variant `unreadable`). The record read path — `governance/lane-record/lane_record.py::_read_json` — maps an `OSError` from `Path.read_text` to `RecordsUnreadable` → `Finding("lane-record-unreadable", …)`. Mode 0 is invisible to uid 0: in the Cloud Build container (root) the record stayed readable, the tree parsed as a clean pair, `evaluate` answered rc 0, and the arm's own `expect` (rc 1 + the refusal named) failed. The provocation control is uid-dependent, so in the root venue it never provoked the refusal it asserts — a control that cannot fail is a formality (GR-12).

## Fix

Make the fixture unreadable for EVERY uid: a **directory** where the record file `alpha.brief.json` is expected, so `Path.read_text` raises `IsADirectoryError` (EISDIR — an `OSError`) and the same read path names `lane-record-unreadable:4242/alpha.brief.json` for uid 0 and non-0 alike. Only that fixture mechanism (and its teardown) change; the arm keeps asserting rc 1 by name, so the check stays self-proving.

## Acceptance

- `bash scripts/check-lane-record.sh` → rc 0 on the box (non-root) **and** inside the Cloud Build venue shape (`docker run --rm --user 0 python:3.14 … bash scripts/check-lane-record.sh`): the arm returns the same verdict for uid 0 and non-0; proven in the python:3.14 container.
- Negative control: the same arm still REFUSES a genuinely unreadable record by name (rc 1 naming `lane-record-unreadable:…`), proven under uid 0 and non-0 by the run above.
- `git diff --stat` limited to `scripts/check-lane-record.sh`.

items.title: gate: check-cloudbuild.sh cannot see the bare dollar-template Cloud Build refuses at SUBMISSION (comments included) — cost two CI round trips in one lane
items.body:
## The gap

Cloud Build **refuses a build at submission time** when its config spells a bare dollar-template whose name is neither a built-in nor a declared substitution — and it reads **comments too**. `scripts/check-cloudbuild.sh` only asserts that each `infra/cloudbuild/*.yaml` **parses**, so this class is undetectable locally and only shows up after a push.

Measured twice, in one lane (#1350 / PR #1354), costing two ~20-minute CI round trips:

1. build `05734838-0cc3-4b35-bd2b-ab5e909fc3a3` (head `14c47552`) —
   `invalid argument: invalid value for 'build.substitutions': key in the template "GH_TOKEN" is not a valid built-in substitution`
2. the submission at head `ec770d47` (check-run started `2026-09-19T00:59:39Z`, **no build id assigned**) — byte-identical statusDetail, caused by the **comment** that was added while *citing* failure (1) as its example.

## Why it is nasty

* It kills the build **before step 0**, so `make verify` never runs and the red build says nothing about the code under review — the same failure class #1350 exists to remove.
* The validator reads **comments**, so the natural act of documenting the defect re-creates it (that is exactly how occurrence 2 happened).
* The local gate cannot see it: `bash scripts/check-cloudbuild.sh` → `cloudbuild: OK (rc 0)` on a file Cloud Build refuses.

## What the validator accepts/rejects (measured)

| shape | verdict |
|---|---|
| `$PROJECT_ID`, `$COMMIT_SHA` (built-ins, bare) | accepted |
| `$rc`, `$?` (lowercase shell names, bare) | accepted — the accepted build `df02b015` carries `$rc` |
| `${GH_TOKEN:-}`, `${COMMIT_SHA:-}` (braced, with a default) | accepted — not read as a template |
| `$GH_TOKEN` anywhere, **including in a `#` comment** | **REFUSED at submission** |

## Proposed remedy (suggested, owned by whoever owns the gate)

Extend `scripts/check-cloudbuild.sh` — a gate-sensitive path per `scripts/lib/gate-paths.txt`, hence this issue rather than an edit from the lane that hit it — to scan every `infra/cloudbuild/*.yaml` for bare `$NAME` templates whose NAME is not a Cloud Build built-in, **including lines inside comments**, and fail by name. A committed allow-list of the built-ins plus the lowercase-tolerated shape is enough; the rule only has to be as strict as the validator that refuses the build.

Suggested `Verify:` `bash scripts/check-cloudbuild.sh` with a provoked fixture: a config carrying a bare `$GH_TOKEN` in a comment must exit non-zero and name the key, and the same config with `${GH_TOKEN:-}` must exit 0.

## Provenance

Found while closing #1350 (PR #1354). The lane verified its own fix by diffing the bare-template set against the last **accepted** build's config (`comm -13` → empty) rather than by asserting it; that diff is the check this gate should carry.

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1350
Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1361

items.title: the composite's venue-invalid verdict has no provocation control (the #1351 half that a /tmp driver covered)
items.body:
## What is missing

Issue #1351's acceptance bullet 4 asked for the venue-invalid verdict to be
"provoked by a control in the gate suite (a scratch venue whose admin dir is
removed), and the mutant that drops the venue check REDs it by name".

The composite half landed in #1351 (PR #1359), but its evidence for that bullet
is a `/tmp` driver — not a durable control. Measured on the merged head:

- `scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh` **does** provoke the destruction: it builds a
  scratch venue, removes the admin dir its `.git` names, asserts `git rev-parse`
  fails inside it, and requires the **reaper** to name it `venue-invalid` — with
  its unheld twin still reaped in the same run, so the arm cannot pass by refusing
  everything. That is the #1345 half, and it is sound.
- **Nothing drives `scripts/verify.sh`'s own venue-invalid verdict**, and no mutant
  drops its venue probe:

  ```
  $ grep -rln 'venue-invalid' scripts/ governance/ | grep -v '^scripts/verify.sh$'
  scripts/prune-worktrees.sh
  scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh
  ```

  i.e. outside the implementation and the reaper, no file mentions it — so a
  regression in `verify.sh`'s venue probe (deleting the `.git`-FILE branch, or the
  read-back assertions `venue-record-does-not-name-the-venue` /
  `venue-record-counts-checks-that-did-not-run`) would be caught by nothing.

## The delivered behaviour (for contrast — this IS reproduced)

```
$ cd /tmp/ao1359/venue && bash scripts/verify.sh verify
verify: CANNOT-ASSESS — venue-invalid: /tmp/ao1359/venue is not usable as a git checkout
 (its .git names a missing admin dir ...); 209 of 209 checks were not run
$ echo $?
2
```

with `venue_invalid` in `.verify/attestation.json` and
`check_count=0 / skipped=0 / checks=[]`.

## Remedy (bounded)

One more end state in `scripts/check-skip-ratchet.sh` — which already drives the
REAL `scripts/verify.sh` on a synthetic root, six end states deep — or a new
`scripts/check-venue-invalid.sh`:

1. build a synthetic root whose `.git` is a FILE naming a missing admin dir (no
   real repository needed), run the real `verify.sh verify` there, and assert:
   exactly ONE `venue-invalid` line naming the venue, rc 2, and
   `check_count=0` / `checks=[]` / `skipped=0` in the record it writes;
2. negative control: a gitless root (`git archive HEAD | tar -x`) must NOT fire it;
3. mutant: strip the `.git`-FILE branch (or the read-back assertion) from a COPY of
   `verify.sh` and require the assertion to fail by name.

## Negative control / acceptance

- Deleting the venue probe from `verify.sh` REDs the new control by name.
- A gitless root stays exactly as it was (no `venue-invalid`, per-check tri-state
  unchanged).

## Why it was filed rather than fixed inside #1351

The landing lane's owned-file list did not include a new check script, and
amending `scripts/check-skip-ratchet.sh` after the CI run that IS the PR's
evidence had started would have invalidated that evidence (the run measures a
frozen tree). A named, filed gap beats a claim.

Refs #1351 · #1345 · #1361
