items.title: cloudbuild: the verify container supplies no gh, docker, crontab or vendor/CMR — 12 checks can never assess there, and the skip ratchet refuses them by name
items.body:
## What is wrong

The Cloud Build trigger that posts the required `ao/gate-of-record` context
(`control-plane-verify (purebliss-ghl)`, `infra/cloudbuild/verify-trigger.yaml`)
runs `make verify` inside a **bare `python:3.14` container**. That container
supplies none of the tools a dozen of this repository's checks need, so those
checks answer `rc 2 CANNOT-ASSESS` on **every** run there:

| check | the container does not supply |
|---|---|
| `branch-protection` | an installable/authenticated `gh` |
| `repo-settings` | an installable/authenticated `gh` |
| `gate-status` | an installable/authenticated `gh` (live status never observed) |
| `module-registry` | `vendor/CMR/catalog/mandatory.tsv` (no network to init the submodule) |
| `module-brief` | `vendor/CMR/catalog/mandatory.tsv` |
| `cmr-pin` | `vendor/CMR/sync/validate-cmr-pin.py` |
| `cmr-knowledge` | `vendor/CMR/sync/validate-cmr-pin.py` |
| `diagrams-declaration` | `vendor/CMR/catalog/schemas/architecture-manifest.schema.json` |
| `codeidx-surface` | `vendor/CMR/templates/module/.mcp.json` |
| `fleet-cron-dev-run` | the docker compose v2 plugin |
| `fleet-cron-image` | docker (and a reachable daemon) |
| `worktree-cap` | the `crontab` binary the reaper's schedule is read from |

Each check already names its own reason, which is the evidence (verbatim from
the build log of PR #1327, `/tmp/b1327.log`, inherited byte-for-byte by PR #1359
— the same commits):

```
check-worktree-cap: CANNOT-ASSESS — reaper schedule could not be determined:
  prune-worktrees: schedule: CANNOT-ASSESS — crontab -l failed with rc=127:
  /workspace/scripts/prune-worktrees.sh: line 194: crontab: command not found
check-module-registry: CANNOT-ASSESS — the pinned hub catalog is absent
  expected vendor/CMR/catalog/mandatory.tsv and vendor/CMR/catalog/modules
  fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address
check-cmr-pin: CANNOT-ASSESS — vendor/CMR/sync/validate-cmr-pin.py not present
  (vendor/CMR submodule not initialized?)
CANNOT-ASSESS gh-unauthenticated: gh is not installed — install gh and run 'gh auth login'
CANNOT-ASSESS compose-plugin-missing: install the docker compose v2 plugin
  (docker compose version must succeed)
check-fleet-cron-image: CANNOT-ASSESS — docker not found; the live controls were not run
```

and the composite's whole verdict was:

```
verify: FAIL (0 of 207 checks failed, 12 skipped: branch-protection, repo-settings,
 gate-status, module-registry, cmr-pin, module-brief, diagrams-declaration,
 codeidx-surface, cmr-knowledge, fleet-cron-dev-run, fleet-cron-image, worktree-cap;
 skip ratchet FAIL: 12 unnamed skip -- named above)
```

## Why it matters (and why it is filed rather than repaired in place)

**Zero checks failed.** The run is red *only* because the skip ratchet
(#1199) correctly refuses to let 12 anonymous `CANNOT-ASSESS` results ride a
`PASS`. That is the ratchet working — and it exposes a second defect: the CI
venue is a *different venue* from every lane's worktree, so a change can be
green locally and red in CI **for an environment reason that no lane can see
from its own box**. That is indistinguishable, in the required check's
conclusion, from a real defect.

## Remedy (two tracks — either closes this)

1. **Supply the venue**: install `gh` (+ a token) and docker with the compose v2
   plugin in the verify image, and make `vendor/CMR` available without network
   (vendored tarball or a shallow fetch with credentials) — then every one of the
   12 assesses and its exemption must be deleted (the ratchet fails a stale
   exemption by name, so this track is self-enforcing).
2. **Name them as venue limits** in `scripts/skip-budget.json`, which is what the
   ratchet's `venue` kind is for: a check that cannot assess because a **named
   precondition of this venue** is absent. This issue is the open board item those
   entries point at, so the blindness is explicit and shrink-only rather than
   silent.

Track 2 is landing with this issue (lane `issue-1351`, PR #1359): 6 entries name
the absent repo-relative path (`vendor/CMR/...`), and 6 name the **command the
venue must be able to run** — and each commanded precondition is the check's OWN
probe, quoted verbatim (`gh auth status`, `docker compose version`,
`docker info`, `crontab -l`), ratified by `scripts/check-skip-ratchet.sh`
against the tree so the budget cannot invent one.

## Acceptance

- Every check in the table above is either **assessed** in the Cloud Build venue
  or **named as a venue limit** in `scripts/skip-budget.json` pointing at this
  issue; the trigger's conclusion is `success` on `master`.
- A named venue limit whose precondition IS supplied while the check still cannot
  assess **fails the run by name** (proved by a provoked control, not asserted).
- Closing this issue requires one of: the container supplies the four tools and
  the submodule (entries deleted), or the checks are repaired to assess without
  them.

Refs #1199 (the ratchet that surfaced this) #1350 (the check's producer) #1341
(the cron cron image's docker rung) #1295 (verify-on-shared-services direction).
GR-12, GR-29 (a doc-only rule is advisory — this one names its gate).

_AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW) — measured from the Cloud Build
log of PR #1327/PR #1359; log retained at `/tmp/b1327.log`._

items.title: reaper: the scheduled rung omits --branches, so landed branches age past the 24h grace and red check-reconcile for every lane
items.body:
## The defect, in one line

`config/fleet-jobs.json:41` declares the nightly reap rung as

```json
"command": "bash scripts/prune-worktrees.sh --apply",
```

and the installed crontab line (marker `ao-fleet-reap`, `47 3 * * *`) is byte-identical.
**Neither passes `--branches`,** so the branch half landed by #1118 (PR #1118: "the reaper
reaps landed lane branches by content") is **never executed by the schedule**. Only the
worktree half runs.

## Measured 2026-09-18 at `origin/master = 4b43c35b`, from a detached worktree

```
$ bash scripts/prune-worktrees.sh --strict --branches        # dry
prune-worktrees: 154 landed branch(es) reapable, 118 kept (not provably landed)
prune-worktrees: schedule: SCHEDULED — 1 installed crontab line(s) invoke prune-worktrees.sh

$ git branch | wc -l
304

$ bash scripts/prune-worktrees.sh --strict --branches --apply
prune-worktrees: 8 stale, 31 kept ...
prune-worktrees: 154 landed branch(es) reapable, 118 kept

$ git branch | wc -l ; git worktree list | wc -l
150                  33        # 154 branches drained, 8 stale worktrees reclaimed
```

The tool already says so in its own exit contract:

```
prune-worktrees: NOT-OK — 154 landed branch(es) still exist; run with --branches --apply
```

## Why it matters — this is what reds the gate of record for everyone

`scripts/check-reconcile.sh` compares the **real tree** (this box's branches and worktrees)
against a committed baseline, with a 24 h grace for young artifacts. A baselined-and-unmatched
entry is *stale* and non-fatal; an artifact **not in the baseline and older than the grace** is
a fatal `NEW` violation, and `check-reconcile` then exits **1**.

So the pile is a time bomb: every landed branch that lives past 24 h eventually crosses the
grace and becomes a fatal violation — **with no code change at all**. Measured twice today:

| artifact | appeared as | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| worktree `ao-1178` (landed by content; patch-id equal to `870eb26`) | `NEW worktree … not in the baseline` | `check-reconcile: FAIL (1 violation(s))` |
| `branch issue-1145-baseline` (`093b2d64`) | `NEW branch … not in the baseline` | same, again at ~22:58Z when a second artifact aged out |
| `branch issue-1145-residue` (`2b3d8475`) | `NEW branch … not in the baseline` | same |

The blast radius is fleet-wide, not local: on pristine master the gate of record reads
`verify: FAIL (1 of 205 checks failed)` with `reconcile` the only non-zero check, and
`governance/landing` refuses **every** landing because `verify` is the one signal it never
attributes (`signal-red-is-not-attributable`). Reclaiming the stray `ao-1178` lane took
pristine master back to `verify: PASS (203 of 203 checks)`; the pile then put it back.

## The two residual branches

`issue-1145-baseline` and `issue-1145-residue` are in the reaper's "118 kept (not provably
landed)" set. Each changes exactly **one** file:

```
governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json     # both, 1 file each
```

That is a baseline **RECORD**, not product work, and master's current copy supersedes both.
Their own `git patch-id --stable` values (`20c0dfbea7854f84f51e19e877a8c63de7606c24` and
`85038cb914f592dbf7df90e30d6db538db3bbc19`) do not match any of the last 400 commits on
`master`, which is why the content test keeps them — the same squash-onto-a-moved-base shape
as #1298. They need a terminal decision (land / push / authorise deletion) under the
real-tree quarantine, whose live tracker is #1338.

## What I am asking for

1. Add `--branches` to the scheduled rung (`config/fleet-jobs.json` + the installed crontab
   via `fleet/cron.py install`), so the branch pile cannot rebuild. The worktree half is
   already scheduled; only the branch half is missing.
2. Make the schedule's own definition of "the reap" a **gate**: a check that fails by name
   when the declared rung omits `--branches`, so it cannot silently regress again.
3. Decide the two residual branches under #1338.

## What I did NOT do

I ran the drain by hand (`--branches --apply`) to unblock the box, and I reclaimed one stray
landed worktree. I did **not** edit `config/fleet-jobs.json` or the crontab, and I did **not**
reap the two residual branches — their disposal is a terminal decision, not a cleanup.

Measured while filing: 47 dangling gate venues were also reported
(`venue-invalid: 47 dangling venue(s) … a gate run inside one reports false CANNOT-ASSESS
verdicts folded into skipped (#1345)`).

items.title: check-gate-status: the gate that polices the required context is green while the context has no producer — a required-but-unproduced check is a bypass generator and must red by name
items.body:
## Defect (measured 2026-09-18, `master` @ `2151f9884593d550f86816f84d2fde574d441d96`)

Branch protection on `master` now **requires** the context `ao/gate-of-record`:

```
$ gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/branches/master/protection \
    --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts'
["ao/gate-of-record"]
```

…and no producer **on the path that produces the verdict** posts it, so every PR head is
`BLOCKED` and merges have only been proceeding because `enforce_admins.enabled` is `false` — an
admin bypass.

Both policing gates are **green** while this is true:

```
$ bash scripts/check-gate-status.sh            -> OK        (rc 0)
$ bash scripts/check-branch-protection.sh      -> OK        (rc 0)
```

`check-gate-status.sh` even prints the inertness and calls it expected:

```
  note  no ao/gate-of-record status on HEAD — expected until the poster runs in the runner
check-gate-status: OK — the mapping is exhaustive, provoked and the poster builds without writing
```

and its own comment still asserts a precondition that is no longer true ("the context is not yet
required (that is a separate, deliberate step)"), while `governance/platform/branch-protection.yaml`
now declares it in `protection.required_status_checks.contexts`.

## The general form

A required context whose producer does not exist is **not a control; it is a bypass generator**.
The existing gate proves only that the two context *strings* agree (declaration vs poster, #1072) —
it never proves that anything **produces** the status, so it is green on a frozen repository.
`check-verdict-contains`-style honesty requires that "no status observed" never be reported as a
pass.

## What to build (detection half only — #1350/#1343 own the producer)

`scripts/check-gate-status.sh`:
1. assert that the required context is actually **produced** — either a status observed on the
   commit under test, or **CANNOT-ASSESS naming the missing producer**, never a green;
2. **fail by name** when the context is required (declared in
   `governance/platform/branch-protection.yaml` / live protection) **and** no producer path exists,
   naming the context and the missing producer.

`scripts/check-branch-protection.sh`:
3. red when `protection.required_status_checks` is required while `gate-status.sh` cannot produce the
   context — a required-but-unproduced check is a **named condition, not a green**.

Provocation (all halves shown, negative control included):
- plant the inert state (required context present, no producer) → red **by name**;
- healthy state (producer present) → green;
- unobservable case → **rc 2 CANNOT-ASSESS**, never 0;
- negative control: context **not** required → the rule must not fire at all.

## Acceptance

- On the real current repository the policing gate reports the inertness **by name**
  (or rc 2 with the missing producer named) — output pasted on the PR.
- Every provocation half shown, including the negative control that stops the rule matching
  everything.
- `check-verdict-contains`-style honesty: no non-zero exit collapsed into a pass.

## Scope / lane ownership

Owns `scripts/check-gate-status.sh`, `scripts/check-branch-protection.sh` only.
Reads (does not edit) `scripts/gate-status.sh`, `scripts/verify.sh`,
`governance/platform/branch-protection.yaml`.

items.title: verify.sh folds a destroyed venue into 20 'skipped' checks instead of one named venue-invalid verdict (the composite half of #1345)
items.body:
## What is wrong

`scripts/verify.sh` folds a check's `rc 2 CANNOT-ASSESS` into `skipped`, so a gate
venue whose git linkage has been destroyed reports **20 independent skips** instead
of **one named venue-invalid condition**. The verdict line then reads like a small,
believable failure instead of "this venue is not a git checkout, so 20 checks
assessed nothing".

Measured while closing **#1345** (2026-09-18, `master` `335c9a34`, gate transcript
`/tmp/ao-hp/gates/M2/run.log`):

```
verify: FAIL (5 of 203 checks failed, 20 skipped: fleet-runbook, reconcile, board-gate,
 lessons, scratch-safety, cto-overlay, module-registry, cmr-pin, module-brief,
 diagrams-declaration, codeidx-surface, cmr-knowledge, cockpit, git-config, gitignore,
 isolation-landed, prune-worktrees, pytest-rootdir, shell-patterns, ungated-suites)
```

and the checks name the cause themselves:

```
check-gitignore:       CANNOT-ASSESS — root is not a git work tree: /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-hpg-M2
check-prune-worktrees: CANNOT-ASSESS — not inside a repository
check-shell-patterns:  CANNOT-ASSESS — no shell file to scan (is this a git checkout?)
```

`shell-patterns`, `gitignore`, `git-config` and `isolation-landed` are pure-local
checks: they can reach `rc 2` only if the **venue** stopped being a checkout. The
composite cannot tell those 20 skips from 20 honest ones.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed in #1345

`scripts/verify.sh` was owned by two open PRs while #1345 was worked — one issue =
one lane = one file (AGENTS.md rule 2), so the lane filed this instead of editing.
Measured 2026-09-18T21:50Z:

```
$ gh pr list --state open --limit 200 --json number,headRefName,files \
    --jq '.[] | select([.files[].path] | any(. == "scripts/verify.sh")) | ...'
1344 [issue-1341] flip: schedule the promote-portal rung, prep cron-image docker, wire PR context
1327 [issue-1199] fix(gate): make verify's skip bucket ratchet, so a permanently blind check cannot read as PASS
```

## What #1345 DID land (the reaper half, in its own lane)

`scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` now NAMES the condition, so it is no longer invisible —
and this is measured on the real box, not asserted:

```
  BROKEN /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-1310-95a6c762 — venue-invalid: its .git names a
    missing admin dir /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/.git/worktrees/ao-1310-95a6c762,
    so no git command can run inside it; NOT a removal candidate (#1345)
  BROKEN /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-hpg-1327 — venue-invalid: its .git names a missing
    admin dir /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/.git/worktrees/ao-hpg-1327, ...
...
prune-worktrees: venue-invalid: 48 dangling venue(s) named above; a gate run inside one
  reports false CANNOT-ASSESS verdicts folded into skipped (#1345)
```

**48 dangling venues** on this box on 2026-09-18 (independently confirmed for two of
them: `gitdir` target absent, `git rev-parse HEAD` → `fatal: not a git repository`,
and `git worktree list` no longer lists them). It is also a `--check` finding (rc 1).

The reaper is where a venue's life cycle lives, but it is not what a reader consults
for a VERDICT — so the composite half stays open here.

## Bounded remedy

Decide the venue's validity **once, before the check loop**, and report ONE named
verdict:

- if `$root/.git` is a file naming a missing admin dir, or `git -C "$root" rev-parse
  HEAD` fails, the run reports exactly one line — `verify: CANNOT-ASSESS — venue-invalid:
  <root> is not usable as a git checkout (<detail>); N of M checks were not run` — and
  records `venue_invalid` in `.verify/attestation.json`, instead of attributing 20
  independent `rc 2` results to 20 checks;
- a venue that IS valid keeps today's per-check tri-state untouched (no new skip, no
  new verdict, no new failure).

#1199's skip ratchet is adjacent but not a substitute: it would flag "too many skips",
not "this venue is invalid", and it cannot name the venue.

## Acceptance / negative control

- A gate run in a venue whose admin dir vanished reports ONE `venue-invalid` line
  naming the venue, and `attestation.json` carries `venue_invalid`.
- That run does NOT report the 20 checks as individual `CANNOT-ASSESS` skips.
- A gate in a healthy venue is byte-for-byte unchanged in its verdict shape.
- Provoked by a control in the gate suite (a scratch venue whose admin dir is
  removed), and the mutant that drops the venue check REDs it by name.

## Verify

```
bash scripts/verify.sh verify     # run inside a venue whose admin dir has been removed
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.verify/attestation.json'));print(d.get('venue_invalid'))"
make verify
```

Refs #1345 #1159 #1199 #724. (GR-12, AO-GR-12.)

_AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash) — measured on this box while closing #1345; reaper evidence at `/tmp/ao1345-reapB.txt`._

items.title: cloudbuild: the verify runner posts ao/gate-of-record with the gate's own rc — the required check gets a producer
items.body:
Parent: #1254

The now-required check `ao/gate-of-record` (#1342) has no producer that posts it on the PR head. The Cloud Build verify runner (infra/cloudbuild/verify.yaml) should run `make verify`, capture rc, and post the status via `scripts/gate-status.sh post --sha <sha> --rc <rc>` using a GH_TOKEN pulled from Secret Manager. rc 2 (CANNOT-ASSESS) must post 'error', never 'success'. If the token secret is absent, log and skip posting without failing the step.

items.title: fleet image: install the docker CLI so the promote-portal rung can pull and recreate the console
items.body:
Parent: #1329

The promote-portal rung (#1336, scheduled-disabled by #1344) needs the docker CLI inside the fleet cron image. #1344 mounted `/var/run/docker.sock` read-only on the `agent-cron-rw` service and documented the requirement under a `state_rw` section of `infra/fleet/inventory.yaml`, but left `infra/fleet/Dockerfile` out of its scope (see that PR's "## Wiring needed").

This issue installs the docker CLI in `infra/fleet/Dockerfile` and declares it in `infra/fleet/inventory.yaml`'s `packages`/`binaries` lists (the ones `scripts/check-fleet-cron-image.sh` cross-checks against the Dockerfile in both directions), so `docker run --rm <image> docker --version` succeeds.

items.title: reconcile: master is red on the lease — remove the resolved /tmp/ao968-pristine exemption (fix-forward from #1339)
items.body:
## What is red

`origin/master` is **red on `reconcile`** — the check that blocks every lane's composite gate.
Measured in a pristine detached worktree at `origin/master = 335c9a347d44d9d420eb21208d90772953acc68b`
(2026-09-18T21:45Z):

```
check-reconcile: FAIL — real tree drifted from governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json (0 new-and-old, 515 stale, not fatal; 1 stale quarantine exemption(s))
real-tree-baseline: 81 unmatched artifact(s) on disk, 557 baselined, 33 young (< 24h, not failed), 515 stale (not failed), 0 vanished (not failed), 6 quarantined by name (reported, not failed)
  quarantine: honoured — #1338 open, measured 1.6h ago (lease 24h, by governance/reconcile (issue #1311 lane))
  STALE-QUARANTINE worktree /tmp/ao968-pristine — quarantined but no longer an unmatched artifact at its declared venue.
check-reconcile: FAIL (2 violation(s))
MASTER-CHECK-RECONCILE-RC=1
```

## Why, exactly

PR `#1339` (this document's own lane) was merged at `20:35:34Z` on head **`afca46e`** — that is
`6c36c6f4` on `master`. Its lane then kept working for one more cycle because the **composite gate
was PARKED behind four peer runs** at the time of the merge, and when it finally ran
(`21:00Z`, `verify: FAIL (1 of 203)`) it reported exactly this violation:

```
check-reconcile: FAIL — … 1 stale quarantine exemption(s)
  STALE-QUARANTINE worktree /tmp/ao968-pristine — quarantined but no longer an unmatched artifact at its declared venue.
```

The artifact was reaped — by the machine's own `/tmp` scratch guard — **after** the document was
written and **before** the gate could run. The exemption stopped targeting an unmatched artifact
while the lane was still open, which is precisely what the document's own rule says must fail:

> an entry that no longer targets an unmatched artifact FAILS as a stale exemption … until it is
> removed in a reviewed edit.

The lane diagnosed it and fixed it in `e93e645` (the entry removed, the resolution recorded in the
note), and that commit verified **green** — `verify: PASS (203 of 203 checks)`,
`git_sha = e93e645148e7855ce5661753563dedbbfc987c16`, `exit_code 0`, no non-zero rows — but by then
`#1339` had already merged, so the fix never reached `master`.

## The measurement that decides the removal (taken before acting)

The document's own stale-entry reason names two cases, and they need different answers:

| question | measured |
|---|---|
| does `/tmp/ao968-pristine` still exist? | only as a dangling directory — `git status` there returns rc 128 (`not a git repository`) and it is absent from `git worktree list`: its git admin directory is gone, so it is no longer an artifact of this repository |
| is it still an unmatched artifact? | no — the audit does not examine it at all |
| what did it hold? | one **uncommitted** file: `portal/tests/test_fleet_syspath_isolation.py` |
| is that file on the default branch? | **yes** — landed by `3aadeda` (`fix(portal): give back the fleet/ entry load_fleet_console() borrows (#968) (#1087)`) |

So this is the **resolution** case ("the work reached the default branch — a resolution — remove
it"), not the reclaimed-with-work-lost case. Nothing was discarded.

## Fix

One reviewed edit to `governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json`: remove that entry (it is the
only stale one), and record in the document's note *why* it went — the resolution and its commit.
The 6 entries that remain are the ones whose work is on no other ref, re-measured at write time.
The lease keeps naming **#1338**, its live tracker, which stays open.

No code changes: the rule that caught this (`RealTreeVerdict.refuted_quarantine` and the pre-existing
stale-exemption rule) is already on `master` from `6c36c6f4`.

**Verify:** `bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh` exits 0 at the fix's head, and the document holds no
stale exemption.

```bash
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json'));print(d['tracked_by'], d['tracking']['state'], len(d['quarantine']))"
bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh
```

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1339
Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1338

items.title: the reaper deletes a gate venue's git admin dir mid-run, and 20 checks silently fold into 'skipped'
items.body:
## What is wrong

The worktree reaper **destroys the git admin directory of a worktree that a running `make verify` is using**, and the gate then reports a **false verdict**: every git-dependent check degrades to `rc 2 CANNOT-ASSESS` and the composite folds them into `skipped`, so the verdict line reads like a small, believable failure instead of "20 checks assessed nothing".

Measured on this box, 2026-09-18, while I was gating `origin/master` (`5c69fd07`) in a fresh detached worktree created for the purpose.

## Measurement

Five gate venues were created with `git worktree add --detach … <commit>` under the normal venue root `/home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/`, each driven by its own detached `make verify`. Six earlier ones (labels `BASE`, `1293`, `1296`, `1216`, `1281`, `NOW`) are **gone entirely**; five later ones still have a directory but are **no longer registered**:

```
$ git worktree list | wc -l
31
$ ls -d /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-hpg-* | wc -l
5
$ git worktree list | grep -c 'ao-hpg'
0
```

The surviving directory still holds its `.git` **file**, pointing at an admin dir that no longer exists:

```
$ cat /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-hpg-M2/.git
gitdir: /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/.git/worktrees/ao-hpg-M2

$ git -C /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-hpg-M2 rev-parse HEAD
fatal: not a git repository: /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/.git/worktrees/ao-hpg-M2
```

The gate that ran **inside** that venue, verbatim:

```
$ grep -E '^verify: ' /tmp/ao-hp/gates/M2/run.log
verify: FAIL (5 of 203 checks failed, 20 skipped: fleet-runbook, reconcile, board-gate,
 lessons, scratch-safety, cto-overlay, module-registry, cmr-pin, module-brief,
 diagrams-declaration, codeidx-surface, cmr-knowledge, cockpit, git-config, gitignore,
 isolation-landed, prune-worktrees, pytest-rootdir, shell-patterns, ungated-suites)
```

and the checks name the cause themselves:

```
check-gitignore:         CANNOT-ASSESS — root is not a git work tree: /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-hpg-M2
check-prune-worktrees:   CANNOT-ASSESS — not inside a repository
check-pytest-rootdir:    CANNOT-ASSESS — not inside a git worktree …
check-shell-patterns:    CANNOT-ASSESS — no shell file to scan (is this a git checkout?)
check-isolation-landed:  CANNOT-ASSESS — the lane tri-state and every provoked control
                         passed, but real landed history in HEAD could not be assessed
```

**20 of 203 checks assessed nothing.** On a stable venue at the same era the same composite reported `2 skipped`. The 20 include `shell-patterns`, `gitignore`, `git-config`, `isolation-landed` — pure-local checks that can only reach `rc 2` if the venue itself has stopped being a git checkout.

## Why the reaper selects live gate venues

A gate venue created for measurement is **detached at a commit that is preserved on `origin`** — the default branch itself, or an open PR's head. That is precisely the class the reaper's own line calls removable:

```
$ timeout 300 python3 fleet/cron.py reap
  STALE  /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-gate-1311 — removable (HEAD afca46ecfae2efae9d7380bad5ffbf535ae2c737 preserved on origin)
  STALE  /home/akushnir/.cache/leaderboard/tmp/claude-1000/apply-work — removable (HEAD 335c9a347d44d9d420eb21208d90772953acc68b preserved on origin)
  … 9 stale, 21 kept
  prune-worktrees: liveness: cwd+open files (cwd fd), under match; 14961 live path(s) seen, 9 of 100 worktree(s) held
```

So the widened `/proc/*/cwd` **and** `/proc/*/fd/*` predicate from #1159 is still not sufficient here, and the reason is structural rather than incidental: a gate's liveness is **not** a long-lived cwd or a long-lived open fd. `make verify` runs a sequence of short-lived check processes; between two checks nothing is guaranteed to hold the directory, and a scan that lands in that window sees a tree with no holder. `cwd` is only held by the *driver* shell, so this also means the driver-shell case is not universally matched — my own driver `cd`s into the venue and stays there for the whole run, and the admin dir was still removed underneath it.

## Why it matters

It corrupts **evidence**, which is this repo's currency. A lane that gates in a reaped venue publishes a false FAIL set and a false `verify:` count, and because `rc 2` is folded into `skipped`, the composite's verdict line still looks like a small honest failure. The blast radius is any session on this box that creates a scratch venue under the venue root (or under `$HOME`) and gates in it — which is how most lanes measure.

## Suggested remedy (not prescriptive)

1. **Never remove a worktree that is in use by a gate.** The gate already holds a **box-wide permit** and a per-worktree lock (`scripts/gate-lock.sh`): the permit store names the holder pid and the holder worktree. The reaper should refuse any worktree named by a live permit/lock, which is a *declared* liveness signal rather than a `/proc` race.
2. **Refuse unnamed/harness-created trees and scratch venues** unless an explicit allowlist authorises them (this is the other half of #1159, already filed as **#1337**).
3. **Make the destruction detectable**: a venue whose `.git` file points at a missing admin dir should be a *named* condition, not 20 independent `CANNOT-ASSESS` verdicts. The composite could refuse to report a verdict at all when the venue is not a repository.

## Acceptance

- A gate venue with a **live permit held by its own driver** is never removed; the reaper reports it `KEEP` naming the permit.
- The mutant that ignores the permit/lock signal **REDs** `scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh`.
- A gate run in a venue whose admin dir vanished reports a **named venue-invalid** condition rather than 20 `CANNOT-ASSESS` checks folded into `skipped`.
- `python3 fleet/cron.py reap` (dry) on a box with live gate venues names none of them removable.

## Evidence lineage

Measured while verifying open PRs for the `#1233`/`#1203`/`#1199` lanes. Related: **#1159** (widened the predicate to open files — necessary but not sufficient for a gate's short-lived readers), **#1337** (refuse unnamed-worktree reaping), **#1265** (worktree/lane cap and the reaper's declared schedule), **#1212** (the sibling class where a venue difference silently changes a verdict).

_AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash) — measured on this box, gate transcripts at `/tmp/ao-hp/gates/M2/run.log`._

items.title: runner: institutionalise the shared-services PR runner — verify each PR head, publish ao/gate-of-record, merge through the guard on merged-tree green; tested, gated, scheduled, with its own lessons
items.body:
Parent: #1295

## What exists (prototype, 2026-09-18, on 192.168.168.42 as nohup shell scripts in ~/ao-runner)
- `host-verify.sh`: every 90–240 s list open non-draft PRs; for each head without green evidence, `git worktree add --detach` in a scratch clone, run `bash scripts/verify.sh verify` (up to 3 parallel, honouring the box gate-lock), record rc to `local-green/<pr>-<sha>`, treat PARKED (rc 11) as retry-later, then `scripts/gate-status.sh post --sha <head> --rc <rc>` (context `ao/gate-of-record`).
- `host-merge.sh`: every 2 min, for each open PR with green evidence (Cloud Build `control-plane-verify` SUCCESS for that exact head, or the local marker `0`) and `mergeable == MERGEABLE`: `check-squash-message.sh --pr N` → `gh pr merge --squash` → verify the new master tip classifies `None` under `governance.isolation.trailer.classify_commit` (stop hard otherwise); `hold.txt` for holds.

## Lessons measured today that the tool must encode (each becomes a control AND a ledger LESSON record)
1. Evidence is per (pr, head sha), never per PR — a pushed head invalidates all prior evidence; stale builds/verifies for old heads must be cancelled/skipped (they ate ~40% of runner capacity today).
2. EXPIRED/CANCELLED/PARKED are terminal-not-green: re-queue by name, never wait (#1267 class).
3. Merge only on green evidence for master+PR at the moment of merging (#1254 step 6; four green-alone-red-together incidents) — consume `pr-queue.sh`'s merged-tree seam (#1332), don't reimplement.
4. Never bare `gh pr merge`: squash guard first; PR body's last paragraph is the trailer; `Closes #<n>` derived from the branch (#1266).
5. A runner that cannot reach a precondition (gh auth, docker compose, AR creds, the auth-gate env) reports CANNOT-ASSESS by name (#1313) and is never counted green; host-env reds must not block merges that Cloud Build proved — evidence sources are ranked and both recorded.
6. Detached scratch worktrees are reapable by the content-equivalence rule (#1335) — the runner must hold its worktree (cwd/open fd) for the whole run and remove it itself afterwards; never leave a worktree the reaper has to guess about.
7. Gate-lock permits leak when a run is killed — prune with `fleet/gatelock.py prune --apply` before each cycle; the runner's own runs carry pids the pruner can verify.
8. Parallel `git fetch` on one clone races (`cannot lock ref`) — serialise fetches with a lock; use explicit refspecs so `refs/remotes/origin/master` exists on a detached checkout (#1332's fix).
9. The loop must survive its supervisor dying (nohup → a declared rung/systemd unit), log to a ledger, and expose a status verb (`what is verifying, what merged, what is blocked and why`).
10. A required check with a context nothing posts blocks everyone forever — the poster (`gate-status.sh`) and the protection (`governance/platform/branch-protection.yaml`) name the same string, proved by `check-gate-status.sh`.

## Shape
- `fleet/runner/` (Python, same style as `infra/fleet/promote_portal.py`): `plan.py` (pure: inputs = open PRs+heads, evidence table, live builds, markers → actions: verify(pr,sha) / cancel-stale(build) / merge(pr) / hold(pr,reason)), `evidence.py` (sources: cloud-build check-run, gate-status read-back, local marker; ranked, per-sha), `verify.py` (worktree lifecycle + gate-lock prune + verify + post status), `merge.py` (calls `scripts/merge-pr.sh` — the guarded entrypoint — never `gh pr merge` directly), `cli.py` (`plan`, `run --once`, `run --loop`, `status`, `hold`, `unhold`), all transports injected; tests for every lesson above as a named negative control.
- Ledger: `.fleet/runner/ledger.jsonl` (verify results, posts, merges, refusals with names).
- Declared schedule: a rung in `fleet/cron.py` + `config/fleet-jobs.json` (`runner`, enabled on the shared-services pair only, via `AO_RUNNER_HOST_ROLE=primary` from the env contract) — the prototype nohup processes are retired when the rung is live.
- Gate `scripts/check-pr-runner.sh`: plan fixtures for lessons 1–5 refuse by name; worktree-held-and-removed (6); prune-before-run (7); serialized fetch (8); status verb answers from the ledger (9); poster/protection context parity reused from check-gate-status (10). Mutants: drop the stale-head skip → caught; drop the merged-tree check → caught.
- `governance/lessons/ledger.jsonl`: one LESSON per lesson above that is not already recorded (check LESSON-0008/RCA-0018 and #1261's chain), each with the measured incident from today and the control that now enforces it; declared local-only in `governance/lessons-sync/cmr-ledger.json` (#1125 rule).
- Docs: `docs/PR-RUNNER.md` (what it does, evidence ranking, how to hold, status, the owner steps), one paragraph in `docs/PR-QUEUE.md`, AGENTS.md sentence: "the runner merges; sessions open PRs".

## Acceptance
- On the pair: `python3 fleet/runner/cli.py run --once` verifies every open head lacking evidence, posts `ao/gate-of-record`, merges the greens through `merge-pr.sh`, and `status` explains every open PR by name.
- Every lesson has a failing fixture that the control refuses by name; `make verify` runs the gate green.
- The nohup prototypes are removed from ~/ao-runner and the rung is scheduled (enabled) on 192.168.168.42.

items.title: reconcile: the 7 residual real-tree quarantine exemptions need a per-artifact owner call (successor to #1311)
items.body:
Parent: #1268

## What this owns

The **residual** of `#1311` — the named exemptions in
`governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json` whose work really does exist on no
other ref, which `AGENTS.md` **rule 17** forbids the worker to discard. `#1311`
re-measured all 25 entries it inherited and took the document from **25 to 7**: 15 were
refuted (their whole committed work is on the default branch by `git patch-id --stable`)
and 3 more had their work preserved on a remote branch (measured live with
`git ls-remote`), and all 18 were recorded by name in the reviewed baseline
(`real-tree-baseline.json`, 539 → 557). This issue is the lease's `tracked_by` from that
edit onward — the document's own rule is that closing its tracker lapses every exemption,
so the tracker must be an issue that stays open while these 7 remain unresolved.

Every row below was re-measured at **2026-09-18T20:02:16Z** against `origin/master`
`0dbb0e681997` with the same refuter the gate runs:
`landing.RepoLanding.surplus_patch_identity` (patch identity over the default branch's
commits touching the artifact's changed paths) plus
`governance/isolation/worktree.foreign_uncommitted` (the repository's own declaration of
the paths a reclaim must refuse — `.board/focus.json`, `.board/snapshot.json` and
`.fleet/` are declared machine-managed, i.e. **not** lane work).

## The 7, and what each needs

| artifact | tip | why it is still here (measured) | needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| branch issue-1028-canon | `88ea96d70a3f` | its work is on **no** default-branch commit (16 candidate(s) — the commits touching its 7 changed path(s) — patch-compared; none carries `e691e5c35b16`); its tip is an ancestor of nothing on `origin/master`; it is carried by no remote-tracking ref; `origin/issue-1028-canon` exists at `a1a8b50e8d6e` and does **not** contain this tip | land it, push it, or authorise its deletion |
| branch issue-1114-dispatch-master-green | `d084114b73e8` | its work is on **no** default-branch commit (101 candidate(s) — the commits touching its 11 changed path(s) — patch-compared; none carries `6b1f931cc10f`); its tip is an ancestor of nothing on `origin/master`; it is carried by no remote-tracking ref | land it, push it, or authorise its deletion |
| branch issue-830-reaper-schedule | `af843aaf8289` | its work is on **no** default-branch commit (8 candidate(s) — the commits touching its 1 changed path(s) — patch-compared; none carries `4c9bf17614f0`); its tip is an ancestor of nothing on `origin/master`; it is carried by no remote-tracking ref; `origin/issue-830-reaper-schedule` exists at `3748194c2d40` and does **not** contain this tip | land it, push it, or authorise its deletion |
| worktree `/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/.claude/worktrees/agent-a1b5cf2e0dceac199` | `d084114b73e8` | its HEAD is on no default-branch commit (101 candidate(s) touching its 11 changed path(s), patch-compared); its only dirty paths are machine-managed (`.board/focus.json`), so the exemption rests on the unmerged commits at its HEAD | land it, push it, or authorise its deletion |
| worktree `/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad284eb1ac275c0c6` | `9e5a61528752` | its HEAD **is** on the default branch by ancestry; it holds **its own** uncommitted work — `governance/ticket/tests/conftest.py` — which is on no branch at all; its tip is contained in refs/remotes/origin/HEAD | land it, push it, or authorise its deletion |
| worktree `/home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/.claude/worktrees/agent-afc588dba96686e4e` | `47ac6de35e04` | its HEAD is on no default-branch commit (45 candidate(s) touching its 81 changed path(s), patch-compared); its only dirty paths are machine-managed (`.fleet/reconcile/ledger.jsonl`, `.fleet/watchdog.lease`), so the exemption rests on the unmerged commits at its HEAD | land it, push it, or authorise its deletion |
| worktree `/tmp/ao968-pristine` | `96ae0fba19c3` | its HEAD **is** on the default branch by ancestry; it holds **its own** uncommitted work — `portal/tests/test_fleet_syspath_isolation.py` — which is on no branch at all; its tip is contained in refs/remotes/origin/HEAD | land it, push it, or authorise its deletion |

Nothing here may be discarded by a lane: rule 17 is explicit that an orphan whose work
exists nowhere else keeps its worktree, its branch and its claim, and is **reported on
every pass until someone resolves it**. The exemption is what makes that report
non-fatal; the resolution is the owner's call, per artifact.

## How a resolution closes

Three terminal states, in the order the document prefers:

1. **land** it — the work reaches the default branch, and the entry is refuted by the
   refuter above (the gate will say so by name on the next pass);
2. **push** it — the branch reaches a remote, so the artifact stops being the only copy
   (the reaper's `parked` outcome, `#1265`);
3. **authorise its deletion** — the only case where work that exists nowhere else may be
   discarded, and explicitly an owner decision.

Whichever is chosen, the entry goes in the **same reviewed edit** that records the
resolution, and this issue closes when the document holds no entry whose work exists
nowhere else — not before.

## Verify

```bash
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json'));print(d['tracked_by'], d['tracking']['state'], len(d['quarantine']))"
bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh
python3 -m pytest -q governance/reconcile/tests
```

items.title: reaper: refuse to reap a tree it did not create without a lane record or a declared allowlist — the residue #1159's widened predicate cannot see
items.body:
## Observed (measured 2026-09-18, `master` `0dbb0e6`, PR #1326 as landed)

`scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` now treats a worktree as in use when a live process has it as its **cwd OR holds any open file under it** (`LIVE_SOURCES="cwd fd"`), landed by PR #1326 for #1159. That closes the measured gap, and the gate proves it: `scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh` exits 0, and reverting the predicate to cwd-only REDs the check by name.

It does **not** close the residue, and PR #1326's own body says so:

> The widened predicate sees a live process that is **holding** the tree ... It cannot see a peer that is *between* commands ... The issue's second remedy — refuse to reap a tree the reaper did not create unless a `.fleet/lanes/` record or an allowlist authorises it — ... is **not** implemented here ...

**The follow-up was not filed.** Measured 2026-09-18: searching every issue (`--state all`, limit 1000) for `reap|prune|unnamed|allowlist|did not create|liveness` returns no tracker for it. (#1265 is the worktree/lane cap and the declared schedule; #1284, closed, declared `.fleet/` as runtime state.) The PR's claim is unsubstantiated on the board, so this issue substantiates it.

## Measured residual (this box, 2026-09-18T19:58Z)

`python3 fleet/cron.py reap` (dry) — the Verify command #1159 shipped with:

```
prune-worktrees: 14 stale, 85 kept (dirty, in use, claimed, parked, or unpreserved)
prune-worktrees: liveness: cwd+open files (cwd fd), under match; 14961 live path(s) seen, 9 of 100 worktree(s) held
```

All 14 stale trees are dead on the evidence available: no process holds them (cwd or open file), none is dirty, every HEAD is preserved on `origin`, and every recent write in them is a **build artifact** — `__pycache__/*.pyc`, `.pytest_cache/v/cache/nodeids`, `.verify/{verify.log,attestation.json,.results.tsv}` — the newest 4 minutes before the sweep. So #1159's acceptance item "0 live trees classified stale" holds, and this issue is **not** a claim that #1159 was mis-closed.

The **shape** that made #1159 a data-loss risk is nevertheless unchanged: 9 of the 14 are `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` and 5 are scratch roots, and **none carries a `.fleet/lanes/` record**. A live harness session working in one of them is invisible to *any* `/proc` scan unless it happens to hold a descriptor at the exact instant the sweep runs — and `ao-fleet-reap` now runs `prune-worktrees.sh --apply` unattended from cron. The residual is bounded (no commits are at risk: HEADs are preserved) but it is real: the working directory is destroyed under a live session.

## Bounded remedy

Refuse to remove a tree the reaper did not create unless ownership is declared: require a `.fleet/lanes/` record, or a declared allowlist of the roots the reaper may reap from, before `--apply` removes a worktree.

This must **not** break #1159's existing acceptance item "a genuinely stale, preserved, unclaimed tree is still reaped" — the allowlist has to be a declared, owned list rather than a blanket refusal of unnamed trees. That ownership list is the reason PR #1326 deferred the remedy instead of guessing at it.

## Acceptance / negative control

- A tree outside the declared roots **and** without a `.fleet/lanes/` record is KEEP under `--apply`, alongside a twin inside a declared root that is still reaped.
- A genuinely stale, preserved tree inside a declared root is **still reaped** — nothing here refuses everything.
- The mutant that removes the ownership check **REDs** `scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh`, naming the arm.
- `python3 fleet/cron.py reap` (dry) reports **0 live trees classified stale**.

## Verify

```
python3 fleet/cron.py reap
bash scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh
make verify
```

items.title: pr-queue: a PR merges only on green evidence for master+PR at the moment of merging — merged-tree-red refused by name
items.body:
Parent: #1254

Measured 2026-09-18: four times, two PRs each green alone were red together — #1110+#1115 (`AO_FROZEN_CLOCK` vs env-surface gate), #1309+#1287 (`board.freshness` vs control-mapping), #1300 (box-local quarantine), #1246 (RCA doc ids) — because merges used per-PR-head build results, so the first build of the merged tree was the NEXT PR's, which inherited the red.

Rule: before `gh pr merge`, the queue requires evidence that `make verify`/`scripts/verify.sh verify` was green on a tree equal to `origin/master` (current tip, re-read immediately before merging) + this PR's head. Evidence sources, any one suffices:
(a) the PR head's merge-base is the current master tip and its gate-of-record commit status is success; or
(b) a local `.verify/attestation.json` produced by `scripts/verify.sh verify` in a scratch worktree of the actual merge of master+head (opt-in via AO_QUEUE_VERIFY_MERGED=1).

Otherwise refuse `merged-tree-unverified:<pr>` (evidence stale/absent) or `merged-tree-red:<check>` (merged tree reds), print the remedy, and continue with the next candidate — after each merge the tip moved, so the next candidate is re-judged against the NEW tip.

items.title: deploy: institutionalised portal promotion on shared-services — pull the immutable AR tag, recreate, healthz-gate, record, roll back; no host-built images
items.body:
Parent: #1295

## Measured 2026-09-18
`ai.purebliss.app` is served by `shared-services-agentconsole` on 192.168.168.42 running `agent-orchestrator-console:master`, an image built ON THE HOST at 2026-09-17T05:11Z from a non-git copy of the repo, up 38 h. Artifact Registry has received immutable `portal:<sha>` images on every master push since #1244 (latest `7bb410d`), and nothing consumes them: `contrib/shared-services/agentconsole.compose.yml` declares `image: ${AGENTCONSOLE_IMAGE:-agent-orchestrator-console:local}` with a `build:` fallback, the hosting checklist's last box ("publish image and set `AGENTCONSOLE_IMAGE`") was never done, and the promoter that existed (`capital-hourly-promote`) is retiring with capital. Health is fine (`/api/healthz` ok); the code is a day old and every merged portal change is invisible.

## Shape (durable, runtime-agnostic — a fleet job, not a person)
1. `infra/fleet/promote_portal.py` + a cron rung in `fleet/cron.py` / the agent-cron compose (same rung shape as watchdog/prune/reconcile/reap): every N minutes, read the newest immutable tag for `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/purebliss-ghl/ao-images/portal` that corresponds to a commit reachable from `origin/master` (never `latest`, never an unmerged sha), compare to the running container's image tag; if different: `docker pull`, `AGENTCONSOLE_IMAGE=<ref> docker compose -f contrib/shared-services/agentconsole.compose.yml up -d --no-build agentconsole`, poll `/api/healthz` (+ the version the image reports) for up to 60 s, on failure `up -d` the previous ref again (rollback) and escalate once (fleet channel), on success append `{sha, image, ts, healthz, previous}` to `.fleet/deploys.jsonl` and post commit status `ao/deploy` on the sha via `scripts/gate-status.sh` (context declared).
2. Registry auth: a declared secret in `infra/fleet/secrets_contract.py` (`AO_AR_READER_KEY` or workload-identity token path) mounted read-only; the job refuses `ar-auth-missing` (CANNOT-ASSESS, escalates once) if absent. The lane declares the contract and the runbook line for the owner to place the credential — it never creates keys (GR-6).
3. The `build:` fallback is removed from the compose (or gated behind `AO_DEV_BUILD=1`): production only ever runs an immutable AR ref. `docs/AGENTCONSOLE-HOSTING.md` checklist box 259 becomes "done by the promote rung".
4. Gate `scripts/check-portal-promotion.sh`: the rung is declared and scheduled (reuse the `--schedule` shape from #1105), the compose has no unconditional `build:`, the job's dry-run against fixtures picks the newest master-reachable tag and refuses an unreachable one by name (`tag-not-on-master`), a failed healthz rolls back (fixture), missing auth → CANNOT-ASSESS `ar-auth-missing`. Wired into verify by the flip lane.

## Acceptance
- A master merge that touches `portal/` is visible at `ai.purebliss.app` within one rung interval, with a `.fleet/deploys.jsonl` line and an `ao/deploy` status on the sha, no human step.
- Killing healthz in a fixture rolls back and escalates once; the record shows `rolled_back`.
- `docker images` on the pair shows no host-built `agent-orchestrator-console:*` in use.

| live process / claim / lane record | `/proc/*/cwd` scan, `.fleet` claims+sessions | none (0 hits) |
| age | tip commit `2026-09-17T18:00:32Z` | ~24.2h ⇒ crossed the 24h grace; it was **23.83h (young)** when the quarantine was measured at 17:50:33Z, which is why it was not named then |

So the artifact is **landed by content**: its patch and its tree are carried by `4c9db94` on the
default branch. The audit's own three proofs still grant nothing — ancestry no; path containment no
(drift); **patch identity no, because `landing.py`'s candidate generator keys on the issue number in
the commit SUBJECT only, and this landing names the pull request (`#1165`) there while `Closes #1158`
is in the body** — the declared-vs-implemented gap #1310 measured (fix open as PR #1312).

## Why this is NOT a quarantine entry

`scripts/check-reconcile.sh` declares the quarantine's class in its own comment: *"named, tip-pinned,
leased exemptions for the residue: the AGENTS.md rule 17 class, **work that exists nowhere else**"*.
This artifact's work **is** elsewhere, so it is not that class — and reaping it loses no work. Its
resolution is the reaper's/owner's call, not a keep-and-report exemption.

It is recorded instead as ONE by-name entry in `governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json` (the
home the gate's own verdict line names: *"not in the baseline (add it, reviewed, or fix it)"*), whose
`reason` carries this measurement. The quarantine document is **untouched** — no entry was added,
removed, widened or refreshed, and **nothing was deleted, pruned or reaped**.

## Known, unfixed here (owner's calls)

1. **Reap the branch.** Its patch is on the default branch, so reaping loses no work — but the tip
   commit exists in no remote-tracking ref, so deleting it is an owner/reaper call, not a lane's
   (`#1265`/`#1159`, tracked by `#1311`).
2. **The twin still over-claims.** Worktree `ao-worktrees/ao-1158 @bce5886` carries a quarantine
   entry whose reason says its HEAD "is on no default branch the audit's proofs can find" — true of
   the *proofs*, but for this tip the patch IS on the default branch (`4c9db94`). `#1311` owns
   restating or removing it; a lane must not shrink that document (a reduction in protection is the
   owner's reviewed decision, per `#1311` itself).
3. **The mechanism gap** (`landing.py`'s subject-only candidate set) is `#1310` / PR #1312.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh        # rc 0, 0 NEW, branch issue-1158 present and baselined
```

items.title: gates: check-reconcile is the last red on master — the by-name real-tree quarantine needs a declared venue (#1317 regression)
items.body:
## What is red

`bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh` is the LAST red check on `origin/master` (`8526c45`):

```
check-reconcile: FAIL — real tree drifted from governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json (26 new-and-old, 478 stale, not fatal; 0 stale quarantine exemption(s))
real-tree-baseline: 124 unmatched artifact(s) on disk, 538 baselined, 38 young (< 24h, not failed), 478 stale (not failed), 0 vanished (not failed), 0 quarantined by name (reported, not failed)
  quarantine: honoured — #1291 open, measured 2.1h ago (lease 24h, by governance/reconcile (issue #1291 lane))
check-reconcile: FAIL (1 violation(s))   # rc=1
```

The 26 are 11 local-only `issue-*` branches and 15 worktrees (`.claude/worktrees/agent-*`, three
lane worktrees, one `/tmp` scratch tree). `AGENTS.md` rule 17 forbids the worker to discard them,
so the gate must report them rather than red on them — which is exactly what #1300 (#1291) built.

## Why it regressed

#1300 quarantined those artifacts **by name** (`governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json`).
#1317 then emptied the document, on a true measurement: the entries name artifacts that exist on
one box, so on any other checkout `real_tree_baseline.check_real_tree` finds them "no longer
unmatched" and every entry **FAILS as a stale exemption** — measured on a pristine clone:

```
check-reconcile: FAIL — real tree drifted from … (0 new-and-old, 538 stale, not fatal; 23 stale quarantine exemption(s))
```

So the red moved from the CI clone to this box, and the artifacts it hides here are the ones the
worker may not delete. Both readings were right about their own checkout and wrong about the other:
**an exemption names a disk artifact of ONE repository instance** — a local branch of this checkout,
a worktree path on this machine — and the document is tracked, so it is read where that artifact was
never there. The missing piece is the venue, not the entries.

## The fix

`real-tree-quarantine.json` declares `venue.git_common_dir` — the repository instance the
exemptions were measured in (every worktree of one checkout answers it; no clone does):

* **at that venue** — every existing rule bites unchanged: named + exact tip ⇒ honoured and
  REPORTED on every pass; gone or no-longer-unmatched ⇒ stale exemption ⇒ rc 1; tip moved ⇒ not
  absorbed; a lease that is closed or past its declared bound ⇒ nothing honoured;
* **at any other venue** — the whole document is **inert**: each entry is reported
  (`NOT-APPLICABLE`), honours **nothing** (an artifact that *is* unmatched there stays a finding —
  fail-closed) and is **not fatal** (a stale exemption is a claim about the declared venue's disk,
  which that checkout cannot observe). The lease is venue-scoped with it;
* **entries with no venue** (missing or empty) ⇒ **rc 2 CANNOT-ASSESS**, never a pass — without a
  venue there is no way to tell "the artifact is gone" from "the artifact was never here".

It cannot be used to buy a green: declaring a foreign venue honours nothing (the artifacts come
back as findings by name), and a **new** artifact crossing the grace window still reds immediately,
by name. Nothing was deleted, pruned or reaped: the 26 artifacts are named and reported as-is, each
`reason` carrying its own measurements (default-branch proofs, remote-ref membership, uncommitted
paths) rather than a blanket "exists nowhere else" claim.

Out of scope by choice: widening `landing.py`'s candidate rule to the `Refs`-in-body half, which
would *reduce* the number of exemptions (5 of the #1291 set are provably landed by patch identity).
#1311 records that as the owner's reviewed decision, not a green-making lane's side effect.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh                        # rc 0 on this box, 26 reported by name
python3 -m pytest -q governance/reconcile/tests        # green
bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh --real-tree-only DIR BASELINE [QUARANTINE]   # the driven step
```

items.title: check-cockpit reds inside make verify: it asserts the whole worktree is pristine, so a sibling check's rewrite of .board/focus.json fails it
items.body:
## What

`scripts/check-cockpit.sh` (landed by PR #1306, issue #1162) **passes when run alone and fails inside the composite**: its final assertion enumerates the whole worktree with `git status` and reads any modification as evidence that the cockpit client wrote fleet state.

Measured at `origin/master = 358a292`, in a full `make verify` run:

```
== the repository was not edited, and the client wrote no fleet state ==
  OK    control-plane/cockpit is byte-identical after the run (9cf185a8…)
  FAIL  the run left changes behind -- the client is a client and writes no fleet state:
           M .board/focus.json
check-cockpit: FAIL -- the terminal cockpit client is not what the registry declares
```

## Why

`.board/focus.json` is a **tracked** file that this repo's own suites rewrite (`fleet/tests/test_brain.py` writes the real board file — a known side effect, recorded in `pre-existing-red-attribution` notes). It is NOT caused by `control-plane/cockpit`. Because the assertion asks for the tree's **absolute** state rather than the **delta this run caused**, the check's verdict depends on which checks ran before it in the same worktree.

Same defect class as `check-docs.sh`'s historical bare `find .` (it read gitignored runtime state, so a clean checkout could fail where a dirty one passed):

- (a) alone in a clean tree -> **rc 0**
- (b) the same tree with `.board/focus.json` pre-dirtied -> **rc 1**, naming it

## Remedy

Measure the delta the run caused, not the tree's absolute state; treat a declared machine-managed path (`governance/isolation/worktree.py`'s `MACHINE_MANAGED_PATHS` / `MACHINE_MANAGED_PREFIXES`, the authority the reaper consumes per #1285 / #1313) as outside the property. A path the run **creates**, or one already dirty whose **bytes it changes**, must still be refused by name — otherwise the fix is vacuity.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-cockpit.sh                              # clean tree: rc 0
printf '\n' >> .board/focus.json && bash scripts/check-cockpit.sh   # pre-dirtied: rc 0 (was rc 1)
# planted: a run that creates a path / rewrites an already-dirty file -> rc 1, naming it
# planted: the declared machine-managed path rewritten -> rc 0, count named
```

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1162
Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1313

Measured 2026-09-18 on shared-services compute-primary (192.168.168.42) running `bash scripts/verify.sh verify` at origin/master 358a292 (first run of the gate on a host other than the laptop / Cloud Build):

items.title: reconcile: the real-tree quarantine's lease and its 23 named exemptions, now tracked here (successor to closed #1291)
items.body:
## What this owns

`governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json` carries **23 named exemptions** — the
`AGENTS.md` rule 17 class: artifacts whose work the worker is forbidden to discard, so the
gate reports them by name instead of reding the whole fleet on them. The document is a
**lease**: an entry is honoured only while the issue that tracks it is `open` and that
state was measured less than `max_age_hours` (24) ago. **This issue is that tracker.**

`#1291` created the document and is now **closed** (its lane landed as PR #1300, merged
2026-09-18T16:35:09Z), so every entry was one measurement away from lapsing — the
15:41:29Z declaration said `#1291` was open when it no longer was. The lease now names
this issue and a fresh measurement.

Closing this issue **lapses all of its exemptions**, so it may only be closed when every
entry below has reached a terminal state. Per the document's own rule, an entry that
"excuses nothing FAILS as a stale exemption until it is removed in a reviewed edit" — so
the list can only shrink, never rot.

## What each entry needs (a human/owner call, one of three)

1. **land** it (the work reaches the default branch), or
2. **push** it (the branch reaches a remote, so the work is safe), or
3. **authorise its deletion** — the only case where work that exists nowhere else may be
   discarded.

## Measured finding — 5 of the 23 reasons over-claim

Five entries' `reason` says *"no commit on the default branch carries its patch"*. That
conclusion was reached from a candidate set built only from the landing convention's
`Closes #n` (body) and the subject's `#n`. A wider search — any `#n` anywhere in the
message, which is the `Refs <owner>/<repo>#<n>` half declared in `AGENTS.md` rule 1 —
finds a commit on the default branch carrying an **identical `git patch-id --stable`**:

| exempted artifact | exempt tip | default-branch commit carrying the identical patch | its subject |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issue-1028-tpl` | `f11abe47bb17` | `96ae0fba19c3` | `feat(templates): ask the #506 clock invariant where a lane is shaped (#1060) (#1063)` |
| `issue-1106-gate-location-independence` | `a3484089df62` | `367f2ca7a01c` | `fix(gates): make gate-lock/lifecycle-reclaim/git-config location-independent (#1124)` |
| `issue-1107-ticket-projection-reds` | `e34e7b6e0030` | `e352ddeb6afe` | `fix(board,lessons-sync): refresh stale board snapshot and CMR local-only baseline (#1117)` |
| `issue-1113-dispatch-queue-prune` | `159cf0058698` | `a43fd1d474a1` | `fix(dispatch): prune closed issues from the committed dispatch queue (#1128)` |
| `issue-830-reap-rung` | `025381c3b5b1` | `2df367d3e5c3` | `feat(fleet): the reaper reaps landed lane branches by content, and generated (#1118)` |

Each row was verified by hand — the tip's and the named commit's `patch-id` are equal, and
the commit is reachable from `origin/master`:

```
git diff --no-color origin/master...<tip> | git patch-id --stable
git diff-tree --root -p --no-color --no-commit-id <commit> | git patch-id --stable
```

The third `#1291` finding of this shape was `issue-1106`/`issue-1107`/`issue-1113` — the
three the previous lane recorded as "work exists nowhere but this box". This measurement
**refutes that** for all three: their patches are on the default branch.

**Not changed by the lane that filed this** (`#1310`): recognising them requires widening
the candidate search past the two halves of the convention, and doing so *reduces* the
quarantine by 5 entries — a reduction in protection should be the owner's reviewed
decision, not a side effect of a lane whose job is to make the gate green. Each of the
five must either have its entry removed (the patch is on the default branch) or have its
reason restated to say what was actually searched.

## Verify

```bash
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json'));print(d['tracked_by'], d['tracking']['state'], len(d['quarantine']))"
bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh
```

items.title: fix(reconcile): the residue #1291 quarantined — two dead worktrees and a lease naming a closed issue
items.body:
## What this owns (successor to the residue of a closed issue)

`#1291` is **closed** (its lane landed as PR #1300, merged 2026-09-18T16:35:09Z) and its
mechanism — the landing proof plus the named, leased quarantine — is on `master`. What it
left behind is this issue's work: **the residue of the quarantine it created.**

`bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh` at `origin/master = bbe3c83860b000c9d26187937e7222298fcbb4e6`
still exits **1**, and the single violation is §6's real tree:

```
check-reconcile: FAIL — real tree drifted from governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json
  (2 new-and-old, 478 stale, not fatal; 0 stale quarantine exemption(s))
real-tree-baseline: 132 unmatched artifact(s) on disk, 538 baselined, 47 young (< 24h, not
failed), 478 stale (not failed), 0 vanished (not failed), 23 quarantined by name (reported,
not failed)
  NEW      worktree /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator/.claude/worktrees/agent-ae1517f27b6ec470f
  NEW      worktree /tmp/ao706-g/venue-base
```

Two items, both measured, neither one a live peer's tree.

### 1. The two `NEW` worktrees — dead, with their committed work already landed

| artifact | HEAD | committed work | uncommitted | live process |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `…/.claude/worktrees/agent-ae1517f27b6ec470f` (branch `issue-878-flip`) | `945385d9ecf2` | landed: PR **#1127** merged, tip's `git patch-id --stable` `f7268785f2ac…` is **identical** to `master`'s landing commit `9e5a61528752` | `.board/focus.json` (generated board focus) + 3 `.fleet/*.lease`/`ledger.jsonl` runtime files | none |
| `/tmp/ao706-g/venue-base` (detached) | `2fa292cc0dee` | landed: HEAD **is an ancestor of `origin/master`**; `git log HEAD --not origin/master` is empty | two symlinks into the shared `.fleet` / `.board` | none |

Neither is excused by the landing proof, and correctly so: `landing.py` refuses to speak
for a worktree holding *anything* uncommitted, because a worktree with uncommitted work
must not be excused into a reaper. Here the uncommitted paths are **generated runtime
state, not work** — so the honest disposition is `AGENTS.md` rule 17's `reclaimed` class
(work landed → remove the worktree), not a baseline entry, which would freeze two dead,
fully-landed artifacts into the baseline permanently.

### 2. The quarantine's lease now names a **closed** issue

`governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json` declares:

```json
"tracked_by": "#1291",
"tracking": {"state": "open", "measured_at": "2026-09-18T15:41:29Z", "max_age_hours": 24}
```

`#1291` has since closed (16:35:09Z). The declaration is therefore **false**, and the
document's own semantics make that load-bearing: an entry is honoured *only* while the
recorded measurement says the tracking issue is `open` and is younger than `max_age_hours`
— so at **2026-09-19T15:41Z** the lease lapses, no entry is honoured, and the 23
quarantined artifacts plus the lease itself become violations (24 findings). The lease
needs a **live** tracking issue and a fresh, truthfully measured state — re-measured from
the API (`REST: repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/<n>`), never assumed.

The 23 quarantined artifacts are the rule-17 class (work that exists nowhere else, which
the worker is forbidden to discard); they are NOT resolved by this issue, and their
resolution remains the reaper lane's (`#1159`, `#1265`).

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh        # must exit 0, and §6b must still refuse by name
python3 -c "import json;json.load(open('governance/reconcile/real-tree-quarantine.json'))"
```

## File scope

`governance/reconcile/**` (including `real-tree-baseline.json` / `real-tree-quarantine.json`),
plus removing worktrees/directories proven dead. No product tree, no `scripts/verify.sh`,
no `scripts/check-reconcile.sh` semantics.

items.title: contract: one lifecycle for every artifact — lane-bound at creation, terminal only by evidenced close-out, runtime-agnostic (Claude/DeepSeek/Copilot/hermes/paperclip), no orphans
items.body:
Parent: #1268

## The rule
Every artifact an agent creates — issue, branch, worktree, lane record, directive, PR, approval, build, heartbeat — is **bound to one lane at creation** and reaches a terminal state **only through the lane's close-out, with evidence**. The close-out is the same verb for a Claude session, a Claude subagent, the DeepSeek sister, hermes or paperclip: the orchestration is the lane, not the agent. An artifact with no live lane and no evidenced close-out is an **orphan** — a finding by name, reaped only when its evidence is reconstructable, never silently.

## Measured 2026-09-18 (why doctrine failed)
126 lane records for closed issues (worktrees held for days); 155 worktrees / 663 local + 168 remote branches (578 deleted by hand after a SHA-recording sweep); 27 squash merges that closed 0 issues; `[lifecycle] VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING` filed for issues already closed; 8 remote branches with commits and no PR ever; 40 local branches with unpushed work and no lane; subagent worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` that no lane record knows. Each runtime cleaned up "its own" — nothing owned the whole.

## Mechanical shape (one contract, consumed by every child of #1268 and #1254)
1. **Binding at creation.** `governance/isolation/cli.py open` is the only way to mint a lane; it records `{lane_id, issue, branch, worktree, runtime, actor, brief_hash}` in `.fleet/lanes/`. Branch name = `issue-<n>[-suffix]`; PR body `lane: <lane_id>` (#1254 step 5); directive `correlation_id = lane_id`; subagent worktrees (`.claude/worktrees/agent-*`) are minted through the same verb (a wrapper the Agent tool's `isolation: worktree` path calls) or are orphans by definition.
2. **One close-out verb.** `governance/lifecycle/cli.py closeout --lane <id>` (exists; widen) is the only terminal path: it verifies, in order, PR merged with trailer (`classify_commit == None`) → issue closed by that merge (`Closes #n` composed by the guard, #1266) → branch deleted local+remote (SHA recorded to `.fleet/reaped-branches.jsonl`) → worktree removed (dirt only machine-managed, #1285) → lane record archived with the evidence bundle (`.fleet/lifecycle/<lane>.json`: sha, gate tails, build id, approval id). Any step it cannot evidence stays open and names itself (`closeout-blocked:<step>`).
3. **Orphan sweep, runtime-independent.** `governance/reconcile/cli.py sweep` (exists; widen) walks all five artifact kinds and classifies anything without a live lane: `orphan-branch`, `orphan-worktree`, `orphan-pr`, `orphan-issue-lane`, `orphan-directive`. Reclaim only when evidence is reconstructable (PR merged + content on master → reap branch/worktree; issue closed + PR merged → archive lane); otherwise file one finding per orphan with the remedy, and red `make verify` above a declared orphan budget (#1265's cap generalised).
4. **Runtime parity.** The close-out and the sweep read only files (lane records, git, the board snapshot, the mailbox) — never a runtime's memory — so a lane opened by DeepSeek can be closed by a Claude session and vice-versa, and a dead runtime's lanes are still closable.
5. **Doctrine retired.** AGENTS.md keeps one sentence: "open a lane, work in it, close it out; the sweep names what you left." The per-artifact rules become the close-out's checklist, not prose.

## Acceptance
- Open a lane in any runtime, merge its PR through the guard → `closeout` runs to terminal with an evidence bundle; issue auto-closed; branch and worktree gone; lane archived. Zero manual steps.
- Kill the runtime mid-lane → the sweep classifies each artifact by name and a different runtime's `closeout --lane` finishes it from evidence alone.
- Negative controls: a PR with no `lane:` → `orphan-pr`; a worktree outside `.fleet/lanes` → `orphan-worktree`; a branch with commits, no PR, no lane → `orphan-branch` with the SHA recorded, never deleted.
- Seven days after landing: orphan count 0 on the box, `landed-baseline.json` unchanged, `[lifecycle] VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING` filed only for open issues.

## Relation

items.title: lifecycle: a filed board finding has no terminal move — report.BoardReporter.resolve is dead code
items.body:
`report.BoardReporter.resolve` is the terminal move for a finding that has been filed
on the board — it comments and drops the dedupe-ledger entry so a genuine recurrence
files again. **Nothing calls it.** `grep -rn '\.resolve(' governance/lifecycle/`
returns only `directive.resolve` (a different module, a different verb), and neither
`cli.py audit` nor `cli.py close` invokes it.

The consequence is measured on #1247 and #1251, which `cli.py close --apply` filed for
`lifecycle:VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING:#627` and `:#629` (issue #321's board reporter).
Once filed, such an issue has **no mechanised path to a terminal state at all**:

- nothing comments on it when the invariant clears, so its text keeps asserting a
  violation that may no longer hold;
- nothing closes it, so a cleared finding and a live one look identical on the board;
- the dedupe ledger still holds the fingerprint, so a genuine recurrence of the same
  named violation (and it is the same fingerprint) is reported as `deduped` and does
  not re-file — the stale entry silences the second occurrence.

So the reporter has a one-way door: `report()` files, and `resolve()` exists but has no
caller. What is needed is a step, beside close-out's own, that for each
`governance/lifecycle` board finding whose code and subject no longer appear in the
audit's findings: comment the measurement that cleared it and close the issue —
`--apply`-gated like every other board write, and dry-run by default.

Filed rather than fixed because it adds a board-writing verb, which is its own change
with its own tests (`tests/test_lifecycle_boardreport.py` covers the reporting half
only).
