items.title: lifecycle: the re-measurement venue gates a commit that never landed, and the #1098 whole-tree arm cannot fire for a squash onto a moved base
items.body:
The re-measurement venue (#786) gates a commit that **never landed**, and the
whole-tree arm (#1098) cannot admit a squash merge onto a base that moved. Between
them, `VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING` is unsatisfiable for a squash-merged item whose lane
is gone — measured on #627 and #629 (board findings #1247, #1251).

## The #1098 arm cannot fire for the case it was written for

`cli.GhOps._admissible` admits a lane that is not *at* the verified commit only when
it **contains the landing** *and* `trees_are_identical(verified_head, landing)` — i.e.
the whole trees are equal. A GitHub squash merge composes the landing from the
**base as it stands at merge time** plus the PR's change, so whenever anything else
lands between the branch cut and the merge, the landing's tree necessarily differs
from the verified head's:

```
$ git diff --quiet 6a7bca938ea6 14dac6a9be79  -> rc 1   (#627)  37 files, +5227/-67
$ git diff --quiet 7a39fad775fa 7d5f6a1a400d  -> rc 1   (#629)  40 files, +5557/-67
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor 6a7bca938ea6 origin/master  -> NO
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor 14dac6a9be79 origin/master  -> YES
```

So the arm can only ever admit a pull request that was up to date with its base at
merge time — which, in a fleet where a wave lands together, is ~never. It is a
control that cannot fire, which is the inverse of GR-12's "a gate that cannot fail is
a formality" and has the same effect: the case it exists for stays red.

## The remaining venue measures a commit that never landed

With the arm unreachable, `_remeasure` (#786) is the only venue left: it checks the
verified head out **detached** and runs the composite gate there. That tree is a
branch tip the squash *replaced*, so the repo's own landed-history checks refuse it —
and their refusal is unanswerable, because the commit's message can never be
corrected (the branch is gone and history is never rewritten):

```
$ git -C <detached 7a39fad> bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh   -> rc 1
  FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:7a39fad775fa is not recorded legacy — if the
        commit has not MERGED yet, put the reference in a trailing trailer paragraph
        and re-push; if it is already landed on a protected branch the message can
        never be corrected
  isolation-enforce: NOT-OK — 1 unrecorded and 0 stale baseline entr(ies) in HEAD
$ git -C <detached 6a7bca9> bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh   -> rc 0
```

Same check, same detached venue, two commits twenty minutes apart in merge order,
opposite verdicts — and the difference is a **message on a commit that never landed**.
The venue decides the verdict, and for a merged item it is measuring the wrong thing.

## What is owed

The landed tree (#1003, `_measure_landed_tree`) is the only venue that can answer the
question — but it is reached only *after* a full gate run at the never-landed tip,
which is red for reasons the item does not own. Either:

1. the merge commit should be measured **first** for an item whose pull request is
   merged and whose lane is gone, on the same argument #1003 already accepts (nothing
   else in the object store holds the landed tree); or
2. the `contains` arm should compare **the change**, not the whole tree — the
   landing's content on the paths the pull request touched, against the verified
   head's — which is what "the tree which was verified is the tree that landed"
   means for a change.

Both are deliberate doctrine decisions and neither is taken here; this issue records
the measurement. Witnesses: #627, #629, and — from the ledger — #877 and #955, whose
re-measurements were likewise answered by the venue rather than by the change.

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1247
Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1251

items.title: EPIC: deployment + verify execute on shared-services, not Cloud Build — runner, promotion, retirement
items.body:
## Escalation

Attempt at L0. Tiers: L0 = Claude Haiku / DeepSeek V4 Flash -> L1 = Claude Sonnet / DeepSeek V4 Pro -> L2 = Claude Opus.
- Max attempts: **N = 3**.
- If blocked after 3 attempts, comment on this issue with the exact failure and label `escalate:L1`, then stop. Never silent abandonment.

## Lifecycle contract (no lingering)

- This issue is closed ONLY via a merged PR whose body contains `Closes #<n>` and evidence: the acceptance command output pasted, plus the negative-control output.
- Picking this issue up = owning it to closure. Do not stop at a partial state or move to another issue. Blockers are part of the task: unblock them (file the blocker as a child issue with `Parent: #1510` if it is a separate lane, fix it, then continue).
- Before the PR is opened: `make verify` green on the branch; no orphan worktrees, no stale branches, no leftover temp files.
- After merge: delete the branch, remove the worktree, confirm the issue auto-closed, post a final comment with the merged PR link and the evidence summary.
- Escalation is the only sanctioned way to hand off; it is a comment + label on THIS issue, never silent abandonment.

Was: child of #706 (closed 2026-09-18) — promoted to an epic 2026-09-19.

## Owner direction (2026-09-18)
The whole deployment path — `make verify` for PRs, terraform apply, the web-image build/push — runs on the **shared-services** container pair (the #706 cutover target: HA pair, host crontab frozen), not on Cloud Build. Cloud Build's role shrinks to, at most, relaying a GitHub commit status from the shared-services run (or is retired when a GitHub App posts the status directly).

## Why (measured this week)
Cloud Build cost ~5 h of the PR drain on 2026-09-18 to things the shared-services pair already controls: a 5-concurrent cap, `queueTtl` expiry, a foreign zombie sweep cancelling PR builds, a runner image that did not match the dev box (Python minor, git identity, shallow clone), and trigger-definition drift. On the pair the toolchain is the fleet's own image (`infra/fleet/*`, #706 lanes), concurrency is ours, and the same worktree/lease machinery that runs lanes runs verify.

## Shape
1. `infra/fleet/`: a `verify-runner` job (container from the fleet image) that, on a PR event (webhook or a 1-min poll via the existing fleet cron rung), checks out `master + PR head` into a scratch worktree, runs `bash scripts/verify.sh verify`, and posts the result as a commit status `shared-services/verify` via the GitHub App token the fleet already holds. Serial per PR, N-wide by declared capacity (`capacity-gate`).
2. `control-plane-apply` and `control-plane-web-image` become fleet jobs on the same pair, flag-gated exactly as today (`_ENABLE_APPLY`, `surfaces.*`), running as the deployer SA via workload identity — never a laptop, never Cloud Build.
3. Branch protection (#1254 step 2 / #803) requires `shared-services/verify`, not `control-plane-verify`.
4. `infra/cloudbuild/*` is reduced to the status relay or deleted; the trigger yamls are declared `disabled: true` for real and #1263's drift gate proves it.
5. GCP-GateKeeper#140's rules still apply where a Cloud Build step survives; the runner-parity rule (#1264) becomes a property of the fleet image instead.

## Acceptance
- A PR gets a green `shared-services/verify` status within one verify duration of its push, with no Cloud Build run.
- An apply is only ever attributable to the pair's deployer identity (audit log).
- `check-cloudbuild.sh` reports every Cloud Build trigger disabled (or relay-only) and matching its yaml.
- Negative control: a PR that reds `make verify` locally gets a red status from the pair, by check name.

## Re-scopes
#1263, #1264, #1267 (Cloud Build-specific) — implement only if a Cloud Build step survives step 4; otherwise close as superseded by this.

items.title: reconcile red at origin/master 99f6b37 is a live-fleet verdict, not a stale baseline (31 unstable findings; 25 misattributed; 3 true, work exists nowhere but this box)
items.body:
## What is red

At `origin/master = 99f6b37b491491695dd5a27f5f9df3a75673c2b1` (2026-09-18),
`bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh` exits **1**:

```
check-reconcile: FAIL — real tree drifted from governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json (27 new-and-old, 373 stale, not fatal)
real-tree-baseline: 284 unmatched artifact(s) on disk, 538 baselined, 92 young (< 24h, not failed), 373 stale (not failed), 0 vanished (not failed)
check-reconcile: FAIL (1 violation(s))
```

Every one of the gate's other sections (§1–§5 declarations/vacuity, §3 the live
sweep proofs, §4 the audit proofs, §6b the old-unbaselined provocation, §7–§10
controls / audit-trail / schema / live-feed provocations) passes. The single
violation is §6, the real-tree step.

## Which condition counted the 1 violation (from the code, not guessed)

`scripts/check-reconcile.sh:560-566`: the embedded `PYREALTREE` exits `1` when
`not verdict.ok`, and the shell's only increment on that path is

```
if [ "$real_tree_rc" -ne 0 ]; then fail=$((fail + 1)); fi
```

`RealTreeVerdict.ok` is `assessable and not new_violations`
(`governance/reconcile/real_tree_baseline.py:159-167`). `stale`, `young` and
`vanished` are explicitly non-fatal, which is why the buckets print
`not failed` / `< 24h grace` while the verdict is still FAIL. **The 1 violation is
`new_violations` being non-empty** — 27 at RUN 1, 30 three minutes later.

## (a) vs (b): the baseline is NOT stale — (b) is confirmed

**(a) refuted.** The baseline's last commit is `2026-09-17T05:15Z` (`9ac4548`,
measured head `d0a20d6`, `2026-09-17T04:29Z`). Every artifact in the NEW bucket is
**24.0h–33.6h old**, i.e. created between `2026-09-17T05:33Z` and now — *after* the
baseline commit. So the baseline is not under-claiming pre-existing reality; its
373 stale entries are **over**-claims (69% of its 538 entries name debris that has
since been cleaned up).

**(b) confirmed, decisively — the count is not stable across two runs with no
commit in between:**

| run | time | unmatched | young | stale | NEW |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RUN 1 | 15:06:41Z | 284 | 92 | 373 | **27** |
| RUN 2 | 15:09:42Z | 286 | 91 | 373 | **30** |

No commit, no fetch, same worktree, the same `99f6b37`: `NEW` **27 → 30** and
`unmatched` **284 → 286** in three minutes (a later re-measure, 15:12Z, read
**31**). The NEW bucket is composed entirely of artifacts **crossing the 24-hour
age grace while the fleet works** — in RUN 1 the same artifacts sat in the YOUNG
list at `23.9h`/`24.0h` (`issue-1056`, `issue-1114-dispatch-master-green`, `ao-1056-c58e7589`,
`agent-a67aa5cb2076746ba`), and were NEW by RUN 2. The gate's own stated purpose
(`real_tree_baseline.py` docstring; PR #1055 "age-gate the real-tree audit **so a
live fleet stays green**") is not achieved: the grace **defers** the red by 24h,
it does not prevent it.

**(b) has a second, independent half — the verdict depends on which checkout runs
it.** `git worktree list` and `for-each-ref refs/heads` are repo-wide (worktrees
share one `.git`), so the *artifact* set is identical from any venue — but the
*evidence* the audit reads is per-checkout, untracked state:

| evidence source | this lane | shared checkout |
|---|---|---|
| `.fleet/sessions/` (beats) | ABSENT | present, **0** entries |
| `.fleet/lifecycle/` (landing) | ABSENT | present, **51** entries |
| `.board/claims/` (claims) | ABSENT | present, **1299** events, **0 active** |

Auditing the same commit with the shared checkout's evidence moves 16 artifacts'
disposition (`unmatched` 283 → 267, `stale` 373 → 385). It explains **0** of the
NEW set, so it is not the cause of *this* red — but it means the check's verdict is
not a function of the commit.

## What the 31 findings actually are

Cross-checking each NEW artifact against the repository's **tracked** landing trace
(the default branch's own commit messages) and against the worker's own
preservation facts (`preserved_on_main`, `preserved_remotely` — both already
implemented in `governance/reconcile/sweep.py`):

* **25 of 31 are misattributed.** 14 lane branches are named in `origin/master`'s
  own history (`Closes #N` / `(#N)`) — leftovers of **landed** work
  (`issue-973`, `issue-873`, `issue-830-*`, …), reported as orphans only because
  the audit's "landing history" source is the gitignored journal
  `.fleet/lifecycle/<issue>.json`, which the fleet did not write for them (51
  journals exist for far more than 51 landings). Others are explained by
  `preserved_on_main` (`/tmp/ao968-pristine`'s HEAD is an ancestor of
  `origin/master`) or `preserved_remotely` (`issue-1056` is on `origin/issue-1056`).
* **Residual — 3 true findings.** These 3 branch tips are **not** ancestors of
  `origin/master` and are contained in **none** of the 52 remote refs known to this
  clone, so their work exists **nowhere but this box**:

  | artifact | tip | where the work lives |
  |---|---|---|
  | `issue-1106-gate-location-independence` | `a3484089df62` | local only (+ `.claude/worktrees/agent-a67aa5cb2076746ba`) |
  | `issue-1107-ticket-projection-reds` | `e34e7b6e0030` | local only (+ `.claude/worktrees/agent-ae391267f79052e9c`) |
  | `issue-1113-dispatch-queue-prune` | `159cf0058698` | local only |

  These are exactly the class `AGENTS.md` rule 17 exists to protect: an orphan
  whose work exists nowhere else is **shelved and reported every pass**, never
  traded for an unlocked issue.

## Why rc 0 is not reachable from this lane's file scope

To reach rc 0 the 3 true findings must reach a terminal state, and both routes are
outside `scripts/check-reconcile.sh` + `governance/reconcile/**`:

1. **Reclaim them** — `git worktree remove` on the two `.claude/worktrees`, `git
   branch -D` on the three branches (or push them). That is a fleet-ops action on
   **other lanes'** artifacts: `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` is held by a peer lane
   right now (#1159 / PR #1285), and rule 17 forbids unilaterally discarding work
   that exists nowhere else.
2. **Baseline them** — record all 31 (or all 284 unmatched) as accepted exceptions.
   That is runtime state being laundered: two thirds of the set are false findings
   that a *correct* landing source already explains, and the true third is the only
   signal in the gate that would then be gone. It also re-arms in under 24h —
   measured growth is **~8–10 new violations/hour** (27 → 30 in three minutes), so
   a refresh buys one day and must be repeated daily, each time hiding more.

A baseline refresh is therefore deliberately **not** proposed here.

## The in-scope defect this measurement does expose (proposed, NOT applied)

`governance/reconcile/audit.py` declares the explanation source as "the **landing
history**" but implements it as a single gitignored runtime journal
(`.fleet/lifecycle/<issue>.json`, `RepoOps.landed_issues`). The repository's own
tracked landing trace — the default branch's commit history — and the preservation
facts the worker already computes (`preserved_on_main`, `preserved_remotely`) are
not consulted. Measured effect: 25 of 31 findings are false.

Fixing that would take this gate from *31 unattributable* to *3 attributable*
violations **without silencing anything** — but it would still exit 1, so it does
not meet this issue's acceptance and is left for the owner's decision rather than
merged as a semantic change to a governed gate.

## Acceptance

* `bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh` exits **0** at the current tip, **and**
* the check is still **shown to fail**: a planted, backdated, unbaselined
  worktree+branch is refused **by name** with rc 1 (the §6b provocation), and an
  unreadable/missing baseline is rc **2**, never read as a pass.

## Evidence

Reproduced on a fresh worktree cut from a freshly fetched `origin/master`
(`99f6b37`); the shared checkout was not used and the composite `make verify` was
not run (gate permits are capped box-wide).

'A DeepSeek executor never asks a Claude session to do a denied action', 'lanes use only their scoped gates', 'no lane touches secrets' — all prose. `adapters/skills`, `adapters/secrets` and `control-plane/control/verbs.yaml` exist but nothing consults them at spawn.
## Mechanical
`verbs.yaml` gains `allowed_runtimes` per verb; `adapters/skills` and `adapters/secrets` declare per-runtime allowlists; the channel validator and the Claude Agent-dispatch wrapper refuse a spawn or directive outside the allowlist (`verb-not-allowed:<runtime>:<verb>`, `skill-not-allowed`, `secret-not-allowed`). items.title: EPIC: mechanical, not doctrinal, between runtimes — paperclip / hermes / Claude / DeepSeek coordination becomes records and gates
items.body:
**Status under single-dev method:** b
## Escalation

Attempt at L0. Tiers: L0 = Claude Haiku / DeepSeek V4 Flash -> L1 = Claude Sonnet / DeepSeek V4 Pro -> L2 = Claude Opus.
- Max attempts: **N = 3**.
- If blocked after 3 attempts, comment on this issue with the exact failure and label `escalate:L1`, then stop. Never silent abandonment.

## Lifecycle contract (no lingering)

- This issue is closed ONLY via a merged PR whose body contains `Closes #<n>` and evidence: the acceptance command output pasted, plus the negative-control output.
- Picking this issue up = owning it to closure. Do not stop at a partial state or move to another issue. Blockers are part of the task: unblock them (file the blocker as a child issue with `Parent: #1510` if it is a separate lane, fix it, then continue).
- Before the PR is opened: `make verify` green on the branch; no orphan worktrees, no stale branches, no leftover temp files.
- After merge: delete the branch, remove the worktree, confirm the issue auto-closed, post a final comment with the merged PR link and the evidence summary.
- Escalation is the only sanctioned way to hand off; it is a comment + label on THIS issue, never silent abandonment.

## Why
Every cross-runtime rule that failed on 2026-09-17/18 was a sentence, not a check: standing rules broadcast by chat with no ack; lane briefs and hand-backs in prose; lanes working in shared checkouts they were told not to; the DeepSeek sister paused and 30 commits behind master for hours; "approved" typed in chat authorising merges and deletions; a control verb (`fleet.drop`) landing with no paperclip opinion row; a cron rung with no paperclip routine, skipped as CANNOT-ASSESS on every build. The pattern to copy already exists in-repo: `integrations/hermes` (a projection that is a pure function of the tree, four parity rules refused by name, provoked on every run).

## Scope
Children below. Sibling of #1254 (the merge-path epic); #1262 and #1176 stay parented where they are and are referenced.

## Definition of done
- Every child's gate runs inside `make verify` with a negative control, and `control-plane-verify` is green with none of them skipped.

items.title: ci: verify builds EXPIRE unrun behind the 5-slot cap — declare queueTtl and make EXPIRED a named failure
items.body:
Parent: #1254

## Measured 2026-09-18
Builds for #1216 (f8685a6), #1134 (0f13399), #1088 (d98c420), created 12:38–12:39Z, reached status **EXPIRED** without ever starting: Cloud Build's default `queueTtl` is 3600 s, the project runs 5 concurrent builds, and a 27-PR round takes longer than an hour to drain. The PR check stayed "pending" and no one — human or the merge loop — was told.

## Fix
1. `infra/cloudbuild/verify.yaml`: `queueTtl: 21600s` (6 h) so a queued PR build survives a full round.
2. `scripts/pr-queue.sh` / any merge loop: treat EXPIRED and CANCELLED as terminal-not-green — re-trigger via update-branch and report by name, never wait.
3. `check-cloudbuild.sh` (#1263) asserts `queueTtl` is declared and ≥ the measured drain time for N open PRs.

## Acceptance
- A queued verify build older than 1 h still runs.
- Negative control: the gate reds a scratch verify.yaml with no `queueTtl`.

Refs #1245

`make verify` "runs the same everywhere". - Runner with 3.12 → red `toolchain:python-minor`. Shallow clone → red `toolchain:shallow`.

items.title: master red (all lanes): check-reconcile's committed real-tree baseline has drifted (18 new-and-old), so no lane can reach a green merge or close-out
items.body:
**Filing this as a measured finding from PR #1258's close-out** — it is the single failing check in the composite gate on this box, and because `governance/lifecycle/cli.py close` runs `make verify` as its verification step (cli.py ~line 112, `cwd=worktree`), it currently makes a green close-out **unreachable for every lane here**, not just mine.

## Measured

```
$ bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh            # in a scratch worktree at the LANDED commit 83ce2ac
check-reconcile: FAIL — real tree drifted from governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json (18 new-and-old, 331 stale, not fatal)
real-tree-baseline: 343 unmatched artifact(s) on disk, 538 baselined, 118 young (< 24h, not failed), 331 stale (not failed), 0 vanished (not failed)
check-reconcile: FAIL (1 violation(s))       rc=1
```

Same verdict in **two** venues, so it is not diff-attributable:

| Venue | Result |
|---|---|
| the verified branch tip `48956f8` (PR #1258) | `FAIL (1 violation(s))` rc=1 |
| the landed commit `83ce2ac`, scratch worktree, **with #1122's reconcile fix present** | `FAIL (1 violation(s))` rc=1 |
| pristine `origin/master` `3aadeda` (measured earlier the same day) | `FAIL (1 violation(s))` rc=1 |

Every category is labelled **"not fatal"** in the check's own summary (`young`, `stale`, `vanished` are all suppressed), yet the verdict is `FAIL (1 violation(s))` — so the counted violation is the **drift itself**: `18 new-and-old` artifacts, i.e. this box's live worktrees/branches no longer match the committed `governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json`. With ~500 worktrees churning on one machine, the committed snapshot is stale by construction.

## Why it matters (blast radius)

1. It is the **only** failing check in `make verify` (177 checks), so it reddens every composite gate run here.
2. `close` runs `make verify` → **no lane can complete a green close-out**, and rule 16's "merged at green evidence" invariant is unsatisfiable fleet-wide. #1122 (`58126e0 "a filed finding reaches a terminal state"`) landed immediately before the PR #1258 merge and did **not** clear it.
3. It is the sort of control GR-12 warns about in the other direction: it cannot distinguish a real drift caused by a lane from the machine's ordinary churn, so it fails constantly and is therefore read as noise — which is how a 331-entry stale baseline survives.

## Remedy the check itself names

```
STALE    worktree /tmp/ao1028-bisect — baselined but no longer unmatched (remove it, e.g. --prune-stale)
```

`--prune-stale` re-records `governance/reconcile/real-tree-baseline.json`. **Not applied here**: it is a shared, cross-lane baseline owned by `governance/reconcile`, and an unattended re-baseline would also erase the drift signal this check exists to provide. Wanted: a reviewed re-baseline **plus** a decision on whether the drift should gate merges at all on a machine that deliberately runs hundreds of lanes (if it should, the baseline needs a generation/GC story, not a hand-pruned snapshot).

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh; echo rc=$?     # expect rc=0 once re-baselined
```

Provenance: measured while closing out PR #1258 / issue #1257 (operator-approved dead-code repair, landed as `83ce2ac`). Adjacent but **different** reds, not duplicates: #1077 (stale board snapshot), #1174/#1136 (master-attestation wiring), #1153 (piped-grep idioms).

items.title: governance/dispatch: an open issue whose parent epic closed can never be claimed (measured on #877)
items.body:
## Objective

Resolve the dead-end: an **open** issue whose parent epic has closed can no longer
be claimed, so its (still-required) work has no sanctioned path.

## Measured (2026-09-18, `origin/master` worktree)

`#877` is open, labelled `class:enterprise`, `priority:P1`, `area:standards`, and
its own body declares work that has **not** landed (retire the declared shell-pattern
gaps). Claiming it is refused by name:

```
$ python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py snapshot --from-github
snapshot: wrote .board/snapshot.json (643 issues, 377 with declared chain edges)

$ python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py claim --issue 877 --agent <id> --lane shell-patterns
claim: snapshot age 0.0m (threshold 15m)
claim REFUSED: epic-closed — #877's epic is closed — evidence: <in-memory snapshot>
  (source kushin77/agent-orchestrator, generated 2026-09-18T12:26:28Z, sha256 80d43548cde3)
  issue #877 state=OPEN parent=#616 milestone=M31 - Gate hygiene & master-red clearance
  labels=area:standards,class:enterprise,epic:git-governance,gdc:enterprise,pillar:governance,priority:P1,type:task;
  epic issue #616 state=CLOSED labels=class:enterprise,pillar:governance,priority:P2,type:epic
```

So the refusal is **correct per its rule** (GR-20: work must advance an *open*
chain) and yet the work is real and unblocked in substance: it is a six-line
retrofit plus two detectors. The rule protects against kanban scavenging; here it
also blocks an open P1 whose epic simply closed first — which is the normal end
state of any epic, and therefore a *permanent* condition, not a transient one.

## Why this is not just #1179 (closed)

#1179 ("the entry point is dead by construction — no producer for the board
liveness contract, **silent epic-closed dead-end**, and `frontier()` naming work
claim refuses") and #1168 (closed) covered the earlier form. This is a
recurrence of the same class, measured live after both closed, and it adds the
case those two did not name: the epic is closed **and the child is still open and
still needed**, so the dead-end is permanent for that issue.

## Acceptance

Choose and implement one, so the condition has an exit:

- [ ] `claim` permits an **open** issue whose parent epic is closed when the
      issue itself carries a live milestone/`priority:P1` — i.e. the epic's state
      is not sufficient evidence that the work is obsolete; **or**
- [ ] the refusal names the remedy (`re-parent the issue under an open epic`, or
      `close the issue as superseded`) instead of only the cause; **or**
- [ ] a governed sweep re-parents / closes the children of a closing epic, so
      `epic-closed` cannot leave an open child behind.

Whichever lands, the refusal must remain **provocable** both ways (an out-of-order
claim is still refused; a legitimately re-parented one is accepted).

## Verify

```
python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py claim --issue 877 --agent <id> --lane shell-patterns
```

must either succeed (work is reachable) or name a remedy that a lane can act on.
An open issue that no path can claim is the defect.

## Cross-references

- `#877` — the open issue this was measured on (its scope was delivered in
  PR #1255, which had to proceed without a claim because of this).
- `#616` — the closed parent epic.
- `#1179`, `#1168` — the closed predecessors of this class.
- `#1189` — `check-dispatch-queue` reports queued-but-closed issues; the mirror
  image of this defect (closed issues still queued vs. open issues unclaimable).

items.title: repair the ungated dead-code population: 7 dangling type names + 4 dead bindings + 1 dead statement (deep review #1201)
items.body:
## GOAL

Repair the **ungated dead-code population** in the tracked Python tree so that every name a
module references actually exists, and hand the linter lane (#1203) a tree whose finding count
is *measured and shrinking* rather than unknown. Success = `pyflakes` reports **zero** findings
on the changed set, the whole-tree `undefined name` count drops 7 -> 2, and no behaviour changes
(all affected suites green).

## Chain markers

Parent: #1201
Root=none
Related: #1203 (the lane that wires the Python linter this class has no gate for)

## Lane

governance

## Model tier

flash / low (mechanical repair; escalation not required)

## What is wrong (measured 2026-09-18, `origin/master` = `53a7d84`)

The repo wires **no Python linter at all** — `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/gate.sh` and
`scripts/merge-gate.sh` each contain **0** references to `pyflakes`/`check-python-lint`; only
`py_compile` runs (`scripts/check-python-syntax.sh`). A whole-tree `pyflakes` pass over all
**1,709 non-vendor `*.py`** finds **366 findings across 218 files** (303 unused imports, 39 unused
locals, 12 f-strings missing placeholders, **7 undefined names**, 5 redefinitions). None is gated.

The sharp end is the **7 undefined names**: a name referenced in an annotation that its module
never imports. Every one of these files carries `from __future__ import annotations`, so the
annotation is never evaluated at runtime — the defect is **latent**, and any
`typing.get_type_hints()` resolves it and raises. All 7 confirmed on `origin/master`:

| file | line | missing name | state |
|---|---|---|---|
| `engine/core/tickets/cli.py` | 76, 133 | `Any` (no `typing` import at all) | fixed here |
| `gateway/sme-routing/smeroute_config.py` | 333 | `Sequence` | fixed here |
| `guardrails/policy/tests/test_example_policies.py` | 135 | `ControlRegistry` (exported by `guardrails/policy/__init__.py`) | fixed here |
| `registry/prompts/feedback.py` | 199 | `Optional` | fixed here |
| `governance/lessons/model.py` | 130 | `Tuple` | **NOT here** — file is dirty in worktree `ao-1028-19816f9d` |
| `integrations/paperclip/reporting/tests/conftest.py` | 141 | `subprocess` (imported function-locally) | **NOT here** — #1208's pillar, and benign |

Plus **4 confirmed dead bindings** and **1 dead statement**:

* `guardrails/isolation/integrity.py:79` — `known_buckets = set(tenants) | reserved`, computed and
  never read (the D1 loop below uses `tenants`/`reserved` directly); its now-orphaned comment goes too.
* `governance/conformance/cli.py:460 + :469` — `unknown_refusal` is assigned twice and never read.
* `control-plane/functions/cockpit_registry.py:489` — `document = registry.document` unused in
  `validate()` (each sub-check re-reads it).
* `governance/dispatch/cli.py:564` — `focus = focus_mod.load(...)`; the **call** validates and can
  raise `FocusInvalid`, so the call is kept and only the binding is dropped.

items.title: class: five module roots (engine, guardrails, identity, control-plane, fleet) are held to no solution class
items.body:
## Objective

Give the five substantial module roots that `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml`
**never inspects** a declared surface (and therefore a solution class) — or record
why each is exempt.

## Measured (origin/master `85e4152`, 2026-09-18)

`surface_roots` is the whitelist of top-level roots the class gate checks:

```
surface_roots: [portal, gateway, telemetry, registry, governance, integrations]
```

A root that exists but is **not** in that list is never inspected —
`make surface-class` prints `OK` because it is not looking. This is the same
defect #590 fixed for `governance/` and `integrations/`; it has recurred for
five roots that now carry real code:

```
engine/         137 tracked files
guardrails/     185
identity/       151
control-plane/  196
fleet/           87
```

Honest rungs, measured with the gate's own
`governance/conformance/surfaces.py:measure_path_evidence`:

| root | contract | tests | controls | audit | schema | live_sync | honest rung |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `engine/` | yes | yes | yes | no | no | no | `pattern` |
| `guardrails/` | yes | yes | yes | **yes** | **yes** | no | `enterprise` |
| `identity/` | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | no | `pattern` |
| `control-plane/` | yes | yes | no | no | yes | no | `pattern` |
| `fleet/` | yes | yes | yes | no | yes | no | `pattern` |

(`engine`, `guardrails` and `identity` are three of the five named architecture
pillars in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; `control-plane` and `fleet` are the declared
cross-cutting modules.)

## Why it matters

`declared_class` is supposed to be **the measured rung**, and the gate refuses
`surface-below-declared-class`. A root outside `surface_roots` is held to *no*
rung at all: it can regress from `enterprise` to `template` and every gate stays
green. The class ladder is the mechanism by which "elite" is a measurement
rather than an aspiration (GR-29/AO-GR-28), and for these five roots that
mechanism is currently inert.

## Acceptance

- [ ] each of `engine/`, `guardrails/`, `identity/`, `control-plane/`, `fleet/`
      has a declared surface path in `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml`,
      **or** the file records a reason it is exempt;
- [ ] `surface_roots` is widened (or the roots are covered by existing entries)
      so the gate actually inspects them;
- [ ] every `declared_class` equals the **measured** rung above — a declaration
      ahead of the evidence will be refused, which is correct;
- [ ] the doc pair `docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md` + `surfaces.yaml` land together
      (a doc row alone is decorative — `make surface-class` reads the policy).

## Verify

```
python3 governance/conformance/surfaces.py check --policy governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml
```

must inspect all five roots, and

```
python3 - <<'PY'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "governance/conformance"); import surfaces as S
from pathlib import Path
for r in ("engine", "guardrails", "identity", "control-plane", "fleet"):
    print(r, S.measure_path_evidence(Path("."), r))
PY
```

must agree with every `declared_class`.

## Provenance

Found by a repo-wide elite-convention review (2026-09-18) that ran every
discovered gate green and then measured what the gates do **not** look at.
Related: #590 (the original instance, closed), #944 (`infra/` — the same defect
for the deploy surface), #878 (the epic that would consume this), #351 (closed,
the per-surface class declaration).

Parent: #878

items.title: EPIC: mechanical, not doctrinal — the merge path, PR contract, and every rule that broke this week become gates (#1145)
items.body:
**Status under single-dev method:** b
## Escalation

Attempt at L0. Tiers: L0 = Claude Haiku / DeepSeek V4 Flash -> L1 = Claude Sonnet / DeepSeek V4 Pro -> L2 = Claude Opus.
- Max attempts: **N = 3**.
- If blocked after 3 attempts, comment on this issue with the exact failure and label `escalate:L1`, then stop. Never silent abandonment.

## Lifecycle contract (no lingering)

- This issue is closed ONLY via a merged PR whose body contains `Closes #<n>` and evidence: the acceptance command output pasted, plus the negative-control output.
- Picking this issue up = owning it to closure. Do not stop at a partial state or move to another issue. Blockers are part of the task: unblock them (file the blocker as a child issue with `Parent: #1510` if it is a separate lane, fix it, then continue).
- Before the PR is opened: `make verify` green on the branch; no orphan worktrees, no stale branches, no leftover temp files.
- After merge: delete the branch, remove the worktree, confirm the issue auto-closed, post a final comment with the merged PR link and the evidence summary.
- Escalation is the only sanctioned way to hand off; it is a comment + label on THIS issue, never silent abandonment.

## Problem (measured 2026-09-17/18)
Eleven trailer-less commits landed on master in ~36 h (see `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` note). Every one came through a **direct** `gh pr merge --squash` that bypassed `scripts/pr-queue.sh` / `scripts/check-squash-message.sh`. Each landing reds `check-isolation-landed` for every open PR until a baseline-record PR merges; two of those unblock PRs re-created the defect. Master had **no required status checks**, so nothing GitHub-side could refuse.

Same class, same day: #1246 (direct merge) landed an RCA doc that minted ledger-owned ids, redding `lessons` + `check-board-gate` for every PR (fixed by #1253).

## Fix (future-proof at the producer, not the baseline)
1. `infra/cloudbuild/verify.yaml`: before `make verify`, run `bash scripts/check-squash-message.sh --pr $_PR_NUMBER` so the PR's **composed** squash message is judged by the same predicate on every push. A red here is the author's to fix (edit the body), never a baseline entry.
2. Branch protection on `master`: add `control-plane-verify` as a **required** status check (strict = false so an update-branch storm is not required). With (1) in place a direct `gh pr merge` of a bad body is refused by GitHub itself.
3. `AGENTS.md` (supersede doctrine) + `docs/PR-QUEUE.md`: one paragraph — the only merge verbs are `AO_QUEUE_APPLY=1 bash scripts/pr-queue.sh` or `check-squash-message.sh --pr N && gh pr merge N --squash`; the PR body's LAST paragraph is `Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#N` (+ `Closes #N`); the `🤖 Generated with` / `AI-assistance:` lines go above it.
4. PR template: move the trailer paragraph to the very end and add an HTML comment `<!-- keep this paragraph LAST: gh pr merge --squash composes the commit from this body -->`.

## Acceptance
- A PR whose body ends in `AI-assistance:` shows a red `control-plane-verify` naming `commit-missing-ticket-trailer` and cannot be merged from the GitHub UI or `gh pr merge`.
- The same PR with the trailer paragraph moved last goes green and merges; the landed commit classifies `None` under `governance.isolation.trailer.classify_commit`.
- Negative control: `landed-baseline.json` gains no new entry for 7 days after this lands.

## Ordering
Land after the current PR queue drains (2026-09-18): (2) turns every currently-red PR into a hard block, so do it once the queue is green.

items.title: [lifecycle] VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING — #629
items.body:
A lifecycle finding has not reached a terminal state.

- item: #629
- violation: `VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING`
- detail: no green verification attestation is recorded
- remediation: run `make verify` on the branch head before merging and record its attestation; evidence names a commit, and a summary is not evidence. Close out BEFORE the lane is torn down (`governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --issue <n>`), or keep the verified commit reachable: the attestation is measured from one of the two, and the driver refuses to reclaim a lane while this invariant is unsatisfied (#786). For a SQUASH-merged pull request the lane may instead be a tree cut from the default branch after the merge: it is admitted when it contains the commit the squash landed as and that landing carries the same tree as the verified head, and the record then names all three commits (#1098)

Reported by `governance/lifecycle` (issue #321).

Reported by `governance/lifecycle` (issue #321).

items.title: check-pr-queue-squash-guard.sh red on master: gate-regression's merge-base lookup runs unconditionally, not scoped to scripts/ files (#1145 regression)
items.body:
## What is red

\`\`\`
$ bash scripts/check-pr-queue-squash-guard.sh
  FAIL  OK verdict: pr-queue.sh exit=1, expected 0
  FAIL  OK verdict: gh pr merge was not called for PR #10
check-pr-queue-squash-guard: NOT-OK — 2 finding(s)
\`\`\`

## Root cause

#1145/#1231 added a gate-regression pre-merge check to \`scripts/pr-queue.sh\`. \`gate_regression_check()\` itself correctly returns 0 immediately when the PR touches nothing under \`scripts/\`. But the CALL SITE (around line 471, before that function even runs) unconditionally does:

\`\`\`bash
git fetch --quiet origin "$base"
git fetch --quiet origin "$number_head_oid"
number_merge_base="$(git merge-base "origin/$base" "$number_head_oid")"
if [ -z "$number_merge_base" ]; then
  echo "pr-queue: REFUSED — gate-regression CANNOT-ASSESS ..." >&2
  exit 1
fi
\`\`\`

for every PR, regardless of whether it touches \`scripts/\`. \`check-pr-queue-squash-guard.sh\`'s pre-existing offline fixture (PR #10, touches only \`README.md\`, no real git remote/head oid to fetch) now hits this unconditional merge-base lookup, gets an empty result, and the merge is wrongly refused before \`check_squash_message\`'s OK verdict is ever honored.

## Fix

Move the same \`scripts/*\`-touched scoping check up to the call site, so the fetch/merge-base/gate_regression_check sequence only runs when the PR actually touches something under \`scripts/\` — matching what the function itself already documents as its scope.

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1240

Closes #1240

items.title: check-verdict-contains red on master: false-positive piped-grep match in check-pr-queue.sh's own self-test (from #1145/#1231)
items.body:
## What is red

PR #1231 (#1145's gate-regression fix) introduced a new `check-verdict-contains` finding on `origin/master`:

```
FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-pr-queue.sh has 1, the record allows 0
```

## Root cause

`scripts/check-pr-queue.sh:232`:

```bash
if grep -q '^MERGE_ORDER:.*\b80\b' "$out" || grep -q '^MERGE_ORDER:.*\b90\b' "$out"; then
```

The scanner's idiom regex matches a literal `|` followed by `grep ... -q`. This line has no pipe into grep at all — both `grep -q` calls read `"$out"` as a file argument — but the shell `||` operator between them supplies the `|` character the scanner is (correctly, conservatively) looking for. This is a genuine false positive of `check-verdict-contains.sh`'s own documented over-count tolerance, not a real SIGPIPE/pipe-loses-matches risk.

## Fix

Rewrite to avoid the shape entirely (no behavior change, self-test proves it — 20/20 assertions in `check-pr-queue.sh`'s own self-test still pass, including the specific `MERGE_ORDER` exclusion assertions):

```bash
merge_order_line="$(grep '^MERGE_ORDER:' "$out" || true)"
if [[ "$merge_order_line" =~ (^|[^0-9])80([^0-9]|$) ]] || [[ "$merge_order_line" =~ (^|[^0-9])90([^0-9]|$) ]]; then
```

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1145

Closes #1236

items.title: aosdk.list_policies() cannot parse the real GET /v1/policies: the SDK and cpapi disagree on every field (controls is int vs List[str])
items.body:
## Finding

`aosdk.ControlPlaneClient.list_policies()` — the **published** SDK's policy
surface — cannot parse the payload the real control plane actually serves for
`GET /v1/policies`. It is not a subtle shape drift: the two sides disagree on
**every** field, and `PolicyBinding.from_dict` raises a hard `TypeError` on the
first row.

Measured, driving the real surface in-process (real `identity/cpapi` app, real
`aosdk` parser) — the server returns:

```json
{"controls": 3, "description": "reviewer posture guardrails",
 "id": "reviewer-bundle", "mode": "enforce"}
```

and the SDK's parser raises `TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable` from
`control-plane/sdk/python/aosdk/model.py:465`:

```python
controls=list(raw.get("controls") or []),   # server sends an int COUNT, SDK wants List[str]
```

| real server — `identity/cpapi/model.py:265` (`PolicyView`) | SDK — `aosdk/model.py:465` (`PolicyBinding`) |
|---|---|
| `id: str` | `policyId` — via `str(raw.get("policyId") or "")`, so a real row yields **`""`** |
| `description: str` | — (SDK's `name` falls back to the empty `policyId`) |
| `mode: str` | — |
| `controls: int` (a **count**) | `controls: List[str]` → `TypeError` |
| — | `bundle`, `version`, `tenantId`, `enabled` |

Two consequences, in severity order:

1. **`list_policies()` cannot work at all** against a real control plane — every
   call raises. A consumer that "integrates via the SDK" is broken at runtime.
2. **Fixing only `controls` is not the fix.** `id` never maps to `policyId`, so
   the SDK would then return bindings whose `policy_id` is `""` — a *silent*
   wrong answer, which is worse than the loud one. The key names must be
   reconciled, not just the type.

This is exactly the class of break that a published-but-unconsumed SDK hides:
lane #1229 (the first in-repo consumer) surfaced it on its first real call.

## Verify

Fails on `master` today; must pass after the fix:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, sys
ROOT = os.getcwd()
sys.path[:0] = [f"{ROOT}/control-plane/sdk/python", f"{ROOT}/identity",
                f"{ROOT}/registry", f"{ROOT}/gateway", f"{ROOT}/guardrails"]
from cpapi.fakes import build_test_app
from aosdk.model import PolicyBinding

rig = build_test_app()
rows = rig.app.handle(
    "GET", "/v1/policies", principal=rig.principal("acme", "u_admin")
)["data"]["items"]
bindings = [PolicyBinding.from_dict(r) for r in rows]   # must not raise
assert all(b.policy_id for b in bindings), "policyId silently empty — id is not mapped"
assert all(isinstance(b.controls, list) for b in bindings)
print("OK", [(b.policy_id, b.controls) for b in bindings])
PY
```

Note the second assertion deliberately catches the *naive* fix (coerce
`controls` to a list but leave `id` unmapped): a gate that the obvious-but-wrong
patch cannot pass.

## Needs a contract decision (do not guess)

Which side is canonical for `GET /v1/policies`?

- **(A)** The server is canonical and `PolicyView` is a *guardrail-store* view
  (`id`/`description`/`mode`/`controls:int` = "this bundle enforces N controls").
  Then the fix is SDK-side: `PolicyBinding` must gain those fields, or the route
  must serve agent-policy bindings instead. Note the route is *labelled* agent
  policy — `Route("GET", "/v1/policies", "policy:read", "policies.list")` — while
  `policies` is a `PolicyStore` of guardrail bundles, so the two readings
  genuinely differ.
- **(B)** The SDK is canonical (`policyId`/`bundle`/`version`/`enabled`) and the
  guardrail-store view is being served under the wrong route/fields.

This is an architecture call (route semantics + which module owns the public
contract), not a mechanical one — routing to `architecture-sme` per `AGENTS.md`
rather than picking a side here. Whichever wins, the loser's public surface
changes, so it needs a deliberate decision.

## Provenance / scope

- Found by lane #1229 (PR #1230), the repo's first in-repo SDK consumer. The
  drift is currently **pinned** by `e2e/tests/test_sdk_control_plane_call.py`
  (it asserts the `TypeError` so the break cannot rot silently) — that pin is a
  placeholder, and should be **replaced by the parse assertion above** once this
  is fixed.
- Not fixed here: this issue's fix touches `control-plane/sdk/python/aosdk/**`
  and/or `identity/cpapi/**`, neither of which lane #1229 owns.

Also observed while driving the seam (separate, lower severity, same module):
`identity/cpapi/fakes.py:build_test_app` documents *"override any seam via
`**overrides`"* but passing a seam `build_test_app(session_verifier=...)` raises
`TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument 'session_verifier'`, because
the name is already bound in the `ControlPlane(...)` call. Callers must assign
the seam after construction (as `identity/cpapi/tests/test_wiring_rbac.py:79`
does). Either the docstring or the signature is wrong.

items.title: the agent instruction still teaches raw `gh pr merge --squash` — the trailer red recurred 8×, and two unblocks re-created it while recording it (#1145)
items.body:
### The defect

`gh pr merge --squash` composes the landed commit message as `"<title> (#N)\n\n<PR BODY>"` —
the repository declares `squash_merge_commit_message: PR_BODY`, verified live by
`scripts/repo-settings.sh verify` (`all 5 declared field(s) match the live settings`). So a PR
body without a **trailing trailer paragraph** lands a commit that carries no
`Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#<n>`, and `scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` reddens on
**master's own tip** — which makes `make verify` red for *every* lane on the box.

Every **programmatic** merge path already consults the guard
(`scripts/check-squash-message.sh`, #1001): `scripts/pr-queue.sh` (now also gate-regression
checked by #1231) and `governance/lifecycle`'s close-out. The **raw** path consulted nothing.

### The producer, measured

`governance/spawn/render.py` — the ONE copy of the instruction prose every spawned lane
receives — told the agent to run the raw command:

```
$ grep -n 'gh pr merge' governance/spawn/render.py
180:        "`gh pr merge <number> --squash --delete-branch`, then close the issue. "
```

That is the shape the offenders walked. **Eight recurrences in one day**, and the last three
cleared the red or recorded it while re-creating it:

| merge | what it was | its own landed message |
|---|---|---|
| `2964d65` #1221 | recorded the 6th offender | trailer-less (`Co-authored-by` last) |
| `b81f18a` #1225 | recorded the 7th + 8th | trailer-less (bare `Closes #<n>`, **0** `Refs` lines) |
| `abdf8dd` #1231 | **carried `Refs …#1145` correctly** | compliant — the counter-example |

`#1221` and `#1225` are two different lanes that both reddened master *while fixing it*, 22
minutes apart; three further unblock PRs (mine included) were closed as superseded. That is
what makes this the durable half rather than another baseline entry.

### Remedy

One guarded entrypoint, and the instruction that names it — no GitHub Actions (GR-15), no
history rewrite, no server-side dependency:

* `scripts/merge-pr.sh` — runs `scripts/check-squash-message.sh` **first** and refuses by name
  (`squash-message-would-drop-trailer`); `gh pr merge` is never invoked on a refusal or on no
  verdict. Dry run by default.
* `governance/spawn/render.py` — the instruction now names the guarded entrypoint.
* `scripts/check-merge-guard.sh` — proves the refusal offline (no network, nothing merged),
  wired into the gate of record by `scripts/verify.sh`: NOT-OK ⇒ rc 1 named and never merged;
  OK ⇒ rc 0 and merged exactly once; no verdict ⇒ rc 2 and never merged. It also asserts the
  instruction surfaces hand out the guarded entrypoint and refuses a **planted** raw
  instruction by name, so the rule cannot pass by matching nothing.

**What this does not do:** it cannot make a deliberate bypass impossible — a human or agent
that calls the CLI merge directly still bypasses every local control. Only the required status
check in **#1138** can do that; that boundary is named rather than papered over.

Measured on the live board while writing this: **9 of 20 open PRs** have bodies that would land
trailer-less, so the obligation is not hypothetical:

```
$ for n in $(gh pr list --state open ...); do bash scripts/check-squash-message.sh --pr $n; done
PR 1120 rc=1 commit-missing-ticket-trailer      PR 1115 rc=1 ...
PR 1111 rc=1 ...  PR 1110 rc=1 ...  PR 1105 rc=1 ...
PR 1097 rc=1 ...  PR 1088 rc=1 ...  PR 1087 rc=1 ...  PR 1083 rc=1 ...
PR 1151 rc=0 OK  ...   (9 refused / 11 clean)
```

items.title: e2e: drive the published aosdk against the real identity/cpapi surface (the SDK has no in-repo consumer)
items.body:
## GOAL

Make the shipped consumer SDK prove itself against the real control-plane surface: add an end-to-end call that drives `control-plane/sdk/python/aosdk` through `identity/cpapi`'s real `ControlPlane.handle(...)`, so SDK↔server drift is detectable **in-repo**.

## Context (measured 2026-09-17, deep review register #1201)

`aosdk` has **no in-repo importer**. Its only consumers are its own tests, which drive a `FakeControlPlane` transport (`control-plane/sdk/python/tests/_fakes.py`); `test_end_to_end.py` is self-referential for that reason. Meanwhile `e2e/golden_path.py` exercises the real pillar modules but through `e2e/wiring.py`'s bundle, never the published SDK. So the SDK can drift from the surface it documents with nothing in the repo to catch it.

The real surface is `identity/cpapi`: `ControlPlane.handle(method, path, *, body, query, token, principal)` (`identity/cpapi/control.py:157`) returns the `{ok,status,requestId,data,error}` envelope the SDK parses; `identity/cpapi/wiring.py` ships the real adapters (`RbacAuthorizer`, `RegistryAgentOps`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new end-to-end call drives `aosdk.ControlPlaneClient` onto a real `cpapi.ControlPlane` assembled from the repo's real adapters, **in process** — no network, no containers, no server socket.
- [ ] The SDK's typed models are produced from the **real** envelope (fail if it falls back to a double).
- [ ] A real refusal surfaces as the SDK's typed `ApiError` carrying the server's own `status`/`code` (from `identity/cpapi`'s error vocabulary, not a hand-written string).
- [ ] It runs under `make e2e` / `make verify` (the `e2e` suite is declared, so a new test under `e2e/tests/` is picked up).
- [ ] `make verify` green.

## Verify command

`python3 -m pytest e2e/tests -q -k sdk && make verify`

## Chain markers

Parent: #1201
Root=none

## Lane

control-plane

## Model tier

flash / low

## Evidence required

The test's real output (including the refusal's code/status as produced by the real router), plus `make verify`.

items.title: master red: #1225 re-created the trailer red in its own merge commit (b81f18a) — the second consecutive unblock to do so
items.body:
### The measurement

Three consecutive lanes tried to clear the `check-isolation-landed` red on
`origin/master` today, and **the first two re-created it in their own merge commit**.
The third one is this issue's subject: the red is live again at `origin/master = b81f18a`.

```
$ cd <pristine detached worktree at origin/master> && bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh
          FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:b81f18a... is not recorded legacy — ...
        isolation-enforce: NOT-OK — 1 unrecorded and 0 stale baseline entr(ies) in HEAD
rc=1
```

`b81f18a` is **#1225** — `fix(isolation): record the seventh and eighth trailer-less
landed commits`. Measured halves:

```
$ git log -1 --format=%B b81f18a | awk 'BEGIN{RS=""} END{print "["$0"]"}'
[Closes #1224]
$ git log -1 --format=%B b81f18a | grep -c '^Refs'
0
```

Its last paragraph is a bare `Closes #<n>` and it has **no `Refs <slug>#<n>` line at
all**. By the shared predicate's own position rule that is `commit-missing-ticket-trailer`
— a paragraph holding only a closing keyword is a *missing* trailer, never a passing one
(the rule that made the baseline SHRINK by 8 entries in #835 was the keyword sharing a
paragraph *with* the reference line, not the keyword alone). So the second unblock
attempt landed the exact defect it was recorded to fix.

### The pattern, measured

| attempt | merged | its own merge commit |
|---|---|---|
| #1221 (`2964d65`) | 22:57:41Z | trailer-less (last paragraph `Co-authored-by`) |
| #1225 (`b81f18a`) | 23:19:54Z | trailer-less (last paragraph bare `Closes #1224`, 0 `Refs` lines) |

Two different lanes, two different sessions, the same outcome within 22 minutes — because
**the landed message is the PR body** (`squash_merge_commit_message: PR_BODY`, declared and
verified live by `scripts/repo-settings.sh`), and nothing on the direct-merge path reads it.

### Remedy

* **Residue (this issue, unblock only):** record `b81f18a` in
  `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` by an explicit reviewed commit.
* **Prevention:** #1145 — the producer. `governance/spawn/render.py` told every spawned lane
  to run `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch` directly, and the raw path consults
  nothing. Only server-side enforcement (#1138) can make a bypass impossible; the reachable
  fix is to stop the instruction from teaching the raw path.

items.title: master red: #1221 cleared `check-isolation-landed` and re-created it in its own merge commit (2964d65) — residue now two commits
items.body:
### The measurement that matters

`check-isolation-landed` was cleared on `origin/master` at 22:57:41Z by **#1221** —
a PR whose *title* is `fix(isolation): record the sixth trailer-less landed commit
in the baseline`. **Fifteen minutes later the check is red again, and it names
#1221's own merge commit:**

```
$ cd <pristine detached worktree at origin/master> && bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh
          FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:2964d65d43ff is not recorded legacy — ...
        isolation-enforce: NOT-OK — 1 unrecorded and 0 stale baseline entr(ies) in HEAD
check-isolation-landed: FAIL (1 violation(s))
rc=1
```

Measured halves for `2964d65d43ffe33e864f80df2d1d426210ad9430`:

* `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2964d65d43ff origin/master` → **landed**;
* `git log -1 --format=%B` → last paragraph is `Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5`; the only
  `Refs` token in the message is the **prose phrase** *"no \`Refs\`/\`Closes\`/\`Fixes\` trailer
  anywhere"*, and `Closes #1214` sits in the `## Closes` section at the **top** of the body.

### Second offender, same window

`b0adff3bcd2d` (#1223, `fix(terraform): commit real GCS backend…`) landed with no ticket
reference anywhere and a last paragraph of only `Co-authored-by`. Measured on a pristine
worktree at `origin/master`.

The residue grew from **one commit to two inside a single measurement window.**

### Why this is the finding, not just another recurrence

This is the **seventh** occurrence of the class today
(#960/#976 → #996/#991 → #1150 → #1171 → #1185/#1188/#1191 → #1196/#1210 → #1213 → #1221).

It is also the one that retires the remedy. A lane whose **entire purpose** was to record the
previous trailer-less commit landed trailer-less itself. Recording residue unblocks a lane and
prevents nothing — and it cannot even hold, because a squash commit cannot record its own SHA
before it exists (`#836`).

### Remedy, split honestly

* **Residue (this issue, unblock only):** record the two measured commits in
  `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` by an explicit reviewed commit.
* **Prevention:** #1145 — the producer. `governance/spawn/render.py` told every spawned lane
  to run `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch` directly; that instruction is what the
  offenders walked. Nothing local can make a *bypass* impossible (that needs the required
  status check in #1138); the reachable fix is to stop the instruction from teaching the raw
  path.

items.title: a stray /tmp/pytest.ini hijacks pytest's rootdir and fakes SIX red checks (and a verify: FAIL) for any lane working under /tmp
items.body:
## What is wrong

A **stray `/tmp/pytest.ini`** on the build box hijacks pytest's rootdir for any lane whose
worktree sits under `/tmp`, and makes **six checks report a false red** — including a false
`verify: FAIL` for the whole composite.

```
$ stat -c '%y %s %U' /tmp/pytest.ini
2026-09-16 21:48:28 -0400  43  akushnir

$ cat /tmp/pytest.ini
[pytest]
addopts = --import-mode=importlib
```

Nothing in this repository references it (`grep -rln 'pytest.ini' scripts/ docs/` → empty; the
repo root has no `pytest.ini`/`pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg`/`tox.ini`). With no closer config,
pytest walks **up** from the worktree, adopts `/tmp/pytest.ini`, and `--import-mode=importlib`
then breaks the `from conftest import …` idiom the suites rely on — the test directory is never
prepended to `sys.path`.

## Measured A/B — same commit, same check, only the venue differs

`origin/master` = `982647c`, two detached worktrees, identical commands:

| check | `/tmp/...` venue | `/home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/...` venue |
|---|---|---|
| `check-telemetry` | **rc 1** — 5× `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'conftest'` | **rc 0** — `check-telemetry: OK`, 0 errors |
| `check-control-audit` | rc 1 — `No module named 'conftest'` | **rc 0** — `OK` (4 negative controls go red) |
| `check-erp-module` | rc 1 — `No module named 'conftest'` | **rc 0** |
| `check-portal-auth-env` | rc 1 | **rc 0** — `OK` |
| `check-ungated-suites` | rc 1 — `engine/core/tickets (exit 4: No module named 'core')` | **rc 0** — `OK` |
| `pytest telemetry/chat/tests` | collection ERROR | **rc 0 — 56 passed** |
| `check-isolation-landed` | rc 1 | rc 1 *(genuinely red — tracked by #1186)* |

Verbatim from the `/tmp` venue:

```
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'conftest'
Hint: make sure your test modules/packages have valid Python names.
```

`True` measured conclusion: **at `982647c` master's only real red is `check-isolation-landed`
(#1186).** The other six are this artifact.

## Why it is not "just a /tmp problem"

It corrupts *evidence*, which is the thing this repo treats as currency. A lane that measures from
`/tmp` and reports the result publishes a false master-red set and a false `verify: FAIL`. That
happened during this session: a lane reported *"`verify: FAIL (7 of 175 checks failed, 5 skipped)` —
all 7 reds reproduce on pristine `fc4bd93`"*; five of those seven are this artifact, reproduced in a
`/tmp` venue. The blast radius is any session on this box that does not happen to put its worktree
under `$HOME`.

## Fix shape (pick one, but make it mechanical)

1. **Delete the debris** — `/tmp/pytest.ini` is ephemeral, one day old, and referenced by nothing:
   `rm /tmp/pytest.ini`. This is the immediate unblock, but it is **not durable**: any future lane
   can drop the same file again and silently re-poison every measurement.
2. **Make the repo's rootdir un-hijackable** — give the repository its own pytest configuration at
   its root (or per suite), so rootdir is pinned to the checkout and an ancestor ini can never win.
   This is the durable half, and it is the one that should be gated.
3. **Gate it** — a control that plants an ancestor `pytest.ini` and asserts the suites still
   collect, i.e. that the venue cannot change the verdict. Without this the fix is a doc.

Prefer 2 + 3; do 1 as the immediate unblock only if the operator confirms no lane is using `/tmp`
as a pytest fixture right now (I did **not** delete it — a peer may be mid-run, and deleting shared
state is the same class of harm as the broad `pkill -f 'scripts/verify.sh'` that already killed a
peer's gate this session).

## Evidence

- `stat`/`cat /tmp/pytest.ini` above; `grep -rln 'pytest.ini' scripts/ docs/` → empty.
- The venue table above, both columns measured at `982647c` in detached worktrees.
- Related prior art: `#1044` (`fix(governance): make governance/* pytest suites collect together`),
  `#1082` (a check mapping an INTERRUPTED suite to FAIL), and the ancestor-config trap this
  reproduces.

items.title: futureproof capstone: add the assesses-real-tree link — a gate that never assesses must not pass with the rest (#1193 follow-up)
items.body:
## What

#1193 landed the futureproof capstone (`governance/tagging/e2e.py`, merged by
#1197 as `9bdddf2`) with four links per mechanism: `authority-declared`,
`gate-wired`, `gate-falsifiable`, `mechanisms-complete-and-disjoint`. **All four
links pass a gate that can never fire**, and that is the gap this issue closes.

## The measured hole

`scripts/verify.sh` records a check that answers **rc 2 CANNOT-ASSESS** as
`SKIP`, and its summary still prints a PASS:

```
verify: PASS (… 2 skipped: dispatch-queue, paperclip-routines)
```

So a gate that is **permanently CANNOT-ASSESS** passes every link the capstone
has today. It is discovered, executable, carries a negative control — and
assesses nothing. Two live witnesses measured on pristine `origin/master`:

| Gate | rc | Verdict line |
|---|---|---|
| `bash scripts/check-paperclip-routines.sh` | 2 | `check-paperclip-routines: CANNOT-ASSESS — could not build the dropped-entry tree` |
| `bash scripts/check-dispatch-queue.sh` | 2 | `check-dispatch-queue: CANNOT-ASSESS — 'dispatch queue --check' could not assess against the current board (see stderr above)` |

`check-paperclip-routines.sh` was already filed as #1176; `check-dispatch-queue.sh`
hides the six queued-but-closed issues of #1189. This is the same doctrine the
issue quotes — *"a gate that cannot fail is a formality"* — applied one level
deeper: **a gate that never assesses is a formality that hides in the `skipped`
bucket.**

## Ask

Add link **`assesses-real-tree`** to the capstone, per mechanism: the mechanism's
declared gate(s) are **run** on the real tree and must reach a **verdict** (rc 0
or 1). A gate that answers rc 2 (or hangs, or cannot be run) makes its mechanism
**DECLARED-ONLY, not ENFORCED** — the verdict vocabulary
`docs/SYSTEM-APP-GOVERNANCE-E2E-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` (#1156) already uses.

Reporting stays per mechanism, with a count per verdict
(ENFORCED / DECLARED-ONLY / IMPLEMENTED-UNGATED / ABSENT).

## Related

- #1193 — the capstone this extends (closed, merged by #1197).
- #1176, #1189 — the two live witnesses above.
- #1199 — the general form: whether the composite's `skipped` bucket should
  ratchet, so a permanently-skipped check stops reading as part of a PASS.
- #1198 — `scripts/check-knowledge-index.sh` declares no provocation of its own
  failure path (measured while building this link).

items.title: make verify: a permanently-skipped check still reads as PASS — the skipped bucket should ratchet (#1176/#1189)
items.body:
Parent: #1254

## What

`scripts/verify.sh` records a check that answers **rc 2 CANNOT-ASSESS** as
`SKIP`, and its summary still prints a PASS:

```
verify: PASS (… N skipped: <names>)
```

Skips are named, which is honest — but nothing makes a *permanently* skipped
check stop reading as part of a green board. A check that can never assess is
not a pass that happens to be skipped; it is a check that does not exist, wearing
the composite's green.

## Measured — two live witnesses on pristine `origin/master` (`04ad55a`)

| Gate | rc | Verdict line |
|---|---|---|
| `bash scripts/check-paperclip-routines.sh` | 2 | `check-paperclip-routines: CANNOT-ASSESS — could not build the dropped-entry tree` |
| `bash scripts/check-dispatch-queue.sh` | 2 | `check-dispatch-queue: CANNOT-ASSESS — 'dispatch queue --check' could not assess against the current board (see stderr above)` |

Both are discovered, executable and carry real provoked controls, so they pass
every "is it wired?" test — and both assess **nothing**. `check-dispatch-queue.sh`
is rc 2 purely because the committed board snapshot is older than its own
15-minute freshness window, which is the *normal* state of this checkout. Each
one hides a filed defect that is only visible when it is allowed to speak:
#1176 (`schedule-unprojected: ao-fleet-reap`) and #1189 (six queued-but-closed
issues).

## The general form

The per-gate instances are tracked. The general gap is that the composite has no
notion of a **ratchet**: a check that is SKIP on one run and SKIP on every run
after it is indistinguishable, in the verdict line, from a check that assessed
and passed. Two shapes to consider, both in the idiom this repository already
uses for legacy drift (`governance/lifecycle/baseline.json`,
`scripts/check-docs.sh`'s docs-index quarantine):

1. **A per-check skip budget** — a discovered check that answers rc 2 for N
   consecutive attested runs is reported as a *named standing skip* in the
   summary and in `.verify/attestation.json`, so a permanently-blind check stops
   being silently part of a `PASS`.
2. **A named exemption with a shrinking list** — a permanently-blind check must
   be exempted by name against an open issue, the exemption is stale the moment
   the check assesses, and the list can only shrink. That is the shape the
   futureproof capstone (issue #1193) uses for its `assesses-real-tree` /
   `gate-falsifiable` links, applied repo-wide.

Neither should change rc-2 semantics themselves — a genuine CANNOT-ASSESS is
still not a failure; what changes is whether the *board* can read it as green.

## Ask

Decide which shape the composite adopts, and wire it so a permanently skipped
check can no longer be quoted as part of a `PASS` without being named as a
standing gap. Filed from the #1193 lane as the general form of #1176 / #1189.

Refs #1193 · witnesses #1176, #1189

items.title: check-knowledge-index.sh declares no provocation — the gate cannot be shown to fail (#1193 capstone)
items.body:
## What

`scripts/check-knowledge-index.sh` is discovered, executable, and invoked by
`make verify`, but it **declares no provocation of its own failure path**. It is
nine lines of dispatch around `python3 governance/knowledge/cli.py validate` and
nothing else:

```bash
python3 governance/knowledge/cli.py validate
rc=$?
case "$rc" in
  0) exit 0 ;;
  2) exit 2 ;;
  *) exit 1 ;;
esac
```

Its own header states the gap rather than hiding it: *"It reports, but does not
fail on, unreachable CMR-hub kinds (submodule absent) and on drift — those are
honest gaps and refresh signals, not violations."*

## Why it matters

`docs/SYSTEM-APP-GOVERNANCE-E2E-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` (#1156) sets the standard this
falls short of: an **ENFORCED** verdict requires the surface be *seen to fail* on
a real violation, provoked externally — not merely that a gate names it. A gate
whose failure path is never exercised is the shape `GR-12` / `AO-GR-4` refuses
("a gate that cannot fail is a formality"), and it is the same class
`governance/dupcheck/check-duplicates.sh` (#1164) was filed for, one step milder:
the gate *runs*, but nothing demonstrates it can go red.

## Measured

Found by the `gate-falsifiable` link of the futureproof capstone
(`governance/futureproof/e2e.py`, issue #1193), which scans each mechanism's gate
for a declared provocation/negative-control/self-test vocabulary **and** a
verdict vocabulary. Against the whole ten-mechanism table on this tree,
`check-knowledge-index.sh` is the only gate that declares neither — the
`authority` mechanism's `check-authority.sh` declares an explicit
`selfcheck` over "every DECLARED behavioral control ... that must return the
verdict it declares", so it holds.

```
FAIL  mechanism 'index' fails gate-falsifiable — gate check-knowledge-index.sh
      declares no provocation (no negative control, self-test or mutation)
```

## Ask

Give `scripts/check-knowledge-index.sh` a provoked half — a mutant catalogue, or
a scratch tree with a mandatory kind removed — that must be refused **by name**,
with its clean twin accepted, in the shape
`scripts/check-paperclip-routines.sh` and `scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh`
already use. The capstone carries this as a named, shrinking exemption
(`governance/futureproof/known-gaps.json`) that FAILS the moment the gap closes,
so the entry cannot outlive the fix.

Refs #1193

items.title: check-dispatch-queue: the committed queue names 6 closed issues, so the check is red on a fresh board and inert on a stale one (#1178 finding)
items.body:
Parent: #1254

## What I measured

`scripts/check-dispatch-queue.sh` runs `python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py queue --check`,
which compares the committed `governance/dispatch/queue.yaml` against the committed
`.board/snapshot.json`. On a **fresh** board it refuses, naming six queued-but-closed
issues:

```
queue: FAIL (6 problem(s))
  - #830 is queued but already closed — drop it from the queue
  - #880 is queued but already closed — drop it from the queue
  - #881 is queued but already closed — drop it from the queue
  - #884 is queued but already closed — drop it from the queue
  - #886 is queued but already closed — drop it from the queue
  - #890 is queued but already closed — drop it from the queue
check-dispatch-queue: FAIL — 'dispatch queue --check' refused the committed queue (rc=1)
```

## Why it is latent (and why any snapshot refresh trips it)

The check is **time-bounded**: it returns CANNOT-ASSESS (rc 2) whenever the snapshot is
older than 15 minutes, and only then runs the `exists/open` rules.

```
$ bash scripts/check-dispatch-queue.sh ; echo rc=$?
queue --check: CANNOT-ASSESS — snapshot-stale (86.2m > 15m); 'exists/open' checks need a fresh board
check-dispatch-queue: CANNOT-ASSESS (tests pass, cycle control provoked and refused; committed board snapshot is stale)
rc=2
```

`verify.sh` maps rc 2 to WARN/SKIP, so the check passes by **not assessing** — which is
why master reads green. Its `exists/open` half only ever executes inside a 15-minute
window after a refresh, so it is either inert or red, and never green for a reason that
means anything. Note `queue.yaml` and `check-dispatch-queue.sh` are a different lane's
surface (this was found while landing #1178, whose own rule needs the snapshot labels and
so refreshed `.board/snapshot.json`); the directed fix belongs to that owner.

## Reproduce

```
$ git worktree add --detach /tmp/q origin/master && cd /tmp/q
$ bash scripts/check-dispatch-queue.sh; echo rc=$?          # stale  -> rc=2 (inert)
$ python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py snapshot --from-github # fresh
$ bash scripts/check-dispatch-queue.sh; echo rc=$?          # fresh  -> rc=1 (six findings)
```

## Why it is worth an issue rather than a one-off prune

Dropping the six ids fixes today; the drift returns the moment another queued issue
closes. The durable half is either (a) a queue entry that is *not* re-checked against a
volatile external state, or (b) a declared, reviewed expectation about which entries may
be stale — plus a decision on whether a board older than 15 minutes should really make
the check unassessable. A check that cannot run when the board is stale is a formality
(GR-12), and this one is currently green only in that state.

Found while landing #1178. This issue is a **direction** report, not a claim — I did not
touch `governance/dispatch/**`.

items.title: isolation-landed: two landed squash commits carry no ticket trailer, so make verify is red on master for every lane
items.body:
**Role (executor):** subagent
**Epic:** none — chain head
**Pillar:** autonomous-ops
**Lane:** governance-isolation
**Model tier (FinOps):** flash
**Thinking effort:** low

## GOAL

Restore `check-isolation-landed` to green on `master` by recording the **two**
already-landed commits whose squash messages carry no ticket trailer, using the
remedy the check itself prescribes — an explicit, reviewed baseline entry per
measured finding.

## Why this is filed now (it blocks every lane)

`make verify` is **red on `master`** for every lane, not just the commit that
caused it: `check-isolation-landed` walks the landed history, so a commit merged
without a trailer fails the gate for every branch that is descended from it. No
lane can produce green `make verify` evidence until this is recorded.

## Measured (2026-09-17)

Reproduced on a **clean checkout of the base commit**, not on a working tree:

```bash
$ git checkout --detach 7fe3efa          # the merge base a live lane branched from
$ bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh
          FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:04e9c1af08ff is not recorded legacy
          — if the commit has not MERGED yet, put the reference in a trailing
          trailer paragraph and re-push; if it is already landed on a protected
          branch the message can never be corrected (history is never rewritten),
          so record it in landed-baseline.json by an explicit reviewed commit
          carrying this measured finding — never automatically, and never to
          silence a run (#836)
check-isolation-landed: FAIL (1 violation(s))
rc=1
```

The same command on the **current** `master` tip reports **two** offenders, because
a second one landed in between:

```bash
$ git rev-parse --short origin/master      # ea391d9
$ bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh
          FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:ea391d9a863b is not recorded legacy
          FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:04e9c1af08ff is not recorded legacy
check-isolation-landed: FAIL
```

| Offender | Subject as it landed | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `04e9c1af08ff` | `chore(feature-flags): promote ci_cd verify/apply triggers (#1177)` | squash message composed from a PR body with no trailing `Refs` trailer |
| `ea391d9a863b` | `feat(terraform): reusable IAM role-bundle pattern for deployer SA (#1185)` | same shape, landed after the base above |

Both are **squash commits whose composed message lost the trailer paragraph** —
the failure mode `check-squash-message.sh` (#1102) exists to prevent, so the
immediate question for the lane is why the composed message still lost it.

## Constraints

- **History is never rewritten.** Both commits are already on a protected branch;
  the message cannot be corrected and must not be. The remedy is a baseline entry.
- **Explicit and reviewed, never automatic** (#836, and the check's own text):
  `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` must gain one entry per measured
  finding, in a commit that carries the finding. Do not silence the run by
  widening the range or dropping the check.
- **A stale entry is refused too** (`quarantine-entry-stale`): the baseline is a
  record of real, measured offenders, not a blanket waiver.
- One issue = one lane = one branch; `governance/isolation/**` is the only surface
  this lane may touch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `landed-baseline.json` carries a measured entry for **each** offender, and
      none for a commit that now complies.
      (checked: `bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh`)
- [ ] The check's own self-test still passes — including
      `quarantine-entry-stale` and `baseline-malformed`, so the baseline is
      provably not a blanket waiver.
      (checked: `bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` → `SELF-TEST: OK`)
- [ ] `make verify` is green on `master` again for a fresh lane.
      (checked: `make verify`)
- [ ] The squash-message gap is dispositioned: either `check-squash-message.sh`
      already refuses this shape and the merges bypassed it (name how), or it does
      not and the missing case is added. (checked: the finding quoted in the PR)
- [ ] `make verify` is green. (checked: `make verify`)

## Verify command

```bash
bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh && make verify
```

Root: none

_To be filled when the lane lands._
