items.title: institutionalize the tag authority: a golden rule, the contract docs, and a mandate gate that cannot rot
items.body:
**Role (executor):** subagent
**Epic:** none — chain head
**Pillar:** autonomous-ops
**Lane:** governance-tagging
**Model tier (FinOps):** pro
**Thinking effort:** medium

## GOAL

Make the tag authority (`governance/tagging/`, landed by #1175) **constitutional**:
a numbered golden rule in `AGENTS.md`, a mandatory section in each contract doc,
the declaration fields an issue form actually offers, and a gate check that FAILS
when any of those stops declaring it — so the rule cannot decay into a doc-only
advisory.

## Constraints (non-negotiable)

- **A doc-only rule is advisory (GR-29).** The rule is not institutionalized until
  a check fails when a contract doc drops it. That check is the deliverable; the
  prose is only half.
- **Do not lower any declared surface class.** `governance/tagging` is declared
  `elite` in `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml`; touching the docs must not
  drop any surface below its declared rung (`make surface-class` must stay OK).
- **Do not break existing forms.** `scripts/check-issue-template.sh` validates
  each issue form's required field ids **by name**; adding fields is allowed,
  dropping or renaming one fails the gate.
- **Do not touch the filing seam here.** `governance/conformance/filing.py` is
  [#1182](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/1182)'s lane. This
  lane makes the rule binding on *prose and forms*; #1182 makes it binding on
  *filings*. Two lanes, two surfaces, no shared file.
- One issue = one lane = one branch. `governance/tagging/**` (except where this
  lane must add the new refusal + provocation), `AGENTS.md`, `docs/GOVERNANCE.md`,
  `docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md`, `docs/QA-GATE.md`, `docs/TAGGING.md`,
  `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/fleet-task.yml`, `scripts/check-tagging.sh`, `Makefile`.

## Context (measured 2026-09-17)

The repository's existing pattern for making a rule non-rotting is
`scripts/check-chronological-dispatch.sh`: it declares
`docs=(AGENTS.md docs/GOVERNANCE.md docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md)`, requires a
case-sensitive **marker vocabulary** in every one of them, requires extra markers
in `AGENTS.md` (it must forbid board scavenging by the word `Kanban`), and then
proves the behavioural half with provocations. A rule that stops being declared
fails the gate by name.

The tag authority has the **behavioural** half already (#1175: five checks,
eleven refusals provoked, artifact round trips, wired into `make verify` by
auto-discovery). What it does not have is the **declarative** half: nothing
anywhere in the constitution says a governed artifact must be tagged, and nothing
would notice if the docs stopped saying it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` carries a numbered golden rule for the tag authority, naming
      the authority path, the two borrowed vocabularies, the `posture` and
      `lifecycle` dimensions, and the gate that enforces it.
      (checked: `grep -n 'tag authority' AGENTS.md`)
- [ ] `docs/GOVERNANCE.md`, `docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md` and `docs/QA-GATE.md` each
      declare the rule with the marker vocabulary the check requires.
      (checked: `bash scripts/check-tagging.sh`)
- [ ] `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/fleet-task.yml` offers `posture` and `lifecycle`
      fields, and `check-issue-template.sh` still passes with its negative
      control. (checked: `make issue-template`)
- [ ] `scripts/check-tagging.sh` gains a **sixth** check, `tagging-mandate`, which
      FAILS naming the specific doc and the specific missing marker, and which is
      itself provoked: a scratch copy with one marker removed must be refused by
      name, and the unmutated docs must be refused nothing.
      (checked: `bash scripts/check-tagging.sh`)
- [ ] The new check is real in both directions: removing a marker from any of the
      four docs turns `make tagging` red, and restoring it turns it green.
      (checked: the provocation's own clean twin)
- [ ] `make lint` names `tagging` as a fine-grained check, so it is discoverable
      outside `make verify`. (checked: `make lint`)
- [ ] `make verify` is green. (checked: `make verify`)

items.title: governance/dispatch: the entry point is dead by construction — no producer for the board liveness contract, silent epic-closed dead-end, and frontier() naming work claim refuses
items.body:
GOAL (done = this): from a clean checkout of `origin/master`, the issue/epic governance entry point works end-to-end — `governance/dispatch/cli.py status` reaches a **verdict instead of `CANNOT-ASSESS`**, an issue that dangles on a **closed** epic is **REPORTED** (with a reachable re-parenting remedy) rather than silently unclaimable, and `status`/`frontier` never name work that `claim` refuses.

WHY — measured on a pristine detached worktree of `origin/master` @ `04e9c1a` (2026-09-17):

```
$ python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py status
status: CANNOT-ASSESS — snapshot-stale (131.9m > 15m) — refresh first: python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py snapshot --from-github
snapshot: kushin77/agent-orchestrator generated 2026-09-17T16:25:50Z (603 issues)
rc=2
```

```
$ crontab -l | grep -c snapshot      # the board-refresh rung …
0                                    # … is not installed
$ crontab -l | grep -c 'ao-fleet-'   # the four OTHER rungs ARE installed
4
$ bash scripts/check-fleet-jobs.sh   # … and the gate passes
check-fleet-jobs: OK …
rc=0
```

`scripts/check-fleet-jobs.sh` proves the manifest drives a **reconciler** and heals drift in a **scratch** crontab; it never asserts the real crontab, and it *affirmatively requires* that the board-refresh rung stay ship-gated OFF (`SNAPSHOT-REFRESH-SHIP-GATED-OFF`, `check-fleet-jobs.sh`). So the gate proves the *reconciler*, not the *installation* — and, more exactly, **nothing connects the entry point's freshness requirement to any producer**:

* `governance/dispatch/snapshot.py` (`SNAPSHOT_STALENESS_MINUTES = 15`, declared once in `governance/policy/lease.py`) is a **liveness** tolerance for a consumer that refreshes in-band;
* the loop *does* refresh in-band (`fleet/terminal.py:2027` → `board.refresh_or_park`, the #727 trigger contract);
* but the four CLI verbs that *are* the entry point (`status`, `eligible`, `claim`, `dispatch`) merely **refuse** and print "refresh first" — they never invoke the one refresh seam the refusal names.

Result: the entry point is `CANNOT-ASSESS` essentially always for anyone not already inside the loop — in one session three lanes got three different refusals for legitimate work: `out-of-epic-pooled`, `unknown-issue`, `snapshot age 195.0m (threshold 15m)`.

## The three defects

### 1. The liveness requirement has no producer the entry point can rely on
There are exactly two candidate producers and neither is connected:
* the `snapshot-refresh` cron rung — declared `"enabled": false` in `config/fleet-jobs.json` (ship-gated OFF, `fleet/cron.py`), so it is *guaranteed* absent, and `scripts/check-fleet-jobs.sh` asserts that;
* the in-band refresh in `governance/dispatch/snapshot.py:refresh` / `refresh_or_park` — reachable only from `dispatch snapshot --from-github` and the fleet loop, never from the verbs that refuse.

**Fix:** the entry point performs the SAME one bounded refresh, then re-measures; `--no-refresh` keeps a hermetic caller honest; the refusal (when the refresh does not clear it) names *both* the attempt and the refresher's installation state. Do **not** widen the 15-minute threshold — that would convert a dead control into a lying one. The committed `.board/snapshot.json`'s 72h offline tolerance (`governance/ticket/freshness.py`, #1077) is a *projection* tolerance and stays different on purpose.

### 2. `epic-closed` is a silent dead-end
`REASON_EPIC_CLOSED` (`governance/dispatch/model.py:60`) refuses an issue declaring `Parent:` to a closed epic. Measured on the live board: **7 open issues** are in exactly that state — **#132, #133, #803, #877, #935, #936, #946**. Nothing surfaces them: they are invisible *and* permanently unclaimable.

**Fix:** report them as a **named finding** with its remediation, and make the remedy reachable (a documented re-parenting path: re-point `Parent:` at the open successor, or close the issue). The refusal itself **stays** — the epic that would own the work is gone, so silently re-allowing it would trade a dead-end for a lie.

### 3. `frontier()` and `claim` disagree — #1168
`frontier()` (`governance/dispatch/order.py`) applies a *weaker* predicate than `eligible()`: it never applies the epic-closed refusal, so `status` advertises work `claim` refuses (measured: `status` named `#132`). Whatever predicate `eligible()` applies before the frontier branch, `frontier()` must apply too.

**Fix:** extract the pre-frontier refusals into one shared helper used by **both**, and add a control that *provokes the disagreement* rather than asserting the happy path. Closes #1168.

## Definition of done
* `dispatch status` reaches a verdict from a clean checkout on an ordinary day (and, when the refresh cannot clear staleness, refuses with a named reason and a named remedy — never a bare age);
* a dangling-on-closed-epic issue is reported by name with its remediation;
* `status`/`frontier` and `claim`/`eligible` cannot disagree, proved by a provoked control;
* every new/ repaired check is **provoked to fail**: rc and the literal refusal string asserted, plus the negative controls (clean tree → rc 0; unreadable input → **rc 2 CANNOT-ASSESS, never 0**);
* tri-state everywhere: 0 OK / 1 NOT-OK / 2 CANNOT-ASSESS;
* tests extend `governance/dispatch/tests/` (declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`).

items.title: Lessons ledger -> board: make every record's linkage real, and provable on real data
items.body:
# Lessons ledger → board: make every record's linkage real, and provable on real data

**Goal (done = this).** The lessons ledger stops being an island: every
incident / RCA / lesson / suggestion is reachable from the board (ledger → issue
→ epic), and the rule that enforces that linkage is *provable able to fail on
real data*, not only against its own mutants.

## Measured today (pristine `origin/master`, ledger + committed snapshot)

`governance/lessons/linkage.py` (landed by this issue) maps all **75** records:

| measure | count |
|---|---|
| records that reach a board issue | 34 |
| records that reach an issue *and* an epic/milestone | 26 |
| **orphans** — no path to any board issue | 41 |
| dangling `issue`-kind `origin.ref`s | 0 |
| `LESSON-*`/`SUGGEST-*` with **no `origin` at all** | 20 |

The board rule the module already ships (`board-incident-without-rca`) keys on
the `incident` **record** label. `cli.py check` measures **1** issue carrying it
(#1029, whose `INC-0007` names it) — while `cli.py status` prints **0**, because
`status` calls `check_ledger(..., snapshot=None)` and so can never count a
holder at all. The direction the ontology needs — **ledger → issue → epic** —
does not exist: a record's only way onto the board is the label rule, which is
enforced over a 1-holder set and cannot see the 41 orphans.

## Direction of the fix

1. **The label lands.** Every issue the ledger names as an `INC-*` origin must
   carry the `incident` record label, and a rule enforces it both ways
   (`board-incident-without-rca` already refuses the label *without* a record;
   the new rule refuses the record *without* the label). The scope becomes the
   ledger's own holder set, which is non-empty by construction.
2. **`LESSON-*`/`SUGGEST-*` must declare.** A lesson or suggestion is either
   board-reachable or explicitly declares itself orphaned (with a reason);
   **silence is the defect**. No `board.exemptions`\-style list: the declaration
   is checked against the reachability computation, so a false declaration is
   refused too.
3. **Dangling refs are real findings.** `origin` of kind `issue` was validated
   for RCAs only; the rule is broadened to every record kind (an incident whose
   origin no longer exists cannot be traced).
4. **Reachability is reported**, as deviations with remediation, so the
   historical backlog is visible and countable rather than invisible.

## Deliverables

- `governance/lessons/linkage.py` — the offline linkage map (ledger +
  `.board/snapshot.json` + `governance/ticket/` cross-check; no network).
- New finding codes in `model.py` + rules in `checker.py`, with the new phase
  wired through the existing `scripts/check-lessons.sh` entry.
- Provoked negative controls in `negative_control.py`: a plant per rule, a
  mutant per refusal, and a **real-data** provocation (a real record with its
  orphan declaration removed; a real labelled issue with the label removed) —
  each asserting rc **and the literal refusal string**; clean tree rc 0;
  unreadable input rc **2 CANNOT-ASSESS**, never 0.
- An honest disclosure of the filings this lane declines, with exact counts.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-lessons.sh                 # rc 0 (part 1 rules + part 2 provoked control)
python3 governance/lessons/cli.py linkage     # the linkage map
python3 governance/lessons/cli.py status      # board-label count, measured
```

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1178

items.title: check-paperclip-routines is CANNOT-ASSESS on master (rc 2) and is skipped by the composite: ao-fleet-reap is scheduled but no routine claims it
items.body:
Parent: #1268

## What is wrong

`scripts/check-paperclip-routines.sh` **cannot assess on `origin/master`**: it returns
**rc 2 (CANNOT-ASSESS)** and, because it cannot assess, the composite gate of record lists it under
the **2 skipped** checks. So it contributes no signal at all — and per the repo's own doctrine
*"a gate that cannot fail is a formality"*, a check that is permanently skipped is not a gate.

Two independent defects are visible in one run:

1. **A real drift it *does* detect** — `schedule-unprojected: ao-fleet-reap` — *"the code schedules
   this marker but no routine claims it — the schedule drifted without a routine change"*.
   This is the **inverse of #830** (closed): #830 scheduled nothing for the shipped reaper; the
   reaper is now scheduled (`ao-fleet-reap`) but no routine claims the marker.
2. **Its own negative control is inert** — the check ends with
   `check-paperclip-routines: CANNOT-ASSESS — could not build the dropped-entry tree`,
   and its control `mutation 'drop-prune' changed nothing — the source string moved`.
   A negative control that cannot build its mutant proves nothing, and it is *why* the check
   degrades to CANNOT-ASSESS instead of giving a verdict.

## Reproduced (bisect — it is not attributable to any recent lane)

On pristine detached worktrees, `bash scripts/check-paperclip-routines.sh`:

```
62be903  (fix(isolation): record 0aa836c as legacy … (#1173))        rc=2
4c9db94  (docs(pmo): board metadata conformance pass (#1165))        rc=2
```

rc 2 at **both** commits, and the diffs between them are docs + `.board/snapshot.json` only
(the snapshot moved 580 → 603 issues and the verdict did not change). The `ao-fleet-reap` drift and
the inert `drop-prune` control both **predate** both commits. It was measured while landing #1165 and
#1166, neither of which touches a schedule, a routine, or a check.

## Why it matters beyond the drift

`verify: PASS (170 of 172 checks, 2 skipped: dispatch-queue, paperclip-routines)` is a **true**
statement whose green hides this: one of the two skipped checks is not skipped by design, it is
skipped because it *cannot reach a verdict*. `RC 2 is never a pass` is already a declared rule here;
the composite should say so rather than fold it into "skipped".

## Suggested remedy (not prescriptive)

- Give `ao-fleet-reap` a claiming routine, or record the intentional schedule change.
- Repair the `drop-prune` mutant so the control can build its tree (it is the reason the check
  cannot assess).
- Decide, explicitly, whether a permanently-CANNOT-ASSESS check belongs in the composite's
  `skipped` bucket or should redden it — silence is the current answer and it is the wrong one.

## Evidence

- `verify: PASS (170 of 172 checks, 2 skipped: dispatch-queue, paperclip-routines)` — PR #1166's gate.
- `check-paperclip-routines: CANNOT-ASSESS — could not build the dropped-entry tree` (rc 2), twice, at
  `62be903` and `4c9db94`.
- `FAIL  schedule-unprojected: ao-fleet-reap` at both commits.
- Mirror-image prior art: closed **#830** (the reaper was scheduled nowhere).

items.title: e2e tagging: one declared tag authority, tag -> gate derivation, and a gate that can fail
items.body:
**Role (executor):** subagent
**Epic:** none — chain head
**Pillar:** autonomous-ops
**Lane:** governance-tagging
**Model tier (FinOps):** pro
**Thinking effort:** medium

## GOAL

Ship an end-to-end **tag authority** for this repo: one declared, closed tag
vocabulary that every governed artifact (issue, PR, branch, commit, surface,
release) is classified against, the **derivation** from a tag set to the gates
that tag set requires, and a **gate that can genuinely fail** when a tag is
unknown, ambiguous or has drifted from the authority it borrows from.

## Constraints (non-negotiable)

- **Borrow, never re-declare.** The `class` ladder, the FinOps tier set, the
  fleet role set and the `type/priority/area/pillar/phase/source/epic` label
  vocabulary already have authorities in this repo. The tag taxonomy must
  *reference* them and a gate must prove the two cannot drift apart — not mint a
  second, quietly-authoritative copy (the failure mode ADR-0012 names and
  `governance/vocabulary/fleet.yaml` exists to prevent).
- **No false green.** The gate is tri-state (0 OK / 1 NOT-OK / 2 CANNOT-ASSESS),
  `CANNOT-ASSESS` is never a pass, and it runs a self-mutating negative control:
  a mutated taxonomy must be refused *by name*, or the gate reports FAIL.
- **Declare no rung above measured evidence.** The surface is declared in
  `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml` at the rung its own tree measures.
- No secrets; no ad-hoc `terraform apply`; no direct push to `master`.

## Context (measured 2026-09-17)

| Authority today | What it closes | What is still open |
|---|---|---|
| `governance/conformance/policy.yaml` | the `class` ladder + required/expectation labels on the **board** | no `posture`, no SDLC stage, no tag→gate derivation |
| `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml` | per-**surface** declared class | same gap |
| `governance/finops/policy.json` | FinOps tier vocabulary + role allowlist | not addressable as a *tag* on an issue/PR |
| `governance/vocabulary/fleet.yaml` | fleet role vocabulary | not a tag dimension |
| `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml` | form shape | the label *vocabulary* is implicit |

So classification exists in **five** places, and nothing derives **which gates a
given piece of work must pass** from how it is tagged. That derivation is the
end-to-end gap.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `governance/tagging/taxonomy.yaml` declares every dimension with a closed
      vocabulary, its owner, and — for every borrowed dimension — the path of the
      authority it is borrowed from. (checked: `python3 governance/tagging/cli.py lint`)
- [ ] `governance/tagging/rules.yaml` derives a **gate plan** from a tag set,
      covering CI/CD, the PR contract, the SDLC stage and the FinOps floor.
      (checked: `python3 governance/tagging/cli.py plan --tag posture:iac`)
- [ ] No drift: every borrowed vocabulary equals its authority exactly.
      (checked: `python3 governance/tagging/cli.py lint` reports `drift=0`)
- [ ] `scripts/check-tagging.sh` is tri-state and refuses a mutated taxonomy by
      name (negative control), reporting FAIL if the mutant passes.
      (checked: `bash scripts/check-tagging.sh`; `make tagging`)
- [ ] The tag→gate matrix is generated, not hand-written, and committed to
      `docs/TAGGING.md`. (checked: `python3 governance/tagging/cli.py matrix --check`)
- [ ] The surface is declared in `surfaces.yaml` at its **measured** rung and
      carries a row in `docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md`. (checked: `make surface-class`)
- [ ] `make verify` is green. (checked: `make verify`)

## Verify command

```bash
bash scripts/check-tagging.sh && make tagging && make surface-class && make verify
```

## Chain markers

Parent: none
Part-of: none
Blocked-by: none
Root: none

## Evidence

_To be filled with the literal command output when the lane lands._

items.title: bootstrap .fleet/master-attestation.json once the box gate cap frees (follow-up to #1114/#1119/#1136)
items.body:
Refs #1114, #1119, #1136

## Problem

Since #1119 merged (`1318550`), `fleet/brain.py dispatch()` refuses non-exempt dispatch unless `.fleet/master-attestation.json` exists and names a head-fresh green verify. The file has never been written on this host: two writers exist (`governance/landing/engine.py land()` on a fleet-driven merge; `make master-attestation` for a manual merge), but no green `make verify` at `origin/master` head has completed yet to seed either path.

## Measured 2026-09-17

Three bootstrap attempts this session, all against a scratch detached worktree at `origin/master`:
- 12:07–12:26 (head `9e5a615`→`d3eb77f`): real reds (docs-lint, gate-coverage, dispatch-reconcile, pytest-fleet, gitignore, isolation-landed, verdict-contains, ungated-sync-suites) — fixed by PR #1144 and #1150.
- 12:07–14:14 (head `2fa292c`, unmoved for 2h): the box-wide gate-lock cap (4 concurrent holders) stayed saturated the entire window under heavy fleet-lane traffic (`ao-1146`…`ao-1158` and others rotating). `make verify` PARKED (rc 11) repeatedly, and even when it did acquire a slot and ran deep into the check list (past e2e, shell-syntax, python-syntax, erp-finops), it never reached a final verdict before losing its slot or the session stopping it. No real check failure was observed in this window — only cap contention.

## Acceptance

- A green `make verify` completes at `origin/master` head on some checkout.
- `make master-attestation` (or the engine's own writer on the next fleet-driven merge) produces `.fleet/master-attestation.json` naming that head.
- `fleet/brain.py`'s `master_health_refusal` admits a non-exempt dispatch afterward (spot-check one dispatch or its test).
- If the box-wide gate cap is the recurring blocker (not a real check failure), consider raising the cap or giving a bootstrap/master-only run priority — file that as a separate infra question if it recurs, don't silently raise the cap here.

## Non-goals

Not a re-litigation of #1119's design; not a general gate-cap-capacity project unless the recurrence data says so.

items.title: master red (recurrence): check-isolation-landed refuses origin/master again — 0aa836c (#1171) landed direct with no trailer, 3 min after #1169 cleared the previous one
items.body:
## Measured

`scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` was **green on `origin/master` for three
minutes** — from `465fb27` (#1169, 2026-09-17T17:41:56Z) until the next commit
landed — and is **red again**:

```
$ git log --oneline -3 origin/master
465fb27 fix(isolation): record origin/master's tip 2fa292c as legacy, unblocking the board (#1154) (#1169)
0aa836c fix(cloudbuild): 2nd-gen repositoryEventConfig for control-plane triggers (#1171)
2fa292c fix(verify): clear remaining master reds ... (#1150)

$ bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh     # pristine detached worktree at origin/master
          FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:0aa836c19bfd is not recorded legacy — ...
        isolation-enforce: NOT-OK — 1 unrecorded and 0 stale baseline entr(ies) in HEAD
check-isolation-landed: FAIL (1 violation(s))          # rc=1
```

`0aa836c` (the squash-merge of #1171) carries **no** trailing trailer paragraph;
its message ends with the `## Test plan` section. It was merged by the owner
(`merged_by: kushin77`, `2026-09-17T17:38:25Z`) — a **direct** merge, so
`scripts/pr-queue.sh` and its pre-merge guard (`scripts/check-squash-message.sh
--pr 1171`) never ran. `check-squash-message.sh --pr 1171` refuses it by name.

#1171's own PR body states it merged with `check-isolation-landed` **already
failing** ("*7/172 pre-existing failures (check-control-audit, erp-module,
check-isolation-landed, check-portal-auth-env), all unrelated to this diff*") —
i.e. the red was known, declared pre-existing, and merged over. That is the
mechanism by which one trailer-less merge keeps every open PR's `make verify`
red until a baseline-entry PR unblocks it.

## Immediate unblock (this issue)

Record `0aa836c` in `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` — legitimate, as
proven above (the check refuses a *stale* quarantine entry by name). This is the
third recorded recurrence of the same class (#960/#976 → #996/#991 → #1150 →
#1171); recording it is the terminal state, **not** a prevention.

## Durable half (filed to #1145)

The composition surfaces are intact (PR template's final paragraph is the
trailer; the landing driver composes one; `repo-settings.yaml` declares
`squash_merge_commit_message: PR_BODY`). The gap is **enforcement on the
non-queue merge path** — nothing mechanical refuses a direct `gh pr merge
--squash` whose composed message drops the trailer. Filed with the measured
evidence to #1145 (the merge-path lane).

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1154

items.title: gate-lock: 160 zero-byte leftover worktree locks accumulate; doctor sits permanently at rc 13 and no safe prune verb exists
items.body:
## Measured

`scripts/gate-lock.sh` (issue #724, AO-GR-22) keeps two stores under
`${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/agent-orchestrator-gates`:

```
worktrees/   total=162  zero-byte=160  non-zero=2      # per-worktree locks
permits/     total=4    held=2                          # the box-wide cap
```

`bash scripts/gate-lock.sh status` (and `doctor`) report **160** entries as
`LEFTOVER (0-byte owner-less lock file)`; `doctor` exits **rc 13
(HEALTH-ATTENTION)**. They accumulated over days and grew again while this was
measured (161 → 162 worktrees/).

## Verdict 1 — they do NOT consume permits (measured, not assumed)

`permits in use: N of 4` is computed from `permit_paths(base)` **only** — i.e.
`permits/slot-*.lock`, never `worktrees/*.lock` (`fleet/gatelock.py`
`_live_permits`/`status`, the loop at l.1013). At the instant of measurement
`status` printed `permits in use: 2 of 4` with **160** leftovers present, so the
leftovers are cosmetic: they pollute `status`/`doctor` output and hold
`doctor` at rc 13, but they do **not** reduce the effective concurrency cap.

## Verdict 2 — there is no prune verb, and that is deliberate (not a defect)

`gate-lock.sh` exposes `acquire|release|status|doctor`. `doctor` is
**alert-only by design** — its docstring states a box-wide sweep reaping a lock
for a worktree it does not own is the "delete every file" risk class that #948
forbids; auto-heal stays on the one path already proven safe (a worktree's own
`release`, which reaps a lock it proves free while holding the flock). So
`gate-lock.sh` lacking a prune verb is intentional, not an oversight.

## The residual gap worth a decision

A **safe** prune is possible but unimplemented: a leftover is provably dead when
(B) its recorded `owner_pid` is gone **and** (C) its recorded `worktree` path no
longer exists. A `doctor --reap` that requires **both** (never either, never a
bare filename glob) would shrink the 160 with no risk of the #948 regression.
Until then the accumulation is unbounded and `doctor` cannot distinguish "one
fresh leftover from a kill that just happened" from "160 historical ones", so
its rc-13 signal is permanently red and therefore carries no information.

## Proposed acceptance criteria

`doctor --reap` (or a `prune` verb) removes a leftover **only** when the owner
pid is dead **and** the worktree path is absent, re-checks both under the flock
immediately before unlinking, and a gate proves it: (a) a leftover with a live
pid is refused, (b) one whose worktree still exists is refused, (c) one with a
dead pid and an absent worktree is removed, (d) the mutation is driven for real
(a fixture store), so the check cannot pass vacuously (GR-12).

items.title: governance/dupcheck/check-duplicates.sh implements the ADR-0010 no-fork rule and is invoked by no gate — the rule is advisory
items.body:
## What

`governance/dupcheck/check-duplicates.sh` implements the **ADR-0010** rule that this repo *consumes
but must never fork* the canonical fleet docs (`MODEL-PROFILES.md` / `SME-PROFILES.md` /
`SOLUTION-CLASSES.md`, the identity schema set, and the `dprs` tree). Its own README says:

> *"This helper makes that rule mechanical and can re-verify the documented byte-identical dprs =
> git-rca-workspace duplicate."*

But the helper is **invoked by no gate**: not `scripts/verify.sh`, not the `Makefile`, not
`gate.sh`/`merge-gate.sh`, and not any `scripts/check-*.sh`. Because it lives *inside* a package
(`governance/dupcheck/`) rather than in `scripts/`, it is also invisible to
`scripts/discover-checks.sh`, whose glob is `scripts/check-*.sh` — so
`scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh` does not even see it as "an unwired script".

Net effect: an ADR-enforcement capability ships and is never run, so the no-fork rule is advisory.

## Measured

```
$ grep -rn 'dupcheck\|check-duplicates' scripts/ Makefile governance/ --include='*.sh' --include='*.py'
(only governance/dupcheck/check-duplicates.sh itself)

$ grep -rn 'dupcheck' scripts/verify.sh scripts/gate.sh scripts/merge-gate.sh Makefile
(empty)

$ head -1 governance/dupcheck/check-duplicates.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
$ bash governance/dupcheck/check-duplicates.sh scan; echo "rc=$?"
(rc per the documented tri-state: 0 PASS / 1 FAIL / 2 usage)
```

- `governance/dupcheck/README.md:1` — the rule and the canonical homes
- `governance/dupcheck/check-duplicates.sh` — the detector (3 subcommands: `scan`, `compare`, `demo-cases`)
- `docs/decision-records/ADR-0010-canonical-copy-ownership.md` — the ADR the detector enforces
- `scripts/discover-checks.sh` — the auto-wiring glob (`scripts/check-*.sh`) that does not reach it

## Remedy

Wire the detector into the gate of record, so the rule is binding:

1. move it to `scripts/check-duplicates.sh` (auto-discovered by #698), **or** name it from an
   existing check / `scripts/verify.sh` entry with a comment saying why it is not in `scripts/`;
2. make it able to fail: provoke a planted same-named protected doc in a scratch tree and require
   rc 1 naming the fork, with a clean tree refused nothing;
3. keep `demo-cases` network-free (it reads `.research/` clones) or mark it an explicit,
   documented opt-in.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-duplicates.sh scan                 # rc 0 on the clean tree
bash scripts/check-duplicates.sh scan --root <scratch> # rc 1, naming the planted fork
bash scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh                   # rc 0: not baselined, not stale
make verify
```

items.title: this repo's own module.json is never validated against cmr.module/v1, though the admission contract requires it of every child
items.body:
## What

`docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md:88` requires that a sub-module *"publishes its own `module.json` at the
child repo root, **valid against `cmr.module/v1`**"*. This repository's **own** root `module.json`
is never validated against that schema: every check here only *reads fields* out of it
(`os_apps`, `submodules[]`, feature flags). A malformed or schema-invalid root manifest — a wrong
`schema`, a mistyped `os_apps` key, a `submodules[]` entry missing a required field — would pass
every gate.

That makes the root manifest the one artifact in the app-model path with **no** binding check.

## Measured

```
$ grep -rn 'cmr.module/v1' scripts/ docs/ governance/
scripts/check-gateway-catalog-parity.sh:214   # a fixture string
scripts/check-module-registry.sh:392,701      # fixtures for OTHER manifests
docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md:30,88                # the requirement
governance/conformance/tests/test_surface_ceiling.py   # reads only MODULE_CLASS_KEY

$ grep -ln 'module.json' scripts/check-*.sh
check-gateway-catalog-parity.sh  check-hermes-integration.sh  check-module-admission.sh
check-module-brief.sh  check-module-registry.sh  check-monitoring-declaration.sh
check-sme-routing.sh  check-system-app-declaration.sh
# ... every one of them reads fields; none validates the root manifest against the schema.
```

- `module.json:2` — `"schema": "cmr.module/v1"` (a declaration with no validator)
- `docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md:219` — the manifest is the machine-readable half of the contract

1. validate the root `module.json` against the pinned

3. confirm the check is auto-discovered into `make verify` (#698) and not baselined.

```bash

bash scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh            # rc 0: the new check is wired, not baselined
```

`control-plane/cockpit/cockpit/` — the terminal cockpit **client** (AgentConsole) — is shipped,
runnable (`make cockpit` → `python3 control-plane/cockpit/cockpit/__main__.py --once`), documented
(`control-plane/cockpit/README.md`), and **gated by nothing**:

- its suite is **not** declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`, so `scripts/check-ungated-suites.sh`

- the one check that touches the cockpit *frame* (`scripts/check-control-functions.sh`) renders
  `fleet/console.py`'s sections — it does not exercise the client in `control-plane/cockpit/`.

So the operator client is IMPLEMENTED-UNGATED: code exists that no check exercises, in the exact
path this analysis covers.

## Measured

```
$ ls scripts/check-cockpit.sh
ls: cannot access 'scripts/check-cockpit.sh': No such file or directory

$ grep -rn 'control-plane/cockpit' scripts/check-*.sh Makefile
Makefile:690:	@python3 control-plane/cockpit/cockpit/__main__.py --once

$ grep -n 'control-plane/cockpit' scripts/pytest-suites.txt
(no match — the suite is undeclared)
```

- `Makefile:690` — `cockpit:` runs the client
- `scripts/check-control-functions.sh` — binds the *registry* + `fleet/console.py` frame, not the client

Land the missing gate and declare the suite, one lane:

1. register `control-plane/cockpit` in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`;
2. add `scripts/check-cockpit.sh` that drives the client headlessly (like
   `check-control-functions.sh` does for the frame), refuses a client that cannot render the
   declared function set, and provokes its own refusal;
3. name the suite as a pytest target from that check (the documented escape hatch), so
   `check-ungated-suites.sh` reads it WIRED.

items.title: check-system-app-declaration.sh observes category:"system" only in .json/.yaml/.yml, so its "the tree matches the claim" line cannot see a .ts declaration
items.body:
## What

`scripts/check-system-app-declaration.sh` (issue #945) claims the tree matches this repo's declared
OS-app exemption — *"no `addons/`, no `apps/`, and no `category: \"system\"` app outside `vendor/`"*.
Its tree scan only reads files ending `.json`, `.yaml`, or `.yml`, so a `category: "system"` app
declared in **any other file type** is invisible to it while the gate prints `OK the tree matches
the claim`.

That is not hypothetical: the app model this repo's exemption names is owned by
`kushin77/shared-frontend`, whose native-addon registration lives in **`shell/src/addons.ts`** — a
`.ts` file (`docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md:219`). If this repo ever grew an app, the most likely shape is
exactly the one the detector cannot see.

## Measured

Same declaration, two extensions, run against a scratch root that carries the real inputs:

```
# plant the shared-frontend shape as a .ts file
$ cat /tmp/aosysapp-prov5/root/addon-registry.ts
export const app = { id: "sys-monitor", category: "system" };
$ bash scripts/check-system-app-declaration.sh --no-controls --root /tmp/aosysapp-prov5/root
  OK    the tree matches the claim: no addons/, no apps/, no category: "system" app outside vendor/
check-system-app-declaration: OK — ...                                    ts_plant_rc=0

# control: the SAME declaration in a .yaml file
$ bash scripts/check-system-app-declaration.sh --no-controls --root /tmp/aosysapp-prov5/root
  FAIL  an OS app is declared (category: "system") at addon-registry.yaml:2, so this repo now hosts OS apps — the exemption no longer holds
yaml_plant_rc=1
```

- `scripts/check-system-app-declaration.sh:157` — `if not name.endswith((".json", ".yaml", ".yml")):`
- `scripts/check-system-app-declaration.sh:115-116` — the two regexes (`JSON_SYSTEM_APP`, `YAML_SYSTEM_APP`)
- `docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md:206` — the claim the scan is supposed to keep true
- `docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md:233` — the reader-facing re-derive command is JSON-only, narrower still

## Remedy

Widen the observation and make the claim match it:

1. scan a declared extension allowlist (or all text files) for the `category: "system"` shape —
   including `.ts`/`.js`/`.mjs`/`.toml`/`.jsonc` — so the detector can observe the declaration
   shape the app model's owner uses;
2. or narrow the claim in `docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md` §9 to the file types actually observed, and
   say so, so the `OK` line is not read as broader than it is;
3. add an external provocation plant for a non-JSON/YAML file to the check's own control set, so
   the breadth cannot silently regress.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-system-app-declaration.sh                 # still rc 0 on the clean tree
# with the fix, a planted .ts declaration must be refused, by name:
bash scripts/check-system-app-declaration.sh --no-controls --root <scratch-root>   # rc 1, naming it
```

items.title: the filing default derives area:governance, which does not exist — every defaulted filing is refused by GitHub while filing-check stays green

## What

`governance/conformance/policy.yaml` declares `filing.defaults.area: governance`, so every filing
that does not override `area` derives the label **`area:governance`** — which **does not exist on
this repository**. GitHub refuses the create, so the *default* filing path is broken end to end,
while the gate that owns the seam (`scripts/check-conformance.sh` → `filing-check`) reports green
because it proves label *derivation* and never label *existence*.

This was measured while filing the tracker for the system-app/app-model/governance E2E gap
analysis: the first filing attempt was refused by GitHub, and had to override `area` to an
existing label to succeed.

## Measured

```
$ python3 governance/conformance/cli.py file --title ... --body ... --class enterprise \
    --declare type=task --declare priority=P1 --declare area=governance --declare pillar=governance
RuntimeError: gh issue create failed: could not add label: 'area:governance' not found
rc=1

$ gh label list --repo kushin77/agent-orchestrator | grep -i '^area'
area:knowledge-index  area:standards  area:incident-response  area:remediation  area:board
area:lessons  area:agent-profiles  area:cto-overlay  area:fleet  area:session-fleet
area:enterprise-workbook  area:erp-module            # no area:governance

$ bash scripts/check-conformance.sh
filing-check: OK (13 of 13 expectations held)         # green while production filing is refused
```

- `governance/conformance/policy.yaml:84` — `area: governance`
- `governance/conformance/filing.py:161` — `derive_declaring_labels`
- `scripts/check-conformance.sh:52` — runs `filing-check`

## Remedy

Make the derived default resolvable, and make the gate able to observe it:

1. point `filing.defaults.area` at an existing label (or create `area:governance` deliberately,
   which is a PMO/label-set decision, not a lane's), and
2. add a `filing-check` expectation that a filing's derived label set is **resolvable against a
   declared label inventory** (recorded offline, like the `.board/snapshot.json` pattern), so a
   policy default naming a label that does not exist is REFUSED by the gate rather than by GitHub.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-conformance.sh                       # must still be green
python3 governance/conformance/cli.py file --title probe --body probe --dry-run \
  --class enterprise | grep -o 'area:[a-z-]*'           # the derived default must be an existing label
```

items.title: fix(fleet): the reaper's "in use" test cannot see a peer session's live worktree — 10 live trees classified removable
items.body:
## Observed (measured 2026-09-17, `master` `2fa292c`, `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` as landed by PR #1118)

The worktree reaper's **fail-closed "in use" test cannot see a peer using a worktree from the shared shell**, so
it classifies live harness worktrees as removable.

Measured during the #830 lane, on the real tree, with the rung's own command (`python3 fleet/cron.py reap`, dry):

```
prune-worktrees: 17 stale, 127 kept
```

Of the 17 "stale", **10 were `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` trees plus 4 scratch trees whose working directories had
been written to 5–31 minutes earlier** (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache/v/cache/nodeids`, mtimes 10:03–10:10Z).
They carry **no `.fleet/lanes/` record** (the Claude harness creates them), so "claimed by an open lane" does not
apply, and "HEAD preserved on `origin`" calls them removable — their **HEADs were preserved** (no commits at
risk), but their **working directories were live**. The predicate is `/proc/*/cwd`, which a peer session driving a
worktree from the shared shell does not appear in.

`--apply` was therefore **not** run against the real tree; the destructive half was proven on a controlled fixture
with the exact installed command text. Every sibling lane named in the dispatch was correctly **KEEP**
(`ao-714-d9219ff0`, `ao-977-2637b9e5`, `ao-978-b4a9af3d`, and the peer `ao-830-2aa73638`).

## Why it matters

The nightly `ao-fleet-reap` line now runs `prune-worktrees.sh --apply` unattended (installed 2026-09-17,
`fleet/cron.py install`). A tree that a live peer session is mid-run in is exactly the state that loses work in a
way no re-run can recover, and the guard that is supposed to prevent it is invisible to the shared-shell pattern
this fleet actually uses.

## Bounded remedy (one of)

1. **Make liveness visible**: treat a worktree as in use when any process's **cwd or any open file** is under it
   (`/proc/*/cwd` **and** `/proc/*/fd/*`), not cwd alone — cheap, and it closes the measured gap.
2. **Refuse unnamed-worktree reaping**: the trees that were misclassified are all outside the lane registry
   (`.claude/worktrees/**`, scratch roots). Require a `.fleet/lanes/` record, or an explicit allowlist, before
   removing a tree the reaper did not create.

## Acceptance / negative control

- A worktree whose **only** liveness evidence is an open file descriptor (or a long-lived process with its cwd
  elsewhere) is **KEEP**, proving the widened predicate — not merely that cwd is checked.
- A genuinely stale, preserved, unclaimed tree is still reaped.
- The mutant that reverts the predicate to cwd-only **REDs** `scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh`.

## Verify

```
python3 fleet/cron.py reap            # dry: 0 live trees classified stale
bash scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh
make verify
```

Refs #830 #516 #207. Related: #736 (fail-open controls), AO-GR-21/22.

items.title: P1: infra/fleet/dev_run.py writes the whole process environment — including live API keys — into .verify/dev-run/decision.json
items.body:
## Defect — the dev-run decision document is an environment dump

`infra/fleet/dev_run.py` writes its decision document with a top-level `env` key holding
**the entire process environment** (`dict(os.environ)`), into
`.verify/dev-run/decision.json` **inside the checkout**. On this box that is the operator's
live shell environment.

Measured 2026-09-17 while running the harness exactly as the container runs it
(`python3 infra/fleet/dev_run.py --once`, dry-run; the file it wrote is 9832 bytes). Key
names only — every value is redacted here and was never reproduced anywhere public:

```
top-level keys: ['dry_run', 'env', 'epic', 'findings', 'finished_at', 'issue', 'jobs',
                 'probes', 'reason', 'schedule', 'schema', 'started_at', 'state', 'stop', 'verdict']
--- env ---
  env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY              = <redacted — a live key, flagged by check-secrets>
  env.DEEPSEEK_MAX_TOKENS           = <redacted>
  env.GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS = /home/akushnir/.config/gcloud/sa-key.json
  env.GITHUB_…                      = …
  env.COPILOT_DEBUG_NONCE           = <redacted>
  env.AO_FLEET_DIR                  = /tmp/…/fleet
  … (~90 more, including DISPLAY, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, SSH_… paths)
```

### Why it is a defect and not just untidy

1. **A live credential now exists in a plain file inside a working checkout.** The only thing
   standing between it and a commit is `.gitignore:39` (`.verify/`). GR-6 says secrets live in
   env/secret manager and never in a file or in history; the mitigation here is an ignore
   rule, which is a convention, not a control.
2. **It reds the gate of record for any tree where the harness has run.** Measured in this
   worktree: `bash scripts/check-secrets.sh` → `FAIL ./.verify/dev-run/decision.json:23:
   "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY": "…" (possible secret: high-signal-shape)`, `secrets: 1 finding(s)`;
   after deleting the file, `secrets: OK (2800 file(s) scanned)`. So a lane that merely
   *exercises its own deliverable* goes red until it deletes the evidence.
3. **The document is handled as evidence by the gates, not only read in place.**
   `scripts/check-fleet-cron-dev-run.sh` `docker cp`s it out of the container, and
   `infra/fleet/healthz.py` re-reads it on every probe. A dump that travels as evidence is a
   dump that leaks wherever the evidence is pasted.
4. It contradicts the image's own contract: `infra/fleet/env_contract.py` is documented as
   **the ONE declaration of the image env** (`AO_FLEET_*`), and `entrypoint.sh`/`dev_run.py`
   validate against it — yet the decision document records ~90 variables nobody declared.

### Proposed shape (not implemented here)

Record the **declared** surface, not the ambient one: the `AO_FLEET_*` values the run is
governed by (read through `env_contract.py`, which already owns that list), plus the redacted
*presence* of anything else if it is genuinely wanted. Never `dict(os.environ)`.

### Provenance

Found while landing #1148 (the `/healthz` job-set drift) — the harness was run to measure
whether the read-only compose service can answer 200 (it can: `verdict: ok`, `state:
UNTOUCHED`, see #1148). The artifact was deleted from that lane when this was found; the lane
is clean and its secrets scan is green.

Parent: #706 (EPIC — port the fleet's cron automation into a shared-services container);
the harness is D2 (#710).

Not fixed in the finding lane (one issue = one lane = one branch): the change touches
`dev_run.py`'s document schema, which `infra/fleet/tests/`, `healthz.py`'s consumers and the
dev-run gate all read.

items.title: master red: check-isolation-landed — origin/master's own tip d3eb77f carries no trailer and is not recorded in governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json
items.body:
## Objective

Clear a master red that is present on a **pristine checkout** and owned by no open issue:
`scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` refuses real history in `origin/master` because a trailer-less
commit landed on master and is not recorded as legacy.

## Measurement (clean detached worktree at `origin/master`)

```
$ git worktree add --detach <pristine> origin/master && cd <pristine>
$ git rev-parse HEAD
d3eb77fa0cb19f4043eeb3a7a1109a498287d752
$ bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh
          FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:d3eb77fa0cb1 is not recorded legacy — if the commit has not MERGED yet, put the reference in a trailing trailer paragraph
        isolation-enforce: NOT-OK — 1 unrecorded and 0 stale baseline entr(ies) in HEAD
  FAIL  the landed enforcement refused real history in HEAD
  ... 10 further halves OK ...
check-isolation-landed: FAIL (1 violation(s))
rc=1
```

`d3eb77f` is `origin/master`'s own tip (`fix(docs,gate): follow the #1042 test renames in READMEs;
drop stale gate-coverage baseline entries (#1144)`, merged 2026-09-17T15:34Z) and its message carries
**no trailing `Refs` block**. `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` does not name it, so the
baseline's grandfathering does not cover it.

The wider picture, from the landed-contract audit over the same history:

```
$ bash scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --landed --range origin/master
  FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:d3eb77fa0cb1
  FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:13185503a075
  FAIL  commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block:4986cb636344
  FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:94e23472a49e
  FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:ea730bee0495
  ... 24 findings in total ...
check-pr-contract: LANDED: FAIL (24 finding(s))
rc=1
```

23 of the 24 are already recorded legacy in the isolation baseline; exactly one — master's own tip —
is not. So the *new* defect is narrow: a merge landed on master without a trailer and without a
quarantine entry.

## Why it matters

This is a red on a **clean checkout of master**, so it is red for every lane's composite gate (the
`make verify` of record), independent of what that lane changed. Measured while landing #1147: the
same check is red on the lane and *identically* red on pristine master.

## Acceptance

1. `scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` is **green on a clean checkout of `origin/master`** —
   `bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh; echo "rc=$?"` → `rc=0`.
2. Take one route and **say which**, with the reason recorded where the rule lives:
   * **quarantine by name**: add `d3eb77f` to `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json`, so the
     offence is recorded legacy rather than silently tolerated (this is what the baseline is for); or
   * **fix the producer**: find why the merge message for `d3eb77f` carried no trailing `Refs` block
     and make the landing path compose one — the same path produced the other 23 recorded offenders,
     so the honest fix is at the producer, not only at the auditor.
   If the answer is that the *merger* dropped the trailer, say so and name the merge route.
3. The check still bites: provoke an unrecorded non-compliant commit and show the refusal by name
   (the check's own `--selftest`-equivalent halves already do this — quote the real run).
4. `make verify` PASS at the merged head.

## Verify

```bash
git worktree add --detach /tmp/redcheck-1148b origin/master && cd /tmp/redcheck-1148b
bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh; echo "rc=$?"
```

_AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW) — measured on a pristine detached worktree at
`origin/master` while landing #1147; the offender is master's own tip, not the lane's commit (the
lane's commit `9e99d43` carries its trailer)._

items.title: check-verdict-contains is red on master again — 3 piped-grep sites from #1118 (#1145)
items.body:
Parent: #1145

### What happened

`scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh` is **red on `origin/master`** and blocks every lane's
`make verify`. The regression is #1118 (`2df367d`, merged by the sanctioned queue): its merge brought
**three** sites that pipe into a quiet `grep`.

Measured on a clean detached worktree at `origin/master` (`d3eb77f`):

```
$ bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh ; echo rc=$?
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh has 2, the record allows 0
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/prune-worktrees.sh has 1, the record allows 0
check-verdict-contains: FAIL (2 finding(s); 9 control(s) passed)
rc=1
```

`git log origin/master -- scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh` names **only `2df367d`** (#1118), so this
is a regression introduced by that merge, not a site the record omits by accident.

### The three sites

| file:line | shape |
|---|---|
| `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh:350` | `printf '%s\n' "$checked_out" \| grep -qxF -- "$branch"` |
| `scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh:160` | `printf '%s' "$report" \| grep -q "STALE  branch issue-42-lane"` |
| `scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh:194` | `printf '%s' "$held_out" \| grep -q 'issue-44-lane'` |

A piped `grep -q` exits on its **first** match and SIGPIPEs its producer, so under `pipefail` the
pipeline is reported as failed for text that *is* present. That is a false verdict, not a style
preference. At `prune-worktrees.sh:350` the false direction is the dangerous one: the test asks
whether a branch a worktree **is** standing on, so a false answer reads that branch as free and lets
the sweep delete it.

### Remedy

The same bash-native containment conversion already made for `check-cmr-pin.sh`,
`check-fleet-vocabulary.sh`, `check-rbac-head-binding.sh` (#1035) and `check-agentconsole-hosting.sh`
(#1051): a line-anchored `while read` loop for the whole-line (`grep -qxF`) test, and
`[[ "$x" == *"$needle"* ]]` for the two substring tests. **No record edit** —
`scripts/verdict-contains-legacy.tsv` stays byte-unchanged; the record is shrink-only and the three
files are absent from it, so the sites are repaired at the source, which is the only thing that
clears the red.

Lane scope: `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` and `scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh` only. The other
deliverables in #1145 (`scripts/pr-queue.sh` defects, the queue's gate-regression seam, and the
`check-isolation-landed` red from #1144) are separate files and stay with #1145.

`Verify:` `bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh` → rc 0, and
`git status --porcelain -- scripts/verdict-contains-legacy.tsv` → empty.

Filed separately from #1145 because that issue carries four further deliverables in files this lane
must not touch, so it must not be closed by this repair.

items.title: lifecycle: a merged item's evidence subject must be the tree that landed, not the branch tip that advanced after the squash
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
## Measured defect — a merged item's evidence subject is the branch tip that advanced, not the tree that landed

`governance/lifecycle/closeout.py` takes the evidence subject from the **live** pull request:

```python
verified_commit = str(pr.get("head_commit") or "")
landing = str(pr.get("merge_commit") or "") if pr.get("state") == "merged" else ""
```

For a branch that received commits **after** the squash merge, that `head_commit` is a tree that **never
landed** and never gated. Measured on PR #984 (the squash merge that closed #977 and #978):

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| `pulls/984.head.sha` (live) | `e3f63457cac093ee90d98bd7ffa732e0809622cc` |
| `pulls/984.merge_commit_sha` | `fed4e7d433e424171201fa3155cf74d09eae2728` |
| `tree(e3f6345)` | `81c146b9967ecc0cffcd561990327202c7f80025` |
| `tree(fed4e7d)` | `05de08122b258fbdc59e5773771715d10f200dc2` |
| `git diff --quiet e3f6345 fed4e7d` | **rc 1** — 54 files changed, 4731 insertions(+), 31 deletions(-) |
| `git merge-base --is-ancestor e3f6345 fed4e7d` | **rc 1** — the live head is not an ancestor of the merge |
| `git merge-base --is-ancestor fed4e7d origin/master` | rc 0 |

`#1098`'s admissibility rule (`GhOps._admissible`: lane == verified commit, **or** merged and the lane
contains the landing **and** the landing carries the verified head's tree) therefore refuses #977 and
#978 for the *right* reason — `contains the landing ? True, landing tree == verified tree ? False` — and
both keep `REMAINS VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING`. The invariant is keyed to a tree nobody verified and which
never landed, so the item is structurally unclosable. PR #984's own checklist records
`make verify — PARKED on box contention after 6 attempts`: the live head `e3f6345` was never green, and
at that head the composite gate fails **19 of 145** checks.

Secondary (small, named in #1098's own report): `_admissible`'s refusal says *"is not the verified commit
X **and does not contain it**"* even when the lane **does** contain the landing and the true reason is
"contains it, but the landing's tree differs". #977/#978 deserve to diagnose themselves in one line.

## Remedy

**The subject of a merged item's evidence must be a commit whose tree is the tree that landed.** The
squash commit `merge_commit` carries the landed tree *by construction*, so it is the canonical subject
whenever the live head cannot be shown to carry that same tree.

Resolution, in `closeout.py`, once per item, using the repo the port already reads:

| live `head_commit` vs `merge_commit` | subject | why |
|---|---|---|
| trees **equal** (the ordinary correctly-merged item) | `head_commit` | unchanged — the landed tree **is** the head's tree, so the existing convention and every existing record stand; the `clean_item` fixture is untouched |
| trees **measured different** (the #977/#978 shape) | `merge_commit` | the live head's tree never landed; the landing carries the tree that did |
| trees **unreadable** | `head_commit` | unchanged behaviour; nothing new is *claimed*, and `_admissible`'s tree half still refuses any lane that would need the unread tree |

The drift is **disclosed, not hidden**: the attestation gains `drifted_head` (the live head whose tree
did not land) and the step detail says so in one line. `GhOps._admissible` and its tree half stay exactly
as #1098 built them — the fix is *which commit is asked about*, never *what is accepted about it*.

`audit.py` (offline, pure over the record) is widened in the same direction and no further: evidence
satisfies the invariant when it names the head commit, **or** names the landing as its subject **and**
records the live head it drifted from. A record that merely names the merge commit stays a finding
(`test_evidence_that_names_the_wrong_commit_is_a_finding`, unchanged).

## Alternatives evaluated, and why they lost

1. **Resolve to "the last PR commit that is an ancestor of the default branch."** *Measured dead on the
   target case*: a squash merge creates a new commit, so **no** commit of the PR branch is an ancestor
   of the default branch — `git merge-base --is-ancestor e3f6345 fed4e7d` is rc 1 and
   `--is-ancestor e3f6345 origin/master` is rc 1. The rule resolves to nothing for exactly the shape it
   was proposed for.
2. **Require an explicitly recorded verified head captured at merge time; `CANNOT-ASSESS` (rc 2) when
   none was recorded.** Honest, but it *remedies nothing*: #977 and #978 have no such record and never
   can — the branch is deleted and the live head is the wrong tree. It also has no seam to capture the
   record at merge time (the close-out runs after the merge, from the shared checkout). It would convert
   two unclosable items into two permanently unassessable ones.
3. **Preferred (this issue): re-point the subject to the landing when the live head is demonstrably not
   the landed content.** It satisfies both hard constraints at once — (a) the subject is the tree that
   landed for a merged PR, (b) an ordinary correctly-merged item (whose branch tip's tree equals the
   landed tree) is never failed — and it is measurable with the git the port already has.

## Proofs required (GR-12: a gate that cannot fail is a formality)

- **positive** — a real squash merge whose branch advanced afterwards records a green attestation naming
  the **landed** tree (journal JSON shown).
- **negative control** — a lane whose tree does not carry the landing is still refused, by name.
- **negative control (port)** — a drifted subject passed straight to `record_verification` is still
  refused *by the distinct message* (`contains the landing, but the landing's tree differs`).
- **mutant** — removing the subject resolution makes the positive case RED (the wedge returns); removing
  `_admissible`'s tree half makes the port-level refusal RED. Restore, re-run green.
- `governance/lifecycle/tests` and #1098's own controls stay green.

Refs #1098, #977, #978, #984, #786.

items.title: P1: `/healthz` job-set check cannot fail — `EXPECTED_JOBS = 3` is a stale literal, so a document missing the 4th enabled rung (`ao-fleet-reap`) still answers 200
items.body:
## Defect — the `/healthz` job-set check cannot fail

`infra/fleet/healthz.py` hardcodes the size of the expected schedule:

```python
#: The number of scheduled jobs a healthy decision document must report. This
#: is a LITERAL 3, not a measurement of `fleet/cron.MARKERS` …
EXPECTED_JOBS = 3
```

The schedule has grown since (`reap` is the 4th enabled rung — folded in by #901/#830), so the
surface now answers **200** for a decision document that is **missing a rung**. A check whose
pass and fail paths cannot be distinguished by the thing it claims to check is a formality
(AO-GR-12), and this one is exactly that.

### Measured BEFORE (base `origin/master` @ `d3eb77f`, base `healthz.py` sha256 `26d50fc5…`)

Driven over the module's **real HTTP surface** (`serve()` + `GET /healthz`), with the decision
documents' markers read from `config/fleet-jobs.json` **through `fleet/cron.py`** so the probe
cannot drift from the schedule:

```
GET /healthz -> 200        # document missing ao-fleet-reap (3 jobs present)
{ "expected_jobs": 3, "jobs": 3, "status": "ok", "verdict": "ok",
  "job_markers": ["ao-fleet-watchdog", "ao-fleet-prune", "ao-fleet-reconcile"] }
```

and a complete document answers `200` too — with the contradictory pair `"jobs": 4,
"expected_jobs": 3` in the same body. A 2-job document answers `503` correctly, which is what
shows the *count* comparison works and the **constant** is what is wrong.

### The one declaration it must be derived from

`config/fleet-jobs.json` declares **5** jobs, **4** enabled (`watchdog`, `prune`, `reconcile`,
`reap`); `snapshot-refresh` is `enabled: false` (ship-gated OFF per #241). `fleet/cron.py` is the
manifest's single owner (`enabled_jobs` / `declared_markers`), `infra/fleet/inventory.yaml` says
`schedule.lines: 4`, and the container installs 4 marked lines. The health surface must read the
**enabled marker set** through that owner — never a second copy, and never a literal.

### Acceptance

- The expected job set is derived from the declaration (`fleet/cron.py`), not a literal.
- A decision document missing **any** enabled rung answers **503 naming the missing marker**;
  a complete document answers 200.
- An **unreadable or empty** declaration fails closed (a named non-200 — never a silent 0 or a
  stale 3).
- Both halves are covered by tests in `infra/fleet/tests/test_healthz.py` **and** by a gate whose
  mutation (restoring the literal / removing the missing-marker check) **REDs**.

`Verify:` `python3 -m pytest -q infra/fleet/tests && bash scripts/check-healthz-jobset.sh`

### Second finding (recorded here; fix decided by its own size)

The shipped compose service `agent-cron` mounts `.fleet` **read-only**, but the `reconcile` role
takes a lease at `/repo/.fleet/reconcile.lease`. So the **read-only service shape can never answer
200** — it answers `503` by construction, while the health surface it serves is documented as the
success criterion. Either the contract changes (the `ro` shape is expected to be 503 unless a lease
root is writable) or the compose/Dockerfile is wrong. Filed here as a recorded measurement; if the
fix is larger than this lane's file set it becomes a child issue of #706.

Parent: #706 (EPIC — port the fleet's cron automation into a shared-services container).

items.title: check-pr-contract --pr uses a two-dot range, so it judges a lane by master's files and refuses correct PRs (every lane cut from an older master)
items.body:
## Objective

Fix a measured defect in the PR-contract gate itself: **`check-pr-contract.sh --pr` derives its
diff range with two dots**, so it diffs *master's* files against a lane head and misfires for
every lane cut from an older master.

## Measurement

Reported verbatim by the #1123 lane (PR #1125, head `84e0bba`) while it was trying to land a
change it had already verified:

> `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --pr` derives its range as `origin/<base>..<head-oid>` —
> **two-dot**. With master ahead of the lane base it diffs *master's* 160 files against mine, so
> a correct `Gate-changing: no` is refused `pr-body-gate-changing-mismatch-no`.
> `--landed --range HEAD^..HEAD` is `LANDED OK` and `check-squash-message --pr 1125` is `OK`;
> only that cross-check misfires, and it misfires for **every** lane cut from an older master.

Two-dot `A..B` is the *set difference* `reachable(A) − reachable(B)`; the lane's intent is the
*merge-base* range (`A...B`, three dots). The consequence is a gate that refuses correct work
for a reason that is about someone else's commits.

## Acceptance

1. `--pr` (and any sibling path with the same derivation) resolves the range against the
   **merge base**, so a PR whose base has moved is judged on **its own diff** — proven by
   reproducing the false refusal on a lane cut from an older master **before** the fix, and
   showing it correct **after**.
2. The gate must not become permissive: a PR that genuinely omits a required trailer, or whose
   `Gate-changing:` declaration really does disagree with its own diff, must still be refused —
   provoke both and show the refusals.
3. `make verify` PASS at the merged head.
4. Audit the *class*: any other check that compares a lane head against a moving base with a
   two-dot range has the same defect. Grep for it, list what you found, and fix or report each.

## Verify

```bash
git worktree add --detach /tmp/redcheck origin/master && cd /tmp/redcheck
bash scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --pr <a PR whose base has moved>; echo "rc=$?"
```

_AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW) — measured by the #1123 lane and filed while clearing the master-red blockers on the operator's "implement all now" directive._

items.title: master red: check-gitignore — .verify/attestation.schema.json is tracked under a root the gate declares wholly generated
items.body:
## Objective

Clear the one master red on a clean checkout that no issue owns: `check-gitignore` fails
because a **tracked schema file lives under a root the gate declares wholly generated**.

## Measurement (clean detached worktree at `origin/master` = `c9040b9`)

```
$ bash scripts/check-gitignore.sh
  OK    .verify/ ignored by .gitignore:41 (.verify/*)
  OK    .board/locks/ ignored by .gitignore:51 (.board/locks/)
  ... 13 coverage halves OK ...
  OK    .board/ holds no untracked, unignored path
  OK    .fleet/ holds no untracked, unignored path
  OK    .verify/ holds no untracked, unignored path
  FAIL  .verify/attestation.schema.json (tracked under a wholly generated root — runtime state already in history)
check-gitignore: FAIL — 1 problem(s); runtime state under .board .fleet .verify is not safely ignored
```

The check is right: its third rule is *"a root declared wholly generated may hold no tracked
file at all"* — a tracked file under `.verify/` is runtime state already in history. The gate
exists precisely because committing runtime state turns a machine's live attestations into a
moving dispatch signal that every later reader treats as evidence (issue #625).

## Acceptance

1. `bash scripts/check-gitignore.sh` → **OK** on a clean checkout of the merged head.
2. The fix must be **honest about which rule it satisfies**: either the schema is **relocated**
   to a non-generated, reviewable home (with every reader/validator updated, and the readers
   proven to still read it), or the check's declared list is changed **with the reason recorded
   in the file that asserts it** — and if you take that second route you must argue why a
   *schema* is runtime state rather than weakening a rule to reach green. State which route you
   took and why.
3. The check can still fail: provoke it (plant a tracked file under a generated root / an
   untracked unignored path) and show the refusal by name.
4. `make verify` PASS at the merged head.

## Verify

```bash
git worktree add --detach /tmp/redcheck origin/master && cd /tmp/redcheck
bash scripts/check-gitignore.sh; echo "rc=$?"
```

_AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW) — measured on a clean checkout while clearing the master-red blockers on the operator's "implement all now" directive._

items.title: the merge queue proves the message but never the work: merging #1118 made master red on verdict-contains, plus 4 measured pr-queue.sh defects
items.body:
### What happened

Ran the sanctioned queue (`scripts/pr-queue.sh`, `AO_QUEUE_APPLY=1`) to drain the open-PR queue. It merged **3 PRs** — #1081 (`be94933`), #1118 (`2df367d`), #1137 (`864bf4d`) — and **stopped**, correctly, on refusals it does not swallow. Queue went 22 open → 16.

**But the merge of #1118 made master red**, and that is the finding that matters most here:

```
$ bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh     # at origin/master after 2df367d
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh has 2, the record allows 0
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/prune-worktrees.sh has 1, the record allows 0
```

Measured across tips: `a43fd1d` rc=0 → `be94933` rc=0 → **`2df367d` rc=1** → still rc=1. `git log origin/master -- scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh` names **only `2df367d` (#1118)**.

**Root cause: the queue proves the merge *message*, never the *work*.** Its only pre-merge gate is `check-squash-message.sh` (the ticket-trailer predicate). Nothing re-runs the checks a diff can affect, and #1118's body declared `## Pre-existing red: None`. So a `gate-changing` PR can introduce a brand-new red and the queue will merge it happily. A tool whose whole purpose is to sequence merges safely has no notion of "would this diff add a red".

Master is currently also red on `check-isolation-landed` from **#1144** (merged by another lane with no trailer — see below).

### Second, unrelated live red

`#1144` was refused by the queue for `commit-missing-ticket-trailer`, and the refusal was **right**: its only ticket-ish line is a bare `Refs #1042` in prose, with no `issue-<n>` branch, no `(#n)` in the title, and no `Closes` line at all — appending a trailer would have fabricated provenance. Another lane merged it anyway as `d3eb77f`, and the landed commit carries no trailer:

```
  FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:d3eb77fa0cb1
check-pr-contract: LANDED: FAIL (1 finding(s))
```

### Five defects measured in `scripts/pr-queue.sh`

1. **`classify()` treats the string `"UNKNOWN"` as mergeable** — only JSON `null` maps to the `unknown` class. Measured: `gh pr list --json mergeable` reported `UNKNOWN`/`UNKNOWN` for #1142 while the single-PR endpoint said `mergeable:false, dirty`, and the plan printed `MERGE_ORDER: 1142` with #1142 classed `ready` and ordered **first**. This is also why `ready`↔`conflict` flap between runs. Severe: it can merge something GitHub will refuse, or mis-order the queue.
2. **`gate_paths()` does not strip `#` comments** from `scripts/lib/gate-paths.txt`, though that file documents that comments are ignored and `check-pr-contract.sh`'s reader *does* strip them. The comment token `scripts/pr-queue.sh` became a glob — the only reason #1135 was classified `gate-changing`.
3. **Two parsers of "pre-existing red"**: the queue prefix-matches `## pre-existing red`; `check-pr-contract.sh` requires the exact heading. #1127's heading is `## Pre-existing red / environment notes` → the queue excludes it, the contract gate finds no section at all.
4. **`check-squash-message --pr` uses a two-dot range** (`origin/<base>..<head>`), so its `Gate-changing:` cross-check compares a false file set. Measured on #1081: two-dot reported **206 files including 12 gate paths** (master's newer files appear as `D`), while the true merge-base range is exactly the 7 `identity/rbac/**` files with **0 gate hits**. The correct `Gate-changing: no` was flagged as a mismatch — a false positive that moves as master's tip moves.
5. **No gate-regression check** (the root cause above).

### Proposed remedy, cheapest first

- Give the queue the same shape it already trusts for the message, for the work: derive the PR's affected `scripts/check-*.sh` from its own file list and run them before `gh pr merge`, refusing **by name**. That closes the §root-cause gap with one seam, and mirrors `check-squash-message`.
- Then the four small defects above, all in `scripts/pr-queue.sh` (a lane already exists on that file — `issue-1056` / PR #1135, which carries the argv→stdin fix this run depended on).
- Separately: repair or revert #1118's three piped-grep sites in `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` and `scripts/check-prune-worktrees.sh` (the same bash-native containment conversion done elsewhere today), so `verdict-contains` returns to rc 0.

**Why this is filed rather than fixed here:** an unfiled finding is invisible, and this one is fleet-blocking — master is red right now because the merge queue has no way to notice.

Measured on 2026-09-17 against `origin/master` between `a43fd1d` and `d3eb77f`.

items.title: Declare the repo merge-message policy as code (squash = PR title + PR body) with a read-back gate; baseline the 5 trailer-less squash commits (#803)
items.body:
Parent: #803
Refs #836, #998, #1009

## Why
Every squash merge by a session using `gh pr merge --squash` was producing a master commit whose ticket trailer was buried mid-body (repo setting `squash_merge_commit_message=COMMIT_MESSAGES` concatenates per-commit messages) — so `check-isolation-landed` went red on a fresh set of commits after every wave (4 baselined in #1130, then #1119 #1044 #1121 #1126 #1103 immediately after). #1009 enforces the trailer only on the landing driver's path.

Applied 2026-09-17 by operator API call and read back:
```json
{"squash_merge_commit_message":"PR_BODY","squash_merge_commit_title":"PR_TITLE"}
```
With PR_BODY the squash message ends with the PR body's trailer block (`Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#<n>` / `Closes #<n>`) — the contract `check-pr-contract.sh` already enforces on the body. Like #807, this is a GR-5 breach until it is declared: nothing in the repo says it, so a restore/fork diverges silently.

## Deliverable
1. `governance/platform/repo-settings.yaml` (schema `ao.repo-settings/v1`, fields exactly as the GitHub repos API returns them: `squash_merge_commit_title`, `squash_merge_commit_message`, `allow_merge_commit`, `allow_rebase_merge`, `delete_branch_on_merge`) with the WHY header in the branch-protection.yaml style.
2. `scripts/repo-settings.sh {apply|verify}` mirroring `scripts/branch-protection.sh` (apply = idempotent PATCH of declared fields; verify = read back, fail on drift naming the field) and `scripts/check-repo-settings.sh` — tri-state, PROVOKED offline (matching fixture passes, drifted fixture fails naming the field, same comparator as verify), live half CANNOT-ASSESS offline never a pass. Wire into `scripts/verify.sh` + `Makefile`.
3. `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json`: records for `13185503a075` (#1119), `4986cb636344` (#1044), `94e23472a49e` (#1121), `ea730bee0495` (#1126), `75d66257fc80` (#1103) — `commit-missing-ticket-trailer`, provenance PR, reason: squash message setting predates this declaration.
4. `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` note: the PR body IS the squash commit message.

## Acceptance
`bash scripts/check-repo-settings.sh`, `bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh`, `bash scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh`, `bash scripts/check-branch-protection.sh` green on a clean detached worktree of master; `bash scripts/repo-settings.sh verify` reads back the live setting with zero drift.

This is the third+ recurrence; the durable fix is #1009 (enforce the trailer at merge time) — reference it, do not re-implement here.

items.title: master red: check-cross-repo-lessons — 19 hub ledger records have no counterpart declaration and are not listed local-only
items.body:
## Objective

Clear one more of the master reds that block every lane's landing: `check-cross-repo-lessons`
is NOT-OK with **19 findings** on a clean checkout. It is unowned — not in #1034's list, not in
#1043's list, and no other issue names it. It is also the one red the #1077 lane measured and
deliberately **left open** rather than silence (its fix is a per-record declaration outside its
file scope), so this issue is that hand-off.

## Measurement (clean detached worktree, twice — `origin/master` `96ae0fb`, then `c9040b9`)

```
$ bash scripts/check-cross-repo-lessons.sh
lessons-sync: FAIL — 19 finding(s):
  local-record-undisclosed CA-0010: authoritative ledger record CA-0010 has no counterpart declaration and is not listed local-only — reported by id, never dropped
  local-record-undisclosed CA-0011: ... CA-0012, CA-0019, CA-0020, CA-0022
  local-record-undisclosed INC-0008: ... INC-0015, INC-0016
check-cross-repo-lessons: FAIL — lessons-sync contract has findings (report: /tmp/ao-cross-repo-lessons.<ts>/report.json)
```

The check is behaving correctly: the **hub's authoritative ledger** (CMR) carries records this
repo has neither declared a counterpart for nor listed as local-only, and the check reports each
one **by id, never dropping it**. A gate that cannot say which records are missing would be a
formality.

## What would be dishonest here

Declaring the 19 records `local-only` to reach green would **silence a signal nobody has
verified** — the #1077 lane refused exactly that, and it is right to. The honest close is one of:

1. the counterpart declaration for each record (read the hub bundle / the CMR ledger and resolve
   each id to what it actually is in this repo), or
2. an explicit `local-only` listing **with the reason recorded per record** (the check's own
   vocabulary), for the ids genuinely not applicable here — and then say, in the PR, which of
   the 19 are (1) and which are (2), with the evidence for each.

## Acceptance

1. `bash scripts/check-cross-repo-lessons.sh` → **OK** on a clean checkout of the merged head,
   with the report's finding count at 0 and **no finding silently dropped**.
2. `make verify` PASS at the merged head.
3. The PR states, per record id, which route closed it (counterpart vs local-only+reason), and
   proves the check can still fail — a NEW hub record with neither declaration must still be
   reported.

## Cross-repo knowledge required

The authority is the **CMR hub** (pinned submodule `vendor/CMR`, `cmr-pin.yaml`) and its ledger;
query the CMR knowledge surface rather than guessing. Local-code-first (GR-17): read this
checkout's `governance/lessons/**` and `governance/lessons-sync/**` before reaching for the hub.

## Verify

```bash
git worktree add --detach /tmp/redcheck origin/master && cd /tmp/redcheck
bash scripts/check-cross-repo-lessons.sh; echo "rc=$?"
```

_AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW) — measured across two masters while clearing the master-red blockers on the operator's "implement all now" directive._
