items.title: check-dispatch-queue: 19 closed issues still queued, exposed by a fresh board snapshot (#1107 follow-up)
items.body:
Parent: #803

## Context

While fixing #1107 (ticket-projection / pmo-rollup / lessons-sync red cluster), the committed `.board/snapshot.json` had to be regenerated via `python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py snapshot --from-github` (its declared make-target-equivalent) because it was stale relative to GitHub (#1029 — closed 2026-09-17 — was absent from a snapshot generated 2026-09-15).

With the fresh snapshot in place, `bash scripts/check-dispatch-queue.sh` flips from `CANNOT-ASSESS — snapshot-stale` to a genuine `FAIL (19 problem(s))`: 19 issues in the committed dispatch queue are already closed on GitHub and should have been dropped:

```
#619 #712 #713 #714 #715 #731 #732 #786 #865 #866 #882 #883 #885 #887 #888 #889 #900 #902 #928
```

This defect was previously masked because the stale snapshot made the check CANNOT-ASSESS rather than a pass or fail — it was never actually exercised against a fresh board.

## Why this is filed, not fixed, here

`governance/dispatch/queue` (and its state file) is outside the file ownership lane for #1107 (`.board/snapshot.json` via generator, `governance/lessons/**`, `governance/pmo/**`, `governance/ticket*/**`, and the three ticket-projection/pmo-rollup/cross-repo-lessons check scripts only if the defect is in a probe). Dropping 19 closed issues from the dispatch queue is a queue-maintenance change to a different owned surface, not a probe defect in one of those three scripts.

## Deliverable

Decide the declared mechanism for pruning closed issues from the committed dispatch queue (a `queue --check --fix` / prune subcommand, or a documented manual reconciliation step) and apply it so `bash scripts/check-dispatch-queue.sh` is green against a freshly refreshed board snapshot.

items.title: gate-lock: a holder reaps its own leftover on exit; the watchdog sweeps only its own worktree (RCA 2026-09-17 fix #3)
items.body:
## Problem (measured)

157 leftover 0-byte gate-lock files sit under the gate-lock permit store
"needing attention" (`bash scripts/gate-lock.sh status`, 2026-09-17,
RCA `docs/rca/2026-09-17-pr-pileup.md`). A holder's normal exit path
(`fleet/gatelock.py:_hold`) truncates its lock/permit records to 0 bytes
on exit but never unlinks the worktree lock file itself, so every clean
holder exit — not just a crash — manufactures a new 0-byte leftover.
Nothing reaps a holder's own lock file on its own exit path (normal exit,
signal, or exception): `release()` does reap a free lock
(`_reap_free_lock`), but only when something later calls `release` for
that worktree; a holder that simply exits (its parent gate process ending)
never gets there.

## Why not a box-wide auto-heal

`docs/rca/2026-09-16-pr-queue-clearing.md` / `governance/lessons/rca/RCA-0015-zero-byte-gate-lock-wedge.md`
already reviewed and refused this: `fleet/gatelock.py`'s `health()` /
`gate-lock.sh doctor` sweep is alert-only by design. `_reap_free_lock` is
flock-safe (it can never unlink a lock a live holder flocks), but a
box-wide sweep can still race a DIFFERENT worktree's in-flight `acquire`
between that acquirer's `os.open(O_CREAT)` and its `_try_lock` — the file
is briefly unflocked and indistinguishable from a leftover, so the sweep
would unlink it, its `_flock_fresh` re-check would fail, and 3 retries
later that unrelated, legitimately-starting gate reports rc 12
CANNOT-ASSESS. Scoped to *its own* worktree, only the sweeper's own
process could be the acquirer in that window, so the race disappears.

## Fix

1. A holder reaps its OWN lock file on its own exit path (normal exit,
   SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP, watched-pid death) in `fleet/gatelock.py`'s
   `_hold` — unlink (not just truncate) the worktree lock while the
   flock it already holds still proves no other holder exists for that
   path. Permit slot files stay truncated-not-unlinked (they're a fixed
   reused pool with no `_flock_fresh` re-check in `acquire`'s permit
   loop; unlinking one would let two future gates flock two different
   inodes both named the same slot path).
2. A new worktree-scoped, proven-free reap (e.g. `reap_own_worktree`) that
   `fleet/watchdog.py` schedules against ONLY its own checkout's
   worktree key — never box-wide — leaving the existing box-wide
   `gatelock.health()` alert-only sweep untouched.

## Acceptance

- A worktree's leftover count returns to 0 after its holder exits
  (normal exit, and the SIGTERM path).
- Negative control: a lock flocked by a live holder is never unlinked by
  either the exit-path reap or the watchdog's own-worktree sweep.
- Negative control: the watchdog's own-worktree sweep given worktree A
  does not touch worktree B's leftover, even though B's is provably free
  (proves "scoped," not a box-wide auto-heal).

Refs #1034
Refs #948

items.title: fix(lifecycle): a squash-merged item can never record verification — the lane must equal the PR head the merge replaced
items.body:
## Observed (measured 2026-09-17, master `96ae0fb`)

Closing a **squash-merged** item can never record a green verification attestation, so the item
keeps `VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING` for ever.

`governance/lifecycle/cli.py:494` (inside `record_verification`):

```python
head = self._run(["git", "-C", str(worktree), "rev-parse", "HEAD"])
if commit and head != commit:
    raise RuntimeError(f"lane head {head[:12]} is not the verified commit {commit[:12]}")
```

`commit` is resolved from the PR, and for a merged PR that is **`pr.head_commit`** — the tip of the
branch the squash-merge *replaced*. A squash merge creates a new commit on `master`; the branch tip
is **not** an ancestor of `master`, so:

1. a lane cut from `origin/master` (the correct, rule-15 venue) can never equal it → immediate
   `RuntimeError`; and
2. resetting the lane to the PR head satisfies the equality, but that tree is **obsolete**, and the
   composite gate is not tree-local (repo-wide invariants — `isolation-landed`, quarantine
   baselines, `.board` snapshot, `docs-lint`, `gate-lock`, `erp-e2e`, `pytest-*` — assert facts about
   the *current* tree), so the gate then fails for reasons that have nothing to do with the change.

Measured on the three EPIC #706 children whose PRs had merged but which had never been closed:

| issue | PR / merge sha | lane reset to PR head | gate at that head |
|---|---|---|---|
| #714 | #905 `fc1bea22` | `a06badc9` (tree `f8d1ed81` == merge tree) | pending |
| #977 | #984 `fed4e7d` | `e3f6345` | **FAIL (19 of 145 checks failed, 10 skipped)** |
| #978 | #984 `fed4e7d` | `e3f6345` | same run |

All three close-outs returned `REMAINS VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING`. The 19 non-PASS checks at
`e3f6345` (`docs-lint, gate-lock, gitignore, isolation-landed, lifecycle-reclaim, pytest-fleet,
pytest-chat, pytest-cockpit, erp-e2e, erp-finops, erp-portal, control-audit, control-functions,
operator-access, operator-terminal, chat-finops, chat-ux, portal-auth-env, fleet-cron-dev-run`) are
repo-wide checks failing because the tree is old, not because of the change under test. PR #984's own
checklist even records `make verify — PARKED on box contention after 6 attempts`: **no attestation
ever existed for `e3f6345`**, so the tool demands evidence that was never produced.

## Why this is the same defect #786 was for

#786 fixed the *other* half of this invariant ("the invariant names the **verified head commit**, and
the commit — not the branch, not the worktree — is what proves it"). It re-measures a **gone** lane
from the commit. The squash-merge half was never covered: the commit the item must name is the one
that **landed**, not the one the merge replaced.

## Remedy (bounded)

1. **Resolve the LANDED commit for a merged PR** — `merge_commit_sha` when the PR is merged, else
   `head_commit`. The tree that landed is the one worth measuring, and on `master` it is still
   present (current master is a descendant of it), so a repo-wide gate run there is meaningful
   instead of misleading.
2. **Accept containment, not only equality** — a lane is admissible when its HEAD *is* the verified
   commit **or contains** it (`merge-base --is-ancestor <verified> <head>`); gate at the lane HEAD and
   journal **both** shas (`{"verify": {"ok": true, "commit": <lane head>, "verified": <landed>,
   "source": "lane", "via": "contains"}}`) so the record names the tree that was measured and the
   landing it stands for.
3. **Kin to the stranding test already learned:** "stranded" is decided by **content equivalence**,
   never ancestry — here ancestry is the *sufficient* direction (a descendant tree contains the
   landing), and the negative control is a lane that does **not** contain it.

## Acceptance / negative control

- A fake merged item whose PR merge commit is an ancestor of the lane HEAD closes with a **green**
  attestation naming both shas.
- **Negative control:** a lane HEAD that does **not** contain the verified commit is still REFUSED by
  name — a mutation that accepts anything must be caught by the gate.
- A not-yet-merged item still requires equality (its verified commit is its head).
- `scripts/check-lifecycle-verify-order.sh` and the close-out gate keep their provoked failures.

## Verify

```
python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --issue 977   # green attestation, both shas recorded
python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py status --issue 977  # no VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING
make verify
```

Refs #706 #714 #977 #978. Related: #786 (gone lane), #834 (dead record shadowing), #269 (end-to-end
closure).

items.title: check-portal-auth-env maps an INTERRUPTED pytest suite to FAIL, reporting a red it cannot evidence
items.body:
## What was measured

`scripts/check-portal-auth-env.sh` was reported as one of the eight master reds, with this line:

```
  FAIL  the offline reproduction of the post-deploy criterion failed (rc=2)
check-portal-auth-env: FAIL — the portal's auth-gate env is not supplied as declared
```

Measured on a **clean lane worktree at `origin/master = 96ae0fba19c36764e1f0251070d7c77bb17b4a5d`**, that is **not** reproducible. The check is green:

```
$ bash scripts/check-portal-auth-env.sh
== portal-auth-env ==
  OK    declaration: 2 secret(s) — 1 mounted file(s), 1 injected value(s)
  OK    the console's environment is closed: portal/server/sso.py reads 3 variable(s), 2 declared + 1 exempted with a reason
  OK    no value where a reference is promised: 191 file(s) under infra/ + portal/ scanned, no secret material
  OK    the acceptance grep names them 38 time(s) in infra/ + portal/, all wiring
  OK    PORTAL_AUTH_GATE_JWKS_FILE <- projects to /etc/ao/auth-gate-jwks.json from secret portal-auth-gate-jwks (version latest)
== portal-auth-env: the post-deploy criterion (offline) ==
......                                                                   [100%]
6 passed in 1.06s
  OK    the mirror reaches the mount path and a real session reaches /api/console/me
check-portal-auth-env: OK — the declaration matches the console, the deploy projects it, no value is carried, and the mirror publishes on stdin
rc=0
```

All 14 provoked refusals pass, and the suite passes standalone (`6 passed`, rc 0).

## Root cause — the check reports a NOT-OK it cannot evidence

The `rc=2` in the observed line is **pytest's own INTERRUPTED exit code**, not a test failure
(pytest exits 1 for failed tests, 2 when interrupted by SIGINT / `KeyboardInterrupt`).

The check maps **every** non-zero suite exit to FAIL:

```bash
suite_rc=0
suite_out="$(env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
  portal/tests/test_auth_gate_secret_env.py 2>&1)" || suite_rc=$?
...
if [ "$suite_rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "  OK    the mirror reaches the mount path and a real session reaches /api/console/me"
else
  printf '  FAIL  the offline reproduction of the post-deploy criterion failed (rc=%s)\n' "$suite_rc" >&2
  fail=$((fail + 1))
fi
```

So a suite that was **interrupted** — which is what a foreground gate run in this box's shared shell
gets from a neighbouring lane's `Ctrl-C`, and which was independently observed killing a
foreground run mid-flight during this measurement — is reported as a product defect.

This is the exact mirror of the no-false-green doctrine. The repo's own contract is
`0 OK / 1 NOT-OK / 2 CANNOT-ASSESS`, and "CANNOT-ASSESS must never be reported as a pass". The
inverse matters as much: **a run the check could not assess must not be reported as NOT-OK**, because
that blames the product for an environment failure and sends an operator to look for a defect that
is not there — which is what happened here.

## Acceptance

- An interrupted suite is reported **CANNOT-ASSESS with the interruption named**, and the check
  still exits non-zero — never a pass.
- A genuinely failing suite is still `FAIL` (rc 1): the mapping must not become a way to pass.
- The two halves are proved **by name**: a provoked interruption yields the CANNOT-ASSESS line, and a
  provoked failing suite yields the FAIL line.
- `scripts/check-portal-auth-env.sh` stays green on an uninterrupted run.

**Verify:** provoke an interruption of the suite (a pytest plugin that raises `KeyboardInterrupt`
during collection, injected through `PYTEST_ADDOPTS`/`PYTHONPATH`) and assert the check prints a
`CANNOT-ASSESS` line naming the interruption and exits 2; then provoke a failing suite and assert it
still prints `FAIL` and exits 1.



---

Clear one of the eight master reds that block every lane's landing: `check-rbac-head-binding`
is NOT-OK because the **identity/rbac pytest suite cannot import the `rbac` package**, while
the check's own behaviour probe passes. A check that is red for a *collection* reason is
red for the wrong reason: it stops measuring the binding contract it exists to prove.

## Measurement (clean detached worktree at `origin/master` = `96ae0fb`)

```
$ bash scripts/check-rbac-head-binding.sh
    from rbac.model import (
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rbac'
check-rbac-head-binding: NOT-OK — identity/rbac pytest suite is red

== default-off (GR-28) + provoked negative control (delete the binding row) ==
  OK    hermes: unbound by default
  OK    hermes: unbound tenant refused (org:read)
  OK    hermes: bound tenant allowed (org:read)
  OK    hermes: control - cross-tenant read refused even though both opted in (org:read)
  OK    hermes: binding row deleted
  OK    hermes: control - deleted binding is refused (org:read)
  ... (14 control halves, all OK)
PROBE_RESULT=OK
check-rbac-head-binding: NOT-OK
```

So the *contract* the check exists to assert is intact and its negative control bites; only
the pytest import path is broken. That is the same defect family as **#968** (`<repo>/fleet`
on `sys.path` shadowing the telemetry package) and **#1071** (`fleet/gatelock.py` doing a bare
`import lease`): a repo that cannot be imported as a package because of a lane-local
`sys.path`/shadowing assumption, discovered by whichever gate happens to run pytest there.

## Acceptance

1. `bash scripts/check-rbac-head-binding.sh` reaches **OK** on a clean checkout of the merged
   head, with the identity/rbac suite genuinely **collected and run** — not skipped, not
   zero tests, not "errors during collection" counted as a pass.

   green).

   same shape), say in the PR what is shared and whether those sites are fixed by this change
   or stay open — a one-site patch that leaves the mechanism in place must say so.

items.body:
## Objective

Clear two of the eight master reds that block **every** lane's landing, by fixing the
*artifact* they assert against — the committed board snapshot — instead of the checks.

These two reds have **no issue**: they are not in #1034's list and not in #1043's list.

## Measurement (clean detached worktree at `origin/master` = `96ae0fb`)

```
$ git worktree add --detach /tmp/redcheck origin/master && cd /tmp/redcheck
$ bash scripts/check-ticket-projection.sh
  FAIL  reference-unresolved: INC-0007 → #1029 — lesson names an issue the board snapshot does not carry [governance/lessons/ledger.jsonl:29]
check-ticket-projection: FAIL — the projection refuses to build (see above)

$ bash scripts/check-pmo-rollup.sh
  FAIL  view deps could not assess the committed graph:
  FAIL  view lanes could not assess the committed graph:
  FAIL  view report could not assess the committed graph:
  FAIL  view raid could not assess the committed graph:
  FAIL  view aging could not assess the committed graph:
  FAIL  raid --check reported a finding on the committed graph:
check-pmo-rollup: FAIL — 6 control(s) did not refuse
```

The input is stale, not the code:

| artifact | generated | issues | carries #1029 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.board/snapshot.json` (committed at `96ae0fb`) | `2026-09-15T04:28:44Z` | 460 | **no** |
| `.board/snapshot.json` after `governance/dispatch/cli.py snapshot --from-github` | `2026-09-17T12:57:22Z` | 571 | yes (CLOSED) |

## The experiment (already run — this is the proof, not a plan)

With only the refreshed snapshot copied into the clean worktree, nothing else changed:

```
ticket-projection rc=0 :: check-ticket-projection: OK — deterministic, rebuildable, one writer per field, 7 control(s) refused
pmo-rollup        rc=0 :: check-pmo-rollup: OK — 5 view(s) derived offline, 7 control(s) exercised, no store written
```

## Why it matters beyond two checks

A red `verify` is never attributable by the landing driver, so these two starve **every**
landing — they are part of the `make verify` PASS that epic #665 owes as its DoD item 5.
They also make *clean-checkout master-health measurement itself* wrong: #1034, #1043 and
#665 all measured "master red" this way, and two of the reds they recorded are the stale
artifact speaking, not master.

## Acceptance

1. `.board/snapshot.json` is current at the merged head, and `check-ticket-projection` and
   `check-pmo-rollup` are **OK** on a clean checkout of the merged head (rc 0, with their own
   negative controls still refusing).
2. **The rot is detected, not hidden.** A one-off refresh that rots again next time the board
   moves is not a delivery: say in the PR which mechanism prevents the next stale snapshot
   (a control that fails on an unresolvable/unaged snapshot, or a documented refresh-in-lane
   discipline), and prove that mechanism can fail. Note the constraint: `scripts/verify.sh`
   is offline by design ("no network and no containers are required"), so the control cannot
   fetch — it must detect.
3. `make verify` PASS at the merged head.

## Out of scope

`portal-offline-spog`'s remaining failure (`GET /api/fleet/snapshot (flag OFF) -> 401,
expected 404`) is **not** this stale snapshot: it is the pre-promotion posture asserted by
#1043. Its `could not assess the committed graph` half *is* this issue (see #1043's comment).

## Verify

```bash
git worktree add --detach /tmp/redcheck origin/master && cd /tmp/redcheck
bash scripts/check-ticket-projection.sh; echo "ticket-projection rc=$?"
```

items.title: fleet/gatelock.py cannot be imported as a package: a bare `import lease` kills the lifecycle close-out tool and reds check-github-lifecycle (25 violations)
items.body:
## Symptom — measured on `origin/master` (`96ae0fb`), shared checkout clean in that area

```
$ python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py status --issue 506
  File "…/governance/lifecycle/cli.py", line 41, in <module>
    from governance.lifecycle import directive, gate
  File "…/governance/lifecycle/gate.py", line 76, in <module>
    from fleet.gatelock import EXIT_PARKED, EXIT_REFUSED, EXIT_STORE_UNUSABLE
  File "…/fleet/gatelock.py", line 86, in <module>
    import lease
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'lease'
```

The same import kills the gate of record's lifecycle check:

```
$ bash scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh
    import lease
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'lease'
check-github-lifecycle: FAIL (25 violation(s))
```

So **`governance/lifecycle` — the close-out tool rule 16 depends on — is currently unusable**, and
`check-github-lifecycle` is red for every lane on the box.

## Root cause

`fleet/` is **not a package** (there is no `fleet/__init__.py`), but consumers import it *as* one with the
repo root on `sys.path`:

```
governance/lifecycle/gate.py:76:        from fleet.gatelock import EXIT_PARKED, EXIT_REFUSED, EXIT_STORE_UNUSABLE
governance/lifecycle/tests/test_gate.py:13:  import fleet.gatelock as gatelock
```

In that venue `sys.path` holds the **repo root**, so `import lease` (a bare top-level name) resolves
nothing — the module only exists as `fleet/lease.py`. The bare form works in the *script* venue, where
`fleet/` itself is on `sys.path` (which is why `fleet/watchdog.py`, `fleet/prune.py` etc. get away with
it), so the defect is invisible from the path that most work takes.

## Attribution

```
$ git log -S'import lease' --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -- fleet/gatelock.py
fed4e7d 2026-09-16 Wire the single-writer lease and freeze/drain refusal into fleet-cron (#977, #978) (#984)
```

Introduced by **PR #984** (`fed4e7d`) — the same commit already recorded on #998/#1001 for putting its
ticket refs in the *subject* rather than a trailer block, i.e. one landing with two independent defects.

## The pattern the repo already uses

Three siblings import the same concept package-relatively, and none of them breaks:

```
fleet/monitor.py:85:                    from governance.policy import lease
fleet/channel.py:51:                    from governance.policy import lease
governance/dispatch/claims.py:50:       from governance.policy import lease
```

Note there are **two** `lease` modules: the older `governance/policy/lease.py` (21.9 KB) and the one this
PR added, `fleet/lease.py` (15.0 KB). The fix therefore needs a decision, not just a mechanical edit:

1. make `fleet/gatelock.py` import the *repo* lease package-relatively (`from governance.policy import
   lease`) and keep `fleet/lease.py` for the script venue only; **or**
2. make `fleet/gatelock.py` importable from both venues (a `sys.path` bootstrap of its own directory
   exactly as `fleet/watchdog.py:114-115` does — `import gatelock` / `import lease` after inserting the
   fleet dir), accepting that the package-import path then carries a path mutation; **or**
3. add `fleet/__init__.py` and make every fleet module import consistently (`from fleet import lease`).

Whichever is chosen, the acceptance should be *both venues*: `python3 -c "import fleet.gatelock"` from the
repo root **and** `cd fleet && python3 -c "import gatelock"`.

## Blast radius (why this is worth fixing first)

- `governance/lifecycle/cli.py` — the close-out tool: `status`/`close`/`audit` all die at import.
- `scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh` — red, 25 violations, for **every** lane's composite.
- `governance/lifecycle/tests/` — package-import consumers of the same module.

## Verify

```bash
python3 -c "import fleet.gatelock"                      # must not raise
cd fleet && python3 -c "import gatelock"                # and the script venue must still work
python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py status --issue 506  # the close-out tool comes back
bash scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh                  # no traceback
```

The #506 date bomb (a fixture whose **seed** is pinned to a literal date while the code under test resolves its **evaluation** bucket from the **live clock** — green on the day it was written, red every day after) is asked about at **filing time**, not detected afterwards, on the two remaining surfaces: the lane/task brief every future task is shaped by, and the parent-side module-admission contract.

1. Does this work introduce a **time-pinned fixture** (a literal date/day/month)?
2. Where is the **evaluation** bucket resolved — from the **entity under test**, or from the **live clock**?

At byte-identical seed lines a *static* detector refuses the defect **and its own repair** (measured in #1039), so the only honest enforcement is behavioural — which is exactly why the question has to be asked when the work is shaped.

- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`

items.title: console sign-out loops: logout clears only the console token, not the gate session (ai.purebliss.app)
items.body:
## Symptom
On the live AgentConsole (ai.purebliss.app) the **sign-out button does not log the user out**. Clicking `↩ sign out` returns to the login page, but the next `/` navigation re-authenticates and drops the user straight back into the console.

## Root cause
The console's logout clears **only its own derived cookie** (`os-session-token`), never the auth gate's real session cookie (`os_session`):

- `portal/server/app.py` `_logout` → `Set-Cookie: os-session-token=; Max-Age=0` only (audit + jti revoke).
- `portal/static/js/console.js` logout button → `CP.post('/api/console/logout')` then `window.location.href = '/views/login.html'`.

`/views/login.html` is the unauthenticated entry, so the browser then hits the gate's `/auth/login` — which finds the still-valid `os_session` and **mints a fresh `os-session-token`**, logging the user back in. The gate's own navigation logout (`GET /auth/logout`, which clears `os_session` + `os_csrf` + `os-session-token` and redirects to `/auth/login`) was never invoked.

The tunnel already routes `ai.purebliss.app/^auth/` → the os-ai gate, so `/auth/logout` is reachable same-origin.

## Fix
The sign-out control delegates to the gate's authoritative navigation logout instead of returning to the console's login view:

`portal/static/js/console.js` — after the console-side logout POST, navigate to `/auth/logout` (clears the full gate session, then 302 → `/auth/login` → Google).

Regression guard: `portal/tests/test_assets.py` asserts the served `console.js` navigates to `/auth/logout` and no longer to `/views/login.html`.

## Verify
```
python3 -m pytest portal/tests/test_assets.py
```
Live: mint a session, click sign out → cookies `os_session`/`os_csrf`/`os-session-token` cleared → `/` redirects to Google (no re-auth loop).

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#1046 (same auth-integration family).

items.title: console refuses the gate's tenant-agnostic os-session-token — ai.purebliss.app login loops (ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS)
items.body:
## Symptom (live 2026-09-17, ai.purebliss.app)

A logged-in visitor to `ai.purebliss.app` hit `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`: the AgentConsole's `/` bounced to `/auth/login` even though the auth gate had authenticated the user.

## Root cause — a cross-repo contract mismatch

`identity/sso/tokens.py:verify_console_session_token` required a `tenantId` claim:

```
auth-gate session token refused: session token carries no tenantId claim
```

But the **shared-frontend** auth gate mints the `os-session-token` **tenant-agnostic** — `{purpose, sub, email, name, role}` and nothing else — because one gate serves every portal origin (`os`/`gws`/`ai`). So a genuine gate token was refused → the console redirected `/` → `/auth/login` → the gate (valid `os_session`) redirected back to `/` → loop.

The console maps a verified identity to tenants from its **org directory** (`state.roles_for(email)`), never from the token, so the tenant claim is not part of the gate's console-token contract.

**Why it was invisible:** the portal test fixture minted tokens *with* a `tenantId` (via `issue_console_session_token`), so the verifier's requirement was never exercised against a gate-shaped token — the same "declared ≠ exercised" class as #1029.

## Fix

PR #1045 (`issue-tenantless-gate-token`):
- `verify_console_session_token(..., require_tenant: bool = False)` — the gate token has no tenant; enforcement is opt-in.
- `SsoService.verify_console` (which mints its own tenant-scoped tokens) passes `require_tenant=True`.
- Regression guard: mint the token in the gate's exact shape (no `tenantId`) and assert the console opens the shell; retire the now-wrong `test_token_without_a_tenant_claim_is_refused`.

## Verify

```
python3 -m pytest portal/tests/test_auth_gate_session.py     # 21 passed
python3 -m pytest identity/sso/tests/ identity/chat/tests/   # 77 + 107 passed
```

**Deployed + measured live** (shared-services cluster, `ai.purebliss.app`): with a valid `os-session-token`, `GET /` → `302 /views/shell.html`; `GET /api/fleet/snapshot` → `200`. Public: `healthz 200 · snapshot 401 · console 302`.

## Cross-references

- shared-frontend #495 / PR #496 — the gate now also sets the `os-session-token` as an HttpOnly cookie for direct-front-door consumers (the delivery half).
- shared-frontend #497 — the shell image build break found while landing #495.

items.title: the #607/#1027 SPoG promotion left three gates asserting the pre-go-live posture — operator-terminal, e2e and portal-offline-spog are red on master
items.body:
## The regression

`32e8c24` — *"feat(flags): promote the SPoG surfaces — ai.purebliss.app now serves the console (#607) (#1027)"* — flipped `surfaces.operator_terminal` in `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml`:

```diff
   operator_terminal:
-    default: off
-    promoted: false
+    default: on
+    promoted: true
```

That promotion is deliberate (it is the #607 go-live). **Three gates still assert the pre-promotion posture**, so master is red on all three — measured on a clean `origin/master` checkout (`4c9055f`):

```
$ python3 -m pytest -q e2e/tests/test_go_live_delivery.py
FAILED e2e/tests/test_go_live_delivery.py::test_the_surface_is_absent_while_it_ships_unpromoted
    >       assert dark["declaresOn"] is False
    E       assert True is False
FAILED e2e/tests/test_go_live_delivery.py::test_a_rollback_returns_the_surface_to_dark_without_a_commit
FAILED e2e/tests/test_go_live_delivery.py::test_every_negative_control_genuinely_blocks
3 failed, 8 passed in 11.82s
```

The `verify` composite names all three, at the same head:

| check | measured failure |
|---|---|
| `operator-terminal` | `surfaces.operator_terminal.default is True, expected off` · `surfaces.operator_terminal.promoted must be false while it ships off` · `read_surface_default resolved operator_terminal to 'on', expected off` |
| `e2e` | the three `test_go_live_delivery.py` failures above |
| `portal-offline-spog` | `view deps/lanes/report/raid/aging could not assess the committed graph` · `readiness on the committed tree -> ready` ... `surfaces.operator_terminal: state ready, declared 'on', 'promoted, no rollback engaged...'` |

So the gates disagree with the shipping product, and the e2e capstone is what surfaced it — which is the capstone working, not failing.

## Why it matters

All three are `verify`-signal checks, and a red `verify` is **never attributable** by the landing driver (`governance/landing/attribution.py`). While they are red, **no lane can land** — including the two implemented-and-verified e2e PRs (#1023, #1018) and the two-red-clearing fix (#1035).

## Acceptance

Each of the three either (a) is updated to the promoted posture with a **reason recorded in the file that asserts it**, or (b) is shown, by name, to be asserting the pre-go-live posture on purpose and is therefore expected to be retired at go-live. No gate may be silenced without saying which of the two it is.

- `operator-terminal`: either the check learns that a surface may be **legitimately promoted** (asserting `default`/`promoted` are *consistent* rather than *off*), or the promotion is reverted — but the two must agree.
- `e2e`: `test_the_surface_is_absent_while_it_ships_unpromoted` must be pinned to a surface that genuinely still ships unpromoted, or re-expressed as "an unpromoted surface is absent" over a controlled fixture; the capstone must not assert a product state the product has left.

items.title: institutionalize the #506 date bomb across RCA / pattern / class / template / system-app (learn it once, refuse it mechanically thereafter)
items.milestone: M24 - Enterprise Knowledge Index & Policy Normalization
items.body:
## Why

**#506** was not a one-off. A test fixture pinned a *seed* to `2026-09-14`
(`telemetry/chat/tests/conftest.py:38-40`) while the code under test resolved its *evaluation* bucket
from the live clock, so the green expired with the calendar: 47 passed on 2026-09-14, **2 failed**
every day after, identically at its own closing squash `eae061d`
([#506 comment](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/506#issuecomment-5707073850)).

Two things follow, and they are different pieces of work:

- the **instance** is repaired by threading the turn's own bucket and putting a mutation-proved
  control on the gate of record (PR **#1026**, lane `issue-506`);
- the **class** is not learned anywhere durable yet — that is this issue.
  The seam consolidation it belongs to is **#1025** (11 raw clock reads, 6 duplicate seams).

This issue exists so the next surface cannot re-learn it from a red gate three days later.

## The five artifacts, each in its canonical home

| # | Surface | Home (this repo) | Enforcement | Evidence this lane must produce |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **RCA** | `governance/lessons/` — one `ledger.jsonl` (kinds `incident`/`rca`/`corrective-action`/`lesson`), the writeup at `governance/lessons/rca/RCA-<n>-<slug>.md` copied from `rca-template.md` | the lessons checker (`governance/lessons/checker.py`) plus its own gate | the measured trace: green 2026-09-14 → red since; `2 failed, 45 passed` at `eae061d` and at master; the four record kinds with their typed edges |
| 2 | **pattern** | **new** `docs/PYTHON-PATTERNS.md`, mirroring [`docs/SHELL-PATTERNS.md`](../blob/master/docs/SHELL-PATTERNS.md) (which is shell-scoped, so it is not the home) | **new** `scripts/check-python-patterns.sh` — auto-discovered into `make verify` (#698) — with per-pattern provocation, exactly like `scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` | the refused shape, the good shape, the measured site count, and a plant per pattern that is refused **by name** |
| 3 | **class** | `docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md` — **owned by open lane #883**, so: request, do not edit | `make surface-class` (declared ≠ measured fails **by name**) | a delta request on #883: a surface at or above `enterprise` carries a clock-safety control; `telemetry/chat` is the measured instance |
| 4 | **template** | `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/fleet-task.yml` (+ `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`) — the lane template every future task is shaped by | `scripts/check-issue-template.sh`, `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` | the lane template asks the two questions that would have caught this: *does this work introduce a time-pinned fixture?* and *where is the evaluation bucket resolved?* |
| 5 | **system/app** | `docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md` — the parent-side admission contract (**`module.json` is #883's**, so that half is a request) | `scripts/check-module-admission.sh` | the admitted-surface contract states the invariant, so a surface this repo serves cannot be admitted without it |

## The first pattern entry (the one #506 is an instance of)

`PP-1` — **a fixture that pins a seed but not the evaluation.**

```
# BAD — the seed is pinned, the evaluation is not: the green expires with the calendar
DAY = "2026-09-14"
rail = StaticLedger(calls={(tenant, DAY): 20})     # seeded on the pinned day
runner.run(turn)                                   # evaluates against *today* → 0 usage → allowed

# GOOD — the subject derives its bucket from the entity under test
runner.run(turn)   # guard derives day/month from turn.ts, so the rail it consults is the turn's own
```

The guard for this shape already exists and is mutation-proved: `scripts/check-chat-finops.sh`'s
`turn-date-scope` control (C1/C2/C3) fails **by name** — *"the evaluation bucket is not the turn's
own (#506)"* — when the derivation is removed.

## Non-goals (deliberate)

- **No heuristic scan of the 63 pinned-date test modules.** With that blast radius it would be noisy,
  and a check that cannot fail for the right reason is a formality (GR-12).
- **No seam consolidation here** — that is #1025, and it touches modules this lane does not own.
- **No edits to `docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md` or `module.json`** (open lane #883 owns both): those two
  halves are requests on #883, not edits.

## Verify

```bash
python3 governance/lessons/cli.py check      # or the checker's own entry point — the RCA half
bash scripts/check-python-patterns.sh        # the pattern half, with its own provocation
bash scripts/check-issue-template.sh         # the template half
bash scripts/check-module-admission.sh       # the system/app half
make verify
```

items.title: the money path reads the live clock in 11 places behind 6 duplicate seams, and 63 test modules pin a date literal — so a green can expire with the calendar (#506)
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
## Why this exists

**#506** is the measured instance: its two quota-refusal tests were green on **2026-09-14** (the day
the lane ran) and have been red every day since, because the fixture seeds the quota ledger under
`DAY = "2026-09-14"` while `GuardedTurnRunner.run` pins nothing and the enforcer resolves the bucket
from the live clock. The issue's own `Verify:` reproduces it:

```
$ python3 -m pytest telemetry/chat -q -p no:cacheprovider
FAILED telemetry/chat/tests/test_budget_guard.py::test_a_quota_exhausted_tenant_never_reaches_the_provider
FAILED telemetry/chat/tests/test_negative_controls.py::test_each_refusal_path_refuses_and_still_meters[quota]
2 failed, 45 passed in 2.49s          # reproduced identically at the closing squash eae061d
```

That one is being repaired in-lane (thread the turn's own bucket; a gate control that a past-dated
turn is judged against its own day, mutation-proved). **This issue is the class, not the instance.**

## Measured scope (today's master)

The clock is read directly, on the metering/FinOps path, in **11 places**:

```
$ grep -rnE 'datetime\.now|date\.today|utcnow|time\.time\(\)' --include='*.py' telemetry/ gateway/finops/
telemetry/role_health.py:670:    return time.time()
telemetry/role_health.py:1108:            "generatedAt": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(...)
telemetry/role_health.py:1295:    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(...)
telemetry/observability/model.py:137:    return datetime.now(UTC).strftime(...)
telemetry/observability/dashboard.py:37:    return datetime.now(UTC).strftime(...)
telemetry/metering/model.py:78:    return datetime.now(UTC).strftime(...)
telemetry/ledger/schema.py:73:    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(...)
telemetry/budgets/model.py:129:    return datetime.now(UTC).strftime(...)
telemetry/budgets/chargeback.py:177:    return datetime.now(UTC).strftime(...)
gateway/finops/metering.py:60:        default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
gateway/finops/metering.py:94:        default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
```

and the "seam" that is supposed to abstract it is **duplicated per module** rather than shared:

```
$ grep -rn "def now_utc_iso" --include='*.py' telemetry/
telemetry/observability/model.py:135     telemetry/metering/model.py:76
telemetry/budgets/model.py:142 (today_utc)   telemetry/ledger/schema.py:73
telemetry/role_health.py:1295            telemetry/observability/dashboard.py:37
```

Consequence: **no test can freeze the clock**, so a fixture that wants determinism gets it only for
its *seed*, and the *evaluation* silently uses whatever day it is. And the blast radius is large —
**63** test modules under the declared suite roots carry a pinned ISO date literal:

```
$ grep -rlE '"(19|20)[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}' --include='test_*.py' telemetry/ gateway/ engine/ registry/ identity/ guardrails/ e2e/ integrations/ | wc -l
63
```

## Why it hid for three days

`make verify` runs `pytest-fleet` and a named set of suites; the **manifest** (`scripts/pytest-suites.txt`,
181 entries) is run in full only by `make gate` / `make tests` (`scripts/verify.sh:510-512`).
`telemetry/chat` is declared at line 114 of the manifest and is *not* run by `make verify`, whose
`pytest-chat` check runs `gateway/chat/tests` instead. So a suite carrying an acceptance proof can rot
behind a green composite — the gate that every lane trusts did not run it.

## Proposed shape (a program, deliberately not rushed)

1. **One seam per layer, or one repo-wide `clock` module**, that every timestamp/date read goes
   through — including `gateway/finops` and the `default_factory` fields. Then "freeze the clock" is a
   single patch, and a fixture can pin evaluation as easily as it pins a seed.
2. **A frozen-clock run in the gate**: execute the manifest's date-sensitive suites with the clock
   frozen to a fixed instant *away from today*. A green that depends on "when it runs" then fails in
   the gate instead of expiring in the calendar. The control must itself be date-agnostic (compute its
   instants relative to the pinned clock, never from a literal), or it becomes the next #506.
3. **Refuse new raw clock reads by name** — a check that a planted `datetime.now()` on the money path
   is refused with its file and line, provable both ways.

Deliberately **not** a heuristic static scan for "pinned literal + live clock": with 63 candidate
modules that would be noisy, and a check that cannot fail for the right reason is a formality.

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest telemetry/chat -q -p no:cacheprovider   # the instance (#506)
```

Once the seam and the frozen-clock run exist, the class's own probe is: freeze the clock to a fixed
instant, run the manifest's date-sensitive suites, and require every one to be either green
deterministically or refused by name.

items.title: e2e: prove the #665 FinOps loop's unproven links — the CRM→ERPNext webhook bridge and cache-optimal inference → metered cost
items.body:
## The gap, measured

EPIC #665's thesis is **one chain**: *conversion event → ERPNext ledger → cache-optimal inference → metered, audited cost.* The e2e suite proves the middle of it — `e2e/erp_finops_golden.py` (#675: signup → billing → revenue recognition) — but has **zero** coverage of the two links that make it a *loop*:

```
$ git grep -lIi webhook   origin/master -- 'e2e/**' | wc -l   # 0  <- the CRM->ERPNext bridge (#671)
$ git grep -lIi mcp       origin/master -- 'e2e/**' | wc -l   # 0  <- the MCP response filter (#672)
$ git grep -lIi cache_hit origin/master -- 'e2e/**' | wc -l   # 0  <- cache-efficiency audit (#673)
```

So the bridge that is the epic's own name — *"from CRM hook to ledger"* — is unproven end to end, and the token half (prefix template #670 → cache-hit accounting #673 → metered cost) is unproven. Every child of #665 closed with its **own** `Verify:` green, and the epic still cannot claim its chain: a per-lane suite cannot prove a cross-module loop.

Measured surfaces to consume (all merged, all on `origin/master`):

| Link | Real module | Public API |
|---|---|---|
| bridge | `integrations/erp/webhooks/bridge.py` | `ConversionBridge` |
| bridge disposition | `integrations/erp/webhooks/hooks.py` | `HookDisposition` |
| bridge auth | `integrations/erp/webhooks/auth.py` | `sign`, `verify` |
| bridge flag | `integrations/erp/webhooks/flags.py` | `FLAG_ID`, `DEFAULT_ENABLED`, `is_enabled` |
| prefix template | `gateway/finops/prefix_templates.py` | `canonical_template`, `validate_prefix`, `footprint` |
| cache efficiency | `gateway/finops/cache_audit.py` | `parse_record`, `load_usage`, `audit`, `AuditResult` |
| cache baseline | `gateway/finops/cache_baseline.py` | `ClassRow`, `_extract_cache_tokens` |
| MCP filter | `gateway/mcp/` | `gateway/mcp/model.py`, `grounding.py` |
| cost authority | `telemetry/metering` | `parse_ts`, `RateCardStore`, `MemoryUsageStore` |

## Deliverable

`e2e/finops_loop.py` (probe) + `e2e/tests/test_finops_loop.py`, consuming the **real** merged modules offline, exactly as `e2e/erp_finops_golden.py` does. **`e2e/**` only** (GR-3 — the e2e suite never edits a pillar file); no registration edit needed (`e2e` is already declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` and named by `scripts/verify.sh`).

## Acceptance

1. **The bridge posts a conversion to the ledger.** A real CRM conversion event crosses `ConversionBridge` with its signature verified through `auth.verify`, and the accounting-side document it produces is read back through the module that owns it (never re-derived).
2. **Fail-closed.** With `erp-webhooks-bridge` off (`flags.is_enabled` → False) the bridge refuses and **nothing is posted** — measured, not asserted.
3. **A forged signature is refused** (`auth.verify` raises) and **nothing is posted**.
4. **Token half — cache-optimal.** The same scenario's inference, served with the canonical prefix template (#670), reports a cache-hit share and a metered cost **strictly lower** than the cold equivalent (#673), from a deterministic fixture.
5. **The MCP filter trims before the model sees it** (#672): a verbose tool output is filtered and the post-filter payload is strictly smaller — proven over the real module.
6. **Cost is not re-derived.** Every figure comes from `telemetry/metering`'s rate cards.
7. **Negative controls** exist for each refusal path and **each is mutation-proved by name** (the repo's anti-formality doctrine).
8. **No date bomb.** No wall-clock read; every clock is injected, so every value is a function of the scenario, never of when the suite ran.

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest e2e -q
make verify
```

(`enable_org_chart`, `enable_skill_studio`, `enable_task_board`,

## The gap, measured

The capstone e2e suite proves the **platform** journey (`e2e/golden_path.py`: signup → org → agents →
routed calls → audit → billing) and the **delivery** journey (`e2e/go_live_delivery.py`, issue #955).
Nothing in it proves the **conversational** journey that EPIC #500 / M30 (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
delivered:

```
$ grep -rliE 'telemetry\.chat|gateway\.chat' e2e/ | wc -l
0
```

Zero files. Meanwhile the repo ships four chat suites (`guardrails/chat`, `identity/chat`,
`registry/chat`, `telemetry/chat`), six chat gates (`chat-tools`, `chat-identity`, `chat-finops`,
`chat-guardrails`, `chat-ux`, `chat-eval`) and a whole serving surface (`gateway/chat`, issue #503).
Their per-lane tests exist; the **end-to-end chain does not**, which is exactly how a rotted green
survived: #506's own `Verify:` has been red since 2026-09-15 (a pinned seed evaluated against the live
clock) with `make verify` green, because `make verify`'s `pytest-chat` runs `gateway/chat/tests` and
`telemetry/chat` only runs under `make gate`/`make tests`.

## Deliverable

A new capstone file under the e2e lane's convention — `e2e/tests/test_chat_surface.py` — plus any
helper under `e2e/**`, consuming the **real** merged modules offline, exactly as `e2e/golden_path.py`
does. The e2e suite never edits a pillar file (GR-3); `e2e/**` only.

## Acceptance

1. **Signup → a real turn.** A tenant provisioned through `identity/onboarding` makes one turn built
   from `telemetry/chat/model.py` and run through `GuardedTurnRunner` + `TurnAttributor` over the real
   rails (`telemetry/budgets`), with the served call going through the real gateway/provider rig the
   suite already wires.
2. **Tier discipline.** The tier comes from `telemetry/chat/tiering.resolve_turn_tier`; a
   client-supplied tier is never authoritative.
3. **Exactly one of each.** Every turn produces exactly one attribution record and one metering
   record; a turn with no record fails a test.
4. **The ledger proves it.** The per-tenant chain verifies `OK` after the turn.
5. **Budget guard.** An over-cap tenant is blocked **and still metered** (`billable=False`); a
   kill-switch-on tenant is refused **before** any provider call (zero provider calls).
6. **Cache accounting.** A cache-hit turn reports a cache share and a strictly lower estimated cost
   than the equivalent cold turn, from a deterministic fixture.
7. **Cost is not re-derived.** Every figure comes from `telemetry/metering`'s rate cards.
8. **Negative controls exist for each refusal path** and each is **mutation-proved by name**.
9. **No date bomb.** Any test that pins a seed day/month must pin the *evaluation* bucket too, and at
   least one test must assert that a turn dated in the past is judged against **its own** day — the
   assertion that would have caught #506.

items.title: check-verdict-contains is red on master again — 2 new piped-grep sites (#961, #963) block every lane's make verify
items.body:
**A red that no lane owns blocks every lane.** Measured while landing the #1001 baseline entry, and filed rather than widened into that diff — the two files are other lanes' surfaces.

## Measured (clean detached worktree at `origin/master` = `80913f6`)

```
$ git worktree add --detach /tmp/base origin/master && cd /tmp/base
$ bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-cmr-pin.sh has 1, the record allows 0
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-rbac-head-binding.sh has 1, the record allows 0
        Use a bash-native containment test (see the header) instead.
check-verdict-contains: FAIL (2 finding(s); 9 control(s) passed)      # rc=1
```

Reproduced identically in a pristine worktree — this is not a lane's stale base, and it is not caused by the commit under record in #1001.

`check-verdict-contains` is **auto-discovered** into `make verify` (`scripts/verify.sh` sources `scripts/discover-checks.sh`; the denylist names only `drift`, `negative-controls`, `policy-schema`, `pr-contract`). So `make verify` is red on `master` for every lane, for a cause no lane owns — the same class as #866 (closed), recurring.

## The two sites

| site | introduced by |
|---|---|
| `scripts/check-cmr-pin.sh:124` — `if ! printf '%s' "$nc_out" \| grep -q "CMR-PIN-DRIFT"; then` | `1b2dd08d` (#961) |
| `scripts/check-rbac-head-binding.sh:152` — `if ! printf '%s\n' "$probe_out" \| grep -q '^PROBE_RESULT=OK$'; then` | `bb0236ac` (#963) |

Both are the **negated** shape the check exists to catch: `grep -q` exits on its first match, the producer is then SIGPIPE-killed, and `set -o pipefail` promotes the 141 to the whole pipeline — so a report larger than the 64 KiB pipe buffer reports the needle ABSENT when it is present. In this polarity that inverts a verdict test: the control reports "not refused by name" for output that names the refusal.

## Why it cannot be recorded away

The record (`scripts/verdict-contains-legacy.tsv`) is a **shrink-only ratchet** — neither file has a row, and `--record` refuses to raise it by design (#931: "`--record` refuses to grow"). So the only terminal state is replacing each piped test with a bash-native containment test (`case "$x" in *needle*) ...`) in the two owning files.

## Expected

```
$ bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh    # rc=0
... (9 control(s); N legacy site(s) ... remain recorded)
```

**Verify:** `bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh` rc 0 in a clean detached worktree at `master`; reverting either file's containment test re-reds it by name.

## Notes

- Filed, not fixed: neither file is in this session's lane (#1001 touches only `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json`).
- Related: #866 (same class, closed), #931 (a different defect in the same check — an **under-counting** coverage gap, explicitly "not a red on master").

items.title: lifecycle close-out verifies the frozen lane head, so an already-merged item can owe VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING forever (#955)
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
## What is broken

`governance/lifecycle` close-out step 2 (`record-verification`) re-runs the gate **inside the lane
worktree, at the lane's branch head**, and asserts that head is the verified commit. When a lane's
PR is already merged and the branch head predates a sibling commit that landed *before* the squash,
the branch head can be **permanently red for a reason the merged tree does not contain** — so the
item can never record a green verification and `reclaim-lane` refuses forever.

Measured on **#955** (`e2e: the go-live delivery capstone`, PR #964). Open finding: **#992**.

## The measurement

| | |
|---|---|
| lane | `dd8d119dbc42`, branch `issue-955`, head `4ed3fc058f59aca15a16aa59e6022e3857d7acc1` |
| PR #964 | merged, squash `494ff91166599a1205300ad9a440745688274b81`, **parent `72dca6c`** |
| close-out | 7 attempts over ~2 h, every one: `close-out #955: NOT-OK ... REMAINS VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING #955` |
| lane attestation at `4ed3fc0` | `FAIL`, 142 checks, **1 failure: `e2e`** |
| `e2e` at the lane head | **3 failed, 53 passed** — all 3 in `e2e/tests/test_go_live_delivery.py`, asserting `go-live-plan.yaml does not declare 'surfaces.fleet_projection'`; `grep -c surfaces.fleet_projection` at `4ed3fc0` → **0** |
| `e2e` at the merged commit `494ff91` | **11 passed, rc=0** |

Timeline, which explains the asymmetry:

- `72dca6c` (issue #959) lands the missing declaration on master at **16:16:48**;
- the lane head `4ed3fc0` is committed at **16:18:30** — it does **not** contain it;
- the squash `494ff91` is composed at **16:19:38** with `72dca6c` as its parent — the **merged**
  tree *does* contain it, and the squash's own diff never touched the plan.

Seven consecutive attempts over ~2 hours refused identically, so **re-running cannot converge**.
This is neither flakiness nor contention: the same target measured across 12 concurrent lanes
passed in 11 of 12 when it passed at all, and failed **deterministically** at `4ed3fc0`, while the
merged commit passes in a throwaway detached worktree that was removed afterwards.

Status today: **7 of the 8 close-out stages are terminal** (`merge-pull-request`,
`delete-branch`, `consume-directive`, `release-claim`, `record-closing-evidence`, `close-issue`
all `skipped: already satisfied`), and only `reclaim-lane` is `refused`/`withheld` — correctly, per
#786, because reclaiming would destroy the worktree the attestation is measured from.

## Why this is a gap in the tool, not a lane's fault

The invariant's real question is "did the change that landed reach a green gate?" For an item whose
PR is already merged, the change that landed is the **merge commit's tree** — and that tree is green
on exactly the check the frozen branch head fails. #786 already established the sibling principle
for a lane that is *gone*: "a lane already torn down is recovered by re-measuring the **verified
head commit** in a throwaway worktree, never by declaring the evidence missing". The same reasoning
should cover an *already-merged* PR whose branch head cannot be made green.

## Suggested shape (not prescriptive)

- In `record_verification`, when the PR is already merged, measure the **merge commit** (or
  whichever tree the item's own journal names as verified) rather than the frozen branch head, and
  **say which tree was measured** in the stage's output.
- Keep the refusal honest: if no available tree is green, `VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING` must still
  stand — this must not become a way to launder a red lane.
- Make persistent un-closability visible: an item that has exhausted its retry budget should read
  as stuck, not as "retry pending".

## Impact

The lane cannot be reclaimed, so its worktree is kept indefinitely (correct, but it is dead weight
on a box that already carried 88 worktrees), and open issue **#992** cannot be closed — closing it
would claim a verification that does not exist.

_AI-assistance: Copilot (qa-sme)._

items.title: squash-merge keeps dropping ticket trailers — master red on check-isolation-landed for the third time today (#960/#976, then #996/#991)
items.body:
**Pattern:** every few hours master goes red on `check-isolation-landed` because a `gh pr merge --squash` from some fleet session produced a squash commit whose message has the ticket ref only in the subject `(#N)` and no trailing trailer paragraph. Today: 7d5f6a1a (#960), f7a7a12c (#976) → fixed by #983/#986; then b3d7144e (#996) and b85cae42 (#991) → red again as of 2026-09-16 23:30Z. Each recurrence blocks every open PR's `make verify` until someone lands a baseline-entry PR, which is the doctrine (#836) but not a fix.

**Root cause:** the squash message is built from the PR title/body, not from the branch commits' trailer blocks, and nothing refuses the merge when the resulting message would violate the gate.

**Fix (systemic, pick one — recommend 1+2):**
1. `.github/pull_request_template.md` (or `governance/lifecycle` PR-create path) puts the trailer block in every PR body by default, and `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --pr N` becomes a required pre-merge step in the merge playbook (`docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md`) and in `governance/lifecycle/cli.py close`'s merge path.
2. A `scripts/check-squash-message.sh` that, given a PR number, renders the squash message gh would produce (`gh pr view N --json title,body`) and runs the same trailer predicate as `check-isolation-landed`; the fleet's merge path calls it and refuses on FAIL.
3. Alternatively switch the repo's merge method to merge-commit with `--body` from the branch head's message (loses the one-commit-per-PR property; not recommended).

**Immediate:** record b3d7144e03d9 and b85cae429ea8 in `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` (same shape as #983) to unblock the queue.

Refs #836, #897, #982, #985. Parent: #878 lane L3 (#882 atomic-commit gates).

items.title: landing path merges PRs without the trailing ticket trailer, so every trailer-less squash re-reds isolation-landed — enforce at merge, not after
items.body:
Parent: #607. Measured across this session — a systemic recurrence, not individual slips.

## The recurrence

Four squash merges landed today **without** the trailing `Refs` trailer, and each re-reds `isolation-landed` the moment it merges:

| commit | lane | red |
|---|---|---|
| `7d5f6a1` | #960 (docs index rule) | `commit-missing-ticket-trailer` → recorded #974 |
| `f7a7a12` | #976 (ERP webhook bridge) | recorded #985 |
| `b85cae4` | #946 (ao-images AR repo) | unrecorded |
| `b3d7144` | #946 (immutable tags) | unrecorded |

The designed terminal state for each is a baseline entry (history is never rewritten) — and each entry is a 2-line reviewed commit. At this rate the baseline grows by hand while the cause is untouched.

## The root cause

Two independent gaps; the first is positional, the second is that **the checked artifact is not the landed artifact**.

**(a) It is not a merge precondition.** `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --pr <n>` audits the **PR body** (trailer, `AI-assistance:`, `Closes`, pre-existing-red), but the landing path never runs it as a precondition: a `PUT /pulls/<n>/merge` (the `make land` / `gh pr merge --squash` path) merges the PR anyway. Measured — PRs **#991** and **#996** merge today even though the contract refuses them (`--pr 991` → rc 1, `--pr 996` → rc 1: no trailer, no `Closes`). The gate that would have refused them (the landed-history one) fires only after the fact.

**(b) The contract audits the wrong artifact.** `GET /repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator` reports `squash_merge_commit_message = COMMIT_MESSAGES`, so a squash merge composes the landed commit body from the **branch commit messages**, not the PR body. Proven: PR #994's body opens `## What`, while its landed commit `039d96b` opens with the commit subject and a rewritten body. So the PR body is *not* what lands — a PR whose body is contract-perfect still lands trailer-less if its **commit message** lacks the trailer, and the predicate the landed-history gate actually consumes is the one on the commit (`check-pr-contract.sh --landed --range HEAD^..HEAD`).

Net effect: the trailer the landed-history gate demands is produced or not **by lane luck** — two artifacts, two checks, neither one a precondition on the thing that lands.

## Required

- The landing path runs the contract as a **merge precondition** — and points it at **the artifact that lands**. Because the setting is `COMMIT_MESSAGES`, that means validating the commits to be squashed (`check-pr-contract.sh --landed --range <base>..<head>`) and/or passing an explicit trailer-bearing squash message (`gh pr merge --squash --subject <t> --body-file <f>`). Checking the PR body alone cannot close this: the body is not what lands.
- A provocation covering **both** artifacts, because either alone is passable:
  1. a branch whose **commit message** lacks the trailer must be refused at merge time **by name**, *even when its PR body carries one* (today the body-only check passes it);
  2. a trailer-less PR body must be refused at merge time **by name**, never merged and then red.

**Verify:** both provoked shapes above are refused by the landing path by name; and `isolation-landed` stops accumulating new unrecorded entries.

A lifecycle finding has not reached a terminal state.

- item: #955

items.title: master is red at 117d312: docs-lint, git-config, isolation-landed — all three attributed, none from the e2e wave
items.body:
Parent: #607

Measured on a clean worktree at `origin/master` **`117d312e3513`** (post-merge composite gate, `make verify`):
`verify: FAIL (3 of 145 checks failed, 5 skipped)`, attestation `result=FAIL git_sha=117d312e3513`.

**Attribution first: none of the three is from the e2e wave (#954 `72dca6c`, #955 `494ff91), which touched only `infra/rollout/*.yaml` and `e2e/*`.** Each is named with its introducing commit; all three landed after the last green post-merge gate (`8cfd1ea`, 138/142 PASS).

## 1. `docs-lint` — two tracked docs are not indexed

```
FAIL  docs/FLEET-CUTOVER.md (tracked doc not indexed in docs/README.md)
FAIL  docs/GIT-ENV-VARIABLES.md (tracked doc not indexed in docs/README.md)
```

Introduced by `9719221` (#907, the D7 cutover runbook) and `14dac6a` (#957, the canonical git/env variable registry). The **rule** is new — `7d5f6a1` (#960, "enforce docs/*.md index completeness in check-docs.sh"), which landed after both docs, so the rule arrived and immediately found two pre-existing docs it made non-compliant. Either index them in `docs/README.md` or exempt them by name with a reason.

## 2. `git-config` — needs a one-time per-checkout bootstrap

```
FAIL  commit.template is unset
check-git-config: FAIL — 3 problem(s); git-config boilerplate is not governed
```

Introduced by `532007a` (#958, "ship .gitattributes and the commit.template bootstrap gate"). The gate ships its own fix — `bash scripts/check-git-config.sh --bootstrap` sets `commit.template` to `.gitmessage` — but **nothing runs it**, so a fresh checkout (and this box, in every worktree) is red until a human runs it.

The other 2 of the 3 problems in that run were **the measuring worktree's own**: they were created with a plain `git worktree add`, which — unlike `governance/isolation/cli.py open` — stamps no `--worktree` identity. Measured: after `git config --worktree user.name/user.email`, only `commit.template` remained. That is worth knowing on its own: **the gate turns `make verify` red in any ad-hoc verification worktree**, which is how most lanes drive it.

## 3. `isolation-landed` — a landed commit without the trailing ticket trailer

```
FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:7d5f6a1a400d is not recorded legacy — if the commit has not MERGED yet, put the reference in …
isolation-enforce: NOT-OK — 1 unrecorded and 0 stale baseline entr(ies) in HEAD
check-isolation-landed: FAIL (1 violation(s))
```

`7d5f6a1` is **#960's own commit** — the lane that added the docs-index rule landed without the trailer the repo's rule 15 requires, and the gate that enforces that rule caught it. It has merged, so it cannot be amended (history rewrite is forbidden); the honest resolutions are a baseline entry if the quarantine permits one for a commit this recent, or an explicit, reasoned acceptance. **Do not rewrite history to fix this.**

## Acceptance

- `make verify` returns `verify: PASS` on `master` with all three addressed *and* the reason recorded for each.
- The `git-config` bootstrap is either run by the checkout path (a `make` target / documented one-liner in `README.md`) or the gate reports an unbootstrapped checkout as a **named** state rather than as three undifferentiated failures.
- The ad-hoc-worktree consequence is decided: either `check-git-config.sh` accepts a worktree with no own-config identity (reporting it as such), or the isolation doctrine is stated as a precondition of running `make verify` anywhere.

**Verify:**
```bash
git worktree add --detach /tmp/redcheck origin/master && cd /tmp/redcheck
bash scripts/check-docs.sh        # the two unindexed docs
bash scripts/check-git-config.sh  # commit.template
bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh 2>/dev/null || bash scripts/check-session-isolation.sh
```

items.title: load_fleet_console() puts <repo>/fleet on sys.path, shadowing the telemetry package (latent ModuleNotFoundError)
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
Found by the e2e lane (#955) while building the delivery probe; latent for the running server today, not yet live.

## Measured

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'telemetry.metering'; 'telemetry' is not a package
```

`portal/server/fleet.py::load_fleet_console()` inserts `<repo>/fleet` on `sys.path`, so the plain module `fleet/telemetry.py` shadows the `telemetry` **package** that ships `telemetry.metering`. Building the portal app *after* the console has been loaded then raises on the next lazy `telemetry.*` import.

It is latent today only because no reachable lazy `telemetry.*` import exists in the server path (`grep -rn 'import telemetry' portal/` → two test files only) — so the shadowing is a trap armed for the next import, not a live break. The same shadowing hazard is documented in `e2e/_paths.py`, which deliberately keeps `telemetry/` out of its top-level roots for exactly this reason.

## Acceptance

- The console load does not put a directory on `sys.path` that can shadow a shipped package (import the console module by a path-safe mechanism instead of a bare `sys.path` insert), or
- the collision is asserted against — a check that fails if any `sys.path` entry introduced at runtime can shadow a top-level package under the repo root.

**Verify:** build the portal app after `load_fleet_console()` and exercise a `telemetry.metering` import; it must resolve to the package, not to `fleet/telemetry.py`.

items.title: nothing projects a promotion's live state into the registry declaration the portal reads — the last manual step
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
Disclosed by the e2e lane (#955, PR #964) as an explicit derivation rather than an existing API — worth deciding, because it is the last manual step between a promotion and a served surface.

## Measured

```
$ grep -rn 'live-state\|live_state' --include='*.py' portal/ | head
(no projection of the rollout's live state into the registry the portal reads)
```

The go-live driver records a promotion in `infra/rollout/live-state.yaml`. The portal decides whether `/api/fleet/*` answers from `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml`'s `surfaces.<name>.default` (plus the `.rollout/surface-state.json` rollback overlay). **Nothing in the repo turns the first into the second**: after the ladder promotes a flag, a human still has to edit the registry declaration by hand for the surface to serve.

That is the same class of gap #954 closed for the *plan*: the machine declares the promotion but the delivery step is manual. The e2e (#955) bridged it inside the test with a one-value `project_registry()` edit, precedent-backed by `scripts/portal-dev-session.py` and `e2e/erp/golden_path.py` — honest, but a derivation.

## Why it matters

It is the difference between "the ordered run promotes the flag" and "the promoted flag actually reaches a client". Today a completed owner-approved go-live can leave the surface dark until someone remembers to edit the registry — which is exactly the failure EPIC #607 was about.

## Acceptance

- Either a declared mechanism projects the rollout's live state into the surface declaration (the apply pipeline, a flag-sync step, or an explicit "the IaC edit IS the projection" with the reviewed PR as the audit record), or
- the manual step is named as the projection and gated — so a promotion that has not been projected is detectable rather than assumed.

**Verify:** after a sandboxed promotion, either the served surface reflects it with no hand edit, or a check reports the promotion as unprojected by name.

items.title: rollout-state declares flags no plan phase reaches, and check_rollout only enforces the reverse direction
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
Found while landing #954 (worktree `ao-954-3ee98360`); the same defect class as #954 and #935, one level up.

## Measured on `master`

```
$ grep -n 'erp_module' infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml
  services.erp_module:      (a drivable row)
  surfaces.erp_module:      (a drivable row)
$ grep -n 'erp_module' infra/rollout/go-live-plan.yaml
(no output)
```

Both flags are declared and promotable by the engine, but **named by no phase of the ordered plan** — so the ladder can never reach them, exactly as `surfaces.fleet_projection` could not before #954.

## The more important half: no gate can see this

`check_rollout.py::check_go_live_plan` validates **plan-flags ⊆ state-flags** (every flag the plan names must resolve in the rollout state). It never checks the **reverse** — that every drivable flag is reached by some phase. So:

- a flag can be declared and drivable and **permanently unreachable**, and
- the only symptom is an operator noticing that a go-live run never mentions it.

That asymmetry is why #954 and #935 both went unnoticed: the gate is one-directional, and the direction it does not check is the one that decides whether a surface can ever ship.

## Acceptance

- Every flag in `infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml` is named by exactly one phase (or carries an explicit, reasoned exemption — e.g. a flag deliberately not go-liveable yet), and the decision is recorded in the file itself.
- `check_rollout.py` gains the reverse-direction check with a **negative probe** in its `--self-test` (the established 11-probe pattern): plant a drivable flag that no phase names, and require the refusal **by name**.
- The probe must distinguish "declared but not planned" from "planned but not declared" — the two failures have different meanings and different fixes.

**Verify:**
```bash
python3 infra/rollout/checks/check_rollout.py --self-test   # the new probe is refused by name
python3 infra/rollout/checks/check_rollout.py               # rc 0 with the current state
# and the mutant: add a flag to rollout-state.yaml only, require rc 1 naming it
```

items.title: Landing driver: a gate PARK (rc 10/11/12) is refused as a red contract, so a green lane cannot land while the cap is full
items.body:
# A gate PARK is refused as a red contract, so a green lane cannot land while the cap is full

## Finding

`governance/landing` converts a **PARK** at the gate of record (admission `rc 10/11/12`) into a
terminal `NOT-OK` refusal, so a lane that is green and clean cannot land at all while the box-wide
permit cap is held. A PARK is a *capacity* condition — `scripts/verify.sh` says so in its own words:

> `verify: PARKED (rc 11, not a pass and not a failure) — the box-wide gate cap is reached; nothing
> was run and no attestation was touched`

and the tell is that the lane's `.verify/verify.log` keeps its previous mtime. It must be
CANNOT-ASSESS-and-retry, never a refusal — the same tri-state discipline `governance/lifecycle/gate.py`
already applies on the close-out path (#840).

Measured by the operator while landing the EPIC #708 children — **six refusals of #728 in a row, five
of them `rc=11`**, with 4–5 sibling gates running for ~1.5 h against `AO_GATE_MAX_CONCURRENT=4`
(quoted from #854, where it was recorded):

```
contract          failed      CANNOT-ASSESS      verify         rc=11
attribution: signal-red-is-not-attributable — the contract is red on signal(s) verify, tests —
  only 'tests' can be attributed to clean master, and the gate of record is never one of them
landing: REFUSED (pre-merge-contract-failed) — ... a red (or unassessable) contract never merges
```

## Mechanism — pinned to the code at `3db5e60` (measured by me, static)

* `governance/landing/engine.py:537-553` — on `contract.rc != 0` the engine consults `_attribute()`;
  when the red is not attributable it sets `refusal_code = "pre-merge-contract-failed"` and
  `result.rc = _normalise_rc(contract.rc)`, i.e. **a refusal for a run that never happened**.
* `governance/landing/attribution.py:609` (and its docstring at `:54`) — "the `tests` signal must be
  the **only** red one (a red `verify` is never attributed)". Correct for a real red, wrong for a
  PARK, where the lane was never assessed.
* **The admission vocabulary is not imported anywhere in `governance/landing/`:**

  ```
  grep -rn "lifecycle.gate\|gatelock\|EXIT_PARKED" governance/landing/*.py   # -> empty
  ```

  so the module has no way to tell a PARK from a red. The seam to reuse already exists:
  `governance/lifecycle/gate.py:76` imports `EXIT_PARKED`/`EXIT_REFUSED`/`EXIT_STORE_UNUSABLE` **from
  their owner** `fleet/gatelock.py` rather than restating them.

## What is NOT the fix

Raising `AO_GATE_MAX_CONCURRENT`. That bound is the remedy for the gate stampede (#724); the cap is
working as designed, and raising it would trade a refusal for a stampede.

## Proposed fix

Treat `rc 10/11/12` from the contract's `verify` signal as **CANNOT-ASSESS-and-retry** (bounded
backoff, exponential, with a terminal dead-letter per GR-18), while any 0/1 verdict keeps today's
strict path — a real red must still never be retried into a merge.

## Verify

Provoke a PARK (real cap, real lane) and show the landing driver **retries instead of refusing**; and
provoke a genuine red (`rc 1`) and show it is **still refused by name** (`pre-merge-contract-failed`).
Both halves, with the exact command and its real output. There is a diagnostic tip from the original
measurement: do **not** infer the permit pool from `ls /tmp/agent-orchestrator-gates/permits | wc -l`
— those are 0-byte flock targets and read as "held" even when the pool is free; the honest probe is a
real acquire/release on a scratch worktree.

## Relations

* Found while closing **#854** (the close-out half, which is **refuted** on `3db5e60` — #786 gates the
  reclaim on the owed attestation; measured with an independent driver and reported on #854).
* Same root gap as #786/#854 (a PARK converted into a terminal signal), **different code path and
  different module** — #786 does not fix this one.
* `governance/lifecycle/gate.py:76` is the existing precedent for the vocabulary seam.
* Origin of the driver: #764.

## Owner

`governance/landing/**` — explicitly **not** the close-out lane's file set, which is why this is filed
rather than fixed there.
