items.title: e2e: the go-live delivery capstone — promotion → live state → a served SPoG (EPIC #607)
items.body:
Parent: #607. The capstone end-to-end proof for the go-live path — the leg `e2e/` does not have.

## Why it is missing

```
$ grep -rln 'go_live\|go-live' --include='*.sh' --include='*.py' scripts/ e2e/
(no output)
$ grep -rln 'infra.rollout' e2e/
(no output)
```

`e2e/` proves the EPIC-00 DoD (signup → org → personas → agents → routed calls → audit + billing) and `e2e/workbook11_portal.py` proves the portal surfaces ship OFF and are invisible unauthorised. `infra/rollout/` has its own unit suite. **Nothing runs the two halves in sequence**, so nothing proves that *the go-live the epic describes actually delivers a surface a client can read* — which is exactly the claim EPIC #607 makes.

This is not hypothetical: writing this e2e is what surfaced the sibling defect in the promotion registration (the flag the portal reads is not in the ladder).

## Deliverable

`e2e/go_live_delivery.py` (the probe) + `e2e/tests/test_go_live_delivery.py` (the suite) — offline, deterministic, no network and no ports required, consuming the **real** modules read-only (`infra.rollout`, `portal.server`), in the established `e2e/` style (probe module + thin asserting suite; see `e2e/workbook11_portal.py` / `e2e/tests/test_workbook11_portal_surfaces.py`).

The path, stage by stage — each stage consumed through the real API, all state written to a **sandbox copy** of the declaration directory (never the repo tree):

| Stage | Real module | What must be proven |
|---|---|---|
| `declared` | `infra/rollout/cli.py validate`, `go_live.py --preflight` | the run is ordered and lawful (rc 0) and *names* the owner-gated transitions |
| `refused` | `go_live.py` with no approvals | rc 1, **nothing written** (sandbox tree byte-identical before/after) |
| `promoted` | `RolloutEngine` / the driver over the plan | every planned flag reaches its `go_live_stage`; `live-state.yaml` records each with a real `audit_record` file that exists, and the hash-chained log verifies |
| `served` | `portal.server.app.build_app` | with the promoted state, an **authenticated** client gets `200` from `/api/fleet/snapshot` carrying a real projection (rungs/lanes), while an unauthenticated one gets `401` |
| `dark` | same app, promoted state reverted | `/api/fleet/snapshot` is `404 feature_disabled` — an unpromoted surface is absent, not merely unauthorised |
| `rolled-back` | `cli rollback` | a rollback returns the surface to dark without a commit |

## Negative controls (no-false-green, `e2e/negative_controls.py` doctrine)

Each guard must be shown to **genuinely block** when provoked, or the check fails:

- a `full` transition carrying a *policy* approval (not human) → refused;
- an approval whose approver **is** the executing actor → refused;
- a `live-state.yaml` entry whose `audit_record` does not exist → refused;
- a phase-7 flag before phases 1-6 → refused, naming the blocking flag;
- the surface served while its flag is off → the probe must detect that as a failure, not pass.

## Sequencing — read this

This test is **RED until the sibling fix that registers `surfaces.fleet_projection` in the rollout machinery lands**. That red is the point: it is the evidence that the test is load-bearing rather than decorative. Land it that way if necessary, then rebase and re-gate — do **not** weaken the assertion to make it green.

## Verify

```bash
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q e2e/tests/test_go_live_delivery.py
bash scripts/check-python-syntax.sh && bash scripts/check-docs.sh
```

`e2e/tests` is already the capstone suite wired into `make verify` (`scripts/verify.sh:408`), so a new file under `e2e/tests` is covered with no wiring change — and must not need one.

items.title: the go-live ladder cannot promote surfaces.fleet_projection — the SPoG the epic delivers is unreachable by the declared path
items.body:
Parent: #607. Measured on `master` `3db5e60`. Found while scoping the end-to-end proof for this epic, and it is the reason the epic's third acceptance criterion is **unreachable by the declared path**.

## The defect

The flag that gates the entire Single-Pane-of-Glass is `surfaces.fleet_projection`:

```
$ grep -n 'FLEET_SURFACE\|fleet_projection' portal/server/fleet.py
38:FLEET_SURFACE = "fleet_projection"
119:    surface: str = FLEET_SURFACE,
$ grep -n 'fleet_projection' infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml infra/rollout/go-live-plan.yaml
(no output)
```

So `/api/fleet/*` is served **only** when `surfaces.fleet_projection` is promoted — and that flag is **not declared in the rollout machinery at all**. `infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml` carries 20 flags; the only `surfaces.*` among them are `surfaces.operator_terminal` and `surfaces.erp_module`. `infra/rollout/go-live-plan.yaml` phase 7 names six flags, none of them this one.

The consequences are mechanical, not a matter of judgement:

1. `go_live.py` walks the plan — it cannot promote a flag the plan does not name.
2. `RolloutEngine.promote` refuses a flag not in the rollout state by name
   (`unknown flag '<name>' (not declared in rollout state)`), and
   `check_rollout.py::check_registry_parity` refuses a rollout flag with no registry surface.

Net effect: **a completed, owner-approved go-live run through phase 7 still leaves `ai.purebliss.app/api/fleet/*` at `404 feature_disabled`.** The epic's AC 3 ("ai.purebliss.app serves the fleet single-pane-of-glass") cannot be met by the declared path — only by a hand-edit of the registry, which is precisely what the rollout machinery exists to replace.

## The registry already declares the intended promotion

`infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml` (the `operator_terminal` entry, lines ~527-530), verbatim:

> Promotion = a reviewed go-live that flips this flag (**and independently promotes `fleet_projection` and `remote_control` for the two halves it composes**), runs `make verify` + `terraform plan`, then applies via the deployer SA.

The declaration names the promotion; the machine does not carry it. Same class as #935 (`surfaces.edge_cutover` never registered).

## Required

Register the surfaces the go-live must actually deliver, at least:

- `surfaces.fleet_projection` — the read half of the SPoG (and of the AgentConsole, which composes it).
- `surfaces.remote_control` — the write half, per the same registry sentence.

The three-file registration (see #935 for the mechanics): a `surfaces:` row already exists in the registry for both — so this is the **rollout** half only:
1. `infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml` — a drivable row at `stage: "off"`, `rollout_pct: 0`, `targeted: []`.
2. `infra/rollout/go-live-plan.yaml` — the intent row in the phase that delivers the portal (phase 7), with the reason the plan must resolve every flag it names.
3. Confirm `check_rollout.py` parity holds (registry surface ↔ rollout flag) and `go_live.py --preflight` names it.

## Verify

```bash
python3 infra/rollout/checks/check_rollout.py            # rc 0
python3 infra/rollout/checks/check_rollout.py --self-test # rc 0
python3 infra/rollout/go_live.py --preflight             # rc 0, and names surfaces.fleet_projection
grep -n 'fleet_projection\|remote_control' infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml infra/rollout/go-live-plan.yaml
```

## Non-goals

Do not flip any default and do not promote anything: this makes the flag **reachable by the ladder**, it does not walk the ladder. `default_policy: off` and the all-`off` rollout state must both survive this change.

items.title: gate-lock: a zero-byte owner-less worktree lock blocks lifecycle reclaim while gate-lock reports the worktree free
items.body:
A **zero-byte, owner-less lock file** in the gate-lock worktree store silently blocks the lane close-out
forever, while `gate-lock` itself reports the same worktree as **free**. The two components disagree
about what "held" means, and the disagreement is invisible from `gate-lock status`.

## Measured (2026-09-16, lane for #619)

```
$ bash scripts/gate-lock.sh status            # no slot names that worktree; 4/4 held by OTHER worktrees
$ pgrep -af 'ao-619-d82ba7a9'                 # (no live process)
$ ls -la …/agent-orchestrator-gates/worktrees/6ef3c6ac9102d0d5.lock
-rw-r--r-- 1 akushnir akushnir 0 Sep 16 15:47 …/6ef3c6ac9102d0d5.lock        # zero bytes, owner-less

$ bash scripts/gate-lock.sh release --worktree /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-619-d82ba7a9
gate-lock: RELEASED worktree=… (already free)          rc=0
$ ls …/6ef3c6ac9102d0d5.lock
…/6ef3c6ac9102d0d5.lock                                 # the FILE survives "RELEASED … (already free)"
```

`governance/lifecycle/cli.py close` reads that surviving file as a live gate and refuses to reclaim the
lane (rc 10):

```
refused/WITHHELD  reclaim-lane: the item still owes record-verification (parked: verify: PARKED
  (rc 10, not a pass and not a failure) — another gate already holds this worktree; nothing was run
  and no attestation was touched) — reclaiming the lane would remove the worktree that attestation
  is measured from, permanently, so the lane is kept …
UNASSESSED        record-verification
UNASSESSED        VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING  #619
```

Two close-out attempts in a row failed this way. Deleting only the zero-byte file — nothing else
changed — turned the very next attempt green:

```
$ rm -f …/6ef3c6ac9102d0d5.lock
$ python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --issue 619 …
close-out #619: OK          rc=0
  performed  record-verification: verify green at 5aa2023aa4f5
```

(For reference, the naming is deterministic: the lock is `sha256(<worktree path>)[:16].lock` —
calibrated against the pair recorded in a gate log, `ao-731-13ad43c6 → b2246eb2bef671b0.lock`.)

## Why it matters

- A lane whose close-out is blocked this way **cannot ever be reclaimed by automation**; it needs a
  human who knows to look at a directory that `gate-lock status` never prints.
- It is the same class as #943: a control that blocks (or doesn't assess) for a reason it cannot
  name, in a system whose whole doctrine is "no false green, no false red, and CANNOT-ASSESS is not
  a pass".
- The store accumulates: 115 lock files were present, the oldest from 2026-09-15, with no reaper
  visible in `gate-lock`'s interface.

## Acceptance

- `gate-lock release` removes the worktree lock file when it reports "(already free)" — the file and
  the verdict must agree.
- `gate-lock status` names stale locks (a lock file with no live owner) rather than omitting them,
  so a blocked lane is diagnosable from one command.
- `lifecycle close` distinguishes "a live gate holds this worktree" from "a stale lock file exists",
  and reports the second as a stale lock to clear — not as an unassessable verification.

**Verify:** create a zero-byte `<sha256(worktree)[:16]>.lock`, run `gate-lock status` and
`gate-lock release --worktree <path>`, and assert the file is gone and status named it.

items.title: EPIC #607 residual: the owner-executed go-live (GCP + approval codes + run-half cutover)
items.body:
Parent: #607. Successor to #619 and #731, whose residual owner-executed work their merge keyword closed out.

`#732` is genuinely done and closed. `#731` (edge cutover) and `#619` (go-live run) were closed by their PRs' `Closes #…` keyword; both were reopened with the evidence below and then **re-closed by `governance/lifecycle/cli.py close`**, whose model is "the change landed and the verification is green" — it does not model an acceptance criterion that no repository change can satisfy. Rather than fight the close-out, the residual work is tracked here.

## The residual, exactly

1. **GCP project + deployer-SA credentials.** Nothing in this repository can supply them. The apply route is `infra/cloudbuild/apply.yaml` as the deployer SA (GR-5: no ad-hoc apply, no console).
2. **Build the web image** (`infra/cloudbuild/web-image.yaml` refuses a missing or `latest` tag):
   `gcloud builds submit --config=infra/cloudbuild/web-image.yaml --substitutions=_AR_REPO=…,_IMAGE=portal,_TAG=$COMMIT_SHA .`
   Until then `web_image_tag` stays at its 40-zero "nothing promoted" sentinel.
3. **Grant the owner's approval codes**, then run the ordered driver — `python3 infra/rollout/go_live.py --preflight` is **rc 0** today and names **16** planned transitions that need a code; `--require-approvals` is **rc 1** until they exist. A real run is a **two-invocation** operation by construction (the declared 24 h `gradual` dwell).
4. **Import the apply trigger** (`disabled: false`, `_ENABLE_APPLY: "true"`) and push to `master`.
5. **Run half**: wire DNS + the Cloudflare tunnel ingress rule for `ai.purebliss.app` to the new service (`192.168.168.42:<port>`), the way `os.purebliss.app` was — the decision and its steps are declared in `docs/EDGE-CUTOVER.md`.

## Acceptance

- `grep -E 'stage: "full"' infra/rollout/live-state.yaml` names the promoted flags (not `rollout-state.yaml` — post-#914 that file must stay all-`off`; #619's original acceptance grep is unsatisfiable and is corrected in `infra/rollout/GO-LIVE-RUNBOOK.md`).
- `grep -E '_ENABLE_APPLY' infra/cloudbuild/apply-trigger.yaml` reads `"true"`.
- `curl -sS https://ai.purebliss.app/api/fleet/snapshot` returns fleet JSON from an authenticated session — not today's `Found. Redirecting to /auth/login` (302, 33 bytes).
- `dig +short ai.purebliss.app` recorded at that point.

**Do not close this on a merge.** It closes when the live `Verify` above passes.

items.title: no system/app (addon) structure here — declare the exemption and how the SPoG is mounted by the OS
items.body:
There is **no `system/app/` (or `addons/`, or `apps/`) structure in this repo** and no `category: "system"` app declaration anywhere outside `vendor/` and `.research/`.

## Measured (master `8cfd1ea`)

```
$ find . -maxdepth 2 -type d \( -name addons -o -name apps \) | grep -v vendor
(no output)

$ grep -rn 'category: *"system"\|"category": *"system"' --include=*.json --include=*.yaml . | grep -v vendor | grep -v .research
(no output)
```

`module.json` declares this repo as **`type: service`**, `class: [backend, service, saas, control-plane]` — i.e. a service module, not an OS-app/addon host. The OS app model (`addons/<id>`, `category: "system"` apps, the à-la-carte OS functions) belongs to the **OS portal host** repo, so its absence here is very likely *correct by design*.

## Why it is still worth an issue

Nothing **declares** that exemption. A reader (or an agent) asked "where is the system-app structure?" gets the same empty result for "by design" and for "forgotten" — there is no statement of which repo owns the app model, and no statement of how the surface this epic is about (`ai.purebliss.app`'s fleet SPoG) becomes reachable **as a system app** in the OS rather than only as a URL.

That last part is the real question this epic raises: the SPoG is now documented, locally reproducible and class-declared as a *portal* surface, but whether it appears as an OS system app — and who registers it — is unstated.

## Acceptance

- A one-line declaration (in `module.json`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, or `docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md`) saying which repo owns the app/addon model and that this module ships **no** OS apps — so the empty `find` is explained rather than mysterious.
- A statement of how the SPoG surface is mounted by the OS host (system app, addon, or plain route + tunnel), or a link to the issue that will decide it.

**Verify:** the declaration exists and names both facts; `grep -rn 'system app\|addon model' docs/ module.json` returns it.

items.title: no declared environment-variable surface, and infra/ is not a declared surface root
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
The repo has no declared **environment-variable surface**: no `.env.example`, no `ENVIRONMENT.md` /
`ENV-VARS.md`, no registry of the variables a deploy or a local run needs. Its variables live in
prose and in code, and the surfaces declared in `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml` do not
include one for it.

## Measured (master `8cfd1ea`)

```
$ find . -path ./vendor -prune -o -type f \( -name '*.env.example' -o -name '.env.example' -o -name 'ENVIRONMENT.md' -o -name 'ENV-VARS.md' \) -print
(no output)

$ grep -rln 'PORTAL_AUTH_GATE_JWKS\|ROOT_ADMIN_EMAILS' --include=*.md --include=*.py --include=*.yaml .
./infra/portal/auth_env.py          ./docs/OPERATOR-ACCESS.md
./scripts/portal-dev-session.py     ./docs/AGENTCONSOLE-HOSTING.md
./identity/chat/frontdoor.py        ./docs/decision-records/ADR-0025-remote-control-transport.md
./docs/PORTAL-OFFLINE-DEV.md        ./identity/chat/__init__.py
```

`governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml:surface_roots` is `[portal, gateway, telemetry, registry,
governance, integrations]` and `infra/` — where every deploy variable and every env seam lives — is
**not a declared surface root at all**. Sibling `governance/*` directories are held at `pattern`;
`infra/rollout`, which decides what is exposed in production, carries no declared class.

## Why it matters, concretely

The go-live work landed in this epic added two new env seams (`AO_SURFACE_REGISTRY` for the portal's
fleet projection, `AO_EDGE_HOST` for the edge-cutover probe) and relies on three pre-existing ones
(`PORTAL_AUTH_GATE_JWKS` / `PORTAL_AUTH_GATE_JWKS_FILE`, `ROOT_ADMIN_EMAILS`). There is **nowhere**
that a new variable is declared, reviewed, or checked for parity with a template — so:

- a variable can be introduced with no record (both of the above were), and
- a reader cannot enumerate what a deployment needs from any single place.

Unlike the feature flags — which have `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml`, a Terraform parity gate
(`scripts/check-feature-flags.py`), and a rollout stage model — the environment has no registry and
no gate.

## Acceptance

- One declared place enumerates every environment variable a deploy or a local run requires, with
  its purpose, whether it is secret, and who reads it.
- A gate fails when code reads an env var the declaration does not name (or the reverse), the way
  `check-feature-flags.py` holds the flag registry to `infra/terraform/variables.tf`.
- `infra/` is declared a surface root with a class, or the reason it is exempt is recorded.

**Verify:** `grep -rn 'AO_SURFACE_REGISTRY\|AO_EDGE_HOST\|PORTAL_AUTH_GATE_JWKS\|ROOT_ADMIN_EMAILS' <the declared env surface>` names all four.

items.title: check-module-registry and check-module-brief cannot assess on a default checkout (vendor/CMR uninitialised) and skip on every make verify
items.body:
Two module gates **cannot assess anything on master** and therefore report as a skip on every `make verify` run — a false-green class rather than a red.

## Measured (master `8cfd1ea`, fresh worktree)

```
$ bash scripts/check-module-registry.sh
check-module-registry: CANNOT-ASSESS — … run 'git submodule update --init vendor/CMR' and re-run     rc=2
$ bash scripts/check-module-brief.sh
check-module-brief:   CANNOT-ASSESS — … run 'git submodule update --init vendor/CMR' and re-run     rc=2
$ bash scripts/check-module-admission.sh
  OK    negative controls passed (the gate can genuinely fail)                                       rc=0
$ bash scripts/check-surface-class.sh
check-surface-class: OK — every declared surface meets its declared class …                          rc=0
```

Every composite gate run in this session — four of them, including the post-merge run whose
attestation is `result=PASS git_sha=8cfd1eaaab6d checks=142` — carries
`{'name': 'module-registry', 'rc': 2, 'status': 'SKIP'}` and the same for `module-brief`. The
attestation records them honestly as SKIP; the *summary* prints `4 skipped: module-registry,
module-brief, diagrams-declaration, codeidx-surface`, which is easy to read as "not applicable here"
rather than "the module contract is unenforced".

## Why it matters

`module.json` (`schema: cmr.module/v1`, with `class`, `integrations`, `governance`, `provenance`,
`submodules`) and `docs/MODULE-{REGISTRY,BRIEF,ADMISSION}.md` are the repo's module-admission
contract. Half of it — the registry and the brief — is enforced **only where `vendor/CMR` is
initialised**, which is not the default checkout state, not this box, and (by the same evidence)
not CI.

## Acceptance

- `make verify` either initialises/ports the input these two gates need, or reports them as **named
  and explained** skips in the summary line (not merely in the attestation) — so the reader learns
  the module contract was unenforced on that run.
- On a default checkout, `bash scripts/check-module-registry.sh` and `check-module-brief.sh` either
  assess (0/1) or state in one line why they cannot, without requiring the reader to run a
  submodule command to find out.

**Verify:** `bash scripts/check-module-registry.sh; echo rc=$?` adjacent to
`grep -c "rc': 2, 'status': 'SKIP'" .verify/attestation.json`

items.title: integrations/hermes is missing while integrations/paperclip is held at faang — peer-integration class asymmetry
items.body:
`integrations` is a **declared surface root** (`governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml:surface_roots`) and the one integration declared in it, `integrations/paperclip/reporting`, is held at the top rung (**faang**). Hermes has no equivalent.

## Measured (master `8cfd1ea`)

| | paperclip | hermes |
|---|---|---|
| gates in `scripts/` | **14** | **0** |
| docs in `docs/` | **3** (`PAPERCLIP-ING-{DEPLOY,GAP-ANALYSIS,INTEGRATION}.md`) | **0** |
| `integrations/` dir | `integrations/paperclip/` | **absent** |
| declared surface | `integrations/paperclip/reporting` @ faang | **none** |
| what exists | — | `gateway/catalog/modules/hermes/module.json` + references in `gateway/finops/tiers.yaml`, `gateway/health/health.yaml`, `gateway/health/fallback.py` |

So hermes is a **gateway catalog entry with a health/fallback mention**, not an integrated peer surface: it has no adapter, no gate, no docs, no declared class, and no entry in `integrations/`.

## Why it matters

The fleet contract treats the peers as an alignment set (`docs/CROSS-REFERENCE-SPINE.md`, the #422 peer-module integration epic, the `guardrails` hermes/paperclip boundary). One peer is held to `faang`; the other is invisible to the surface-class gate — a class asymmetry that no gate would ever catch, because a surface that is never declared can never sit *below* its declaration.

## Acceptance

- Either `integrations/hermes/` exists with an adapter + docs + a declared class in `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml` (and its own `scripts/check-hermes-*.sh`), or
- the asymmetry is recorded as a deliberate decision with the reason, in the same file — not left implicit.

**Verify:** `python3 -c "import yaml;d=yaml.safe_load(open('governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml'));print([s['path'] for s in d['surfaces']])"` names a hermes surface, or the decision is written down.

items.title: fix(gates): fleet-cron-dev-run is red on origin/master, so make verify is red for every lane (#706 stack blocked)
items.body:
## The gate of record is red on `origin/master`, and it is not the PR stack

`make verify` cannot be green for **any** lane today: the `fleet-cron-dev-run` check
(D2 / #710, `scripts/check-fleet-cron-dev-run.sh`) exits **rc=1 on plain
`origin/master`**, measured directly, with no PR from the fleet-cron stack applied.

This is a second, independent red alongside #933 (which tracks the portal
`finops_reports` failure). Together they mean the #706 stack (#904, #905, #906,
#908, #909, #907) **cannot be taken green**, because each PR's `Verify:` is
`make verify` and the gate is red on the base those PRs sit on.

## Reproduce

```
git fetch origin
git checkout --detach origin/master          # measured at 8cfd1ea
bash scripts/check-fleet-cron-dev-run.sh ; echo "rc=$?"
```

Reproduce: `bash scripts/check-fleet-cron-dev-run.sh` — measured `rc=1` at
`8cfd1eaaab6d22772ba57c87ad664d3f70e1f243`.

```text
== fleet-cron-dev-run: the issue's own commands ==
  OK    docker compose up -d started the container (entrypoint validated the environment, installed the schedule, dispatched)
  OK    the run reached its verdict (ok) 5s after up -d
  OK    /healthz answers 200 and names all 3 scheduled job(s)
              status=ok jobs=3 markers=['ao-fleet-watchdog', 'ao-fleet-prune', 'ao-fleet-reconcile']
  FAIL  an unserved path answered 0, not 404
  FAIL  the container's log carries no 'dry-run' line
  FAIL  the run did not report an untouched snapshot
  FAIL  the compose healthcheck reports unknown, not healthy
  FAIL  the container exited with unknown, so the stop was not the handled one
```

## What is and is not the defect

The **product under test works**: the container starts, the entrypoint validates
its environment, the dev-run reaches its verdict (`ok`), `/healthz` answers `200`
and names all three scheduled jobs (`ao-fleet-watchdog`, `ao-fleet-prune`,
`ao-fleet-reconcile`).

Five of the **check's own assertions** fail. At least one of them is a
*measured host limitation the check already documents*:

> `NOTE  MEASURED: this host cannot reach a PUBLISHED container port (a trivial
> probe answers 200 inside the container and 'Connection reset by peer' from the
> host), so the issue's request is made from inside the container`

`an unserved path answered 0, not 404` is that same limitation seen from the
other side — the host-side probe cannot connect at all, so it reads `0` instead
of the `404` the assertion expects. A check that cannot pass on the host it runs
on is red for every lane, which makes it a formality in the wrong direction
(GR-12: a check whose pass and fail paths collapse is not a gate).

The other four (`no 'dry-run' line in the container log`, `unknown` compose
healthcheck, `unknown` container exit) are consistent with the compose/healthcheck
surface changing under the check since it was written — the same class of drift
#897 (`shell-patterns` red from a file that landed after the check) already
measured once in this repo.

## Why it blocks the epic

Every PR in the #706 stack states `Verify: make verify`. With this check red on
master, `scripts/merge-gate.sh` and the autonomous-merge doctrine both refuse
every one of them, *including PRs whose own diff is clean*. Measured on PR #904's
gate at `8d3dd600`: `verify: FAIL (8 of 139 checks failed)` — of those eight,
seven are not attributable to #904 (five pass when run directly on master,
`fleet-cron-dev-run` is this issue, `gate-lock` failed because the box-wide permit
cap was saturated at 4/4), and exactly one — `secrets`, a literal password shape
in the lane's own new test file — was.

## Suggested remedy (a lane's call, not prescribed here)

1. Make the host-unreachable probe an explicit, named outcome of the check rather
   than a failed assertion — the check already measures and documents that the host
   cannot reach a published port; asserting `404` through a probe that cannot
   connect is asserting the opposite of a measurement the check itself made.
2. Re-derive the compose healthcheck and container-exit expectations from the
   compose file the way the rest of the check derives its facts, rather than
   hard-coding `healthy`/handled-stop.
3. Keep a negative control so the check can still fail: a mutant that really does
   stop the container unhandled must still be refused by name.

## Impact

Blocks: #706 (EPIC, fleet-cron containerisation) and every child PR (#904, #905,
#906, #908, #909, #907), plus any unrelated lane whose change happens to sit on
this base.

items.title: check-secrets: the placeholder exemption never fires — RE_PLACE starts with a PCRE (?i) under grep -E
items.body:
\`scripts/check-secrets.sh\` line 30 defines \`RE_PLACE='(?i)(example|sample|placeholder|dummy|fake|...)'\` and applies it with \`grep -qiE\`. GNU grep -E does not understand the PCRE inline flag: it warns \`? at start of expression\` and the pattern then requires a literal \`?i\` in the text, so the exemption never matches. Every generic \`password=\"...\"\` / \`token=\"...\"\` assignment with a >=8-char value is reported as a possible secret even when the value says \`fake\` or \`placeholder\`.

Repro (any checkout):
\`\`\`
printf 'password="fake-keydb-placeholder-1234567890"' | grep -qiE "$(sed -n "s/^RE_PLACE='\(.*\)'$/\1/p" scripts/check-secrets.sh)"; echo rc=$?   # rc=1, should be 0
\`\`\`
Seen live on PR #904 (\`fleet/tests/test_lease.py:299\`), worked around in-lane by building the placeholder from parts (551732d).

Fix: drop the \`(?i)\` prefix (the \`-i\` flag already makes it case-insensitive), add a provoked negative control to the script's self-test that proves a \`fake\`/\`placeholder\` value is exempt and a bare value is not. Do not widen RE_PLACE.

Refs #904

items.title: check-edge-cutover.sh deletes the terraform log that names its own failure cause
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
Parent: #731 (found by the verification lane on PR #926; non-blocking, fails closed)

`scripts/check-edge-cutover.sh` deletes its own evidence on failure. When the
behavioural mutant probe cannot complete, the gate correctly fails closed:

```
check-edge-cutover: FAIL — the behavioural mutant was NOT accepted, so the refusal may come from
  something other than the rule under test. The probe said (CANNOT the default-posture plan did not
  complete offline (see /tmp/ao731-edge-cutover.2372651.1789580606/tf-mutant/plan-default.log)):
CANNOT the default-posture plan did not complete offline (see …/tf-mutant/plan-default.log)
check-edge-cutover: FAILED — the gate could not prove itself, so its verdict means nothing
```

…but the `log` path it names lives inside its scratch dir, which `trap cleanup
EXIT` removes — so after the run the named evidence is gone and the cause cannot
be established from the report alone.

**Not a false green and not a false red.** Measured 2026-09-16: on a planted tree
(the `dns-record-ungated` plant) this is deterministic — 3/3 runs, rc 1 — and on
the unmodified tree 4/4 runs rc 0 under full box load (4/4 gate permits held). It
was originally reported as a possible load flake; that explanation is refuted.

## Acceptance

- On the failure path, the terraform log (or the tail that names the cause) is
  preserved — written into the report, or copied to a path that outlives the
  scratch dir — instead of being deleted with it.
- The message distinguishes "the mutant was ACCEPTED" (a real finding about the
  rule) from "the probe did not complete" (cannot-assess), naming which.

items.title: rollout: register surfaces.edge_cutover (deferred by #731 — surfaces.* rows + rollout registration)
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
Parent: #731 (disclosed in `docs/EDGE-CUTOVER.md` as a deliberate deferral)

PR #926 landed the fronting decision for `ai.purebliss.app` as **code** (the
retired GCP edge route is no longer created by default, and
`scripts/check-edge-cutover.sh` proves it). It did **not** register the surface in
the rollout machinery, because a sibling lane owned `infra/rollout/**` in the same
wave and the two file sets must stay disjoint (rule 2/21).

## What is missing (measured)

A `surfaces.edge_cutover` flag is not declared anywhere, so the edge cutover is
**not promotable** through the ordered go-live ladder. Registering it is a
three-file move, not one — omitting either companion leaves the surface
undeclarable:

1. `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml` — a `surfaces:` row (`default: off`,
   `promoted: false`, a real `service`, a `tf_flag` that already exists — a new
   `surfaces.*` row needs no new `enable_*` variable, unlike `services.*`, which
   is set-equality-checked against `infra/terraform/variables.tf` by
   `scripts/check-feature-flags.py:138-146`).
2. `infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml` — the drivable row `stage: "off"`. Without
   it the engine refuses the flag by name: `unknown flag '<name>' (not declared
   in rollout state)`, and `check_rollout.py::check_registry_parity` (lines
   120-151) refuses a rollout flag with no registry surface.
3. `infra/rollout/go-live-plan.yaml` — the intent row under a phase.

## Verify

```bash
python3 infra/rollout/checks/check_rollout.py                       # rc 0
python3 infra/rollout/go_live.py --plan --phase <phase>             # names the new flag
grep -n edge_cutover infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml infra/rollout/go-live-plan.yaml
```

items.title: A lane that follows the doctrine cannot pass make verify: the prescribed identity env defeats the isolation gates, and the mandated claim ledger is unignored (#848)
items.body:
Parent: #160

## The gate of record cannot be green in the state the doctrine requires a lane to be in

`make verify` is the gate of record (AGENTS.md GR-12) and the merge precondition.
Measured today, **no lane that follows the doctrine can satisfy it**, for two
independent reasons, each reproduced on a *pristine* worktree cut from
`origin/master`:

```
$ git worktree add --detach /tmp/ao160-base origin/master   # 3f80273, nothing touched
```

### Half 1 — the identity env AGENTS.md rule 15 prescribes defeats the isolation gates

Rule 15 (and `governance/isolation/cli.py open`'s own `env` block) tells every
lane to export `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME`/
`GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL`. With that env exported — and **nothing else changed** — on
the pristine worktree:

```
$ bash scripts/check-session-isolation.sh                                     rc=0  OK
$ env GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=agent-subagent-999 GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=agent+subagent-999@agents.invalid \
      GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=agent-subagent-999 GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=agent+subagent-999@agents.invalid \
      bash scripts/check-session-isolation.sh                                 rc=1  FAIL (5 violation(s))
  FAIL  the commit is authored by 'agent+subagent-366@agents.invalid'
  FAIL  a commit without the ticket trailer is refused (the violation went undetected; expected commit-missing-ticket-trailer)
  FAIL  a later commit does not repair an untraceable one (…)
  FAIL  a reference only in the subject line is refused (…)
  FAIL  a reference buried in prose is refused (…)
```

The audit compares **landed history authored by other identities** against the
ambient environment. Four of the five failures are its *vacuity controls* reading
"the violation went undetected" — i.e. the ambient env also blinds the mechanism
that proves the rule is enforced. It does not just fail; it fails in a way that
would let a real violation through.

Attributed on a real lane (issue #366, worktree `ao-366-4adf5d58`, head
`d4a62fb`), same tree, env the only variable:

| check | env cleared | mandate env exported |
|---|---|---|
| `check-session-isolation` | **OK** rc=0 | **FAIL (5)** |
| `check-isolation-landed` | **OK** rc=0 | **FAIL** |
| `check-gitignore` | FAIL (1) — half 2 | FAIL (1) |

Its composite attestation (`check_count: 135`) reports exactly those three
non-PASS checks, all three of them for reasons that are not its diff.

**Secondary finding, measured while fanning out four lanes:** the identity env is
carried by a **shared** shell, so it does not survive concurrency either — several
lanes exporting theirs into one shell means a lane's commit is authored by
*whichever lane exported last*. `check-session-isolation.sh` correctly calls that
a violation; nothing prevents it. `isolation/cli.py open` already stamps the
signature with `git config --worktree`, so the export is redundant **and**
hazardous.

### Half 2 — the claim the doctrine mandates is untracked-and-unignored (#848)

Rule 14 requires `claim` before working; `governance/dispatch/claims.py` writes
`.board/claims/<event>.json`, which `.gitignore` does not cover, so
`check-gitignore` fails. Already filed as **#848** (measured 2026-09-15 in
`ao-793-1889fcda`), still open, unfixed, unowned. On the pristine worktree it is
green only because no lane has claimed there yet.

### The cost, measured today

Four lanes were dispatched for `#160`'s remaining children. Two reported the
composite as un-greenable for reasons that were not theirs; one merged only by
declaring the residue under the PR contract's *Pre-existing red* slot; one
stopped at an open PR (`#930`) because "never merge failing work" and "the gate
is always red for a working lane" are jointly unsatisfiable. That is the same
shape `#799` describes one layer up: **the fleet behaves well when every stage
succeeds and becomes unbounded the moment one refuses.**

## Proposed direction (for the owning lane)

1. **Scope the audit to its subject.** The isolation gates must judge *the lane
   they are auditing* (its worktree, its range, the signature in
   `git config --worktree`) — never compare unrelated landed history against the
   ambient environment. Run the real-repo audit with the identity env **cleared**,
   and keep the vacuity controls independent of it.
2. **Make the safe form the documented one.** Prefer per-commit
   `git -c user.name=… -c user.email=…` (or rely on the `open`-stamped worktree
   config) over exporting `GIT_AUTHOR_*` into a shared shell; say so where rule 15
   is read.
3. **Trap the contamination, don't absorb it.** A commit authored by a *different*
   session's identity inside this lane must still fail **by name** — the fix must
   not weaken the rule, and the new control must provoke it.
4. **`.gitignore` += `/.board/claims/`** (half 2 / #848): the per-event directory
   is runtime state; `.board/claims.jsonl` stays tracked as the frozen legacy
   ledger, per #848's own proposed direction.

## Acceptance

- [ ] On a pristine worktree at `master`, `check-session-isolation` and
      `check-isolation-landed` are green **with** the rule-15 identity env
      exported, and green without it.
- [ ] In a lane that has claimed (so `.board/claims/<event>.json` exists) and
      whose subagent exported the identity env, `make verify` is green — the
      composite reaches a verdict that reflects the diff.
- [ ] The rule is not weakened: a commit authored by another lane's identity, a
      trailer only in the subject, a trailer buried in prose, and a missing
      trailer each still fail **by name** (provoked, with the provocation shown).
- [ ] `.board/claims/` is ignored and `check-gitignore` is green in a claiming
      lane (closes #848).
- [ ] `make verify` green; every new or changed control can genuinely fail.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-session-isolation.sh
bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh
bash scripts/check-gitignore.sh
make verify
```

items.title: make gate is red on master: portal/tests/test_finops_reports.py::test_live_cost_budget_and_usage_per_agent_is_served (pre-existing)
items.body:
Parent: #607 (found while verifying the epic's go-live lanes)

`make gate` is **red on `origin/master` today**, independently of any lane's diff.

## Measured

```bash
python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q portal/tests
# 1 failed, 510 passed
# portal/tests/test_finops_reports.py:199: AssertionError
#   > assert breakdown["costComplete"] is True
#   E assert False is True
```

Reproduced identically at the base commit `69ae5af` and at three independent lane
heads (`1104ced` #732, `696625e` #731, `5aa2023` #619) — same test, same line,
same assertion. It is **not** introduced by any of those diffs; their file sets do
not touch `portal/server/finops.py` or the telemetry cost sources.

## Why it matters beyond one test

`scripts/pytest-suites.txt:56` declares the `portal` suite, so
`scripts/run-pytest-suites.sh` runs it from `make gate` (`scripts/gate.sh:85`) and
`make merge-gate` (`scripts/merge-gate.sh:99`). Both are therefore red on a clean
`master`. `make verify` is unaffected — it declares a fixed pytest list that names
no `portal` suite — which is precisely why the red has been invisible: the gate
every lane is told to quote (`make verify`) does not run the suite that fails.

## Acceptance

- `python3 -m pytest -q portal/tests` is green, or the assertion is shown to be
  itself wrong and corrected with evidence.
- `make gate` is green on `master`.
- If the fix is "do not declare `portal` in the suite manifest", that must be an
  explicit, reasoned decision recorded here — not a silent de-listing, which would
  hide the failure instead of fixing it.

items.title: [bug] check-verdict-contains under-counts: four pipe-into-grep shapes escape its "must never under-count" anchor
items.body:
**A defect that cannot be reproduced cannot be fixed.**

**GOAL** — close the gap between the invariant `scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh`
states about its own counter and what that counter actually measures. The header
claims it "must never under-count"; four pipe-into-`grep` shapes under-count.
**Zero live occurrences exist in the tree today**, so this is a coverage gap in a
control, not a red on `master`.

**Constraints** — the counter lives in `scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh`, which
is not owned by the lane that measured this (#865). Filed, not fixed, per that
lane's brief. Do not widen `scripts/verdict-contains-legacy.tsv`: `--record`
refuses to grow by design, and the ratchet is shrink-only.

## Observed

Measured on a scratch worktree of `origin/master` = `1c6e184`, with the plants
written **outside** the repo (`/tmp/ao865-fix`) so no corpus fixture is involved
and nothing is being counted twice.

```
$ awk -v pat='[|][[:space:]]*grep[[:space:]][^|]*(-[[:alnum:]]*q|--quiet)' \
    '$0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*#/ {next} $0 ~ pat {n++} END{print n+0}' "$plant"
  p1-plain                 count=1   printf … | grep -qF …
  p2-env-grep              count=0   printf … | env grep -qF …
  p3-abspath               count=0   printf … | /usr/bin/grep -qF …
  p4-command               count=0   printf … | command grep -qF …
  p5-continued             count=0   printf … |\   <newline>   grep -qF …
  p6-comment               count=0   (a comment — correctly not counted)
  p7-double-pipe-file      count=0   || ! grep -qF … "$file"   (correctly not counted)
```

The gate's own run over that fixture, with an **empty** record, names only `p1` —
so the named set *is* the seen set, and the four escapees are invisible to it:

```
$ bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh --root /tmp/ao865-fix --baseline /tmp/ao865-fix/empty.tsv
== 5. the repository against its record ==
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/p1-plain.sh has 1, the record allows 0
        Use a bash-native containment test (see the header) instead.
  legacy still recorded: 1 site(s) in 1 file(s)

check-verdict-contains: FAIL (1 finding(s); 9 control(s) passed)
```

`p6` and `p7` being uncounted is **correct** and stays: a comment cannot run, and
`|| ! grep -qF … "$file"` has no pipe into `grep`, so there is no SIGPIPE and no
false verdict. The defect is `p2`–`p5` only.

**Nothing escapes today.** A wider one-line scan over every tracked `.sh` returns
exactly one match the ratchet does not count —
`scripts/check-session-isolation.sh:165`
(`if [ ! -f "$trailer_module" ] || ! grep -qF -- "$predicate" "$trailer_module"`)
— and that is the `p7` shape, correctly uncounted.

## Expected

The script's own header, which is the contract this issue measures against:

> The counter is deliberately CONSERVATIVE: it can over-count (it also matches
> the idiom inside quoted fixture data and inside a printed message), and it
> must never under-count -- over-counting is recorded and reviewed, whereas a
> miss would let a real occurrence through, which is the whole failure mode this
> check exists for.

The `[|][[:space:]]*grep` anchor exists for a sound reason — it is what keeps
`p7` out — but it also requires `grep` to be the command *immediately* after the
pipe, so `grep` behind `env`, `command` or an absolute path, and a pipe continued
across a line break, all carry the identical defect and are all recorded as 0.

## Reproduction command

```bash
FIX=$(mktemp -d /tmp/ao865-repro.XXXXXX); mkdir -p "$FIX/scripts"
printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' \
  'if ! printf "%s" "$out" | env grep -qF -- "$marker"; then echo missing; fi' \
  > "$FIX/scripts/escapee.sh"
printf '# floor\n' > "$FIX/empty.tsv"
bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh --root "$FIX" --baseline "$FIX/empty.tsv"
```

Run verbatim on `1c6e184`, section 5 reports the site as invisible:

```
== 5. the repository against its record ==
  OK    no file exceeds its recorded count
  legacy still recorded: 0 site(s) in 0 file(s)

check-verdict-contains: OK -- … (10 control(s); 0 legacy site(s) in 0 file(s) remain recorded)
```

An `env grep -qF` piped verdict test is in the tree and this control returns `OK`
with an empty record — that is the gap.

## Severity

low

## RCA link (governance/lessons/)

`governance/lessons/` — not yet recorded. The lesson is owed with the fix: a
detector is only as wide as the anchor it was written with, and a header that
names its own invariant ("must never under-count") is a claim someone can
provoke. Keep one, and the claim becomes measurable; keep it unprovoked and the
narrowing is invisible — the same family as #730, where a gate asserted an
expression's *text* and never that it *resolved*.

## Fix sketch (for whoever owns the file)

Widen the anchor to accept an optional command prefix
(`(env|command|[^[:space:]]*/)?grep`) and join backslash-continued lines before
matching, then re-run `--record` — it will only ever *lower* the record, so a
widening that starts seeing real sites turns them into `NEW` refusals by name,
which is the intended outcome. The seven plants above are the negative control:
`p1` must be 1, `p2`–`p5` must become 1, and `p6`/`p7` must **stay** 0 — a
widening that starts counting `p7` has traded a false negative for a false
positive.



---

Part-of: #803

items.title: dispatch: enforce the owner's ordered queue — refuse out-of-order claims
items.body:
Parent: #878

## The gap (measured on `.board/snapshot.json`, 2026-09-16)

`governance/dispatch/order.py` and `governance/dispatch/claims.py` already
refuse an out-of-order `claim` when `Issue.blocked_by` is non-empty
(`order.py:120` `REASON_BLOCKED`; `claims.py:487`
`raise ClaimRefused(REASON_BLOCKED, ...)`). That refusal is real code, not a
stub — 86 issues in the current snapshot do carry populated `blocked_by`
edges and are correctly gated.

But the two dependency chains the owner is driving **today** carry no edges
at all:

- EPIC #878 lanes #880–#890: every lane's `blocked_by` is `[]`; all ten are
  siblings under `parent: 878` with no sequencing between them, so `claim`
  will accept L1 through L11 in any order, including reverse.
- EPIC #706 chain #711–#715, #900–#902: same — `blocked_by: []` on every
  entry, despite #712/#713/#714/#715 being an explicit D3→D4→D5→D6→D7
  dependency chain in the issue titles/bodies and #901 explicitly folding
  into #900's work.

So the enforcement mechanism exists and works on its declared input, but
nothing populates that input from the owner's actual intended order. An
agent free-claiming today is refused only by the issues that already had
`blocked_by` set by a prior lane's author — not by anything derived from the
epic's own stated sequence.

## What to add

A single source of truth for the *owner's* ordered queue — e.g.
`docs/QUEUE.md` or `.board/queue.json`, committed, human- and
machine-readable — listing issue numbers in forced order with explicit
`blocked_by` lists per wave. Wire it into the existing gate:

1. At snapshot-build/claim time, load the committed queue file if present.
2. For any issue listed in it, union its declared `blocked_by` from the
   queue file into `Issue.blocked_by` (in addition to, not instead of, any
   GitHub-derived edges).
3. Let the existing `order.py`/`claims.py` refusal path do the rest — no new
   refusal codes needed, just a new edge source.
4. Add a regression test asserting that an issue in the queue file with an
   unmet `blocked_by` is refused even when GitHub carries no edge for it
   (mirrors the existing `test_claims.py`/`test_arbitration.py` fixtures).

Without this, the "Owner queue" posted as a comment on #878 is advisory only
— nothing in dispatch actually refuses an agent that ignores it and claims
#889 before #880, or #715 before #712.

cc @kushin77

items.title: The fleet's code prose still names retired roles (comments/docstrings), while the contract declares the new vocabulary
items.body:
Parent: #160
Refs #777

## The gap (measured on `eb0b0e3`, the commit that landed #777)

#777 declared the fleet's role vocabulary (`governance/vocabulary/fleet.yaml`) and
migrated it across the **contract surface**: the envelope's `schema` version, the
validator, the write seam, the gate, and every declared normative surface
(`fleet/CONTRACT.md` §1, `fleet/README.md`, `docs/OPERATOR-ACCESS.md`,
`docs/GLOSSARY.md`, `fleet/profiles/brain.md`, the standing directive).

What it did **not** migrate is **code prose** — comments and module docstrings
inside `fleet/`:

```
$ for f in fleet/channel.py fleet/brain.py fleet/terminal.py; do
    printf '%-20s %s\n' "$f" "$(grep -ciE '\b(operator|brain|sister|subagent)\b' "$f")"
  done
fleet/channel.py      107
fleet/brain.py        136
fleet/terminal.py     112
```

The great majority are comments and docstrings. `fleet/channel.py`'s own module
docstring still reads:

```
"""Steering channel CLI — the transport between the brain and the fleet.

Operating model (M26, issue #160): the **brain** (advisor session) issues
directives; the **sister** session (a dumb terminal on DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, no
thinking) executes them …
```

So a reader of the code gets the retired vocabulary while a reader of the contract
gets the declared one. That asymmetry is **named and declared** in
`governance/vocabulary/fleet.yaml` → `out_of_scope` ("CODE PROSE — DECLARED, NOT
SILENTLY DONE"), not left to be discovered. This issue is that declaration made
actionable.

## Why it was NOT done inside #777

Doing it there would have buried a ~350-line prose sweep in a diff whose evidence
is a *protocol* migration, and the sweep has **no gate behind it** — so it could
regress with nothing to catch it. #777's own rule (declare the closed set, refuse
by name) argues for doing this with its own check.

## What this issue must NOT do

**Do not rename the artifacts.** A large share of those hits are literal data with
live consumers:

* `CAPABILITY_RUNGS = ("brain", "sister")` and `rungs=("brain", …)` in
  `fleet/channel.py` — the rung names `fleet/watchdog.py` reports and
  `governance/reconcile` matches;
* `FLEET_DIR / "brain" / "inbox"`, `FLEET_DIR / "sister.heartbeat.json"` — mailbox
  and heartbeat paths;
* `fleet/brain.py`, `fleet/terminal.sh`, the `brain-inbox` / `brain-outbox`
  subcommands, the `make operator` target, `--rung brain`;
* the `[brain] …` / `[sister] …` lines those commands **print** — recorded
  evidence, which a rename would falsify.

`governance/vocabulary/fleet.yaml` `out_of_scope` names each of these. Renaming
the *files* (and the rung identity) is a third, separate migration.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A grep for the four retired names over `fleet/*.py` returns **only**
      artifact identifiers, literal rung/mailbox values, and lines inside a marked
      legacy-gloss region — no comment or docstring names a retired role.
- [ ] The sweep is covered by a **check that can fail**, not by a one-off script:
      extending `scripts/check-fleet-vocabulary.sh` (or a sibling) so the code
      prose is a declared surface, provoked by planting a retired name in a
      docstring and requiring the gate to refuse it by name.
- [ ] The rung/mailbox artifacts above are unchanged, and
      `fleet/tests/test_capability_drift.py` + `fleet/tests/test_controls.py`
      still pass — they pin the rung names.

## Verify

```
python3 -m pytest -q fleet/tests && bash scripts/check-fleet-vocabulary.sh && make verify
```

items.title: Fleet acceptance test: the runnable parity instrument and a drop the loop cannot swallow (#799 delta)
items.body:
Parent: #799 · Refs #861 (the drain-path refusal classification — a different lane's surface, deliberately not touched here)

## Why the delta is a separate issue from #799

#799 is the **finding**, and its own text names five things that must be built before
the acceptance test can pass. Three belong to other lanes (`#727` refresh-or-park
landed; **`#861`** per-directive bounded consumption is *not* landed; `#724` one gate
per worktree landed), and one of its acceptance boxes — *"one issue, ordered through
`fleet/channel.py order`, reaches a merged PR with quoted gate evidence and a closed
issue, with no operator intervention after the order"* — is a property of a **running
fleet**, which a single lane cannot demonstrate.

This issue is the part a lane CAN demonstrate: the runnable instrument, and the
remedy an operator can actually reach. Keeping it separate means merging it cannot
close #799 on evidence that does not support the claim.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `bash scripts/check-fleet-parity.sh --issue <n>` prints a per-dimension verdict
      for a real lane and refuses to claim a PASS from an unreadable input
      (CANNOT-ASSESS), naming what could not be read.
- [ ] Every dimension is **provoked**: a subject that fails a dimension fails the
      harness, proved by planted subjects, with a healthy subject that clears all of
      them (so a harness that fails everything cannot satisfy the plants).
- [ ] `python3 fleet/control.py drop --directive <id> --reason <text>` is effective
      with **no loop running**: the order leaves the inbox and is terminal, and a
      second drop cannot degrade the first's record.
- [ ] The `#821` invariant holds: a drop cannot retire an order whose change has
      already landed, and an undecidable landed state is refused, never defaulted.
- [ ] `make verify` is green on the lane's commit, and the branch is pushed before
      the composite gate (AO-GR-23).

## Verify

```
bash scripts/check-fleet-parity.sh --issue <n>
python3 -m pytest fleet/tests/test_control_drop.py -q
bash scripts/check-fleet-parity.sh && make verify
```

## Out of scope (named, so it cannot be mistaken for done)

The drain-path refusal classification (#861) and the brain-side live-claim guard. The
harness scores the **outcome** ("a lane produces work product, and one refusing stage
does not unbound the cycle"); it does not implement the bound.

items.title: session identity: GIT_COMMITTER_* is minted but absent from the spawn envelope
items.body:
Parent: #160

Target solution class: enterprise
Pillar: governance

## Observed

`governance/isolation/identity.py:147-150` exports all four identity variables —
`GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`, `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`, `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME`, `GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL` — and
`governance/isolation/worktree.py` stamps them into the lane worktree's own config
(`git config --worktree`). But the spawn envelope (`governance/spawn/sources.py:257-258`) reads
only the two `GIT_AUTHOR_*`; the **committer half of the session identity never reaches the
envelope**.

```
$ grep -n "GIT_AUTHOR\|GIT_COMMITTER" governance/spawn/sources.py governance/isolation/identity.py
governance/isolation/identity.py:147:   GIT_AUTHOR_NAME
governance/isolation/identity.py:148:   GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL
governance/isolation/identity.py:149:   GIT_COMMITTER_NAME
governance/isolation/identity.py:150:   GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL
governance/spawn/sources.py:257:        "author_name"  -> GIT_AUTHOR_NAME
governance/spawn/sources.py:258:        "author_email" -> GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL
```

## Expected

The envelope carries **both** halves, so an envelope audit can prove `committer == author ==
session agent` the same way it already proves authorship. Rule 15 declares the committer identity
is exported; the envelope is the only audit surface that could prove it reached the child.

## Reproduction

`grep` above; or read the envelope projection in `governance/spawn/sources.py` `session_field`.

## Severity

`high` — identity is the proof-of-isolation seam, and half of it is currently unauditable.

## RCA

No incident — this is a mint→envelope threading asymmetry, not a failure. If it ever surfaces as an
incident it will be recorded in `governance/lessons/`; nothing to record today.

## Verify (proposed)

`python3 -m pytest governance/spawn/tests -q` (or the spawn module's own suite) plus
`bash scripts/check-session-isolation.sh`, and the envelope projection asserted for all four
fields.

items.title: Session close-out governance: close every session, reconcile orphans, and make session identity visible to the sweeper
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
## Objective

Make session close-out real and repeatable: **every session ends in a terminal state**, orphaned
sessions are reconciled rather than left as directories on disk, and session identity is
*visible* to the tool that is supposed to sweep them.

Today it is not. Measured on the shared checkout, 2026-09-16:

```
$ ls .fleet/sessions/ | wc -l
0                                   # the heartbeat plane is EMPTY
$ ls .fleet/lanes/ | wc -l
78                                  # …while 78 lane records exist
$ python3 governance/reconcile/cli.py status
0 session(s), 0 orphan(s)           # so the sweeper sees nothing at all
$ git worktree list | wc -l
110                                 # 83 of them under ao-worktrees
```

`governance/reconcile` is the module whose whole purpose is #304's orphan reconciliation —
`reclaimed` / `parked` / `shelved`, decided by *where the work lives*. It reads
`.fleet/sessions/`, so with that directory empty its verdict is vacuously green: it reports **0
orphans** while 83 lane worktrees and 78 lane records are on disk. That is the same
"a control that cannot fail is a formality" shape the golden rules name (GR-12), reached by a
route nobody had measured.

## Why this is not just housekeeping

1. **The close-out is already known-broken for exactly this population.** `lifecycle close
   --issue N` fails `record-verification` when no lane record exists (#786), and I measured the
   *inverse* variant today on #655: the record set exists for other lanes, the lane worktree is
   present and its attestation green, and close-out still cannot resolve the lane because
   `.fleet/lanes/` has no entry for that issue. Both directions of the same hole.
2. **Branch ancestry is the wrong landed-test.** Every lane in this fleet lands by **squash
   merge**, so a landed lane's branch tip is *never* an ancestor of `master`. A classifier built
   on `git merge-base --is-ancestor` reports "unlanded" for work that shipped — I hit this
   measuring the 78 records (18 classified `landed`, 59 `unlanded`, and the `unlanded` set is
   dominated by squash-merged lanes). The decision has to be made on **content**.
3. **Work that exists nowhere else must not be deleted.** The doctrine is explicit: never trade
   unmerged work for an unlocked issue. A reclaimer that cannot prove "landed" must *shelve* and
   report, never reclaim.

## Scope

* `governance/sessions/` — a session close-out classifier + CLI: for every `.fleet/lanes/` record,
  decide `reclaimed` (provably landed → worktree/branch/record are safe to retire), `shelved`
  (unlanded work that exists only here → keep and report), or `unknown` (cannot assess, named).
* `scripts/check-session-closeout.sh` — the gate proving the classifier both ways, including the
  **vacuity control**: a record set with no landed lanes must not report reclaimed, and a planted
  unlanded lane must never be reclaimed.
* A **report** over the real 78 records + 110 worktrees, with the reclaim list and the shelve list
  measured — the operational half of "close all sessions".
* The heartbeat gap: state why `.fleet/sessions/` is empty while `.fleet/lanes/` is not, and what
  makes `reconcile status` non-vacuous.

## Acceptance

1. `python3 -m governance.sessions.cli report` (or the equivalent verb) prints a verdict per lane
   record, and the verdict for a **squash-merged** lane is `reclaimed`, not `unlanded`.
2. The gate refuses a reclaimer that would retire a lane with unlanded content, by name.
3. The measured report: N reclaimable, M shelved (named), K unknown (named with the reason).
4. `reconcile status` is non-vacuous — either the heartbeat plane is populated for live sessions,
   or the tool says out loud that it cannot see the lane records it sweeps.

`Verify:` the new gate's own command, plus `make verify`.

AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW)

items.title: rollout: promoted stages cannot be persisted — validator requires every committed flag off (blocks #607)
items.body:
## Problem

`infra/rollout/model.py::validate_rollout_state_doc` refuses any flag in
`rollout-state.yaml` whose committed `stage` is not `"off"`:

```
flag '<name>' must default to off, got '<stage>'
```

This validator is invoked by both `RolloutEngine.load` (`infra/rollout/engine.py`)
and the gate (`infra/rollout/checks/check_rollout.py`). Meanwhile
`GO-LIVE-RUNBOOK.md`'s acceptance criterion is:

```
grep -E 'stage: "full"' infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml
```

and `RolloutEngine.write_state` / the CLI's `promote --state-out` target that
same file. These three facts contradict each other: the committed
`rollout-state.yaml` structurally cannot record a promoted flag, so the
runbook's own acceptance check can never be satisfied by the file the model
layer validates.

## Repro (from the #607 go-live promotion attempt audit,
`infra/rollout/audit/2026-09-16-go-live-607-promotion-attempt.md`, added in
PR #913)

```bash
python3 -m infra.rollout.cli promote ci_cd.verify_trigger --to canary \
  --verify-green --actor deployer-sa --state-out <scratch>/state-after.yaml
# succeeds, writes a mutated file

# Reloading that file:
python3 -c "
from infra.rollout.engine import RolloutEngine
RolloutEngine.load(
    stage_model_path='infra/rollout/stage-model.yaml',
    rollout_state_path='<scratch>/state-after.yaml',
)
"
# RolloutError: flag 'ci_cd.verify_trigger' must default to off, got 'canary'

# And running check_rollout.py against that file as rollout-state.yaml:
python3 infra/rollout/checks/check_rollout.py
# fails with the same message, exit 1
```

Consequence: no flag can ever reach `full` in the committed
`rollout-state.yaml` without breaking every subsequent CLI load and the
lane's own gate. This blocks #607 go-live — every promotion in the
runbook's ladder is refused before any state changes.

## Fix direction (this issue)

Keep `rollout-state.yaml` as the declared-default document (GR-28: every
flag ships OFF by default; validator unchanged) and persist live promoted
stage to a separate `infra/rollout/live-state.yaml`, enforced by a new
validator requiring an audit trail for every non-off entry and a human
approval id for `full`. Engine/CLI/checks/docs/tests updated accordingly.

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#607

items.title: fix(gates): the shell-pattern gate refuses a file that landed after it — master is red
items.body:
## `master` is red: the shell-pattern gate refuses a file that landed after it

`make verify` on a clean `origin/master` fails. Nothing to do with any lane's
work in flight — the failure is inside `master` itself, both sides of it landed
in the last hour, and the lane that added the file branched before the gate
existed (the #852 ratchet shape: a green branch gate says nothing about the
union).

```
$ git worktree add --detach /tmp/clean origin/master     # 51048ca062f41c55dfaeddfa74588fdd6319e849
$ cd /tmp/clean && bash scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh
…
  scanned 164 shell file(s)
  REFUSED  SP-2 ifs-collapse
           scripts/check-control-coverage.sh:186
               IFS=',' read -r -a mods <<< "$modules"
           why: a standalone field-separator assignment collapses adjacent tabs and empty fields, so a TSV row is mis-split and a field silently shifts
  REFUSED  SP-3 ifs-comma-read
           scripts/check-control-coverage.sh:186
  REFUSED  SP-2 ifs-collapse
           scripts/check-control-coverage.sh:207
               IFS=',' read -r -a ctrls <<< "$controls"
  REFUSED  SP-3 ifs-comma-read
           scripts/check-control-coverage.sh:207
check-shell-patterns: NOT-OK — 4 occurrence(s) refused above (docs/SHELL-PATTERNS.md)
$ echo $?
1
```

`check-shell-patterns.sh` is auto-discovered (`scripts/discover-checks.sh`) and
**not** denylisted, so it runs inside `make verify`; its `rc 1` is a FAIL, which
is why the whole gate is red for every lane on this box.

## Who owns it

* `scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` — #621 (`ddacd26`), *closed*.
* the violating file — `scripts/check-control-coverage.sh`, added by #876
  (`51048ca`, "the enterprise control map, and the gate that keeps it true"),
  issue #874, *closed*.

`ddacd26` is an ancestor of `51048ca`, so the gate existed when #876 merged — but
#876's lane had branched before it, so its own `make verify` never ran the new
check, and the merge-commit verify that would have caught the union apparently
did not run. This is exactly the failure mode #852/#868 was landed to stop.

## Why this is not #877

#877 retires the **declared-only** patterns (SP-7, SP-8). The two refusing here
are SP-2/SP-3, which #621 enforced from day one — so this red is **untracked** by
any open issue as far as I can tell (`gh issue list --search` for the gate, the
file and the two codes returns only #877, #874, #891).

## The remedy (cheap, local, two lines)

Both are the same shape, and the sanctioned replacement is a split that cannot
collapse or drop fields:

```bash
mapfile -t mods < <(tr ',' '\n' <<<"$modules")
mapfile -t ctrls < <(tr ',' '\n' <<<"$controls")
```

`scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` itself assembles the shapes from fragments, so
the fix carries no occurrence of its own. `docs/SHELL-PATTERNS.md` is the
doctrine; `docs/SCRATCH-SPACE-DISCIPLINE.md` is the sibling statement.

## Acceptance

- `bash scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` exits 0 on a clean checkout of `master`;
- `make verify` is green on the merge commit that fixes it (not merely on the
  fixing branch — this red is itself the proof that the branch gate is not
  enough);
- `scripts/check-control-coverage.sh` still passes its own `--self-test`.

## Found by

Lane `issue-710` (EPIC #706 D2), while verifying its own branch. #710's PR
declares this red under `Pre-existing red`, with the reproduction above, rather
than folding another lane's fix into its diff: one issue = one lane.

items.title: AO-GR-13: the verification artifact carries no identity, so the auditor's independence is not observable on it
items.body:
Parent: #873 · Last remaining item of the epic · Blocks #890 (lane L11, acceptance: "#803, #873 closed")

## Objective

Make **AO-GR-13** (independent auditor) fully `ENFORCED` by giving the verification artifact the one thing it lacks: **identity**.

## The measurement

AO-GR-13 is already enforced further than the epic first claimed — `check-landing.sh` refuses a red attestation, refuses a green one naming *another* commit, and returns CANNOT-ASSESS on none (*"never on self-report"*); and `governance/merge` (a declared suite, 79 tests) is the state machine requiring verify-gate green + an **independent SME reviewer** + no self-merge, with the landing seam delegating to it and refusing if it cannot be loaded.

What is missing is narrow and specific. The artifact the landing gate actually judges carries **no identity field at all**:

```python
>>> import json; sorted(json.load(open('.verify/attestation.json')))
['branch', 'check_count', 'checks', 'exit_code', 'gate', 'git_sha', 'host', 'mode', 'result', 'timestamp']
```

`host` is the machine, not the party. And `governance/landing/verdict.py` types the reviewer as `reviewer_id: Optional[str]`:

```
$ grep -n 'reviewer_id' governance/landing/verdict.py
52:    reviewer_id: Optional[str]
```

So independence is guaranteed **inside the merge model's state machine** and is **not observable on the landed artifact**. Under autonomous merge one agent can author a change, run its own `make verify`, and merge — the gate is a different *mechanism* but the artifact cannot show it was a different *party*. That is precisely AO-GR-13's *"never by the author alone"*.

## Deliverables

1. **Record the verifying identity on the artifact.** The session identity already exists in the environment (`AO_SESSION_ID`, `AO_ISSUE`, `AO_BRANCH` — rule 15, `governance/isolation/`) and the claim ledger already knows the agent (`governance/dispatch`). Write it into `.verify/attestation.json` so a landed artifact can be attributed.
2. **Assert what can be asserted.** Where the author is known (the issue's claim / the branch's session), a check must be able to compare it against the verifying identity. Do **not** claim more than that: recording the identity is what makes independence *observable*; whether a given pair differs is a policy the landing path can then enforce.
3. **Flip AO-GR-13 to `ENFORCED`** in `scripts/control-coverage.tsv`, naming the control.
4. **Empty the shrink-only record** with `bash scripts/check-control-coverage.sh --record` — the first time it reaches zero, which is the epic's exit condition.

items.title: gates: 3 committed suites (162 passing tests) are run by no gate — and check-drift cannot see two of them
items.body:
## Summary

**162 passing tests are run by no gate**, in 3 committed suites — and neither mechanism that should catch this can: the discovery that *does* see them only **warns (rc 0)**, and its scope is a hardcoded prefix list that excludes two of the three.

Found while measuring something else, and refined twice before I believed it — each earlier version of this number was wrong. The refinements are kept below because they are the point.

## The measurement

```bash
$ git ls-files | ... # every tracked module holding test_*.py, vs the manifest
tracked modules with test_*.py  : 98
declared in pytest-suites.txt   : 87
absent from the manifest        : 11
```

The naive reading is "11 ungated suites". **That is wrong**, because *declared* is not the only way a suite gets run — 8 of the 11 are run by a dedicated check:

```
governance/landing                    -> scripts/check-landing.sh
governance/onboarding/shared-frontend  -> scripts/check-shared-frontend-onboarding.sh
integrations/erp/{api,core,crm,finops,ops,tx} -> scripts/check-erp-{api,core-model,crm,finops,ops,tx}.sh
```

That leaves **3 suites run by nothing**, all of which pass today:

| suite | tests | why the manifest does not cover it |
|---|---|---|
| `control-plane/instructions/csuite` | 93 | `control-plane/instructions` **is** declared (line 57) — but the runner executes `"$mod/tests"`, so a *nested* suite is not collected |
| `engine/core/tickets` | 39 | `engine/core` **is** declared (line 50) — same nesting |
| `governance/waves` | 30 | not declared, and no check names it |

```
$ env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q control-plane/instructions/csuite/tests   # 93 passed
$ env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q engine/core/tickets/tests                  # 39 passed
$ env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q governance/waves/tests                     # 30 passed
```

`scripts/run-pytest-suites.sh:70` — `local tdir="$mod/tests"`: **path-exact and non-recursive.** So a suite nested under a declared module is invisible *while looking covered*, which is worse than being plainly absent: a reviewer checking "is `engine/core` declared?" gets yes.

## Why the two mechanisms that should catch this do not

**1. `scripts/check-drift.sh` sees one of the three, and only warns.** It discovers suites via `git ls-files '*/tests/conftest.py'` and then filters:

```bash
case "$mod" in
  guardrails/*|gateway/*|registry/*|identity/*|engine/*|telemetry/*)
```

That hardcoded prefix list is the whole scope. `control-plane/*`, `governance/*`, `integrations/*`, `fleet/*`, `portal/*` and `e2e/*` are **never examined** — which is also why the 6 ERP suites were invisible to it. And `engine/core/tickets` *is* in scope and *is* reported:

```
$ bash scripts/check-drift.sh
check-drift: WARN — 'engine/core/tickets' has a committed tests/ dir but is not declared in
scripts/pytest-suites.txt (register it or drop it)
RC=0
```

**RC=0.** `check-drift.sh` is denylisted from `make verify` and runs under `scripts/gate.sh` / `scripts/merge-gate.sh`, so this is a gate control whose only signal on this whole class is a stderr line that cannot fail anything. GR-12: a gate that cannot fail is a formality.

**2. The discovery also requires a `conftest.py`**, so a suite without one is not merely undeclared — it is undiscoverable by the mechanism meant to report it.

## Deliverables

1. **Register the 3** — `control-plane/instructions/csuite`, `engine/core/tickets`, `governance/waves` — or delete them. Registering is one line each; the tests already pass, so this is 162 tests of coverage currently being paid for and not collected.
2. **Fix the nesting blind spot.** Either declare nested suites, or make the manifest's semantics explicit and asserted (path-exact is a defensible choice — it just has to be *checked*, not assumed). An assertion that every tracked `*/tests/` holding `test_*.py` is either declared **or** named by a `check-*.sh` closes it regardless of nesting.
3. **Replace the prefix list with discovery**, so `control-plane/`, `governance/` and `integrations/` are covered rather than assumed.
4. **Make it fail.** A committed suite that no gate runs is a coverage loss; at minimum it should be a failure for a suite the repo tracks, not a stderr warning — and the 8 cases above show the correct escape hatch already exists (a dedicated check satisfies the requirement).

## A note on how this was measured

Three wrong numbers preceded this one: `147` (a nested `.claude/worktrees/` checkout was counted as committed suites), `11` (treating "not in the manifest" as "not gated", when 8 have dedicated checks), and the first pass looked only at one mechanism. `docs/CONTROL-COVERAGE.md` records the same lesson from the other direction. **"Is this covered?" has several mechanisms, and a single grep answers the wrong question.**

AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW)
