items.title: EPIC: every surface to elite, zero-human operation, paperclip/hermes at the head
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
# EPIC — Every surface to `elite`, zero-human operation, paperclip/hermes at the head

**Goal:** every measured surface in this repo reports `elite` on the solution-class ladder (`docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md`), the whole intake → dispatch → execute → verify → merge → observe loop runs with zero human steps after the single bootstrap defined in #160, and the paperclip/hermes seam is the admitted head of the org — all delivered as flag-gated IaC with no-false-green gates. Done is when `make verify` and `make gate` are green and the conformance gate measures `elite` for every row in `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml`.

## Lineage — where this sits

- **Parent:** EPIC-00 (#4, closed). That epic is the E2E blueprint (five pillars + identity, control-plane/portal, autonomous ops) and its definition of done ("entirely agent-built and flag-gated"). This epic is the ladder-promotion and hands-off pass over the surfaces #4 produced; it does not reopen #4.
- **Depends on, does not duplicate:** #160 (Session Fleet Operating Model). #160 owns session topology, the steering channel, the fleet-brain dispatcher, the FinOps chooser and the single-bootstrap runbook. This epic consumes that operating model as the execution engine for its lanes and inherits its "zero human steps after the DSv4FNone switch" bar.
- **Sequenced as children (subsumed by this epic's DoD, tracked in their own issues):** #607 (portal live surfaces to production), #706 (cron automation into the shared-services container), #708 (runaway prevention and governance controls), #803 (delivery controls), #873 (every spine rule traceable to a control), #696 (contract-first dispatch), #665 (DeepSeek/ERPNext FinOps engine). Each remains its own lane; this epic closes only when all of them are closed and the ladder measurement confirms the class they claim.
- **Cross-repo dependencies (named, not closable here):** see "Head of the org" below.

## Why — the measured gap, in the repo's own units

`docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md` measures each surface by artifact presence: `pattern` (contract + suite + gate) → `enterprise` (+ `controls`, `audit`, `schema`, `rollback`) → `faang` (+ dedicated `scripts/check-*` gate) → `elite` (+ a `live_sync` module under the path). As of the 2026-09-14 measurement **nothing is `elite`:**

| Surface | Path | Measured | What holds it down |
|---|---|---|---|
| `portal` | `portal` | `pattern` | declares no shared schema |
| `gateway` | `gateway` | `faang` | no live-sync module |
| `telemetry` | `telemetry` | `enterprise` | no dedicated `check-*telemetry*` gate |
| `registry` | `registry` | `faang` | no live-sync module |
| `module-registry` | `governance/modules` | `faang` | no live-sync module |
| `module-brief` | `integrations/paperclip/reporting` | `faang` | no live-sync module |
| `dispatch` | `governance/dispatch` | `pattern` | no controls/audit/schema |
| `isolation` | `governance/isolation` | `pattern` | no controls/schema |
| `lifecycle` | `governance/lifecycle` | `pattern` | no controls/schema |
| `reconcile` | `governance/reconcile` | `pattern` | no audit/controls/schema |

The acceptance criterion for every lane is therefore mechanical: the measurement gate (#351, #590, #620) reports `elite` for that row, with the artifacts real (no-false-green — the #852 ratchet and #868/#871 repairs apply).

## Head of the org — paperclip / hermes (cross-repo dependency)

The owner intent is paperclip (operator/ING seam, ADR-0013) and hermes (agent head, ADR-0012 boundary) at the top of the org chart. Inside this repo the seam already exists: `integrations/paperclip/` adapters + auth bridge, 14 `scripts/check-paperclip-*.sh` gates, `gateway/providers/hermes.py`, `registry/profiles/seeds/hermes.1.0.0.yaml`, `registry/personas/cards/hermes.yaml`, and the reachability e2e. What blocks "at the head" is **module admission**, which lives outside this repo:

| Dependency | Where | Owner | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| hermes-agents, paperclip, ollama admitted as hub modules | kushin77/CMR catalog (drift noted in CMR#952) | CMR hub owner | `admission='requested'` in `docs/MODULE-REGISTRY.md` |
| hermes-agents manifest / parent block | kushin77/hermes-agents#3 | hermes-agents owner | open |
| Diagrams capability register C10–C16 | kushin77/diagrams#513–#516 | diagrams owner | direction issues filed |

This epic's lanes L9 and L10 make this repo's side of the seam `elite` and keep the register honest; they do **not** claim admission. Admission flips when the hub owner lands it, and `docs/MODULE-REGISTRY.md` records that as a follow-up, not as a criterion this epic can close.

## Other stated gaps folded in as children

- Solution-class ladder is defined in kushin77/CMR, not copied locally; ADR-0010 defers copy ownership. Child: decide and record (L4).
- Model / SME / solution-class trio canonicity is "TO BE DECIDED" in `docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md` §3.1. Child: decide and record (L4).
- CMR vendor compliance gaps #132 / #133. Child: L8.

## Lanes — one issue = one lane = one branch = disjoint files (`docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md`)

Tiers follow the fleet FinOps ladder (L0 flash/haiku default; L1 sonnet for multi-file, security, IaC — never below L1 for auth/secrets/IaC; L2 opus only for decisions). Every lane ships flag-gated OFF (GR-28), pushes before gate (AO-GR-23), and is admission-controlled (GR-22).

| # | Lane | Goal (one line) | Files owned (disjoint) | Tier | Target class | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Portal live surfaces ("load all new") | Portal owns a schema and a live-sync module so every new surface/lane/claim appears in the console without a deploy | `portal/server/livestore.py`, `portal/server/app.py` (routes only), `control-plane/cockpit/**`, `portal/schemas/**` (new) | L1 | `portal`: `pattern` → `elite` | `scripts/check-surface-class.sh portal` → `elite`; #607 closed |
| L2 | Portal env / Secret Manager | All console runtime config sourced from Secret Manager via IaC; no env drift between local, Cloud Run and Terraform | `infra/portal/auth_env.py`, `infra/terraform/modules/web-surface/**`, `portal/Dockerfile` | L1 (secrets) | IaC cross-cut | `make verify` secrets check green; `terraform plan` clean under flag OFF |
| L3 | Atomic-commit gates | Every merge carries a per-check attestation; a red is never reported green; gate output is tri-state and machine-read by the fleet | `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/check-*.sh` (gate contract only), `.verify/attestation.json` schema | L1 | gate spine | `make gate` green; #852 ratchet holds; #865/#866 closed |
| L4 | Class / pattern / template canon | Ladder copied or pinned locally per ADR-0010; trio canonicity decided; every module declares its class in `module.json` and the conformance gate reads it | `module.json`, `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml`, `docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md`, `docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md` §3.1, new ADR | L2 (decision only), then L0 | governance: `pattern` → `elite` | conformance gate reads declared vs measured, no row `< declared` |
| L5 | IaC | Terraform root + modules cover every deployed surface (control-plane, web-surface, fleet scheduler image), all behind flags OFF; no ad-hoc apply (GR-5) | `infra/terraform/**` (except web-surface, L2), `infra/fleet/**` | L1 | `class:iac` mandate | `terraform validate` + plan-no-diff in CI; #706 closed |
| L6 | Fleet reconcile / runaway | Reconcile, isolation, lifecycle, dispatch each own controls + audit + schema + live feed; runaway bounded | `governance/reconcile/**`, `governance/isolation/**`, `governance/lifecycle/**`, `governance/dispatch/**`, `fleet/brain.py` | L1 | 4 governance rows: `pattern` → `elite` | `check-reconcile.sh`, `check-session-isolation.sh`, `check-github-lifecycle.sh`, `check-chronological-dispatch.sh` all green at `elite`; #708, #696 closed |
| L7 | Telemetry | Dedicated `scripts/check-telemetry.sh` gate plus a live feed so FinOps metering is observable in the portal | `telemetry/**`, `scripts/check-telemetry.sh` (new) | L0/L1 | `telemetry`: `enterprise` → `elite` | measurement → `elite`; #665 consumes feed |
| L8 | CMR intent & management | Knowledge indexer consumes the CMR pin live; vendor compliance gaps closed; pin drift is a red gate | `governance/knowledge/**`, `vendor/CMR` pin (submodule ref only), `scripts/check-cmr-*.sh` | L0/L1 | knowledge: → `elite` | `validate-cmr-pin.py` green; #132, #133 closed |
| L9 | Paperclip activation & org management | Paperclip seam owns live sync of tickets/heartbeats/budgets into this org; auth bridge measured `elite` | `integrations/paperclip/**`, `scripts/check-paperclip-*.sh` | L1 (auth) | `module-brief`: `faang` → `elite` | all 14 paperclip gates green; ADR-0013 contract tests pass |
| L10 | Hermes head | Hermes provider + profile + persona are the registered head; gateway/registry gain live-sync modules | `gateway/providers/hermes.py`, `gateway/sync/**` (new), `registry/profiles/seeds/hermes.1.0.0.yaml`, `registry/personas/cards/hermes.yaml`, `registry/sync/**` (new) | L1 | `gateway`, `registry`, `module-registry`: `faang` → `elite` | measurement → `elite`; `test_hermes_ollama_reachability.py` green |
| L11 | Control coverage | Every spine rule (GR-1…29, AO-GR) maps to a control with a gate; delivery controls present | `governance/controls/**`, `docs/GOVERNANCE.md` | L1 | governance | #803, #873 closed |

No two lanes share a file. `portal/server/app.py` is split by route ownership between L1 (live surfaces) and nothing else; L2 does not touch `portal/server/`. Any lane that discovers a file conflict files a split issue before touching it.

## Definition of done (epic level)

- Zero human steps after the #160 bootstrap: a brain directive flows brain → sister → subagent → PR → merge with evidence, for every lane above.
- `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml`: every row measures `elite`, with `live_sync` a real module (not a stub), and the #852 no-false-green ratchet still passing.
- All new infrastructure flag-gated OFF (GR-28); `terraform plan` shows no diff at OFF.
- `make verify` and `make gate` green on `master` HEAD.
- Cross-repo admission for paperclip/hermes recorded in `docs/MODULE-REGISTRY.md` with current state; not a blocker for closing this epic.
- Child epics #607, #706, #708, #803, #873, #696, #665 closed.

## Non-goals

- Does not rebuild #160's session topology or the hub's A2A layer (M9).
- Does not claim hub-side module admission (CMR#952 / hermes-agents#3).
- No tenant-facing product features beyond what makes surfaces measurable.

## Verify

```bash
make verify
make gate
```

## Chain

Lanes L1–L11 are filed as child issues, one per lane, labeled `type:task`, `class:elite`, with the lane's tier and files in the body. Filing order follows the gate spine first (L3, L4), then IaC (L5, L2), then surfaces (L1, L6, L7, L8, L9, L10), then coverage (L11).

items.title: Retire the measured shell-pattern gaps (SP-7 SP-8) and enforce them (EPIC #616, after #621)
items.body:
## Objective

Retire the **measured** shell-pattern gaps that issue #621's doctrine declares but
does not yet enforce, and turn the two declared detectors on in
`scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` — one lane, one edit, at the point the repo is
already clean.

## Why this is separate from #621

#621 shipped the doctrine and the gate. Two of the patterns it names could not be
enforced on landing without reddening `master` on day one — a gate that is red on
master is either disabled or ignored, which is strictly worse than no gate. They
are therefore **declared and measured** in `docs/SHELL-PATTERNS.md`, with the exact
sites, and graded DECLARED-ONLY rather than silently loosened or grandfathered.

## Measured sites (2026-09-16, at #621's landing commit)

**SP-7 — scratch created with no template (the shared, periodically-cleaned `$TMPDIR`):**

```
scripts/check-chronological-dispatch.sh:106  work="$(mktemp -d)" || {
scripts/check-fleet-runbook.sh:130           work="$(mktemp -d)"
scripts/check-orphan-handoff.sh:173          tmp="$(mktemp -d)" || { ... }
scripts/check-terraform.sh:59                td="$(mktemp -d)"
scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh:214        tmp="$(mktemp -d)" || { ... }
```

**SP-8 — a `cd` whose failure is not handled:**

```
infra/cloudflare/ao-ssh-access.sh:68         cd "$root"
```

The good shape is already the repo's majority idiom (10 sites use an explicit
`/tmp/<name>.XXXXXX` template; `docs/SCRATCH-SPACE-DISCIPLINE.md` is the canonical
statement), so this is a retrofit of six lines, not a change of practice.

## Scope

- the six sites above (one line each: an explicit `/tmp/<name>.XXXXXX` template, and
  `cd "$root" || exit 2`);
- `scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` — promote SP-7 and SP-8 from DECLARED to
  ENFORCED (add the two detectors, two plants, and the labels);
- `docs/SHELL-PATTERNS.md` — move the two rows out of the gap table and into the
  enforced table.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `bash scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` reports 8 patterns, each refused by
  name, with every detector proven load-bearing (the gate's own mutation half)
- [ ] the six sites are fixed, not recorded: no new baseline, no allowlist
- [ ] `make verify` green

## Verify

```
bash scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh && bash scripts/check-docs.sh
```

items.title: EPIC: enterprise control coverage — every platform/SaaS spine rule (AO-GR-12…20) traceable to a control that can fail
items.body:
## Objective

Make the platform/SaaS spine **auditable as a product**: every rule in Part B of
`docs/GOLDEN-RULES.md` (AO-GR-12…20) traceable, in machine-checkable form, to

1. the **module(s)** that implement it, and
2. the **control** that enforces it — which must exist and be **gate-discovered**,
   never merely cited.

Enterprises do not buy "we have tenant isolation"; they buy **the control, its owner,
and its test**. Today this product has the controls but not the traceability.

## The measurement (2026-09-16, `origin/master`)

For each Part B rule, which `scripts/check-*.sh` cites it:

| Rule | Subject | Gate check citing the rule |
|---|---|---|
| AO-GR-12 | control plane never executes | **none** |
| AO-GR-13 | independent auditor | **none** |
| AO-GR-14 | separation of duties | **none** |
| AO-GR-15 | tenant isolation is structural | **none** |
| AO-GR-16 | DLP + prompt-injection on every interaction | **none** |
| AO-GR-17 | tamper-evident audit ledger | **none** |
| AO-GR-18 | per-tenant budgets, quotas, kill switch | `check-chat-finops.sh` |
| AO-GR-19 | guard honesty: tri-state + negative controls | 12 checks |
| AO-GR-20 | private by default | **none** |

**7 of 9 have no control that names them.** By contrast Part C already has exactly
this machinery: `scripts/check-fleet-durability-rules.sh` asserts each of AO-GR-21…27
carries Rule/Why/Verify **and** a backing control, and is the only check in the repo
that maps rules to controls generically.

The asymmetry is the gap. The *controls* largely exist — they simply do not cite the
rule they enforce, so no reader (human or auditor) can go from rule → control.

> ### Correction (2026-09-16, after the first lane landed)
>
> Two claims this epic opened with were **wrong**, and the way they were wrong is
> the most useful thing the lane produced, so it is recorded rather than edited
> away.
>
> **`7 of 9 have no control that names them` is a citation count, not a coverage
> count.** The controls largely exist — `guardrails/isolation` fails closed on a
> foreign row and its deliberately-leaky fixture proves the scanner reports a
> planted leak. What was missing was the **edge** from rule to control. The
> sentence above ("has the controls but not the traceability") was right; the
> number was read as coverage, which it never was.
>
> **`AO-GR-15 ships inert` was false.** It rested on
> `grep -rn test_tenant_isolation scripts/*.sh scripts/pytest-suites.txt` → empty. The
> grep was really empty; `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` declares **module
> directories**, never test filenames (`telemetry/ledger` is line 51,
> `guardrails/isolation` line 25), so a search for a filename could not have
> matched. **An empty grep for the wrong pattern is not evidence of absence.** Both
> suites are declared and gate-run (`make gate` runs every declared suite in
> isolation). The child issue was corrected and closed: #875.
>
> Measured, on the corrected map: **8 of 9 rules ENFORCED, 1 PARTIAL.** The
> remedy was structural — a suite control (`suite:<dir>`) is now asserted
> *against the manifest*, with its own provocation, instead of searched for by name.

## Deliverables

1. a **machine-checkable `Control:` line** on every AO-GR-12…20 rule naming its
   enforcing check(s) and implementing module(s);
2. **`docs/CONTROL-COVERAGE.md`** — the enterprise control map (rule → module →
   control → status), which doubles as the vendor-review document;
3. **`scripts/check-control-coverage.sh`** — the gate: every rule carries a `Control:`
   line, every named control exists **and is gate-discovered**, every named module
   path exists; a **shrink-only record** carries the rules that have no control yet
   and **refuses a NEW gap**; with a vacuity control proving the check can fail.

## Children

- the coverage map + gate + spine `Control:` lines (this lane);
- **AO-GR-15**: DONE — enforced by `suite:guardrails/isolation` (fail-closed
  scope gate + a leaky fixture proven to be caught) and `suite:telemetry/ledger`.
  The child (#875) was closed as based on a false measurement.
- **AO-GR-13 — the only remaining item, and the residual is now a named field**:
  enforced as far as `check-landing.sh` (refuses a red attestation, refuses a green
  one naming *another* commit, CANNOT-ASSESS on none) **and** `suite:governance/merge`
  (a declared suite — the state machine requiring verify-gate green + an
  **independent SME reviewer** + no self-merge, whose own words are *"A reviewer is
  never the author/executor of the work it reviews"*; the landing seam delegates to it
  with no fallback). What is **not** proven is the **attribution**: the attestation
  the landing gate judges carries **no identity field at all** (`branch, check_count,
  checks, exit_code, gate, git_sha, host, mode, result, timestamp`) and
  `verdict.reviewer_id` is `Optional[str]`, so independence is guaranteed *inside the
  merge model* and is not observable *on the landed artifact*. That is a field to add.
- the remaining Part B rules whose controls are domain checks that do not name the
  rule (12/14/16/17/20) — one lane per rule group as the record shrinks.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-control-coverage.sh
make verify
```

items.title: check-isolation-landed produced a false red in the gate of record, and its own output disproves it (#852 idiom, fired)
items.body:
## What happened

A gate run on `#868` (worktree `ao-868-a2f27554`, head `788a852`) ended:

```
verify: FAIL (1 of 127 checks failed, 4 skipped: module-registry, module-brief, diagrams-declaration, codeidx-surface)
make: *** [Makefile:146: verify] Error 1
```

The single failure is **not reproducible** — and its own output disproves it.

```
== isolation-landed ==
  OK    no lane records is CANNOT-ASSESS, never OK (rc=2, naming CANNOT-ASSESS)
  OK    an isolated lane with a trailed commit is OK (rc=0)
  FAIL  a recorded lane whose commit omits the trailer is NOT-OK (rc=1 but commit-missing-ticket-trailer was never named)
          FAIL  lane 56bfc450d778
                  commit-missing-ticket-trailer: 1 commit(s) authored by agent+gate-agent@agents.invalid lack
                  'Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#264' in their trailing trailer block, as named by the shared
                  predicate in scripts/check-pr-contract.sh: eb3dcc73 (commit-missing-ticket-trailer)
        session-isolation: FAIL (1 of 1 lane(s) not isolated)
check-isolation-landed: FAIL (1 violation(s))
```

**Read those two blocks together.** The assertion says `commit-missing-ticket-trailer was never named`
— and then the check prints the captured output as its detail, in which
`commit-missing-ticket-trailer` appears twice. The string it claims is absent is right there in the
evidence it printed.

## The line

`scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh:136` — one of the three legacy sites `#852` recorded for this file:

```bash
128:  local label="$1" want="$2" name="$3" out rc
130:  out="$("$@" 2>&1)"
131:  rc=$?
132:  if [ "$rc" -ne "$want" ]; then
133:    printf '  FAIL  %s — expected rc=%s, got rc=%s\n' "$label" "$want" "$rc" >&2
135:    fail=$((fail + 1))
136:  elif ! printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF -- "$name"; then
137:    printf '  FAIL  %s (rc=%s but %s was never named)\n' "$label" "$rc" "$name" >&2
```

Under `set -uo pipefail`, `grep -q` exits on its **first** match, `printf` is then killed by SIGPIPE
while still writing, and `pipefail` promotes that 141 to the status of the pipeline — so the negated
test reads *not named* for text that **is** named. That is exactly the defect `#852` is about, and
this is no longer hypothetical: **a recorded legacy site fired and produced a false red in the gate
of record.**

Size is the trigger, which is why it is intermittent and why it hit under load: this box was running
four concurrent gates at the time, so the audit's report was large enough to pass the 64 KiB pipe
buffer. When the report is small, the same line behaves.

## Measurement

| run | where | result |
|---|---|---|
| the gate run above (4 concurrent gates) | lane `ao-868-a2f27554` | **FAIL** on this check |
| 3 × standalone, same lane, same commit | lane `ao-868-a2f27554` | rc=0, rc=0, rc=0 — `check-isolation-landed: OK` |
| standalone | shared checkout on master | rc=0 — `check-isolation-landed: OK` |

The lane and commit it named do not exist afterwards (`isolation list` does not contain
`56bfc450d778`; `eb3dcc73` is not a revision in the repository) — they are the fixture the control
fabricates for itself, which the audit then correctly refused. So the *verdict* was right and its
**reporting was wrong**: it failed the control by failing to see its own name in the evidence.

## Fix

Replace the piped test at `check-isolation-landed.sh:136` — and the two other recorded sites in the
same file (lines 235 and 299) — with a bash-native containment test, exactly as `#843` and `#852` did:

```bash
contains() { case "$1" in *"$2"*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }

  elif ! contains "$out" "$name"; then
```

Then re-run `bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh --record` to **shrink** the record by three.

## Why this is worth doing now rather than when convenient

It is a **false red in the gate of record** — the worst direction for a fleet gate, because it stops
correct work and teaches lanes to re-run until green. Three of the four `#840`/`#852`/`#694`/`#868`
gate runs on this box were affected by contention in some way, and this is the first one traced to a
specific line rather than inferred.

Verify: `bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` · `bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh` · `make verify`

Pillar: autonomous-ops · Area: fleet · Class: elite

items.title: A baseline ratchet reds the gate for every lane that branched before it (master red after #852)
items.body:
## What happened

`#852` merged a **shrink-only ratchet** for the piped-`grep -q` idiom
(`scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh` + `scripts/verdict-contains-legacy.tsv`). A post-merge
verification of `origin/master` (`4dd0114`) then found three files **exceeding the record**, so
the gate of record is **red on master**:

```
$ bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh        # on origin/master
== 5. the repository against its record ==
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-docs.sh has 1, the record allows 0
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-marker-scan.sh has 1, the record allows 0
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-orphan-handoff.sh has 1, the record allows 0
  legacy still recorded: 118 site(s) in 55 file(s)
check-verdict-contains: FAIL (3 finding(s); 9 control(s) passed)
RC=1
```

Every one of the three is the same latent defect, not a false alarm:

| file | site | polarity | why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scripts/check-docs.sh` | `printf '%s' "$out" \| grep -qF "$d/$f" \|\| missing=…` | positive | a large report makes the test fail and the file is reported **missing** — a false red |
| `scripts/check-marker-scan.sh` | `… \| grep -qF 'marker-scan\|bash scripts/check-marker-scan.sh'` | positive | the wiring assertion can be skipped — the check **fails open** |
| `scripts/check-orphan-handoff.sh` | `… sweep --help \| grep -q -- '--apply'` | positive | can report "no longer offers --apply" spuriously (mine, from `#694`) |

## The general defect this exposes (the part worth keeping)

**A baseline ratchet is unsound while sibling lanes are in flight.** The record is written from
the bytes of *one* branch, but it is *enforced on master* — and any lane that branched **before**
the record existed merges code the record has never seen. Its own gate passes (the ratchet was
not on its base at all), and it reds the gate **for everyone** at merge time.

That is exactly what happened here: `#852` wrote the record at 23:55; `#856` (ERP-06), `#766`
and `#804` merged after it, each having branched before it, so each injected a site the record
could not have known about. The `#694` lane went further: it branched before `#852` merged, so
its gate never ran the ratchet at all, and it added a file with one.

Two things follow, and neither is "loosen the ratchet":

1. **An introduced ratchet needs a merge-time re-derivation**, not just a branch-time baseline:
   the record must be re-derived against `master` after the merges that followed it, and any
   difference resolved *before* the next lane merges — otherwise the ratchet converts one lane's
   improvement into every other lane's red.
2. **A ratchet whose only remedy is "fix it elsewhere" needs the fix to be cheap and local.**
   Here it is: all three sites are a one-line bash-native replacement.

This is the same shape as the `#843` false-negative it descends from: the control was right, and
the *system around it* was what could not fail.

## The fix in this change

Repair all three sites bash-natively (as `#843`/`#852` did), then **shrink** the record, which is
the direction `--record` accepts without a review of the code it describes.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh
bash scripts/check-docs.sh
bash scripts/check-marker-scan.sh
bash scripts/check-orphan-handoff.sh
make verify
```

Pillar: autonomous-ops · Area: gates · Class: elite

items.title: fleet: check-verdict-contains is red on master — 3 new containment sites block every lane's make verify
items.body:
## Summary

`check-verdict-contains` is **red on `master`**, and it reddens **every lane's
`make verify`** — including lanes unrelated to the files it names. The findings
are *new* occurrences of the pattern the check forbids, in files this lane does
not own.

Measured while landing #651 (ERP-06), whose own gate is green; the red is
**inherited**, not introduced.

## The measurement

```
$ git rev-parse origin/master
4dd0114898ad1f34917062d5953dbe6498fd3153

$ bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh                      # rc=1
== 5. the repository against its record ==
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-docs.sh has 1, the record allows 0
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-marker-scan.sh has 1, the record allows 0
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-orphan-handoff.sh has 1, the record allows 0
        Use a bash-native containment test (see the header) instead.
  legacy still recorded: 118 site(s) in 55 file(s)

check-verdict-contains: FAIL (3 finding(s); 9 control(s) passed)
```

At the merge of #651 (`d817d35110f96627593f2fc364574cf5a2b19752`, whose parent is
`7fb7923da0f756ad8bf82a7df1b2f04ac9a9f5cc`) there were **two** findings; the third
(`scripts/check-orphan-handoff.sh`) arrived with #864. The set is growing.

## Why it is not this lane's, proved two ways

1. **The merge touched only its own files.** `git diff --name-only 7fb7923d d817d35`
   lists exactly 25 paths — 24 under `integrations/erp/api/` plus
   `scripts/check-erp-api.sh`. Neither named file is among them, and their blob
   hashes are identical on both commits
   (`scripts/check-docs.sh` → `f2bdaf982927822399cb4f8ba37d108930bf9e31`,
   `scripts/check-marker-scan.sh` → `2e9b8799683d214634b537582ecc0de45c80008f`).
2. **The check fails identically on the pre-merge master.** Run on a scratch
   worktree at `7fb7923d`, `check-verdict-contains` exits **1** with the same two
   findings, so the reds existed before the merge and the merge neither introduced
   nor fixed them.

## Why it matters (the check is right, and it is load-bearing)

Per `scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh`'s own header: `printf '%s' "$report" |
grep -qF -- "$needle"` is not a containment test — `grep -q` exits on its first
match and the producer is killed by **SIGPIPE** while still writing, which
`set -o pipefail` promotes to the status of the whole pipeline. The defect is
latent (it depends on the report outgrowing the 64 KiB pipe buffer) and, negated
(`if ! … | grep -q`), it reports **ABSENT for text that is PRESENT** — a check that
fails **open**. That is worth fixing rather than recording.

The fix belongs to the files' own lanes (`scripts/check-docs.sh`,
`scripts/check-marker-scan.sh`, `scripts/check-orphan-handoff.sh`): replace the
containment with a bash-native test (e.g. `[[ $report == *"$needle"* ]]`, as the
header directs). `--record` deliberately **refuses** to raise
`scripts/verdict-contains-legacy.tsv`, so adding the sites to the record is not the
route the tool offers.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

1. `bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh` exits **0** on `master` (all three
   occurrences replaced, no new ones).
2. `make verify` is green on `master` — currently **no lane** can be, so this
   blocks every in-flight PR's union gate.
3. The nine controls inside the check keep passing (`9 control(s) passed`), i.e.
   the check keeps refusing a planted occurrence.

## Verify

```
bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh          # rc 0
make verify                                      # green on master
```

items.title: make verify is red on master since 7fb7923: three piped-`grep -q` sites the ratchet refuses by name (#852 follow-up)
items.body:
## Measured: `make verify` is red on `master`, and it has been since the ratchet landed

`scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh` (#863, committing #852) landed with a
shrink-only record, `scripts/verdict-contains-legacy.tsv`. Running the check on
the commit that **introduced it** — its own parent history — it already fails:

```
$ git worktree add --detach /tmp/parent 7fb7923   # the ratchet's own landing commit
$ bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh
== 5. the repository against its record ==
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-docs.sh has 1, the record allows 0
  FAIL  a NEW occurrence: scripts/check-marker-scan.sh has 1, the record allows 0
        Use a bash-native containment test (see the header) instead.
  legacy still recorded: 117 site(s) in 54 file(s)
check-verdict-contains: FAIL (2 finding(s); 9 control(s) passed)
RC=1
```

So the red is **not** attributable to any lane that merged after it. Every commit
that has landed since — including the ERP-06 merge `d817d35` (#856) — ran its
own gate green on its own head and then inherited this failure on the union.
`d817d35110f96627593f2fc364574cf5a2b19752` is red with exactly one non-zero
check in its attestation, and it is this one:

```
$ python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.verify/attestation.json'));print(d['result'],d['exit_code'],d['check_count'])"
FAIL 1 126
  NONZERO verdict-contains rc=1
```

The count has since grown from two to three: `4dd0114` (#864) added a site as
well.

## The three sites

| File | Line | Site |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/check-docs.sh` | 151 | `printf '%s' "$out" \| grep -qF "$d/$f" \|\| missing="$missing $f"` |
| `scripts/check-marker-scan.sh` | 191 | `printf '%s\n' "$wired" \| grep -qF 'marker-scan\|bash scripts/check-marker-scan.sh'` |
| `scripts/check-orphan-handoff.sh` | 135 | `python3 ... sweep --help 2>/dev/null \| grep -q -- '--apply'` |

Each is the defect the ratchet exists for: `grep -q` exits on its first match, the
producer is killed by SIGPIPE, and `set -o pipefail` promotes that `141` to the
pipeline's status — so a report larger than the 64 KiB pipe buffer reports ABSENT
for text that is PRESENT. Negated (check-docs) that is a **false red**; positive
(check-marker-scan, check-orphan-handoff) the control is skipped and the check
**fails open**. `check-orphan-handoff.sh` already defines the bash-native
`contains()` helper it should be using.

## Fix

Replace the piped idiom with the bash-native containment test in all three
checks — the remedy the ratchet's own message prescribes — and lower the record's
total with `--record` (shrink-only; the record may only shrink). No occurrence is
recorded: recording a new one is refused by design.

## Verify

- `bash scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh` — rc 0, 0 findings
- `bash scripts/check-docs.sh`, `bash scripts/check-marker-scan.sh`,
  `bash scripts/check-orphan-handoff.sh` — each still rc 0 (the fix removes the
  idiom, it does not weaken the control)
- `make verify` — green

items.title: A directive for an issue closed while it sits in sent has no retire path, and the loop still spends K attempts on it
items.body:
## The gap

An authorisation already sitting in `.fleet/sent/` whose issue is **closed** (as superseded, duplicate or otherwise) has **no path that retires it**:

* `governance/lifecycle/directive.py:171 consume()` is the only terminal move, and it refuses `by name` when *"the issue's change has not landed"* — correct for work still in flight, but a superseded issue has no change of its own, so it can never satisfy the predicate;
* `fleet/brain.py:534 closure_refusal()` prevents a **new** directive being issued for a closed issue (`state != open` ⇒ refuse, naming the board that said so, and writing no sent-marker) — but it does nothing about a marker already written;
* nothing else moves the file: `grep -rn supersed governance/lifecycle/*.py governance/dispatch/*.py fleet/brain.py` → **no matches**.

The record therefore strands in `sent/` while the issue is closed and unclaimable, and `governance/reconcile`'s audit reports a pending authorisation for work that cannot be done. `.fleet/sent/` is not a delivery queue (the inbox is separate — the #821 finding), so nothing re-dispatches it: it is board noise, not duplicate work. That is the only reason this is filed as a task and not as an incident.

## The measured cost at the loop level

The runaway guard (#723) **bounds** a failure rather than classifying it, so an order for a closed issue is retried up to K times before it retires:

```
$ AO_RUNAWAY_ATTEMPTS=3 AO_RUNAWAY_BACKOFF=1 python3 …     # scratch base
attempt=1/3 exhausted=False next_attempt_at=…
attempt=2/3 exhausted=False next_attempt_at=…
attempt=3/3 exhausted=True
dead-letter target: d-closed-234.json exists: True
```

with defaults read from `fleet/runaway.py` (`AO_RUNAWAY_ATTEMPTS=5`, base `AO_RUNAWAY_BACKOFF=30 s`, `BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS=300`) that is 30 + 60 + 120 + 240 ≈ **450 s of a held queue slot** before the closed-issue order dies (arithmetic from the measured constants; I did not wait it out). The terminal state is reached — it is just the slow road for work that was dead on arrival.

## The two halves, one cause

Both halves are the same missing idea: **a refusal that is terminal by definition** (closed issue, closed epic, unowned unit) is not distinguishable from a refusal that is worth retrying, so it is handled by the generic bounded retry and its authorisation cannot be retired.

## What I would build

1. A **named terminal classification** at the refusal site: a refusal for a closed issue/closed epic/unowned unit goes straight to the dead-letter path on the FIRST refusal instead of consuming K attempts.
2. A **retire path for the authorisation**: `directive.consume()` gains a terminal mode for an issue that is closed *without* a change of its own (the supersession case), recording the reason and the issue that superseded it — so the mailbox stops carrying an order nobody can execute.
3. A control that provokes it: a `sent` marker for a closed issue must be retireable, and must NOT be retireable while the issue is open and its change has not landed (the #821 invariant, preserved — this is the negative control that stops the new mode becoming a bypass).

## Concrete standing example

`brain-directive-a2a-692-6b3951b31bb3db7d.json` is in `.fleet/sent/` for **#692**, which I closed as superseded by #723 + #727 + #754 (evidence: [#692 comment]). It is inert and I have deliberately **not** hand-edited the mailbox to remove it — an unreviewed state change to a governed store is the drift #821 exists to prevent. It is the live example this issue asks to be made retirable.

## Verify (proposed)

```bash
bash scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh
bash scripts/check-dispatch-reconcile.sh
make verify
```

items.title: close-out: a transient gate PARK strands VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING, because reclaim-lane then removes the only tree the evidence could come from
items.body:
## Finding (measured 2026-09-15 closing out #793)

`governance/lifecycle/cli.py close` drives its steps in dependency order and each
step is idempotent on its own. **`record-verification` (step 2) can be defeated by
a transient PARK, and `reclaim-lane` (step 8) then removes the only tree the
evidence could have come from — so the invariant is stranded permanently.**

The transcript (close-out run from the main checkout, `origin/master` =
`f01b45d3`, lane record present, lane worktree present and clean):

```
close-out #793: NOT-OK
  skipped   merge-pull-request: already satisfied
  failed    record-verification: RuntimeError: d 2026-09-15T23:28:15Z
verify: PARKED (rc 11, not a pass and not a failure) — the box-wide gate cap is
reached; nothing was run and no attestation was touched
make: *** [Makefile:146: verify] Error 11
  ...
  performed reclaim-lane: close: OK — lane 1889fcda71c7 removed
  REMAINS  VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING  #793  no green verification attestation is recorded
```

Every subsequent pass is now guaranteed to fail the same step, for a different
reason that nothing can repair:

```
  failed    record-verification: RuntimeError: no lane worktree for #793; the verified tree no longer exists
  REMAINS  VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING  #793  ...
```

### Why this is the driver's order, not the operator's mistake

* the PARK is the **by-design** outcome of the gate admission control (#724,
  `docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md` §9): "work that cannot get a permit is **parked, not
  started**". On a box with four other lanes gating, it happens constantly and it
  is transient by construction;
* `record-verification` is the *only* step that produces `{"verify": {"ok": true,
  "commit": <verified head>}}` (`governance/lifecycle/closeout.py:173`,
  `ops.record_verification`), and it needs the lane worktree;
* `reclaim-lane` is step 8 and removes that worktree, so the retry the design
  relies on ("each step idempotent") cannot reach its subject again.

### Proposed direction (for the owning lane)

Either (a) do not `reclaim-lane` while a step above it is unsatisfied — a
close-out that is NOT-OK should leave the artifacts it still needs, which is what
`governance/reconcile` already reasons about ("the worker never trades unmerged
work for an unlocked issue"); or (b) make `record-verification` accept an
attestation produced elsewhere for the same commit (the SHA is the evidence, and
the branch field of a detached worktree's attestation is empty) so a PARK is
retried rather than fatal. Option (a) is the smaller change and keeps "evidence
names a commit" intact.

Found while landing #793. The green attestations exist and are quoted on #793 and
on PR #849 (`5940775` — the PR's verified head — and `f01b45d3`, the merge
commit, which is `origin/master`), but the invariant wants the attestation
*journalled by the driver*, and the driver's own step order prevented that.

items.title: The same false-negative idiom (printf | grep -q under pipefail) remains in four other gate checks
items.body:
## Objective

Four other checks in the gate of record carry the same false-negative idiom that
#843 removed from `scripts/check-session-isolation.sh`. This is a **filed
finding**, not work in progress: those files belong to other lanes and were not
touched.

## The mechanism (measured)

```bash
if ! printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF -- "$marker"; then   # under set -o pipefail
```

`grep -q` exits on its **first match**, SIGPIPE then terminates the producer, and
`pipefail` promotes that 141 to the status of the whole pipeline — so the test
reports **ABSENT for text that is PRESENT**. Measured on this box:

```
$ bash -c 'set -uo pipefail; big=$(printf "commit-missing-ticket-trailer\n%.0s" $(seq 1 5000)); \
           if printf "%s" "$big" | grep -qF -- "commit-missing-ticket-trailer"; then echo matched; else echo NO-MATCH; fi'
output bytes: 149999
IDIOM: reported NO-MATCH  <-- false verdict
```

The condition is the size of the report relative to the 64 KiB pipe buffer, so
each instance below is **latent** rather than observed red — a *large* report
from the thing being grepped is what converts it into a false red (or, where the
polarity is positive, a false green). `grep` is also a second process that under
load can fail to start or be killed, which is the same false verdict with no size
condition at all.

## The instances (measured, at the tree where #843 landed)

```
scripts/check-chronological-dispatch.sh
    143:  if ! printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF -- "$reason"; then
    151:    if ! printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF -- "$marker"; then
    183:elif ! printf '%s' "$grant_out" | grep -qF -- '"provenance"'; then
scripts/check-cto-overlay.sh
    179:if [ "$broken_rc" -ne 0 ] && printf '%s' "$broken_out" | grep -q 'PROBE-BROKEN.sh'; then
    199:if [ "$config_rc" -eq 2 ] && printf '%s' "$config_out" | grep -q 'CANNOT-ASSESS'; then
scripts/check-fleet-durability-rules.sh
     70:    printf '%s' "$body" | grep -qF -- "$part" || missing="$missing ${part}"
    105:  if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -qF -- "$ref"; then
scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh
    228:  if ! printf '%s' "$output" | grep -qF -- "\"$1\""; then
    276:elif ! printf '%s' "$output" | grep -qF -- "#300"; then
```

Note the polarity difference: `! printf … | grep -q` turns a pipeline failure
into a **FAIL**, while a bare `printf … | grep -q` turns it into a **PASS** — the
second shape is the more dangerous of the two.

## Suggested shape

Adopt the fix #843 used in `scripts/check-session-isolation.sh`: a bash-native
presence test, with no second process and no pipe.

```bash
contains() { # contains <haystack> <needle>
  case "$1" in
    *"$2"*) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}
```

`case` with a quoted pattern is an exact literal substring match, so it needs no
escaping for the markers these checks use, and it cannot be SIGPIPE'd or
OOM-killed. A check whose report could not be searched should say
**CANNOT-ASSESS**, never FAIL — the same rule #843 applied to the isolation
control's verdict mapping.

## Negative control to ask for

Each rewritten site needs one provoked case per polarity:

* a report that **contains** the marker must reach the same branch it always did;
* a report that does **not** contain it must still be reported as absent;
* and the rewritten helper must be shown to survive the shape that broke the old
  one (a report far larger than the pipe buffer, with the match early in it).

A helper that cannot be shown to fail is a formality, and one that fails *open*
is worse than none.

Refs #843

items.title: check-gitignore is red for every lane that claims locally: .board/claims/ is runtime state .gitignore does not cover
items.body:
## Finding (measured 2026-09-15, worktree `ao-793-1889fcda` @ `9598b62`)

A lane that follows `AGENTS.md` ("Claim the issue — `python3
governance/dispatch/cli.py claim --issue <n> --agent <id> --lane <lane>`") and
then runs the gate of record **in its own lane worktree** cannot pass
`check-gitignore`:

```
== 2. no untracked, unignored path under a runtime-state root ==
  FAIL  .board/claims/01789511881152259193-00793-copilot-brain-claim.json
        (untracked and not ignored — a git add would carry this runtime state into history)
check-gitignore: FAIL — 1 problem(s); runtime state under .board .fleet .verify is not safely ignored
```

The claim event is written by the tracked code (`governance/dispatch/claims.py`,
`DEFAULT_CLAIMS_DIR = .board/claims`) into `.board/claims/`, and `.gitignore`
covers `.board/locks/` and `.board/pool.jsonl` but **not** `.board/claims/`.

### Why it is not the lane's red

* a fresh worktree cut from `origin/master` (`/tmp/ao793base` @ `738d03d`) passes
  `check-gitignore: OK — 13/13 declared state directories ignored` — the check is
  green until a claim exists;
* the **shared checkout** is red for the same rule and always has been: it holds
  **1239** claim events under `.board/claims/`;
* `scripts/check-gitignore.sh` documents this itself: *"Tracked code writes
  runtime state to `.board/claims/` … and `.gitignore` covers none of the three.
  They are deliberately NOT on the declared coverage list … Extending
  `.gitignore` to cover them is a `.gitignore` change and belongs to a different
  lane."*

### Proposed direction (for the owning lane)

Add `/.board/claims/` to `.gitignore` (the per-event directory; `.board/claims.jsonl`
stays tracked as the frozen legacy ledger). That makes a claiming lane worktree
clean, which is the state `check-gitignore.sh` says it expects ("A lane worktree
cut from `master` is clean"), and removes a trap that costs every lane that
claims locally a diagnosis cycle.

Until then the workaround is to run the gate in a tree with no live claim state
(a detached worktree at the commit), which is what `#793`'s evidence does.

Found while landing #793 (the spawn envelope). Not fixed there: `.gitignore` is
not that lane's file, and the check's own documentation assigns the change to the
`.gitignore`/claims owner.

items.title: medium: the runner hold flaps every cycle — the release predicate is resolvability, and the hold is also taken for capability [G5]
items.body:
## Objective

`fleet/terminal.py` holds the queue for two runner conditions since #841 — the runner does not
**resolve**, or it cannot **honour** the model — but it releases the hold on the *first* condition
alone. So when the runner resolves and the capability fails, the two sites fight and the hold
**flaps every cycle**.

## Observed

Live, in `.fleet/sister.log` minutes after #841 merged (PR #844, master `4189bb6a`):

```
[terminal] RUNNER CANNOT HONOUR A DISPATCH — runner profile 'claude-byok' needs
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and it is unset — … — queue held, no directive dispatched
[terminal] runner resolvable again — queue hold released
[terminal] RUNNER CANNOT HONOUR A DISPATCH — … — queue held, no directive dispatched
[terminal] runner resolvable again — queue hold released
```

The mechanism, both sites named:

* `release_runner_hold()` is called at `fleet/terminal.py:2342`, inside `if runner_ok:` — i.e. on
  **resolvability**;
* the capability hold is taken lower down for the *same* cycle, so the next cycle's preflight
  releases what the previous cycle's capability check took;
* `release_runner_hold()` returns the line `"runner resolvable again — queue hold released"`, which
  is therefore printed every cycle and is **untrue** — the runner is still unable to honour a
  dispatch.

## Expected

One release site, on the **conjunction**: release only when the runner resolves *and* can honour the
model. The two conditions have one remedy each and must not be able to contradict each other in the
same log.

## What this does *not* break, stated so it is not overstated

The work stays held: the capability hold is taken *after* the release in each cycle, and the cycle
checks `paused()` afterwards, so no directive is dispatched. The measured defect is the **signal** —
a release line printed every cycle asserting something false — plus the churn of deleting and
rewriting `.fleet/runner-hold.json`, which makes the operator's view of the hold unusable.

## Severity

medium — no work is lost or dispatched; the defect is that a governed surface reports the opposite of
the truth, every cycle, from the change that exists to stop exactly that class of thing.

## Reproduction

```bash
# with the BYOK environment absent and a runner that resolves:
cd /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator && tail -6 .fleet/sister.log
grep -n 'release_runner_hold()' fleet/terminal.py      # two call sites: 2342 (resolvability) and the capability branch
```

## RCA link (governance/lessons/)

To record when it lands: **a hold and its release must be the same predicate.** Two checks were
added to one gate and only one of them was given the release, so the pair inverted.

items.title: Two checks in the gate of record report a FALSE RED under load (session-isolation, pytest-chat) — the same tree passes 6/6 when run directly
items.body:
## Objective

Decide and implement what a **load-sensitive check** may do. Two checks in the gate of
record produced a **false red** under load today, each costing a full ~15-minute gate
re-run, and in both cases the same tree passed the same check when run directly.

## Measured (2026-09-15, `master` @ `dd8cbfc` / `b89c480`)

### `session-isolation` — failed in a gate run, passes 6/6 directly

Lane `ao-835-917dfc5b` (PR #839), first gate run:

```
$ make verify
verify: FAIL (1 of 117 checks failed, 4 skipped: …)
non-zero non-skip: [('session-isolation', 1)]
```

Inside that run:

```
== session-isolation ==
  OK    a commit without the ticket trailer is refused (audit refused: commit-missing-ticket-trailer)
  FAIL  a later commit does not repair an untraceable one (audit failed without naming
        commit-missing-ticket-trailer)
          FAIL  lane 9eadd9fe49be
                  commit-missing-ticket-trailer: 1 commit(s) authored by agent+gate-agent@agents.invalid
                  lack 'Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#264' in their trailing trailer block … : 8f4d5d34
        session-isolation: FAIL (1 of 1 lane(s) not isolated)
  …  (all other 21 controls OK)
```

Note the shape: the audit **did** refuse the lane and **did** name
`commit-missing-ticket-trailer` in the lane detail — the control's own `expect_fail` helper
did not see it in the summary text it greps.

Directly, same tree, same commit:

```
$ for i in 1 2 3; do bash scripts/check-session-isolation.sh; done     # in the lane
run1 rc=0 22 OK, 0 FAIL
run2 rc=0 22 OK, 0 FAIL
run3 rc=0 22 OK, 0 FAIL

$ # and on master, in a scratch worktree with NONE of the lane's changes
master run1 rc=0 22 OK, 0 FAIL
master run2 rc=0 22 OK, 0 FAIL
master run3 rc=0 22 OK, 0 FAIL
```

So it is **not** a regression from the change under test: 6 consecutive passes, including
3 on unmodified `master`. The gate was re-run and came back
`verify: PASS (113 of 117 checks, 4 skipped)`, 0 non-zero non-skip.

### `pytest-chat` — same shape, seen twice

`pytest-chat` is `pytest -q gateway/chat/tests`. It **failed inside** two different gate
runs and **passes standalone twice** on the same tree:

```
$ python3 -m pytest -q gateway/chat/tests
50 passed in 29.11s
50 passed in 29.77s
```

Its failure inside the gate was `test_stream_content_matches_the_single_body`
(`json.loads` on an SSE frame) — and a second attempt at the whole gate then passed it, so
the post-merge verdict flipped between FAIL and PASS with no code change.

### The conditions were the same in both cases

Load average ~6–7 with 4–6 sibling `verify.sh` runs on the box (the admission control caps
concurrent **gates** at 4, but each gate fans out to many subprocesses). Both checks
provision real scratch repos / start real servers; both pass alone and fail interleaved.

## Why it matters

- **A false red is worse than a missing check.** It consumes a full gate cycle, and the
  honest response is a re-run — which is exactly the "re-run until green" habit a gate of
  record must not teach. Meanwhile a lane that *trusts* the first red either blocks a good
  merge or learns to ignore the check.
- **"Flaky" is not a verdict.** This repo's own tri-state (0/1/2, "an unmeasured run is
  never a pass") says a run the system cannot trust should be **CANNOT-ASSESS**, not FAIL.
  Today both checks report FAIL, which is a claim about the code that the evidence does not
  support.
- It compounds with the admission control: every parked/again-run gate costs another
  ~9–19 minutes, and the box is at its cap.

## Suggested shape (pick one, state it)

1. **Retry-once inside the check, with the retry recorded.** A control that fails on a
   *resource* (scratch repo provisioning, port bind, subprocess timeout) retries once and
   reports `CANNOT-ASSESS` if both attempts fail — and prints that it retried, so a retry
   can never silently become a pass. Cheap, and it is honest about what happened.
2. **Make them deterministic.** For `pytest-chat` the failure is a parsed SSE frame; for
   `session-isolation` it is a scratch-lane provisioning step. Both have a race or a
   timeout under contention; widening/fixing it is better than retrying, but needs the
   owner's context.
3. At minimum, **do not let a single-shot FAIL claim the code is wrong** when the same
   command passes 6/6 directly — the check should say what it observed.

**Negative control to ask for:** with the box loaded (sibling gates running), a deliberately
resource-starved control must report CANNOT-ASSESS under (1)/(3) — never FAIL — while a
genuinely broken control must still FAIL. A retry that cannot be observed is the same class
of defect as a gate that cannot fail.

Measured on `master` @ `dd8cbfc` (pre-merge) and `b89c480` (post-merge).

Parent: #160

items.title: P0: the fleet's executor cannot run — every subagent run dies on an unrecognized model, and nothing signals it
items.body:
{"body": "## Objective

Make the fleet's executor able to run, and make its *inability* to run visible. Today every subagent run fails on an unrecognized model, the watchdog reports both rungs **healthy**, and the only record of the failure is a log line nobody reads.

## Observed

`master` @ `dd8cbfc`, measured 2026-09-15. Re-dispatching the four ERP lanes (#648/#649/#651/#654) produced a claim → run → release loop with ~11–14s per attempt, and every run logged:

```
[subagent] "deepseek-v4-flash" isn't described by this version's model catalog; update Claude Code, or map it with behavesAs on a modelPicker row (or modelOverrides, if it is a provider id of a model this version knows).
[subagent] [claude-code:unrecognized_model] {"model":"deepseek-v4-flash","query_source":"sdk"}
[sister]   run finished: rc=1 status=failed | issue declares no runnable Verify: command | `make verify` rc=2: -649-6c01daaa, mode verify, started 2026-09-15T21:30:34Z); refusing to run a second composite gate in one worktree
```

Across `.fleet/runs/*.log` (10 logs):

```
unrecognized_model / model catalog matches   192
  earliest  2026-09-15T03:08:51Z   model deepseek-v4-pro   (the #796 dispatch at pro/medium)
  latest    2026-09-15T21:31:57Z   model deepseek-v4-flash
run finished: … status=failed                40
run finished: … status=ok                     0
```

And the environment the contract requires is absent — names only, no secrets printed:

```
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL   unset
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN unset
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY    unset
ANTHROPIC_MODEL      unset
FLEET_RUNNER         unset
```

Meanwhile both rungs report themselves fine:

```
$ python3 fleet/watchdog.py capabilities
brain:   capabilities current — on HEAD dd8cbfc; its build is the declared build
sister:  capabilities current — on HEAD dd8cbfc; its build is the declared build
```

## Expected

`fleet/terminal.py` says it honours a BYOK contract and refuses anything else explicitly rather than silently defaulting (`fleet/terminal.py:83-105`; `RC_REFUSED = 78`, "the order cannot be executed as declared"):

- `TIER_RUNNERS` maps `flash → deepseek-v4-flash`, `pro/auditor → deepseek-v4-pro`, and the runner is `DEFAULT_RUNNER = "claude -p"` invoked as `claude -p --model <tier-model>`.
- The comment at `fleet/terminal.py:87-100` states the `--model <tier-model>` argv shape *is* "kushin77/deepseek's Claude-CLI-on-DeepSeek **BYOK** contract (#88, #91: `claude --model <tier-model>` with the BYOK environment applied)", and that `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`/`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` "come from the operator's environment or a secret manager and are never written here (GR-6)".

So the module is correct and fail-closed. What is missing is the thing it is fail-closed *about*: this box has no BYOK environment and no wrapper that maps `deepseek-v4-*`, so the model the policy declares is not a model the runner knows. Two of the three are broken and only one is declared:

1. **The declared model vocabulary and the runner's catalog disagree.** `governance/finops/policy.json` (`tier_models`) and `fleet/terminal.py` (`TIER_RUNNERS`) both say `deepseek-v4-flash`/`deepseek-v4-pro`; the installed CLI's catalog says neither exists. Nothing checks the two against each other — unlike the profile/policy drift, which refuses to start (`fleet/brain.py:188-205`).
2. **Nothing surfaces the failure.** A run that cannot execute is recorded in a log and nowhere else: `watchdog` reports `capabilities current`, the brain reports `orders pending=0 | claims=N`, and the escalation that would tell an operator is one `warn`/`critical` pair among many. **The fleet cannot distinguish "idle" from "unable to execute"** — the same class as the "declared vs running process" drift already noted as a gap. The doctrine's own line applies: a signal that cannot fail is a formality, and here a *silence* is being read as health.

## Reproduction command

```bash
# 1. the model the policy declares, and the runner that is supposed to honour it
grep -n 'TIER_RUNNERS' -A4 fleet/terminal.py
python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('governance/finops/policy.json'))['tier_models'])"

# 2. the environment it needs (names only; never print values)
for v in ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_MODEL FLEET_RUNNER; do
  [ -n "${!v:-}" ] && echo "$v=SET" || echo "$v=unset"
done

# 3. the recorded outcome of every run the fleet has kept
grep -ho 'run finished: rc=[^"]*' .fleet/runs/*.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn   # all status=failed
grep -rho 'status=ok'  .fleet/runs/ .fleet/done/ | wc -l                          # 0
grep -h  'unrecognized_model' .fleet/runs/*.log | head -1                          # earliest failure
```

Everything above prints in under a second and needs no network.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A dispatch whose model the runner cannot honour **fails loudly at dispatch time**, naming the model, the tier, and the runner — not in a subagent's stdout ten seconds later. The refusal already exists as `RC_REFUSED = 78`; it is the *reachability* of the refusal that is in question.
- [ ] Startup (or a check in `make verify`) proves the declared tier→model map is a map the **installed runner** can resolve, by name, and fails when it is not — so "the policy declares a model nothing can run" cannot be a green state.
- [ ] Fleet health reports **last run outcome** (at minimum: the age of the last successful run, and a count of consecutive `status=failed`), and a rung whose recent runs all fail is not reported healthy. `brain: healthy` while 100% of subagent runs fail is the defect this bullet closes.
- [ ] Negative control: with the BYOK environment unset, the fleet refuses to dispatch — and says so from the health surface, not only from a log.

## Severity

**critical.** The consequence is total: no directive the fleet dispatches can execute, so no lane can produce work — the ERP wave (#645) is the live victim — and the failure is silent, so an operator reading `brain: healthy | sister: healthy` concludes the fleet is idle rather than broken. Two independent defects compound here: the model contract is unmet, and nothing signals it.

Immediate mitigation for an operator who needs the fleet now: point `FLEET_RUNNER` (documented in `fleet/README.md`) at the BYOK wrapper, which is the escape hatch `fleet/terminal.py:107-112` already provides — that restores execution without touching this issue's fix.

## RCA link (governance/lessons/)

To be recorded in `governance/lessons/` when the fix lands — the lesson is *"a control plane that reports healthy while its executor cannot execute has no health signal at all"*, and it is the second instance today of the same shape (the first is #727, where a refusal no consumer could act on became a crash loop). The registry memory for this session already carries the duplicate-lane variant of "a silence read as a green".

AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW)

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-runner-capability.sh
```

Added after a dispatch of this issue logged `issue declares no runnable Verify: command`
(`.fleet/runs/brain-directive-34dcbd8b…log`) — a defect brief with no runnable Verify
falls back to the 1800s `make verify`, which is a slow way to learn the contract moved.
The check is auto-discovered into `make verify` (#698): it runs the contract's own suite,
probes the behaviour **both ways**, and proves the check can FAIL by mutating
`unhonourable` to always allow and requiring the probe to notice.
"}

items.title: close-out: a PARKED verification (admission rc 10/11) is reported as VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING, with a remediation the cap makes unreachable
items.body:
## Objective

Make the close-out understand the gate admission control's **PARKED** outcome. A parked
verification is reported today as `VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING` with a remediation that cannot
be performed while the box is at its gate cap.

## Measured (2026-09-15, `master` @ `dd8cbfc`)

Closing out #836, `record-verification` failed like this:

```
close-out #836: NOT-OK
  skipped   merge-pull-request: already satisfied
  failed    record-verification: RuntimeError: d 2026-09-15T20:57:44Z
verify: PARKED (rc 11, not a pass and not a failure) — the box-wide gate cap is
reached; nothing was run and no attestation was touched
make: *** [Makefile:146: verify] Error 11
  …
  REMAINS  VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING  #836  no green verification attestation is recorded
           -> run `make verify` on the branch head before merging and record its attestation;
              evidence names a commit, and a summary is not evidence
```

The line that matters is softwares' own: **`verify: PARKED (rc 11, not a pass and not a
failure) … nothing was run and no attestation was touched`.** The admission control (#724,
`fleet/gatelock.py`) has its own exit vocabulary, deliberately outside the gate's 0/1/2
tri-state (`fleet/gatelock.py:44-45`, `EXIT_PARKED = 11`): `10` = another gate already holds
this worktree, `11` = every box-wide permit slot is taken (`DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT = 4`).

`governance/lifecycle/cli.py::record_verification` runs `make verify` and treats any
non-zero exit as *no green attestation*. So an outcome the gate itself declares to be
**neither a pass nor a failure** is recorded as a **missing** verification.

## Why that is the defect, not just a bad message

1. **It is the wrong verdict.** PARKED means *not assessed* — the gate ran nothing and
   touched nothing. CANNOT-ASSESS is the honest verdict; `VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING` asserts
   something was measured and came back absent.
2. **The remediation is unreachable.** "Run `make verify` on the branch head" re-parks while
   the box is at its cap, so the operator is sent to do a thing the system will refuse. The
   remedy for a *capacity* condition is to **retry when a permit frees**, not to re-run.
3. **It leaves the item permanently non-hygienic by accident.** #836 now sits
   `NOT-OK` with `VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING`, and the lane is also `LANE_NOT_RECLAIMED`, so a
   correct, merged, verified-by-the-gate-of-record change reads as unclosed.
4. **The board surfaces it as a real finding.** `close --apply` would file
   `lifecycle:VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING:#836` — a false defect report generated by capacity.

## Suggested shape

- In `record_verification`, distinguish the admission outcomes: `10`/`11` ⇒ **CANNOT-ASSESS**
  naming `PARKED` and the cap (`AO_GATE_MAX_CONCURRENT`), never `VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING`.
- Optionally retry with a bounded wait: the permit is held by another gate and does free.
- The remediation text for a parked run should say *retry when capacity is free*, and the
  finding should be `lifecycle:VERIFY_EVIDENCE_NOT_ASSESSED`-shaped rather than
  "missing" — a name that claims nothing was recorded when in fact nothing was *run*.

**Negative control to ask for:** with the cap held by a live gate, `close --issue <n>` must
report CANNOT-ASSESS (rc 2) naming `PARKED`, and must **not** report
`VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING`; with capacity free it must record the attestation and reach `OK`.
A close-out that cannot tell "the gate was queued out" from "the gate failed" will keep
producing false findings under load — which is exactly when the fleet runs.

## Related, and deliberately not duplicated here

- **#834** already names a companion wedge — *board state in the lane worktree* — which is
  the other half of the `LANE_NOT_RECLAIMED` seen in the same run: the lane's
  `.board/focus.json` was rewritten to `active_epic: 160` by a fleet process, so
  `reclaim-lane` refused with `worktree … has uncommitted work`. Not re-filed here.
- **#724** is the admission control itself (its exit codes are correct; the consumer is not).
- **#786** is the same family from the other direction (an invariant that cannot be
  satisfied once the lane is reclaimed).

## Verify

```
# with the cap held by a live gate:
python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --issue <n>     # must be CANNOT-ASSESS naming PARKED
# with capacity free:
python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --issue <n>     # must reach OK
```

Refs #724 #834

items.title: The landed-trailer control's two remedies contradict: master is red on a landed commit whose trailer cannot be fixed
items.body:
## Objective

Resolve the contradiction in the landed-trailer control (#287) that leaves `make verify`
**red on `master`** for a landed commit nobody can un-land, and settle which of the two
remedies is the contract.

## Measured (2026-09-15, `master` @ `27763d7`)

The check `scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` (auto-wired by #698, delivered in #287 /
PR #831) fails on master:

```
$ bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh
  FAIL  commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block:4e3d62da166f is not recorded legacy —
        add the trailer in a trailing paragraph, or record the commit in the baseline
        with its measured finding
  FAIL  the landed enforcement refused real history in HEAD
check-isolation-landed: FAIL (1 violation(s))          # rc 1

$ python3 governance/isolation/cli.py enforce --main . --range origin/master
  INFO  370 non-merge commit(s) reachable in origin/master; …
isolation-enforce: NOT-OK — 1 unrecorded and 0 stale baseline entr(ies) in origin/master
```

The commit is `4e3d62da166f` — the squash-merge of **PR #826 (#724)**, which landed
*after* the #287 merge (`bdce21d5`). Its own predicate agrees:
`bash scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --repo . --landed --range 4e3d62da166f^..4e3d62da166f`
→ `FAIL commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block:4e3d62da166f`.

**So the control works** — it re-checked landed history, which #287's whole point was that
nothing did, and found a fresh violation within minutes of merging. That part is right.

## The defect: the two documented remedies contradict each other

The check's FAIL message offers two remedies — *"add the trailer in a trailing
paragraph, **or** record the commit in the baseline with its measured finding"*. But
`governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json`'s own `note` says:

> "This list can only SHRINK: … **adding an entry for a newly landed non-compliant
> commit is the defect the check exists to catch, not a fix.**"

For a commit already squash-merged onto a protected branch, remedy 1 is **impossible**
(history cannot be rewritten — GR hard floor) and remedy 2 is **forbidden by the file's
own contract**. The result is that `make verify` is red on `master` with no admissible
fix, which is the AO-GR-21/GR-29 shape this repo keeps rediscovering: a control whose
remediation is unreachable.

The note's intent is right — *don't let the baseline become the way new violations are
silenced* — but stated as an absolute it is unimplementable, because post-boundary
residue on protected history is a permanent fact.

## Suggested resolution (pick one, state it in the file)

1. **Recording is a first-class, reviewable act** (recommended). The baseline is a
   *tracked file*: adding an entry is a commit that a reviewer sees, with the measured
   finding and the `measured_head` it was measured at. Restate the contract as: *residue
   must be recorded by an explicit reviewed commit — never silently skipped or
   auto-extended* — and keep `quarantine-entry-stale` / `quarantine-entry-not-assessed` /
   missing-baseline-is-a-failure as the guards. This makes the two remedies consistent and
   keeps the control's teeth: a *new* violation still reds the gate, which is what forces
   the conversation (as it just did).
2. **Only pre-boundary commits are grandfathered**, and a post-boundary violation is
   reported as a **finding on the offending PR** without failing `make verify` — a
   reporting surface rather than a gate. Weaker (a red board is not a red gate), and it
   needs an owner for the follow-up.

Whichever is chosen, `check-isolation-landed.sh` must not leave `master` red for a fact
its own remediation cannot change.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The FAIL message and the baseline `note` state **one** contract, not two.
- [ ] `bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh` is green on `master`, with `4e3d62da166f`
      recorded with its measured finding (or the reporting-only design implemented).
- [ ] The guards survive: a *new* non-compliant commit still fails; a stale entry fails;
      a missing baseline fails; `no lanes recorded` is CANNOT-ASSESS.
- [ ] The reason this cannot simply be "fix the trailer" is stated in the file, so the next
      reader does not rediscover the dead end.

## Verify

```
bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh && make verify
```
