items.title: pr-contract: the landing path composes a trailer paragraph the rule refuses (a bare `Closes #<n>` line)
items.body:
## Summary

The trailer rule enforced by `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --landed` (and, since
#831, by `governance/isolation/cli.py enforce`) refuses a commit whose trailing
paragraph starts with a bare `Closes #<n>` line — the exact shape the repository's
own **landing path** composes. Measured while landing #287: of the thirteen
post-boundary commits that the predicate flags, eleven are this shape.

## Measurement

```
$ python3 governance/isolation/cli.py landed --main . --range HEAD
  FAIL  commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block:90a0500bbf55
  ... 11 of the 13 findings are commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block
$ git log -1 --format=%b 90a0500bbf55
Closes #509
AI-assistance: GitHub Copilot (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash/LOW)
Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#509
```

One paragraph, three lines. `is_trailer_line` accepts `Token: value` lines, the
`Refs …#n` line, and continuations — but `Closes #509` has no colon, so the whole
paragraph is classified `other`, the walk-back stops immediately, and the `Refs`
line *above* it is reported as outside the block. The commit is recorded legacy in
`governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` (issue #287) rather than fixed, because
the predicate is not that lane's file.

The same trap applies to a **PR body that ends with `Closes #<n>`**: the squash
message GitHub composes then ends in a paragraph the rule refuses. Measured by
simulating the composed message:

```
A: body ending with the `Refs …#n` paragraph as the last paragraph   -> rc 0 PASS
B: body ending with a bare `Closes #<n>` paragraph                   -> rc 1
   FAIL  commit-missing-ticket-trailer:<sha>
```

## Why it matters

* Every PR that ends its body with `Closes #<n>` **lands a commit that fails the
  landed audit**, so `cli.py enforce` now reds for it (until someone records a new
  baseline entry, which the design forbids as a fix) — a rule that disagrees with
  the tool that produces the artifact.
* The landing path is the repository's own composition (`gh pr merge --squash`);
  a rule that refuses its output will keep generating recorded-legacy entries.

## Suggested fix (choose one, and make it explicit)

1. **Accept the GitHub-standard bare `Closes #<n>` line** as a trailer line in
   `is_trailer_line` (`^Closes[ \t]+#\d+$`). It is a trailer in GitHub's own
   vocabulary, and accepting it removes 11 of the 13 recorded-legacy entries —
   the quarantine then shrinks, which is the property `landed.py` enforces.
2. **Or** stop producing it: the PR template ends bodies with the `Refs …#n`
   paragraph, and the merge happens with an explicit `--body` that does the same.

Whichever is chosen, `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` must be pruned to
match (the enforcement fails on a stale entry by design, so the two changes ship
together).

## Provenance

Filed from the #287 lane (landed as #831) while measuring what could be enforced
without reddening the gate for every lane on day one.

items.title: governance/lifecycle: the close-out wedges on three measured cases (directive with no inbox copy, a dead lane record, board state in the lane worktree)
items.body:
## Summary

Closing out #287 (`governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --issue 287`) reached `OK`
only after **three** measured wedges, each of which makes the close-out report
`NOT-OK` for a reason unrelated to the work. All three were hit in the same lane
on 2026-09-15 and each was worked around by hand; recording them so the next lane
does not have to rediscover them, and so the driver can be fixed.

## 1. `consume-directive` cannot consume a directive that lives only in `.fleet/sent/`

The invariant reads the brain's own copy and asks whether the *done* artifact
exists:

```python
# governance/lifecycle/cli.py
for path in sorted((root / ".fleet" / "sent").glob("*.json")):
    ...
    consumed = (root / ".fleet" / "done" / path.name).exists()
    return {"id": ..., "state": "done" if consumed else "sent"}
```

but the remediation it runs operates on the **inbox**:

```python
# governance/lifecycle/cli.py -> fleet/channel.py
def consume_directive(message_id):      # fleet/channel.py
    source = INBOX / f"{message_id}.json"      # INBOX = .fleet/inbox
    if not source.exists():
        return False                            # -> "nothing to consume"
```

A directive written straight into `.fleet/sent/` (which is what a dispatcher that
authorises a claim by directive id does) never has an inbox copy, so the
documented remedy can never succeed. Measured:

```
$ ls .fleet/sent/brain-directive-76a361566054b60ea914bad3b1822e5e.json
.fleet/sent/brain-directive-76a361566054b60ea914bad3b1822e5e.json
$ python3 fleet/channel.py consume --id brain-directive-76a361566054b60ea914bad3b1822e5e
channel consume: nothing to consume for brain-directive-76a361566054b60ea914bad3b1822e5e   # rc 1
```

so the close-out reports, correctly but unhelpfully:

```
  failed    consume-directive: RuntimeError: channel consume: nothing to consume for brain-directive-76a3...
  REMAINS  DIRECTIVE_NOT_CONSUMED  #287  directive brain-directive-76a3... is sent, not consumed
```

**Workaround used:** `cp .fleet/sent/<id>.json .fleet/inbox/<id>.json` and then the
sanctioned `channel.py consume --id <id>` (which moved it to `.fleet/done/`).

**Suggested fix:** have the consume step move the *sent* copy when there is no
inbox copy (or have the invariant key on `.fleet/done` alone and give the driver a
command that can reach it); the current pair can never agree for this shape.

## 2. `_lane_records` keeps ONE record per issue, so a dead record blocks the live lane

`.fleet/lanes/` held two records for #287: the live `3acf396f43ea` (worktree
present, `isolation audit` rc 0) and a dead `d9caf9d11ee2` whose worktree had been
removed (`isolation audit` rc 1, named `worktree-missing`). `_lane_records` maps
by issue and the later-sorted record won, so `record-verification` refused:

```
$ python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --issue 287
  failed    record-verification: RuntimeError: no lane worktree for #287; the verified tree no longer exists
```

even though the live lane existed, audited clean, and its HEAD *was* the verified
commit:

```
$ python3 governance/isolation/cli.py audit --main . --session d9caf9d11ee2
  FAIL  lane d9caf9d11ee2
          worktree-missing: /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-287-d9caf9d1 does not exist
$ python3 governance/isolation/cli.py audit --main . --session 3acf396f43ea
  OK    lane 3acf396f43ea
```

**Workaround used:** deleted the dead record (evidence above: it is a lane that
does not exist, and the isolation audit already calls it a violation).

**Suggested fix:** resolve the lane by `present` (and prefer a record whose HEAD is
the verified commit), reporting the dead one as `LANE_NOT_RECLAIMED`
/`worktree-missing` rather than letting it shadow the live lane.

## 3. `.board/focus.json` is rewritten inside lane worktrees, so `reclaim-lane` refuses

`closer.reclaim_lane` runs `governance/isolation/cli.py close --session <id>`
**without** `--force`, and `close()` refuses a dirty worktree. The fleet loop
rewrites `.board/focus.json` in the lane (focus moved to epic #160 mid-run), so:

```
  failed    reclaim-lane: RuntimeError: close: NOT-OK — worktree /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-287-3acf396f
            has uncommitted work; commit it or pass --force
  REMAINS  LANE_NOT_RECLAIMED  #287
```

with the tree's only dirty path being machine-managed board state:

```
$ git -C <lane> status --porcelain
 M .board/focus.json
```

**Workaround used:** reverted the board file and re-ran the close-out immediately
(`performed reclaim-lane: close: OK — lane 3acf396f43ea removed`).

**Suggested fix:** exclude machine-managed board state from the reclaim's dirty
test (or have the driver pass `--force` when the only dirty paths are declared
generated ones) — as it stands the close-out is racy against the loop that owns
that file.

## Provenance

Measured in the #287 lane, whose work landed as #831 (`bdce21d5`). The close-out
reached `OK` only after the three workarounds above; each is a wedge a lane cannot
clear without hand-editing fleet runtime state.

items.title: landed-history trailer block: reconcile the #826 squash commit (4e3d62da) and document the colon-less-keyword trap
items.body:
## What happened (measured)

Landing #724 (PR #826) merged as squash commit `4e3d62da166fee2afc1f90f74fb1e60bb184cb61`
on `master`. The post-merge gate on that commit is RED:

```
== isolation-landed ==
  FAIL  commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block:4e3d62da166f is not recorded legacy — add the trailer in a trailing paragraph, or record the commit in the baseline with its measured finding
  isolation-enforce: NOT-OK — 1 unrecorded and 0 stale baseline entr(ies) in HEAD
verify: FAIL (1 of 116 checks failed, 4 skipped: module-registry, module-brief, diagrams-declaration, codeidx-surface)
```

`4e3d62da` is the ONLY unrecorded non-compliant commit named. `master` was green before
it (`bdce21d`), so this merge caused the red — no lane's `make verify` can be green until
it is reconciled.

## Root cause (measured, not guessed)

The squash message was composed as:

```
Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#724
Closes #724

AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW)
```

Git builds the trailing trailer block from paragraphs that consist **entirely** of
`Token: value` lines. `Closes #724` has no colon, so that paragraph is not a trailer
paragraph: the block stops there and contains only `AI-assistance:`, leaving `Refs …`
**outside** the block. The ticket reference is present in the message — it is just in the
wrong position, which is exactly what `commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block` means.

This is systemic, not a one-off: no repo-owned tooling composes the squash
`commit_title`/`commit_message` (`grep -rl commit_message --include='*.sh' --include='*.py'`
is empty), so every lane composes its message by hand and any colon-less keyword line in
the trailer region silently produces this finding.

## Remedy

1. Reconcile `4e3d62da` in `governance/isolation/landed-baseline.json` with the measured
   finding and its cause — the second option the check's own refusal names, and the only
   mechanically available one for a commit that has already landed (its history is on a
   protected branch: no force-push).
2. Document the trap where the trailer rule lives (`governance/isolation/README.md`) with
   the compliant shape, so the next landing composes a message whose trailing block holds
   the reference.

## Verify

```
bash scripts/check-isolation-landed.sh ; echo rc=$?   # expect rc 0, 0 unrecorded, 0 stale
make verify                                            # expect PASS, attestation git_sha = <head>
```

AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW)

items.title: fix(fleet): the worktree reaper shipped for #516 and is scheduled nowhere — the pile rebuilt, and 302 branches have no reaper at all
items.body:
## Observed

`scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` shipped in #597 (closing **#516, "the machine's unreclaimed worktree
pile"**) and is a finished, tested, documented tool — **and nothing runs it.** The pile #516 named
has rebuilt: 142 worktrees.

The crontab schedules exactly one prune job:

```
23 4 * * * cd /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator && /usr/bin/python3 fleet/prune.py run --apply >> .../.fleet/prune.log 2>&1 # ao-fleet-prune
```

`fleet/prune.py` prunes the **`.fleet` mailbox**, and says so in its own docstring:
"``scripts/prune-worktrees.sh`` reclaims lane *worktrees*, not the mailbox". There is no cron
entry, no `ops/run.sh` hook and no gate for `prune-worktrees.sh`. It has a `make` target
(`Makefile:146`) and a test file (`scripts/tests/test_prune_worktrees.py`, 9 passed), so it is
not unfinished — it is unscheduled. #597's body does not mention scheduling; the fix for #516
therefore does not recur.

Measured on the real tree, 2026-09-15 20:0xZ at `master 022d931`:

```
$ python3 governance/reconcile/cli.py status --disk
reconcile-audit (<tree>): 459 artifact(s) — matched=26, unmatched=432, exempt=1
reconcile-audit: NOT-OK — 432 artifact(s) no session beat, claim record or landing record explains
   130 unmatched worktrees + 302 unmatched branches
rc=1
```

…while the gate of record was green in the same window:

```
verify: PASS (109 of 113 checks, 4 skipped: module-registry, module-brief, diagrams-declaration, codeidx-surface)
```

### Running the tool by hand reclaims most of it

```
$ bash scripts/prune-worktrees.sh            # dry run
prune-worktrees: 75 stale, 66 kept (dirty, in use, claimed, parked, or unpreserved)

$ bash scripts/prune-worktrees.sh --apply    # rc=0, same summary
```

`git worktree list` went **142 → 67**, and the audit moved **432 → 358** unexplained
(130 → **56** worktrees; **302 branches unchanged**). Nothing was lost: the tool is fail-closed
and preserved every claimed, in-use, dirty and unpreserved worktree.

Three things this exposes:

1. **302 unmatched branches have no reaper at all.** The worktree reaper does not look at
   branches; the 75-worktree reap left the branch count at exactly 302.
2. **The "dirty" test counts generated runtime state.** Of the 66 kept worktrees, **11 are kept
   by a single uncommitted file**, and both ERP lanes landed today are among them:

   ```
   KEEP   /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-646-erp-foundation — 1 uncommitted file(s)
   KEEP   /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-647-erp-core-model — 1 uncommitted file(s)
   ```

   The file is `.board/focus.json` — fleet-written runtime state the lane never authored, and a
   *tracked* file, so it is always dirty in any worktree the fleet has touched. A finished lane
   whose only "uncommitted work" is generated state can never be reclaimed. (Relates to #625,
   "enforce runtime-state ignore coverage instead of trusting it".)
3. **39 of the 66 keeps are "claimed by an open lane"** — a `.fleet/lanes/` record that is only
   deleted when the lane closes, so a lane that closes by another path pins its worktree.

## Expected

A tool that exists to stop worktrees accumulating should be scheduled like the other fleet jobs,
so the condition it was written for (#516) does not silently rebuild. Its verdicts should be
reproducible rather than dependent on a human remembering to run it — GR-29: only a
platform-enforced control is binding.

## Reproduction command

```bash
crontab -l | grep -c prune-worktrees          # 0 — the reaper is scheduled nowhere
cd /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator
bash scripts/prune-worktrees.sh               # "75 stale, 66 kept"
bash scripts/prune-worktrees.sh --apply       # git worktree list: 142 -> 67
bash <a-worktree-at-origin/master>/scripts/prune-worktrees.sh --check   # see below
```

## Severity

medium — no production surface is down, but this is the measured mechanism behind the fleet's
capacity ceiling (`resource_ceiling=11 (bound by RAM: RAM 17946 MiB / 1536 MiB)`, 11 live claims)
and behind stranded lanes: `ao-646-erp-foundation` / `ao-647-erp-core-model` sat unpushed and
unclaimed for ~15h and were two of the artifacts the audit named. Worktrees under the 16 GiB
`/tmp` tmpfs are also the RAM hazard #516's own text names.

## Bounded proposal (three separable changes)

1. **Schedule it** — the one-line fix, alongside the existing `ao-fleet-prune` cron entry (or
   from `fleet/watchdog.py`'s periodic cycle, so it survives the #706 cron port).
2. **Give branches a reaper** — 302 unmatched lane branches are invisible to every current tool.
   The landing path should delete a merged lane's branch (or the reaper should), and closing a
   lane should delete its `.fleet/lanes/` record.
3. **Do not let generated runtime state keep a worktree** — exclude declared runtime state (the
   `.board/*` generated files) from the "dirty" test. This weakens a fail-closed guard, so it
   should land last and alone, with the claimed/in-use/preserved checks unchanged.

## RCA link (governance/lessons/)

`governance/lessons/rca/worktree-reaper-unscheduled.md`

_AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW)._

items.title: AgentConsole: the epic's completion RCA (enterprise class requires one)
items.body:
Parent: #800

The enterprise epic #800 closes at `enterprise` class, which expects a short completion RCA per `docs/SOLUTION-CLASSES.md`. This records it: INC-0006 / RCA-0006 / CA-0008 / SUGGEST-0004 in `governance/lessons/ledger.jsonl` + `governance/lessons/rca/RCA-0006-agentconsole-wrong-host.md`.

The finding: the go-live was designed against agent-orchestrator's own GCP Cloud Run pipeline (the retired model) while the fleet's live-hosting contract (shared-frontend `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, owner directive 2026-09-04) fixes the remote shared-services cluster as the only host.

Verify: `python3 -m governance.lessons.cli check` → OK; `make verify`.

items.title: sent is not done: `channel.py consume` is inbox-only, so a brain-minted directive can never satisfy `consume-directive` (118 stranded)
items.body:
## Objective

Make the `consume-directive` closure invariant **satisfiable by the documented CLI**
for a brain-minted authorisation directive, and stop `.fleet/sent/` growing without
bound. Today the documented remedy cannot consume the artifact it names, so **every
brain-dispatched lane** hits `REMAINS DIRECTIVE_NOT_CONSUMED` and the unavoidable
workaround is a hand-move.

## Measured (2026-09-15, `master` @ `4c3a8ae`)

Reproduced **independently by two lanes in one wave** (#693 → PR #818, #695 → PR
#815). Both reported the identical close-out failure:

```
close-out #N: NOT-OK
  REMAINS  DIRECTIVE_NOT_CONSUMED  directive brain-directive-a2a-<n>-… is sent, not consumed
```

The remedy the failure names fails too:

```
$ python3 fleet/channel.py consume --id brain-directive-a2a-695-…
nothing to consume        # rc 1
```

### Root cause — `consume` is inbox-only

`fleet/channel.py:1351`:

```python
def consume_directive(message_id: str) -> bool:
    """Mark a directive complete: move it out of the inbox into .fleet/done/."""
    source = INBOX / f"{message_id}.json"
    if not source.exists():
        return False
```

It reads **only** `INBOX`. But a brain-minted authorisation directive is written to
**`.fleet/sent/`** (`.fleet/sent/<id>.json`, the chain edge `claim --directive <id>`
validates against — AGENTS.md rule 14). It is never in the inbox, so `consume`
returns `False` for it *by construction*, and the lifecycle step
`consume-directive` can never reach its terminal state.

### The backlog this produces on this box

| directory | entries |
|---|---|
| `.fleet/sent/` | **118** |
| `.fleet/done/` | 104 |
| `.fleet/inbox/` | **0** |

The measure is the finding, not a guess: `.fleet/sent/` holds **118** directives —
every one of them an authorisation that no documented command can retire.

### Why existing lanes sometimes looked fine

`governance/lifecycle/cli.py::_directive_for` resolves *a* directive for the issue and
checks its state, so a lane whose issue **also** has an older directive already in
`.fleet/done/` passes on that one, while the lane's own authorisation silently stays
`sent` forever. That is why the failure is intermittent across lanes and looks like a
flaky close-out — it is not; it depends only on whether *another* directive happened
to exist for the same issue.

### Why it matters

- It is the **same "sent is treated as done" confusion** filed as #796: a marker that
  records that an order was *sent* is being read as if the order were *finished*. Here
  the confusion is on the closure side; there it is on the brain's dispatch-marker side.
- It is the **AO-GR-21 / GR-29 family**: an invariant the documented path cannot
  satisfy is a formality, and the recommended remedy is unreachable — a control only
  reachable from outside the loop is not a control (#799 records the same shape for
  `control.py drop`).
- The only way lanes currently pass is a **hand-move of another lane's runtime state**
  (`sent/<id>.json` → `done/<id>.json`), which is exactly the kind of off-book action
  the doctrine exists to remove — and it is not documented anywhere.

## Remedy — pick the mechanism, not a number

At least one, plus a provoked negative control:
1. **Teach `consume_directive` about `sent`.** It already means "the order is finished";
   a directive in `.fleet/sent/` whose issue is closed/merged is finished by the same
   definition. Move it to `.fleet/done/` from whichever mailbox holds it, and keep the
   runaway-guard counter semantics unchanged.
2. **Make the lifecycle step own the terminal move** instead of delegating to a CLI
   whose mailbox differs, so close-out cannot be blocked by a mailbox-shape mismatch.
3. **Retire `sent` at dispatch** — record the authorisation in the ledger and delete
   the file once the claim is accepted, so no artifact outlives its authorisation.

**Negative control:** a lane authorised by a brain-minted directive and nothing else
must reach `close-out: OK` **without** a human touching `.fleet/`; and a directive
whose issue is still open must **not** be consumable. Ask for both, provoked — the
first is the reproducer above and the second prevents the fix from becoming a
"consume anything" verb that can retire live work.

## Verify

```
cd /home/akushnir/agent-orchestrator && python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --issue <n>
```
must print `close-out #n: OK` for a lane whose only authorisation is a directive in
`.fleet/sent/` — with `.fleet/sent/` shrinking by one and no hand-move.

items.title: The control-plane API contract is accurate but undefended: no gate compares identity/cpapi/openapi.yaml to the router
items.body:
Parent: #803

## The control-plane API contract is accurate — and nothing defends it against drift

`identity/cpapi/openapi.yaml` is a real, complete contract: **865 lines, OpenAPI 3.0.3, 28 paths**
across tenants/agents/registry/governance, and its own description says *"This spec is the contract
the generated clients in `clients/` are built against."*

**Measured 2026-09-15 — the spec and the router AGREE:**

```
router routes (Route(...) table in identity/cpapi/control.py): 29
spec routes   (a real YAML parse of paths × methods):          29
in ROUTER, not in SPEC : 0
in SPEC, not in ROUTER : 0
==> AGREE
```

So the contract is honest today. **The problem is that nothing keeps it honest.** There is no gate:
`scripts/check-paperclip-openapi.sh` guards the paperclip seam only, and nothing compares this spec
to `identity/cpapi/router.py`/`control.py`. A route added, renamed or removed in code silently
invalidates a published contract that clients are generated from — **and a contract that has drifted
is worse than no contract, because a consumer trusts it.**

### What to build

A gate that proves the spec and the code agree, and fails when they stop:

1. **A comparator in its own file** (`scripts/cpapi-spec-drift.py`) so the gate provokes the *same*
   code path the check uses — a proof that drives a copy proves nothing about the path that runs.
   It must take the two artifacts as **arguments** so it can be driven against fixtures.
2. **Normalisation is the subtle part**: the router declares `/v1/tenants/{tenantId}` while the spec
   declares `/tenants/{tenantId}`, because the version lives in the spec's `servers` URL. The gate
   must apply that mapping explicitly and *say* it does, or a future reader will "fix" a false drift.
3. **BOTH directions provoked.** A planted route absent from the spec must be caught, **and** a
   planted spec path absent from the router must be caught. Asserting one direction would pass a
   comparator that only ever reports one class of drift.
4. **The fixture is a temp directory**, never the real files, so `make verify` cannot mutate the
   repository it is checking and an interrupted run leaves nothing behind.
5. **Registered in `scripts/verify.sh`** (the array is explicit, so an unregistered check is inert)
   and therefore covered by `check-gate-coverage.sh`.

### Acceptance

- [ ] `bash scripts/check-cpapi-spec-drift.sh` passes on the current tree (29/29).
- [ ] A planted router route missing from the spec fails **by name**.
- [ ] A planted spec path missing from the router fails **by name**.
- [ ] A compare that fails open — e.g. exits 0 when it could not parse either artifact — is refused.
- [ ] Registered in `verify.sh`; `gate-coverage` reports it WIRED.
- [ ] `make verify` green.

### Verify

```
bash scripts/check-cpapi-spec-drift.sh && make verify
```

items.title: GR-15 is declared and enforced by nothing — and the repo is violating it (active ci-failure-scanner workflow)
items.body:
Parent: #803

## GR-15 is declared and enforced by nothing — and the repo is currently violating it

`AGENTS.md` and the CMR fleet doctrine both state, without qualification:

> **No GitHub Actions workflows.** Automation is code-native: `make` targets run by the ops runner
> and cron.

Measured 2026-09-15:

```
gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/actions/workflows
  CI Failure Scanner & Auto-Issue Creator | state=active | .github/workflows/ci-failure-scanner.yml
  recent runs: 03:11:10Z success, 02:13:33Z success, 01:22:13Z success   (10-minute cron)
```

### The rule is declared and NOT enforced

No gate checks it. The three scripts that mention `github/workflows` are incidental —
`scripts/check-docs.sh`, `scripts/check-yaml.py` (they parse YAML), `scripts/check-paperclip-routines.sh`
(its own concern). **`scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh` does not look at `.github/workflows` at all**, so
a workflow is not even an artifact the coverage registry knows about.

That is the same defect this epic was filed about, one level down: a rule that lives in prose cannot
refuse anything, and this one has been silently violated for as long as the workflow has existed.

### The workflow's function is real and its implementation is redundant

It scans open PRs and files an issue when a check failed:

```yaml
gh pr list --state open --limit 50 --json number,statusCheckRollup \
  --jq '[.[] | select(.statusCheckRollup | any(.conclusion == "FAILURE")) | .number]'
```

Those are `gh` commands. They need no Actions — the identical logic runs from cron, which is exactly
what GR-15 prescribes. **Retiring the workflow therefore loses no capability.** (It also scans for a
CI that does not otherwise exist, so in practice its runs find nothing and exit `success`.)

### What to build

1. **A code-native replacement** — the same `gh pr list --json statusCheckRollup` scan, run by cron,
   filing an issue only when none already references the PR. Same behaviour, no Actions.
2. **A gate that ENFORCES GR-15** — a `scripts/check-*.sh` that fails when a workflow file exists,
   with an explicit reasoned baseline so a deliberate exception is possible and visible rather than
   silent. Registered in `scripts/verify.sh` (the array is explicit) so it is not itself inert.
3. **Retire the workflow** in the same change, so the gate is green on the commit that introduces it.
4. **A provoked negative control** — the gate must be shown to FAIL for a planted workflow file, and
   to PASS when only the baseline is present. Asserting only the pass half would accept a gate that
   matches nothing.

### Acceptance

- [ ] No active Actions workflow; `.github/workflows/` is empty or contains only reasoned exemptions.
- [ ] The scanner's function is preserved code-natively and runs from cron.
- [ ] `scripts/check-no-actions.sh` fails BY NAME for a planted workflow, proven with a provocation.
- [ ] The gate is registered in `verify.sh` and `gate-coverage` reports it WIRED.
- [ ] `make verify` green.

### Verify

```
bash scripts/check-no-actions.sh && make verify
```

items.title: P0-2: the gate of record becomes a REQUIRED check without GitHub Actions — ADR-0028 (#803)
items.body:
Parent: #803
Refs #807

## P0-2: the gate of record becomes a *required* check without GitHub Actions — ADR-0028

Resolves the question #807 deliberately left open:

> a required check needs a check-run; a check-run needs an App or Actions; **Actions is banned by
> GR-15**.

They are not incompatible. A required check needs a check-run **or a commit status**, and a commit
status is one authenticated POST. Measured before the ADR was written, with the existing `repo`
scope and no Actions anywhere:

```
POST /repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/statuses/03f075236c48
  state=success context="ao/gate-probe"
→ {"id":54169930500, "context":"ao/gate-probe", "state":"success"}
GET /repos/.../commits/03f075236c48/status
→ {"state":"success","statuses":[{"context":"ao/gate-probe","state":"success"}]}
```

**Delivered** — `docs/decision-records/ADR-0028-gate-status-without-actions.md` (the decision, the
four options with three rejected and why, and the deadlock risk stated plainly), the mapper, the
poster, the provoked gate, and the declared context in `governance/platform/branch-protection.yaml`.

**The mapping is the control, and the gate provokes it:**

| gate outcome | status | why |
|---|---|---|
| `verify: PASS` (rc 0) | `success` | |
| `verify: FAIL` (rc 1) | `failure` | |
| CANNOT-ASSESS (rc 2) | **`error`** | never `success` — that is the #739 false-green class; never `failure` — that trains the operator to ignore red |
| unknown rc | **REFUSED** | a mapper that succeeds on what it does not recognise cannot fail |

Mutation-proved, each mutation asserted to have **landed** (sha256 before ≠ after) and restored
byte-identical: CANNOT-ASSESS → `success` is caught and named as *"a false green, the #739 defect
class"*; a defaulted unknown rc is caught; a poster context differing from the declared one is caught.

**NOT done here, deliberately.** The context is not yet in `protection`, so nothing is required yet.
Requiring a context that nothing posts would block **every** merge, including the fix — and #724 is
this repository's own precedent for an inert control whose gate could not see that it was inert.
Declaring it is a separate step, taken once the poster has been observed posting from the runner.

**Disclosed:** the mechanism probe left a real `ao/gate-probe` `success` status on master's head
commit. It is inert (no protection requires that context) and GitHub exposes no delete for commit
statuses, so it is recorded in the ADR rather than quietly left behind.

items.body:

Refs #6

## P0-3: branch protection as code — declared, applied idempotently, read back, and gated

Closes the P0-3 workstream of #803. `master` was measured **unprotected**
(`{"message":"Branch not protected","status":404}`) while `AGENTS.md` claimed it was "protected by
convention" and that branch protection as code "ships with issue #6".

Delivered:

  NOT required and the reasons stated in the file.
- `scripts/branch-protection.sh` — `apply` (derives its PUT body from the declaration, idempotent) /
  `verify` (reads the live protection **back** and diffs it) / `show`.
- `scripts/branch-protection-compare.py` — the comparator, in its own file so the gate provokes the
  **same** code path `verify` uses.
- `scripts/check-branch-protection.sh` — the gate: structural + **provoked** + live. An unobservable
  live state is **CANNOT-ASSESS (2)**, never a pass.
- registered in `scripts/verify.sh` (the array is explicit; `gate-coverage` reports `WIRED=100
  UNWIRED=0`).

**Still open, tracked separately:** the ADR for "how does a code-native gate become a REQUIRED

items.title: mktemp -d and the unfinished-marker scanner are mutually unsatisfiable (missing leading word boundary)
items.body:
Parent: #803
Refs #526

## `mktemp -d` and the unfinished-marker scanner are mutually unsatisfiable

### Measured 2026-09-15, lane `issue-803-platform-protection`

```
FAIL  ./scripts/check-branch-protection.sh (unfinished marker)
unfinished markers: 1 file(s) FAILED
```

for this line, which is the *standard* way to make a scratch directory:

```bash
work="$(mktemp -d /tmp/cbp.XXXXXX)" || exit 2
```

### The mechanism

`scripts/check-docs.sh` scans every `*.sh`, `*.py` and `*.go` for:

```bash
mk_pattern="(TO""DO|FIX""ME|HA""CK|XX""X)\\b"
```

The last branch is three `X` followed by a **trailing word boundary and no leading one**. A word
boundary after `XXX` is satisfied whenever the next character is not a word character — including
end-of-string and `"`. So the pattern matches the **tail of any run of three or more `X`**.

`mktemp` *requires* a template ending in at least three consecutive `X`. Therefore:

> **the standard `mktemp` template cannot be written in any file this scanner reads.**

Every lane that needs a scratch directory hits this, and the failure message
(`unfinished marker`) describes a `TODO`, not a placeholder — so the flag looks like a real defect
and the fix looks like deleting the marker, which is not possible.

### Why it is worth fixing rather than working around

- **The gate is not wrong to fire and the author is not wrong to use `mktemp`.** The pattern has a
  real bug: it is missing a LEADING boundary. `\bXXX\b` would match only the standalone marker and
  leave every `mktemp` template alone.
- **It has already cost a full gate cycle** (`verify: FAIL (1 of 107)`) and it silently pushes
  authors toward worse code — the workaround here was `python3 -c tempfile.mkdtemp()`, which is fine
  but is not what a shell author would reach for, and the *documented* repo convention recommends
  the template that fails.
- **The explanation trips it too.** The first fix removed the `mktemp` line and kept a comment
  explaining the trap — and the comment contained the template, so the file failed again, for the
  comment. A control that fires on the documentation of itself will keep firing.

### What to build

1. **Fix the pattern**: `(TODO|FIXME|HACK)\b|\bXXX\b` — a leading boundary on the marker branch
   only. Verify `mktemp -d /tmp/x.XXXXXX` no longer matches and `// XXX: fix` still does.
2. **A provoked control**: the gate must assert BOTH halves — the template is not flagged, and a
   real marker (`XXX:`, `TODO:`, `FIXME:`) still is. Asserting only the second half would pass a
   scanner that matches nothing.
3. **Record the convention**: whatever the pattern becomes, the repo's own guidance for scratch
   directories must name a form that passes the gate it recommends.

### Acceptance

- [ ] `mktemp -d /tmp/<name>.XXXXXX` in a `*.sh` does not fail `docs-lint`.
- [ ] A real `TODO` / `FIXME` / standalone `XXX` marker still fails, by name.
- [ ] The provocation asserts both halves.

### Verify

```
bash scripts/check-docs.sh && make verify
```

items.title: EPIC: Enterprise readiness — strong engineering, absent delivery controls (master unprotected, no required checks, GR-15 violated)
items.body:
Parent: #4
Refs #6

## EPIC: Enterprise readiness — the engineering is strong; the *delivery controls* are absent

### Measured 2026-09-15 against `master` = `d455fda`

This is an assessment, not an opinion. Every line below was read from the repository, the API, or
the gate's own output.

| # | Dimension | Measured | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Code surface | 2,162 tracked files, **~290K LOC** (excl. vendor), 5 pillars + 4 cross-cutting | ✅ Strong |
| 2 | Automated tests | **655** test files, **88** tracked suites | ✅ Strong |
| 3 | Gate of record | `make verify` — 128 checks, **provably able to fail**, mutation-proved; `gate-coverage` refuses an unwired check by name | ✅ Excellent |
| 4 | Governance + fleet | 24 governance modules, 16 fleet gates, AO-GR-1…27 with originated controls | ✅ Exceptional |
| 5 | Suite declaration | 84 declared / 88 actual — **4 undeclared**, gate WARNs only | ⚠️ Minor |
| 6 | **Branch protection on `master`** | **`{"message":"Branch not protected","status":404}`** | ❌ **P0 — FIXED, see below** |
| 7 | **Required status checks on a PR** | **none — no CI exists** | ❌ **P0 (design problem)** |
| 8 | **GR-15 compliance** | **violated: `ci-failure-scanner.yml` is `state=active`**, on a 10-minute cron | ❌ **P0 (doctrine)** |
| 9 | Branch-protection **as code** | **no tooling exists** (issue #6 promised it) | ❌ P0 |
| 10 | API contract for the product | **`identity/cpapi/openapi.yaml` EXISTS** — 865 lines, OpenAPI 3.0.3, **28 paths** (tenants/agents/registry/governance), referenced by its own tests. The real gap is narrower: **no gate drift-checks it against `identity/cpapi/router.py`** | ⚠️ Drift-check missing (corrected — the original “no spec” was a `head -8` truncation; see correction 2) |
| 11 | Multi-tenant isolation, *proven* | negative controls at **both** layers: 4 "another tenant" refusals in `engine/memory/tests/test_isolation.py`, 12 tests in `identity/chat/tests/test_isolation.py` (incl. a bypass test and dual counters), 15 fail-closed tests | ✅ **Proven** (corrected — the original "4 tests / Unproven" was a filename-glob miscount; see the correction comment) |
| 12 | `CODEOWNERS` | absent | ⚠️ |
| 13 | Release version | `module.json` → **`v0.1.0`** | ⚠️ Pre-1.0 |
| 14 | Deployment | **65 files**: 3 real TF modules (control-plane-service, deployer-sa, web-surface), 10 CloudBuild files incl. triggers, and a tested `rollout/` engine (9 test files: canary rollback, promotion gates, default-off) | ✅ **Real** (corrected — “19 files” was a code-file count reused as an infra count) |

### The headline

**This is not a toy.** Nearly 300K lines across five pillars, 88 test suites, and a governance spine
more rigorous than most funded products have. What is missing is not engineering.

**What is missing is that nothing *requires* any of it.** The gate of record is excellent and
**the platform does not enforce it**:

- `master` had **no protection at all** — any process, human or agent, could push straight to it.
- There is **no required status check**, so a merge never had to present a green gate.
- `AGENTS.md` states *"`master` is protected by convention"* and *"Branch protection as code ships
  with issue #6"*. **Neither was true on disk.** `master` was open, and no tooling exists.

That is the same defect this epic's own governance has been cataloguing at the *fleet* level all
week — **declared but not enforced** — found one level up, at the *platform*. The product has a
magnificent gate and no mechanism that makes anyone run it.

### P0-1 — `master` protection (DONE, but by hand — see the doctrine breach)

Applied and read-back verified:

```json
{"required_linear_history":{"enabled":true},"allow_force_pushes":{"enabled":false},"allow_deletions":{"enabled":false}}
```

Deliberately **not** applied, with reasons, because the obvious settings would break the repo:

- `required_status_checks` — **omitting it is the correct call today**: no CI exists to satisfy a
  check, so requiring one would deadlock every merge in the repo. This is the design problem in
  P0-2.
- `required_pull_request_reviews` — requiring a review would **break the autonomous-merge doctrine**
  (`AGENTS.md` rule 10). Verification replaces the reviewer here; encoding the opposite would be
  worse than no protection.

**⚠️ Honest breach to record, not hide:** this was set by an **operator API call** — a console
equivalently — which is exactly what **GR-5** forbids. It was applied as urgent protection for an
unprotected default branch, and it is **not reproducible**: nothing in the repo declares it, so a
fork, a restore, or a second repo diverges silently. P0-3 is the repair.

### P0-2 — How does a code-native gate become a *required* check, with Actions banned?

GR-15 forbids GitHub Actions, and Actions is the only mechanism GitHub offers for a required status
check. So the repo has an unsolved tension:

> *a required check needs a check-run; a check-run needs an App or Actions; Actions is banned.*

This is the real enterprise blocker and it needs an ADR, not a workaround. Options to evaluate:
a **GitHub App** that runs the gate out-of-band and posts a check-run (no Actions, satisfies the
ban, and the App token already exists — `controller/app-token.sh`); a **required commit status**
posted by the ops runner's `make verify`; or accepting **PR-required + linear history** as the
enforceable subset and documenting the residual risk loudly. **Do not silently pick one.**

### P0-3 — Branch protection as code (issue #6's unkept promise)

`branch-protection-{apply,verify}.sh` driven by a declared, versioned policy
(`governance/platform/branch-protection.yaml`), with:
- `apply` that PUTs the declared state and is **idempotent**;
- `verify` that **reads back** and fails on any drift (the same read-back discipline the fleet
  already uses for claims and drift);
- a **gate** that fails when the declared policy and the live protection differ — so the protection
  cannot be silently removed, which is precisely how it was silently absent.

### P1 — The remaining enterprise surfaces

4. **GR-15 violation**: `ci-failure-scanner.yml` is `active` on a 10-minute cron. Either retire it
   and replace it with a code-native scanner (ops runner + cron, per GR-15), or record a dated,
   reasoned exemption. Its 5 runs in 4 hours also mean it is *creating issues on a schedule* —
   measure whether it is a board-noise source before deciding.
5. **API contract**: an OpenAPI document for `control-plane` + `identity`, generated-or-checked in
   the gate so the contract cannot drift from the code. A SaaS without a published API contract is
   not consumable by an enterprise buyer.
6. **Tenant-isolation proof**: multi-tenancy is the security property an enterprise actually buys.
   Four tests is not a proof. Requires a provoked cross-tenant negative control (tenant A must be
   *unable* to read tenant B), in the gate.
7. **`CODEOWNERS` + release discipline**: owners per pillar; a `v1.0.0` plan with the SemVer
   contract the product actually promises.

### Acceptance

- [ ] `master` protection is **declared as code**, applied idempotently, and **read-back verified**
      by a gate that fails on drift.
- [ ] The required-check question is **decided in an ADR** and implemented, or the residual risk is
      documented by name.
- [ ] GR-15 holds: no active Actions workflow, and the scanner's function is code-native or exempted
      in writing.
- [ ] `control-plane` publishes a checked OpenAPI contract.
- [ ] A provoked cross-tenant isolation negative control is in the gate.
- [ ] `CODEOWNERS` exists; the release plan names the version the product commits to.

### Verify

```
bash scripts/check-branch-protection.sh && bash scripts/check-gr15.sh && make verify
```

items.title: The fleet acceptance test FAILS: a fleet lane produces no work product and loops unbounded when one stage refuses
items.body:
Parent: #160
Refs #727 #723 #754 #793 #796

## The acceptance test: a fleet lane does not complete e2e, and produces no work product

### The test, stated in advance

> give the fleet a single github issue and have it complete e2e and ensure the quality is as good as
> if it was from this exact terminal — that is the test

Run on 2026-09-15 against `master` = `d455fda`, with the brain and sister both verified on that
commit. Test vehicle: **#796**, ordered through the documented A2A path.

### Verdict: **FAIL — no work product, and an unbounded loop**

The lane the fleet minted (`ao-796-b9cfeb6a`, branch `issue-796-brain-di`) ended with **0 commits,
0 changed files, no PR, and the issue still open.**

### What worked — the chain is real, and it is the designed chain

Every stage below was measured, not assumed:

| Stage | Evidence |
|---|---|
| operator → brain | `channel order: OK — operator-796-parity queued for the brain` |
| brain consumed it | `[brain] order operator-796-parity (#796) \| task={"issue": 796, …}` |
| brain dispatched + acked | `[brain] → dispatched #796 at pro/medium — channel send: OK` ; outbox `ack` with `correlation_id: operator-796-parity` ; `dispatched=46 → 47` |
| capacity gate (#718) | `[terminal] capacity: #796 admitted — effective=1 bound_by=disjoint (pool=10 disjoint=1 resource=11)` |
| runner preflight (#733) | `runner=claude -p --model deepseek-v4-pro risk=normal` — the process was observed alive with the STANDING MANDATE prompt |
| claim + lane | lane `ao-796-b9cfeb6a` minted, branch `issue-796-brain-di` |
| the subagent ran the gate | `.verify/verify.log` 5996 B, `.results.tsv` 29 rows, **no non-zero rows** |
| runaway guard (#723) | `DEAD-LETTERED by runaway-guard — run did not land: failed` |

So the A2A control plane, the FinOps routing, the capacity bound, the runner preflight and the
runaway guard **all functioned**. The failure is not in any of them.

### What failed

**1. The fleet could not claim the issue for 15 minutes at a time.** The board snapshot's TTL is 15
minutes and **nothing refreshes it on a trigger**:

```
claim REFUSED: snapshot-stale — snapshot is 36.9m old (threshold 15m)
           — refresh first: python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py snapshot --from-github
```

The crontab carries three fleet entries — `*/2 fleet/watchdog.py run`,
`*/2 governance/reconcile/cli.py watch --once --apply`, `23 4 fleet/prune.py run --apply` — and
**none of them refreshes `.board/snapshot.json`.** After an operator refresh
(`snapshot: wrote .board/snapshot.json (448 issues, 278 with declared chain edges)`) the *same*
directive immediately proceeded to claim → lane → gate. That is **#727 "board triggers:
refresh-or-park on a stale snapshot"**, unbuilt.

**2. The refusal did not bound anything — the directive re-executed 13 times.** Measured:
`grep -c "executing directive brain-directive-0250e1e2" .fleet/sister.log` → **13**. The directive
stayed in `.fleet/inbox/` and was re-drained every cycle, and each execution **minted the same lane
and spawned a gate**:

```
8 gates  /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-796-b9cfeb6a      ← AO-GR-22, again, in one worktree
sister escalations: 6208
load: 8 → 22.89
```

This is the same unbounded shape as the 26-gate lane from earlier today. #723 bounded the
*dead-letter*, but the cycle **claim refused → directive stays in the inbox → re-drain → re-execute**
has no counter, no backoff, and no terminal state.

**3. The remedy is unreachable from inside the loop.** `python3 fleet/control.py drop --directive
<id> --reason <text>` answers `drop sent — the sister will dead-letter directive … to the mailbox` —
the drop is a **message the sister must process**. A loop that is not draining its mailbox cannot
process the remedy for not draining its mailbox. (It did eventually take effect through the runaway
guard, after ~13 cycles; the operator's own move was redundant and failed with `FileNotFoundError`
because the sister had already consumed it — recorded here so the remedy is not credited with
stopping a loop it was too late to reach.)

### Why this is the finding, not a bug report

The test is the right test, and it answers the operator's governance question directly: **every
governance control the fleet has is enforced at a boundary the loop does not cross.** Capacity is
checked at admission, the runner at preflight, the claim at claim time, the attempt budget at
dead-letter — and **nothing between them bounds the cycle that runs when one of them refuses.** The
fleet behaves well when the whole chain succeeds and becomes unbounded the moment one stage refuses.

### What must be built before this test can pass

1. **#727** — refresh-or-park on a stale snapshot, as a **board trigger** (the crontab already runs
   three fleet jobs every 2 minutes; the refresh belongs to one of them), so a 15-minute TTL never
   refuses work that is otherwise valid.
2. **Per-directive consumption, bounded.** A refusal must be a **state transition** on the
   directive, not a no-op that leaves it drainable: a directive that is refused N times is
   **dead-lettered with the refusal named**, never re-executed. This is AO-GR-21 applied to the
   *sister's* drain path, not only to the brain's dispatch path.
3. **One gate per worktree, enforced** — #724 is built and green (`5f6981a`) but **still unlanded**;
   `ao-796` re-proved the need for it with 8 concurrent gates.
4. **A remedy the loop can actually reach.** A control verb that only takes effect once the loop is
   healthy is not a control. `drop` must be effective from outside the loop (the mailbox must be
   honoured, or the verb must act on the file), and that must be **provoked** in a gate.
5. **The parity harness.** This run was scored by an operator reading logs. The acceptance test must
   be a **repeatable instrument**: give it an issue number, and it produces the verdict per
   dimension — `Verify:` output quoted, attestation `git_sha` == merged commit, gate WIRED,
   negative control provoked, commit trailer, PR contract, isolation audit, branch pushed then
   deleted, issue closed with evidence, and **no claim stated without its measurement**.

### Acceptance

- [ ] One issue, ordered through `fleet/channel.py order`, reaches a **merged PR with quoted gate
      evidence** and a **closed issue**, with **no operator intervention** after the order.
- [ ] A refusing stage **bounds** the directive: refused N times ⇒ dead-lettered by name, and the
      lane never accumulates more than one gate (AO-GR-22 holds throughout).
- [ ] The parity verdict is produced by a **runnable** harness, not by an operator reading logs.
- [ ] Every dimension above is **provoked** (a lane that fails a dimension fails the harness).

### Verify

```
bash scripts/check-fleet-parity.sh --issue <n> && make verify
```

items.title: `sent` is treated as `done`: a dispatched directive that dies suppresses its issue forever, and the brain idles with ready work
items.body:
Parent: #160

## `sent` is treated as `done`: a dispatched directive that dies suppresses its issue forever, and the brain idles with ready work on the board

### Measured on this box, 2026-09-15 ~03:1x

The brain reported itself idle for **25+ minutes** while the board carried **63 open issues**:

```
[brain] idle 1535s | orders pending=0 | dispatched=46 | claims=0 | HEAD=d455fda | watchdog=recovering
```

Its own idle path calls `advance_ready()` every tick, and that function **does** find work:

```
advance_candidates -> 3 ready
   #132  CMR vendor compliance gap: shared-services
   #133  CMR vendor compliance gap: googleworkspace
   #786  Close-out: record-verification is permanently unsatisfiable once the lane is reclaimed
```

Every one of the three was silently suppressed, forever, by a marker that only records that the order was **sent**:

```
.fleet/brain/dispatched/advance-132.json
.fleet/brain/dispatched/advance-133.json
.fleet/brain/dispatched/advance-786.json

brain log: [brain] → advanced waves: dispatched [132, 133]
           [brain] → advanced waves: dispatched [786]
```

### The mechanism

`fleet/brain.py::dispatch` refuses on marker **existence**:

```python
marker = order_marker(order)
if marker is not None and marker.exists():
    return False, f"{DUPLICATE_SUPPRESSED} — {marker.name} records that this order was already sent"
```

and `write_marker(marker, order, "sent")` writes it permanently. The docstring states the
intent — *"Restart-safe by construction … the at-most-once property this exists for"* — and the
at-most-once property is **correct for delivery**. The defect is that **`sent` is not `done`**:

- a directive that was sent and **completed**, and
- a directive that was sent and **died** (quarantined, dead-lettered, runner crash, phantom run)

are **indistinguishable**, because the only surviving evidence is that the send happened.

### Why each of the three died — and why nothing noticed

- **#132 / #133** — their directives were the source of the unbounded re-dispatch that took the
  box to `load 51.80` earlier today; they were **quarantined** to stop it. The markers remain.
- **#786** — this is the shape that matters most. Its directive went to the sister, which wrote a
  run marker with **`child_pid: null`** and **never executed it** (the same defect as #793's
  liveness finding and #366 defect (a)). The run produced nothing; the dispatch marker persisted.

In all three cases the issue is **still open, still ready, and now unreachable** — the pipeline for
it is welded shut by a marker that says only *"we sent something once"*.

### Why this is a P1, and what it breaks

- **AO-GR-13 "never idle" cannot hold.** The fleet reports idle and looks healthy while it refuses
  work it has itself just declared ready. Idle is exactly when the board should be advancing.
- **It is silent.** `DUPLICATE_SUPPRESSED` is a *normal* return value on the happy path (a restart
  re-reading a plan), so the idle path `continue`s without printing. Nothing distinguishes
  "suppressed because it is genuinely in flight" from "suppressed because it died 4 hours ago".
- **It compounds.** Every directive that dies welds one more issue shut, so the reachable ready set
  only ever shrinks. A fleet that has dispatched 46 orders and completed fewer ends up idle by
  construction — which is precisely the "it appears to run but does not progress" failure this
  spine exists to remove.
- **It hides itself from the operator.** `.fleet/brain/done` holds 46 markers and
  `.fleet/brain/dispatched` 32; nothing reconciles either against the board.

### What to build

1. **Reconcile the marker against reality, not against its own existence.** A dispatched marker
   whose issue is **still open**, which has **no live claim**, **no live run**, and **no in-flight
   directive**, is **stale** — the issue is **re-eligible**, and the re-dispatch is **counted**
   (so it is bounded by #723's attempt budget and backoff, never an unbounded retry loop).
2. **Make the three states distinguishable.** `sent` / `in-flight` / `terminal(completed|dead)`
   must be separable from the marker set alone. A marker must not be the only evidence of
   completion.
3. **Report the reconciliation.** A stale marker that is re-armed, and one that has exhausted its
   attempt budget and is therefore **parked with the issue named**, are both findings — never a
   silent `continue`.
4. **Do not break at-most-once.** The marker must still suppress a genuine duplicate (a restart
   re-reading a plan) — the fix is to add completion/expiry, not to weaken the delivery guarantee.
5. **A provoked negative control.** The gate must **provoke** it: write a dispatched marker for an
   open issue with no live claim/run, and require the reconciler to classify it stale and re-arm it
   — while a marker for an issue with a **live** run stays suppressed. Asserting the re-arm without
   the second half would pass a reconciler that simply ignores the marker set.

### Acceptance

- [ ] `advance_candidates`' ready set is no longer permanently suppressed by a marker whose
      directive died — measured by re-running the idle path and observing the dispatch.
- [ ] A stale marker is re-armed **at most** its attempt budget, then parked with the issue named.
- [ ] A marker for an issue with a live claim/run is still suppressed (at-most-once preserved).
- [ ] The reconciliation is a **printed finding**, not a silent `continue`.
- [ ] The gate provokes both halves and is WIRED (`scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh`).
- [ ] `make verify` green, with the attestation naming the merged commit.

### Verify

```
bash scripts/check-dispatch-reconcile.sh && make verify
```

items.title: portal roster test is filesystem-order dependent: seed selected by next(glob()) instead of highest revision
items.body:
Found while landing EPIC #708's lanes with the code-native landing driver (#764).

## Problem

`portal/tests/test_live_registry_telemetry.py::test_roster_identity_is_resolved_from_the_live_registry`
selects a registry seed by **filesystem order**:

```python
next(_SEEDS.glob(f"{profile_id}.*.yaml"))
```

`scandir` order is arbitrary and differs between directories, while the loader resolves the
**highest revision**. So the test asserts against one seed while the code under test uses
another, and the verdict depends on where the checkout happens to live.

## Measured

At the **same commit**, two worktrees disagree:

| tree | `portal/tests` |
|---|---|
| long-lived lane worktree | `1 failed, 356 passed in 76.50s` |
| fresh worktree, same commit | `357 passed` |

Both trees contain `registry/profiles/seeds/paperclip.1.0.0.yaml` **and** `paperclip.1.1.0.yaml`;
only the directory's `scandir` order differs. The failure is
`portal/tests/test_live_registry_telemetry.py:54: AssertionError`.

## Impact

A lane whose code is correct is refused by the pre-merge contract (#764), so the unattended
landing path (`make land`) cannot land anything from a long-lived worktree — the red is neither
pre-existing-on-master nor lane-caused, so the driver conservatively refuses it by name.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Seed selection is **deterministic**: highest revision wins (semver order), never `next(glob())`.
- [ ] A negative control proves the selection is order-independent — e.g. the same test passes when
      the seeds directory is materialised in the opposite order (two temp dirs, both orders).
- [ ] The test asserts against the same seed the loader resolves (one resolver, not two).
- [ ] `portal/tests` is green in a long-lived worktree **and** in a fresh one.

## Verify

```
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q portal/tests
bash scripts/check-landing.sh
```

**Relates:** #764 (landing driver), #642 (an earlier instance of the same order trap).

items.title: Governance is declared in governance/** but not enforced at spawn — local and fleet subagents obey different rules, and one lane ran 26 gates
items.body:
Parent: #708

## Governance is *declared* in `governance/**` but not *enforced at spawn* — so a local subagent and a fleet subagent obey different rules, and one lane ran 26 gates

### The operator's report (verbatim)

> governance/** around agent's should be built into the agent e2e upon spawning as i am
> noticing inconsistent behavior between direct subagents that are run locally in this
> copilot session and sub agents that are being spawned by the remote cron process and
> remote fleet and its maxing out the host again

### Measured, on this box, at the time of filing

```
load average: 51.80   on 14 cores            ← 3.7x oversubscribed
distinct worktrees running a gate: 9
        26  /home/akushnir/ao-worktrees/ao-786-507a704a   ← TWENTY-SIX gates, one worktree
         1  every other worktree                          ← every other lane is compliant
gates seen=33  terminated=25  kept=8
```

Every other lane ran exactly **one** gate — the intended behaviour. **`ao-786` ran 26.** That
single lane was the peg. AO-GR-22 ("at most one composite gate per worktree") is **declared**
in `docs/GOLDEN-RULES.md` and **not enforced anywhere**, so the rule held for 8 lanes and
failed silently for the 9th.

### The two spawn paths, and where they diverge

| | Remote (fleet) | Local (this session) |
|---|---|---|
| entry point | `fleet/terminal.py::build_prompt` (line 281) | the agent tool, ad hoc |
| standing mandate | **yes** — inlined into the prompt | none |
| session identity | **yes** — `AO_SESSION_ID`/`AO_BRANCH`, trailer demanded | none |
| worktree minted | **yes** — one per lane | none |
| claim | **yes** — loop claims, loop releases in `finally` | self-run or skipped |
| context pack | **yes** — issue body + acceptance + prior lessons | none |
| lane/one-gate bound | declared, **not enforced** | not enforced |
| attempt budget | #723, **only if the loop is on current code** | none |

The remote path is **better behaved** — but its governance lives **inline in a prompt string**,
not in a verifiable contract. Nothing checks that a spawn carried the envelope; the guarantee
is that someone remembered to write it into `build_prompt`. And the local path shares none of
it. So the same task executed on the two paths gets two different governance regimes, which is
exactly the inconsistency reported.

### Two live proofs that "declared" is not "enforced"

**1. One lane, 26 gates, no gate could see it.** `scripts/check-gate-lock.sh` and
`fleet/gatelock.py` exist in lane `ao-724-0d3d26dc` (committed `5f6981a`, green, **#724 still
OPEN, unlanded**), so on `master` there is *no* admission control at all. A rule that is only
in a doc cannot refuse anything.

**2. The fleet's own liveness evidence contradicts itself, and the wrong half wins.**

```
.fleet/runs/487c3aa7-….json    issue 234  pid 17797  child_pid null  started 21:18:00Z
.fleet/runs/brain-directive-b351….json  issue 234  pid 17797  child_pid null  21:18:54Z
.fleet/runs/brain-directive-fb82….json  issue 170  pid 17797  child_pid null  21:18:54Z
.fleet/sister.heartbeat.json   {"pid":17797, "state":"idle", "commit":"592b132", "runs":0}
```

`fleet/watchdog.py::run_in_flight()` reads **the loop's** pid:

```python
def run_in_flight() -> bool:
    """True when a run marker names a loop pid that is still alive."""
    for path in RUNS_DIR.glob("*.json"):
        record = read_beat(path)
        if record and process_alive(record.get("pid")):   # 17797 is alive, forever
            return True
```

`child_pid` is **`null`** in all four markers — no child — yet each holds the lock open because
the *loop* is alive. So markers written **5.6 hours ago** pin the loop, the watchdog refuses to
respawn a rung it believes is busy, and the sister's own heartbeat (`state: idle`, `runs: 0`)
is ignored for that decision. The rung therefore stays on `592b132` — pre-#723, with **no
attempt budget** — and re-dispatches without bound. That is the same causal chain as #366
defect (a), and it is what regenerates the 26 gates.

### Why this is the root, not a symptom

`governance/**` is a large, well-tested surface — claim ledger, lane isolation, lifecycle
close-out, reconcile, runaway guard, capacity. **None of it is applied by the act of spawning.**
Each is enforced only where someone wired it, so:

- a spawn that omits the contract is a spawn **nothing can refuse**;
- the enforcement that *does* exist (claim, isolation) is reachable only from the remote path;
- and the fleet's liveness evidence is trusted even when it contradicts itself.

### What to build

1. **One spawn envelope, one producer.** A `governance/spawn/` module emits the canonical,
   versioned envelope — issue, lane, worktree, session identity, commit trailer, claim owner,
   epic focus, capacity permit, attempt budget, gate bound, `Verify:` clause — as a **document**
   plus its rendered prompt block. `fleet/terminal.py::build_prompt` consumes it instead of
   inlining governance prose; the local path consumes the same document.
2. **The envelope is a precondition, not a suggestion.** A spawn that cannot present a
   well-formed envelope is **refused** (fail-closed, distinct exit code), the way the gate's
   tri-state already works.
3. **The local path is a first-class citizen.** Whatever governs a fleet spawn governs a
   session subagent — same envelope, same refusal — so the two regimes converge by
   construction rather than by convention.
4. **Fleet liveness must not contradict itself.** `run_in_flight()` must consider the
   **child**, and a marker whose `child_pid` is null/gone past the TTL must not hold the lock;
   a heartbeat saying `idle` while a marker says `busy` is a **reported** finding, never a
   silent win for the marker. (This closes #366 defect (a) and unblocks the rung from receiving
   #723's budget.)
5. **A provoked negative control.** Prove the refusal: a spawn missing each required field is
   refused **by name**, and the "one gate per worktree" bound is provoked with a real second
   gate — the shape `scripts/check-gate-lock.sh` already uses.

### Acceptance

- [ ] One module produces the envelope; both spawn paths consume it (no second copy of the
      governance prose in `fleet/terminal.py`).
- [ ] A spawn missing any required field is **refused**, provably, by a gate that can fail.
- [ ] `run_in_flight()` no longer holds the lock on a dead child, and the heartbeat/marker
      contradiction is reported.
- [ ] The one-gate-per-worktree bound is enforced on `master` (blocked on #724 landing).
- [ ] `make verify` green; the new checks WIRED in `scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh`.

### Verify

```
bash scripts/check-spawn-envelope.sh && bash -n governance/spawn/cli.py && make verify
```

items.title: Close-out: record-verification is permanently unsatisfiable once the lane is reclaimed, and nothing enforces the ordering
items.body:
## Objective

Make the close-out's `record-verification` invariant **satisfiable and order-safe**.
Today the invariant can be permanently unsatisfiable, and nothing stops the action
that makes it so.

## Measured evidence (2026-09-15, `master` @ `40a8c48e`)

Reproduced **3 times** on the three lanes I landed for epic #616 (#622 → PR #784,
#623 → PR #782, #626 → PR #783). For each, I merged, then reclaimed the lane, then
ran close-out:

```
$ python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --issue 622
close-out #622: NOT-OK
  skipped   merge-pull-request: already satisfied
  failed    record-verification: RuntimeError: no lane worktree for #622; the verified tree no longer exists
  skipped   delete-branch: already satisfied
  skipped   consume-directive: already satisfied
  skipped   release-claim: already satisfied
  performed record-closing-evidence: closing evidence journalled
  skipped   close-issue: already satisfied
  skipped   reclaim-lane: already satisfied
  REMAINS  VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING  #622  no green verification attestation is recorded
```

Same for #623 and #626. `lifecycle status --issue {622,623,626}` reaches the terminal
`stage: reclaimed` with all 8 stages traversed, yet `close` still reports `NOT-OK`.

### Root cause — the ordering is required but unenforced

`governance/lifecycle/cli.py:307-311`:

```python
def record_verification(self, issue: int, commit: str) -> str:
    """Re-run the repo gate in the lane and journal the attestation it writes."""
    lane = _lane_records(self.root).get(issue)
    if not lane or not lane.get("present"):
        raise RuntimeError(f"no lane worktree for #{issue}; the verified tree no longer exists")
```

`record_verification` **re-runs the gate inside the lane worktree**. So the instant the
lane is reclaimed the invariant can never be satisfied again — and
`governance/isolation/cli.py close` will remove a lane without asking whether the
lifecycle item still owes it. Two agents (me; and the #626 subagent, who flagged it
explicitly) hit this in one dispatch because the safe order — **close-out *before*
lane teardown** — is stated nowhere an executor reads at teardown time, and nothing
refuses the unsafe order.

### Why it matters beyond bookkeeping

A permanently-unsatisfiable invariant is the AO-GR-21 / GR-29 class: a control that
cannot succeed is a formality, and here it *inverts* — the record is permanently red
for work that **is** verified, so:
- `lifecycle audit` reports the item forever, and `close --apply` would file a stale
  `lifecycle:VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING` finding on the board (new noise per lane), while
- the *real* evidence (the lane's quoted `make verify` PASS **and** the post-merge
  gate `PASS (100 of 104 checks)` at `40a8c48e`, attestation `result=PASS`,
  `check_count=104`, `git_sha=40a8c48e613396745354566ef699cbe4c4a84bda`) is discarded
  because it was not recorded before teardown.

## Remedy — pick the mechanism, not a number

At least one of:
1. **Refuse the unsafe order.** `isolation close` (and any lane teardown) refuses to
   remove a lane while `lifecycle` says that issue still owes `record-verification`,
   naming the command to run first. `--force` remains the documented escape hatch.
2. **Make the invariant order-independent.** `record_verification` accepts the
   attestation of the **merged commit** (what actually ships) when the lane no longer
   exists, instead of requiring the lane tree.
3. **Run close-out as part of teardown**, so the two cannot be sequenced wrongly by
   an executor who never read this rule.

Ask for the negative control with whichever is chosen: a lane reclaimed before
close-out must produce a **named refusal** (option 1), or a satisfied invariant
(option 2) — never today's silent permanent `VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING`.

## Verify

```
python3 governance/lifecycle/cli.py close --issue <a lane reclaimed before close-out>
```
must not report `REMAINS VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING` for a lane whose gate was green —
either it refuses the teardown up front (naming the ordering), or it records the
merged commit's attestation.
