items.title: EPIC: ERPNext & DeepSeek FinOps — token-optimal subscription engine from CRM hook to ledger (operator mandate)
items.milestone: M32 - ERPNext & DeepSeek FinOps (ledger-faithful subscription engine)
items.body:
# EPIC — ERPNext & DeepSeek FinOps: from manual reconciliation to a token-optimal, ledger-faithful subscription engine

> Operator mandate 2026-09-14: document the current multi-product subscription flows, manual reconciliation points and API cost structures; architect ERPNext as the financial system of record with localized AI inference; deploy caching/FinOps controls; and validate the whole stack end-to-end. **Target: elite — maximum cost reduction, every claim measured.**

## Why this epic exists

Today money and tokens flow through disconnected surfaces: customer acquisition lives in the CRM front-end, revenue lives in manual invoices and spreadsheets, and inference spend accrues per-API-call with no cache-efficiency discipline. The measured consequence is the silo between acquisition and ledger plus unbounded token spend. This epic closes the loop with one mechanical chain: **conversion event → ERPNext ledger → cache-optimal inference → metered, audited cost**.

The ERPNext module epic **#645** (ordered by #612) is the system-of-record foundation this epic builds on; the production go-live #607 is where the measured outcome surfaces. This epic owns the *financial and token economics* of that stack — not the ERP feature surface (#645 owns that) and not the deploy (#607 owns that).

## Phase 1 — Current-State Mapping & Gap Identification

**Action items:**
1. Document the exact multi-product subscription flows and every manual data reconciliation point across the infrastructure.
2. Map the exact token flows from the DeepSeek API (request/response shapes, `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` vs `prompt_cache_miss_tokens` baselines, cost per call class).
3. Inventory the current CRM conversion hooks and establish current-state SaaS metric collection: MRR/ARR tracking, cloud compute burn, manual invoicing bottlenecks.

**Gap identification:** locate every data silo between front-end customer acquisition and back-end financial ledgers — name each silo, its owner surface, and what breaks when it loses sync.

## Phase 2 — To-Be Architecture: ERPNext & DeepSeek Integration Blueprint

**Action items:**
1. Architect the target state: ERPNext as the core financial system of record, integrated with localized AI inference pipelines (ADR, diagrams, contract).
2. Define strict DeepSeek API prefix templates that maximize disk-level cache-hit tokens (`prompt_cache_hit_tokens`) and minimize inference overhead.
3. Implement webhook bridges that connect CRM conversion events directly to ERPNext accounting modules.

**Gap identification:** pinpoint the payload formats that require localized MCP trimming to avoid cache misses and extraneous token consumption.

## Phase 3 — Implementation & Caching Execution: FinOps & Token Optimization

**Action items:**
1. Build a localized MCP response-filtering layer that truncates verbose tool outputs before they reach the DeepSeek model context.
2. Ship automated tracking scripts that audit DeepSeek cache-efficiency headers (`prompt_cache_hit_tokens` vs `prompt_cache_miss_tokens`) relative to operational billing queries inside ERPNext.
3. Measure token-efficiency gains and adjust sliding-window memory rules to eliminate redundant context processing.

**Gap identification:** measure token-efficiency gains (before/after deltas, not claims) and adjust memory rules on the measured evidence.

## Phase 4 — End-to-End Testing & Compliance Audit: Validation & Governance

**Action items:**
1. Run end-to-end sandbox simulations: an AI agent triggers a customer sign-up, initiates automated billing routines in ERPNext, and validates revenue recognition rules — with no manual intervention.
2. Confirm compliance with system security standards.

**Gap identification:** resolve latent transaction discrepancies, webhook latency delays, and edge cases in automated journal-entry posting — each found edge case gets a test before it is fixed.

## Definition of done (epic level)

1. The current-state map is a committed doc with every silo named and measured (`docs/erp-finops/`).
2. The target architecture is an ADR in `docs/decision-records/` and the prefix-template contract is enforced by a gate that can fail (GR-12).
3. The MCP filtering layer, cache-efficiency audit and memory-rule tuning all land with before/after token-cost evidence in their PR bodies.
4. The e2e sandbox simulation passes in `e2e/` (golden path + negative controls) with the revenue-recognition assertion exercised.
5. `make verify` PASS at every merged head; no child closes without its own `Verify:` output.

## FinOps discipline (this epic dogfoods its own subject)

Every child carries a model tier chosen by the brain's FinOps block; cost-reduction work is judged by measured cost deltas — a PR claiming savings without a before/after number is a finding, not a delivery. Cache-efficiency metrics are reported against the audit script from Phase 3, never a hand-counted table.

## Non-goals

- Not the ERP feature surface — that is #645. Not the production deploy — that is #607.
- No ERPNext code vendored or committed (GPL-3.0; pattern harvest only, provenance per GR-10).
- No ad-hoc infra, no console clicks, no secrets in code (GR-5/GR-6); new surfaces ship flag-gated OFF.

## Verify

```bash
make verify
make gate
```

## Children

- Phase 1: #666 current-state money map (subscription flows + reconciliation points) · #667 DeepSeek token-flow baseline + CRM hook inventory · #668 SaaS metrics current state + silo map.
- Phase 2: #669 ADR (ERPNext system of record + localized inference) · #670 DeepSeek prefix-template contract + gate · #671 CRM→ERPNext webhook bridges (Blocked-by #645).
- Phase 3: #672 localized MCP response-filtering layer · #673 cache-efficiency audit scripts · #674 sliding-window memory-rule tuning.
- Phase 4: #675 e2e sandbox simulation (sign-up → billing → revenue recognition; Blocked-by #645/#607) · #676 compliance audit + journal-posting edge cases.

_AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW) — epic authored by the brain (copilot-brain) on the operator's mandate._

items.title: ERP-01: Module foundation — integrations/erp skeleton, manifest, indexer data contract
items.body:
Parent: #645

## Objective

Stand up the ERP module as a declared, mandatory, flag-gated module whose
**entire data contract is served by the knowledge indexer** — the
`governance/knowledge/` catalogue becomes the single source of ERP domain
knowledge, so later enhancements change the catalogue, not scattered files.

## Scope

- `integrations/erp/README.md` — module contract, pointer to
  `docs/ERP-MODULE-GAP-ANALYSIS.md`.
- `integrations/erp/module.yaml` — module manifest: `mandatory: true`,
  feature flag `erp-module` default `off` (GR-5), `data_source: indexer`.
- `integrations/erp/catalog/**` — the ERP domain catalogue (module map,
  document families, capability list) in schema-validated form.
- `governance/knowledge/sources.py` — register the catalogue and module docs
  as indexer sources (existing kinds: `pattern-template` for schemas,
  `architecture` for docs); regenerate `governance/knowledge/catalog.json`.
- Cannibalize: paperclip manifest/admission shapes and the knowledge-index
  source-spec pattern. Upstream ERPNext is a pattern source only (GPL-3.0) —
  record provenance (GR-10), copy no code.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `integrations/erp/module.yaml` declares the module mandatory with its
   flag defaulting OFF, and validates against a schema.
2. The indexer build succeeds with the new sources and `validate` exits 0;
   the catalogue carries ERP items with complete provenance.
3. `query --text "sales order"` returns the ERP catalogue entry, proving the
   module's information really comes from the indexer.
4. No second knowledge store is created — no duplicated rules, no hardcoded
   ERP facts outside the catalogue.
5. The gap-analysis doc is referenced from `docs/README.md`.

## Verify

- `python3 governance/knowledge/cli.py build && python3 governance/knowledge/cli.py validate`
- `python3 governance/knowledge/cli.py query --text "sales order" --kind pattern-template`
- `make verify`

items.title: EPIC: ERP module — indexer-fed enterprise integration of the ERPNext feature surface (e2e-mandatory, ordered by #612)
items.body:
Parent: #4

## Objective

Ordered by #612 ("ERP module"): add an ERP capability to the
agent-orchestrator control plane as a **complete, mandatory module** — the
frappe/erpnext feature surface, gapped feature-by-feature in
`docs/ERP-MODULE-GAP-ANALYSIS.md`, rebuilt as backend + frontend
integration with end-to-end verification, and with **every module datum
flowing from the knowledge indexer** (`governance/knowledge/`).

The module lives at `integrations/erp/` — the `integrations/paperclip/`
assembly is the precedent. Upstream ERPNext (GPL-3.0) is a **pattern
source only**: no code is copied, every harvested shape records provenance
(GR-10), and upstream's end-to-end test discipline is cannibalized into our
`e2e/` harness.

## Definition of done

1. `integrations/erp/` ships the document model, transactional flows,
   REST surface, auth scoping and metering for the gapped feature set.
2. The portal carries the module's frontend surfaces (dashboards, lists,
   forms, reports), behind a feature flag that defaults **OFF** (GR-5).
3. Everything the module knows is indexer-fed: ERP schemas and catalogues
   are registered in `governance/knowledge/sources.py`; nothing re-declares
   knowledge the indexer already carries.
4. `e2e/` covers the ERP module as a **mandatory** enterprise stage —
   golden path plus negative controls — cannibalized from ERPNext's e2e
   patterns, not its code.
5. Tenant identity/RBAC scopes ERP data per tenant, and ERP usage is
   metered on the telemetry ledger.

## Non-goals

- Not an ERP rewrite and not a fork: ERPNext stays upstream; no
  third-party code is vendored or committed (GPL-3.0; `.research/` is
  gitignored).
- Vertical industry apps (Education, Healthcare, Agriculture, Non-Profit,
  Hospitality) and the split-out Frappe HR/Payroll app are dispositioned
  **deferred** in the gap doc; if ever needed they arrive as their own
  direction issues.
- No console clicks or ad-hoc infra; the module ships flag-gated OFF
  like every other surface.

## Child lanes

| Child | Lane | Owns | Pillar |
|-------|------|------|--------|
| [#646](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/646) ERP-01 | erp-foundation | `integrations/erp/{README.md,module.yaml,catalog/**}`, `governance/knowledge/sources.py` + regenerated `catalog.json` | governance |
| [#647](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/647) ERP-02 | erp-core-model | `integrations/erp/core/**` — schemas, validators, workflow data | control-plane |
| [#648](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/648) ERP-03 | erp-tx-spine | `integrations/erp/tx/**` — selling to stock to accounting loop | control-plane |
| [#649](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/649) ERP-04 | erp-procure-mfg | `integrations/erp/ops/**` — procurement + manufacturing | control-plane |
| [#650](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/650) ERP-05 | erp-crm-projects | `integrations/erp/crm/**` — CRM, projects, quality, support | control-plane |
| [#651](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/651) ERP-06 | erp-api | `integrations/erp/api/**` — REST + OpenAPI | control-plane |
| [#652](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/652) ERP-07 | erp-portal | `portal/static/erp/**` + one `portal/server/` route module | control-plane |
| [#653](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/653) ERP-08 | erp-rbac | `integrations/erp/auth/**` — role/permission + field policy | identity-rbac |
| [#654](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/654) ERP-09 | erp-finops | `integrations/erp/finops/**` — metering, budget hooks | observability-finops |
| [#655](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/655) ERP-10 | erp-e2e | `e2e/erp/**` + `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` registration | control-plane |

Dependencies: ERP-03/04/06/09 blocked by ERP-02; ERP-07 by ERP-06;
ERP-08 by ERP-01; ERP-10 by ERP-06/07/08. One issue = one lane = disjoint
files (GR-3).

## Basis

- `docs/ERP-MODULE-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` — the feature-by-feature gap (this
  epic's contract).
- ERPNext public docs (`docs.frappe.io/erpnext`, `frappe.io/erpnext`) read
  2026-09-14; no upstream clone was made and no upstream code was copied.

items.title: RC-14: Owner-approved go-live run — phase 0 + phase 7 promotions
items.body:
Parent: #607

## Owner-approved go-live run — phase 0 + phase 7 promotions

This is the owner-gated execution lane for #607. Everything below is PREPARED code; nothing here runs until the operator grants the approvals (`infra/rollout/stage-model.yaml`: every transition requires `verify_green` + `approval_code` + `audit_record`; the deployer-SA `apply.yaml` pipeline is the only apply route — GR-5, no console, no ad-hoc apply).

## Pre-conditions (must all be measured green first)

- Web image wired (child #A merged) and `make verify` PASS at its merge commit.
- Readiness audit (child #B) reports all checks green, promotion-refusal negative control proved.
- `infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml` still all `"off"`; `infra/cloudbuild/apply-trigger.yaml` `disabled: true`.

## Execution sequence (each step = one approval + one promote + one audit record)

1. **Phase 0**: for `ci_cd.verify_trigger`, then `ci_cd.apply_trigger`:
   `python3 -m infra.rollout.cli grant-approval <flag> --to canary --approver <operator> --approval-id <id>` → `promote <flag> --to canary --approval <id> --actor deployer-sa`; repeat to `gradual` (requires `canary_health_ok`) and `full` (requires `gradual_complete`, 24h dwell).
2. **Apply trigger import**: import `infra/cloudbuild/apply-trigger.yaml` with `disabled: false` and `_ENABLE_APPLY: "true"`, only after `ci_cd.apply_trigger` reaches `full`.
3. **Phases 1-6**: promote `services.registry|gateway|engine|guardrails|telemetry|identity` through the same ladder — `promotion_order: strict-by-phase` forbids phase 7 before 1-6.
4. **Phase 7**: promote `services.portal` and `services.web` to `full`; the apply pipeline deploys the web surface at ai.purebliss.app.
5. **Acceptance**: `grep -E "stage: \"full\"" infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml` shows all promoted flags; `ai.purebliss.app` serves the fleet SPoG (`portal/server/fleet.py` routes), not the legacy seed.

## Close evidence

Every promotion's `verify_green` + `approval_code` + `audit_record` committed; the final apply pipeline run log quoted; the acceptance greps quoted.

_AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW)._

items.title: RC-13: Go-live readiness audit — rollout checks + apply route negative controls

Parent: #607

## Goal

Produce the `verify_green` evidence the #607 go-live promotions require, and validate the apply route end-to-end **without enabling or applying anything**. The stage model (`infra/rollout/stage-model.yaml`) gates every promotion on `verify_green` + `approval_code` + `audit_record`; this lane produces the measured readiness matrix the owner's go-live will cite.

## Task (read-only audit — no flag, trigger, or rollout-state edits)

1. Run the rollout conformance check: `python3 infra/rollout/checks/check_rollout.py` (or its wired path) against `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml`, `infra/rollout/go-live-plan.yaml`, `infra/rollout/rollout-state.yaml`, `infra/rollout/stage-model.yaml` — record the exact output.
2. Validate the rollout engine's dry paths: `python3 -m infra.rollout.cli` subcommands that can run without approvals (e.g. `validate-approval` refusal paths, `status`/`plan` if present) — prove the promotion would be REFUSED without an approval (negative control) and that the vocabulary is closed.
3. Validate the apply route configs fail-closed as declared: `infra/cloudbuild/apply.yaml` gate-flag step refuses when `_ENABLE_APPLY != "true"`; `infra/cloudbuild/apply-trigger.yaml` is `disabled: true` today; `infra/cloudbuild/web-image.yaml` refuses a mutable/empty tag. Quote the exact config lines + your check output.
4. Confirm the SPoG code and the portal serving surface exist on `origin/master` (the epic's Verify: `git cat-file -e origin/master:portal/server/fleet.py` and the SPoG suites), so the go-live has code to serve.
5. `make verify` in the lane worktree — quote the attestation (git_sha, result, check_count).

## Scope

READ-ONLY. No file edits in this lane; findings are reported in the issue comment, not patched here. If you find a code defect, list it with file+line and let the orchestrator file it.


items.title: EPIC: Git-ecosystem templates & governance — class/pattern/template/env/clobber/RCA/orphan gaps (issue #608)
items.body:
## Objective

Close the measured gaps across this repository's **git ecosystem** so every
surface is governed by **class, pattern, template, env contract, governance,
clobber prevention, RCA and orphan checking**, and every artifact is findable
through the **knowledge indexer** — making the system faster, smarter, more
accurate and consistent (issue #608, item 9). The gap analysis is
[`docs/GIT-TEMPLATES-GAP-ANALYSIS.md`](../blob/master/docs/GIT-TEMPLATES-GAP-ANALYSIS.md)
delivered by issue #608 (docs-only lane); the children below are its
remediation lanes. **One issue = one lane = one file-surface** — no two children
share a file.

## Measured landscape (2026-09-14, from issue #608's analysis)

| Checklist item | Surface (measured) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| class | `docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md` + `make surface-class` gate | **GAP** — git-ecosystem surfaces (`.github/**`, `.gitmessage`, git-governance packages) are not declared rows |
| pattern | no `docs/SHELL-PATTERNS.md` in this repo (hub has one) | **GAP** — no pattern doctrine, no enforcement |
| template | `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/fleet-task.yml` (one form, gated); `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (gated); `.gitmessage` (**`commit.template` unset**) | **PARTIAL** — no epic/bug forms; commit template unenforced |
| env variable | `governance/isolation` exports `AO_*` + `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` (AGENTS.md rule 15) | **PARTIAL** — no canonical env registry doc, no drift check |
| governance | `AGENTS.md`, `docs/GOLDEN-RULES.md`, dispatch/lifecycle claim gates | **OK** — this epic adds the missing inventory doc |
| clobber prevention | `.gitignore` (tracked), lane isolation, `O_EXCL` claim locks, atomic heartbeats | **PARTIAL** — no gate that runtime-state dirs stay ignored; no `.gitattributes` |
| RCA | `governance/lessons/rca-template.md` + `ledger.jsonl` + board-re-run gate | **OK** — shipped by #141, re-run by `check-board-gate.sh` |
| orphan checker | `governance/reconcile/` heartbeats + sweep/watch + gate | **PARTIAL** — session-scoped; worktree/branch-vs-ledger audit not gated |
| missed items | hooks are `.sample`-only; `.gitattributes` missing; ADR numbering manual; `docs/README.md` index completeness ungated; templates not in the knowledge index | **GAP** |
| indexer | `governance/knowledge/sources.py` | **PARTIAL** — git-ecosystem artifacts are not registered sources |

## Children (one lane per file-surface — no two children share a file)

| # | Issue | Owned files | Verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **#620** Surface-class rows for the git ecosystem | `docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md` | `make surface-class && bash scripts/check-docs.sh` |
| 2 | **#621** Shell-patterns doctrine + enforcement gate | `docs/SHELL-PATTERNS.md`, `scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` (new) | `bash scripts/check-shell-patterns.sh` |
| 3 | **#622** Epic + bug issue forms with gate coverage | `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**`, `scripts/check-issue-template.sh` | `bash scripts/check-issue-template.sh && make verify` |
| 4 | **#623** Commit contract: `.gitmessage` trailer layout + PR-template epic edge | `.gitmessage`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` | `bash scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` |
| 5 | **#624** Git-config boilerplate: `.gitattributes` + `commit.template` bootstrap gate | `.gitattributes` (new), `scripts/check-git-config.sh` (new) | `bash scripts/check-git-config.sh` |
| 6 | **#625** Clobber-prevention gate: runtime-state dirs stay ignored | `scripts/check-gitignore.sh` (new) | `bash scripts/check-gitignore.sh` |
| 7 | **#626** Register git-ecosystem artifacts in the knowledge indexer | `governance/knowledge/sources.py` | `make knowledge-index-build && make knowledge-index` |
| 8 | **#627** Canonical git/env variable registry doc | `docs/GIT-ENV-VARIABLES.md` (new) | `bash scripts/check-docs.sh` |
| 9 | **#628** Reconcile hardening: worktree/branch audit vs claims ledger | `governance/reconcile/**`, `scripts/check-reconcile.sh` | `bash scripts/check-reconcile.sh` |
| 10 | **#629** Docs index gate: every tracked `docs/*.md` is indexed | `scripts/check-docs.sh` | `bash scripts/check-docs.sh && make verify` |
| 11 | **#630** Wire the new gates into `make verify` (Blocked-by #621, #624, #625) | `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/gate-coverage-baseline.txt`, `Makefile` | `make verify` |

## Purpose (faster / smarter / more accurate / consistent — issue #608 item 9)

- **Faster:** templates and a canonical env registry mean a new lane or repo
  starts without rediscovering contracts; the knowledge indexer answers
  "where is this artefact, is it current" in one query.
- **Smarter:** class and pattern declarations let the dispatcher hold each
  git-ecosystem surface to its measured rung instead of an ad-hoc guess.
- **More accurate:** every recommendation above lands with a gate whose
  negative control must fail — no declaration without enforcement.
- **Consistent:** one form contract, one commit contract, one env contract,
  all re-derived from the same docs the gates read.

## Verification contract

Each child ships a `Verify:` command; no child closes without its real output.
This epic closes only when every declared child is closed with evidence (an
epic cannot close while a declared child is open — #611).

items.title: [fleet-task] governance/lifecycle: an epic can close completed while its declared children are open — and no invariant can express it
items.body:
Role (executor): subagent Epic: #269 Pillar: autonomous-ops Lane: autonomous-ops Model tier (FinOps): pro Thinking effort: medium Verify command: `bash scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh && python3 -m pytest governance/lifecycle -q -p no:cacheprovider` ## Goal Make **"an epic was closed while a declared child is still open"** a named, provoked lifecycle failure — so `governance/lifecycle/` can *express* it, `audit` reports it by code, and `scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh` provokes it like every other invariant. Success is: the vocabulary contains the invariant, a fixture provoking it makes `audit` report that code **by name**, the gate's own cross-check (provoked set == model set) still passes, and a *clean* fixture item still passes. ## The measurement that proves the gap `governance/lifecycle/model.py` declares a closed vocabulary of **10** codes, and every one is scoped to *the item's own artifacts*: ``` PR_NOT_MERGED · VERIFY_EVIDENCE_MISSING · BRANCH_NOT_DELETED · CLAIM_STILL_HELD DIRECTIVE_NOT_CONSUMED · LANE_NOT_RECLAIMED · CLOSING_EVIDENCE_MISSING ISSUE_NOT_CLOSED · FILING_LABELS_MISSING · QUARANTINE_STALE ``` `subject_kind` has exactly two values, `item` and `baseline`: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class Invariant: code: str requires: str remediation: str subject_kind: str = "item" ``` There is **no subject kind** whose subject is *an epic's child set*, so the defect class cannot be written down — and therefore cannot be caught: ``` $ git grep -n -i -E 'open child|children|sub_issue|type:epic' \ governance/lifecycle/ scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh # (no output) ``` The gate cannot be blamed for the omission; its own header explains why it is scoped this way, and that decision is sound: > *"It ships **no committed point-in-time GitHub record**: rules are asserted > against fixtures this script writes. A gate that reads live board state is green > whenever that state is stale."* That is a correct choice for *item* invariants. But it leaves the parent/child relation unguarded, because a child set is a board fact and no fixture can assert it. ## Reproduction — a real false closure, not a hypothetical Epic **#160** ("Session Fleet Operating Model") was closed `completed` at `2026-09-14T04:07:10Z` with the following closing sentence: > *"**Nothing else is outstanding for this epic.**"* Five of its declared children — each carrying `Parent: #160` as the first line of its own body — were **created before that closure and were still open**: ``` $ gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/160 --jq '.state,.closed_at' closed 2026-09-14T04:07:10Z $ for n in 241 287 309 366 367; do gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/$n \ --jq '"#\(.number) \(.state) created=\(.created_at) parent=\((.body|capture("^\\s*Parent:\\s*#(?

[0-9]+)").p))"' done #241 open created=2026-09-13T21:07:01Z parent=160 #287 open created=2026-09-13T22:18:38Z parent=160 #309 open created=2026-09-13T23:15:58Z parent=160 #366 open created=2026-09-14T01:50:58Z parent=160 <- labelled P0 #367 open created=2026-09-14T01:54:33Z parent=160 ``` Every row predates the closure by ≥2h15m. `make verify` was green throughout, and stayed green for 10 hours after — an epic closed with a **P0** child open raised no failure anywhere. #160 has since been reopened ([evidence](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/160#issuecomment-5668664414)). That reopen is a *manual* correction; this issue is what makes the next one fail by itself. ## Design constraints 1. **The invariant must be provoked, or it must not ship.** The gate is explicit that an invariant added without a provocation fails the gate rather than shipping an unexercised rule; the provoked-set cross-check is the load-bearing part, so both halves land together. 2. **No live board read in the gate.** Keep the gate network-free and fixture-driven. The child-set fact must arrive as *input* (a supplied child set / snapshot), exactly as the other invariants' facts do — do not make the gate depend on `.board/snapshot.json` being fresh, which is the trap already tracked by #170. 3. **An epic is closed only when its declared children are terminal.** "Declared" must be mechanical (the `Parent: #` marker the dispatcher already parses), not a hand-maintained list. 4. **Do not invent a violation class the vocabulary cannot carry.** If the shape needs a third `subject_kind`, add it deliberately and say why in the docstring. ## Scope `governance/lifecycle/model.py`, `governance/lifecycle/audit.py`, `governance/lifecycle/tests/**`, `scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh`, `governance/lifecycle/README.md`. ## Explicitly out of scope - **Must not touch** `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`, `Makefile` — contended, and #559 is the declared sole writer of the shared build files. - **No new `scripts/check-*.sh`**: a newly delivered check script that no gate invokes fails `gate-coverage` **by name**. Extend the existing lifecycle gate. - No GitHub Actions workflows (GR-15, fleet-wide disabled). - Do not re-open or repair any other epic's children; audit only. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `audit` reports the new code **by name** on a fixture epic that is closed while a declared child is open (`pytest governance/lifecycle -q`). - [ ] The same fixture with every child terminal is **clean** — the invariant can fail *and* pass (GR-12), asserted in the same test. - [ ] A child that names a *different* parent does not excuse or provoke it (negative control: the marker is read, not guessed). - [ ] `scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh` provokes the new invariant, and its provoked-set == model-set cross-check passes. - [ ] `bash scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh` exits 0; a mutation of the new predicate (e.g. treating a closed child as open) exits non-zero with the code named; the file is restored byte-identically (sha256, not just rc). - [ ] `make verify` PASS on the branch head, evidence quoting the attestation's `git_sha`. ## Chain markers ``` Parent: #269 Part-of: #269 Blocked-by: none ``` `#269` is closed, so the dispatch gate will refuse a claim on this issue until the brain issues a directive naming it (`claim --directive `) — **that is intended**. This is filed as a finding; it is not scavenging, and it must not be claimed ahead of the active chain. ## Evidence _(to be filled by the lane: the audit code list before/after, the provocation's rc, and the gate's attestation.)_ _AI-assistance: Copilot (Relentless, flash/LOW) — finding measured from the GitHub API and `origin/master`; no claim was taken and no lane work was done under it._

items.title: The gate-coverage baseline cannot enforce its own 'never grandfathered' rule — a lane can mute the detector for its own new check, and the rows go stale in a file no lane owns
items.body:
## The gate-coverage baseline cannot enforce its own "never grandfathered" rule

`scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh` states its own contract in its header:

> a NEWLY declared suite or a **NEWLY delivered `scripts/check-*.sh` is NEVER grandfathered — it fails immediately**, naming the path
> the baseline is checked in BOTH directions: an entry whose artifact is **now wired** … is a **STALE entry and fails**
> **REMOVING AN ENTRY is the only way to shrink the list**

**The first rule cannot bind.** "Newly delivered" is not computable from the baseline: it is a per-path list of strings with **no provenance** — no date, no commit, no author, no owner. So a lane that delivers a new check and cannot wire it (`scripts/verify.sh` is a single-writer file) can add a row for its *own* new check and the detector passes. The row is indistinguishable from a legitimate legacy one. GR-29: a doc-only rule is advisory; only a platform-enforced gate is binding. GR-12: a check that cannot fail is a formality.

### Measured, not theorised — three instances within one hour

| # | artifact | row planted | by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scripts/check-control-audit.sh` | `script  scripts/check-control-audit.sh  uninvoked  #559` | #595, **merged to master** |
| 2 | `scripts/check-control-functions.sh` | `script  scripts/check-control-functions.sh  uninvoked  #559` | #601 (open) |
| 3 | `scripts/check-control-functions.sh` | same row | #593 (closed unmerged as a duplicate) |

Three lanes reached for the same mechanism independently, which is what makes this systemic rather than a single lapse.

**The row is load-bearing, and the check never runs.** On `master` (`e9b4242`):

- no gate file names it — `check-control-audit` occurs **0** times in `scripts/verify.sh`, `Makefile`, `scripts/gate.sh`, `scripts/merge-gate.sh`, `scripts/qa-loop.sh`;
- in the entire `make verify` output the string occurs **exactly once**, under `== shell-syntax ==`, alphabetically between `check-context-pack-consumption.sh` and `check-control-verbs.sh` — that is a **`bash -n` syntax listing**, not an execution. The script's *syntax* parses; the check does not *run*;
- delete the row and the detector fails **by name** (`rc 1`): `FAIL  script scripts/check-control-audit.sh (invoked by no gate file: …)`.

So **#555 is CLOSED** — a `priority:P1`, `class:elite`, control-plane lane about exactly-once effects, the audit record and the refusal path — and its enforcing check is **inert**, while three downstream issues (#556, #559, #566) were unblocked on that basis. The verification of that lane currently rests on the lane's own word.

### The landmine this plants in #559's path (time-sensitive)

#559 (RC-8) is mandated to wire exactly these checks, and its own scope says it plainly: *"an unwired check is inert"*. Its **lane glob is `Makefile`, `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`, `docs/README.md`** — **`scripts/gate-coverage-baseline.txt` is in no lane's glob**, yet three lanes have now edited it.

Consequence: **the moment #559 wires `check-control-audit.sh`, its row becomes STALE and the detector fails** — in a file #559 does not own. The wiring commit that unblocks the chain is therefore on a collision course with a red gate it cannot fix within its declared lane. That is exactly the kind of surprise that stalls a blocker.

### Proposed fix — make deferral accountable instead of forbidden

The mechanism already exists (stale-entry detection); it needs **provenance**, in the detector's own per-path, no-glob idiom:

1. **Every row carries the issue that will retire it and the sha at which it was added.** A row without both is malformed and already fails.
2. **A row whose wiring issue is CLOSED while its artifact is still unwired fails**, naming both. A deferral to an open lane is honest; a deferral to a closed one is a permanent excuse.
3. **A row for an artifact that did not exist at the baseline's own last-touched commit fails.** This makes "newly delivered" *computable* and mechanically restores the rule the header already claims.
4. **Name an owner for `scripts/gate-coverage-baseline.txt`** — either add it to RC-8's lane glob (it is the wiring lane, and it is the lane the rows are deferred to), or declare a baseline owner. An unowned file that the gate requires to be edited is a blocker in waiting.

Keep the file per-path, keep removing entries as the only way to shrink it, keep the closed reason vocabulary — the fix adds provenance, it does not relax the gate.

### Verify (each provocation must fail; GR-12)

```bash
# 1. a brand-new check that nobody wires is NOT accepted by adding a row
#    (row names no wiring issue) -> rc 1, naming the path
# 2. a row whose wiring issue is CLOSED while the artifact is unwired -> rc 1, naming both
# 3. a row for an artifact absent at the baseline's last-touched commit -> rc 1
# 4. wire a baselined check and LEAVE the row -> rc 1 STALE (must stay red)
# 5. remove that row -> rc 0 (the honest path must be the cheap one)
# 6. the two live rows on master today must be reported, not silently accepted
```
Plus a mutation proof of the detector itself: mutate the assertion anchor, confirm the mutant's own `rc 1` naming the fault, restore, and confirm **sha256 byte-identical**.

### Proposed targets

`scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh` (the detector) and the lane glob of **#559** (to make the baseline owned). `scripts/gate-coverage-baseline.txt` must **never** be widened — the two live rows retire when #559 wires their checks.

--- 

*Reported by the lane that produced instance 3. It is filed rather than fixed because `scripts/verify.sh` and the baseline are RC-8's (#559) single-writer territory and this must land coordinated with that wiring, not in front of it. Duplicate PRs #593 and #600 were closed unmerged with full disclosure — two implementations of one issue must not both land.*

items.title: Raise the M28 surfaces (module registry + module brief) to enterprise class and declare them in the surface registry
items.body:
## Problem (measured on `origin/master` `6a3d216`)

The M28 surfaces delivered by #445 and #447 are held to **no solution-class at all**, and both sit at `pattern`:

```
$ git show origin/master:governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml | sed -n '/^surface_roots:/,/^waived_roots:/p'
surface_roots:
  - portal
  - gateway
  - telemetry
  - registry
waived_roots: []
```

`governance/` and `integrations/` are **not** in `surface_roots`, so `scripts/check-surface-class.sh` never looks at them — the gate is green and says nothing about the two surfaces this program just shipped. Measured by the gate's own rules (`governance/conformance/surfaces.py`, `measure_path_evidence` + `measured_class`):

| Surface | Path | contract | tests | controls | audit | schema | gate | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| module registry | `governance/modules` | yes | yes | **no** | **no** | **no** | yes | `pattern` |
| module brief | `integrations/paperclip/reporting` | yes | yes | **no** | **no** | **no** | yes | `pattern` |

Per `docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md`, the rungs are `template → class → pattern → enterprise → faang → elite`, and `enterprise` **adds `controls`, `audit`, `schema`** (plus the manual `rollback`). So both surfaces are two rungs below the class the rest of the program is held to, and nothing enforces it.

## Why this is real work, not label-chasing

For these two surfaces the missing evidence is exactly what a consumer needs and what compliance expects:

- **schema** — the registry's row shape is currently implicit in `model.py`; its only external promise is prose in `docs/MODULE-REGISTRY.md`. #447 composes a brief from it and future consumers will read it. Freezing the row shape as a `*.schema.json` turns that promise into a checkable contract.
- **controls** — the registry decides what is *fatal* (hub drift, a registered module with no seed, a duplicated id, in-tree source, inferred membership). Today that policy lives only as code branches. A declared control/policy artifact makes the acceptance policy explicit and reviewable.
- **audit** — the registry's **refusals are its compliance signal**, and the brief's **unresolved claims are its honesty signal**. Neither is recorded; both are currently only printed by a gate. An append-only audit trail is what an operator can point at.

## Scope

1. Give `governance/modules/**` the `enterprise` rung's machine evidence: a frozen `*.schema.json` for the registry row, a declared controls/policy artifact, and an append-only audit trail of every refusal and judged state — **each wired into the real code path**, not decorative files.
2. Same for `integrations/paperclip/reporting/**`: a frozen brief schema, a claim-resolution policy artifact, and an audit trail of claim resolution (resolved / finding-by-line).
3. Declare both surfaces in `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml` — at the rung their **measured** evidence supports, never above it — and add `governance` + `integrations` to `surface_roots`, so the class gate actually looks at them from now on.
4. Update the `docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md` table and its scope note.
5. Existing gates must keep passing and must cover the new artifacts (extend `scripts/check-module-registry.sh` / `scripts/check-module-brief.sh`; **no new check script**, so the shared build files are untouched and this lane cannot collide with #488/#555).

## Acceptance

- `bash scripts/check-surface-class.sh` → OK, with both surfaces listed at their declared class and **no** `surface-undeclared` finding for the newly scoped roots.
- The declared class equals the measured class (the gate refuses a declaration above the evidence — its own negative control proves that).
- The new schema/controls/audit artifacts are exercised by the packages' own suites, and the two existing gates still provoke every refusal by name.
- `make verify` green on the merged tree; the gate count rises only by what the existing gates cover.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `governance/modules/**`, `integrations/paperclip/reporting/**`, `governance/conformance/surfaces.yaml`, `docs/SURFACE-CLASS.md`, `scripts/check-module-registry.sh`, `scripts/check-module-brief.sh`.
- Does **not** own: `Makefile`, `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` (contended by #488/#555 — deliberately untouched).

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-surface-class.sh
bash scripts/check-module-registry.sh
bash scripts/check-module-brief.sh
python3 -m pytest governance/modules integrations/paperclip/reporting -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify
```

items.title: The chat serving surface's own suite (gateway/chat/tests, 50 tests) runs in no gate
items.body:
Parent: #500

## The gap, measured

`gateway/chat/tests` exists and **passes 50 tests**, but it is neither declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` nor named by any gate file — so the chat serving surface's own suite has **never run** in the gate of record, nor in the `make gate` manifest sweep (an undeclared suite is not swept).

```
$ python3 -m pytest gateway/chat/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
50 passed in 23.78s

$ grep -c '^gateway/chat$' scripts/pytest-suites.txt
0
$ grep -c 'gateway/chat' scripts/verify.sh
0
```

`scripts/check-drift.sh` already sees it and says so — at **WARN**, which is rc 0, so nothing enforces it:

```
check-drift: WARN — 'gateway/chat' has a committed tests/ dir but is not declared in scripts/pytest-suites.txt (register it or drop it)
```

This is the same defect class as #568 (`check-chat-surface.sh` landed unwired and made `master` red) and as #331 (a red `fleet` suite sat on master because the gate ran no pytest). Here the suite is green, so nothing is *broken* — it is simply **unenforced**, which is how the next regression gets in.

## Why it has no owner

`#503` (which delivered `gateway/chat/**`) is `closed/completed`, and `#502` — the lane its body names as the gate-wiring owner for the conversational surface — is also `closed/completed`. So the wiring obligation outlived both lanes and nobody holds it.

## The fix (and the trap in it)

Declaring the suite is **not** sufficient and is **not** the first step. `scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh` (EPIC #524 / #526) **never grandfathers a newly declared suite** — its own contract says so:

> *a NEWLY declared suite or a NEWLY delivered `scripts/check-*.sh` is **NEVER grandfathered** — it fails immediately, naming the path*

So a bare one-line addition to `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` turns the gate of record **red**. The declaration must land **with** the wiring, mirroring the `pytest-fleet` precedent (which runs `fleet/tests` from `scripts/verify.sh`), so the suite is both declared and named in the same change.

## Acceptance

- `gateway/chat` is declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`.
- A check in `scripts/verify.sh` names it as a pytest target (`gateway/chat/tests`), so `make verify` runs it and `check-gate-coverage` reads it as WIRED.
- `bash scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh` returns **rc 0** with the suite counted WIRED, and the baseline is **not** widened.
- `check-drift.sh` no longer warns about `gateway/chat`.
- `make verify` green on a clean checkout of the merge commit, with the new check recorded as PASS.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`.
- One writer per wave; no other lane may touch these two files in the same wave.

## Verify

```bash
grep -n 'pytest-chat' scripts/verify.sh
grep -n '^gateway/chat$' scripts/pytest-suites.txt
bash scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh
make verify
```

items.title: Pin the FinOps runnner selection and the refusal path with a mutation-proved test (follow-up to #218)
items.body:
## Why

#218 makes the FinOps block select the runner — `model.tier` maps to the model the runner is invoked
with, tier/model/thinking are exported to the child environment, and an unexecutable block
**refuses** the dispatch with `RC_REFUSED = 78` — instead of the block being decorative.

The implementation landed green (`fleet/tests` 506 passed; `make verify` PASS 78/80), but **no test
pins any of it**. The issue's acceptance asked for a test that fails when the wiring is removed, and
that mutation proof does not exist. So the behaviour can be reverted by a future refactor with every
gate still green.

## What is needed

A test in `fleet/tests` that:

1. drives `terminal.loop` with a directive carrying a `model.tier`, and asserts the runner is invoked
   with the tier's model (not the default);
2. asserts the tier/model/thinking reach the child environment;
3. asserts that a block this build cannot turn into a runner **refuses** — rc `RC_REFUSED` (78), no
   silent fallback;
4. **mutation-proves** (1)–(3): break the wiring, show the test fail by name, restore, and prove the
   file byte-identical (sha256).

Precedent for the shape: the behavioural rewrite in #286, which replaced a source-text grep with a
test that drives the real run path.

items.title: Wire check-chat-surface.sh into the gate of record — master is RED (gate-coverage fails by name)
items.body:
Parent: #500

## The gate of record is RED on `master` — measured

`#503` (PR #564, merge `fcc105a`) landed `scripts/check-chat-surface.sh`. The `gate-coverage` detector (EPIC #524 / #526) fails **by name** on a delivered check script that no gate file invokes, and `chat-surface` was **not** baselined.
```
$ bash scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh
      FAIL  script scripts/check-chat-surface.sh (invoked by no gate file: scripts/verify.sh, Makefile, scripts/gate.sh, scripts/merge-gate.sh, scripts/qa-loop.sh)
    check-gate-coverage: NOT-OK — 1 finding(s)
    check-gate-coverage: check scripts WIRED=73 UNWIRED=7 (baselined 6)
```

`gate-coverage` **is itself wired** into `scripts/verify.sh` (line 59), so this is a genuine red `make verify` on `master` — the gate of record is broken for every lane in the fleet until it is fixed. This is exactly the class the detector was built to catch, so the detector is right and its detection is the evidence.

## Why it was not caught in the delivering lane

`#502` (the chat gate-wiring owner) is the lane whose acceptance names this seventh gate — its table lists `check-chat-surface.sh` as one of the gates to wire. But `#502`'s PR (#561) was **opened before #503 landed**, so it wires the six gates that existed at the time and cannot know about the seventh. This is the serialization hazard already recorded in #567: any lane delivering a new `scripts/check-*.sh` is *necessarily* a build-file lane, because an unwired artifact now fails the gate.

## Lane owns

- `scripts/verify.sh` (the `checks=(...)` array)
- `Makefile` (+ `.PHONY`) — only if a `chat` target is needed to satisfy the detector's universe

`scripts/gate-coverage-baseline.txt` is expected to need **no** change: this is a *wiring*, and the baseline is for accepted-unwired artifacts. Confirm rather than assume — and do **not** widen the baseline to make the gate pass.

## Acceptance

- `'chat-surface|bash scripts/check-chat-surface.sh'` is named in `scripts/verify.sh`'s `checks=(...)`, keeping the **two-space `  'name|cmd'` prefix**.
- `bash scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh` returns **rc 0** with `UNWIRED` at or below the baseline.
- `make verify` is **green** on a clean checkout of the merge commit, with `chat-surface` recorded as **PASS** (rc 0).
- **No duplicates** in the check array; `duplicates` is `{}` in the attestation.
- `scripts/gate-coverage-baseline.txt` is **not widened**.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh
grep -n "chat-surface" scripts/verify.sh
make verify
```

items.title: Stray-issue wave: 6 lanes dispatched (#522 #517 #309 #286 #218 #174) — Tier-2 triage pending
items.body:
## Dispatch status — CORRECTED

The fan-out was requested and **was dispatched**. Six lanes were launched; the dispatch
calls *returned* transient provider errors —

```
[402] You have run out of balance            # platform.deepseek.com
[429] You are sending requests too quickly   # burst of 6 simultaneous dispatches
```

— **but the agents started anyway.** Verified after the fact: all six have live worktrees
and isolation session rows, and two had already committed within minutes:

| Lane | Session | Agent | Status at time of writing |
|---|---|---|---|
| **#522** | `a5a5fdbe50a5` | `copilot-522` | ahead=1 — `fix(pr-contract): a squash separator is a boundary inside …` |
| **#286** | `e2dfe7c7449e` | `ao286-lane` | ahead=1 — `test(fleet): assert the run path's telemetry by effect …` |
| **#517** | `de2a792c0519` | `copilot-relentless` | worktree live at `fcc105a` |
| **#174** | `089bac208320` | `copilot-relentless` | worktree live at `fcc105a` |
| **#309** | `eafb15c92163` | `copilot-309` | worktree live at `fcc105a` |
| **#218** | `59dbb33b9105` | `copilot-finops` | worktree live at `fcc105a` |

**Correction of record:** the first revision of this issue claimed the wave was blocked on
credits and had not run. That was **wrong** — a 402/429 response to a dispatch is not proof
that no agent started. The lesson (and the check that caught it): after a failed dispatch,
**verify by session/worktree/commit, not by the error text** —
`python3 governance/isolation/cli.py list` and `git rev-list --count origin/master..issue-<n>`.

The reconnaissance below is unchanged and remains the plan of record for **Tier 2**.

## The reconnaissance (measured)

- **48 open issues**, **2 open PRs** (`#564` → #503, `#561` → #502), **96 registered worktrees** (~15–60 `ao-*` lanes live at any moment).
- Ownership map derived by intersecting the open-issue list against live worktrees, remote `issue-*` branches, and open PRs.

### Tier 1 — confirmed stray, no lane/branch/PR/worktree, scope read and bounded

| Issue | Scope measured | Files it would own |
|---|---|---|
| **#522** | `--landed` flags squash commits because GitHub appends `---------` + its own `Co-authored-by:` *after* the `Refs` line, pushing it out of the trailing block. Measured: 2 findings in a 20-commit range (`07b3d5d` ← PR #520, `8c0669f` ← PR #493) | `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh`, `scripts/merge-gate.sh` |
| **#517** | `governance/conformance/cli.py file --declare` silently **drops** a declared companion label outside the class's set (`pillar=`, `phase=` accepted then absent; exit 0, no warning). Doctrine is *refuse rather than drop* | `governance/conformance/**`, `scripts/check-conformance.sh` |
| **#309** | The isolation ticket-trailer rule is a **substring** test and landed history is never audited. Reusable position-based predicate already exists in the PR-contract gate | `governance/isolation/**`, `scripts/check-session-isolation.sh` |
| **#286** | `test_loop_wires_record_run_into_the_run_path` is a **source-text grep**, not a behavioural test — a false-green generator | `fleet/tests/**` (+ the `fleet/` module if a seam is needed) |
| **#218** | Fleet terminal: declared tier/thinking must select the **real** routing tier | `fleet/terminal.py`, the routing module |
| **#174** | Assign `class:` labels to the six issues with declared-vs-actual conformance mismatches (metadata-only; may need no PR at all) | issue labels (no files) |

Each was verified unowned: no local branch, no remote `issue-<n>` branch, no worktree, no open PR, zero claim comments.

### Tier 2 — open but NOT safe to take without a decision

- **#126–#137** (11) `CMR vendor compliance gap: <module>` — each targets **another repo** (`diagrams`, `shared-services`, `code-indexing`, …), so the work is not in this workspace. Needs a triage decision, not a lane.
- **#553–#559, #563** (RC-2…RC-9) — live `ao-rc1` / `ao-rc2` / `ao-rc9` / `ao-rcgap` worktrees exist, so the RC family is **already owned**. Do not dispatch.
- **#445, #447** — `ao-pc-gap` / `ao-pc-upstream` worktrees suggest ownership. Verify before taking.
- **#329, #358, #516** — `ao-sweep-conf` / `ao-reap` worktrees suggest ownership (board-sweep and worktree-reclamation respectively). **#516 is the one that matters most operationally**: 96 worktrees are registered, many stale.
- **#511, #512** — **identical titles** ("Chat shell-mount integration: the mount/bridge/auth contract and the vendor di…"). Almost certainly a duplicate pair; needs a merge/close decision before either is worked.
- **#500, #338, #399, #551** — open EPICs (parents), not workable items.

## THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THIS A PLAN, NOT A BATCH LAUNCH

**`scripts/verify.sh`, `Makefile`, and `scripts/gate-coverage-baseline.txt` are the fleet's single serialization point: at most ONE lane may touch them at a time.** Two consequences that the naive "fan out everything" reading gets wrong:

1. **Wiring lanes must be sequential.** Any lane that adds or wires a check edits all three. So a "wire the conversational-surface gates" lane (#502) and a "wire X" lane can never run concurrently.
2. **A NEW `scripts/check-*.sh` now FAILS the gate unless it is wired.** The `gate-coverage` detector (EPIC #524 / PR #560) fails **by name** on a delivered check script that no gate invokes. There is no silent-skip escape: an unwired artifact must be either wired (build files) or recorded in the baseline (build files). So *any* lane delivering a new gate script is **necessarily** a build-file lane.

Therefore the Tier-1 lanes above were selected precisely because **none of them touches those three files** — they are genuinely parallel-safe. That is the wave to launch:

```
wave:  #522 | #517 | #309 | #286 | #218 | #174     (6 lanes, disjoint files, no build-file contention)
then:  one build-file lane at a time (#516, #502-adjacent wiring, scratch-guard #488, ...)
```

## Also worth noting while dispatching this wave

The `gate-coverage` baseline now carries **72 entries** (6 unwired check scripts, 66 unwired suites), and it **fails as STALE** when a baselined artifact becomes wired. So every wiring lane now has a second obligation: **delete the baseline entry in the same change**. Precedent: `e08f358` wired two baselined scripts, the gate failed naming both, entries were removed (74 → 72).

## Acceptance for this issue

- The Tier-1 wave is dispatched (each lane: isolated worktree, `make verify` green on a clean checkout of its merge commit, mutation proof, closure evidence comment).
- Tier-2 items are triaged: each becomes a lane, a duplicate-close, a cross-repo redirect, or an explicit "not this repo".
- This issue closes when Tier-1 is landed and Tier-2 has a disposition — **not** when the inventory is merely written.

## Remaining work

**Tier 1** is in flight (six lanes above) — it closes when each has landed with a green
`make verify` on a clean checkout of its merge commit, a mutation proof, and a closure
evidence comment.

**Tier 2** is untriaged and is where the next wave's value is: the 11 `CMR vendor compliance
gap` issues (other repos), the #511/#512 duplicate pair, and the ownership-ambiguous
#329/#358/#445/#447/#516. Note **#516** (reclaim the /tmp worktree pile) now matters more than
when this was written: **102 worktrees** are registered.

items.title: RC-11: The terminal cockpit — the Bloomberg-grade AI console for IT/CTO to analyst
RC-10: The cockpit function registry — panels, views and commands declared once
items.body:
GOAL comes first. GOAL: declare every cockpit **function** exactly once — the closed catalogue of panels, views and commands that the terminal cockpit renders and the operator types — so a domain is added by declaration, never by a fork.

## Scope

One declarative registry: per function — stable id (the operator-typed mnemonic, Bloomberg-function style), human title, the API endpoint(s) it binds to, its **parameters** (name, type, required, default), the **scope requirement** (which `identity/rbac` capability and tenant scope it needs), its **effect class** (`read` | `hold` | `stop` | `irreversible`, reusing RC-2's vocabulary rather than inventing a second one), the **stream** it subscribes to if it is live, and its **role suitability** (which of CTO / VP-Eng / Manager / Analyst it is designed for).

The registry is the extensibility contract from RC-9 decision 10: adding FinOps, SLO, audit, tickets or paperclip is a declaration, not a code change to the client.

## Acceptance

- every function the cockpit renders, and every mnemonic the command line accepts, is declared here — or the gate fails **naming the undeclared function**;
- a function whose `effect_class` is unknown, whose parameter has no type, or which references an API endpoint that is not in RC-3's declared route set, fails;
- an **unknown parameter** on an otherwise-declared function is refused by name;
- `read`-class functions may not declare an audit action; `hold`/`stop`/`irreversible` ones must;
- the check carries a self-mutation negative control proving it can fail (GR-12), and the registry is exercised headlessly (a test renders each declared function against fixtures — no live plane needed in the gate);
- the role suitability set is **additive filtering only**: a function may be recommended for a role, never *permitted* by it — permission stays with `identity/rbac` (RC-9 decision 9).

Lane glob (sole writer): `control-plane/functions/**`, `scripts/check-control-functions.sh`, its tests.

items.title: RC-9: ADR — retire tmux as the control plane: the supervision and live-view substrate
items.body:
GOAL: decide the **substrate that replaces tmux** as the fleet's supervision and live-view mechanism — so "control" stops meaning "keystrokes in a multiplexer on the fleet host". The operator is not attached to tmux; decide what they attach to instead.

## Why this is now on the critical path

ADR-0025 (#552) froze the **control channel** (operator-inbound authenticated API, console-session identity, RBAC per call, one audit record per applied command) — that decision stands and is the foundation here. It did **not** decide the **runtime substrate**, and the gap analysis (`docs/REMOTE-CONTROL-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` §2) measured that today every control verb is delivered by `os.kill`, a `.fleet/` flag file, the host crontab or **`tmux attach`**, with zero network-reachable verbs. `pause/resume/stop/kill` currently mean "signal a local PID"; the console is a TUI rendered into a tmux pane.

**tmux is structurally unable to be the SaaS control plane here**, and this is measured, not asserted:
- the fleet's own services run on **Cloud Run v2** — `infra/terraform/modules/control-plane-service/main.tf:30` and `infra/terraform/modules/web-surface/main.tf:45` are `google_cloud_run_v2_service`, **ingress internal by default**, scale-to-zero. There is no host, no pod, no tty and no persistent session to attach to.
- tmux carries **no caller identity, no RBAC, no audit, no receipts and no exactly-once**, which is precisely the gap ADR-0025 exists to close.

## What must be decided

1. **Supervision.** What actually stops, pauses, resumes and restarts a rung once it is not a local PID that `os.kill` can reach? Map each control verb onto a **substrate primitive** and name it: Cloud Run **revisions + traffic split + min/max instances** (canary/rollback are native), a GKE **Deployment + rollout/scaling**, or supervision by the durable engine itself. `pause`/`resume`/`stop`/`kill` must each name a real primitive — **`os.kill` is refused**.
2. **Durable execution.** Decide whether the run state machine is our own (`engine/core` — already durable, resumable, per-tenant namespaced, with sagas and retries) or the **Temporal transport** already seamed behind a flag (`engine/core/temporal.py` fixes the contract and the engine↔Temporal mapping table, and is deliberately not wired). State the trigger that would promote it.
3. **The live view.** The "attach and watch" affordance must survive without a host-local multiplexer: the **existing authenticated SSE stream** (`portal/server/live_feed.py`) consumed by a CLI `--follow`, and — if a terminal is wanted — an **audited, RBAC-scoped** browser terminal over the same API. Decide whether a web terminal ships at all, and if it does, state that it can never be a bypass around ADR-0025's identity/audit path.
4. **What tmux becomes.** State the rule explicitly: tmux is a **developer convenience and local debug multiplexer only** — never the control mechanism, never the source of truth, never a path that can write fleet state un-audited.

## Acceptance

The record is `accepted`; each of `pause | resume | stop | kill` names a substrate primitive and **no path uses `os.kill` as the control mechanism**; the live-view path is authenticated and audited or explicitly declined; the promotion trigger for the durable transport is stated; and the standing rules hold — no second dashboard (ADR-0022), no second ledger (ADR-0012/0015), nothing ON by default (GR-5), no peer edited (NG4).

Lane glob (sole writer): `docs/decision-records/ADR-00NN-control-substrate.md` + its one row in `docs/decision-records/README.md`. Number it by measuring free files **and** existing citations (a prior lane learned that "free as a file" is not the test — an *unprefixed* `ADR-00NN` citation in merged code means the number is already taken).
Blocked-by: #552 (merged) — the channel decision this builds on.

Role: subagent
Epic: #551
Pillar: control-plane
Lane: architecture
Model tier (FinOps): pro
Thinking effort: high

Verify command: `bash scripts/check-docs.sh && make verify`



---

## Amendment (approved 2026-09-14) — the cockpit substrate, not just "what replaces tmux"

The operator approved the product direction this decision must now also fix: the replacement is a
**modern AI terminal cockpit — a Bloomberg-terminal-grade surface for IT/CTO, all the way down to
analyst** (live, dense, keyboard-first, drillable, role-tiered). Decide the substrate accordingly.

6. **The client architecture.** Decide that the terminal is a **client of the same served API a
   browser would use** — not a surface that owns state. The API is the product; the terminal is one
   client of it. Concretely: the interactive cockpit is a terminal-native client over the RC-3
   control API plus the **existing** authenticated SSE stream (`portal/server/live_feed.py`), and it
   must be able to run from a machine that is not the fleet host. Name the client framework and
   justify it against the alternatives (extend the current tmux TUI; a local-only Rich TUI; a bespoke
   web dashboard; a systems-language client). Reuse ADR-0025's identity/audit path verbatim — the
   cockpit may never hold its own credentials or write fleet state directly.
7. **The ruling that keeps ADR-0022 intact.** State explicitly that a **terminal cockpit is a client
   of one API, not a second dashboard**: it consumes the same served projection the web SPoG
   consumes. No second data plane, no second ledger, no re-derived human surface. This is what makes
   adding a second client later a client choice rather than an architecture change.
8. **Terminal-first, browser-later (decided).** Ship the terminal client first; a browser client is
   explicitly deferred and, when it lands, must be a **second client of the same API**, never a
   parallel surface. A web terminal is not approved by this decision.
9. **Role tiers are views, not products.** CTO / VP-Eng / Manager / Analyst are **named workspaces
   over one function set**, scoped by the existing `identity/rbac` + entitlements — never four
   builds, never four permission systems. State that a role can only narrow what the API would
   already let that caller see.
10. **The extensibility contract.** Adding a domain (FinOps, SLO, audit, tickets, paperclip) must be
    a **declaration, not a fork** — i.e. the cockpit is driven by a closed function registry, which
    is scoped as its own child (RC-10) and must be decided before the cockpit is built (RC-11).
11. **Honesty in the client.** Carry the repo's existing honesty rules into the cockpit explicitly: a
    panel that cannot load says so (never an empty "all quiet"), `NO_DATA` is never rendered as OK,
    an unpromoted surface is invisible with the flag named, and every action prints a receipt or an
    explicit refusal.

**Additional acceptance for this decision.** It names the client framework and the rejected
alternatives; it states the client-not-dashboard ruling; it states terminal-first/browser-deferred;
it states that role tiers are scoped views over one function set; and it fixes the function-registry
requirement that RC-10 and RC-11 depend on. The RC-9 lane glob is unchanged.

items.title: EPIC: Remote control command center CLI — a reachable, identified, audited control channel for the fleet
items.body:
Parent: #160

## Objective

A **remote control command center CLI** — a reachable, identified, audited control channel for the fleet. Today every control verb we ship is local (see `docs/REMOTE-CONTROL-GAP-ANALYSIS.md`, §2): 18 verbs in `fleet/control.py`, 13 in `fleet/channel.py`, 22 across the governance CLIs, all delivered by `os.kill`, a `.fleet/` flag file, the host crontab or `tmux attach`, and **zero** network-reachable verbs. Every HTTP surface we ship is GET-only and binds loopback. The operator must be at the fleet host, in its tmux session, to control anything.

**Paperclip is the star player here**: its control plane already ships the control semantics (`agent pause|resume|approve|terminate|heartbeat:invoke|config-revision:rollback`, per-agent budget hard stops, immutable activity) and our seam to it is a **read/projection** seam only (`integrations/paperclip/api/surface.py`: *"A method that needs arguments (a mutation) is skipped: this is the *read* surface."*). **The tmux workspace is a back door, not the control plane.** The operator is not married to tmux: the control mechanism is an authenticated API (ADR-0025), the execution substrate is a durable engine, and a terminal — tmux or otherwise — is a **view** over that API, never a path that writes fleet state. The substrate decision that retires tmux is **RC-9 (#563)**.

## Definition of done

An operator on a machine other than the fleet host can (a) **see** the fleet's standing, (b) issue a named control verb from a **closed, declared vocabulary**, (c) have it carry a **caller identity**, (d) have it produce **exactly one effect and exactly one audit record**, and (e) receive an **explicit refusal** — never a silent no-op — when the plane is unreachable, the verb is not permitted for that caller, or the command was already applied.

## Children (dependency-ordered)

Critical path: **RC-1 → RC-2 → RC-3 → RC-4 → RC-5 → RC-8**.

- **RC-1** — #552 — ADR: the remote control transport and the authority split *(keystone, unblocked)*
- **RC-2** — #553 — the control-verb vocabulary (one declaration) *(blocked by #552)*
- **RC-3** — #554 — the control API (server half, flag-gated OFF) *(blocked by #552, #553)*
- **RC-4** — #555 — exactly-once control, with the audit record and the refusal path *(blocked by #554)*
- **RC-5** — #556 — the remote command center CLI (client half) *(blocked by #554, #555)*
- **RC-6** — #557 — the upstream control-verb mapping (a mapping, never authority) *(blocked by #553)*
- **RC-7** — #558 — the seam doc's §5 mismatch list gains the control rows *(blocked by #557, #552)*
- **RC-8** — #559 — gate wiring + docs index (sole writer of the shared build files) *(blocked by #553, #554, #555, #556, #557)*
- **RC-9** — #563 — ADR: retire tmux as the control plane — the supervision and live-view substrate *(blocked by #552, now merged)*

## Non-goals (so a child cannot drift into them)

No new dashboard or UI (ADR-0022). No second knowledge store or second ledger (ADR-0012/0015). No upstream code edited, vendored, forked or mirrored (NG4, GR-10) — peer needs go to the peer's board as direction issues. No workflow file (GR-15). Nothing ON by default (GR-5).

## Safety rails every child inherits

1. **No silent action** — a control verb is operator-requested and audited; a monitoring signal files a **ticket** (ADR-0022 refusal 4) and may never write fleet state.
2. **Default-OFF** — the surface ships flag-gated OFF (`surfaces.remote_control`), invisible before AuthN, per `docs/LIVE-DATA-BRIDGE.md`.
3. **One writer per shared build file** (`Makefile`, `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`) — that lane is RC-8, serialized behind every child it wires.
4. **Delegate, never re-derive** — the new API translates into the *existing* local levers by calling them; it never grows a second implementation.
5. **Cite, never mirror** — upstream behaviour is cited by path; nothing under it is edited from here (NG4).
6. **A terminal is a view, not a mechanism** — no TUI/multiplexer/web-terminal may write fleet state except through the identified + audited control path (ADR-0025).

## Evidence base

`docs/REMOTE-CONTROL-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` (merged, PR #550) — our surface inventoried from source, upstream's control surface cited by path, the three-way gap classification, and the boundary analysis. DeepSeek and other peer enhancements that this program consumes are mapped in `docs/CROSS-REPO-DEEPSEEK-ENHANCEMENTS.md` (merged, PR #549).

### Cockpit substrates (approved 2026-09-14 — the Bloomberg-terminal direction)

- **RC-9** — #563 — ADR: retire tmux as the control plane — the supervision and live-view substrate, **now amended** to also decide the cockpit client architecture, the client-not-dashboard ruling, terminal-first/browser-deferred, role tiers as scoped views, and the function-registry requirement *(unblocked — #552 merged)*

- **RC-11** — #566 — the terminal cockpit: the Bloomberg-grade AI console for IT/CTO to analyst *(blocked by #554, #555, #565)*

**The product direction this serves (operator-approved):** a modern AI terminal cockpit — live, dense,
keyboard-first, drillable — serving CTO → VP-Eng → Manager → Analyst as *scoped views over one
function set*, as a **client of the served API**. tmux is demoted to a developer convenience and
local debug multiplexer: never the control mechanism, never the source of truth, never an un-audited
path that can write fleet state.

Parent: #462

## Objective

`scripts/check-diagrams-capability-register.sh` (#469) enforces rule 6 — *a capability named in the integration EPIC #461 that is absent from the register* — in two ways: by extracting capability tokens from #461, and by cross-checking the register's own `Capability #461 relies on | Rows` mapping table (sub-checks 6a/6b/6c).

The register (`docs/DIAGRAMS-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md`, #467) **carries no such mapping table** — it references #461 in prose only. So the gate prints, on every run:

> `NOTE - the register carries no '#461 relies on' mapping section, so the rule-6 mapping cross-check (6a/6b/6c) is inert; rule 6 coverage is enforced`

The token-based half still enforces rule 6, so the rule is not unenforced. But a sub-check that **can never fire** is a formality (GR-12), and it is the exact failure this repo's no-false-green doctrine rejects. The sibling register (`docs/CODEIDX-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md`, #478) **does** carry the mapping table — its gate reports `13 #472 mapping rows` and exercises 6a/6b/6c live. The diagrams register is simply missing its half.

## Lane owns

- `docs/DIAGRAMS-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md` — the **new mapping section only** (append-only; no existing row may be altered, reordered or reformatted)

## Acceptance

- The register carries a table with the header `Capability #461 relies on | Rows` (matching the sibling's, so the same parser shape works), mapping **every capability EPIC #461 names** to the register row ids that answer it.
- `bash scripts/check-diagrams-capability-register.sh` returns **rc 0** and the `NOTE … inert` line is **gone** — proving 6a/6b/6c now execute.
- Sub-checks 6a/6b/6c are each **shown to be live** (they can fail): provoke each on a copy (empty the mapping; point a mapping row at a non-existent row id; drop a capability #461 names) and show rc 1 naming the fault. Restore and prove **sha256 byte-identical**.
- Append-only: the register's existing bytes are unchanged (prove the new file's prefix equals the old file byte-for-byte).
- `make verify` green; `bash -n` clean on anything added; no build-file edits.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-diagrams-capability-register.sh
bash scripts/check-diagrams-capability-register.sh --self-test
make verify
```

items.title: Gate-coverage detector — fail by name when a declared suite or delivered check script is invoked by no gate
items.body:
Parent: 524
Blocked-by: #525

## Objective

Add the **detector** that makes this whole class of gap impossible to reintroduce silently: a gate that **fails by name** when a suite declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` — or a script delivered as `scripts/check-*.sh` / `scripts/check-*.py` — is invoked by **no** gate.

## Why this is the systemic fix

The epic's RCA is not "someone forgot to wire `e2e`". It is that **coverage is opt-in per suite and nothing complains when it is missing**. The evidence is that an entire *family* of issues exists for one defect class:

- **#466** — wire the diagrams gates into the gate of record
- **#499** — wire the monitoring exposition + declaration gates into the gate of record
- **#502** — wire the conversational-surface gates into the gate of record

Each was found by hand. A recurring issue *title* for a defect class is the signal that the class has no detector. `scripts/verify.sh` already carries the scar from the first instance: *"a red fleet suite sat on master undetected because this gate ran no pytest at all … (gate gap, issue #331)"* — and #331's fix wired **one** suite, leaving the other 66 unenforced.

## Lane owns

- `scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh` (new, mode `100755`)
- `Makefile` (+ `.PHONY` + target)
- `scripts/verify.sh` (one new `checks=(...)` entry — the detector must be **in** the gate of record, or it is itself the defect it detects)

## Acceptance

- The detector is **offline**, **deterministic**, and **tri-state** (`0` OK / `1` NOT-OK / `2` CANNOT-ASSESS).
- It enumerates two universes and their invoked sets:
  1. every suite declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`,
  2. every `scripts/check-*.sh|py`,
  against every place a gate is invoked (`scripts/verify.sh`, `Makefile`, `scripts/gate.sh`, `scripts/merge-gate.sh`, `scripts/qa-loop.sh`) — and **fails by name**, printing the offending suite/script path.
- An **explicit, documented baseline** of accepted exceptions is committed (a shrinking allowlist, each entry naming why it is not in the gate of record) so the existing 67 suites do not have to be wired in one change — but a **newly declared** suite that is unwired **fails immediately**. The baseline only ever shrinks.
- **Mutation-proven:** declare a new suite in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` and confirm the detector **fails naming it**; remove it and confirm the tree is byte-identical (sha256) and green.
- Internal negative controls construct each violation class; `bash -n` clean; no unfinished markers.
- `make verify` green on a **clean checkout** of the merge commit.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh
bash -n scripts/check-gate-coverage.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- **Matching must be by script PATH, not by check name.** A rough pass by name falsely flags `check-python-syntax.sh` / `check-board-gate.sh` (whose check names differ from their filenames). Measured correctly, **0 of 69** check scripts are unwired today — the detector must reproduce that, and must not manufacture findings.
- **One writer per wave:** shares `Makefile` / `scripts/verify.sh` with #A; that is why this lane is `Blocked-by:` it.

- `scripts/verify.sh` (the `checks=(...)` array)
- `e2e/README.md` (record that the suite is now in the gate of record)

- `make verify` green on a **clean checkout of the merge commit** (not a dirty tree).
