items.title: EPIC: the gate of record exercises 4 of 71 declared suites — the e2e capstone Definition-of-Done proof is not in make verify
items.body:
## Summary

`make verify` is **the gate of record** (`AGENTS.md` GR-12; GitHub Actions is disabled fleet-wide, GR-15). It runs **4 of the 71 suites declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`**:

```
fleet
integrations/paperclip
integrations/paperclip/adapters/routines
scripts
```

The other **67 declared suites — including the capstone `e2e` suite — are exercised only by `make gate` / `make tests`** (`scripts/run-pytest-suites.sh`, invoked from `scripts/gate.sh`). Nothing enforces that those two are ever run, so a red suite in any of the 67 can reach `master` while the gate of record stays green.

This is **not** a hypothetical: `scripts/verify.sh` already carries the scar from the first instance of exactly this defect —

> "a red fleet suite sat on master undetected because this gate ran no pytest at all — only `make gate` / `make tests` did (gate gap, issue #331)"

That fix (issue #331) wired **one** suite (`fleet`). The same defect still applies to the other 67, and to the most consequential member of them: `e2e`.

## The e2e capstone is green, load-bearing — and not in the gate of record

`e2e/README.md` describes the subtree as "the **capstone E2E gate** of the whole product build … proving the EPIC-00 Definition of Done: *a multi-provider agent org can be provisioned by a new tenant end-to-end (signup → org → personas → agents → routed model calls → audit + usage billing) entirely agent-built and flag-gated*."

Measured on `origin/master`:

| Fact | Measured |
|---|---|
| `e2e` declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` | **yes** (line **67**) |
| suite result | **`32 passed in 62.12s`** (rc 0) |
| `python3 -m e2e.golden_path` | **`GOLDEN PATH: PASS`** |
| real negative controls in `e2e/negative_controls.py` | **10** (`len(NEGATIVE_CHECKS)`) (cross-tenant denied, DLP blocks secret, prompt injection blocked, policy block enforced, invalid policy rejected, budget breach blocked, kill switch refuses, dead model failover, invalid typed output cannot assess, audit tamper detected, …) |
| `make e2e` target | **does not exist** |
| `e2e` entry in `scripts/verify.sh` `checks=(...)` | **does not exist** (fixed by #525, below) |
| `scripts/verify.sh` pytest invocation | `pytest-fleet` only (`fleet/tests`) |

So the one suite that proves the product's end-to-end Definition of Done is **inert with respect to the gate of record**. It is a gate nobody is required to run — a formality (GR-12), and the exact failure mode this repo's doctrine forbids.

## RCA — why this happened and why it recurs

1. **Coverage is opt-in, per suite.** `verify.sh` holds an explicit `checks=(...)` list with no discovery. Wiring a new gate or suite is a *manual* step performed by whichever lane happens to own the file at the time; if it is forgotten, nothing complains.
2. **The wiring is contended.** `Makefile` and `scripts/verify.sh` are single-writer files, so wiring lanes serialise with every other lane that touches them — taking the cheap path (don't wire) is always available and always silent.
3. **The symptom appears as a family, not a defect.** Repeated sibling issues of the same shape — **#466** (diagrams gates), **#499** (monitoring exposition + declaration), **#502** (conversational-surface) — each is a manual "wire X into the gate of record" lane. That a *recurring issue title* exists for this is itself the finding: the class has no detector, so each instance must be found by hand.
4. **No self-check.** Nothing asserts that a suite declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`, or a script delivered as `scripts/check-*.sh`, is actually **invoked** by any gate. Delivery and invocation are unrelated.

## Why it matters

- The gate of record can be **green while the product's end-to-end journey is broken**. The 67 unexercised suites are the repo's real verification surface for identity, RBAC, gateway, telemetry, guardrails, engine and paperclip parity.
- The e2e suite is the only artifact asserting the EPIC-00 Definition of Done. Leaving it out of the gate of record means the DoD claim is **unverified at merge time**.
- It is the same false-green class as #331, one suite wider.

## Scope note — corrected, because the class has already RECURRED

At the time of the first measurement (2026-09-14 morning) **0 of 69** `scripts/check-*.sh|py` scripts were unwired: every one was referenced by some gate (`verify.sh`, `Makefile`, `gate.sh`, `merge-gate.sh`, `qa-loop.sh`). That note is now **superseded by measurement, and the supersession is the finding**:

> Re-measured later the same day at `ffb2688`: **WIRED=70, UNWIRED=8** — eight delivered check scripts are invoked by **no** gate:
> `check-chat-{eval,finops,guardrails,identity,tools,ux}.sh` (six, delivered by EPIC #499's chat surface), plus
> `check-codeidx-capability-register.sh` and `check-diagrams-capability-register.sh`.

A class that was clean in the morning and had eight members by the afternoon, with **no detector to notice**, is the whole argument for the sibling lane that builds the detector. It makes that lane the highest-value half of this epic, not the cleanup.

(An even earlier rough pass suggested ~22 unwired scripts; that was a measurement artifact of matching script *filenames* against check *names*, and is retracted.)

## Children

- **#525 — wire the e2e capstone suite into the gate of record.** Owns `Makefile`, `scripts/verify.sh`, `e2e/README.md`. Closes the specific measured gap above.
- **#526 — the coverage detector.** A gate that enumerates the declared suites and the delivered check scripts and **fails by name** on any not invoked by the gate of record, with an explicit, documented, shrinking baseline for accepted exceptions. This is the enforcement that stops the class recurring. `Blocked-by: #525` — it shares the single-writer files `Makefile` / `scripts/verify.sh`, one writer per wave.

## Acceptance for this epic

- `make verify` exercises the `e2e` capstone suite; a deliberately broken e2e assertion makes `make verify` **FAIL** (proven, not asserted).
- The coverage detector exists, is itself in the gate of record, and **fails by name** on a newly-declared-but-unwired suite (mutation-proven).
- The epic closes only when both children have landed with clean-checkout evidence at their merge commits.

## Pre-existing red

None.

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#331

items.title: governance(pr-contract): a squash-merged PR can land the Refs trailer outside the trailing block, failing --landed
items.body:
## What

`scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --landed` refuses a commit whose
`Refs <owner>/<repo>#<n>` line is not in the commit's **trailing trailer block**.
The fleet's landing path (`gh pr merge --squash`, which lets GitHub compose the
squash message) can break that position: GitHub appends its own co-author
trailer after a `---------` separator, and that separator is not a trailer line,
so the walk-back stops and the `Refs` line is reported
`commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block`.

```
...
Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#466

---------

Co-authored-by: agent-copilot-466 <agent+copilot-466@agents.invalid>
```

## Measured (2026-09-14, origin/master)

```
$ bash scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --landed --range 07b3d5d~20..07b3d5d
  FAIL  commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block:07b3d5dbcad1   # PR #520 (issue #466)
  FAIL  commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block:8c0669fe30aa   # PR #493 (issue #418)
check-pr-contract: LANDED: FAIL (2 finding(s))

$ for sha in 2c24f3b 5ddb30d aaf8b4d 07b3d5d; do printf '%s: ' $sha; \
    bash scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --landed --range ${sha}^..${sha} | grep -E 'LANDED (OK|FAIL)'; done
2c24f3b: check-pr-contract: LANDED OK — every merged commit since the enforcement gate carries the ticket trailer
5ddb30d: check-pr-contract: LANDED OK — every merged commit since the enforcement gate carries the ticket trailer
aaf8b4d: check-pr-contract: LANDED OK — every merged commit since the enforcement gate carries the ticket trailer
07b3d5d:   FAIL  commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block:07b3d5dbcad1
```

2 of the last 20 master commits are non-conforming, from **two different lanes**
(#466 and #418) — so the merge path and the contract gate disagree; it is not one
lane's slip. The PR body is not the cause: the stored #520 body ends exactly on
the `Refs` line (`gh pr view 520 --json body | tail -1`), and
`check-pr-contract.sh --body-file … --range origin/master..HEAD` printed OK
before the merge. GitHub inserted the separator during the squash (PR #477's
squash, `5ddb30d`, got the co-author trailer *without* the separator, so its
block stayed intact).

## Why it matters

`AGENTS.md` rule 1 / AO-GR-1 make the trailing `Refs` trailer the audit anchor
for "every commit points at its ticket". A commit that satisfies the substring
rule but not the position rule fails the repo's own landed audit, so that
audit's output becomes noise that can hide a real finding.

## Options (owner of `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` / `scripts/merge-gate.sh`)

- compose the squash message in the lane and document it
  (`gh pr merge --squash --body <file>` / the REST merge API), or
- have `--landed` treat a `^-+$` separator line between trailer paragraphs as a
  block boundary that does not terminate the trailer block.

Not this lane's file — #466 owns `scripts/verify.sh`/`Makefile` only — so it is
filed rather than fixed.

Reproduce: `bash scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --landed --range 07b3d5d~20..07b3d5d`

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#466

items.title: governance/conformance: file --declare silently drops declared companion labels (pillar/phase) instead of passing or refusing them
items.body:
Root=none

## GOAL

`governance/conformance/cli.py file --declare <name>=<value>` silently **drops** a
declared companion label whose name is not in the policy's per-class label set
(`pillar`, `phase`, ...), instead of passing it through or refusing it. The seam's
own doctrine is "refuse rather than drop" — an ignored declaration is silent
board-metadata loss, the same class of defect as a silently-dropped chain marker.

## Evidence (measured 2026-09-14)

    $ python3 governance/conformance/cli.py file --dry-run --title T --body b \
        --class enterprise --declare type=governance --declare priority=P1 \
        --declare area=fleet --declare pillar=autonomous-ops --declare phase=8-autonomous-ops
    filing: DRY-RUN — nothing was filed
      labels:  class:enterprise, type:governance, priority:P1, area:fleet, gdc:enterprise
      command: gh issue create --repo kushin77/agent-orchestrator --title T --body b \
               --label class:enterprise --label type:governance --label priority:P1 \
               --label area:fleet --label gdc:enterprise

`pillar=autonomous-ops` and `phase=8-autonomous-ops` were accepted on the command
line and are **absent** from the derived labels: no warning, no refusal, exit 0.

Cause: `derive_declaring_labels()` iterates only
`policy.filing_label_names(declared_class)` (the `required` set plus the class's
`expectations`), so any declared name outside that set is never read —
`governance/conformance/filing.py` `derive_declaring_labels()`. Meanwhile
`governance/conformance/policy.yaml` lists `pillar` and `phase` in its `prefixed`
declaring fields, and the CLI help advertises "declare a companion label
explicitly (type/priority/area/gdc/...)".

Workaround used today, which proves the labels themselves are wanted:
`--label pillar:autonomous-ops --label phase:8-autonomous-ops`.

## Why it matters

The conformance doctrine is that a filing which cannot derive a required label is
**REFUSED before `gh` runs**, precisely so the board is never silently
unconformant. Dropping a *declared* label is the same failure in reverse: the filer
believes `pillar:*`/`phase:*` were declared and the issue lands without them.
`check-conformance.sh`'s `filing-check` exercises only the required set, so this
drop is invisible to the gate — and `expectations` (pillar/gdc) are reported as
non-fatal deviations, so nothing catches the loss afterwards either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] an unrecognised `--declare name=value` is either honoured (emitted as
      `name:value` to `gh issue create`) or **REFUSED by name**; silence is not an
      option
- [ ] the chosen behaviour is stated in `governance/conformance/README.md`
- [ ] `filing-check` provokes the new path: a declaration dropped on the floor must
      make the self-control FAIL (a check that cannot fail is a formality)

## Verify

```bash
python3 governance/conformance/cli.py filing-check
make conformance
make verify
```

## Lane / files

- Owns: `governance/conformance/filing.py`, `governance/conformance/cli.py`,
  `governance/conformance/checker.py`, `governance/conformance/tests/`,
  `governance/conformance/README.md`.

## Provenance (GR-10)

Found 2026-09-14 while filing two governance issues through the supported path
(`governance/conformance/cli.py file`), which is the only sanctioned way to file
labelled work.

items.title: Reclaim this machine's unreclaimed /tmp worktree pile (30 registered, 20 with vanished directories) and refuse new lane worktrees on tmpfs
items.body:
Root=none

## GOAL

Reclaim the unreclaimed lane worktrees tied to this machine's `/tmp` tmpfs, and
close the gap that keeps producing them: **30 registered worktrees live under
`/tmp`, 20 of them with a directory that no longer exists**, and
`governance/isolation` will provision a new lane worktree under `/tmp`
(tmpfs = RAM + inodes) because nothing refuses a tmpfs path.

## Measured state (2026-09-14, this machine, read-only)

`scratch-guard --check` (the machine-level guard from #488):

    [TMP-WORKTREE] 30 registered git worktree(s) on /tmp (tmpfs) - costs inodes+RAM,
    lost on reboot. Remove with: git worktree remove <path>.

Classification (`git worktree list --porcelain` + `git merge-base --is-ancestor`
against `origin/master` = `b4c9fb5`); nothing was deleted:

| property | count |
|---|---|
| registered worktrees under `/tmp` | **30** |
| directory already gone (metadata-only, reclaimable by `git worktree prune`) | **20** |
| HEAD already reachable from `origin/master` (work landed) | **17** |
| still on disk, HEAD **not** on `origin/master` (needs its lane's call) | 4 |

Growth is itself evidence: **11** such worktrees when `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh`
was written (2026-09-13, issue #207), **23** when #488 was filed, **30** now.

## What is already tracked (do not duplicate)

- `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` (**issue #207**) + `make worktrees` reclaim stale
  lane worktrees, dry-run by default, and its header already names the `/tmp`
  tmpfs ones as the RAM hazard.
- `governance/reconcile/` (**issue #304**) sweeps **heartbeated sessions** only —
  the detached measurement worktrees here (`/tmp/ao*pf.*`, `/tmp/ao*-base-*`)
  never recorded a beat, so reconcile cannot see them.
- `governance/dispatch/cli.py audit` audits the **claim ledger**, not worktrees.
  (`dispatch audit` returns OK today: 0 violations.)

## The gap (what is NOT tracked)

1. Nothing on the board owns **running** the reclaim on this pile — the tool
   exists (#207) and is unexecuted.
2. Nothing **prevents** a new worktree under `/tmp`. Static check: the only
   `ProvisionRefused` sites in `governance/isolation/worktree.py` are the shared
   checkout itself, a path *inside* the shared checkout, an existing non-worktree
   path, a failed `git worktree add`, and an unsafe lane name. `grep -n 'tmp'
   governance/isolation/worktree.py` returns **nothing** — there is no tmpfs
   refusal, and `--root` is accepted verbatim. Ad-hoc `git worktree add /tmp/...`
   is unguarded entirely.
3. The vendor board's `kushin77/code-indexing#158` / `#159` track this hazard for
   *that repo's single* worktree; this repo's pile of 30 has no owner.
4. The agent-facing discipline is named only inside #488's body; it is not
   enforced anywhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bash scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` reports no removable stale worktree under
      `/tmp` (any remainder justified by name in the closure comment)
- [ ] `git worktree list` shows **no** worktree under `/tmp` that is not a
      currently-running lane
- [ ] `governance/isolation` refuses to provision a lane onto a tmpfs path, by
      name, before `git worktree add` runs
- [ ] the new refusal code is added to `governance/isolation/README.md`'s refusal
      table, and a self-control provokes the refusal (`make verify` green)

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/prune-worktrees.sh --check          # 0 stale
git worktree list | grep -c '^/tmp/'             # 0
python3 governance/isolation/cli.py open --issue 999 --agent probe --root /tmp   # refused, by name
make verify
```

## Lane / files

- Owns: `governance/isolation/worktree.py`, `governance/isolation/cli.py`,
  `governance/isolation/README.md`, `governance/isolation/tests/`,
  `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh`.

## Related (NOT chain edges)

- #488 — the tmpfs incident this piles on top of; its own issue, its own owner.

items.title: Chat design tokens: extend the --os- token twin for the conversational components (CSS+JSON parity)
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501, #502

## Summary

Extend the portal's **design-token twin** for the conversational components, so
the chat surface is styled from declared tokens (never ad-hoc colours) and the
twin's CSS/JSON parity gate covers the new tokens. #508 *consumes* the tokens
("consume the existing design tokens … no new visual language"); nothing owns
**authoring** the new component tokens a chat view needs.

## Measured facts (path / command)

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| The portal has a real token system with a hard provenance rule | `portal/static/design-tokens/PROVENANCE.md` — "styled from the harvested OS-portal design-token system (CSS + JSON twins), never from ad-hoc colors"; source table with upstream repo/file/rev |
| The twin is **gate-enforced**, not advisory | `portal/tests/test_assets.py` — `tokens.css <-> tokens.json` are exact twins (names **and** values, light + dark); **every `var(--os-*)` referenced by CSS/HTML/JS resolves to a declared token**; every view links `tokens.css` + `console.css` itself |
| Dark mode is a real second mode | `tokens.json` `modes.dark.css` block + the `[data-theme='dark']` hook (PROVENANCE.md) |
| The vendor shell keeps its own `--os-` twin | `shared-frontend/shared/design-tokens/tokens.{css,json}` + `docs/DESIGN-TOKENS.md` |
| No chat view or chat tokens exist yet | `git ls-tree -r origin/master -- portal/static/views` → 13 views, no `chat.html`; `portal/static/design-tokens/` has only `tokens.css`, `tokens.json`, `PROVENANCE.md` |

## Why this is a lane, not a bullet

The a11y/semantics live in the view (the a11y lane), but the **values** live in
the twin, and the twin has an enforced invariant: a `var(--os-*)` that is not
declared in **both** `tokens.css` and `tokens.json` fails
`portal/tests/test_assets.py`. New conversational components therefore need new
declared tokens in **both** files simultaneously, with provenance recorded for any
value not grounded in an existing group. That is authoring work with its own gate,
distinct from rendering the view.

## Scope

1. **Declare the conversational component tokens** in `tokens.css` **and**
   `tokens.json` (light + dark), with provenance: message bubble (user /
   assistant), streaming caret, citation chip / source pill, unsupported-claim
   marker, tier pill (LOW/MED/HIGH/MAX), cost/latency badge, budget state
   (warning vs hard-stop — **distinct without relying on colour alone**),
   degradation banner, composer focus ring.
2. **Parity is the acceptance**, not styling: `portal/tests/test_assets.py` must
   pass with the new tokens (names + values, both modes), and no
   `var(--os-*)` introduced by the chat view may be undeclared.
3. **No invented values.** A value not grounded in an existing token group or an
   upstream token file is either reused from an existing token or documented as a
   flagged local choice in `PROVENANCE.md` (the file's own rule).
4. **Shell alignment.** Where the chat view is framed by the OS shell, the tokens
   must reconcile with the vendor `--os-` twin so the surface does not visually
   diverge from the shell (note the reconciliation in `PROVENANCE.md`; do not edit
   the vendor repo — a direction issue if the vendor twin needs a new token).

## Overlap note

Overlaps **#508**'s `portal/**` glob. It owns the narrower
`portal/static/design-tokens/**` + `portal/tests/test_assets.py`; #508 consumes
the tokens in the view. A comment is posted on #508 proposing it narrow to the
view/js/css/server surfaces. The a11y lane owns the a11y **semantics**; this lane
owns the token **values**.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every chat component style resolves to a declared `--os-*` token; a test proves
  no undeclared token is referenced.
- `tokens.css` and `tokens.json` are exact twins (names + values, light + dark)
  after the change — `portal/tests/test_assets.py` passes.
- Any value not grounded in an existing source is either reused or recorded as a
  flagged local choice in `PROVENANCE.md`.
- The budget hard-stop and warning states are distinguishable without colour
  alone (a token/semantic distinction the a11y lane can consume).
- No ad-hoc hex/px in the view styles (the view consumes tokens only).

## Lane / files

- Owns: `portal/static/design-tokens/**`, `portal/tests/test_assets.py`.
- Does **not** own: `portal/static/views/chat.html` / `portal/static/js/chat.js` /
  `portal/static/css/chat.css` / `portal/server/**` (#508, proposed),
  `portal/static/views/chat/**` (a11y lane), `shared-frontend/**` (vendor),
  gate files (#502).

## Verify

```bash
python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('portal/static/design-tokens/tokens.json'))"
python3 -m pytest portal/tests/test_assets.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify
```

items.title: Chat accessibility & responsive behaviour: keyboard, live regions, reduced motion and mobile
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501, #502

## Summary

Make the chat surface **usable by everyone, on every device**: full keyboard
operation, screen-reader semantics for a **streaming** answer (live regions,
announced citations and state changes), focus management across stop/retry, and
responsive layout down to a phone. #508 carries accessibility as a single bullet
("accessible by keyboard with live-region announcements") inside an already very
wide lane (view + streaming + citations + model picker + cost + degradation +
tokens); a streaming, multi-region, mobile-capable surface cannot be validated as
one bullet.

## Measured facts (path / command)

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| No accessibility/responsive issue exists on the board | `gh issue list --state all --json number,title` → the only keyword hits for `accessib\|a11y\|mobile\|responsive` are unrelated (#39 closed design tokens+SSO, #49, #331/#345 streaming *feeds*) |
| Every portal view is a self-contained frame that links tokens.css + console.css itself | `portal/tests/test_assets.py` ("every view is a self-contained frame linking tokens.css + console.css itself") |
| Streaming is asynchronous, incremental text into the DOM | #503 (`SSE` frames, terminal `[DONE]`), #508 (token-by-token render, stop-generation) |
| The surface is framed in the shell with no shared runtime | `shared-frontend/docs/BRIDGE.md` (iframe, `os:*` only) — keyboard focus enters/leaves across a frame boundary |

## Why a streaming answer is a distinct a11y problem

A live-updating answer cannot be announced naively: a screen reader that re-reads
a growing region is unusable, and one that never announces it is silent. The
surface needs a deliberate policy — an `aria-live` region that announces a
**stable, throttled** summary (not every token), a "generating / stopped / done"
status the reader can reach, and `aria-busy` semantics during the stream. The
**citations** and the **cost/budget** figures are separate landmarks that must be
reachable and labelled, not decoration. Mobile adds a collapsing history drawer
and a composer that must not be obscured by the on-screen keyboard. These are
testable properties, not styling.

## Scope

1. **Keyboard + focus** (`portal/static/views/chat/**`): every control reachable
   and operable by keyboard (composer, send, stop, retry, conversation list,
   model/tier picker, citations toggle); a visible focus order; focus is not lost
   when a stream starts/stops or a conversation switches; Escape stops a stream.
2. **Screen-reader semantics**: labelled landmarks (log, composer, citations,
   cost), a throttled `aria-live` policy for the streaming answer (announce state
   transitions — "generating", "stopped", "complete" — not every token),
   `aria-busy` during generation, and citations/unsupported-claim markers exposed
   as text, not colour alone.
3. **Motion + contrast**: honour `prefers-reduced-motion` (no caret/typing
   animation that cannot be reduced); every state distinguishable without colour
   (the tokens lane owns the values; this lane proves the semantics).
4. **Responsive**: usable at the platform's mobile breakpoint — history as a
   drawer, composer stays reachable with the keyboard open, tap targets meet the
   platform minimum, no horizontal scroll.
5. **Automated evidence**: a DOM/accessibility test (`portal/tests/test_chat_a11y.py`)
   that asserts the landmark/label/`aria-live` policy and the reduced-motion path,
   so the property is **gate-enforced**, not asserted in prose.

## Overlap note

This lane overlaps **#508**'s `portal/**` glob. It owns the narrower
`portal/static/views/chat/**` + `portal/tests/test_chat_a11y.py`; a comment is
posted on #508 proposing it narrow to the chat view render
(`portal/static/views/chat.html`, `portal/static/js/chat.js`,
`portal/static/css/chat.css`, `portal/server/**`). Without that narrowing the two
lanes would share files (GR-3). The tokens lane owns the token **values**; this
lane owns the a11y **semantics**.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every interactive element is keyboard-operable; a test drives the full flow
  (compose → send → stop → retry → switch conversation) with the keyboard only.
- The streaming answer is announced via a throttled live-region policy, with an
  `aria-busy` state and reachable status transitions; a test asserts the policy.
- Citations and the cost/budget state are labelled landmarks, readable as text.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables non-essential motion; a test asserts
  the reduced path.
- The layout is usable at the mobile breakpoint with no horizontal scroll and a
  reachable composer.
- The a11y test runs offline and fails if a landmark/label is removed (negative
  control).

## Lane / files

- Owns: `portal/static/views/chat/**`, `portal/tests/test_chat_a11y.py`.
- Does **not** own: `portal/static/design-tokens/**` (tokens lane),
  `portal/static/views/chat.html` / `portal/static/js/chat.js` /
  `portal/static/css/chat.css` / `portal/server/**` (#508, proposed),
  `gateway/**`, `identity/**`, `telemetry/**` (consumed), gate files (#502).

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest portal/tests/test_chat_a11y.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify
```

items.title: Chat conversation state: the transcript store, retention and the GDPR data-subject surface
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501, #502

## Summary

Own **where a conversation lives**: the ordered transcript (roles, message
bodies, citations, per-message metadata), its lifecycle (list / search / rename /
pin / delete), its **tenancy**, and its **retention / export / erasure** — the
data-subject surface GDPR requires. #503 says a "conversation store bound to
`engine/memory` SESSION scope" but owns `gateway/chat/**` (the serving surface),
so nothing currently owns the transcript structure, and #505 isolates *access* to
a conversation without defining what a conversation **is**.

## Measured facts (path / command)

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `engine/memory` is a **semantic memory store**, not a transcript | `engine/memory/README.md` — three scopes (`TENANT`/`AGENT`/`SESSION`), containers `session:<tenant>:<agent>:<session>`, TTL 7d/200-cap, content-addressed **key→entry** memories, semantic retrieval + enrichment |
| It already exposes the GDPR data surface | `engine/memory/gdpr.py` — `export_memory(store, tenant_id, …, dry_run)` and `forget(store, tenant_id, …, older_than)`; `engine/memory/tests/test_gdpr.py` |
| It already enforces isolation + TTL/eviction | `engine/memory/store.py` (`MemoryIsolationError`, counted `cross_scope_violations`), `engine/memory/lifecycle.py` (per-scope TTL/capacity) |
| A transcript is a **different shape** — ordered, role-tagged, append-only, per-message metadata | nothing in `engine/memory/**` models an ordered message log. `git ls-tree -r origin/master -- engine` shows `engine/{core,loop,memory,multiagent,queue}`, none of which is a transcript store |
| `engine/memory` is **consumed**, not owned, by the chat lanes | #503 Scope §3 ("this lane consumes it and does not edit `engine/memory/**`"); #505 Scope §4 ("the store already does this") |

**Design correction:** binding the chat transcript *to* `engine/memory`'s SESSION
containers conflates two structures — a conversation is an **ordered message
log** (rendered as history, and the model's `messages[]`), while a memory entry is
a **keyed semantic fact**. They have different lifecycles (a transcript is
append-only and shown verbatim; memory is evicted/forgotten by relevance and TTL)
and different read patterns. This lane keeps `engine/memory` as the semantic/recall
and GDPR substrate (consumed, unchanged) and adds the transcript beside it.

## Scope

1. **Transcript store** (`engine/conversation/**`): a conversation object
   (id, `(tenant, agent)`, title, created/updated), an ordered message log
   (role, content, the **citations envelope** from #504, model/tier used, token +
   cost ref from #506, timestamps), and a stable serialisation the serving
   surface (#503) and the UX lane (#508) both consume — one shape, not two.
2. **Lifecycle**: list (tenant-scoped, cursor-paged), search (title/content,
   tenant-scoped), rename, pin, delete; soft-delete vs. hard-delete declared.
3. **Tenancy + isolation.** A transcript is reachable only by the exact
   `(tenant, agent, conversation)` scope, reusing the isolation semantics
   `engine/memory` already proves; a cross-tenant or cross-conversation read
   raises and is counted. #505 mints and verifies the credential; this lane
   proves the store **cannot** be read outside that scope.
4. **Retention + data subject.** Declare retention per scope (default, configurable),
   and expose **export** (deterministic JSON snapshot) and **erasure** (`forget`),
   delegating the data-subject boundary to the tenant exactly as
   `engine/memory/gdpr.py` does; `dry_run` reports what would be erased. Nothing
   is retained past its declared window; a deleted conversation is gone from
   both the transcript and its `engine/memory` SESSION container.
5. **Offline + deterministic.** Python stdlib only, no network, no model calls;
   TTL/retention deterministic under an injected clock (the `engine/memory`
   convention).

## Overlap note

- **#503** "conversation primitive" bullet: this lane is the **correction** —
  #503 keeps `gateway/chat/**` and *consumes* this store; the transcript is owned
  here so #503 stays a serving surface. No file overlap (`engine/conversation/**`
  vs `gateway/chat/**`).
- **#505** proves credential/scope *enforcement*; this lane proves the *store*
  cannot be read outside scope. Distinct globs (`identity/chat/**` vs
  `engine/conversation/**`).
- **#509** owns prompt modules and the eval harness (`registry/chat/**`), not the
  transcript.

## Acceptance criteria

- A conversation round-trips: append N messages, read back in order, with the
  citations envelope and the per-turn refs preserved byte-for-byte.
- Tenant A cannot read/list/search tenant B's conversation; conversation X cannot
  read conversation Y even in the same `(tenant, agent)` — both refuse and the
  cross-scope counter increments (negative controls, AO-GR-19).
- `export` returns a deterministic, JSON-serialisable snapshot; `forget`
  erases and `forget --dry-run` reports without deleting.
- Retention: an entry past its declared window is not returned, and its
  `engine/memory` SESSION counterpart is gone (proven with an injected clock).
- The store is fully offline (stdlib only); a test proves no network import.
- No secret or real tenant data in fixtures.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `engine/conversation/**`.
- Does **not** own: `engine/memory/**` (consumed, unchanged), `gateway/chat/**`
  (#503), `identity/chat/**` (#505), `telemetry/chat/**` (#506),
  `portal/**` (#508), gate files (wiring owner #502).

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest engine/conversation -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify
```

items.title: Chat shell-mount integration: the mount/bridge/auth contract and the vendor direction set
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501, #502

## Summary

Decide and pin **how the chat surface appears in the OS shell**, and own the
cross-repo **direction set** that makes it mountable. The EPIC's option E leaves
the mount unspecified: #503 mentions it in prose ("record the shell-mount
requirement as a direction issue") but owns no artifact for it, and #508 owns
`portal/**` only — so nothing currently owns the mount contract or tracks the
vendor work to completion.

## Measured facts (path / command)

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| The shell mounts by `mount.type` ∈ `iframe \| tab \| native` | `shared-frontend/modules/schema.json` (`mount.type`, `mount.url`, `mount.entry`, `mount.sandbox`, `mount.ephemeral`; `allOf` requires `entry` for `native` and a non-empty `url` for a live `iframe/tab`) |
| `native` = a React addon recreated in-shell, body-only, `addons/<id>/` | `shared-frontend/shell/src/addons.ts` (`const ADDONS`, one dynamic import per addon), `addons/README.md`, ADR-0007 |
| `iframe` = sandboxed document, **no shared JS runtime**; all talk is `os:*` postMessage | `shared-frontend/docs/BRIDGE.md` (envelope `os:session`, `os:auth`, `os:theme`, `os:navigate`), ADR-0001 |
| `tab` opens a **new browser tab** — leaves the Single Pane of Glass | `modules/schema.json` `mount.type` description ("tab = open in a new browser tab") |
| The EPIC's cited precedent is wrong: `diagrams` is `native`, not `tab` | `shared-frontend/registry/modules.json` → `diagrams` = `{"type":"native","entry":"diagrams"}`, `status: live`. The only `tab` entry is `dialplane` (`status: planned`). |
| Auth is ONE Google login across the OS and every client portal (HttpOnly cookie + `/auth/me`) | `shared-frontend/docs/AUTH.md` |
| Our portal views are same-origin static documents served by our own server | `portal/static/views/*.html` (13 views, no `chat.html`), `portal/server/app.py` (`.html` content type; `/views/shell.html`) |
| OpenWebUI is fronted by proxy auth + a trusted email header, i.e. its own identity | EPIC #500 §1.1 (`WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER=X-Forwarded-Email`, oauth2-proxy → Keycloak) |

## The tension this lane must resolve

Option E recommends (a) swapping the **client** to point at our gateway and
(b) mounting that client as `mount.type: tab`. Those two recommendations
**conflict with the owner's intent** ("the openwebui experience *inside* our
frontend portal"):

- `tab` leaves the shell entirely — the surface is not "in the Single Pane of Glass".
- Framing OpenWebUI as `iframe` reintroduces exactly the **double-auth
  anti-pattern** the EPIC's own §1.1 lessons doc records as the bug that was
  fixed (OpenWebUI's cookie/trusted-header model vs. our auth-gate
  `os-session-token`), and BRIDGE.md gives a framed module **no shared runtime**,
  so session handoff is `os:*` postMessage — which OpenWebUI does not speak.
- The alternative that actually satisfies the intent is option **D behind the E
  contract**: mount **our own** `portal/static/views/chat.html` (same origin →
  inherits the session cookie, speaks `os:*` for theme/navigation) as an
  `iframe`/portal route, and keep OpenWebUI as one *non-authoritative* client.

This lane records that decision and requests the vendor work; it writes no
product code beyond the contract doc.

## Scope

1. **The mount contract** (`docs/CHAT-MOUNT.md`): name the chosen mount
   (`iframe` of our own portal chat view), the origin/session model (same-origin
   cookie; `os:session`/`os:theme` participation), the `surfaces.chat`
   flag-before-AuthN rule that makes an unpromoted surface **invisible**, and the
   `bridge: {session, auth, navigate}` declaration the vendor entry needs.
2. **The vendor direction set** (tracked to completion, the #468/#479 pattern):
   file and keep open the direction issues on the boards that own the work —
   `kushin77/shared-frontend` (a `registry/modules.json` entry for the chat
   surface with `mount` + `bridge`, and, only if `native` is chosen, the six
   wiring surfaces a native addon needs: `shell/src/addons.ts`, the module entry,
   `registry/fixtures/*.json`, the mount-coverage baseline, the vendor-deploy
   compose, `docs/INVENTORY.md`) and `kushin77/shared-services` (re-point the
   running OpenWebUI's OpenAI-compatible connection from the Ollama VIP to our
   gateway). **Nothing under those repos is edited from here** (NG4,
   `docs/CROSS-REPO-EXECUTION-BOUNDARY.md`).
3. **ADR coordination.** If #501's ADR can carry the mount decision, fold it
   there and reduce this lane to the direction set; otherwise this doc is the
   record and the ADR cites it.

## Overlap note

- **#503** owns `gateway/chat/**` + flags + IaC and *mentions* the mount in
  prose; this lane takes that bullet out of #503's lane-body into a tracked lane.
  No file overlap (#503's globs do not include `docs/`).
- **#508** owns the chat view itself; this lane owns only the **contract doc**
  and the **vendor direction set**.
- **#501** may absorb the decision (see Scope §3).

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/CHAT-MOUNT.md` exists and states: the chosen `mount.type`, the
  origin/session model, the `os:*` messages the surface participates in, the
  flag-before-AuthN rule, and the rejected mounts with reasons.
- The doc explains **why `tab` is rejected** (it leaves the SPoG) and why framing
  OpenWebUI is rejected (double-auth; no `os:*` speaker).
- A direction issue on `kushin77/shared-frontend` exists for the module entry and
  its URL is recorded **as prose** in the doc and the PR (never a `Blocked-by:`
  marker — board numbers collide across repos).
- A direction issue on the shared-services board exists for the client re-point
  (or the doc states why it is not needed yet, with the reason).
- No file in another repo is edited; no product code is written in this lane.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `docs/CHAT-MOUNT.md` only.
- Does **not** own: `portal/**` (#508), `gateway/**` (#503),
  `docs/decision-records/ADR-*` (#501), any file in `shared-frontend` or
  `shared-services`.

## Verify

```bash
test -f docs/CHAT-MOUNT.md
grep -q 'mount.type' docs/CHAT-MOUNT.md
bash scripts/check-docs.sh
make verify
```

   `kushin77/shared-frontend` (a `registry/modules.json` entry for the chat
   surface with `mount` + `bridge`, and, only if `native` is chosen, the six
   wiring surfaces a native addon needs: `shell/src/addons.ts`, the module entry,
   `registry/fixtures/*.json`, the mount-coverage baseline, the vendor-deploy
   compose, `docs/INVENTORY.md`) and `kushin77/shared-services` (re-point the
   running OpenWebUI's OpenAI-compatible connection from the Ollama VIP to our
   gateway). **Nothing under those repos is edited from here** (NG4,
   `docs/CROSS-REPO-EXECUTION-BOUNDARY.md`).
3. **ADR coordination.** If #501's ADR can carry the mount decision, fold it
   there and reduce this lane to the direction set; otherwise this doc is the
   record and the ADR cites it.

## Overlap note

- **#503** owns `gateway/chat/**` + flags + IaC and *mentions* the mount in
  prose; this lane takes that bullet out of #503's lane-body into a tracked lane.
  No file overlap (#503's globs do not include `docs/`).
- **#508** owns the chat view itself; this lane owns only the **contract doc**
  and the **vendor direction set**.
- **#501** may absorb the decision (see Scope §3).

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/CHAT-MOUNT.md` exists and states: the chosen `mount.type`, the
  origin/session model, the `os:*` messages the surface participates in, the
  flag-before-AuthN rule, and the rejected mounts with reasons.
- The doc explains **why `tab` is rejected** (it leaves the SPoG) and why framing
  OpenWebUI is rejected (double-auth; no `os:*` speaker).
- A direction issue on `kushin77/shared-frontend` exists for the module entry and

  marker — board numbers collide across repos).
- A direction issue on the shared-services board exists for the client re-point
  (or the doc states why it is not needed yet, with the reason).
- No file in another repo is edited; no product code is written in this lane.

## Lane / files

- Does **not** own: `portal/**` (#508), `gateway/**` (#503),
  `docs/decision-records/ADR-*` (#501), any file in `shared-frontend` or
  `shared-services`.

## Verify

test -f docs/CHAT-MOUNT.md
grep -q 'mount.type' docs/CHAT-MOUNT.md

items.title: Chat quality: the eval harness, prompt modules and the feedback loop
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501, #502

## Summary

Give the conversational surface a **quality loop**: declared prompt modules for
chat behaviour, an offline eval harness with fixtures, and a feedback capture
that turns real turns into per-version regression evidence — the same shape the
prompts view already exposes (versions + FP/FN metrics).

## Scope

1. **Chat prompt modules** (`registry/chat/**`): frozen system/user bodies
   (versioned, immutable per version, like `registry/prompts/modules/*.yaml`) and
   a declared `outputSchema` for grounded answers — the answer must carry its
   citations in the schema so the envelope is checkable, not aspirational.
2. **Eval harness + fixtures.** Offline, deterministic evaluation of a fixed set
   of conversational cases: a grounded question, an unanswerable question
   (`NO_DATA` expected), a cross-tenant probe (refusal expected), a
   secret-carrying prompt (block expected), a poisoned retrieved document
   (refusal/flag expected). Expected outcomes are declared, and the harness fails
   when an expectation is not met.
3. **Feedback loop.** Capture per-message feedback (thumbs / a correction) keyed
   to `(prompt module version, model, tier)` and project it as the FP/FN metrics
   the prompts view already renders — one metrics vocabulary, not a second.
4. **Regression gate.** A changed prompt module version must be evaluated against
   the fixtures before promotion; a version that regresses a case fails by name.
5. **Honesty.** The harness never reports a pass for a case it could not run — an
   unrunnable case is `CANNOT-ASSESS`, not green (AO-GR-19).

## Acceptance criteria

- Each chat prompt module has a version, a frozen body, and an output schema that
  requires the citations envelope.
- The eval fixtures cover the five cases above and each has a provable failing
  path (mutate the expectation, the harness goes red).
- A prompt-module version change that regresses a case fails the gate by name.
- Feedback is captured against `(module version, model, tier)` and projected into
  the existing per-version metrics vocabulary.
- An unrunnable case is reported `CANNOT-ASSESS`, never a pass.
- No secrets or real tenant data in fixtures.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `registry/chat/**`.
- Does **not** own: `registry/prompts/**`, `registry/profiles/**`,
  `registry/personas/**`, `portal/**` (the metrics view is the portal lane's),
  gate files (wiring owner).

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest registry/chat -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify
```

items.title: Chat experience: streaming, citations and honest degradation in the portal
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501, #502

## Summary

Ship the **experience**: a chat view in the portal console that consumes the
serving surface's stream, renders **grounded answers with provenance**, exposes
the FinOps tier and the per-turn cost, and degrades honestly when a source is
missing. This is the "elite SaaS" half of the intent — the part a user actually
judges.

## Scope

1. **Chat view** (`portal/static/views/chat.html` + assets) over the portal's
   existing server (`portal/server/**`): a message list, a composer, streaming
   render (token-by-token over the serving surface's SSE), stop-generation,
   retry, and multi-conversation history.
2. **Citations / provenance.** Every grounded fragment renders the source it came
   from (bridge family + revision, tool call, or ticket id) from the citations
   envelope — a claim the envelope does not back is rendered as unsupported, not
   as fact.
3. **Model picker with tiers.** The picker shows the platform's LOW/MED/HIGH/MAX
   tiers with the model the chooser resolves for the turn — the client selects a
   *tier*, never an arbitrary provider model.
4. **Cost + latency surfacing.** Per-turn tokens, latency and estimated cost from
   the FinOps lane's read model, plus the tenant's budget state (soft warning vs
   hard stop), visibly distinct.
5. **Honest states.** Missing source → an explicit "no data for this" state, not
   an empty success; a degraded turn (fallback tier) says it degraded and why;
   an unpromoted surface is **invisible** (flag checked before AuthN), not merely
   forbidden.
6. **Design system.** Consume the existing design tokens
   (`portal/static/design-tokens/`) and the shell's `os:*` bridge conventions
   where the view is hosted in the OS shell; no new visual language, dark mode
   included, accessible by keyboard with live-region announcements for streamed
   content.

## Acceptance criteria

- The view renders a streamed answer incrementally and a terminal state; a
  cancelled stream stops cleanly.
- Each grounded fragment shows its source; an unsupported claim is visibly
  unsupported.
- The tier picker offers only tiers; a resolved model is displayed, not chosen.
- Per-turn cost/latency and the tenant's budget state render, with the hard-stop
  state distinct from the warning state.
- With the surface flag off, the route and the view are absent (not rendered,
  not merely 403).
- An empty/absent source renders a `NO_DATA` state; a degraded turn is labelled.
- Static-asset twin/appliance tests follow the existing portal conventions; the
  suite passes offline.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `portal/**` (views, static assets, `portal/server/**`,
  `portal/tests/**`).
- Does **not** own: `gateway/**`, `identity/**`, `telemetry/**`,
  `guardrails/**`, `registry/**` (all consumed over HTTP/contracts), gate files
  (wiring owner).

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest portal/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify
```

items.title: Chat guardrails: DLP egress, inbound re-validation and retrieval-injection defense
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501, #502

## Summary

Guard **both directions of every conversational turn**. Outbound, a tenant's
prompt is untrusted input about a tenant's data and may carry secrets/PII across
the perimeter; inbound, the model is an untrusted consultant whose output must
not land in tenant state verbatim. Grounding adds a third direction: a retrieved
ticket or knowledge document can itself smuggle instructions (AO-GR-16).

## Scope

1. **Egress scrub per turn** (`guardrails/chat/**`). Every outbound turn — the
   user prompt, the assembled grounding prefix, and any tool arguments — passes
   the `guardrails/dlp` scrub before it leaves. A blocked payload **aborts the
   call**; a redacted payload is recorded redacted, and neither the verdict nor
   the finding echoes the matched secret.
2. **Inbound re-validation.** The model's output is treated as untrusted: it is
   validated before it lands in conversation state, and a claim that cites no
   supplied source is flagged (the citations envelope from the grounding lane is
   the contract this consumes — never re-implements).
3. **Retrieval-injection defense.** Grounded material (tickets, KB documents,
   ledger excerpts) is scanned by `guardrails/dlp/injection.py` **before** it
   enters the prompt, so a poisoned source cannot escalate into an instruction.
4. **Tri-state, fail-closed.** Every guard returns an explicit
   BLOCK / WARN / LOG verdict (AO-GR-19); an undecidable guard does not default
   to allow. Verdicts are attached to a turn only on an exact identifier match
   (the existing verdict-attachment rule).
5. **Policy binding.** The turn honours the `guardrails/policy` controls registry
   (the default-OFF controls the portal's Policies view toggles), so flipping a
   control genuinely changes the turn's behaviour.

## Acceptance criteria

- A payload containing a seeded secret is **blocked** outbound and the call is
  aborted; the finding never echoes the matched value.
- A redaction path exists and is tested (the payload proceeds, the secret does
  not).
- A poisoned retrieved document fails to inject an instruction, with a
  **negative control** proving the detector fires.
- Model output that contradicts a supplied source — or cites a source that was
  never supplied — is flagged/refused.
- Every guard emits BLOCK/WARN/LOG; no path logs "OK" on a path that never ran.
- Turning a `guardrails/policy` control on changes the observed verdict for a
  fixed input.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `guardrails/chat/**`.
- Does **not** own: `guardrails/dlp/**`, `guardrails/policy/**`,
  `guardrails/sandbox/**`, `guardrails/isolation/**` (all consumed), gate files
  (wiring owner).

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest guardrails/chat -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify
```

Dispatch tier: security work — never below the HIGH floor (fleet FinOps
doctrine).

items.title: Chat FinOps: per-turn attribution, budget caps and prompt-cache accounting
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501, #502

## Summary

Make every conversational turn **metered, attributed and budget-capped** —
because a chat surface is, financially, the cheapest way to burn an unbounded
amount of a tenant's budget by holding a key down. Reuse the existing rails;
add only the conversational attribution layer.

## Scope

1. **Per-turn attribution** (`telemetry/chat/**`). Derive one attribution record
   per turn from the turn's `GatewayCallRecord`:
   `tenant` + `agent` + `conversation` + promoted `model/provider`, `tokens`,
   `latency`, `estimated_cost` — and, when the turn was spawned from a ticket,
   the ticket id (the join node, ADR-0014). No figure is re-derived: cost comes
   from `telemetry/metering`'s rate cards, the ledger event from
   `telemetry/ledger`.
2. **Budget guard.** Read `telemetry/budgets`' quota/cap state and enforce it per
   turn: soft warning at `warn_at_pct`, hard stop at the cap
   (`gateway/finops/budget.py`'s semantics), with the tenant/global kill switch
   (`telemetry/budgets/config/killswitch.yaml`) honoured **before** the model
   call. A blocked turn is refused and **still metered** (AO-GR-18: metering is
   the mechanism, enforcement the guarantee).
3. **Tier discipline.** The chooser (`gateway/finops/chooser.py`,
   `tiers.yaml`) picks the tier for the turn; the surface must not accept a tier
   from the client as authoritative. Escalation is observed-difficulty only.
4. **Prompt-cache accounting.** Report the cache footprint / cache-hit share for
   the turn so a tenant's repeated context is visibly cached, not re-billed
   (`engine/memory/prompt_cache.py` discipline, consumed).
5. **Surfacing read model.** Expose the turn's cost/latency/budget state to the UX
   lane as a small read model (the UX lane renders it; this lane owns the
   numbers).

## Acceptance criteria

- A budget-violating turn is **blocked and metered**, proven by test.
- A kill-switch-on tenant is refused before any provider call, proven by test.
- Every turn produces exactly one ledger event and one metering record; a turn
  with no record fails a test.
- Attribution carries tenant + agent + conversation, and a ticket id when the
  turn came from a ticket.
- A cache-hit turn reports a cache share and a lower estimated cost than the
  equivalent cold turn (deterministic fixture).
- No cost figure is computed in this lane from raw tokens where a rate card
  exists — the rate card is the authority.
- Negative controls exist for the block paths (AO-GR-19).

## Lane / files

- Owns: `telemetry/chat/**`.
- Does **not** own: `telemetry/metering/**`, `telemetry/budgets/**`,
  `telemetry/ledger/**`, `gateway/finops/**` (all consumed), gate files (wiring
  owner).

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest telemetry/chat -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify
```

items.title: Chat identity: scoped (tenant, agent, conversation) credentials and structural tenant isolation
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501, #502

## Summary

Own **who the conversation is**: prove the identity at the front door, bind it to
exactly one tenant, scope it to one `(tenant, agent, conversation)`, and refuse
every crossing fail-closed — without creating a second identity model.

This is the lane that answers ADR-0013's embed warning head-on: embedding a
client that has its own users and sessions duplicates the tenant/RBAC model
forever. Here that client's users are **advisory**, and ours are authoritative.

## Scope

1. **Scoped chat credential** (`identity/chat/**`). Mint and verify a credential
   scoped to `(tenant_id, agent_id, conversation_id)` in the **existing**
   registry service identity claim vocabulary (`iss/sub/aud/iat/exp/jti` +
   scoped `tenantId/agentId/role/allowedTools`) that
   `gateway/mcp/authn.py` already verifies — no new token format, no new
   verifier.
2. **Front door.** Consume the auth-gate identity exactly as the portal does:
   the shared-frontend auth-hub relay + the RS256 `os-session-token`
   (`purpose: os-session-token`) verified offline against the gate's JWKS mirror,
   fail-closed. `portal/server/sso.py` and `identity/sso/` are **consumed, never
   re-implemented**.
3. **Client binding.** Define how an external client's own identity (for the
   shared-services OpenWebUI: the proxy-injected
   `X-Forwarded-Email` trusted header) maps to a tenant. The mapping is explicit
   and declared; an unmapped identity is **refused**, never defaulted to a
   tenant. Where the client's role vocabulary and ours disagree, **ours wins**.
4. **Isolation.** A conversation's memory and history live in exactly one
   `engine/memory` SESSION container (`session:<tenant>:<agent>:<session>`); the
   credential's scope must match that container, and a mismatch raises and is
   counted (the store already does this — prove the chat path cannot bypass it).
5. **Approvals.** A turn that proposes an action is routed to
   `identity/cpapi`'s approval gate (`202 approval_required` → approve executes).
   The chat surface never gains a direct write.
6. **Fail-closed defaults.** No anonymous mode, no "tenant from the request body",
   no cross-tenant fallback, no impersonation shortcut (AO-GR-15, AO-GR-20).

## Acceptance criteria

- A credential minted for tenant A is refused for any tenant B read/write,
  including with a foreign `tenantId` in the body or a query parameter.
- A revoked session is refused while unexpired.
- An unmapped client identity is refused (not defaulted); a mapped one resolves
  to exactly one tenant.
- A conversation whose credential scope disagrees with its memory container is
  refused, and the cross-scope counter increments.
- An approval proposal reaches `identity/cpapi` and executes only after
  approval; a direct write attempt from the chat path is refused.
- Negative-control tests exist for each refusal above (AO-GR-19).
- No secret is read from, or written to, a request body or a tracked file.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `identity/chat/**`.
- Does **not** own: `identity/sso/**`, `identity/rbac/**`,
  `identity/entitlements/**`, `identity/cpapi/**` (all consumed),
  `portal/server/sso.py` (consumed), gate files (wiring owner).

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest identity/chat -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify
```

Dispatch tier: this is authN/authZ work — never below the HIGH floor (fleet
FinOps doctrine).

items.title: Chat grounding: the read-only enterprise tool family + the citations envelope
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501, #502

## Summary

Make a turn **"fully aware of the enterprise e2e"** — and do it as a *read of
existing authorities*, never a re-derivation (ADR-0012: no two authoritative
engines). Deliver the read-only enterprise tool family on `gateway/mcp` and the
grounding assembler that turns those reads into a cache-stable prompt prefix with
a citations envelope.

## Scope

1. **Extend the declared, fail-closed tool catalogue** (`gateway/mcp/tools.py`,
   `registry.py`) — the existing seven tools stay; add a **read-only** enterprise
   family with JSON schemas, each tenant-scoped and audited per call (the
   gateway's existing pipeline is reused unchanged):
   - `ticket.get` / `ticket.search` — the claim ledger + board snapshot
     (`governance/dispatch/`, `.board/snapshot.json`) projected read-only. The
     ticket stays the **single join node** (ADR-0014) — this is a read of it, not
     a writer of it.
   - `budget.status` — `telemetry/budgets` quota/cap/kill-switch state.
   - `ledger.tail` / `ledger.verify` — `telemetry/ledger`'s hash-chained events.
   - `agent.list` / `agent.status` — `registry/profiles` seeds.
   - `kb.query` / `kb.freshness` — the **real** index surface (the codeidx/KB
     contract), not the declared fake.
   - `fleet.snapshot` — the `ao.bridge/v1` families already served by the portal
     bridge (`docs/LIVE-DATA-BRIDGE.md`), consumed, not re-derived.
2. **Grounding assembler** — builds the turn's context as a **static-first /
   delta-last** prefix so it is provider-cache compatible
   (`engine/memory/prompt_cache.py` discipline, consumed not edited). It selects
   only what the turn needs, reports the token budget it used, and hashes its
   cache footprint.
3. **Citations envelope** — every grounded fragment carries its source
   identifier (bridge family + revision, tool call id, or ticket id) so the UX
   lane can render provenance and the model can be held to what it was given.
4. **Honesty.** An absent or empty source returns `NO_DATA` (AO-GR-19) — never an
   empty "success". If the real index surface is unavailable, the tool says so
   and the turn degrades explicitly.
5. **Read vs propose.** No tool in this lane writes. A turn that wants an action
   emits an **approval proposal** for the identity lane to route
   (`identity/cpapi` `202 approval_required`); this lane must not create a write
   path.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every added tool is declared with a schema, is tenant-scoped, refuses an
  unverified/foreign tenant fail-closed, and emits the existing `tool_call` /
  `tool_call_denied` audit records.
- A cross-tenant probe is refused; a tool argument can never select a tenant.
- The grounding block for a fixed input is **byte-stable** (deterministic) and its
  cache footprint is reported.
- The citations envelope maps each fragment to a real source id; a fabricated
  source id fails a test.
- `NO_DATA` is returned (not an empty success) when a source is missing.
- The declared-fake index is **not** used as a grounding source for a production
  path; if it remains reachable it is labelled as fixture-only.
- No second projection of ticket/board/budget/fleet state is added.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `gateway/mcp/**`.
- Does **not** own: `gateway/chat/**`, `engine/memory/**` (consumed),
  `governance/dispatch/**`, `telemetry/**`, `registry/**` (all read-only),
  gate files (wiring owner).

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest gateway/mcp -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify
```

Cross-repo note: if the real index consumption needs a contract change from
`kushin77/code-indexing`, file a **direction issue on that board** and name it in
the PR — never edit the peer repo (NG4).

items.title: Chat serving surface: OpenAI- and Ollama-compatible endpoints on the gateway, flag-gated OFF
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501, #502

## Summary

Deliver the **serving surface** of the conversational surface: an
OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/chat/completions` and an Ollama-compatible
`POST /api/chat` on the model-gateway pillar, dispatching every turn through the
existing `gateway/proxy` funnel, plus the **feature flag** and the **IaC
declaration** that ship it OFF. Compatibility is the frozen seam that makes the
client swappable (ADR-0013's mode: across a process boundary over a versioned
API).

## Scope

1. **Endpoints** (`gateway/chat/**`):
   - `POST /v1/chat/completions` — OpenAI-compatible request/response
     (`model`, `messages`, `stream`, `tools`) plus a streaming **SSE** form
     (`data: {...}` frames, terminating `data: [DONE]`).
   - `POST /api/chat` — Ollama-compatible form, matching what
     `gateway/providers/ollama.py` already speaks, so an Ollama-shaped client can
     point at us unchanged.
   - `GET /v1/models` — the advertised model list, derived from
     `gateway/catalog/modules/*/module.json` + `gateway/proxy/config/routing.yaml`
     (never a hand-written list).
2. **Dispatch.** Each turn calls `gateway/proxy`'s `dispatch`/`dispatch_stream`
   — no parallel model path. The serving layer resolves
   `(tenant, agent, conversation) → profile → promptModule → provider/model`
   through the existing resolver, so routing, caps, budgets and fallback are the
   already-tested ones.
3. **Conversation primitive.** A conversation store bound to `engine/memory`'s
   `SESSION` scope container `session:<tenant>:<agent>:<session>` (TTL + isolation
   are already enforced there); this lane **consumes** it and does not edit
   `engine/memory/**`.
4. **Grounding hand-off.** The endpoint accepts the assembled grounding prefix and
   the tool declarations from the grounding lane and passes them through
   unchanged; it declares no tool itself.
5. **Flag + IaC.** Add `surfaces.chat` to `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml`
   (`default: off`, `promoted: false`, `service: portal`, `tf_flag: enable_web`
   or a dedicated `enable_chat`) and the matching variable in
   `infra/terraform/variables.tf`, defaulting `false`. The flag is checked
   **before** AuthN. `scripts/check-feature-flags.py` must pass.
6. **Client-wiring contract + direction issue.** Document, in
   `gateway/chat/README.md`, how a client points at the surface (the
   OpenAI-compatible connection), and record the shell-mount requirement as a
   **direction issue on `kushin77/shared-frontend`** (a `registry/modules.json`
   entry, `mount.type: tab`, the `diagrams.purebliss.app` precedent). This repo
   edits no file in that repo (NG4,
   `docs/CROSS-REPO-EXECUTION-BOUNDARY.md`).

## Acceptance criteria

- Both endpoints exist behind the flag and are **refused while the flag is off**,
  before AuthN.
- A turn reaches a provider through `gateway/proxy` and yields a
  `GatewayCallRecord` (audit + metering sinks), proven by test.
- Streaming yields incremental frames and a terminal frame; a `stream: false`
  call returns one JSON body.
- No API key, tenant id or budget is accepted from the request body as
  authoritative — they come from the verified credential (identity lane).
- Illegal/unknown model, malformed messages, and an unknown tenant are refused
  with the OpenAI-compatible error shape, fail-closed.
- `gateway/chat/README.md` documents the contract; the direction issue URL is
  recorded in the PR body.
- No unfinished markers and no debug output.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `gateway/chat/**`, `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml`,
  `infra/terraform/**`.
- Does **not** own: `engine/memory/**` (consumed), `gateway/proxy/**` (consumed),
  `Makefile` / `scripts/verify.sh` / `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` (the wiring
  owner).

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest gateway/chat -q -p no:cacheprovider
python3 scripts/check-feature-flags.py
make verify
```

items.title: Wire the conversational-surface gates into the gate of record
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

Blocked-by: #501

## Summary

This is the **gate-wiring owner** for the conversational surface. In this repo a
new `scripts/check-*.sh` is inert until it is named in the explicit check list:
`scripts/verify.sh` iterates a hand-maintained `checks=(...)` array, and suites
are only run when registered in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`. The chat lanes
therefore **do not** touch these files; this lane does, once, and every
gate-producing chat lane is `Blocked-by` it.

Same shape as the existing wiring owners #420 (paperclip boundary/adapters),
#466 (diagrams declaration/projection) and #481 (codeidx surface/backend).

## Scope

- Add the chat gates to `scripts/verify.sh`'s `checks=(...)` array as they land,
  and the chat suites to `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`.
- Keep `Makefile` `check-*` targets and `.PHONY` entries complete.
- Prove each newly wired gate can genuinely fail (AO-GR-4 no-false-green): a gate
  whose pass and fail paths collapse into one exit code is rejected.

Gates expected from the sibling lanes (wire each when it lands, by name):

| Gate (`scripts/`) | Produced by |
|---|---|
| `check-chat-surface.sh` — the OpenAI-/Ollama-compatible contract + flag gate | serving-surface lane |
| `check-chat-tools.sh` — the read-only enterprise tool catalogue + fail-closed allowlist | grounding lane |
| `check-chat-identity.sh` — scoped credential + tenant isolation negatives | identity lane |
| `check-chat-finops.sh` — per-turn attribution + budget cap/kill-switch proof | FinOps lane |
| `check-chat-guardrails.sh` — DLP egress + retrieval-injection negative controls | guardrails lane |
| `check-chat-ux.sh` — streaming/citations contract + honest degradation | UX lane |
| `check-chat-eval.sh` — eval fixtures + feedback loop regression | eval lane |

## Acceptance criteria

- Every chat gate named above is present in `scripts/verify.sh`'s check array and
  runs inside `make verify`; every chat pytest suite is registered in
  `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`.
- At least one chat gate is proven to fail by a deliberate mutation (log the
  mutation, the failing output, and the restore).
- `scripts/check-feature-flags.py` still passes: the new `surfaces.chat` entry and
  its `enable_*` counterpart stay in 1:1 parity with `infra/terraform/variables.tf`.
- Gate-file edits are union merges (keep every sibling lane's entry) — no entry is
  dropped when two lanes land together.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `Makefile`, `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`.
- Does **not** own: any `scripts/check-chat-*.sh` (each is delivered by its own
  lane as a standalone script that this lane references).

## Verify

```bash
bash -n scripts/verify.sh
make verify
```

Report the literal output of `make verify` and the mutation that proved a chat
gate can fail.

items.title: Decision: the conversational surface — gateway-authoritative chat with a swappable client (ADR claimed at implementation time)
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #500

## Summary

Record the decision this EPIC's options paper recommends — the
conversational surface is **gateway-authoritative**, and the shared-services
OpenWebUI is a **swappable, non-authoritative client** of it. The recommendation
must be an accepted ADR **before** any implementation lane starts — the EPIC's
design is a proposal until this record freezes it.

**ADR number: claimed at implementation time.** The executing lane takes the
next free number from `origin/master`'s `docs/decision-records/`, exactly as the
sibling decision lanes did (`#463` self-corrected to `ADR-0017`; `#474` to
`ADR-0018`). A candidate verified free at filing time is **ADR-0023** (0001-0018
are on `origin/master`; `ADR-0022` is claimed by the monitoring decision `#495`).
Do not treat a number as frozen here: re-derive it when the lane starts.

## What the ADR must decide (and cite)

1. **Mode.** Adopt the already-running upstream OpenWebUI **across a process
   boundary over a versioned, OpenAI-/Ollama-compatible contract** — explicitly
   **not** embed (would duplicate the tenant/RBAC/session model) and **not**
   fork (unbounded rebase cost). Follow `docs/decision-records/ADR-0013-paperclip-ing-integration.md`'s
   reasoning, which rejects embed and fork for exactly these costs.
2. **Single authority.** `gateway/` remains the one model path: routing
   (`gateway/sme-routing/`, ADR-0015's "map the policy, do not couple the
   runtime"), tier choice (`gateway/finops/`), caps (`gateway/limits/`),
   budgets (`telemetry/budgets/`), guardrails (`guardrails/`), metering and the
   ledger (`telemetry/`). No second authoritative engine (ADR-0012).
3. **The authority boundary for grounding.** The turn may **read** the existing
   authorities (`ao.bridge/v1` families, the `gateway/mcp` tool catalogue,
   `governance/dispatch`, `telemetry/budgets`, the knowledge index) and may
   **propose** writes only as approvals. It is never the writer of `status`,
   `blocked_by` or `facets.budget` — the one-writer map frozen by
   `docs/decision-records/ADR-0014-ticket-single-join-node-contract-v2.md` and
   `docs/contracts/paperclip/ticket.schema.json`.
4. **Identity.** The auth-gate `os-session-token` is the front door; OpenWebUI's
   own user table is **advisory, never authoritative**; a scoped chat credential
   is minted per `(tenant, agent, conversation)` in the claim vocabulary
   `gateway/mcp/authn.py` already verifies.
5. **Flag posture.** A `surfaces.chat` entry in
   `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml`, `default: off`, with the matching
   `enable_*` in `infra/terraform/variables.tf` and 1:1 parity enforced by
   `scripts/check-feature-flags.py`; the flag is checked **before** AuthN
   (the `live_bridge` precedent). AO-GR-6 / GR-5.
6. **Rejected alternatives and why** — option A (mount OpenWebUI pointed at the
   Ollama VIP: no enterprise awareness, second identity model, second
   conversation store), option B (rebuild the chat UI in the portal: recurring
   maintenance against a one-time boundary cost), option D (portal-native on MCP
   only: same rebuild cost, thinner grounding). Option C is adopted as the
   *contract*, not as a coupling.

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/decision-records/ADR-00NN-conversational-surface.md` exists (NN = the
  next free number at implementation time, per the note above) with the
  house front-matter (`id`, `status: accepted`, `date`, `deciders`, `req`,
  `supersedes`) matching the ADR template.
- The record states the mode, the single authority, the read/propose-only
  boundary, the identity rule, the flag posture, and the rejected options with
  reasons.
- The record is registered where ADRs are discovered (the knowledge catalogue
  picks up `docs/decision-records/ADR-*.md` automatically — no second list to
  edit).
- No implementation file is touched by this lane.

## Lane / files

- Owns: `docs/decision-records/ADR-00NN-*.md` only.

## Verify

```bash
python3 governance/knowledge/cli.py validate
make verify
```

items.title: EPIC: Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass — a gateway-authoritative conversational surface grounded in the enterprise e2e (OpenWebUI × Ollama)
items.milestone: M30 - Enterprise chat in the Single Pane of Glass (OpenWebUI × portal × Ollama)
items.body:
# EPIC — the conversational surface in the Single Pane of Glass

**Goal (one line).** Give the control-plane portal a first-class **conversational
surface** — chat with your enterprise environment like a normal AI chatbot, but
grounded end-to-end in this control plane (agents, tickets, budgets, guardrails,
telemetry, the knowledge index) — by making **our gateway the authority** and
treating the already-running shared-services **OpenWebUI as a swappable,
non-authoritative client**.

## 0. Owner intent (verbatim)

> "how we can have the openwebui experience inside our frontend portal that is
> now mostly paperclip - i want to be able to chat with my environment just like
> its a regular ai chat bot but its fully aware of my enterprise e2e - since we
> use ollama and already have the shared-services openwebui already running give
> me options to integrate this intent into our single pane of glass using elite
> saas methods and functionality"

## 1. Measured current state (each fact with its path / command)

### 1.1 What already exists

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| OpenWebUI is a **real deployed container** | `.research/fleet/shared-services/scripts/deploy-openwebui-container.sh` — container `shared-services-openwebui`, image `ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main`, host `8081` → container `8080`, network `shared-services-net`, volume `shared-services-openwebui-data:/app/backend/data`, `--memory 2g --memory-swap 2g --cpus 1.0`, `--restart unless-stopped`. |
| It is **fronted by proxy auth**, not our identity | `infra/modules/openwebui/variables.tf`: `WEBUI_AUTH=true`, `WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER=X-Forwarded-Email`, `ENABLE_SIGNUP=true`, `DEFAULT_USER_ROLE=user`; `docs/enterprise/LESSONS-LEARNED-OPENWEBUI-OAUTH2-2026-07-19.md` records Cloudflare `ai.purebliss.app` → HAProxy → oauth2-proxy (Keycloak `auth.purebliss.app`) → OpenWebUI, and names the double-auth anti-pattern as the bug that was fixed. |
| Its model path **bypasses our control plane** | `infra/modules/openwebui/variables.tf` `ollama_base_url` = the HAProxy Ollama VIP (`http://192.168.168.10:7434`, `ollama_back`). `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` points OpenWebUI straight at Ollama — no gateway, no budget, no DLP, no ledger. |
| In **IaC it is declared OFF** | `infra/modules/openwebui/variables.tf` `enable_openwebui` default `false` ("plan-neutral"); `infra/modules/host-platform/ollama-webui.tf` is the same shape. The lessons doc records the **live** deploy was done by hand (`docker run`), i.e. live state is **ahead of** declared state. |
| Ollama is already a **first-class provider here** | `gateway/providers/ollama.py` (`POST {base}/api/chat`, `stream: false`, keyless, "the graceful-degradation target for every cloud provider"); `gateway/providers/contract.py` freezes `chat(messages, schema, opts) -> {content, model_used, usage, latency_ms}` + the LOW/MED/HIGH/MAX tier vocabulary. |
| The gateway owns routing, budgets, limits, health, fallback | `gateway/sme-routing/` (single routing authority, ADR-0015), `gateway/finops/` (tier chooser + `budget.py` `warn_at_pct`/`hard_cap_pct`), `gateway/limits/` (context/token caps), `gateway/health/fallback.py` (cloud → local chain). |
| A dispatch funnel + streaming already exist — **but no HTTP server** | `gateway/proxy/README.md`: `dispatch()`/`dispatch_stream()` with per-event envelopes; `handler.GatewayHandler` is deliberately **transport-free** and says *"the phase-7 control-plane REST issue mounts it behind real HTTP"*. |
| An MCP tool surface exists, tenant-scoped and fail-closed | `gateway/mcp/` — 7 declared tools (`code.definitions/references/search`, `kb.query/freshness/summary`, `platform.whoami`), allowlist not denylist, per-call `tool_call`/`tool_call_denied` audit, HS256 session verified by `authn.verify_token`, rate gate per `tenant:agent:tool`, and a **declared fake** index backend `kb.py` (issue #472/#476). |
| Portal surfaces exist, all **flag-gated OFF** | `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml` `surfaces:` — `fleet_projection` (SSE), `portal_surfaces`, `finops_reports`, `telemetry_live_feed` (SSE), `ops_health`, `live_bridge` (`ao.bridge/v1` + SSE revision signal). `docs/LIVE-DATA-BRIDGE.md` is the contract; the flag is checked **before** AuthN. |
| Portal identity is **already ours** | `portal/server/sso.py` verifies the shared-frontend auth-gate RS256 `os-session-token` offline against the gate's JWKS mirror (`purpose: os-session-token`), fail-closed, issues nothing; `portal/server/authz.py` runs the `identity/rbac` scope-then-permission gates. `identity/cpapi/openapi.yaml` exposes `/agents/{agentId}/tasks`, `/policies`, `/audit`, `/approvals` (destructive ops are `202 approval_required`). |
| Conversation memory already exists | `engine/memory/` — `SESSION` scope container `session:<tenant>:<agent>:<session>`, TTL 7d, `MemoryIsolationError` on a boundary crossing (counted, never quiet), plus `prompt_cache.py` (static-first / delta-last, hashed cache footprint). |
| **No chat surface exists anywhere here** | `git grep -i -E 'openwebui\|open-webui'` over `origin/master` → **0 hits**; a scan of all 273 board issues for `openwebui\|chat\|conversation` → **0 hits**. This EPIC is greenfield. |
| The vendor shell already has a mount + bridge contract | `shared-frontend/modules/schema.json` `mount.type` ∈ `iframe \| tab \| native`; `docs/BRIDGE.md` is the authoritative `os:*` postMessage envelope; `docs/AUTH.md` is the auth-hub relay; `registry/modules.json` currently has **no OpenWebUI entry**. |
| The "mostly paperclip" SPoG is already the decided direction | `docs/FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` §"Repointed" — EPIC #359 / ADR-0013 supersede the greenfield web build; six capabilities come from upstream, not from scratch. |

### 1.2 What is missing

1. **No HTTP serving surface** for models at all — nothing answers
   `POST /v1/chat/completions` or `POST /api/chat`. OpenWebUI therefore *cannot*
   be pointed at this control plane today; the only reachable model path is
   Ollama directly.
2. **No enterprise tool surface for conversation** — `gateway/mcp` declares only
   code/KB index shapes plus `platform.whoami`. There is no read tool for
   tickets, budgets, the ledger, or fleet state, so a turn cannot be grounded.
3. **No conversation primitive** — no session/thread object, no history
   projection, no per-conversation isolation outside `engine/memory`'s generic
   SESSION scope, no citations envelope.
4. **No chat identity binding** — nothing maps an auth-gate identity to a
   `(tenant, agent, conversation)` scope, and OpenWebUI's own user table is a
   second, unbound identity model.
5. **No metering/guardrail binding for a turn** — the pieces exist per call
   (`GatewayCallRecord`, `guardrails/dlp`, `telemetry/ledger`) but nothing
   composes them into a conversational turn.

### 1.3 Honest caveats (do not paper over)

- The live OpenWebUI runs **outside** its own IaC flag (hand-deployed). Any lane
  that touches the client must reconcile declared vs live, or say why it does
  not.
