- The MCP index backend is a **declared fake**; grounding a chat turn on it would
  be a fabricated answer. The chat grounding lane must consume the **real**
  codeidx/KB surface or report `NO_DATA` honestly (AO-GR-19).
- The image tag is `:main` (unpinned) — a production promotion must pin it
  (the variable's own description says so).

## 2. The options (with an explicit tradeoff table)

| | **A. Mount OpenWebUI in the OS shell** (status quo wiring) | **B. Chat UI in the portal; OpenWebUI as a model gateway only** | **C. Gateway-proxied, portal-embedded** | **D. Portal-native chat on MCP, no OpenWebUI** | **E. Gateway authority + OpenWebUI as a swappable client** (recommended) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Where the surface lives** | `shared-frontend` module entry (`iframe`/`tab`) → `os.purebliss.app` | `portal/static/views/chat.html` + `portal/server/` | `gateway/` serving endpoint; OpenWebUI iframed in the shell | portal views + `gateway/mcp` tools | `gateway/chat/**` serving endpoint; OpenWebUI mounted as a client |
| **Blast radius** | shared-frontend 6 wiring surfaces (registry + 18 fixtures + mounts baseline + compose + INVENTORY); shared-services oauth2-proxy + `enable_openwebui`; **zero** here | large: a whole chat UX + conversation store + streaming, owned forever | medium: one new serving subtree + flag + parity; portal view | large: both the UX *and* the tool surface | medium: serving subtree + tool family + identity binding + flag — the client stays upstream's |
| **Identity owner** | OpenWebUI + oauth2-proxy (Keycloak) — **a second identity model** | ours (auth-gate + `identity/rbac`) | ours, but the framed client still has its own login unless bound | ours | **ours** — a scoped chat credential in the existing registry claim vocabulary; OpenWebUI's user table is advisory only |
| **Conversation-state owner** | OpenWebUI's volume (second store) | ours (new store) | ours | ours | **ours** — `engine/memory` SESSION scope, tenant-scoped |
| **Upgrade path** | upstream image; our tree untouched | ours forever | upstream client + our versioned endpoint | ours forever | upstream client **and** our flagged endpoint — both upgrades cost nothing in-tree |
| **What it forecloses** | enterprise awareness (no bus/grounding), AO-GR-15/16/17/18 compliance, tenant isolation | ADR-0013's "do not fork/rebuild" posture; a permanent maintenance surface | a swappable client (couples us to OpenWebUI's framing) | a mature chat UX and streaming; a thin grounding story for v1 | nothing structural — the client is replaceable; only the OpenAI/Ollama-compatible contract is a commitment |
| **Honest verdict** | cheapest to start, **fails the intent** (a plain Ollama chatbot) | **builds a product we would then maintain** | viable, but embeds the client | viable for a later phase | **the only option where the intent is met without a second engine** |

## 3. Recommendation — option E, with C as the frozen contract

**Make the gateway the single authoritative path for every conversational turn,
and let OpenWebUI be one interchangeable client of it.** Concretely:

1. **`gateway/chat/`** serves an **OpenAI-compatible** `POST /v1/chat/completions`
   *and* an **Ollama-compatible** `POST /api/chat`, with SSE streaming, by
   dispatching through the existing `gateway/proxy` funnel. Compatibility is the
   seam: it is the one contract both OpenWebUI and a future portal-native UI can
   speak, so the *client is swappable*.
2. **Point the already-running OpenWebUI at our gateway** (its OpenAI-compatible
   connection) instead of at the Ollama VIP. Nothing is forked, nothing is
   embedded at the code level — the mode is exactly ADR-0013's: **across a
   process boundary, over a versioned API**.
3. **Grounding is a read, never a re-derivation.** A turn may read the existing
   authorities — `ao.bridge/v1` families, the `gateway/mcp` tool catalogue
   extended with read-only `ticket.*` / `budget.*` / `ledger.*` / `agent.*` /
   `kb.*` tools, `engine/memory` conversation memory — and may **propose** writes
   only as **approvals** (`identity/cpapi` `202 approval_required`). It never
   becomes the writer of `status` / `blocked_by` / `facets.budget` (ADR-0014's
   frozen one-writer map).
4. **Identity stays ours.** The auth-gate `os-session-token` is the front door;
   `identity/` mints a **scoped chat credential** per `(tenant, agent,
   conversation)` in the vocabulary `gateway/mcp/authn.py` already verifies.
   OpenWebUI's trusted-header email is bound to a tenant; where it disagrees with
   our model, ours wins.
5. **Every turn is one metered, guarded, audited dispatch** — one
   `GatewayCallRecord` → `telemetry/metering` → `telemetry/ledger` (AO-GR-17),
   budget-capped through `telemetry/budgets` + the kill switch (AO-GR-18), DLP +
   retrieval-injection-checked through `guardrails/` (AO-GR-16), and
   prompt-cache-aligned through `engine/memory/prompt_cache.py` so a tenant's
   repeated context is cached, not re-billed.
6. **The shell mount is the vendor's decision, requested by direction issue.**
   ⚠️ **CORRECTED 2026-09-14 — the mount type first proposed here was wrong.**
   The original text recommended `mount.type: tab` and cited `diagrams` as the
   precedent. Measured on `origin/master` + the `shared-frontend` checkout:
   `registry/modules.json` registers `diagrams` as **`native`** (the only `tab`
   entry is `dialplane`, `status: planned`), and `tab` opens a **new browser
   tab** — which *leaves* the Single Pane of Glass and is the opposite of the
   intent ("the experience **inside** our portal"). Framing OpenWebUI itself is
   the worse failure mode: it has its own auth (`WEBUI_AUTH` +
   `X-Forwarded-Email`) and speaks no `os:*`, reintroducing the **double-auth
   anti-pattern** recorded in the shared-services lessons doc.
   The mount is therefore **not decided here**: the candidate shapes are a
   same-origin `iframe` of our own `portal/static/views/chat.html` (the auth
   cookie already applies and it can speak `os:*`) or a `native` addon, and the
   contract is owned by **#512**. The vendor ask is filed as a **direction issue
   on `kushin77/shared-frontend`** — never an edit from here (NG4,
   `docs/CROSS-REPO-EXECUTION-BOUNDARY.md`).
7. **Everything new ships flag-gated OFF** — a `surfaces.chat` entry in
   `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml` with a 1:1 `enable_*` in
   `infra/terraform/variables.tf`, checked **before** AuthN (the `live_bridge`
   precedent, AO-GR-6 / GR-5).

### Why the rejected options are rejected

- **A is rejected** because it does not meet the intent. Pointing OpenWebUI at the
  Ollama VIP yields a competent chatbot that knows **nothing** about the
  enterprise: no tickets, no budgets, no guardrails, no tenant isolation, no
  ledger. It also creates a **second identity model** (OpenWebUI users +
  oauth2-proxy/Keycloak) and a **second conversation store** — the exact
  "two authoritative engines" outcome ADR-0012/ADR-0013 forbid.
- **B is rejected** because it rebuilds a mature product (streaming, history,
  model picker, markdown, file context) that upstream maintains for free, and it
  makes the portal the owner of a model call path — adjacent to the AO-GR-12 line
  that the control plane decides and routes but does not execute work. ADR-0013's
  own reasoning — the recurring cost of a fork/rebuild against a one-time
  boundary cost — applies verbatim.
- **C is rejected as a *destination*, adopted as the *contract***. Gateway-proxied
  chat is the right authority model, but coupling the portal to OpenWebUI's
  framing makes the client unswappable. Freezing only the OpenAI/Ollama-compatible
  contract leaves the client (upstream today, portal-native tomorrow) free.
- **D is rejected for v1** — same rebuild cost as B with a thinner grounding story;
  it also discards upstream's streaming/UX maturity. It remains the natural
  **phase-3** option *behind the same contract*, and is explicitly not foreclosed.

## 4. The NOT-do list

- **Do not point OpenWebUI at the Ollama VIP for the enterprise chat.** That path
  bypasses budgets, DLP, metering and the ledger.
- **Do not embed OpenWebUI's identity** as authoritative. Its user table is
  advisory; tenants, roles and scopes come from `identity/`. (ADR-0013's embed
  warning, restated.)
- **Do not fork or vendor OpenWebUI.** Consume it over a versioned contract, or
  not at all (GR-10, ADR-0013).
- **Do not give the model a write path.** Reads and *approval proposals* only;
  the one-writer map in ADR-0014 stays frozen.
- **Do not re-derive ticket / board / budget / fleet state** to ground an answer.
  Consume `ao.bridge/v1`, `governance/dispatch`, `telemetry/budgets` — a second
  projection is a second engine.
- **Do not ground on the declared-fake MCP index backend.** Consume the real
  codeidx/KB surface or return an honest `NO_DATA`.
- **Do not let the portal execute tenant work** (AO-GR-12) — a chat turn is a
  *dispatch*, not an execution.
- **Do not ship anything ON.** Flag-gated OFF, checked before AuthN.
- **Do not edit another repo.** The shell mount and the shared-services wiring go
  as direction issues to their boards (NG4).
- **Do not self-report success.** "Done" is the `Verify:` command's real output
  plus a green `make verify` (AO-GR-3/AO-GR-13).

## 5. Definition of done

A tenant user signs in at the auth gate, opens **chat** in the portal, and gets a
**streamed** answer grounded in **that tenant's** agents, tickets, budgets,
guardrails and knowledge index; the turn is **cited** (every grounded claim names
the bridge family / tool call / ticket it came from), **metered** and
**budget-capped**, **DLP- and injection-checked**, and recorded on the ledger.
A cross-tenant probe is refused fail-closed; a budget-violating turn is blocked
and metered; a poisoned retrieved document cannot smuggle an instruction; an
absent data source reports `NO_DATA`, never an empty success. Every new surface
ships **flag-gated OFF**; the decision is recorded as **the conversational-surface ADR** (`#501`; its number is claimed at implementation time); `make verify`
is green with the real output pasted as evidence.

## 6. Children (one lane each; the ADR blocks the implementation lanes)

| Lane | Issue | Owns (disjoint globs) | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decision | #501 | `docs/decision-records/ADR-00NN-*.md` | — |
| Gate wiring owner | #502 | `Makefile`, `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` | Decision |
| Serving surface / mount + flag + IaC | #503 | `gateway/chat/**`, `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml`, `infra/terraform/**` | Decision, wiring |
| Grounding + enterprise tool surface | #504 | `gateway/mcp/**` | Decision, wiring |
| Identity + tenant isolation | #505 | `identity/chat/**` | Decision, wiring |
| FinOps + metering | #506 | `telemetry/chat/**` | Decision, wiring |
| Guardrails / DLP + injection | #507 | `guardrails/chat/**` | Decision, wiring |
| Streaming + citations UX | #508 | `portal/**` | Decision, wiring |
| Eval + feedback loop | #509 | `registry/chat/**` | Decision, wiring |

A lane that produces a gate **must not** edit `Makefile`, `scripts/verify.sh` or
`scripts/pytest-suites.txt`; those belong to the **wiring owner** (#502), and
every gate-producing lane is `Blocked-by` it.

Rollout order: **the #501 conversational-surface ADR** → wiring owner → the serving surface + gate wiring →
grounding/tools → identity → FinOps → guardrails → UX → eval. The Ollama pin
(issue #337) gains its first real routed consumer here; the paperclip operator
surface (ADR-0013) is untouched — this is a *new* surface beside it, not a change
to it.

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest gateway/chat portal/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify
```

Parent EPIC-00 is issue #4; this EPIC closes only when every child above is
closed with evidence and the surface is live **flag-gated OFF**.

items.title: Wire the monitoring exposition + declaration gates into the gate of record
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
Parent: 494
Blocked-by: #420, #496, #497, #498

## Objective

Make the monitoring program's gates real. A check that is not wired into `scripts/verify.sh` is
inert: this repo's gate of record iterates an **explicit** `checks=(...)` list, so a new
`scripts/check-*.sh` is never auto-discovered.

## Deliverable

Wire the lanes above into the gate of record:

- `scripts/check-monitoring-declaration.sh` (the declaration lane) into `scripts/verify.sh`'s
  `checks=(...)` array;
- the exposition and fleet-signal suites into `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` as appropriate;
- any `Makefile` target the lanes rely on.

## Hard constraints

- **One writer per wave on the three build files.** `Makefile`, `scripts/verify.sh` and
  `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` are the shared surface every wiring lane touches. Do not add an entry
  another lane is already adding — a duplicate check is a gate defect, not a harmless no-op.
- **Assert no duplicates.** After wiring, `duplicates` in `.verify/attestation.json` must be `{}`.
  A previously-landed sibling wiring lane can already have added the entry this lane would re-add
  (measured on this board before: a re-added `cross-reference` entry produced
  `duplicates: {'cross-reference': 2}`).
- **Gate from a clean checkout.** Prove the new checks pass from the **committed** tree, not the
  working tree — a gate that is green only because its own contract docs are uncommitted is a false
  green this repo has already shipped once.

## Verify

```bash
make verify
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.verify/attestation.json'));print(d['result'],d.get('duplicates'))"
```

items.title: Publish the fleet-health signals to the monitoring plane — heartbeat, orphan-sweep and watchdog verdicts as monitoring events
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
Parent: 494
Blocked-by: #495

## Objective

Publish the **fleet's own** health signals — the ones this repo computes about itself and its
agents — to the monitoring plane, so an operator sees a stalled rung, a stale heartbeat or an
unresolvable orphan as a monitoring event instead of only inside a tmux pane.

This is a deliberately **different signal family** from the SLO/budget/metering feed: that one is
about tenants and cost, this one is about the control plane's own liveness.

## Measured position (2026-09-14) — the verdicts exist, the exit does not

- `fleet/monitor.py` and `fleet/watchdog.py` — the rung monitor and the watchdog verdict lines.
- `governance/reconcile/` — `heartbeat.py` and `sweep.py`: a session records a heartbeat while it
  runs, a beat past the TTL (15 minutes) is orphaned, and each orphan is *reclaimed*, *parked* or
  *shelved* by where its work lives (`AGENTS.md` rule 17).
- `fleet/telemetry.py` writes `.fleet/runs.jsonl`; `.fleet/slog.jsonl` carries the event stream;
  `fleet/console.py` is the terminal view (`docs/FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md`).
- **None of these verdicts leave the host.**

## Deliverable

A flag-gated-OFF publisher mapping the fleet's own verdicts onto the monitoring plane's event/alert
shape (per ADR-0022), covering at least: rung state + commit + beat age, orphan/suspect/reclaimed/
parked/shelved outcomes, and watchdog verdicts.

Requirements that are part of the acceptance:

- **Stable machine shape** per signal kind, declared in-tree.
- **A negative control per refused shape.** A stale beat must publish as *stale*, never as
  *healthy*; an orphan with unmerged work must publish as *shelved*, never as *reclaimed* — the
  refusal is the point of `governance/reconcile/` and must survive the export.
- **Honest emptiness.** No state must publish a *no-data* signal, never a fabricated *healthy* one
  (the repo's tri-state 0/1/2 honesty precedent: a surface that cannot be established is never a
  pass).
- **Flag-gated OFF** (GR-5) and no new always-on service.

## Files

`fleet/**`, `governance/reconcile/**`. Do not touch `telemetry/**` (sibling lane) or the build
files (the wiring lane).

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest fleet/tests governance/reconcile/tests
make verify
```

items.title: Publish the telemetry pillar as a scrapeable exposition surface — a flag-gated metrics export over the SLO + budget + metering feeds
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
Parent: 494
Blocked-by: #495

## Objective

Give the telemetry pillar a way out of the process: a **flag-gated-OFF** exposition surface that
renders the SLO / budget / metering feed in the transport ADR-0022 fixes, so the fleet monitoring
plane can observe this control plane.

## Measured position (2026-09-14) — the feed exists, the exit does not

- `telemetry/observability/` — `slos.py` (per-tenant SLO definition + evaluation; closed kinds and
  verdicts `OK`/`AT_RISK`/`BREACHED`/`NO_DATA`; `slo_templates/{availability-requests,latency-p95,cost-budget}.yaml`),
  `breach.py`, `dashboard.py`, `store.py`, `intake.py`, `usage.py`.
- `telemetry/budgets/exporter.py` — `BudgetStateExporter`, described in-tree as *"machine-readable
  budget/quota/SLO/audit state snapshot … the SLO feed for tenant dashboards/alerting"*, consuming
  the `telemetry/observability` SLO vocabulary verbatim.
- `telemetry/metering/` — `rate_cards/{anthropic,deepseek,gemini,ollama,openai}.yaml`, `intake.py`,
  `report.py`, `store.py`; `telemetry/ledger/` — the audit ledger.
- **None of it is reachable from outside the process**: the only outputs are local JSONL files.
  A repo-wide grep for `prometheus|grafana|jaeger|opentelemetry|otel|alertmanager` (excluding
  `vendor/**`, `.research/**`) finds no exporter and no scrape endpoint.

## Deliverable

A flag-gated-OFF exporter (GR-5) that renders, in ADR-0022's transport:

- the per-tenant SLO results — **consuming** `slos.py`'s kinds and verdicts verbatim, never
  re-declaring them;
- the `BudgetStateExporter` budget/quota/audit state;
- the metering usage aggregate.

Requirements that are part of the acceptance, not decoration:

- **No vocabulary copy.** A gate proves the exported verdicts are produced by
  `telemetry/observability/slos.py` and not by a second, parallel definition in the exporter.
- **No silent coercion.** A negative control proves `BREACHED` and `NO_DATA` leave the process as
  `BREACHED` and `NO_DATA` — never coerced to `OK` and never dropped.
- **No cross-tenant leak.** The export honours tenant scoping; a per-tenant label set must not
  carry another tenant's identifiers (the repo's own `live_feed.py` authz precedent applies).
- **Bounded cardinality.** The label set is fixed by ADR-0022 in light of the vendor's `#178 Zero
  Metric Cardinality Management` — a per-tenant × per-agent × per-SLO free-form label is a defect.
- **Flag-gated OFF** in `infra/feature-flags/registry.yaml` (default off, promoted false), and the
  route gate sits before authN if it is an HTTP surface — the established repo pattern.

## Files

`telemetry/observability/**`, `telemetry/budgets/exporter.py`, `telemetry/metering/**` (read),
plus the feature-flag entry. Do not touch `telemetry/ledger/**`.

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m pytest telemetry/observability/tests telemetry/budgets/tests
make verify
```

items.title: Declare this repo's monitoring integration and observability surface — module.json integrations[] + docs/OBSERVABILITY.md + a gate
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
Parent: 494
Blocked-by: #495

## Objective

Declare the integration. The repo has an observability *implementation* and no observability
*declaration*: `module.json` names no monitoring integration and there is no `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md`.

## Measured position (2026-09-14)

- `module.json` `integrations[]` = `anthropic`, `deepseek`, `openai`, `gemini`, `ollama`, `oidc`,
  `saml`. Nothing monitoring-shaped.
- `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md` — **absent**. The repo-wide grep for
  `prometheus|grafana|jaeger|opentelemetry|otel|alertmanager` (excluding `vendor/**`,
  `.research/**`) returns no exporter and no scrape endpoint.
- The Prometheus declaration this repo should mirror already exists in CMR:
  `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/shared-services/module.json:52` —
  `{ "id": "prometheus", "type": "monitoring" }` — beside its `observability` capability
  (`"default": "on"`, flag `sharedservices.observability`).

## This is NOT a `mandatory_consumer_assets` lane

`vendor/CMR/catalog/mandatory.tsv` carries exactly three rows — `code-indexing`, `diagrams`,
`shared-frontend` — with their consumer assets (`.mcp.json`, `gdc-manifest.yaml`,
`architecture.yaml`, `tokens.json`). **Monitoring is not one of them and there is no
`vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/monitoring/` directory**, so there is no mandatory asset to carry and
this lane must not invent one. Declaring a `.mcp.json`-shaped artefact for monitoring would be a
false claim about a vendor contract that does not exist.

## Deliverable

1. **`module.json`** — add the monitoring integration to `integrations[]`, in the shape the ADR
   fixes, mirroring `shared-services`' declaration.
2. **`docs/OBSERVABILITY.md`** — declare the producer/consumer boundary: this repo produces signals
   (`telemetry/observability/` is the SLO SSOT), `monitoring-stack` owns alerting, `shared-services`
   owns the Prometheus plane, and a signal drives a ticket. Name the exposition surface from the
   integration lanes and point at `docs/FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` as the *different* gap.
3. **`scripts/check-monitoring-declaration.sh`** — assert the integration entry exists and is
   well-formed, and that the doc names the boundary. It must **fail by name** when either is
   missing, and it must be mutation-proven (the check is a formality until a deliberate deletion
   turns it red).

## Lane note

Root `module.json` and `docs/**` are `foundation`-lane files (`docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md` §3); the
wiring lane touches `Makefile`/`scripts/verify.sh`. Different files, but one writer per wave on the
foundation surface — coordinate, do not both edit root config in the same wave.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-monitoring-declaration.sh
make verify
```

items.title: Decision: the telemetry-exposition authority split + the no-second-dashboard rule (ADR-0022)
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
Parent: 494

## Objective

Freeze the boundary this program is built on and pick the one thing that cannot be picked later:
**how this control plane's telemetry reaches the fleet monitoring plane.** Everything else in the
EPIC is mechanical once this is decided; without it, three lanes would each invent a transport.

## What must be decided

1. **The authority split.** This repo *produces* honest signals; `kushin77/monitoring-stack` owns
   aggregation, alerting, routing and runbooks; `shared-services`' `observability` capability
   (`sharedservices.observability`) owns the Prometheus plane; and a signal **drives a ticket** —
   the single join node (ADR-0014) — never a silent action. State that this repo will never run a
   second Prometheus/Grafana/Alertmanager and never build a second dashboard
   (`docs/FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` owns the human surface).
2. **The transport.** A scrape endpoint versus an OTLP push, decided against the *actual* runtime:
   the control plane is a **Google Cloud service** (`infra/terraform/modules/control-plane-service`,
   `infra/cloudbuild/`) and **not** a Kubernetes pod with a service-monitor. Say who holds the
   scrape/remote-write configuration — the plane, not this repo — and what this repo owes.
3. **The integration identity.** The `module.json` `integrations[]` entry shape this repo will
   declare, mirroring `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/shared-services/module.json:52`'s
   `{ "id": "prometheus", "type": "monitoring" }` shape, and which capability name ties it back to
   `sharedservices.observability`. Note plainly that monitoring is **not** a GR-18 mandatory module
   (`vendor/CMR/catalog/mandatory.tsv` = `code-indexing`, `diagrams`, `shared-frontend`) and there
   is **no** `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/monitoring/` manifest to pin against — so no pinned id
   exists and the ADR must not invent one.
4. **The SLO-vocabulary boundary.** `telemetry/observability/slos.py` defines a **closed** SLO kind
   and verdict vocabulary (`OK` / `AT_RISK` / `BREACHED` / `NO_DATA`). Freeze the rule: the export
   renders those verdicts **verbatim** and never re-declares, re-names or coerces them — a
   `BREACHED` that leaves the process as anything else is a defect, not a formatting choice.
5. **The alert-identity question.** What, if anything, this repo tells the plane about *which* SLO
   breached (a stable, non-cardinality-exploding label set). The vendor's own board carries
   `#178 Zero Metric Cardinality Management` — the decision must respect it.

## Constraints

- Consumes, never re-derives: this ADR may **not** restate `monitoring-stack`'s alert or SLO schema;
  it points at `docs/INTEGRATION.md` / `app-instrumentation-guide.md` / `sli-definition-templates.md`
  on that board and consumes them.
- No new always-on service; anything shipped is flag-gated OFF (GR-5).
- No second dashboard; the EPIC's "will NOT do" list is binding here.
- One-way, always: signal → ticket → human. Nothing in the monitoring path writes fleet state.

## Deliverable

`docs/decision-records/ADR-0022-<slug>.md` plus its index row.

ADR numbering, measured 2026-09-14: the highest ADR **file** in `docs/decision-records/` is
`ADR-0012`; `ADR-0020`/`ADR-0021` are **CMR hub** ADRs cited by `governance/merge/README.md`, and
`ADR-0013`–`ADR-0019` are claimed by the in-flight diagrams/codeidx lanes. **ADR-0022 is the next
free number in this repo's own space** — confirm before writing.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-docs.sh
make verify
```

items.title: EPIC: Consume the fleet monitoring plane — publish this control plane's telemetry, declare the integration, and track the vendor direction set
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
## Objective

Make `kushin77/monitoring-stack` — the fleet's real observability platform — able to **observe this
control plane**, by publishing the telemetry this repo already computes on a declared, scrapeable
exposition surface. Today this repo is a **signal producer nobody scrapes**: it has a complete
internal telemetry pillar (SLOs, breaches, budgets, metering, an audit ledger, fleet heartbeats)
and **no way for any of it to leave the process**.

**Honest framing — monitoring is NOT a GR-18 mandatory module, and this EPIC does not pretend it
is.** `vendor/CMR/catalog/mandatory.tsv` carries exactly three rows — `code-indexing`, `diagrams`,
`shared-frontend` — and there is **no** `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/monitoring/` directory (the
module dirs are `code-indexing diagrams googleworkspace hermes-agents erp-crm paperclip ollama
shared-governance saas-rbac shared-frontend shared-services`). Monitoring therefore has **no
`mandatory_consumer_assets`**, so this EPIC carries **no consumer-asset declaration lane**. What it
carries instead is the exposition surface this repo genuinely lacks plus the declaration of an
integration it genuinely has not made.

## Measured position (2026-09-14, `origin/master`) — this is not a blank slate

**"The monitoring module" is three repos with three different roles, not one.** Read via
`gh api repos/kushin77/<name>` and `gh issue list --repo kushin77/<name> --state all`:

| Repo | Role | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| `kushin77/monitoring-stack` | **the module** — Prometheus + Grafana + Alertmanager + Thanos, with `alerts/`, `dashboards/`, `slo-framework/`, `slo_remediation/`, `templates/`, `policies/`, `automation/`, `gitops/`, `terraform/`, and a deep docs tree (`INTEGRATION.md`, `FAST_INTEGRATION.md`, `app-instrumentation-guide.md`, `sli-definition-templates.md`, `alert-templates.md`) | Python, **MIT**, default branch `main`, size 2657 KB, 27 open of 100+ issues, last push `2026-09-10T16:43:52Z` |
| `kushin77/infrastructure-monitoring` | **legacy, decommissioning** — its *only* open issue is `#3 [SHARED-SERVICES] Migrate Ollama alert rules to shared-services; decommission standalone Prometheus/Grafana` | Python, **no license**, branch `master`, 3 issues total, last push `2026-09-10T14:54:05Z` |
| `kushin77/monitoring-agent` | **empty — skip** — CMR `canibalization/registry.csv` rows `R57` and `AA25` both mark it `skip` (*"empty repo (0 commits) — nothing to harvest yet"*) | size 0, no language, last push `2026-01-23T17:33:31Z`, only 2 pilot-invitation issues |

**CMR does not declare monitoring as a module.** `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/` has no `monitoring`
entry; the closest declaration is **`vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/shared-services/module.json:52`** —
`{ "id": "prometheus", "type": "monitoring" }` in `integrations[]`, alongside an `observability`
capability (`"default": "on"`, flag `sharedservices.observability`, *"Operational telemetry,
alerting, and SLO surface for shared platform services"*). So the **Prometheus plane is owned by
`shared-services`, and the alerting/runbook plane is owned by `monitoring-stack`.**

**There is no vendor direction set and no register.** `grep -i monitoring vendor/CMR/channels/inbox.tsv`
returns **no rows** — no `CMR:ENH-*` register for this module. And **no `monitoring-stack` issue
mentions this repo**: `gh issue list --repo kushin77/monitoring-stack --state all` filtered on
`agent-orchestrator|orchestrator` returned **zero** rows. The vendor has never been told this
control plane exists as a consumer.

**This repo emits files, not metrics.** The telemetry pillar is real —
`telemetry/observability/` (`slos.py` with a **closed** SLO kind + verdict vocabulary
`OK`/`AT_RISK`/`BREACHED`/`NO_DATA`, `slo_templates/{availability-requests,latency-p95,cost-budget}.yaml`,
`breach.py`, `dashboard.py`, `store.py`, `intake.py`, `usage.py`), `telemetry/budgets/exporter.py`
(`BudgetStateExporter` — *"machine-readable budget/quota/SLO/audit state snapshot … the SLO feed
for tenant dashboards/alerting"*), `telemetry/metering/rate_cards/*.yaml`, `telemetry/ledger/`,
`fleet/monitor.py`, `fleet/watchdog.py`, `governance/reconcile/{heartbeat,sweep}.py`,
`portal/server/live_feed.py` (SSE). But its only outputs are local JSONL files
(`.fleet/runs.jsonl`, `.fleet/slog.jsonl`, `.telemetry/calls.jsonl`, `.telemetry/security.jsonl`)
— and a repo-wide grep for `prometheus|grafana|jaeger|opentelemetry|otel|alertmanager` (excluding
`vendor/**` and `.research/**`) returns **no exporter, no scrape endpoint and no OTel SDK**: every
hit is the `telemetry/**` SLO vocabulary itself.

**`module.json` declares no monitoring integration.** `integrations[]` is
`anthropic, deepseek, openai, gemini, ollama, oidc, saml` — nothing monitoring-shaped.

**`docs/OBSERVABILITY.md` is ABSENT** in this repo (`test -f` → absent; `docs/` is
`ARCHITECTURE.md CANNIBALIZATION.md EXECUTION-PLAN.md FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md
GOLDEN-RULES.md GOVERNANCE.md QA-GATE.md README.md decision-records/ spikes/`). The repo has
observability *code* and no observability *declaration*.

**`infra/` declares no monitoring stack.** `infra/terraform/modules/` is exactly
`control-plane-service`, `deployer-sa`, `web-surface` — no OTel collector, no scrape config, no
alerting wiring. `infra/` is Terraform + `cloudbuild/` + `feature-flags/` + `rollout/`.

**The existing gap doc is about a different gap.** `docs/FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` names the
**TUI-vs-web operator** gap (#330 → #331/#332/#333, *"Live streaming to a browser"*) and never
mentions metrics export, Prometheus, OTel or alerting once. That is the *human* surface; this EPIC
is about the *machine* surface. Neither is re-derived here.

## The authority boundary (three surfaces, and this EPIC touches exactly one)

| Question | Owner | Posture |
|---|---|---|
| *Is the control plane alive and within SLO?* | this repo — `telemetry/observability/slos.py`'s **closed** kind + verdict vocabulary | **ours — unchanged, consumed verbatim** |
| *Does an alert fire, and who is paged?* | `kushin77/monitoring-stack` (Alertmanager routing, runbooks, SLO framework) on the Prometheus plane owned by `shared-services`' `observability` capability | **consume — this EPIC** |
| *What is the human operator's live view?* | the web single pane of glass (`docs/FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md`, #331/#332/#333) | **untouched — never re-derived** |
| *Does a monitoring signal decide anything?* | nowhere: it drives a **ticket**, the single join node (ADR-0014) | **never a decision authority** |

## Children

| Child | Issue | What it closes |
|---|---|---|
| **Decision: the telemetry-exposition authority split + the no-second-dashboard rule** (ADR-0022) | #495 | the transport (scrape vs OTLP push for a non-Kubernetes Google Cloud service), the declared integration identity, and the frozen SLO-vocabulary boundary |
| **Declare the monitoring integration and the observability surface** — `module.json integrations[]` + `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md` + a gate | #496 | the absent declaration (*not* a `mandatory_consumer_assets` lane — monitoring is not mandatory) |
| **Publish the telemetry pillar as a scrapeable exposition surface** | #497 | `telemetry/observability/**` + `telemetry/budgets/exporter.py` — the SLO/budget/metering feed, flag-gated OFF |
| **Publish the fleet-health signals to the monitoring plane** | #498 | `fleet/**` + `governance/reconcile/**` — heartbeat / orphan-sweep / watchdog verdicts as monitoring events |
| **Wire the monitoring exposition + declaration gates into the gate of record** | #499 | the three build files — one writer, serialized behind the root build-file owner |

Chain edges: the decision (`#495`) precedes both exposition lanes (`#497`, `#498`) and the
declaration (`#496`), because the ADR fixes the transport and the integration identity all three
consume. The wiring lane (`#499`) is serialized behind the root build-file owner (this repo's
`Makefile` / `scripts/verify.sh` / `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` writer) and behind every lane it wires
— one writer per wave on those three files, which this repo keeps re-learning.

> **A vendor reference is never a `Blocked-by:` marker.** A bare number means *this* board's issue;
> board numbers collide across repos. The vendor dependency is named in prose, deliberately, and its
> issue URL is recorded below.

## What this EPIC will NOT do

- **No second monitoring stack.** No Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager or Thanos is deployed from
  this repo. `monitoring-stack` is consumed; it is never mirrored, forked or vendored (GR-10), and
  nothing under it is edited from here — needs go out as a direction issue on that board (NG4/NG6).
- **No second dashboard.** `docs/FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md`'s web SPoG is the *operator*
  surface; the monitoring plane is the *machine* surface. Re-deriving one from the other is the
  failure this EPIC exists to prevent.
- **No capability register and no `mandatory_consumer_assets` lane.** Monitoring is not mandatory;
  inventing a mandatory-module shape for it would be the dishonest move. The declaration lane
  declares the integration, nothing more.
- **No re-defined SLO vocabulary.** `telemetry/observability/slos.py`'s kinds and verdicts are
  consumed verbatim at the export boundary; a `BREACHED` verdict must never be coerced to `OK`.
- **No new always-on service.** Whatever surface lands ships **flag-gated OFF** (GR-5); no
  `terraform apply`, no console clicks.
- **No module-registry view.** #445 (*"Ecosystem module registry + state federation"*) owns the
  "one view of every module" surface; this EPIC publishes signals and does not federate state.

## Definition of done

The telemetry pillar exposes a flag-gated-OFF surface whose SLO verdicts are provably the ones
`telemetry/observability/slos.py` computes (a gate proves the export re-uses the vocabulary rather
than copying it); fleet-health signals publish with a stable machine shape and a negative control
per refused shape (a stale beat must publish *stale*, never *healthy*); `module.json` declares the
monitoring integration and the repo carries a declared observability surface with a gate asserting
both; a direction issue naming this repo as a consumer exists on the vendor board and its URL is
recorded here; every new gate is mutation-proven, wired into `make verify`, and `make verify` is
green on a **clean checkout** of the merge commit.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-monitoring-declaration.sh
python3 -m pytest telemetry/observability/tests telemetry/budgets/tests
make verify
```

## Provenance (GR-10)

Vendor repos read via `gh api` / `gh issue list` 2026-09-14: `kushin77/monitoring-stack` (Python,
MIT, `main`, the module), `kushin77/infrastructure-monitoring` (Python, no license, `master`,
decommissioning), `kushin77/monitoring-agent` (empty, CMR `R57`/`AA25` skip).
CMR declarations read 2026-09-14: `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/shared-services/module.json:52`
(`prometheus` integration, `observability` capability), `vendor/CMR/catalog/mandatory.tsv`
(three rows; monitoring absent), `vendor/CMR/canibalization/registry.csv` row `R35`
(*"monitoring-stack + infrastructure-monitoring → metric/alert shapes, observability patterns"*,
P2/candidate/EPIC-07/CMR-701/702), `vendor/CMR/channels/inbox.tsv` (no monitoring register).
Direction issue filed on the vendor board: https://github.com/kushin77/monitoring-stack/issues/200

items.title: A single 14.8 GB scratch log filled this machine's tmpfs (100%) — add the scratch-space guard + codify the driver discipline
items.body:
## What happened

On **2026-09-14** a single agent-written file filled this machine's `/tmp`:

| Measured | Value |
|---|---|
| `/tmp/ao412.makeverify.log` (peak) | **14,837,231,616 bytes ≈ 14.8 GB** |
| tmpfs total / used | 16 GB / **16 GB (100 %)** |
| `/` free at the same moment | 72 GB (the space existed; it was in the wrong place) |
| My own artifacts in `/tmp` that session | ~500 KB |

`/tmp` on this box is **tmpfs** — RAM. A full tmpfs is not "a full disk": it is a
hard stop for **every** parallel lane at once, and it is not recoverable by
compacting. The failure was invisible until something unrelated broke.

## The mechanism (two lines in a scratch driver)

```bash
L=/tmp/ao412.makeverify.log
: > "$L"
env -C "$W" make verify >> "$L" 2>&1
tail -6 "$L" >> "$L"          # <-- self-referential append
```

- **Unbounded capture** — the whole gate log appended, with no size cap anywhere.
- **Self-referential append** — `tail -6 "$L" >> "$L"` reads and writes the *same*
  file. It cannot converge under repetition, and combined with a re-run loop it is
  guaranteed growth. This is a **logic bug**, not a style nit.

The same unbounded-`>> "$L"` pattern is present in **three** sibling scratch drivers
still on the box (`/tmp/ao401.makeverify.sh`, `/tmp/ao401.mv.sh`, `/tmp/ao412.mv.sh`),
so this is a *class* of defect, not one accident.

## Why it was not caught

Nothing was watching. Detection depended on a human noticing a full disk — the same
"governance that depends on someone remembering is not governance" failure the
`laptop-manage` toolkit already names for editor state. **This repo's tracked tooling
is clean** (`grep` over `scripts/` and `Makefile` finds no such pattern) — the defect
lives entirely in *agent scratch scripts*, which nothing lints.

## What was fixed (done, with evidence)

A machine-level guard was written, installed, and put on a timer — outside any fleet
repo (`~/laptop-manage`, the machine-governance toolkit), so it needs no lane and
protects every repo at once:

| Capability | Mode |
|---|---|
| tmpfs/inode ceiling, single-file size cap, registered `/tmp` worktrees | `--check` (default, read-only, **0.031 s**) |
| runaway-pattern lint (self-append = FAIL, unbounded capture = NOTE) | `--lint <dir>` |
| deleted-but-open space holders (the invisible case) | `--deep` |
| reclaim abandoned agent scratch, **allowlist + liveness proven** | `--reap [--apply]` (**0.15 s**) |
| prove every detector fires and no false positives | `--self-test` |

Timer: `scratch-guard.timer`, 2 min after boot then **every 15 min**, `SuccessExitStatus=0 1`
(a reported condition is not a failed unit; only *cannot-assess* is). Log is
**self-trimming** to 200 lines — a detector for unbounded logs must not create one.

**Measured now:** tmpfs **1.3 GB / 16 GB (9 %)**, the 14.8 GB log removed, no live writer
(only two read-only `grep`s held the inode, both gone).

## The finding that matters most (a near-miss worth recording)

The first cut of `--reap` used an **age-only** rule and offered
**`/tmp/.X11-unix`** and other lanes' live `mktemp` directories for deletion.
Measured: `/tmp` held **4,523 top-level entries and only 80 matched `ao*`**. So the
rule is now: *reap only what is recognisably agent scratch*
(`SG_REAP_PATTERN`, default `ao*`), never remove a dot-entry, and **report** the rest.
`--self-test` carries that exact case as a regression control.
**A cleanup tool whose default is "anything old" is a data-loss incident waiting for
a busy afternoon.**

## What remains (this issue)

1. **Adopt the guard.** It lives in `~/laptop-manage` and is not referenced anywhere
   in this repo. Decide whether the fleet's agents are expected to run
   `scratch-guard --check` (and where that is documented for agents).
2. **Codify the scratch-driver discipline** in the agent-facing surface
   (`AGENTS.md` / the fleet runbook / a `docs/` pattern note), because the fix that
   *prevents* the incident is the discipline, not the detector:
   - never read and write the same log file in one command;
   - every appended capture gets a **cap** (`head -c` / `tail -c` / a bound);
   - a file count of 1 is not "small" on tmpfs;
   - **worktrees on disk, not `/tmp`** — see the sibling fleet hazard tracked on the
     vendor board as `kushin77/code-indexing#158` / `#159` (this box currently has
     **23 registered git worktrees under `/tmp`**).
3. **Consider a gate** for the repo's own tooling if the discipline is to be
   mechanical here (the `--lint` logic is already written and mutation-proven via
   `--self-test`).

## Verify

```bash
scratch-guard --self-test          # every detector fires; no false positives
scratch-guard --check              # verdict (0 healthy / 1 condition / 2 cannot-assess)
scratch-guard --lint "$TMPDIR"     # flag runaway driver patterns
systemctl --user list-timers scratch-guard.timer
```

## Provenance (GR-10)

Guard: `~/laptop-manage/bin/scratch-guard` (+ `config/systemd/scratch-guard.{service,timer}`,
wired through `install.sh`), written 2026-09-14 in response to the measurement above.
The "never guess" reaping rule and the exit-code convention are inherited from the
toolkit's existing `vscode-hygiene` / `machine-awareness` pattern.
Related: `kushin77/code-indexing#158` / `#159` (worktrees on tmpfs on this workstation).

items.title: Enforce the codeidx capability register — a gate that fails by name on an unowned or unreferenced row
items.body:
Parent: #473
Blocked-by: #478

## Objective

Make the register binding rather than advisory: a rule that lives only in a doc is a suggestion
(GR-29); a gate that fails by name is a policy.

## Lane owns

- `scripts/check-codeidx-capability-register.sh`

## Acceptance

The gate fails **by name** on each of:

1. a row with **no owner** (blank or unknown — must be `kushin77/code-indexing`/`us`/`both`);
2. a row with **no acceptance** criterion;
3. a row whose `ref` is neither the literal `GAP` nor a real issue **URL**;
4. a row marked `shipped` that cites **no completion signal**;
5. a row marked `gap` with **no filed direction issue** recorded;
6. a capability named in the consumption EPIC (#472) that is **absent** from the register.

Plus: exit contract `0`/`1`/`2`; offline and deterministic; `bash -n` clean; **internal negative
controls** constructing each of the six violations and requiring rc 1 **with the offending row
named**; and a mutation proof of the exact assertion anchor with a sha256-verified byte-identical
restore.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-codeidx-capability-register.sh
bash -n scripts/check-codeidx-capability-register.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- Wiring into `make verify` is the designated wiring lane's (#420 / #466) — one writer per wave.
- **Do not use `mktemp -d …XXXXXX`**: this repo's own unfinished-marker scan greps code files for

items.title: The code-indexing capability register — what "fully capable" means, grounded against the vendor board
items.body:
Parent: #473

## Objective

Write the capability register that says, per capability, what the fleet needs from the code-indexing
module and how we know we have it — grounded row by row against the vendor's own board, **not** a
wish list.

## Lane owns

- `docs/CODEIDX-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md`

## Required row shape (every row, no exceptions)

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `capability` | what the fleet needs, one line |
| `needed-for` | `decision-making` \| `task-completion` \| `futureproofing` (one or more) |
| `owner` | `kushin77/code-indexing` \| `us` \| `both` — never blank |
| `ref` | a real vendor issue URL (a closed issue needs a **completion-signal** citation) or the literal `GAP` |
| `status` | `shipped` \| `in-flight` \| `gap` \| `UNVERIFIED` |
| `acceptance` | a criterion that **can fail**, phrased as an observable |
| `verify` | the command that checks it |

## Acceptance

- Every capability the consumption EPIC relies on appears — including the two that are currently
  **absent**: the MCP tool contract and per-repo freshness.
- **No capability is marked `shipped` on the strength of a closed vendor issue alone**; without a
  cited completion signal the row is `UNVERIFIED`, and saying so is the point of the row.
- The three direction issues this EPIC files are recorded with their URLs and the row each answers.
- Rows cite the *measured* facts (the module manifest's 13 features; the vendor board read
  2026-09-14: 121 issues, the ENH-IDX register), each with the path or URL it came from.
- All bare `#N` refs are stated to be the **vendor board's** — the two boards' numbers collide, and
  the doc must say so explicitly.
- No unfinished markers; passes `scripts/check-docs.sh`.

## Verify

```bash
test -f docs/CODEIDX-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md
bash scripts/check-docs.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- Mirror the sibling diagrams register's structure (`docs/DIAGRAMS-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md`, #467) so
  the two read as one program; do not fork its gate, reuse the pattern.

items.title: Consume a pre-fetched codeidx context-pack in assemble_prefix — collapse the re-derived static prefix
items.body:
Parent: #472
Blocked-by: #474

## Objective

Close `kushin77/code-indexing#130` **here**: make `assemble_prefix` accept and place a pre-fetched
`codeidx` context-pack so the two static regions collapse into **one** shared, cacheable prefix per
tenant/repo — instead of two independently-generated "static-first" blocks whose bytes differ and
therefore share no provider cache entry.

The vendor's own suggested pickup (verbatim intent): *have `assemble_prefix` accept and place a
pre-fetched code-indexing context-pack as (or ahead of) the locally-derived memory block.*

## Lane owns

- `engine/memory/prompt_cache.py`
- `engine/memory/tests/` (+ fixtures)
- `scripts/check-context-pack-consumption.sh`

## Acceptance

- `assemble_prefix` (`engine/memory/prompt_cache.py:237`) accepts an **optional pre-fetched pack** and
  places it as, or ahead of, the locally-derived memory block — keeping the static-first /
  delta-last invariant intact and provable.
- **Absent pack ⇒ today's behaviour, byte-identical.** The change is additive: with no pack the
  output must be exactly what it is now (asserted against a recorded pre-change vector), because a
  silent change to the injected prefix would invalidate every existing cache entry.
- The pack is consumed **as bytes from the published contract**, never re-derived; the
  `codeidx.context-pack/v1` shape comes from the vendor's contract (`kushin77/code-indexing#128`),
  not from a local guess. If that contract has not landed, this lane ships the **seam + fixture**
  and records the row `UNVERIFIED` rather than inventing a shape.
- **Determinism preserved**: the injected block stays a pure function of the logical memory set —
  no run timestamp, no ordering nondeterminism, no env-dependent bytes — and a test proves two
  assemblies are byte-identical.
- Negative controls, each shown to fail by name: a pack whose declared `schema` version is unknown;
  a pack containing a dynamic token (a run id / timestamp) that must be rejected by the existing
  anti-pattern list; a malformed pack; and the empty-pack case.
- Mutation-proven with a sha256-identical restore.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-context-pack-consumption.sh
python3 -m pytest engine/memory/tests
make verify
```

## Notes

- **Vendor dependency, named in prose on purpose:** the published contract is
  `kushin77/code-indexing#128` (OPEN). A bare `#128` here would resolve to *this* board's #128 — the
  numbers collide, so it must never be written as a `Blocked-by:` marker.
- The existing provenance comments in this file stay; the harvest was correct. Add a line recording
  that the module is now a **consumer** of the contract as well as an adapter of the pattern.

## Objective

Close `kushin77/code-indexing#129` **here**, where it belongs: give the gateway a **real backend
option** that proxies to the actual indexer, instead of only ever querying a declared fake graph.

The vendor's own suggested pickup (verbatim intent): *add a real backend option to `KbRegistry` that
proxies to code-indexing's actual MCP server (stdio or the eventual gateway wiring) for tenants that
have opted in, falling back to the declared fake graph only where no real index exists — gated the
same way the rest of the gateway is flag-gated OFF by default.*

- `gateway/mcp/kb.py` (the backend seam + `KbRegistry`)
- `gateway/mcp/tests/` (+ fixtures)
- `scripts/check-codeidx-backend.sh`

## Acceptance

- A **real backend** implements the same protocol as the declared graph, so every declared tool
  (`definitions` / `references` / `search` / `query` / `freshness`) is served from it unchanged —
  the *tool contract* is not redefined, only backed differently (ADR-0018's rule).
- It is **flag-gated OFF by default**, per the vendor's pickup and GR-5; the declared path stays the
  default until an operator opts a tenant in.
- **Fallback is explicit, never silent.** A caller can tell whether an answer came from the real
  index, the declared graph, or a fallback — and the existing `FIDELITY_NOTE` is made *accurate per
  path* rather than a blanket "fake index" claim (today it would mislabel a real answer).

  no test or gate needs the network or a running indexer; the live path is never exercised by
  `make verify`.
- Negative controls, each *shown* refused and naming the field: an unknown tool `-32601`; a
  malformed envelope; a tenant that exists only in another tenant's index (no cross-tenant
  fallback); an indexer that is unreachable (must degrade to the declared path **and say so**, not
  invent results); `authorized=false`.
- Mutation-proven: break the exact assertion anchor, show rc 1 with the fault named, restore and
  prove sha256-identical.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-codeidx-backend.sh
python3 -m pytest gateway/mcp/tests
make verify
```

items.title: Decision: the two-index authority split + the no-re-derivation rule (ADR-0017)
items.body:
Parent: #472

## Objective

Decide, before any code, **which index answers which question** and freeze the rule that makes the
re-derivation stop recurring — as **ADR-0017**.

## The decision required

This repo carries **three** index-shaped surfaces and no record of their relationship:

1. `governance/knowledge/` — this repo's **institutional knowledge** catalogue (kinds:
   golden-rules, governance, architecture, adr, policy, pattern-template, issue-metadata, lessons,
   rca). Documents and decisions. Ours.
2. `gateway/mcp/kb.py` — a **declared, in-memory fake symbol graph**, per tenant, whose tool shapes
   were harvested from `codeidx/mcp_server.py` (`FIDELITY_NOTE` says so on every result).
3. `kushin77/code-indexing` — the real, compiler-accurate org-wide symbol index. **Not consumed.**

That is how `kushin77/code-indexing#129` and `#130` happened: shapes were harvested (correctly, with
provenance) and then re-implemented, because nothing recorded the difference between *adapting a
pattern* and *depending on a service*.

Decide, with a reason for the rejected option:

- **The authority split** — which surface owns *institutional facts* (ours), which owns *code facts*
  (theirs), and the explicit statement that neither decides anything.
- **The gateway's posture** — is the declared in-memory graph (a) **retired**, (b) kept as the
  **offline fixture** for tests/gates (legitimate *if* it is contract-faithful and labelled), or
  (c) kept as the **fallback** where no real index exists (the vendor's own pickup suggests this)?
  State what a consumer sees in each case, and how a caller can tell which one it got.
- **The no-re-derivation rule** — the frozen, citable rule: a shape that exists in a published
  contract is *consumed*, never mirrored; provenance in `docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md` records where an
  idea came from, and is never a licence to re-implement it.
- **The freshness question** — a consumer that cannot tell whether the index is current for *this*
  repo cannot gate on it (this is directional to the vendor, ``kushin77/code-indexing#162``; state how we behave until
  it lands).

## Lane owns

- `docs/decision-records/ADR-0017-codeidx-consumption-and-index-authority.md`
- `docs/decision-records/README.md` (one row)
- `docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md` (a **pointer line** only — the harvest entries themselves are untouched;
  they stay accurate)

## Acceptance

- ADR-0017 states the three-surface authority split, the gateway posture with the rejected
  alternative, the no-re-derivation rule, and the honest freshness position — each citing the file
  it rests on (the `gateway/mcp/kb.py` docstring, the `engine/memory/prompt_cache.py` docstring,
  the catalog manifest) by path.
- The ADR is indexed in the README table and carries the repo's ADR front-matter shape.
- It does **not** weaken `docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md`'s existing provenance entries or `#120`'s record;
  it explains why a closed EPIC's namesake acceptance criterion did not hold.
- `make verify` green.

## Verify

```bash
test -f docs/decision-records/ADR-0017-codeidx-consumption-and-index-authority.md
grep -q "ADR-0017" docs/decision-records/README.md
make verify
```

## Notes

- Highest ADR on `origin/master` is **ADR-0015**; the sibling diagrams lane takes **ADR-0016**
  (#463). If that lane has already landed, this is 0017; if the two land in the same wave they must
  not both take 0016 — coordinate by the README table.
- The re-derivation is *already recorded* as correct provenance. The finding is not "someone did it
  wrong"; it is "nothing recorded the difference between harvesting and depending".

items.title: EPIC: code-indexing capability for the fleet — the capability register, the vendor direction set, and our consumer half
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
## Objective

Make `kushin77/code-indexing` **fully capable for the fleet's needs** — *where is X / who references
Y* answered from a live, cache-shared index that drives decisions and completes tasks — and
**futureproof**: every capability we depend on is either (a) shipped upstream and *cited*, (b) in
flight upstream and *tracked to a completion signal*, or (c) a **named gap** with a direction issue
on the vendor's board. No capability we rely on may be an assumption.

Deliberately **separate from the consumption EPIC** (#472): that one consumes the index *as it is
today*; this one changes *what it can be*. Different owners (us vs `kushin77/code-indexing`),
different lanes, different completion semantics — conflating them makes "done" hostage to the
vendor's roadmap.

## Milestone

**Unmilestoned by design** — the owner places it (proposed: one program milestone covering the
mandatory-module adoption work, holding the sibling diagrams epics #461/#462 too). `code-indexing` is
a GR-18 **mandatory module**, not a peer, so it does not belong in M28's peer register.

> **All bare `#N` refs in this EPIC are issues on `kushin77/code-indexing`** unless prefixed. The two
> boards' numbers collide — never write a vendor ref as a `Blocked-by:` marker.

## The honest starting position (measured 2026-09-14)

This is the **most mature** vendor surface this repo consumes, and its own board already carries the
CMR-issued enhancement register (`CMR:ENH-IDX-001..008` = vendor `#104`–`#111`, `ENH-IDX-009..012` =
`#126`–`#129`/`#132`, `ENH-IDX-SSOT-001` = `#134`). Most are **still open**, which is the point:
"fully capable" here is not "add features", it is **finish the contract half**.

| Vendor ref | Capability | State |
|---|---|---|
| `#104` | `ENH-IDX-001` — wire the L1 cache into the MCP query path | open |
| `#106` | `ENH-IDX-003` — per-repo pre-indexed context packs for dispatch frontloading | open |
| `#107` | `ENH-IDX-004` — cache-hit telemetry export for cost-report ingestion | open |
| `#108` | `ENH-IDX-005` — per-agent / per-SME query cost metering through the gateway ledger | open |
| `#111` | `ENH-IDX-008` — declare prompt-cache features in the module + GDC manifests | open |
| `#128` | `ENH-IDX-011` — publish a **stable consumption contract** for `codeidx.context-pack` | open |
| `#132` | `ENH-IDX-012` — publish the **measurement artifact** behind DR-069's cited baselines | open |
| `#134` | `ENH-IDX-SSOT-001` — declare code-indexing in the diagrams SSOT | open |
| `#126`/`#127` | `ENH-IDX-009`/`-010` — reconcile / define the publish path for `codeidx.cache-report/v1` | open |
| `#129`/`#130` | cross-repo lessons that **name this repo** — re-implemented tool shapes, re-derived discipline | open |
| `#118`–`#125` | their own QA block (testing-suite adoption, coverage, mutation, property-based, flaky, chaos, perf-regression) | open |
| `#147` | mcp/lsprotocol incompatibility skips 3 test modules | open |

So this EPIC is a **gap analysis against the vendor's own board**, not a wish list. **An open vendor
issue is not a shipped capability, and a closed one is not evidence either** — the register records
the completion signal that proves it, or the row is `UNVERIFIED`.

## Children

| Child | Issue | What it closes |
|---|---|---|
| **The capability register** — `docs/CODEIDX-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md`, grounded row by row against the vendor board | #478 | what "fully capable" means; no invented capability, no unowned row |
| **The direction set's completion tracker** — vendor issue state → the register's status column | #479 | drift between the register and the vendor's board |
| **Enforce the register** — a gate that fails by name on an unowned / unreferenced / unverified row | #480 | GR-29: a doc-only rule is advisory; only a gate binds |

Chain edges: `#478` → (`#479`, `#480`).

## Direction issues filed on the vendor board (2026-09-14)

| Direction | Vendor issue | The gap it names |
|---|---|---|
| Publish the **MCP tool contract + a recorded fixture**, not only the context-pack doc | `kushin77/code-indexing#161` | the root cause of `#129` — with no citable tool contract, a consumer mirrors shapes and drifts |
| **Per-repo freshness as a machine-readable contract**, plus an exit-code query mode | `kushin77/code-indexing#162` | you cannot gate "this task is done" on an index whose currency for a given repo is unknowable |
| **Cross-repo query semantics + a resolvability tri-state** | `kushin77/code-indexing#163` | one artifact covers 6 languages and `lang-shell` references are *unresolvable* — a consumer cannot tell "no references" from "references not resolvable", a **false absence** that silently produces wrong decisions |

## What this EPIC will NOT do

- **No vendor code from here** (NG4/NG6); nothing under `kushin77/code-indexing` is edited.
- **No capability invented on the vendor's behalf** — a row without a ref or a filed direction is `GAP`.
- **No LLM / embedding / fuzzy re-ranking** added on our side; the module's value is reproducibility.
- **No build-file edits** — gate wiring belongs to the designated wiring lane (#420 / #466).

## Definition of done

Every capability row has an owner, a falsifiable acceptance, and either a vendor ref with a
completion signal or a filed direction issue; the register is enforced by a mutation-proven gate; and
the consumption EPIC (#472) depends on **nothing** here to be done — only to be better.

## Verify

```bash
test -f docs/CODEIDX-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md
bash scripts/check-codeidx-capability-register.sh
make verify
```

## Provenance (GR-10)

`kushin77/code-indexing` — CMR catalog manifest `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/code-indexing/module.json`
(`mandatory: true`, 13 features, `lsp` default **off**), read 2026-09-14. Vendor board read via REST
2026-09-14 (121 issues), including the ENH-IDX register and `#160` (institutional enhancements +
north-star alignment, which records this repo as orthogonal to the ERP-CRM bound set).

items.title: EPIC: Consume the canonical codeidx index — the org-wide symbol SSOT on the agent surface, closing the two cross-repo lessons this repo was sent
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
## Objective

Consume `kushin77/code-indexing` — the fleet's compiler-accurate, no-LLM symbol index and CMR's
**first GR-18 mandatory module** (the GR-17 pairing) — as the org-wide **code-location** SSOT on the
agent surface, instead of re-deriving its shapes locally. This repo already has the *relationship*;
what it does not have is the *dependency*.

## Measured position (2026-09-14, `origin/master` `6ebf926`) — this is not a blank slate

- `gateway/mcp/kb.py` says it itself: *"The compiler-accurate indexing tool shapes (definitions /
  references / search / query / freshness) are re-used from the code-indexing MCP catalog … but this
  gateway does NOT implement a real indexer: each tenant's code/KB is represented as a declared,
  in-memory graph."* `gateway/mcp/README.md` lists `code-indexing codeidx/mcp_server.py` under
  **cannibalization provenance** — a source of tool *shapes*, not a live backend — and its
  `FIDELITY_NOTE` labels every result a per-tenant **fake index**.
- `engine/memory/prompt_cache.py`'s own docstring records the same harvest: the static-first /
  delta-last discipline is *"lifted from `codeidx/docs/prompt-cache.md`"*, and its rejection
  regexes are *"derived from the codeidx anti-pattern table"*.
- **The vendor has already filed both of these at this repo, and nothing on this board tracks
  them.** `kushin77/code-indexing#129` (OPEN) — *"agent-orchestrator's MCP gateway re-implements
  codeidx tool shapes as fake data, never queries the real indexer"*; `kushin77/code-indexing#130`
  (OPEN) — *"engine/memory/prompt_cache.py re-derives the static-first/delta-last discipline instead
  of consuming codeidx context-pack"*. Both state the fix is **this** repo's lane and both carry a
  suggested pickup. Two open cross-repo lessons addressed here and untracked here is the cleanest
  possible statement of the gap.
- **This repo does not carry the GR-17 mandatory consumer surface.** No root `.mcp.json` was found
  (measured: absent), while `code-indexing`'s `mandatory_consumer_assets` are `[".mcp.json",
  "gdc-manifest.yaml"]` and the contract is **no opt-out**. `module.json` declares **no**
  code-indexing integration.
- **A closed EPIC already claimed this.** #120 (*"Fact-accurate code-indexing KB + module health for
  all CMR modules"*, CLOSED) carried as acceptance *"code-indexing is present, healthy, and pinned
  as a mandatory consumer asset"* and *"each CMR repo must declare the KB dependency and version in
  its module manifest"* — while `.mcp.json` is absent and `module.json` declares nothing.
  *All children closed is not the namesake deliverable existing*; read the tree, not the child list.

## The authority boundary (three index-shaped surfaces — this EPIC fixes exactly one)

| Question | Owner | Posture |
|---|---|---|
| *What does the institution state or decide?* | this repo's `governance/knowledge/` catalogue (kinds: golden-rules, governance, architecture, adr, policy, pattern-template, issue-metadata, lessons, rca) | **ours — unchanged** |
| *Where is symbol X, and who references it?* | `kushin77/code-indexing` (SCIP + universal-ctags, one `index.db`, atomic symlink publish) | **consume — this EPIC** |
| *Does the index decide anything?* | nowhere — the index reports **facts** (no LLM, no embeddings, no fuzzy matching; every answer reproducible from compiler output) | **never a decision authority** |

## Children

| Child | Issue | What it closes |
|---|---|---|
| **Decision: the two-index authority split + the no-re-derivation rule** (ADR-0018) | #474 | which index answers which question, the gateway's posture, and the frozen rule *consume the published contract, never re-derive a shape* |
| **Carry the GR-17 mandatory surface** — root `.mcp.json` + a gate asserting it and the pin | #475 | the absent mandatory consumer asset |
| **Converge `gateway/mcp/` on the real backend** — a flag-gated proxy; the declared graph only where no index exists | #476 | `kushin77/code-indexing#129` (the vendor's own suggested pickup) |
| **Collapse the re-derivation in `engine/memory/prompt_cache.py`** — accept a pre-fetched codeidx context-pack | #477 | `kushin77/code-indexing#130` (the vendor's own suggested pickup) |
| **Wire the codeidx surface gates into the gate of record** | #481 | the build files — one writer, serialized behind the sibling wiring lane |

Chain edges: `#474` → (`#476`, `#477`). `#475` is `Blocked-by: #464` — that lane owns the
root `gdc-manifest.yaml`, which already carries the pre-declared `code-indexing.mcp` pin, and two
writers on one file in one wave is the failure this repo keeps re-learning. `#481` is
`Blocked-by: #475, #476, #477, #466`, serialized behind the sibling wiring lane on the same
three build files.

> **A vendor ref is never a `Blocked-by:` marker.** A bare `#128` in this repo's marker grammar means
> *this* repo's issue #128 — the two boards' numbers collide. Vendor dependencies are named in prose,
> deliberately.

## What this EPIC will NOT do

- **No re-implementation, ever.** A shape that exists in `codeidx` is consumed, not mirrored. The
  provenance already recorded in `docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md` is accurate — the *integration* is what
  changes.
- **No vendoring of codeidx code** (GR-10), and nothing under `kushin77/code-indexing` is edited from
  this repo — needs go out as direction issues on that board (NG4/NG6).
- **No LLM / embedding / fuzzy layer.** The module's whole value is that every answer is reproducible
  from compiler output; a re-ranking layer here would destroy the property we are consuming it for.
- **No new always-on service invented here.** The real-backend path ships **flag-gated OFF** (GR-5),
  exactly as the vendor's pickup suggests.

## Definition of done

Both vendor lessons are closed **at the source, by a real dependency**: `gateway/mcp/` can proxy to
the actual indexer for opted-in tenants and falls back to the declared graph only where no index
exists; `assemble_prefix` (`engine/memory/prompt_cache.py:237`) consumes a pre-fetched `codeidx`
context-pack so the two static regions collapse into one shared, cacheable prefix; this repo carries
`.mcp.json` and a gate proves both it and the pin; every new gate is mutation-proven and wired into
`make verify`; green on a **clean checkout** of the merge commit.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-codeidx-surface.sh
python3 -m pytest gateway/mcp/tests engine/memory/tests
make verify
```

## Provenance (GR-10)

`kushin77/code-indexing` — CMR catalog manifest `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/code-indexing/module.json`,
`mandatory: true` (row 1 of `catalog/mandatory.tsv`), `mandatory_consumer_assets:
[".mcp.json","gdc-manifest.yaml"]`, `versions.latest v0.1.0`, direction issue `CMR:ONBOARD-0002`.
Vendor board read via REST 2026-09-14 (121 issues): lessons `#129`/`#130` name this repo, and `#128`
is publishing the `codeidx.context-pack/v1` consumption contract. The harvest provenance already
recorded in this repo (`gateway/mcp/README.md`, the `engine/memory/prompt_cache.py` docstring,
`docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md`) is accurate; this EPIC is about the integration that did not follow it.

items.title: Enforce the diagrams capability register — a gate that fails by name on an unowned or unreferenced row
items.body:
Parent: 462
Blocked-by: #467

## Objective

Make the register binding rather than advisory. A rule that lives only in a doc is a suggestion
(GR-29); a gate that fails by name is a policy.

## Lane owns

- `scripts/check-diagrams-capability-register.sh`

## Acceptance

The gate fails **by name** on each of:

1. a row with **no owner** (blank or unknown — `owner` must be `kushin77/diagrams`/`us`/`both`);
2. a row with **no acceptance** criterion;
3. a row whose `ref` is neither the literal `GAP` nor a real issue **URL**;
4. a row marked `shipped` that cites **no completion signal**;
5. a row marked `gap` with **no filed direction issue** recorded;
6. a capability named in the integration EPIC (#461) that is **absent** from the register.

Plus: exit contract `0`/`1`/`2`; offline and deterministic; `bash -n` clean; **internal negative
controls** that construct each of the six violations and require rc 1 **with the offending row
named**; and a mutation proof of the exact assertion anchor with a sha256-verified byte-identical
restore.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-diagrams-capability-register.sh
bash -n scripts/check-diagrams-capability-register.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- Wiring into `make verify` is the designated wiring lane's (`#420`) — one writer per wave. The
  script is still covered by `check-shell-syntax.sh` in the meantime.
- **Do not use `mktemp -d …XXXXXX`**: this repo's own unfinished-marker scan greps code files for
  `(TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX)\b` and a 6-X template matches it. Use
  `scratch="/tmp/<name>.$(date +%s%N).$"; mkdir "$scratch" || exit 2`.

items.title: Track the diagrams capability direction set to completion — vendor issue state → register status
items.body:
Parent: 462
Blocked-by: #467

## Objective

Keep the register from going stale: a **code-native** tracker that reads each referenced vendor
issue's state and reconciles it with the register's status/ref columns — so a capability cannot
silently drift from `in-flight` to `shipped` (or back to `UNVERIFIED`).

## Lane owns

- `scripts/track-diagrams-capabilities.sh`
- `docs/DIAGRAMS-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md` — the **reconciliation section only** (a table generated
  from the tracker's output). `#467` owns the rest of the file and lands first.

## Acceptance

- The tracker reads the register, extracts every vendor issue URL, and reports each one's state
  (`open`/`closed`) next to the register's declared status — **naming every mismatch**: a row
  claiming `shipped` whose issue is open, and a row claiming `in-flight`/`gap` whose issue is closed
  **with no cited completion signal** (that case is `UNVERIFIED` — a finding, not something to hide).
- **Offline and deterministic**: it accepts a recorded snapshot (a fixture file) so the check runs
  with the network blocked, like the other gates here; the live path is opt-in.
- Exit contract `0` OK / `1` NOT-OK (a named mismatch) / `2` CANNOT-ASSESS (no register, no snapshot),
  and it **fails closed**: an absent register or an unparsable row is rc 2, never OK.
- Mutation-proven: flip one register row's status, show rc 1 with the row named, restore and prove
  byte-identical.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/track-diagrams-capabilities.sh
bash -n scripts/track-diagrams-capabilities.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- **No scheduled automation is added here** — GitHub Actions is disabled fleet-wide (GR-15);
  automation is code-native and run by the ops runner / cron. Wiring a schedule is the ops lane's
  call, not this lane's.
- Do not try to **close** the vendor's issues: they are the vendor's to close under their own
  completion contract.

items.title: The diagrams capability register — what "fully capable" means, grounded against the vendor board
items.body:
Parent: 462

## Objective

Write the capability register that says, per capability, what the fleet needs from the diagrams
module and how we know we have it — grounded row by row against the vendor's own board, **not** a
wish list.

## Lane owns

- `docs/DIAGRAMS-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md`

## Required row shape (every row, no exceptions)

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `capability` | what the fleet needs, one line |
| `needed-for` | `decision-making` \| `task-completion` \| `futureproofing` (one or more) |
| `owner` | `kushin77/diagrams` \| `us` \| `both` — never blank |
| `ref` | a real vendor issue URL (a closed issue needs a **completion-signal** citation, GR-16) or the literal `GAP` |
| `status` | `shipped` \| `in-flight` \| `gap` \| `UNVERIFIED` |
| `acceptance` | a criterion that **can fail**, phrased as an observable |
| `verify` | the command that checks it |

## Acceptance

- Every capability the integration EPIC relies on appears, and **no capability is marked `shipped`
  on the strength of a closed vendor issue alone** — a closed issue without a cited completion
  signal is `UNVERIFIED`, and saying so is the point of the row.
- Rows cite the *measured* facts of this session (features read from
  `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/diagrams/module.json`; the vendor board read 2026-09-14), each with
  the path or URL it came from — no un-cited capability claim.
- The three direction issues this EPIC files are recorded here with their URLs and the row each
  answers.
- No unfinished markers; the doc passes `scripts/check-docs.sh`.

## Verify

```bash
test -f docs/DIAGRAMS-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md
bash scripts/check-docs.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- Follow this repo's `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` as the house pattern for a grounded gap
  analysis — it is the reason this EPIC is an analysis, not a roadmap.
- **All bare `#N` refs in this register are issues on `kushin77/diagrams`** (the vendor board) unless
  the text prefixes them. State that explicitly in the doc.

items.title: Declare this repo's diagrams SSOT membership — architecture.yaml + the gdc-manifest diagrams.blueprint pin + a gate
