items.title: Decision: the diagrams blueprint's authority on the operator surface + the ticket-evidence contract (ADR-0016)
items.body:
Parent: 461

## Objective

Decide — before any code — **where a diagram signal lives on the ticket**, and record it as
**ADR-0016**, so the projection lane implements a frozen contract instead of inventing one.

## The decision required

`docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` §3.1 froze two constraints that collide with the obvious first
implementation:

1. `facets` is a **closed set** — `lessons`, `raid`, `budget`. "An unknown facet fails; a new facet
   is a contract change, not a silent extension."
2. `authority{}` is the **one-writer-per-field** map, and the ticket is a **projection, never
   authority**.

So: is a diagrams signal **structured `evidence[]`** (additive, explicitly *not* authority-tracked
— the cheap, safe option), or a **new `facets.diagrams`** (a contract change that must move
`scripts/check-paperclip-integration.sh` with it, and must name a single writer)?

A second, smaller decision belongs here too: does the blueprint's drift→decide loop need a ticket
**`kind`** (v2's `kind` is also a closed vocabulary), or is a drift finding simply a `task` whose
evidence is the finding?

## Lane owns

- `docs/decision-records/ADR-0016-diagrams-authority-on-the-operator-surface.md`
- `docs/decision-records/README.md` (one row)
- `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` (a **new §7**, additive — §1–§6 untouched)

## Acceptance

- ADR-0016 records **which question the blueprint owns** (ADR-0018's answer, restated for this
  surface, not re-litigated), that the projection is **read-only and one-way**, and the chosen
  evidence-vs-facet shape **with the reason the other was rejected**.
- If a facet is chosen, the ADR names its **single writer** (`kushin77/diagrams`) and the gate
  change it forces; if evidence is chosen, the ADR says so and the adapter lane needs no contract
  move.
- §7 of `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` states the seam shape and **does not contradict** the
  closed-set rule — a new facet is never added by prose.
- The ADR is indexed in the README table, cites its anchors by path, and carries the repo's ADR
  front-matter shape (`id/status/date/deciders/req/supersedes`).
- `make verify` green (docs-lint included).

## Verify

```bash
test -f docs/decision-records/ADR-0016-diagrams-authority-on-the-operator-surface.md
grep -q "ADR-0016" docs/decision-records/README.md
grep -q "^## 7" docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md
make verify
```

## Notes

- Highest ADR on `origin/master` is **ADR-0015** (`docs/decision-records/`) — this is 0016.
- Do **not** soften §3.1's closed set by prose: "a new facet" is a contract change with a gate, not
  a sentence.

items.title: EPIC: Diagrams capability for the fleet — the capability register, the vendor direction set, and our consumer half
items.milestone: M29 - Module adoption & capability (diagrams · code-indexing · monitoring)
items.body:
## Objective

Make `kushin77/diagrams` **fully capable for the fleet's needs** — decision-making and task
completion from the live-state SSOT — and **futureproof**: every capability we depend on is either
(a) already shipped upstream and *cited*, (b) in flight upstream and *tracked to a completion
signal*, or (c) a **named gap** with a direction issue on the vendor's board. No capability we rely
on may be an assumption.

This EPIC is deliberately **separate from the integration EPIC** (#461): the integration consumes
the module *as it is today*; this EPIC changes *what the module can be*. Different owners (us vs
`kushin77/diagrams`), different lanes, different completion semantics — conflating them would make
the integration's "done" hostage to the vendor's roadmap.

## Milestone

**Unmilestoned by design** — the owner places it (proposed: a new `M29 — Diagrams SSOT capability`).
Filed without a milestone so the program call stays with the owner and M27's adoption scope is not
silently inflated.

> **All bare `#N` refs in this EPIC are issues on `kushin77/diagrams`** (the vendor board), not on
> this board, unless the text prefixes them.

## The honest starting position (measured 2026-09-14)

The vendor's board already carries a CMR-issued enhancement register — `CMR:ENH-DIAG-001..008`
(vendor `#368`–`#375`). **Six of the eight are closed**; three touch exactly the surfaces this EPIC
cares about:

| Vendor ref | Capability | State |
|---|---|---|
| `#368` | `CMR:ENH-DIAG-001` · fleet-wide auto-ingest: repo topology → `architecture.yaml` on every governed repo | **OPEN** — the input the integration's declaration lane feeds |
| `#373` | `CMR:ENH-DIAG-006` · architecture-cost attribution + agent-hour-savings telemetry | **OPEN** |
| `#369` | `CMR:ENH-DIAG-002` · blueprint-as-verified-artifact: drift → exit code | closed |
| `#372` | `CMR:ENH-DIAG-005` · cross-reference layer: `cmr-refs` markers on findings + distributed issues | closed |
| `#374` | `CMR:ENH-DIAG-007` · agent-facing blueprint API for SME agents | closed |
| `#375` | `CMR:ENH-DIAG-008` · blueprint diff/PR rendering + drift→direction-issue automation | closed |

So this EPIC is **not a fresh wish list** — it is a **gap analysis against the vendor's own board**,
in the style of this repo's `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-GAP-ANALYSIS.md`: cite what exists, name what does
not, file only the difference. **A closed vendor issue is not evidence of a shipped capability** —
the register records the completion signal (GR-16) that proves it, or marks the row `UNVERIFIED`.

## Children

| Child | Issue | What it closes |
|---|---|---|
| **The capability register** — `docs/DIAGRAMS-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md`, grounded row by row against the vendor board | #467 | what "fully capable" means, with no invented capability and no unowned row |
| **The direction set's completion tracker** — the vendor issues' state → the register's status column | #468 | drift between the register and the vendor's board |
| **Enforce the register** — a gate that fails by name on an unowned, unreferenced or unverified row | #469 | GR-29: a doc-only rule is advisory; only a gate is binding |

Chain edges: `#467` → (`#468`, `#469`).

## Direction issues filed on the vendor board (2026-09-14)

| Direction | Vendor issue | The gap it names |
|---|---|---|
| Carry the **decision** alongside the **state** — supplied/dependency-graph rendering + a decision annotation on nodes and edges | `kushin77/diagrams#513` | the module renders *infra* topology from extraction; a ticket DAG and the decision that authorized a node have no surface |
| A diagram as a **gate artifact** — deterministic offline render + `content_hash` + first-class Mermaid export | `kushin77/diagrams#514` | "always-current + timestamped" is a culture, not a machine-checkable artifact; `generated.content_hash` is shaped but nothing produces it offline |
| A **versioned consumer contract** + published offline fixture + a completion signal on `#368`/`#373` | `kushin77/diagrams#515` | consumers cannot pin a contract or test offline; the two open register items carry no completion signal |

## What this EPIC will NOT do

- **No vendor code from here.** `kushin77/diagrams` is a vendor (NG6: the fleet directs, the vendor
  executes). Nothing under it is edited, vendored or forked from this repo (GR-10); needs go out as
  direction issues on **that** board (NG4).
- **No capability invented on the vendor's behalf** — a row without a vendor ref or a filed
  direction issue is `GAP`, never "assumed".
- **No re-opening ADR-0018.** The blueprint stays the live-state authority; decisions stay ours.
- **No build-file edits** — gate wiring belongs to the designated wiring lane (`#420`).

## Definition of done

Every capability row has an owner, an acceptance criterion that can fail, and either a vendor **ref
with a completion signal** or a **filed direction issue**; the register is enforced by a
mutation-proven gate; the direction set is filed and tracked; and the integration EPIC (#461)
depends on **nothing** here to be "done" — only to be better.

## Verify

```bash
test -f docs/DIAGRAMS-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md
bash scripts/check-diagrams-capability-register.sh
make verify
```

## Provenance (GR-10)

`kushin77/diagrams` — MIT; catalog manifest `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/diagrams/module.json`
(`mandatory: true`, features read 2026-09-14). Vendor board read via REST 2026-09-14: 329 issues,
enhancement register `#368`–`#375`, institutional-enhancements issue `#503` (whose standing rule —
every issue states in one line how it advances the north-star goal or is orthogonal — the three
filed directions below observe).

items.title: EPIC: Diagrams blueprint on the paperclip operator surface — the live-state SSOT drives decisions and task completion
items.body:
## Objective

Make `kushin77/diagrams` (the GR-18 mandatory SSOT architecture-blueprint module) a **first-class,
read-only input to the paperclip operator surface**, so the *live-state* picture — extracted
topology, rendered blueprint, drift Findings — is what decisions are made against and what closes
the tasks those decisions create. It is the missing consumer of the boundary that
`integrations/paperclip/**` already implements: today the surface projects agents, tickets,
heartbeats and budgets, and **nothing about architecture**.

**Measured position (2026-09-14, `origin/master` `6ebf926`):**

- The canonical boundary adapter exists — `integrations/paperclip/{client,mapping,model,cli}.py` +
  `tests/` (fixture transport) — and is **stdlib-only** (no `yaml`, no `jsonschema`; `mapping.py`
  carries its own YAML parser and JSON-Schema subset). The diagrams surface must therefore arrive
  **over the seam**, never as an import.
- **This repo does not declare its diagrams SSOT membership.** `git ls-tree -r --name-only
  origin/master` carries **no** `architecture.yaml`, no `gdc-manifest.yaml`, no `.mcp.json` and no
  `tokens.json` at the root — the GR-18 mandatory consumer surface for `diagrams.blueprint` is
  absent, so the vendor's sync has no input to read here.
- Nothing under `docs/**` or `integrations/**` mentions diagrams/blueprint/topology today — this is
  new scope, not a half-built thing.

## Authority boundary (this is the whole design)

ADR-0018 already split the two questions; this EPIC does not re-open it.

| Question | Owner | This EPIC's posture |
|---|---|---|
| *What is live, today?* | the diagrams blueprint (`ssot-extract` + `blueprint-gen` + `drift-detect`) | **consume, read-only** |
| *What did we decide, and why?* | `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` + `docs/decision-records/` | **never** taken from the blueprint |
| *Who acts?* | the ticket (ADR-0014 — the single join node) | the blueprint supplies **evidence**; the ticket stays the join |

ADR-0018 is explicit that a blueprint drift is a **signal to open an ADR/ticket, never a silent
absorption** — so the projection is one-way: diagram → decision → ticket. Never diagram → write.

## Children

| Child | Issue | What it closes |
|---|---|---|
| **Decision: the blueprint's authority on the operator surface + the ticket-evidence contract** (ADR-0017) | #463 | whether a diagram signal is a ticket `evidence[]` kind or a *new* facet — `facets` is a **closed set** (`lessons`/`raid`/`budget`), so a new facet is a contract change, not a silent extension |
| **Declare this repo's SSOT membership** — `architecture.yaml` + the `gdc-manifest.yaml` `diagrams.blueprint` pin + a gate | #464 | the absent GR-18 consumer surface; the input `kushin77/diagrams#368` is waiting on |
| **The diagrams projection adapter** — `integrations/paperclip/diagrams.py` on the existing transport | #465 | the projection itself (topology / blueprint / Finding → seam shapes) |
| **Wire the diagrams gates into the gate of record** | #466 | `Makefile` / `scripts/verify.sh` / `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` — single writer, behind the sibling wiring lane |

Chain edges: `#463` → `#465`. `#466` is `Blocked-by: #464, #465, #420` (the sibling
wiring lane owns the same three build files — one writer per wave).

## What this EPIC will NOT do

- **No write path.** The blueprint is read-only input; nothing here lets a diagram mutate fleet
  state. `blueprint-engine`'s diagram→Terraform codegen, if ever used, is **PR-only, flag-gated
  OFF, never `terraform apply`** (GR-5) — and is out of scope here.
- **No second authority.** The fleet stays authoritative for dispatch, claims, budgets and audit
  (ADR-0012); the ticket stays the join node (ADR-0014).
- **No vendoring, no forks.** Nothing under `kushin77/diagrams` is copied in (GR-10); the vendor's
  code is never edited from this repo — needs go out as direction issues on that board (NG4/NG6).
- **No renderer of our own.** We consume the module's renderer; we do not build a second one.

## Definition of done

A drift Finding has a stable machine shape and rides a ticket's evidence; this repo declares its
`architecture.yaml` + `diagrams.blueprint` pin and a gate proves the declaration schema-valid **and
pinned**; `integrations/paperclip/diagrams.py` projects the surface offline through the existing
fixture transport with a negative control per refused shape; every new gate is mutation-proven and
wired into `make verify`; the gate is green on a **clean checkout** of the merge commit.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-diagrams-declaration.sh
bash scripts/check-paperclip-diagrams.sh
make verify
```

## Provenance (GR-10)

`kushin77/diagrams` — CMR catalog manifest `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/diagrams/module.json`,
`mandatory: true`, `mandatory_consumer_assets: ["gdc-manifest.yaml","architecture.yaml"]`,
`versions.latest v0.1.0`; features read from that manifest 2026-09-14. The SSOT authority split is
ADR-0018 in `vendor/CMR/docs/decision-records/`. The boundary rule is ADR-0012/ADR-0013 and the
join is ADR-0014 (both this repo's).

items.title: Reconcile the two paperclip boundary modules — paperclip/adapters/** (EPIC #410) vs integrations/paperclip/** (#428)
items.body:
## Context

EPIC #410 landed a paperclip parity-adapter tree at **`paperclip/adapters/{approvals,heartbeat,secrets,skills}/**`** (57 files under `paperclip/`), self-declared in `paperclip/__init__.py`. Meanwhile #428 landed the boundary adapter at **`integrations/paperclip/**`** (`client.py` transport seam + `mapping.py` deterministic mapper + `README.md`).

Two top-level modules now implement the *same boundary* (fleet ↔ paperclip.ing) — the exact half-coupling **ADR-0012** calls the worst outcome ("two authoritative engines"). #448's guard (`scripts/check-paperclip-canonical-module.sh`, now in `make verify`) can only *report* this: it distinguishes the **declared** sibling (printed as `KNOWN`) from an **undeclared/stray** module (refused by name), so `master` stays green while the drift is visible. Deciding the two modules' relationship is an **architecture** call, not a gate tweak — hence this issue.

## Measured state (on `master` at `6ebf926`)

| Module | Files | Declares | Role as written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `integrations/paperclip/**` | 8 | #428 / ADR-0013 | transport seam (`client.py`) + deterministic mapper (`mapping.py`) onto the frozen ticket contract |
| `paperclip/adapters/<family>/**` | 57 | EPIC #410 | one subpackage per upstream capability family: approvals, heartbeat, budget, secrets, routines, skills — "projection, not authority" |

Both claim to be the *derivation* layer over the same frozen seams (`docs/contracts/paperclip/`). Neither owns the other.

## Decision required

Pick one and record it as an ADR (extend **ADR-0012** or a new ADR):

1. **Two layers of one integration** — `integrations/paperclip/` = transport + canonical mapper; `paperclip/adapters/` = per-family projections **over** it. If so: state the *dependency direction* (adapters import the mapper; the mapper must never import an adapter), make `check-paperclip-canonical-module.sh` assert that direction instead of tolerating the sibling, and re-point `paperclip/__init__.py` to name `integrations/paperclip/` as its dependency rather than a peer.
2. **One module** — consolidate `paperclip/adapters/**` under `integrations/paperclip/**` (or vice-versa) in a reconciliation lane; the loser's per-family adapters become subpackages of the winner. No adapter may be duplicated.

## Acceptance

- An ADR records the chosen relationship and the dependency direction (or the consolidation).
- `check-paperclip-canonical-module.sh` asserts the decision — it **fails by name** on a violation, rather than reporting a `KNOWN` sibling.
- A reconciliation lane lands any file moves; `make verify` stays green with the stricter gate.
- Issue bodies for any still-open briefed lane (#412, #413, #415, #418, #447) keep pointing at the single surviving home.

## Outstanding

#448 (merged) delivered the guard + the corrected bodies; the module reconciliation is this issue's scope.

Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#448

items.title: Adapter module already landed at integrations/paperclip/** — re-point the boundary/adapters lanes and gate against a second module
items.body:
Parent: #409

## The finding (measured 2026-09-14)

The paperclip seam adapter **already exists** — and it is not where our lane briefs point.

Commit `9cd5794` — *feat(integrations): paperclip.ing adapter over the HTTP seam — transport-seamed
client, deterministic mapper, offline gate (#428) (#433)* — landed:

| Artefact | What it is |
|---|---|
| `integrations/paperclip/client.py` | a `Transport` protocol + `HttpTransport` (stdlib `urllib.request` only) + `FixtureTransport` (offline); builds `{base}/api/...`, company-scopes the resource families, sends `Authorization: Bearer`, sends `X-Paperclip-Run-Id` on **mutating calls only**, and maps `400/401/403/404/409/422/503` onto typed errors |
| `integrations/paperclip/mapping.py` | stdlib YAML-subset loader + JSON-Schema-subset validator, then a **deterministic** mapper: seeds + persona cards → agents, claims + board snapshot → tickets, the budget rail → costs, rung beats → heartbeats |
| `integrations/paperclip/{model,cli}.py` | `plan` (offline dry-run sync plan), `check` (tri-state conformance), `push` (the network path — implemented, never run by the gate) |
| `scripts/check-paperclip-integration-adapter.sh` | tri-state, **fully offline**, with a self-mutating negative control (dropped required field; closed-vocabulary drift) — wired into `make verify` as `paperclip-adapter` (`scripts/verify.sh:65`) |

So `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` §5's eleven mismatches are **already being resolved** by a
working, gated, offline adapter. That is good news — and it exposes the defect below.

## The collision — this is the finding

The M27 lanes were briefed with paths that **do not exist**:

| Issue | Briefed lane glob | Reality |
|---|---|---|
| #412 | `paperclip/auth/**` | the module is `integrations/paperclip/**` |
| #413 | `paperclip/api/**` | same |
| #414–#419 | `paperclip/adapters/<name>/**` | same |
| #447 | `paperclip/reporting/**` | same |

A lane following any of those briefs would build a **second adapter module beside the real one** —
the duplicate-lane failure this repo has already paid for twice (the `#307`/`#304` cron-manager
collision; the two competing `#284` implementations) — and it is precisely the half-coupling
ADR-0012 forbids: **two adapter implementations for one boundary**.

## Acceptance

- `integrations/paperclip/**` is named **canonical** for the boundary adapter in every briefed lane
  (#412, #413, #414–#419, #447), and each of those lanes becomes an **extension of that module**
  (`integrations/paperclip/<concern>.py` or a subpackage) — never a parallel module.
- The affected issue bodies are corrected (**this issue owns that edit**), so a lane claiming one of
  them cannot miss the convention.
- A **guard exists, not a convention**: a check fails **by name** when a second top-level module for
  the same integration appears (precedent: the refusal style of `check-module-admission.sh`).
- `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` §5 records #428 as the lane resolving the mismatch list, with
  whatever remains open named honestly — so the work-order is not read as unstarted.
- Lanes already briefed with `paperclip/**` are corrected **before** dispatch; no duplicate is
  started while this is open.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-paperclip-integration-adapter.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- This finding is **ours, not a peer's**: the briefs were written before #428 landed. #428 is the
  correct implementation; our lane contract is the stale part.
- Related: #409 (boundary EPIC), #410 (adapters EPIC), #399 (join layer), #422 (peer-module
  integration), #447 (reporting brief — its `paperclip/reporting/**` becomes
  `integrations/paperclip/reporting/**`).

items.title: Reporting agent: the paperclip persona composes each mandatory module's distributable brief
items.milestone: M28 - Peer-module integration (paperclip / hermes / deepseek / ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #422
Blocked-by: #445

## Objective

Make the **paperclip reporting agent** the thing that composes each mandatory module's
**distributable brief** — the organized, per-module statement of *what every repo must carry, at
which pin, and whether it is current*.

This is the correct home for the intent, and it is already the declared architecture: ADR-0012 gave
`paperclip` the **reporting half** of the fleet (hermes owns orchestration), and the persona card
confirms it — *"provider-neutral research and documentation assistant that fetches, summarizes and
stores knowledge with typed output"*, `posture: executor`, `defaultModelTier: LOW`.

**But the capability does not exist yet, and that is the gap.** Measured on
`registry/personas/cards/paperclip.yaml`:

| Declared today | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `capabilitySet: research, docs-authoring, memory-ops` | **no reporting / module-brief capability** — nothing the agent can be dispatched to produce here |
| `toolAllowlist: file_read, web_fetch, search_memory, store_memory` | **no access to the module registry, the board, or the hub catalog** — it cannot read what it must brief |
| `memoryScope: user, repository` | no fleet/module scope, so a module brief has nowhere canonical to live |
| `ownedLanes: paperclip, knowledge` | the brief's lane is undeclared |

So "integrate it into our reporting agent support" is a concrete change: **declare the capability,
grant the read access, and freeze the artifact** — not a new subsystem.

## Lane owns

- `registry/personas/cards/paperclip.yaml`
- `registry/profiles/seeds/paperclip.1.0.0.yaml`
- `paperclip/reporting/**`
- `docs/MODULE-BRIEF.md`
- `scripts/check-module-brief.sh`

## Acceptance

- The persona declares the capability explicitly (e.g. `module-brief` alongside
  `research`/`docs-authoring`) with the **read-only** tool access it needs (module registry, board
  snapshot, hub catalog). A capability that requires a tool the allowlist does not grant fails the
  registry gate — declared and usable must not diverge.
- `docs/MODULE-BRIEF.md` **freezes the artifact**: per module — `id`, owning repo,
  **mandatory status in three honest states** (`registered-mandatory` / `target-pending` /
  `catalog-not-mandatory`), the pin/rev, the **consumer assets** the repo must carry, the seed path
  each asset comes from, health, board ref, and drift.
- The brief composes **only** from #445's registry and the hub files it cites — every claim in a
  brief resolves to a registry row or a cited hub path. A statement that resolves to nothing is a
  **finding naming the line**, not prose (this is `kushin77/deepseek#117`'s lesson: *runnable but
  not truthful* is the failure mode to design against).
- **Pending is never rendered as shipped.** A target-set module without a vendor `module.json`
  appears as `target-pending` with the blocking hub issue named — the two-part-surface discipline
  `docs/MANDATORY-MODULES.md` requires of the hub itself.
- The brief is **deterministic** (two runs over one revision are byte-identical) and the gate is
  **mutation-proven**: a module with no pin, a consumer asset with no seed, and a mandatory module
  reported as satisfied when the registry says pending must each be refused by name.
- The brief, not a copy, is what is distributed alongside the assets: **distribution stays with the
  existing channel** (`controller/standards-sync.sh`, `controller/standards-manifest.txt`,
  `templates/module/` seeds). This lane produces the organized statement; it does not invent a
  second push mechanism and it **vendors nothing** (GR-10 / ADR-0013 / NG4).

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-module-brief.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- Today's brief covers **3 registered mandatory modules** (`code-indexing`, `diagrams`,
  `shared-frontend`) with **3 target-pending** (`pmo`, `shared-governance`, `shared-services`) —
  a brief that cannot represent the difference is not fit for purpose.
- Reporting the brief into the console/PMO surfaces is #403's job; the operator surface is #413.
  This lane owns the **composer and the contract**, not the display.
- The PMO harvest provenance already names `kushin77/paperclip` as a primary reporting source
  (`doc/plans/*.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `FINAL-STATUS-REPORT.md`, `.agents/skills/pr-report/**`) — the
  brief should inherit that shape rather than invent one.

---

**Canonical module (corrected 2026-09-14):** the boundary adapter has **landed** at
`integrations/paperclip/**` — issue #428, PR #433, commit `9cd5794`; gate
`scripts/check-paperclip-integration-adapter.sh`, wired into `make verify` as `paperclip-adapter`.
This lane **extends that module** (`integrations/paperclip/<concern>.py` or a subpackage) — it does
**not** create a parallel one. Read every `paperclip/...` path in the lane contract above as
`integrations/paperclip/...`, and treat a second top-level module for this integration as a defect.
Tracked by #448.


---

> **Correction (#448, 2026-09-14) — canonical module path.**
> The paperclip boundary adapter already landed at **`integrations/paperclip/**`**
> (commit `9cd5794`, issue #428). The `paperclip/<concern>/**` globs in this brief
> (`paperclip/auth/**`, `paperclip/api/**`, `paperclip/reporting/**`,
> `paperclip/adapters/<name>/**`) are **not** a legitimate lane home — read them as
> **extensions of the canonical module**: `integrations/paperclip/<concern>.py` or
> `integrations/paperclip/<concern>/`.
> Guard: `scripts/check-paperclip-canonical-module.sh` (in `make verify`) refuses an
> undeclared second top-level module by name.

items.title: Ecosystem module registry + state federation — one view of every module (mandatory status, pin, health, consumer assets)
items.milestone: M28 - Peer-module integration (paperclip / hermes / deepseek / ollama)
items.body:
Parent: #422
Blocked-by: #423

## Objective

Give the ecosystem **one honest view of every module** — mandatory status, consumer assets, pin,
owning repo, board, health — assembled by **reference from the hub's own registry**, never by
copying module code into any repo.

This is the missing middle between two things that already exist:

- the hub **already** has "what ships where": GR-18 mandatory flags in
  `catalog/modules/<id>/module.json`, the `catalog/mandatory.tsv` registry, the
  `catalog/validate.py` gate, and seeds in `templates/module/` propagated by
  `controller/onboard.sh` / `controller/standards-sync.sh`;
- we are building the **consumers** of that truth: #403 (PMO rollup), #413 (paperclip HTTP
  projection), #427 (peer-board triage).

Nothing today answers *"what is the module set, what is mandatory, what is pending, and what is
drifting?"* in one place. `kushin77/CMR#952` says the same thing at the hub: **portfolio membership
and module membership are not the same set and have drifted** (`#862`: the PMO board carries
100% foreign-repo content).

## Lane owns

- `governance/modules/**`
- `docs/MODULE-REGISTRY.md`
- `scripts/check-module-registry.sh`

## Acceptance

- A generated registry records, per module: `id`, **mandatory status**, `consumer_assets`, pin/rev,
  owning repo, board ref, and a health probe. It is **read from** the hub's
  `catalog/mandatory.tsv` and `catalog/modules/*/module.json` — drift between the two fails the
  gate (mirroring `catalog/validate.py`).
- **Three states, never two:** `registered-mandatory` · `target-pending` (with the blocking hub
  issue named) · `catalog-module-not-mandatory`. A module in the target set that is not yet
  registered is **not** reported as shipped — the honest two-part-surface discipline
  `docs/MANDATORY-MODULES.md` requires.
- **Membership is refused, not inferred:** a repo that is absent from the hub catalog is reported
  `not-a-module` **by name** (the CMR#952 drift guard). A finding about a non-module is not
  membership.
- **No vendoring — gated.** The registry stores **references** (id, repo, pin, path). A gate
  finding fires if a module's *source* is carried in-tree rather than referenced; the only vendor
  path in this repo stays `vendor/CMR` (pinned submodule, read-only).
- **Deterministic + mutation-proven:** two builds over one revision are byte-identical; an
  unregistered-but-mandatory module, a registered module whose consumer asset has no seed, and a
  duplicated module id must each be refused by name.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-module-registry.sh
make verify
```

## Current inventory this registry must reproduce (2026-09-14, measured)

| Set | Members |
|---|---|
| **Registered mandatory (3)** | `code-indexing` (GR-17/GR-18 indexer KB) · `diagrams` (SSOT blueprint) · `shared-frontend` (`--os-` token twin) |
| **Target-pending (3)** | `pmo` (`CMR#435`, `kushin77/pmo#1`) · `shared-governance` (`CMR#264`, ADR-0019 dual-role) · `shared-services` (`CMR#442`, `kushin77/shared-services#4040`) |
| **Catalog modules, not mandatory (3 — corrected 2026-09-14, was 8)** | `erp-crm` · `googleworkspace` · `saas-rbac`. **Correction:** `paperclip`, `hermes-agents` and `ollama` are *not in the hub catalog at all* — measured against `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/` they are `not-a-module`, together with `deepseek`, `gcp-gatekeeper` and `monitoring-stack`. Counting them as catalog modules **was** the CMR#952 drift this registry exists to stop, so the original row described the drift rather than the hub. The delivered registry reports what the hub says (#445, merge `26bff7aa`). |
| **Becoming a module** | `monitoring-stack` — contract + mandatory-set registration is `CMR#765` (MON-005), **not yet a module** |
| **Open admission decision** | `gcp-gatekeeper` — `CMR#734` |
| **Not modules** | the remaining repos in the hub inventory (106 repos total) — repos, not modules |

## Notes

- **Distribution is not this lane's job.** The propagation channel exists (`controller/onboard.sh`,
  `controller/standards-sync.sh`, `controller/standards-manifest.txt`, `templates/module/` seeds).
  This lane answers *what should be distributed and is it current*, not how to push it.
- Bound by NG4: we read peers and the hub; we never write into them. A need becomes a direction
  issue on their board.

items.title: P0: Paperclip.ing integration adapter — the ai.purebliss.app serving layer via paperclip (ADR-0013), EPIC #338
items.body:
Parent: #338

## GOAL

Implement ADR-0013's decision — **adopt paperclip.ing as the operator surface, driven as a
process-boundary client over its HTTP API** — as a real, gated adapter in this repo. This is
EPIC #338's live-data bridge delivered **via paperclip** instead of a from-scratch HTTP serving
layer plus a hand-built dashboard. Success = the adapter exists, maps our state into
paperclip.ing's shapes deterministically, is offline-testable, and a gate wired into `make verify`
fails when the mapping or the contract drifts.

## Constraints

- **No network in the gate.** The upstream HTTP client must sit behind a transport seam with a
  fixture so the gate and tests are offline (GR-15: no GitHub Actions; the gate runs from cron/make).
- **Do not re-open the decision.** ADR-0013 chose CLI-adopt-over-HTTP; this issue implements it.
- `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` §5 (the 11-item MISMATCH list) is the work-order — each
  mismatch you resolve must be marked resolved in the doc; unresolved ones stay listed.
- Do not edit `governance/board/`, `governance/dispatch/`, `gateway/catalog/`, `registry/**`, or
  `docs/README.md` — sibling lanes own those.

## Context

- ADR-0013: `docs/decision-records/ADR-0013-paperclip-ing-integration.md` (accepted; adopt the CLI).
- Seam spec + mismatch list: `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md`; schemas in
  `docs/contracts/paperclip/{heartbeat,ticket,budget}.schema.json`.
- Upstream surface: prefix `/api`; company-scoped `/api/companies/{companyId}/...`;
  `GET /api/health`; `GET /api/openapi.json`; agent auth `Authorization: Bearer <agent-key-or-jwt>`;
  board auth session cookie or `Bearer <board-token>`; mutating requests during a run carry
  `X-Paperclip-Run-Id`. Resources: companies, agents, issues, approvals, goals-and-projects,
  costs, secrets, activity, dashboard, routines. Errors 400/401/403/404/409/422/503.
- Fleet state to map: `registry/profiles/seeds/*.yaml` + `registry/personas/cards/*.yaml`
  (agents), `gateway/finops/` + `telemetry/budgets/` + `telemetry/metering/` (costs),
  `telemetry/observability/` (health/activity), `guardrails/policy/controls.yaml` (approvals).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `integrations/paperclip/` exists with a transport-seamed client (`client.py`), a deterministic
      mapper (`mapping.py`) and a CLI (`cli.py`), plus tests that run **offline**
- [ ] the mapper reproduces the closed vocabularies and required fields of the three seam schemas
      (`heartbeat`, `ticket`, `budget`) — asserted by the gate
- [ ] `scripts/check-paperclip-integration-adapter.sh` is wired into `make verify`, is tri-state
      (0 OK / 1 NOT-OK / 2 CANNOT-ASSESS) and is **mutation-proven** (a drifted mapping is refused)
- [ ] the MISMATCH list in `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` is updated: each resolution marked,
      each deferral still named
- [ ] `make verify` PASS, quoted from `.verify/attestation.json`

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-paperclip-integration-adapter.sh
make verify
```

Refs: EPIC #338, ADR-0013, `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md`, EPIC #359.

items.title: Bidirectional sync owner — a scheduled peer-board triage that files direction issues with provenance
items.milestone: M28 - Peer-module integration (paperclip / hermes / deepseek / ollama)
items.body:
Parent: 422

## Objective

Give cross-repo sync an **owner and a machine surface**, so "the peers' boards point at us" is a
scheduled, evidence-producing pass rather than something rediscovered when a lane happens to look.

This re-files #181's gap register items 9 and 10 — *"a standing lane that reviews their boards each
wave and files direction issues"* and *"their enhancements enter our waves only via reviewed
direction/harvest issues with provenance; no silent adoption"* — because #181 closed without leaving
a standing mechanism. `kushin77/CMR#865` names the same hole one level up: board sync is
one-directional (spoke → CMR) with no path back down; `kushin77/CMR#867` notes the sync script has
no unattended trigger; `kushin77/CMR#864` says a fully-built board-sync was never wired.

## Lane owns

- `governance/sync/**`
- `docs/CROSS-REPO-SYNC-OWNER.md`
- `scripts/check-cross-repo-sync.sh`

## Acceptance

- A **code-native pass** (no GitHub Actions — GR-15) produces a report of, per peer repo:
  issues opened/closed since the last pass, any that name us, and any that map onto a lane we own
  but have **no** corresponding issue here. Cron owns the schedule; the pass is deterministic given
  a pinned board snapshot.
- The report distinguishes the three dispositions explicitly: **track here** (we own the half),
  **direction issue on their board** (they own it — NG4), **no action** (with a reason). An item
  with **no disposition** fails the gate rather than defaulting to silence.
- **Provenance is mandatory** (`#181` gap 10): anything adopted from a peer enters with repo, issue
  and SHA recorded; a peer artifact with no provenance fails.
- **No silent adoption and no silent close:** the gate refuses a run that would close a peer issue
  from here (cross-repo `Closes` is not used) and reports any peer issue referenced without a link
  back to the issue that consumes it.
- The pass is **dirt-cheap by construction** — one API read per peer, cached, with the report
  written to a file, not streamed into the shared shell.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-cross-repo-sync.sh
make verify
```

## Related

- #403 (PMO rollup — the local consumer of the report)
- #399 (the join layer: the report is another projection over the same truth)
- `docs/CROSS-REPO-EXECUTION-BOUNDARY.md` (the NG4 boundary + direction channel this pass must obey)
- #181 (closed — its gap register items 9/10 named this; cite it for continuity)
- `kushin77/CMR#865`, `#867`, `#864`, `#862`; `kushin77/deepseek#53`

items.title: Routing seam: a reusable tier-routing package vs gateway/sme-routing — one authority (ADR-0015)
items.milestone: M28 - Peer-module integration (paperclip / hermes / deepseek / ollama)
items.body:
Parent: 422

## Objective

Decide the seam between a **reusable tier-routing package** and our routing authority, before
`kushin77/hermes-agents#2` ("[assimilation] Extract the tier-routing brain as a standalone reusable
package") produces a second engine that we then quietly consume.

ADR-0012 already fixed the rule for exactly this class of decision — **map the policy, do not couple
the runtime**, with one authoritative engine, the `RoutingPolicy` seam, and *half-coupling* (two
authoritative routing engines) named as the **worst** outcome and the thing that makes a migration
unrunnable. This issue applies that rule to the peer's artifact.

## Lane owns

- `docs/decision-records/ADR-0015-*.md`
- `docs/decision-records/README.md`
- `docs/contracts/routing/**`
- `scripts/check-routing-seam.sh`

## Acceptance

- An ADR records the decision with the **three-fact test** ADR-0012 established (availability /
  dependency / ownership) and answers: is the extracted package a **library we consume**, a
  **policy source we map**, or **not adopted**? Each answer has a consequence section, and "consume
  the runtime" is either chosen explicitly or rejected explicitly.
- The routing **contract** is frozen in `docs/contracts/routing/`: the inputs (task type,
  complexity, capability, tier), the outputs (tier, model, escalation), and which side owns each —
  one writer per field, the same rule as the ticket contract.
- The gate is mutation-proven: a routing decision with **two** declared producers, and a policy
  field with **no** producer, must each be refused by name.
- The **existing local authority is respected**: `gateway/sme-routing/` owns routing here today, so
  this lane writes **no** file under it — the seam is declared in the ADR and the contract, and any
  change to the router is a separate issue on that lane.
- `kushin77/hermes-agents#2` is addressed by a **comment/direction issue on their board** (NG4), not
  by us editing or forking their package.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-routing-seam.sh
make verify
```

## Related

- ADR-0012 (`docs/decision-records/ADR-0012-hermes-paperclip-boundary.md`) — the rule this applies
- #337 (hermes/ollama team pins are unreachable — no routed task requires their capability: the
  symptom of the missing seam)
- #349 (gateway provider catalog completeness + parity gate)
- `kushin77/hermes-agents#2`, `#3`; `kushin77/deepseek#91`, `#90`, `#89`, `#88`, `#54`

items.title: Metering/budget schema parity across the boundary — one receipt shape before ours is frozen
items.milestone: M28 - Peer-module integration (paperclip / hermes / deepseek / ollama)
items.body:
Parent: 422
Blocked-by: 415

## Objective

Freeze **one** metering/budget schema across the boundary before our budget adapter ships its
receipt shape, so we do not create a third variant.

`kushin77/deepseek` is building the same thing we are, independently and openly:
`#55` (align telemetry export with the fleet's metering schema), `#71` (back the cost claim with
this repo's own metering), `#29` (budget enforcement promotion path, end to end), `#30` (expose
usage and cost through CLI and MCP), `#115` (attribution has the record shape but not the producer
seam). `kushin77/ollama#199` (token-budget enforcement at the context window) is a third producer.

## Lane owns

- `docs/contracts/metering/**`
- `scripts/check-metering-parity.sh`

## Acceptance

- A single **record shape** is documented and gated: identity (which agent/tenant/run), the measured
  quantity (tokens, cost, currency), the **receipt** that ties it to a ticket, and the attribution
  fields — with the field names our `telemetry/metering/` and the deepseek export both map to.
- A field that exists on one side only is **named**, not silently dropped; a mapping with an
  unmapped field fails the gate.
- The **producer seam** is addressed (`deepseek#115`): the contract says *who emits* each field, so
  "the record shape exists but nothing produces it" cannot recur silently on either side.
- **Truthfulness is gated** (`deepseek#106`'s lesson): a saving or a cap that cannot be measured is
  not claimed — the gate refuses a metering claim whose evidence field is empty.
- A **direction issue** is filed on `kushin77/deepseek` with the field list we need, and its URL is
  recorded in the doc. No peer repo is edited (NG4).

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-metering-parity.sh
make verify
```

## Related

- #415 (budget adapter — the local producer this contract constrains; `Blocked-by` it deliberately,
  the receipt shape must not be frozen first)
- #401 (ticket projection — carries `facets.budget` and the receipt id)
- #403 (PMO rollup — reports spend per goal/agent off this shape)
- `kushin77/deepseek#55`, `#71`, `#29`, `#30`, `#115`, `#106`; `kushin77/ollama#199`

items.milestone: M28 - Peer-module integration (paperclip / hermes / deepseek / ollama)
items.body:
Parent: 422
Blocked-by: 402

## Objective

There is a lessons loop on each side of the boundary and **no declared relationship** between them.
`kushin77/deepseek#84` ("auto-file lessons as GitHub issues and keep the mandated board in sync")
and `kushin77/deepseek#79` ("close the lessons loop: record EPIC-13 lessons in the CMR ledger and
feed them back via dispatch hints") build one; #402/#403 build ours. Both are open.

This is **not a new finding**: #181's gap register named it as gap 6 — *"Lessons-loop sync —
deepseek #84/#79 and our #141 must share one ledger, not two"* — and pointed it at #141, which has
since closed while the peer issues are still open. It is being re-filed because the substance is
still unowned.

## Lane owns

- `docs/CROSS-REPO-LESSONS-SYNC.md`
- `scripts/check-cross-repo-lessons.sh`

## Acceptance

- The doc states the decision in one line: **one authoritative ledger**, and if two must exist,
  which is the writer, which is the derived view, and the direction of the sync — never two
  symmetric stores.
- The gate checks the **contract**, not the prose: the deepseek ledger reference resolves, a lesson
  recorded on one side is discoverable from the other, and a lesson whose peer-side counterpart is
  missing is **reported by id** rather than passing silently.
- The **dispatch-hint half** is covered: `deepseek#79` wants lessons fed back as dispatch hints —
  our equivalent is the brain directive / claim chain, so the doc names the mapping and the gate
  asserts the hint carries provenance (issue ref + commit) rather than a bare string.

```bash
bash scripts/check-cross-repo-lessons.sh

```

items.title: Parent-side sub-module admission — publish and gate the contract the four peers are declaring against
items.milestone: M28 - Peer-module integration (paperclip / hermes / deepseek / ollama)
items.body:
Parent: 422

## Objective

Publish the **parent-side** half of the sub-module contract, so the four peer repos asking to
declare themselves sub-modules of this repo have something to declare against — and so `module.json`
can be **gated** rather than trusted.

**Measured (2026-09-14):** `module.json` at the repo root carries no `parent` and no `dependencies`
key, and no admission contract exists anywhere in the tree. Four peers are blocked on exactly this:

- `kushin77/hermes-agents#3`, `kushin77/deepseek#1`, `kushin77/ollama#429` — "Declare as CMR
  sub-module of agent-orchestrator (module.json + parent declaration)"
- `kushin77/paperclip#10` — same, plus the hub's doubt in `kushin77/CMR#794` that paperclip is a
  sub-module at all ("appears to be an independent product")

## Lane owns

- `module.json`
- `docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md`
- `scripts/check-module-admission.sh`

## Acceptance

- `docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md` states the contract: what a **sub-module** is, what the **parent**
  declares, what the child declares, how versions pin, and what a module must **not** inherit
  (identity, secrets, tenancy — the same rule ADR-0012 applies to runtimes).
- `module.json` gains the parent-side fields the contract requires (`parent`, `dependencies`,
  and the sub-module list), each matching a real peer repo — an entry naming a repo that does not
  exist fails the gate.
- `scripts/check-module-admission.sh` is **mutation-proven**: an undeclared sub-module, a declared
  sub-module with no `module.json` on the peer side, and a dependency pin that does not resolve must
  each exit non-zero naming the module.
- The gate distinguishes the three cases the peers represent: **declared child** (hermes-agents,
  deepseek, ollama), **independent product, explicitly not a sub-module** (the `paperclip`
  question — an answer either way, recorded, with `kushin77/CMR#794` and `kushin77/paperclip#10`
  cited), and **undeclared** (a registry entry with no declaration fails).
- **No peer repo is edited** (NG4). The child-side declaration is their issue; this lane only
  publishes the contract and the parent-side registry, and files/points at direction issues for
  anything we need from them.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-module-admission.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- The truthfulness bar is the point: a sub-module list that nothing validates is a claim, not a
  fact — and three repos are about to build their declaration against it.
- `kushin77/CMR#952` ("portfolio master view membership = module membership") shows the same
  membership question is already load-bearing at the hub; answering it here is what makes that
  mapping resolvable.

items.title: EPIC: Peer-module integration — paperclip / hermes / deepseek / ollama (cross-repo gap register)
items.milestone: M28 - Peer-module integration (paperclip / hermes / deepseek / ollama)
items.body:
## Objective

Close the **integration** gaps between this repo and the peer modules it must interoperate with —
`paperclip`, `hermes-agents`, `deepseek`, `ollama` — and make the two-way traffic a tracked,
owned mechanism instead of a periodic rediscovery.

Method: read each peer repo's board, map what already points at us, and register what does **not**
have a home on our side. The map below is the deliverable; the children are the gaps that need
work.

## The measured cross-repo landscape (2026-09-14)

The peers' boards already point at this repo. Nothing here is speculative — each row is an **open
issue in another repo** that either addresses us by name or maps onto a lane we already own.

### 1. The sub-module declaration cluster — four repos, one missing mechanism

| Peer issue | Title |
|---|---|
| `kushin77/paperclip#10` | Clarify relationship to agent-orchestrator CMR sub-module (ADR-0044) |
| `kushin77/hermes-agents#3` | Declare as CMR sub-module of agent-orchestrator (module.json + parent declaration) |
| `kushin77/deepseek#1` | Declare as CMR sub-module of agent-orchestrator (module.json + parent declaration) |
| `kushin77/ollama#429` | Declare as CMR sub-module of agent-orchestrator (module.json + parent declaration) |
| `kushin77/CMR#794` | Clarify sub-module candidacy: `kushin77/paperclip` appears to be an independent product |

Four peers ask the same question and the hub explicitly doubts one of them. Measured on our side:
our root `module.json` carries **no `parent` and no `dependencies` key**, and there is no
admission contract anywhere — so there is nothing for those four issues to declare against.
**→ gap child 1.**

### 2. The lessons / PMO loop — being built twice

| Peer issue | Title | Our lane it collides with |
|---|---|---|
| `kushin77/deepseek#84` | Auto-file lessons as GitHub issues and keep the mandated board in sync | #402 (lessons → ticket facets) |
| `kushin77/deepseek#79` | Close the lessons loop: record EPIC-13 lessons in the CMR ledger, feed back via dispatch hints | #402, #403 |
| `kushin77/deepseek#74` | pmo-sme board organization: milestones, status columns, sequencing | #403 |
| `kushin77/deepseek#78` | Declare the mandated Projects v2 board as code | #403 (board as code) |
| `kushin77/CMR#982` | Harvest DefragSuite weighted health scorer into pmo intake-scoring + priority-tiers | #403 |
| `kushin77/CMR#971` | Board taxonomy: make Class/Pattern/Template/RCA machine-readable | #403 |
| `kushin77/CMR#973` | **[P0 regression]** PMO category views lost clauses — rollup broken | #403 |
| `kushin77/CMR#759` | Program (PMO) portal tab: deps/raid tiles | #403 |
| `kushin77/CMR#865` | Board sync is one-directional only (spoke → CMR) | #403 / gap child 5 |

This is the same defect our own join layer (#399) exists to remove, reproduced **across repos**:
two lessons loops, two board-sync directions, one of them broken. #181's own gap register already
named this as gap 6 ("deepseek #84/#79 and our #141 must share one ledger, not two") and pointed
it at #141 — which has since closed while the peer issues are still open.
**→ gap child 2.**

### 3. Metering / budget / FinOps schema — no parity contract

| Peer issue | Title | Our lane |
|---|---|---|
| `kushin77/deepseek#55` | Align telemetry export with the fleet's metering schema | #415 (budget adapter) |
| `kushin77/deepseek#71` | Back the cost claim with this repo's own metering | #415, #401 |
| `kushin77/deepseek#29` | Budget enforcement promotion path, end to end | #415 |
| `kushin77/deepseek#30` | Expose usage and cost through CLI and MCP resources | #415, #419 |
| `kushin77/deepseek#115` | Metering attribution has the record shape but not the producer seam | #415 |
| `kushin77/deepseek#106` | Terse-output default is ON and saves nothing measurable — decide | #415 |
| `kushin77/ollama#199` | Token budget enforcement — reject prompts exceeding the context window | #415 |

Two repos independently claim to produce cost/usage for the same fleet, with **no shared schema and
no shared receipt**. Our budget adapter (#415) is about to freeze a receipt shape; if it does so
without parity, we build the third variant. **→ gap child 3.**

### 4. Routing — the half-coupling risk, named by a peer

| Peer issue | Title | Our lane |
|---|---|---|
| `kushin77/hermes-agents#2` | [assimilation] Extract the tier-routing brain as a standalone reusable package | `gateway/sme-routing/`, #337, ADR-0012 |
| `kushin77/deepseek#91/#90/#89/#88` | Steer-dispatch / Claude-CLI sub-agents on DeepSeek BYOK + capability declaration | #337, #349 |
| `kushin77/deepseek#54` | Model-profile recognition for the DeepSeek tiers | #349, `gateway/finops/chooser.py` |
| `kushin77/deepseek#66` | BYOK: make DeepSeek the model Copilot thinks with | #349 |
| `kushin77/deepseek#60` | Bridge: adapter pinning the `deepseek_agent` public API | #349, `gateway/providers/deepseek.py` |
| `kushin77/deepseek#116` | `reasoning_content`: the Responses path omits it | #349 |

`hermes-agents#2` proposes extracting a **second routing authority** as a reusable package, while we
now run `gateway/sme-routing/`. ADR-0012 already names *two authoritative routing engines* as the
worst outcome and requires a declared seam — this is that decision, one repo over.
**→ gap child 4.**

### 5. Consumption links (no new work — these map onto lanes we already own)

| Peer issue | Our lane | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `kushin77/paperclip#9` | #400, #416 | their ticket/approval state-machine + dashboard IA is a **design reference** for the contract we are freezing |
| `kushin77/deepseek#67` | #419 | MCP bridge: register `deepseek-agent` with Copilot |
| `kushin77/deepseek#34` | registry | prompt registry with publish + pin rollback |
| `kushin77/deepseek#53` | #403 | dispatch integration: context-pack + issue-hint consumption |
| `kushin77/deepseek#52` | #411 | DS worker-tier integration with **read-only default** — our flag-gated-OFF posture |
| `kushin77/ollama#167` | #417 | vault integration, zero `.env` credentials |
| `kushin77/ollama#200` | `guardrails/` DLP | PII scrubbing before logging |
| `kushin77/ollama#125` | #349 | multi-model orchestration platform |
| `kushin77/deepseek#117` | gate discipline | two repaired `Verify:` clauses are runnable but **not truthful** — the same "a gate that cannot fail is a formality" lesson |
| `kushin77/CMR#967` | #337 | mandatory module runtime health + deployment gate for sibling modules |
| `kushin77/CMR#968` | SPoG #338 | shared-frontend compliance + visible agent-ecosystem UI |
| `kushin77/CMR#980` | `guardrails/` | harvest the DefragSuite guardrail rule set **into agent-orchestrator** |
| `kushin77/CMR#992` | dispatch doctrine | GR-20b chronological, dependency-gated selection |
| `kushin77/CMR#974`, `#883` | `governance/dispatch/` | lane collision prevention, pre-dispatch owner resolution |
| `kushin77/code-indexing#128/#129/#130/#132` | `engine/memory/` | context-pack consumption + DR-069 baselines (per #181) |

## Children (the gaps)

| Gap | Child | Issue | Owning lane | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Parent-side sub-module admission** — declare + gate the contract the four peers are asking for | #423 | `module.json`, `docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md`, `scripts/check-module-admission.sh` | **landed** — `docs/MODULE-ADMISSION.md` + `scripts/check-module-admission.sh` on master |
| 2 | **Cross-repo lessons: one ledger** — reconcile the deepseek lessons loop with #402/#403 | #424 | cross-repo half of the lessons register | open |
| 3 | **Metering/budget schema parity** — one receipt shape across deepseek's metering and our rail | #425 | `docs/contracts/metering/**` | open |
| 4 | **Hermes tier-routing ↔ `gateway/sme-routing` seam** — one routing authority, declared | #426 | ADR-0015 + routing contract docs | **landed** — `ADR-0015-routing-seam-single-authority.md`, `docs/contracts/routing/**`, gate |
| 5 | **Bidirectional sync owner** — a standing, code-native peer-board triage that files direction issues | #427 | `governance/sync/**` | **landed** — `docs/CROSS-REPO-SYNC-OWNER.md` + gate |
| 6 | **Ecosystem module registry + state federation** — one honest view of every module (mandatory status, pin, consumer assets, health), by reference, never vendored | #445 | `governance/modules/**` | open |
| 7 | **Reporting agent composes the module brief** — the `paperclip` persona declares the capability and freezes the per-module distributable artifact | #447 | `registry/personas/cards/paperclip.yaml` + `paperclip/reporting/**` | open |

Progress: three children landed via PR #440 (`feat(governance): wire the EPIC-422 integration gates
into the gate of record`, merge `12fa0f05f`); their gates are in the gate of record. Four remain, of
which #445 → #447 is the registry-then-report pair.

Chain edges: #424 is `Blocked-by: #402` (the local lessons lane it reconciles with), #425 is
`Blocked-by: #415` (the budget adapter whose receipt shape must not be frozen first), and #445/#447
form their own pair — **#447 is `Blocked-by: #445`**, because the reporting agent composes the brief
*from* the registry and must not invent a second source. #423, #426 and #427 are unblocked; none of
the seven is blocked by this EPIC (an epic is never an eligible claim target, so a `Blocked-by` on it
would deadlock the frontier).

## The distribution rule (why this is a registry and a report, not a vendored pile)

Every child obeys the same rule, and it is the rule that answers "should we vendor the modules?" with
**no**:

- **Declare** — `module.json` + parent declaration (#423);
- **Federate by reference** — the hub's `catalog/mandatory.tsv` + module flags + consumer-asset
  seeds are read, never copied (#445);
- **Compose** — the reporting agent turns the registry into each module's brief (#447);
- **Distribute** — the channel that already exists ships the **consumer assets**
  (`.mcp.json`, `gdc-manifest.yaml`, `architecture.yaml`, `tokens.json`) via
  `controller/onboard.sh` / `controller/standards-sync.sh` / `controller/standards-manifest.txt` and
  the `templates/module/` seeds. **Do not rebuild it.**

Vendoring module *source* would duplicate the truth (ADR-0012 half-coupling), break GR-10 /
ADR-0010 canonical-copy ownership, violate NG4, and contradict ADR-0013's explicit *no vendoring* —
so the registry gate **fails a module carried in-tree as source rather than referenced**, and the
only vendor path in this repo remains `vendor/CMR` (pinned submodule, read-only).

## Boundary (non-negotiable)

Per `docs/CROSS-REPO-EXECUTION-BOUNDARY.md` (NG4): **we never edit a peer repo.** A need is a
**direction issue on that repo's board**; a peer's defect is tracked here only as the half we own.
No child of this EPIC writes outside this repository, and no foreign issue is closed from here —
cross-repo `Closes` is explicitly not used.

## Definition of done

1. A peer can declare itself a sub-module of this repo against a published, gated contract.
2. There is **one** lessons ledger and **one** PMO rollup, or a declared adapter between two —
   never two undisclosed.
3. The budget/metering receipt has one shape, agreed with deepseek's export.
4. The routing seam between a reusable tier-routing package and `gateway/sme-routing/` is decided
   by an ADR, per ADR-0012.
5. Peer-board review is a scheduled, code-native pass that files direction issues with provenance —
   not a memory.

## Verify

```bash
make verify
bash scripts/check-module-admission.sh
```

## Provenance (GR-10)

Every foreign issue above was read from the live board on 2026-09-14 and is cited by
`owner/repo#N`. No peer repo was modified, cloned into this tree, or vendored.

items.title: Wire the paperclip boundary and adapter gates into the gate of record
items.body:
Parent: 410
Blocked-by: #411, #412, #413, #414, #415, #416, #417, #418, #419, #401, #403

## Objective

Wire every paperclip boundary and adapter gate into the **gate of record**, so none of them is a
script that only runs when someone remembers to run it. This lane owns the three shared build files
so no two of the sibling adapters edit them in the same wave.

## Lane owns

- `Makefile`
- `scripts/verify.sh`
- `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`
- `docs/README.md`

## Acceptance

- Every `scripts/check-paperclip-*.sh` is in `scripts/verify.sh`'s `checks=()` array with its own
  name, and every adapter's pytest suite is declared in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt` (run in
  isolation — a combined run collides on sibling `conftest` imports).
- Each new check is **provably able to fail**: the attestation lists it with a real rc, and the
  mutation proof for the check itself is attached as evidence (GR-12).
- `make paperclip` (or equivalent) exists as a convenience target, and the wiring is reflected in
  `make help`.
- `docs/README.md` indexes the new docs, and **no check is registered that cannot fail** — a
  formality is rejected rather than counted.
- The gate verdict is quoted from `.verify/attestation.json` (`result`, `exit_code`, `git_sha`,
  `check_count`), not from make's exit code.

## Verify

```bash
make verify
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.verify/attestation.json'));print(d['result'], d['check_count'], [c['name'] for c in d['checks'] if c['status']!='PASS'])"
make paperclip
```

## Notes

- **Serialized by construction:** `Makefile`, `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`
  are also owned by #401 (ticket projection) and #403 (PMO rollup), so this lane is `Blocked-by`
  both — one writer per wave, which is exactly the lesson from the #307/#304 cron-manager
  collision.
- **ENOSPC check before wiring:** every new check must be measured for runtime; a check that makes
  `make verify` slower than a lane will tolerate gets disabled within a week. Report the measured
  delta.

items.title: Skills, plugins and MCP — a SKILL.md registry and the MCP tool projection
items.body:
Parent: 410
Blocked-by: #400

## Objective

Map upstream's **extensibility** family — skills (`SKILL.md`), plugins/extensions and MCP tool
access — onto what we already run: `gateway/mcp/` for tools, `guardrails/` for policy, and this
repo's own skills tree. Today there is no registry that says *which* skill an agent may load or
*which* MCP tool a run may call.

## Lane owns

- `paperclip/adapters/skills/**`
- `scripts/check-paperclip-skills.sh`

## Acceptance

- A **`SKILL.md` registry**: every loadable skill is declared with its origin and provenance
  (GR-10 — a harvested or third-party skill records repo/path/license), and an **undeclared** skill
  is refused rather than silently loaded.
- **MCP tools are projected, not duplicated**: the tool list derives from `gateway/mcp/`, and a
  tool that is callable but absent from the projection is a FAIL (the projection must be a view,
  not an allowlist maintained by hand).
- A skill or plugin that requires a capability the agent's profile does not grant is **refused at
  load**, so extensibility cannot widen an agent's authority — the profile stays the authority.
- No upstream code is vendored; a skill is a declaration plus a reference, never a copied
  implementation (GR-10).

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-paperclip-skills.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- Registry discipline mirrors the agent registry (`registry/profiles/`, `registry/personas/`): one
  declaration, one owner, one gate.
- Keeping the tool projection derived is what prevents the classic drift where the docs list of
  tools and the callable set diverge.

items.title: Routines — expose fleet/cron.py schedules as projected routine objects
items.body:
Parent: 410
Blocked-by: #400, #403

## Objective

Project **routines**: upstream models scheduled recurring work as a first-class object (trigger +
params + owner). We have the mechanism — `fleet/cron.py`, code-native scheduling (no GitHub
Actions, GR-15) — but nothing an operator can see, name or reason about.

## Lane owns

- `paperclip/adapters/routines/**`
- `scripts/check-paperclip-routines.sh`

- Every scheduled entry in `fleet/cron.py` projects to exactly one routine with its **trigger**,
  its **owner** and its **params**, and a routine whose schedule exists only on the upstream side

  entry added/removed with no routine change) is reported rather than passing silently.
- A routine with no owner, or a schedule that cannot be expressed as a trigger, fails closed.
- The gate is mutation-proven: delete an entry from a copy and require the adapter to notice.

  program-management truth the rollup reports; the routine view must agree with it rather than

items.title: Per-agent secret vault primitive — GSM-backed, never upstream's store as source of truth
items.body:
Parent: 410
Blocked-by: #400

## Objective

Give the fleet a **per-agent secret primitive** — upstream ships a secrets resource family scoped
per company/agent; we have a GR-6 mandate (env / Secret Manager only) but no first-class primitive
for "this agent, this credential, this rotation".

## Lane owns

- `paperclip/adapters/secrets/**`
- `scripts/check-paperclip-secrets.sh`

## Acceptance

- The primitive **names** a secret (its GSM path, the agent and scope it belongs to) and never
  carries the value: no secret in code, in a file, in git history, in a log, or in a finding
  message (GR-6). A finding reports the rule and the location, never the matched value.
- **Secret Manager remains the store of record.** Upstream's secret store is **not** adopted as
  our authority — the adapter is a reference/rotation view over GSM, and the gate asserts no
  second store is introduced.
- **Rotation is expressible**: a secret records when it was last rotated and which agent consumes
  it, and a secret with no consumer is reported (not silently kept).
- Reading a secret requires an authenticated, scoped caller (the auth lane's identity) — an
  unscoped read is refused, and the refusal is tested.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-paperclip-secrets.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- A secrets adapter is the one place where "adopt the product's feature" would be actively
  harmful: two secret stores means two answers to "what is the credential", which is exactly the
  half-coupling ADR-0012 forbids.
- `guardrails/` DLP and `identity/` remain the enforcement points; this lane adds the primitive
  and the projection.

`integrations/paperclip/**` — issue #428, PR #433, commit `9cd5794`; gate

items.title: Approvals as a projected resource — hire, top-up and override mapped to directive + claim
items.body:
Parent: 410
Blocked-by: #400

## Objective

Make **approvals** a projected resource. Upstream models them as first-class objects (approve a
hire, approve a budget top-up, approve/override a strategy) with an actor and an audit trail. We
have the *authority* already — a top-up is a brain directive, a hire is the claim gate — but no
object an operator or an API consumer can act on.

## Lane owns

- `paperclip/adapters/approvals/**`
- `scripts/check-paperclip-approvals.sh`

## Acceptance

- An approval is a **projection of an existing authority**, never a second one: top-up →
  `.fleet/sent` directive; hire/assign → `governance/dispatch/` claim; override → the control
  verb. The adapter names the authority for each kind, and a kind with no authority behind it is
  refused.
- **Approve and deny both land** in the authoritative record (a directive id, a claim event), with
  the actor recorded — an approval that changes only a projection is a bug, and the gate proves it
  by mutating the projection without the record and requiring a FAIL.
- A **pending** approval is distinguishable from a granted one; an item approved twice, or decided
  by an actor with no authority to decide it, is refused.
- The autonomy posture is unchanged: autonomy is **granted, never default** (ADR-0013 /
  the repo's governance rules) — the adapter cannot grant what the fleet did not grant.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-paperclip-approvals.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- This is the cleanest example of the whole EPIC's rule: *project, do not duplicate*. If this
  adapter ever needs its own store, the design is wrong.
- Scope deliberately excludes UI: the approval surfaces in the shell are SPoG-owned.

items.title: Budget adapter — agent/team/project scope, currency, boolean hard stop and per-task receipts (§5.7–§5.10)
items.body:
Parent: 410
Blocked-by: #400, #401

## Objective

Close `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` §5 items **7–10** — the budget rail is scoped by
**tenant and vendor** (`telemetry/budgets/budget.py` `VendorBudgetCap`, window `month`) rather than
by **agent / team / project**; USD is a convention with no `currency` field; the stop is a
percentage (`hard_cap_pct`) rather than an absolute cap with a hand-off; and there is **no
per-task receipt** tying a spend to the work it paid for.

## Lane owns

- `paperclip/adapters/budget/**`
- `scripts/check-paperclip-budget.sh`

## Acceptance

- `scope.level` ∈ `agent | team | project` is derived from the existing rail, and a level with no
  producer fails closed rather than silently reporting `tenant`.
- `cap` / `spent` / `currency` are derived from `limitUsd` and the metering store; currency is
  **stated**, not assumed.
- `hard_stop` is a **boolean** derived from `hard_cap_pct` (default 100), and the hand-off is
  described — at the cap the work stops and asks, it does not silently continue.
- **`receipt_ref` ties a spend to a ticket**: the adapter emits the receipt id that the ticket's
  `evidence[]` carries (#400/#401), so a charge is attributable to the delivery it funded. A spend
  that resolves to **no ticket** is a FAIL, not an orphan row.
- `burn_rate_alert_pct` is mapped from `warn_at_pct` / `hard_cap_pct`, and a spend with no
  declared cap is refused rather than treated as unlimited.
- The gate is mutation-proven on: a receipt with no ticket, a cap with no scope level, and a
  currency-less row.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-paperclip-budget.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- This is the FinOps half of the ticket contract: once a receipt lands on the ticket, the SPoG
  FinOps reports (#341) can attribute spend per agent from **one** node instead of joining a
  vendor bucket to an issue by hand.

items.title: Heartbeat adapter — synthesize wake.cause, wake.delta and outcome from rung activity (§5.1–§5.3)
items.body:
Parent: 410
Blocked-by: #400

## Objective

Close `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` §5 items **1–3** — the fleet beat is a flat
process-liveness record (`pid`, `state`, `started_at`, `commit`, `ts`) with **no** `wake.cause`,
**no** `wake.delta` and **no** `outcome`, and no explicit tick or cadence. Upstream's heartbeat is
an event wake or a scheduled tick that carries the delta and ends in durable progress or a named
blocker with an owner.

## Lane owns

- `paperclip/adapters/heartbeat/**`
- `scripts/check-paperclip-heartbeat.sh`

## Acceptance

- The adapter **synthesizes** `wake.cause` (`assigned` / `commented` / `unblocked` /
  `review-requested` / `scheduled`) from real rung activity — `fleet/monitor.py`,
  `fleet/brain.py` and `fleet/terminal.py` — and never fabricates a cause it cannot source.
- `wake.delta` carries **the change since the last beat** (what was claimed, closed, blocked or
  unblocked), so a consumer needs no history re-read; a delta is not a state dump.
- `outcome.status` is `progress` **or** `blocked` with a named `owner`; a beat that ends in
  neither fails closed rather than reporting progress it cannot evidence.
- `tick` and `cadence_seconds` are **derived** from the actual emit count and `POLL_SECONDS`, with
  the staleness ceiling (`STALE_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS`) declared — the fleet's implicit cadence is
  made explicit without inventing a second scheduler.
- The mapping is **deterministic** and the gate is **mutation-proven**: a beat that carries no
  delta, an unknown `wake.cause`, and a `blocked` outcome with no owner must each be refused by
  name.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-paperclip-heartbeat.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- The fleet remains the writer of liveness; this adapter only *derives* the upstream shape
  (ADR-0012: map the policy, do not couple the runtime).
- The wake/delta semantics are what the SPoG live feed (#345) consumes — feed it, do not rebuild
  it here.

items.body:
Parent: 409

## Objective

Project the fleet's state over upstream's HTTP surface — `GET /api/health`,
`GET /api/openapi.json`, the company-scoped route shape
`/api/companies/{companyId}/...`, and upstream's error taxonomy — so the operator surface reads
**our** truth across the boundary.

## Lane owns

- `paperclip/api/**`
- `scripts/check-paperclip-openapi.sh`

## Acceptance

- **The contracts are the source:** the OpenAPI document is emitted from the frozen contracts in
  `docs/contracts/paperclip/` (ticket, heartbeat, budget — and the v2 fields #400 adds) plus the
  adapters' shapes, never hand-written in parallel with them.
- **Company scope is a projection of our tenancy**, not a new one: `{companyId}` maps onto
  `identity/` tenants/orgs with one declared mapping, and a cross-company read is refused (`403`).
- **The error taxonomy is mapped, not invented**: `400` validation · `401` bad caller identity ·
  `403` known-but-not-allowed · `404` missing/outside company scope · `409` conflict/owned/locked ·
  `422` business-rule rejection · `503` dependency unreachable — each with at least one test.
- **`/api/health` reflects real dependencies** (ledgers readable, projection fresh), and reports
  `503` rather than a green lie when one is unreachable.
- The emitted document is **deterministic** — two builds over one revision are byte-identical, so
  a diff means a real change.

```bash
bash scripts/check-paperclip-openapi.sh
make verify
```

- **Transport is not this lane.** The serving layer is SPoG #339; this issue owns the

items.title: Cross-boundary auth for the paperclip seam — agent key/JWT mint+verify, board token adapter, run-id bridge
items.body:
Parent: 409
Blocked-by: #411

## Objective

Make the two auth models meet **once**, correctly, at the process boundary — closing
`docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` §5 item **11 (auth models do not meet natively)**: upstream
has agent keys/JWTs, a board session cookie and a board token; the fleet has no HTTP caller
identity at all.

## Lane owns

- `paperclip/auth/**`
- `scripts/check-paperclip-auth.sh`

## Acceptance

- **Agent identity** is minted and verified from the fleet's own records: a key/JWT bound to a
  registered agent, with the tenant/company scope carried in the claim — no parallel identity
  store, no second source of truth (ADR-0012).
- **Human identity** maps to the board token / session path, so an operator authenticates to the
  operator surface without a third login.
- **Run correlation** is bridged: the upstream `X-Paperclip-Run-Id` binds to the fleet's existing
  `correlation_id` (`fleet/channel.py`, `fleet/schema/message.schema.json`), so one run is
  traceable on both sides.
- **Negative controls are first-class and proven** — each must be *shown* to be refused:
  an expired/unknown token, a token for the wrong company, a replayed run id, a missing
  `Authorization` header, and a caller that is authenticated but not allowed (`403`, not `404`).
- No secret value is written to the repo, a log, or a finding (GR-6), and a finding never echoes
  the matched value.

## Verify

```bash
bash scripts/check-paperclip-auth.sh
make verify
```

## Notes

- Cross-boundary auth is explicitly named in ADR-0013 as **one-time integration work**, not a
  recurring cost — this issue pays it once and pins it with a gate.
- The refusals matter more than the happy path: a boundary that authenticates everything is worse
  than one that authenticates nothing.

## Objective

Declare and run the upstream paperclip.ing runtime **beside** the control plane as an external

items.title: EPIC: Paperclip parity adapters — six thin adapters onto the frozen ticket contract
items.body:
## Objective

Ship the six **thin adapters** that make upstream's capability families real against our own
ledgers — each one a *projection* onto the frozen ticket contract (#400), never a new store and
never a second authority.

**Measured position (2026-09-14):** the gap analysis shows the fleet already ships the hard parts
of every upstream family; what is missing is the mapping. Six upstream families have no fleet-side
producer today: event-wake heartbeats (§5.1–§5.3), agent/team/project budgets with receipts
(§5.7–§5.10), first-class approvals, per-agent secrets, routines, and the skills/MCP loader.

## The rule every adapter obeys

1. **Projection, not authority.** The ledger stays the writer; the adapter derives and maps.
   One writer per field, declared in the contract's `authority{}` (#400).
2. **Deterministic.** Two runs over one revision produce byte-identical output.
3. **Fail closed.** An unmappable value is a FAIL naming the field — never a silent default.
4. **Mutation-proven gate.** Each adapter ships `scripts/check-paperclip-<adapter>.sh` and is
   *shown* to fail on a mutated input before it merges (GR-12).

## Children

| Child | Issue | Upstream family | Closes | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Heartbeat adapter** — synthesize `wake.cause`, `wake.delta`, `outcome` from rung activity | #414 | heartbeats | §5.1–§5.3 | #400 |
| **Budget adapter** — agent/team/project scope, currency, boolean hard stop, per-task receipt | #415 | costs | §5.7–§5.10 | #400, #401 |
| **Approvals as a projected resource** — hire / top-up / override | #416 | approvals | new family | #400 |
| **Per-agent secret vault primitive** — GSM-backed | #417 | secrets | new family | #400 |
| **Routines** — `fleet/cron.py` schedules as projected routine objects | #418 | routines | new family | #400, #403 |
| **Skills / plugins / MCP** — `SKILL.md` registry + MCP tool projection | #419 | extensibility | new family | #400 |
| **Gate wiring** — every new check into the gate of record | #420 | — | GR-12 | #414–#419, #401, #403 |

## Gate wiring

Every adapter ships its own `scripts/check-paperclip-<name>.sh` and its own pytest suite. The
three shared build files (`Makefile`, `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`) are owned
by **one** wiring issue (**#420**) so no two lanes edit them in the same wave — the EPIC-144
precedent, and the fix for the #307/#304 cron-manager collision.

## What this EPIC will NOT do

- **No new ledger.** An adapter that needs persistence is out of scope; the ledgers already exist.
- **No adoption of upstream's stores as authority** — in particular the secrets family maps to
  Secret Manager, not to upstream's secret store (GR-6).
- **No duplication of SPoG work.** The activity feed and dashboard families are owned by the SPoG
  children (#344 catalog UX, #345 SSE feed, #347 audit surface); this EPIC feeds them the
  wake/delta semantics rather than rebuilding them.

## Definition of done

All six adapters map their family onto the frozen contract; each gate is mutation-proven and
wired into `make verify`; the ticket graph is the single place a consumer reads task, agent,
lesson, budget and approval state from; `make verify` is green on a clean checkout of the merge
commit.

## Verify

```bash
for g in heartbeat budget approvals secrets routines skills; do
  bash "scripts/check-paperclip-$g.sh" || exit 1
done
make verify
```

## Provenance (GR-10)

Upstream: `paperclipai/paperclip` (product **paperclip.ing**), **MIT**, `v2026.831.1`
(2026-09-02). Adapters are written against the frozen contracts in `docs/contracts/paperclip/`;
**no upstream code is vendored** and no upstream file becomes a dependency.

---

## Landed while this EPIC was open (measured 2026-09-14)

`integrations/paperclip/**` landed via `9cd5794` (issue #428, PR #433) — the transport-seamed
client, the deterministic mapper and a fully offline gate that resolve
`docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` §5's mismatch list, checked in `make verify` as `paperclip-adapter`.

**That module is canonical for the boundary adapter.** The lane globs in this EPIC's children were
written before it landed and are corrected by #448; a child that builds its own top-level
`paperclip/**` module would duplicate it (the `#307`/`#304` collision lesson).

## Objective

Stand the upstream paperclip.ing runtime up **beside** the control plane and wire the frozen
seam end-to-end across the process boundary — the adoption work ADR-0013 decided and #370 froze
but deliberately did not run.

(`docs/decision-records/ADR-0013-paperclip-ing-integration.md`,
`docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md`, `docs/contracts/paperclip/*.schema.json`) and **nothing is

`docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` §5's **item 11 (auth models do not meet natively)** and the
process boundary itself are the whole of this EPIC.

| Leg | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Join layer — the ticket as the single join node | #399 + #400–#403 | filed |
| **Boundary — this EPIC** | milestone *M27* | filing now |
